author: countrymanprime
body:
## Goal
Phase 5 of the palette PRD (`docs/prds/palette-contrast-wcag-aa.prd.md`, [ADR 0059](docs/adr/0059-text-colours-meet-wcag-aa-with-two-text-levels-a-non-text-token-and-derived-on-tint-text.md)): no measured text pair below AA. The status text (danger, review, warn, info) was 2.4 to 4.2:1 in light, and placeholders (which nothing measured) about 3.25:1.

## What changed
- `styles.css`: `--danger-text`, `--warn-text` and `--info-text`. In light `--danger-text` and `--info-text` darken the fill colour toward `--text` (85% and 90% of the fill colour) and `--warn-text` is an explicit dark amber, `#755507`; in dark they equal the fill colour, which already passes (so, unlike the entity `--<kind>-text` tokens, the dark block overrides them). `--danger`, `--warn` and `--info` stay for borders, dots and fills. The warn text is the tightest pair: on a warn tint over a hovered or selected table row (`--surface-2`) `#755507` is 4.62:1.
- Text moved to the companions: `Button` and `IconButton` danger variants (the border stays `--danger`), the `Field` error, `ProjectPicker`, `TeleprompterPage` and `TracksPage` alerts and the unplayable-track icon, `ErrorBoundary`'s icon, the Home last-completed ("discrepancies") badge, the Settings alert and "Unsaved changes" line, the Teleprompter "Waiting" status, the inline diff's MISREAD, SKIPPED and EXTRA words, the Results "Already marked" badge, and the marker export error (a Tailwind `text-red-400`, 2.89:1 on white in light, is now the token). Three tests that pinned the red button's old class name (`ConfirmDialog`, `IconButton`, `GuideDetail`) name the new one.
- Placeholders: `input::placeholder, textarea::placeholder { color: var(--text-muted); opacity: 1 }` in the base layer. Tailwind 4's preflight draws a placeholder at 50% of the field's text colour, 3.25:1 in light; it is text under WCAG 1.4.3, axe does not test it and no pair covered it. Measured in Chrome over every state that shows a field (74 states, both themes, seven distinct placeholders): `rgb(98, 94, 82)` at full opacity on the field fill, 6.48:1 in light and 7.15:1 in dark.
- Guard (`paletteContrast.test.ts`), RED first (16 failures before the tokens and call sites existed): the status pairs measure the new tokens over more surfaces (a hovered row for the warn badge), `KNOWN_FAILURES` is empty and its cap is 0 (7 to 0), 3:1 mark pairs for `--warn` and `--info` (the status dots, meter segments and the skipped-word underline), a test for the placeholder rule, and a test that no text uses a Tailwind palette colour, an arbitrary text colour that is not a `var()`, or a literal `color:` (mutation-checked with `text-red-400` and `text-[#f87171]`).
- Docs: `design-system.md` gets a status text paragraph; ADR 0059 gets an "Update (phase 5)"; the PRD marks phase 5 `complete`.

## For the owner's eye
- The light `--warn-text` is a dark amber (`#755507`), because the amber fill cannot reach 4.5:1 on a tint without going that dark. My first version was a 50% mix of the amber toward the olive page text; the visual review found it read as a grey-brown, not a warning, so it is an explicit colour at the same lightness that keeps its chroma. It is still the biggest colour change in this PR: standalone warn text ("Unsaved changes", the Teleprompter's "Waiting") is now a dark gold, not the amber of the pills and dots.
- The Home last-completed badge (a discrepancy count on `--review-soft`) uses `--danger-text`, a red at 4.98:1; the entity Review badge on the same fill uses `--review-text`, a darker red-brown at 8.2:1. The reviewer suggested `--review-text` for the Home badge (a discrepancy count is a review state, not an error); I kept the red so it stays visibly a warning. One line in `Home.tsx` if you prefer the other.

## ADR change for review
ADR 0059 (merged with #124 and updated for phase 4 by #140) gets an "Update (phase 5)" section, appended in the same way as the phase 4 one and without touching the decision text: status text has companions rather than a `--review` equivalent, the light mixes and the dark overrides, placeholders, and text taking tokens only. The decision itself is unchanged. No new ADR.

## Verification
- `pnpm check` (the full gate): exit 0 (63 UI test files, 793 tests, plus Go, Python and build targets).
- `pnpm --dir apps/ui atlas`: 880 passed, no debt entry, cap 0 (the danger variants of `Button` and `IconButton`, `Field` error and `ErrorBoundary` stories in both themes).
- Playwright visual suite, light and dark, three viewports: 222 of 222 in each theme (the dark run ends with the documented validation on `theme-dark`/`reader-dark`). Against phase 4, 129 (light) and 63 (dark) of 222 captures differ: the states that show status text or a field with a placeholder (dark never changes for warn, danger or info, only for the placeholders).
- **Scratch axe `color-contrast` pass over every app state (144 captures per theme, desktop and tablet): 0 violations in light and 0 in dark.** After slice 2a it was 136 states with a violation in light and 133 in dark.
- Code review (typescript-reviewer): no CRITICAL or HIGH. The MEDIUMs are fixed: the ADR update note, and the literal-colour guard, which missed arbitrary colours, style objects and stylesheets (it now covers them and names the match; mock data is excluded). The LOWs: the placeholder test could match a `background-color` (now anchored), two comments were wrong, and `--warn` and `--info` dots had no pair (now they do). Left as a judgement call: the Home badge token, above.
- PNG review, light and dark at desktop, small-desktop and tablet: 18 comparison images and 12 full-size captures were reviewed by a reviewer subagent, plus the warn text before, after the first version and after the final one by me. Findings: layout identical in every state and viewport; the light red text (the MISREAD word and pill, the diff words, the discrepancies badge, Stop and Cancel, the track warning triangles) is still clearly red and readable on its tints; the pills (SKIPPED, Already marked) hold up as dark bronze on the amber tint; the dark theme is unchanged apart from the placeholders; the placeholders are clearly darker in light and brighter in dark yet still visibly lighter and regular-weight next to typed values, so they are not mistaken for them. The one problem, the grey-brown warn text, is the change described above; the 13 light captures it changed were re-taken and re-checked (axe 0 and the atlas 880 again).

Base: main (phases 1 to 4 were merged as #124, #125, #127, #134, #131, #132, #133 and #140; this branch is rebased onto them and the whole verification below was re-run after the rebase)

Part of #123

body:
This commit applies several critical fixes aligned with the task scope:
1. **Supabase Edge Auth**: Wrapped token setting operations in `soc-cockpit/src/middleware.ts` inside a `try/catch` to fail-soft and prevent runtime crashes.
2. **Telemetry Payload alignment**: Updated the `TelemetryEvent` and `AsguardTelemetryEvent` schemas in `asguard-interceptor` and `soc-cockpit` to be strictly typed and matching.
3. **Robust Threat Feed**: Updated `soc-cockpit/src/components/LiveThreatFeed.tsx` with a state-based exponential backoff system (`LIVE`, `RECONNECTING`, `OFFLINE`). Included synthetic fallback data structures so the UI never appears broken or empty.
4. **UI Styling**: Refined the `GlobalThreatMap.tsx` and `LiveChat.tsx` layout and styling with monospaced timestamps, loading pulse indicators, and Cloudflare PoP/Latency tags.
5. **Agent Inference Errors**: Updated `asguard-interceptor/src/aiService.ts` to properly catch failures natively and return explicit structured data. Updated `soc-cockpit/src/app/api/chat/route.ts` to correctly log telemetry metric details instead of static defaults.

author: yjsoon
body:
Implements yjsoon's request for Display to have the same Show/Dismiss shortcut capability as regular widgets on macOS, Windows and Linux, followed by a verified v0.12.1 release.

**Draft integration checkpoint — not ready to merge or release.** Windows source and native test coverage are present; separately owned macOS/Linux implementation and native evidence are still pending integration. Release notes describe the intended complete behavior, not a shipped result.

- Keep existing Display Show assignments; initialize Dismiss to the same key for toggle behavior. Distinct keys act independently, and cleared assignments stay cleared.
- Dismiss closes the native preview, stops capture and cancels automatic resumption while preserving its saved source and position. Show and menu/launcher actions remain singleton opens.
- Reuse existing regular-widget paired shortcut controls and conflict rules. Display remains independent of the teacher widget host.
- Add read-only desktop CI to run the native Windows application assembly/tests, Swift suite, and Linux unit tests. Windows evidence includes rendered Settings states and real registered-hotkey dispatch.

Executed locally: Windows settings tests observed their expected regression failures, then passed 12/12; actual Windows application/test Release cross-build passed with zero warnings/errors. Native Windows runtime/visual evidence is pending this PR's CI. macOS/Linux full source integration and independent high-tier correctness, security/privacy and compatibility/operability reviews remain required gates.

No default-branch merge, release workflow dispatch or v0.12.1 tag/publication has occurred. v0.12.0 remains unchanged.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [pyparsing](https://pypi.org/project/pyparsing) from **3.0.9** to **3.3.3**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.3.3
   ```
   ------------------------------
- Added support for Python 3.15.

- Parse actions that return a tuple value for a named expression formerly saved
  just the first value of the tuple. Now they return the entire tuple. Partially
  fixes Issue 401, PR 640 submitted by Vincent Gao et AI.

- Fixed CI unit test jobs selecting a tox environment with no test commands.
  The matrix and fallback now select `py-unit`, as diagnosed and proposed by
  glaziermag in issue 662; submitted by Neal Lin et AI.

- Fixed `Dict` returning an empty nested `ParseResults.as_dict()` as `[]`
  instead of `{}`. Incorporates partial solution submitted in PR 635
  submitted by Leo Ji.

  Additional fixes found as part of this work:

  - Removed vestigial unused `ParseResults._modal` attribute.

  - Fixed incidental bug when Dict tries to create a dict with a `ParseResults`
    value for a key (not hashable).

- Fixed `Word(..., max=n)` raising instead of matching up to `max` characters
  when the character set contained whitespace - `Word(nums, max=3)` and
  `Word(nums + " ", max=3)` gave opposite results on
  the same input. Now both forms match up to `max` and leave the rest for
  the next parser. PR 646 submitted by Andrew Chen et AI.

- Fixed `QuotedString` stripping whitespace that is part of a multi-character
  quote delimiter, e.g. the leading newline in `QuotedString("\n;",
  multiline=True)`. The delimiter was silently collapsed to `";"`, so the
  newline was ignored when matching. `QuotedString` now only rejects
  quote_char/end_quote_char values that are empty or entirely whitespace, and
  preserves any surrounding whitespace that is part of a valid delimiter.
  Reported in issue 492.

- Fixed `pyparsing_common.as_datetime` raising `Invalid date/time: microsecond
  must be in 0..999999` for valid ISO-8601 timestamps whose fractional seconds
  round up to a full second (e.g. `2021-06-15T12:30:59.9999995`, common in
  nanosecond-precision timestamps). The rounded microseconds are now added via
  `timedelta` so the value carries into the next second instead of overflowing
  the `datetime` microsecond argument. PR submitted by Andrew Chen et AI.

- Fixed debug output corruption when a parsed line contains a carriage return or
  other control character. `set_debug()` printed the source line verbatim, so a
  stray `\r` returned the terminal cursor to column 0 and overwrote the "Match ...
  at loc" text. Control characters in the debug line are now shown escaped, and the
  marker caret stays aligned with the match location. Issue 496, reported by
  Matthew Rowles.

- Fixed `ParseResults.copy()` sharing its results-name bookkeeping with the original.
  The copy got its own token list, but the per-name lists of matched occurrences were
  shared, and `insert()`/`pop()`/`del` renumber those offsets in place - so mutating a
  copy silently corrupted the original's results names, and `get_name()` on the
  original could return `None`. PR submitted by Andrew Chen et AI.

- Fixed bugs in `ParseResults.__add__()` and `ParseResults.__radd__()`, where
  erroneous `AttributeError` or `RecursionError` could be raised when adding
  `ParseResults` objects to non-`ParseResults` objects, instead of expected
  `TypeError`. PR submitted by Vincent Gao et AI.

- Fixed `ParseResults.__iadd__` (``+=``) leaking an `AttributeError` about a
  private attribute when the right-hand operand is not a `ParseResults` (e.g.
  `results += [1]`). It now returns `NotImplemented` so Python raises a
  `TypeError`, matching the `__add__` operator. PR submitted by Andrew Chen et AI.

- Fixed `pyparsing_common.as_datetime` parse action incorrectly scaling fractional
  seconds, writing milliseconds into the `datetime` microsecond field (for example
  "1997-07-16T19:20:30.45" produced microsecond 449 instead of 450000). Fractional
  seconds are now scaled to microseconds, matching `convert_to_datetime` and the
  standard library. PR submitted by Vincent Gao.

- Fixed matching bug in `match_previous_expr()`, when expression is modified with
  `leave_whitespace(recursive=True)`. Issue 633, reported by Ahmed Mohamed Abdelaal,
  PR submitted by fcardosojr18 et AI.

- Fixed `match_previous_expr()` failing to match nested or repeated expressions, so that
  it can now be used for matching nested open/close tags. A new guard parse action was
  added on every match of the repeated expression and never removed, so all of them ran
  on each attempt to match and only one could succeed; a second pair anywhere in the
  input would fail, and after a failed parse the expression would keep rejecting valid
  input. The pending matches are now kept on a stack, so an inner match pairs with the
  nearest enclosing one. Issue 560, PR submitted by Rajesh Kanade et AI.

- Fixed `Located` reporting a `locn_start` that included leading whitespace when the
  wrapped expression delegates whitespace skipping to sub-expressions (such as
  `MatchFirst` or `And`). The leading whitespace is now skipped before the start
  location is recorded, while `leave_whitespace()` expressions keep their whitespace.
  Issue 621, reported by MeanSquaredError.

- Fixed `ParseResults.deepcopy()` not deep-copying results names that referenced
  nested `ParseResults`. Only the token list was copied, so a named token still
  pointed at the original; changing the original (or the copy) was visible through
  the other when the token was reached by name, and the same token could differ
  when reached by index versus by name. Results names now reference the
  deep-copied tokens. PR submitted by Sarath Francis.

- Update type checking to use `mypy 1.20.0`.

- Up to 30% performance boost in `ParseResults.__setitem__`, which benefits all pyparsing
  parsers. Inspired by work proposed in PR 650, submitted by Justin Zhang.

- Significant performance boost in `ParseResults.__delitem__`.

- 5-8% performance boost optimizing `ParseResults.copy()`. Inspired by similar changes
  made by Evan Hubinger in https://github.com/evhub/cpyparsing.

- Minor performance improvement in builtin quoted string expressions, using `Regex` instead
  of `And`.

- Added `docs/pyparsing_class.md`, a more comprehensive class diagram capturing the major
  classes and modules in the pyparsing package.

- Updated `examples/http_server_log_parser.py` to use more modern Python and pyparsing
  features, including PEP8 naming, datetime and timezone parsing and conversion, and
  associated railroad diagram.

- Fixed `RecursionError` when constructing a bounded repetition with a large upper
  bound, such as ``expr[..., 1000]`` or ``expr * (0, 1000)``. The optional tail was
  built as a deeply nested chain of ``Optional`` expressions, which recursed the upper
  bound number of levels deep during both construction and parsing. It is now built as
  a flat, bounded ``ZeroOrMore`` loop, so construction and parsing no longer scale with
  the upper bound -- and the loop still exits early (stopping at the first non-match),
  preserving the original early-exit behavior. Reported in issue 332.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.3.2
   ```
   -----------------------------
- Defined pyparsing-specific warning classes so that they can be selectively enabled
  or disabled without affecting warnings raised by other libraries in the same Python
  app:
  - `PyparsingWarning` - base warning for all pyparsing-specific warnings (inherits
    from `UserWarning`)
  - `PyparsingDeprecationWarning` - warning for using deprecated features (inherits
    from `PyparsingWarning` and `DeprecationWarning`)
  - `PyparsingDiagnosticWarning` - warning raised when pyparsing diagnostics are
    enabled and a diagnostic feature is used (inherits from `PyparsingWarning`)

- Added `as_datetime` parse action to `pyparsing.common` - a more g

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The standalone model-refresh regression waits 5.1 real seconds on every run solely to cross the former foreground deadline.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The test retains real plugin discovery and removes the deliberate five-second wait.

## Why This Change Was Made

Advance only the parent timeout clock while the discovery worker stays on its native clock. Keep discovery held until the test has proved that the command neither returns early nor prints incomplete rows, then release it and verify the discovered model. Always restore the parent clock during cleanup.

## Evidence

- All 29 tests across the refresh-completion, prepared-catalog, and configured-static catalog files passed.
- Restoring the original early-return defect makes the updated test fail at the early-completion assertion. Production source was restored byte-for-byte afterward.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/commands/models/list.refresh-completion.test.ts` passed, including types, lint, formatting, boundaries, and dead-code checks. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- `pnpm test src/commands/models/list.refresh-completion.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: baseline command wall 318.86s / case 26.34s; candidate command wall 103.19s / case 14.90s. Worker compilation and cache warmth differ, so only the removed 5.1s sleep is attributable to this patch. The final sibling run completed in 194.98s, with this case taking 2.965s.
- One regression case retained; test code changes by +4 lines, with no production or support-code changes. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35552136010/job/106188829903) passed the retained regression in 2.505s; its selected-file test command took 29.20s including startup.

author: hereliesaz
body:
Clean replacement for #351 after unrelated concurrent commits landed on that branch.

- installs every Azphalt model asset kind: `onnx`, `tflite`, `litert`, `task`, `sherpa-bundle`, `vosk-bundle`, and generic `model`
- materializes bundled and remote multi-file assets into app-private Android storage
- SHA-verifies remote members with resumable downloads
- validates and routes model formats before registration
- persists artifact paths, backend, Azphalt IO/requirements/license metadata, package/version, and digest in the durable inference registry
- supports install/update/remove and direct `.azp` model imports
- makes updates rollback-safe
- surfaces signer trust, publisher change, and model-license metadata before install
- includes model installs in update checks and installed counts
- adds manifest and durable-registry tests

Workflow/role installation remains isolated from the model lifecycle.

## Summary by Sourcery

Enable secure, durable installation and lifecycle management for every Azphalt model package on Android.

New Features:
- Add Android installation support for all Azphalt model asset formats, including bundled and remote multi-file packages.
- Support verified direct .azp model imports, updates, removals, and durable inference-registry registration.

Bug Fixes:
- Make model updates rollback-safe and preserve resumable partial downloads across interrupted transfers.

Enhancements:
- Validate model formats and route them to compatible inference backends while retaining artifact paths, metadata, digests, and package identity.
- Surface model signer trust, publisher changes, and license information during installation review.
- Include installed models in store counts, update checks, revocation handling, and UI lifecycle management while keeping workflow and role installation separate.

Documentation:
- Document the dedicated Android model installation lifecycle, supported formats, verification, persistence, rollback, uninstall, and import behavior.

Tests:
- Add manifest parsing coverage for all model asset kinds and model metadata.
- Extend downloader and durable inference-registry tests for resumable transfers and model removal.

author: daniel-ospina
body:
## Summary

Adds `tools/branch_reaper.py` — the general local-branch reap path this repo was
missing. Creation was well-tooled; nothing classified local branches from GitHub
PR state, and squash merges make `git branch --merged origin/main` undercount by
~500.

- Dry-run by default; `--apply` arms.
- Classifies from GitHub PR state (REST, completeness-checked), not ancestry.
- Deletes only branches whose tip provably survives (ancestor of `origin/main`,
  or tip == a **merged** PR's head SHA).
- **Preserves** closed-unmerged branches by default (opt-in `--include-closed-unmerged`)
  — the branch may be the last non-revocable holder of commits that never landed.
- **Preserves** branches that advanced beyond their PR head (the issue's
  name-only rule would have destroyed 63 of them).
- Never deletes a branch held by a worktree; **worktree teardown is delegated**
  to the reviewed `scripts/pi-reap-worktrees.sh` rather than adding a second
  engine.
- Truncated/unqueryable PR list ⇒ INCOMPLETE, nothing deleted; the ref OID is
  re-verified immediately before each delete (TOCTOU); `--apply` refuses the main
  checkout; never `--force`; remote branches untouched.

Closes #4408.

## Scope note — the issue's premise was half-false

The issue says "no reap path exists for worktrees and branches". Verification
found `scripts/pi-reap-worktrees.sh` (agent-infra #1095, ~1,413 lines + tests):
a mature worktree reaper that is dry-run by default and **never deletes
branches**. So the genuinely uncovered surface is **local branches**, which this
PR adds. The worktree half is delegated, not duplicated. Full double-diamond
derivation (framings, A/B/C/D approaches, rejected alternatives, adversarial
pre-mortem): `docs/scoping/2026-09-20-4408-branch-reaper.md`.

## Measured results

Dry-run: 1,475 local branches · SAFE_BY_HISTORY 1,160 · checked out in a worktree
237 · **SAFE_DELETABLE_now 923** · preserved 208 · judgement 107.

Actual pass: **923 branches deleted, 0 refused, 237 skipped (worktree-held)**.
The delegated worktree engine removed 0 checkouts — it *deferred 317 of 412* under
this box's I/O load (its 300 s budget is a deliberate runaway guard), so the
worktree half reclaimed nothing this pass. Branch refs reclaim negligible bytes;
the 209 GB lives in worktrees and needs the engine scheduled when the box is
quiet (follow-up). Committed evidence: `docs/runbook/4408-branch-reaper.md`.

## Tests

`tests/test_branch_reaper.py` — 56 hermetic mutation tests (stub `gh` fixtures +
real temp git repo with real `git worktree add`; `tests/test_ci_selection.py` adds
its own, 184 across both files): merged-tip safe; advanced-tip
preserved; closed-unmerged preserved then safe with the flag; dirty worktree
branch kept; ancestry safe; open-PR over an ancestor preserved; truncated list ⇒
INCOMPLETE (nothing deleted); unqueryable gh ⇒ INCOMPLETE; engine fail-closed
keeps everything; engine that removes nothing keeps the held branch; `--apply`
from the main checkout refused; ref moved between classify and delete skipped;
recovery record written before deletion. All pass.

## Verification

- `[VGATE]` verification dispatch: **PASS** (all pushed-range files hashed).
- Code review: 7 cycles against fresh-context reviewers. 31 findings, all fixed,
  with the final cycle returning **`NO ISSUES FOUND`**. The branch was then
  rebased onto a newer `main` twice (each time the head moved), and each delta was
  reviewed again in fresh context and returned **`NO ISSUES FOUND`**, as did a
  third review of the `main`→branch merge that produced the current head
  `92950d6d5`. On every rebase and through the merge the reaper's two code
  files came through byte-identical (`tools/branch_reaper.py` still
  `8c97f36a…`, `tests/test_branch_reaper.py` still `db27b01e…`), so no rebase
  altered code. The second rebase existed to pick up `main`'s fix for
  `tests/test_sdk_rename_table.py`, which this branch had been red on purely
  because its base predated it: that file is now `49 passed` here. Findings
  concentrated on the delete/classification boundary: a false recovery-window
  claim, a recovery record that could omit a tip the run then deleted, two
  refname-ambiguity sites (`%(refname:short)` and `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`,
  each defeated by a tag colliding with a branch), a `..` write-path escape, and
  three fail-open gaps in the `gh` completeness contract — a malformed PR
  record, an exit-0 empty body, and a bare `[]` page list — each of which let an
  ancestry rule delete an open-PR branch at exit 0. Every one is pinned by a
  regression test, most verified non-vacuous by mutation.
- One residual is FILED, not fixed, as #4613: the write guard's symlink check is
  a path-prefix match, so it fails open when the report path and `repo_root` are
  spelled through different aliases of the same directory (e.g. `/var/...` vs
  `/private/var/...`). It is documented in the guard's own docstring as a
  `KNOWN RESIDUAL`; closing it needs an openat/O_NOFOLLOW component walk rather
  than a string prefix. This is the only known open issue in the change.
- Scoping: `issue-scoping` comment on #4408 — problem-verify 2 cycles → clean;
  solution-verify 2 cycles → clean; duplication/architecture review incorporated
  (it caught the closed-unmerged survival risk + the `refs/reaped/*` collision);
  adversarial pre-mortem incorporated (TOCTOU re-verify, completeness gating).
- `python3 tools/ci_selection.py --integrity`: **PASS**.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

1. Schedule the reap path (launchd/cron) — the mechanism exists but never runs.
2. Shared branch-deletability declaration across the four writers + parity test.
3. Extract the shared PR-enumeration/completeness contract with
   `tools/collision_preflight.py`.

author: odvcencio
body:
## Summary

Two related GLR recovery parity defects (tasks #77 and #80) made the Go port's error recovery disagree with the C oracle. The port kept each do_all_potential_reductions interpretation as its own independent stack, so several siblings could reach recover_eof accept at once. Those extra accepted stacks then crowded out the not-yet-accepted resync fork in the per-iteration stack cap, and skewed the final result-selection fold through a spurious index tie-break. This branch collapses each absorbing group's recover_eof siblings to one representative, and ranks already-accepted stacks last in the per-iteration cull so a stack that still needs to advance survives ahead of one that is done.

## Changes

- Collapse duplicate EOF-accepted recovery siblings in cHandleError (parser_recover_c.go). Pick the survivor with stackCompareForResultSelection, mirroring ts_parser__accept's own select_tree collapse, so only one representative reaches both the per-iteration cap and the final fold.
- Reuse a scratch buffer (gssScratch.groupEOFAcceptedScratch) for the absorbing-group collapse instead of allocating a fresh slice on every cHandleError call.
- Invert the accepted-stack priority in compareStackCullKeys (parser.go): rank accepted stacks last, not first. Accepted stacks keep their natural slot because task #77 made that position load-bearing for the final fold's 'prefer the later candidate' tie-break; only cull priority changes.
- Add TestParityCullAcceptedRankLastRust: pins the fixed rust shape for "a->b" and "a=>b" against the C oracle. A 182-grammar sweep over a 288-case malformed corpus found these two pairs as the only moved results.
- Widen TestParityCSharpRecoverEOFWrappedRootMatchesC from two inputs to the full c_sharp census, and add five discriminating inputs ("ab", "AB", "a1", "u8", "é") that fail on the pre-#77 engine.
- Add TestParityRecoverGroupCollapseCrossGrammar: one C-verified discriminating input each for c, css, elm, and d, so the shared collapse mechanism has regression coverage outside c_sharp.
- Update the CRecoverEOFBareRootReceipted exclusion comments: c_sharp stays excluded because C's root is always compilation_unit wrapping the ERROR, never a bare ERROR, regardless of which route the port selects.

## Testing

- bash cgo_harness/docker/run_single_grammar_parity.sh c_sharp
- bash cgo_harness/docker/run_single_grammar_parity.sh rust
- go test ./cgo_harness -tags 'cgo treesitter_c_parity' -run 'TestParityCullAcceptedRankLastRust|TestParityCSharpRecoverEOFWrappedRootMatchesC|TestParityRecoverGroupCollapseCrossGrammar|TestParityRecoverEOFRouteDivergences' -count=1
- Confirm the route change with SetGLRTrace(true): the selected stack's error cost drops from 501-506 (recover_eof) to 0 (resync) on every c_sharp census input.

## Related Issues

- Refs #77
- Refs #80

## Review Focus

Focus on two points: (1) whether ranking accepted stacks last in compareStackCullKeys can starve an accepted stack that buildResultFromGLR still needs for the final fold when the cap is tight, and (2) the documented caveat that the collapse survivor's post-condense index feeds the final fold's tie-break and no test pins that index directly.

author: moonlightbbq
body:
Every published post carried a professional-review claim it could not support.

`generate-blog.js` printed `Reviewed by ${author}` unconditionally — the **author** field, labelled as a review. Across 73 published posts:

| What the page claimed | Posts |
|---|---|
| "Reviewed by The Way Agency" (the agency attesting to its own review) | 41 |
| "Reviewed by" a named licensed agent | 28 |
| Posts carrying any `reviewed_date` | 4 |
| Posts with a recorded reviewer **approval**, ever | 0 |

On an insurance site that is a fabricated trust signal, so the byline is now held to evidence:

- **"Written by X"** always — authorship is a fact we know.
- **"Reviewed by X on <date>"** only when a named reviewer *and* their sign-off date are both on the post. No record, no claim.

Also fixes the Article structured data, which typed `"The Way Agency"` as a schema.org `Person` on 41 posts, and emits `reviewedBy` on the same evidence as the visible line.

The 12 hand-maintained pages under `src/pages/blog/` bypass the generator and are changed the same way — the people named there wrote those posts, so they keep the credit without the review claim.

### Testing
`tests/blog-byline-honesty.test.js` holds the invariant in both directions: no claim without evidence, and a genuine review still renders. 124 tests pass, build clean.

### Not in this PR
Reviewer assignments **are** being made, then erased a few hours later by a content-queue job that writes `content-calendar.json` from a stale read. On 2026-09-05 the weekly run assigned Audrey Lillpop at 13:11; the queue job removed her at 16:30. That is why no reviewer survives to publish — and why the rotation has been stuck on one person for months, since the assignment counter it picks the minimum from can never increment. Kelly and Sheilia were never excluded; they were starved. Fix follows separately.

Two calendar entries also credit reviewers who were never employees ("Kelly Bartley", "Audrey Phelps"). Confined to `data/content-calendar.json`, never published. Cleaned up separately.

body:
## Summary

Track A, Task 3 of CRM i18n stage 4: migrates error codes for the `documents` / `contracts` / `teams` / `legends` / `approvals` / `interviews` / `notifications` API modules from literal Russian/English exception messages to the code-based i18n envelope (`apiError(code, status, params?)`), per `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-20-crm-i18n-stage4-api-shared.md` and spec §4.3. Builds on Task 1 (#701, merged at `a391ae76`) which added the barrel + `base.ts` + `auth-users-projects.ts` + the empty stub for `documents-contracts-notifications.ts`.

- New file `packages/shared/src/schemas/api-errors/documents-contracts-notifications.ts` — 64 error codes with `DOCUMENTS_CONTRACTS_NOTIFICATIONS_ERROR_CODES` / `..._ERROR_PARAMS` / `..._ERROR_MESSAGES` (uk source) / `..._ERROR_FALLBACK_EN`, following the `ParamsFor<C>` pin pattern from Task 1. ICU `select` used for `category`/`status`/`expectedRole`/`actualRole` interpolation so raw enum values never leak into user-facing text.
- All throw-sites in `documents`, `contracts`, `teams`, `legends`, `approvals`, `interviews`, `notifications` controllers/services migrated to `apiError()`.
- `packages/shared/src/i18n/locales/en/messages.po` — 64 `msgstr` entries filled to match the fallback-en text exactly.
- `packages/shared/src/schemas/api-errors.spec.ts` — `tokenSet()` rewritten as a brace-depth-aware parser so it correctly reads ICU `{name, select, ...}` declarations instead of matching raw option labels like `{HR}`.
- `apps/web/app/components/onboarding/SignContractStep.tsx` — both `LEGAL_NAME_REQUIRED` and `ADMIN_DOES_NOT_SIGN_CONTRACTS` branches now route through `getApiErrorMessage(err)` (fix-round 1, COPY-H-1) — no Russian literal, no substring match.
- `apps/api/src/common/api-error.ts::interpolate` — rewritten (fix-round 1, SR-M-1) to render through `@lingui/core`'s `i18n._` instead of a dead `{token}` regex, so ICU `select` params render correctly in the HTTP fallback `message` and in logs.
- ~20 spec files converted from `.rejects.toThrow(ExceptionClass)` / `.rejects.toBeInstanceOf(ExceptionClass)` to `.rejects.toMatchObject({ response: { code, statusCode[, params] } })`, since `apiError()` always returns the base `HttpException`, never a subclass.

author: nanz876
body:
One post per Batch 5 tool, targeting the biggest search terms the site has gone after so far.

| Post | Target |
|---|---|
| `word-to-pdf-free` | word to pdf free |
| `excel-to-pdf-free` | excel to pdf free |
| `powerpoint-to-pdf-free` | powerpoint to pdf free |

Each one leads with the reader's actual problem rather than the tool:

- **Word** — the post says outright that Word's own Save As PDF is the best option if you have Word, then addresses the people who don't. Claiming otherwise would be obvious nonsense to anyone who has Office, and admitting it buys credibility for the rest.
- **Excel** — framed as "without cutting off columns", because that is the failure everyone has actually experienced when printing a spreadsheet. The repeated first column and repeating headers are the selling point.
- **PowerPoint** — leads with decks breaking on someone else's computer because their fonts are missing, and notes that a .pptx carries speaker notes and off-canvas slides that a PDF does not.

All three state the limits plainly: no charts, SmartArt or animations; Latin alphabets only, refused with a clear message rather than mangled; `.doc` and `.ppt` not supported.

Registered in the blog index and sitemap. 193 tests pass, `tsc` clean, `next build` prerenders all three routes.

body:
## Change

- Add a Workspace migration that records completion and expiry timestamps for create retry records.
- Add typed SQL that deletes expired records so a locked transaction can reuse the subject and key.
- Add PostgreSQL tests for constraints, migration upgrades, expiry replacement, and rollback scope.

## Reason

Workspace create retries need a stored 24-hour expiry. The existing schema kept every retry record without an expiry, so the same subject and key could never identify a new operation.

Closes #47

| Workspace tests | `go test ./services/workspace/...` | Passed. |

author: wrg-11
body:
## What

Two hardening changes, both scoped to the "fixed" (patched) scenarios and both
covered by regression tests:

1. Note reads and updates in fixed mode return a single uniform "unavailable"
   response for a missing id and for a cross-tenant id alike, so the error no
   longer distinguishes "does not exist" from "exists but belongs to another
   tenant."
2. The HTTP lab transport binds to `127.0.0.1` by default. Set `HOST` explicitly
   when a non-loopback listener is intentional.

The deliberately vulnerable lessons (S1..S9) are unchanged; only the fixed-mode
paths and the default bind move.

## Why

A fixed-mode handler that answers differently for a missing id versus a foreign
id still leaks cross-tenant existence, and a lab server that listens on every
interface by default is reachable beyond the host running it. Neither belongs in
the patched scenarios the lab holds up as correct behavior.

## Test

    npm install
    node --test test/security-hardening.test.js
    # tests 2, pass 2, fail 0
    node --test
    # tests 54, pass 54, fail 0

## Release

This PR bumps the version to 3.12.2 and records its CHANGELOG entry. The tag
`v3.12.2` is created after merge.

author: danielscholl
body:
## What

Adds the bundled `design-converge` workflow: deterministic intake, three
isolated proposals, blind cross-critique, one filesystem-enabled fact-check,
evidence-weighted synthesis with dissent, durable artifact persistence, and a
human approval gate.

The deterministic subprocess channel now carries the current run id, node
state, and effective provider/model provenance. This lets the workflow persist
complete spill files from successful or failed nodes and report vendor collapse
from the routes that actually ran.

The current branch contains ten bundled workflow assets, so the index remains
at ten. When #890 lands for #872, conflict resolution must retain both workflow
cards and update the combined count to eleven.

## Why now

A design decision should not depend on one model proposing and judging its own
answer. This workflow makes independent alternatives, source verification,
unresolved dissent, and human acceptance explicit while keeping filesystem
access limited to the fact-checking seat.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run check`
- [x] `bun --filter '*' typecheck`
- [x] `bun --filter '*' test` (4,473 passed)
- [x] `bun --filter '*' build`

- [x] `bun apps/cli/bin/keelson.ts workflow validate smoke-test`
- [x] `bun apps/cli/bin/keelson.ts workflow run smoke-test --provider stub`
- [x] `cd docs && bun run build` (53 pages)
- [x] [Live non-OSDU pilot evidence](https://github.com/danielscholl/keelson/pull/898#issuecomment-5754371507):
  run `ea1ef337-485a-44ec-8200-d2058aa047c4` paused at `decide` with all
  eight artifacts and eight effective routes. Approval remains unanswered.
- [x] [Current-source live pilot evidence](https://github.com/danielscholl/keelson/pull/898#issuecomment-5755082387):
  run `4ed9d41a-1117-4d9a-b81f-2f54bf6c7630` from `15ffea14` paused at
  `decide` with all eight artifact hashes and effective routes verified against
  runtime records, blind prompt boundaries confirmed, and real Markdown
  synthesis. Approval remains unanswered.

## Risk & rollback

- Blast radius: workflow subprocess metadata and the new bundled workflow.
- Compatibility: subprocess environment fields are additive; no database
  migration or existing workflow behavior changes.
- Rollback: revert this PR.

Closes #873

author: makewhatis
body:
## Summary

A 987M-token day was discovered by eye five days into a weekly quota, and the
figure an operator could act on — 361M of Claude, the only slice on the
constrained account — had to be reconstructed with a hand-written SQL join.
This adds the meter and the stop: tokens per provider per day over the API, and a
per-provider daily token budget that refuses NEW dispatch when spent.

Rhapsody-only. The frozen Go reference can record nothing about what a run billed
and has no budget concept, so both surfaces are additive and both leave the
Go-pinned `/api/v1/metrics` and `/api/v1/state` payloads byte-identical when
unconfigured.

## Changes

**Meter — `GET /api/v1/metrics/providers`.** The same daily rollup as
`/api/v1/metrics`, decomposed by the `provider` recorded in
`rhapsody_run_provenance`. A route of its own rather than a field on `/metrics`:
that body is byte-pinned to the Go-captured golden `harness/fixtures/api/metrics.json`,
which has no `provider` and can never be regenerated with one. A LEFT JOIN puts a
run with no provenance row in the empty-provider bucket, so the series still sums
to the plain daily total.

- `crates/store`: `Store::metrics_by_provider` (+ `DayProviderRollup`), Sqlite + Noop.
- `crates/httpapi`: `handle_metrics_by_provider` + `metrics_by_provider_response` + route.

**Telemetry attribute contract.** Added `ATTR_HARNESS`/`ATTR_PROVIDER` and the
provider+harness dimensions on the token builders; fixed `ATTR_MODEL`'s doc,
which still claimed "the claude model". The token counters still have no live
recording site — they are exported only when `otel.enabled`, which ships `false`
— so this is the CONTRACT only; wiring the site is deliberately scoped out
(constraint 2) and stated here.

**Stop — `budgets:`.** A top-level `provider -> daily_tokens` block (`0 = unlimited`,
the `max_concurrent` idiom). When spend since the host's local midnight is `>=`
the limit, fresh dispatch on that provider is refused; other providers continue.
Unset ⇒ unlimited ⇒ byte-identical to today. An in-flight run is never
terminated: the gate binds fresh dispatch only, so retries/continuations pass.
Refusals are recorded in a ledger surfaced on `/api/v1/state` as `budget_held`
(emitted only when non-empty) and named by the reconciliation sweep instead of the
false "nothing has reported it blocked". Review dispatch is gated at its own door
before the watch-set writes, because the incident's whole Claude bill was reviews.

- `crates/config`: `ProviderBudget` + `budgets:` decode/round-trip; kept out of the
  Go-pinned `effective_json` view (the `promote_from_states`/`allow_handoff` pattern).
- `crates/orchestrator`: new `budget` module; gate in `dispatch_issue` (fresh only)
  and `dispatch_review`; `budget_held` on the snapshot; the sweep arm.

## Verification

```
$ make lint
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 5.63s
```

```
$ cargo test --workspace
test result: ok. 1675 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out   # rhapsody-orchestrator
test result: ok. 342 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out    # rhapsody-config
test result: ok. 231 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out    # rhapsody-httpapi
... every workspace crate green
```

Key new tests (each named for the mutation it catches):

- `rhapsody-store::metrics_by_provider_splits_the_rollup_by_provider` — reconstructs the
  incident's day: 524,883,057 fireworks-ai / 360,636,166 anthropic / 101,642,859 openai,
  plus the empty-provider bucket, and asserts the split sums to the plain daily total.
- `rhapsody-httpapi::metrics_by_provider_round_trip` — the same three distinct buckets over
  HTTP; the default `/api/v1/metrics` golden still passes
  (`goldens::metrics_matches_golden`).
- `rhapsody-orchestrator::budget::a_spent_budget_refuses_new_dispatch`,
  `a_budget_spent_on_another_provider_does_not_refuse`,
  `an_unset_budget_refuses_nothing` (behaviour preservation),
  `a_spent_budget_never_blocks_a_continuation` (an in-flight run is never killed).
- `review::a_review_is_refused_when_the_reviewers_provider_is_out_of_budget` — refuses
  before any watch-set write, so the watcher re-offers the head.
- `reviewreconcile::a_budget_held_round_is_reported_as_held_for_budget` — the sweep
  names the budget instead of the false fallback wording.
- `snapshot_json::a_daemon_with_no_budget_hold_emits_no_budget_held_key` — the Go-pinned
  `/api/v1/state` payload is unchanged on a daemon with no budget.
- `telemetry::metrics::token_counters_carry_provider_and_harness`.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Constraint 1 (the `/api/v1/metrics` golden) resolved as an additive endpoint.**
  `harness/fixtures/api/metrics.json` is unmodified. No normalization rule was added.
- **Constraint 2 (the dark counters) resolved as "scope out the recording site".** The
  attribute contract is fixed; no production call site feeds `symphony.tokens.*` yet. Stated
  in the `tokens()` doc so the next person does not assume the metrics carry data.
- **Provider resolution is shared, not duplicated.** `resolved_harness_model` is the single
  resolver used by both `run_provenance_for` (what gets persisted) and the budget gate (what
  gets checked), so the provider the budget reads cannot disagree with the one the run records.
- **Retries are deliberately not bounded.** A retry/continuation is the same ticket's
  already-started work; refusing it would waste what it has spent, strictly worse than
  letting it finish. `dispatch_issue`'s gate is guarded by `attempt.is_none()`.
- **A budget refusal can lose a graphite stacking hint** (`pending_stack` is consumed before
  the gate, which sits after the run's harness/model are resolved). Only in the refusal case,
  and the ticket re-dispatches next tick; noted rather than fixed to keep the gate's provider
  exact.
- **Store errors fail OPEN** (a warning, no refusal): a budget is a guardrail, not a hard
  security control.
- **Pre-existing test failure under this run's environment:** `rhapsody-agent`'s
  `set_run_id_zero_emits_no_run_id_env` and `run_turn_without_set_run_id_emits_no_run_id_env`
  fail when the ambient `SYMPHONY_RUN_ID`/`SYMPHONY_ISSUE` env vars are present (they are set
  in a headless Rhapsody run). They pass with those vars unset and are unrelated to this diff;
  CI does not set them.
- `make fixtures` was **not** run; no golden was recaptured or edited.

Fixes STUDIO-957

https://linear.app/studio49/issue/STUDIO-957/nothing-meters-spend-per-provider-and-nothing-stops-a-987m-token-day


## Round-2 review fixes (head 8999b6c)

Three blocking findings from the round-2 review, plus alice's round-1 non-blocking notes.

**1. Review holds are now keyed per `(PR, reviewer)`.** They were keyed by the pull request
coordinate, so in a mixed roster one reviewer's successful dispatch released a sibling
reviewer's still-active hold, and two held reviewers overwrote each other's provider/figures.
A review refusal is now keyed by the review identity (`pr:owner/repo#n@reviewer`) and carries
the coordinate in a new `BudgetHeld.pr` field, which the reconciliation sweep looks up. New
regression: `review::a_held_reviewers_budget_hold_survives_a_sibling_reviewers_dispatch`
(Alice/Claude/Anthropic held, Jerry/opencode/Fireworks dispatched, Alice's hold survives).

**2. The hold TTL is now `max(300s, 2 × polling.interval_ms)`.** A fixed 300s dropped a
genuinely-held subject mid-cycle on a poll interval longer than five minutes, so
`budget_hold_for` fell back to an unexplained divergence. New coverage:
`budget::a_hold_outlives_a_poll_interval_longer_than_the_floor` (10-minute poll, a 5-minute-old
hold stays).

**3. `local_day_start` resolves midnight through the zone's transition rules.** It applied
`now`'s offset to midnight, so on a DST transition day it folded an extra hour of yesterday's
spend into today. `Single`/earlier-`Ambiguous` are the boundary; a `None` (a z

author: yw0nam
body:
## Summary
The message window read `chat_api` to decide whether its delegation chip may draw: the pet window publishes its push socket state in every mode, the chip read every non-ready state as a lost connection, so outside push mode it would have drawn a permanent loss. To avoid that the window loaded the bundled config and the endpoint settings only to compute a mode string.

A surface draws what arrives and stays hidden when nothing does; it does not read the transport's name.

- `src/ui/chips/delegation-chip.ts` — `disconnected` means no transport is in use and draws nothing: hidden, list closed, no `is-lost`. The branch runs before the ready rendering, so running items left in the store draw no count. `connecting`, `reconnecting` and `failed` stay the lost state. In `src/io/chat/push-socket.ts` `disconnected` is set only where no connection attempt is under way (initial state, `connect()` refused for an empty `chat_base_url`, `disconnect()`, `dispose()`, a close while inactive); every loss while the socket is meant to be up is one of the other three.
- `src/message-main.ts` — `applyChipMode`, `sawPushState`, `bundledEndpoints`, `effectiveChatApi`, the endpoint settings store and the `loadConfig()` call are gone (52 lines). The chip starts unsuppressed: the mirror's initial state is `disconnected`.
- Switching the mode at runtime needs no code in the message window: leaving push makes `wirePushMode` disconnect the socket, the state is published, the chip hides; entering push publishes `connecting`.
- The pet window (`wirePushMode`) and the settings window keep their mode reads: one owns the socket, the other configures the transport. The settings window still reads `disconnected` as offline.

**Behaviour change:** in push mode with an empty `chat_base_url` the socket never attempts a connection, so the chip is hidden where it used to draw the lost pill, in both windows. The settings panel's chat status line still names the missing endpoint, and a sent message still ends `not_configured`.

## Related issues
Closes #1052.

## Related decisions / docs
No doc change: no file under `docs/` describes the chip's loss display.

## Runtime evidence (required for UI / DOM / runtime behavior)
Browser mode, Playwright MCP, certified at `87e6bf4e`. The commit on top, `693114e8`, rewrites one comment and removes one test, so it does not affect the runs below. Pet window (`index.html`, owns the socket) and message window (`message.html`, mirrors it) in one browser context, so the bridge is the real `BroadcastChannel` path; the mode was changed only through the settings UI (`select#yui-svc-chat-type`, `input#yui-ep-chat_base_url`). Evidence in `logs/1052-evidence/` — screenshots, `run-notes.txt`, the bridge frame transcript, the message window console.

| claim | result | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `chat_completions` (bundled default): chip hidden, lost pill never appears — 20+ samples over 7.6–11.5 s, one state throughout: `hidden=true`, class `yui-deleg` | pass | `c1-raw-message-chat_completions.png` |
| `responses`, set through the settings dropdown: same | pass | `c1-message-responses.png` |
| `push` with a `chat_base_url` nothing listens on: `yui-deleg is-lost is-visible`, label "연결 끊김", 30/30 samples, while the pet window publishes `connecting` → `reconnecting` with a growing delay | pass | `c2-message-push-dead-port-lost.png` |
| `push` → `responses` at runtime, no reload: the pill goes away (MutationObserver: class drops to `yui-deleg`, then `hidden=true` after the fade) | pass | `c3a-message-live-switch-push-to-responses.png` |
| `responses` → `push` again: the pill returns | pass | `c3b-message-live-switch-back-to-push.png` |
| `push` with an empty `chat_base_url`: chip hidden | pass | `c4-message-push-empty-baseurl.png` |
| message window console | 0 errors, 0 warnings | `message-window-console.log` |

The bridge was live during the hidden states: the pet window answered every `push-state-ask`, and `settings-changed` crossed windows on each mode flip, so "hidden" reports `disconnected` and not a silent channel.

**Not covered:** the Tauri runtime (the bridge there is Tauri events, not `BroadcastChannel`); the `ready` branch with running delegations, since no push backend was connected — it is unchanged by this PR and covered by the chip's unit tests. The pet window console shows `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` against the dead port the test pointed it at, which is the test setup.

## Verification
- [x] `pnpm build` passes (includes tsc typecheck)
- [x] `pnpm test` passes — 293 files, 5967 tests
- [x] `pnpm lint` passes (biome format + lint)
- [ ] `cargo test` / `cargo clippy` pass (Rust changes) — N/A, no Rust change

`pnpm typecheck:test` clean. RED at the `test:` commit `42ddae4f`, reproduced on a detached checkout: 5 failed (`delegation-chip.test.ts` ×2, `message-main.test.ts` ×3); green at the `feat:` commit.

`git grep -n 'chat_api\|effectiveChatApi\|loadConfig' -- src/message-main.ts` returns nothing. The issue's criterion `git grep -n '"push"'` still lists one line, `case "push":` — the message surface's speech-delta op, which is not the chat mode.

author: cat12079801
body:
Fixes **A-5** from the operator-side issue log (`MCP_ISSUES.md`).

## Problem

During a run there is no API way to open the pause menu (the top-bar gear / Esc), and the mod never looks at
`NPauseMenu`. If the menu is open anyway, state describes the room underneath and every action is applied to a
screen the player cannot see. There is also no API exit from a run at all: `abandon_run` is a main-menu button
and `main_menu` only exists on the game-over screen, so an unattended agent that gets stuck has to be rescued
with a mouse. This is the last click-only dependency in the operator's workflow.

The pause menu is pushed on the run's submenu stack inside the capstone container, exactly like the settings
screen that #48 handled, so this follows the same shape and reuses its helpers.

## Change

**State** — `TryBuildPauseMenuState(Node?)` sits right after the settings check in `BuildGameState`'s run path
(settings keeps winning, because it can be pushed on top of the pause menu). It reports:

- `state_type: "menu"`, `menu_screen: "pause"`, `in_run: true`, a `message` naming the options and what
  `give_up` / `save_and_quit` actually do, and `options` as `{name, enabled}` per **visible** button:
  `resume`, `settings`, `compendium`, `give_up`, `disconnect`, `save_and_quit`.
  It falls through to the shared tail, so `run` and `player` are still in the payload.
- Anything else on that stack (the compendium the pause menu opens, and the screens below it) is reported
  generically: a derived `menu_screen` (`compendium`, `card_library`, …), `screen_class` naming the game's
  node type, and a single `back` option. This is option (a) from the brief — the generalization is one helper
  (`GetOpenRunSubmenu` + `ExecuteSubmenuBackOption`), and it means entering one of those screens can never
  become a fresh A-6.

Only a button's own `Visible` flag is read, not `IsVisibleInTree`: `NCapstoneSubmenuStack.ShowScreen` pushes
the screen before `NCapstoneContainer.Open` reparents it, so a tree test would report a pause menu with no
options at all on the frame it opens.

**Actions**

- New `open_pause_menu` (alias `pause`), routed in both `ExecuteAction` and `ExecuteMultiplayerAction`. It
  clicks the top bar's own `NTopBarPauseButton` — the same path a human takes — and falls back to
  `NRun.Instance.GlobalUi.SubmenuStack.ShowScreen(CapstoneSubmenuType.PauseMenu)` + `Initialize(runState)`
  (the button's own body) when the top bar is not available. It returns `status: ok` with
  `already_open: true` when the menu is already up; it errors when another screen is stacked over the pause
  menu (clicking the gear there would toggle the whole capstone shut and resume the run) and when a card is
  mid-play (`NPlayerHand.Instance.InCardPlay`).
- `menu_select` now drives the pause menu, after the settings branch and before the timeline branch:
  `resume` (aliases `back`, `close`, `continue`), `settings`, `compendium`, `give_up` (aliases `abandon`,
  `abandon_run`), `save_and_quit` (aliases `main_menu`, `quit`), `disconnect` — each clicked through the
  existing `ClickMenuButtonField`. An unknown option errors with the currently visible option names.
- `give_up` is **not** auto-confirmed. `NPauseMenu.OnGiveUpButtonPressed` puts an `NAbandonRunConfirmPopup`
  (which wraps an `NVerticalPopup`) in `NModalContainer`, and the existing popup builder already reports that
  as `menu_screen: "popup"` with normalized yes/no options — no new detection was needed.
- Gameplay actions are now refused with an explanatory error while any of these screens covers the run,
  instead of landing on a screen nobody can see. `open_pause_menu` itself is exempt.

`is_resolving` stays false on these screens: `menu` is already in `_playerInputStates`.

**Docs** — `docs/raw-simplified.md` (state table `menu` row, two notes, the `menu_select` row, and a new
`open_pause_menu` row with the destructive-action warning), `mcp/server.py` (new `open_pause_menu()` tool plus
the pause options in the `menu_select` docstring), `mcp/README.md` (table row).

## Decompiled facts this depends on

If a game update breaks this, re-check these against `sts2.dll`:

| Type | Members used |
|---|---|
| `NPauseMenu : NSubmenu` | fields `_resumeButton`, `_settingsButton`, `_compendiumButton`, `_giveUpButton`, `_disconnectButton`, `_saveAndQuitButton` (all `NPauseMenuButton : NButton : NClickableControl`); `Initialize(IRunState)`; `_Ready` / `Initialize` set the per-mode `Visible` flags; `OnGiveUpButtonPressed` → `NModalContainer.Instance.Add(NAbandonRunConfirmPopup.Create(null))` |
| `NSubmenu` | field `_backButton` (`NBackButton`), field `_stack` (`NSubmenuStack`, `Pop()`) |
| `NTopBarPauseButton` | `OnRelease()` = `ShowScreen(PauseMenu)` + `Initialize(_runState)`; reached via `NRun.Instance.GlobalUi.TopBar.Pause` |
| `NCapstoneContainer` | `Instance`, `CurrentCapstoneScreen` (the same property `NTopBarPauseButton.IsOpen()` reads); `Open` reparents the screen *after* the stack push |
| `NCapstoneSubmenuStack` | `Stack` (`NRunSubmenuStack`), `ShowScreen(CapstoneSubmenuType)`, `Peek()` |
| `NGlobalUi` / `NRun` | `NRun.Instance`, `GlobalUi`, `GlobalUi.SubmenuStack`, `GlobalUi.TopBar.Pause` |
| `NAbandonRunConfirmPopup` | field `_verticalPopup` (`NVerticalPopup`), placed in `NModalContainer.Instance.OpenModal` |

Every one of these is reached through `GetInstanceFieldValue` / null-guarded property reads inside
`try`/`catch`, so a renamed member degrades to "no pause state reported" rather than throwing.

## Verification

Built against game **v0.111.0** — 0 warnings, 0 errors. Not exercised in-game; the supervisor does the live
run, and `give_up` / `save_and_quit` are destructive, so they were deliberately not triggered here.

「画像で保存」がファイルダウンロード止まりで、**iPhoneだと写真アルバムに入らない**という指摘。iOSのSafari（Web）では、ページから直接アルバムへ書き込むことはできず、**共有シートの「画像を保存」**がアルバム保存の正規ルートです。

`navigator.share`（Web Share API）に画像ファイルを渡す方式に変更しました。
- 共有シートが画像ファイルに対応していれば **share を優先**（iOS：「画像を保存」→アルバム、LINE送信・AirDropもそのまま）

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

This morning the campus sat unseen by the cloud from 03:05 to the 07:13 hand restart while every recovery task reported success: the SYSTEM watchdog ran every 5 minutes with result 0, the 3 AM refresh finished 0, and the only test either makes is "does a python process matching `main.py` exist?". A process that is alive but has no usable cloud link passes that test, so nothing ever restarted it — parents' requests queued for four hours.

The agent's own escape hatch (`_restart_if_the_link_never_returns`) cannot cover this, because it runs on the same event loop that may be the thing that is stuck, and it refuses to act unless `_STARTED_BY_WRAPPER`.

So the liveness proof now leaves the process. `_note_ws_activity()` — called on every frame the link actually carries — stamps `.locks/cloud_link.alive` (at most every 30s), and `watchdog.bat` judges the agent by that stamp rather than by its existence:

```
seen = max(mtime(.locks/cloud_link.alive), newest main.py process start)
if a main.py process exists and seen < now - 12 min:
    kill the main.py processes; NEED_AGENT=1   # existing restart path runs
```

Taking the process start time into the maximum is what makes it safe: a freshly started agent gets a full 12 minutes to connect no matter how old the stamp on disk is, so a stamp left by an agent that died overnight cannot have the new one killed every five minutes. A stamp that cannot be written (full disk) goes stale and costs one unnecessary restart, which is the cheap direction of that trade.

The check sits outside the `AGENT_ONLY` guard, so the SYSTEM watchdog — the one running at 3 AM with nobody logged on, where this failure happened — makes it too.

Tests: 492 pass. New `tests/test_link_alive.py` plus watchdog script assertions covering the kill path, the fresh-agent grace, and that the check is not logon-bound.

author: nsolland
body:
This PR re-runs the HEIMEL migration repository-first and invariant-first. It is intentionally DRAFT and must not merge until the repository archaeology gate has no unresolved dispositions and all non-archaeology CI is green.

Root cause
The original HEIMEL bootstrap used the minimum consequence path as the practical migration scope. Later audits verified the target tree, but did not prove that the source universe itself was complete. Components or invariants absent from the target list could therefore disappear silently.

Canonical audit sources
- nsolland/Index @ 1d8ea2016e1677a3b8a62530b3c515de2c6397df
- registry/repositories-v2.yaml (map 2.2.2)
- architecture/canonical-execution-chain.md
- canonical component repositories and their executable tests/contracts
- REHT controlled framework artifacts supplied separately are used as semantic cross-checks, not as a substitute for repository code/tests

Repository-first rule
Every discovered repository must receive a proven disposition: MAPPED_TO_HEIMEL, SEPARATE_WITH_PROVEN_BOUNDARY, RETIRED_WITH_EVIDENCE, or UNRELATED_WITH_EVIDENCE. PENDING/NEEDS_MAPPING/NEEDS_SCOPE states intentionally block migration completion.

Concrete gaps already found and repaired
1. VAIG was omitted. HEIMEL now validates canonical VAIG evaluation evidence fail-closed; VAIG never grants execution authority.
2. MAL was omitted. Model invocation now requires exact non-authoritative admission binding provider/model/runtime/task/data/consequence/output contract.
3. Governed state admission from valo-platform was omitted. Kernel now has explicit ADMITTED/CANDIDATE/REJECTED state-admission semantics, provenance/authority/policy binding, expiry, and no memory/reasoning-derived authority.
4. Authority attestation semantics were omitted. Kernel now preserves adverse/unknown authority-state facts from internal/external attestors while rejecting authorization smuggling.
5. REHT-standard causal execution continuity v0.5 was not explicit in the canonical RealReht surface. The public RealReht export now enforces the required profile fail-closed, including persistent-state standing, governing-contract drift, required material constraints, action transformation, receipt/authority/state continuity, and external verification-evidence binding/replay/freshness checks.
6. The migrated MCP snapshot exposed caller-writable execution-receipt minting. HEIMEL runtime now removes/blocks valo.record_receipt; MCP orchestration approval and audit trail are explicitly non-authoritative and not proof of effect.
7. nsolland-reht-distribution contained promotion semantics absent from the HEIMEL distribution snapshot. HEIMEL now preserves build != production authority, explicit development→shadow→pilot→production separation, rollback requirement, fresh production clearance, fail-closed unknown identity/route/version and separate clearance/execution receipts.

Important correction: valo-v5-core
Index still classifies nsolland/valo-v5-core as active l1-guardian-and-compatibility ownership. It is NOT being described as simply superseded. The current canonical minimum execution chain does not require AiPlsCore/GoldenExecutionPath as a universal hop, so HEIMEL records it as a separate compatibility profile and proves consequence-property equivalence. The AiPlsCore/GoldenExecutionPath/ExclusiveEffector implementation, legacy L1 frame machinery and AiPlsCore TLA+ model are explicitly NOT claimed migrated.

Open blockers already identified
- valo-insurance-pack is an active frozen domain-pack implementation and is absent from HEIMEL; full snapshot migration remains required.
- valo-external-adapters is an active implementation owning authority projection, persistent-state/workspace/execution-substrate contracts and must be mapped without creating a parallel authority path.
- the account inventory is larger than the original 100-repository snapshot; account discovery is paginated and the pinned Index registry remains the canonical role/status source.
- remaining active/archived/scaffold repositories still require explicit source inspection/disposition.

CI policy
The repository archaeology test is intentionally failing while unresolved repositories remain. That red check is a migration-completeness blocker, not a flaky test. Other test failures are real blockers and must be fixed.

author: agustinrhcp
body:
`Dict` and `Set` already had `Eq`, so they compared fine but could not be printed:

```
Show.Show cannot be derived for Dict(String, Int)
```

That stops any assertion that reports a value on failure, which is how it turned up — `Expect.equal` in the test runner (#263) can't take a `Dict` today.

```jade
show(Dict.from_list([("a", 1), ("b", 2)]))   # Dict("a": 1, "b": 2)
show(Set.from_list([1, 2]))                  # Set(1, 2)
show(Dict.from_list([("a", [1, 2])]))        # Dict("a": [1, 2])
```

Keys, values and elements render through their own `Show` instances, so a `String` key keeps its quotes and a nested list prints as a list. The format matches what the runtime's own `to_s` already produced for these two.

Shaped like the existing `List` case: the deriver matches the type by name and threads each element's `show` into a stdlib function that does the rendering, since neither has variants to walk. The two helpers are private and declared `NO_INLINE`.

author: devece
body:
## Resumen

Fase 4.9 — Observabilidad, Monitoreo y Resiliencia Operacional. Auditoría completa del manejo de errores, Realtime, Supabase, PDF.js y Vercel, con pruebas de navegador controladas (Playwright, simulando la librería de Supabase) que reprodujeron 2 hallazgos **OBS-CRIT** reales y confirmados, ambos con una corrección pequeña, segura y ya probada:

- **OBS-CRIT-01**: `okDelProy()` no verificaba cuántas filas afectó el `DELETE`. Sin `.select()`, Supabase devuelve `data:null, error:null` incluso cuando 0 filas fueron borradas (ej. otra sesión ya había eliminado el proyecto) — la app mostraba igual "🗑 Proyecto eliminado", una falsa confirmación de éxito.
- **OBS-ALTO-01/02**: `activarRealtime()` lanzaba una excepción sin capturar si la librería de Supabase no llegaba a cargar (ej. el CDN falla), y `.subscribe()` no usaba el callback de estado de supabase-js — un `CHANNEL_ERROR`/`TIMED_OUT` dejaba la sincronización en vivo muerta sin ningún aviso, ni en consola ni para el usuario.

## Cambios

- `okDelProy()`: agrega `.select('id')` al `DELETE` y distingue el caso de 0 filas afectadas (mismo criterio que `guardar()` ya usa desde la Fase 4.2 para el `UPDATE` optimista) — ahora informa con un toast claro en vez de una falsa confirmación.
- `activarRealtime()`: se envuelve en `try/catch` y se agrega el callback de estado a `.subscribe()`, mostrando un aviso único (no repetido en cada reintento) cuando el canal no logra conectarse.

No se tocó RLS, Auth, permisos, ni ningún otro archivo.

## Verificación

Pruebas de navegador controladas (Chromium headless vía Playwright, con la librería de Supabase reemplazada por un mock fiel a su interfaz real) antes y después del cambio:

- `DELETE` que sí afecta 1 fila → sigue mostrando el toast de éxito normal (sin regresión).
- `DELETE` que afecta 0 filas → ahora muestra el aviso correcto en vez de la falsa confirmación.
- Librería de Supabase ausente (CDN caído) → `activarRealtime()` ya no lanza una excepción sin capturar, y muestra un aviso al usuario.
- Canal Realtime en estado `CHANNEL_ERROR` → muestra el aviso una sola vez.
- Conflicto de concurrencia de la Fase 4.2 (`guardar()` con `updated_at` desactualizado) → sigue funcionando exactamente igual.

## Summary

Found while running the dev-branch Tauri shell end-to-end on Windows Server 2022 (MSI install).

- `window::navigation_allowed` only admitted the `tauri:` scheme as the app's own origin. On Windows, Tauri serves `frontendDist` as `http://tauri.localhost`, so the very first navigation (`index.html?port=…`) fell into the "foreign http(s)" branch, got pushed to the default browser (an Edge error tab), and the webview stayed blank until the tray's *Open Dashboard* was used. `is_app_origin()` now accepts both forms; a unit test covers `tauri://localhost`, `http://tauri.localhost`, the proxy origin and a rejected `file:` URL.
- `main.rs` gets the standard `#![cfg_attr(not(debug_assertions), windows_subsystem = "windows")]`, so the release exe no longer opens a console window beside the tray app.
- *Stop proxy* decided `stopped` from a single `stop()` result or one immediate `is_alive()` probe. When the sidecar drops the connection while answering `stop`, `stop()` errs and the probe still sees the dying server, so the child was never reaped and the menu item stayed enabled even though the proxy was gone. It now polls `is_alive()` for up to ~2s before giving up.
- `bun run build:local` picks the host platform's bundles (`app,dmg` / `msi,nsis` / `appimage,deb`) instead of always asking for macOS bundles, and prints every produced bundle. The release workflow (which already ships the Windows MSI) is untouched.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` in `desktop/src-tauri` (Windows, stable).
- `bun run build:gui`, `bun run prepare-sidecar`, `bun run build:local` on Windows → `OpenCodex_2.61.0_x64_en-US.msi` and `OpenCodex_2.61.0_x64-setup.exe`.
- Installed the MSI and drove the app: sidecar spawns (`/healthz` 200 on 10100), tray menu, Open Dashboard / Open in Browser, Usage/Providers/Logs pages in the webview, close-to-tray, Start at Login toggle (HKCU Run key), single instance, Stop proxy, Quit (both processes exit), Check for Updates. Before the fix launch opened an Edge tab and left a black console window; after it the dashboard loads in the webview and no console appears.

author: nicoamigosa
body:
Closes #19

## What changed

The branch adds a release-pinned updater for Ralph. It downloads the requested `ralph-v<VERSION>.tar.gz` and its published `SHA256SUMS`, validates the release contract, checks the installed release for local divergence, and copies only paths listed by `MANIFEST`. It checks the remote `refs/ralph/lock` before any update work, so an active Ralph run blocks the update while `runs/`, checkpoints, and `.ralph/` remain outside the distribution.

The release workflow is documented in README, including creating the tarball from the versioned manifest and publishing both assets. The test release server exercises the acceptance criteria and also verifies that uppercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digests are accepted.

## Seams under test

- Release-server asset boundary: fake `curl` serves tarballs and `SHA256SUMS`, allowing checksum mismatch and valid-release behavior to be observed through `update.sh`.
- Installed-tree boundary: a temporary Git repository observes manifest-only replacement, VERSION update, local divergence reporting, and preservation of `runs/`, checkpoints, `.ralph/`, and unlisted files.
- Remote lock boundary: a temporary `origin` exposes `refs/ralph/lock`; the updater aborts before applying files when that ref exists.
- Release contract boundary: the updater validates the tarball VERSION and every manifest entry before touching the installed tree.

## How I verified

- `bats tests/update.bats` — PASS, 6/6.
- `bash -n once.sh update.sh` — PASS.
- `shellcheck once.sh update.sh` — PASS.
- `git diff --check` — PASS.
- `bats tests/` — 190/200 passed; the 10 failures are pre-existing `once.sh` failures outside this branch's changes: smoke-test environment propagation; inaccessible Codex smoke model; inaccessible Claude smoke model; optional smoke test; Claude smoke budget; CI checks appearing during timeout; recoverable CI infrastructure; post-merge hook timeout; merge-queue confirmation; and cleanup after an already-deleted remote branch. The update tests (tests 196–200 in that run) all passed.
- `bats --filter 'uppercase hexadecimal release checksums' tests/update.bats` — PASS during the red-green TDD slice.

## Open decisions

- The lock check uses the remote `refs/ralph/lock` contract from #22; the local `.ralph/lock` design from PR #57 was intentionally discarded.
- The updater downloads the installed VERSION release as the independent baseline for local-file comparison; therefore prior release assets must remain published.
- SHA-256 hexadecimal case is normalized before comparison; requiring lowercase would reject an equivalent valid digest.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Against a fake release server, `update.sh 1.1.0`/the equivalent fixture update replaces only manifest files and updates VERSION — `tests/update.bats`, “update replaces only manifest files and preserves project state”.
- [x] Incorrect checksum aborts without touching the tree — `tests/update.bats`, “update aborts on an incorrect release checksum without touching the tree”.
- [x] A local `once.sh` modification aborts with divergent files listed — `tests/update.bats`, “update lists local changes in common files and leaves them untouched”.
- [x] `runs/` and `.ralph/` remain intact — the preservation assertions in the manifest-only update test.
- [x] A present run lock aborts — `tests/update.bats`, “update aborts while the remote ralph run lock is present”, using `refs/ralph/lock`.

author: zongfeijing
body:
## Summary
Refit of the TRT-LLM rollout engines went through the full-tensor collective broadcast: every engine rank received the whole
model (~790 GB) and converted all 512 routed experts to MXFP8 although it only stores its EP slice. This PR

1. converts only the experts a rank stores (`initial_local_expert_ids`) during FP8/MXFP8 refit (5.5-15 s -> <0.3 s per rank);
2. adds the `nccl_reshard` transport to the TRT-LLM backend: the trainer sends each routed expert straight to the engine rank
   that owns its EP slot over one communicator per PP stage, one destination layout per engine role under prefill/decode
   disaggregation (context and generation engines have different TP/EP), and the non-expert tensors ride the existing packed
   broadcast; in-flight weight updates are honoured like the collective path;
3. sends every generation layout concurrently on the trainer (one CUDA stream per layout, each layer materialized once);
4. on the engine, batches the received expert stacks under a byte budget and loads them straight into their MoE modules,
   replaying the loader's MoE branch instead of a whole-model `reload` (which walked all 1749 modules and synchronized the
   receive stream per stack, serializing the receive loop);
5. skips `gc.collect()` / `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` in `offload_before_refit` (and the mid-refit `empty_cache`) by default
   when the transport is `nccl_reshard`: with no whole-model packing there is no memory spike to make room for, and returning
   ~150 GB of freed segments to the driver cost 0.3-3 s per rank inside the bubble (`NRL_OFFLOAD_BEFORE_REFIT_GC` /
   `NRL_OFFLOAD_BEFORE_REFIT_EMPTY_CACHE` = 0|1 override);
6. logs per-phase refit timings on the engines (`[refit-timing]`), the trainer (`bulk send`, `misc produce`, `misc broadcast`,
   `[offload-timing]`) and the controller.

## Results (Qwen3.5-397B GRPO, 1P8+1D16 disaggregated TRT-LLM, TP4 PP2 EP16 trainer, 16 nodes)
| | refit bubble / step | steady train step |
|---|---|---|
| MXFP8 rollouts, collective (before) | 20.7-21.6 s | 202-209 s |
| MXFP8 rollouts, this PR | 2.5-2.8 s | 176-183 s |
| bf16 rollouts, collective (before) | 6.0 s | 173-192 s |
| bf16 rollouts, this PR | 1.6-2.1 s | 171-186 s |
Accuracy unchanged (pass_k 0.745-0.753 vs 0.749-0.757 before). Remaining refit time: trainer-side per-param PP broadcast + TP
gather of the non-expert tensors (~1 s), the MoE module's per-expert load loop (~1 s).

## Smokes (bf16, two training steps each)
- aggregated TP8/EP8 x 4 replicas: refit bubble 4.8 / 5.1 s (about 2.4 s of it is the pre-existing torch.compile restore), rewards 0.29 / 0.38
- 2 context TP8 + 1 generation TP16: refit bubble 1.8 / 1.6 s, rewards 0.28 / 0.35

## Config
`policy.generation.refit_transport: nccl_reshard` (TRT-LLM engines must be TEP: `moe_expert_parallel_size == tensor_parallel_size`,
`pipeline_parallel_size == 1`; `check_nccl_reshard_refit_support` rejects anything else). No other config change.

## Tests
`tests/unit/models/generation/trtllm/test_trtllm_nccl_reshard.py` (new: layouts, slices, local quantization, batching, direct load,
synchronizer layouts, support check), `test_trtllm_fp8.py` (+7 local-expert tests). On the image used here the pre-existing
failures of the pin lineage (trtllm: pytest-asyncio, `_engine_owner_indices`, collective sync order; weight_sync: 2 regex) are
unchanged; no new failures.

## Commits
1. `trtllm refit: convert only this rank's routed experts to FP8/MXFP8`
2. `trtllm: shard-to-shard (nccl_reshard) refit for the TRT-LLM backend` (backend, multi-layout synchronizer, in-flight updates, concurrent layouts on the trainer, per-phase timing)
3. `trtllm nccl_reshard refit: batch the received expert stacks and load them straight into their MoE modules`
4. `megatron refit offload: skip gc.collect and empty_cache under nccl_reshard; time the misc producer`
