author: bertcalm
body:
## Summary

Builds §1 of `docs/PHOTO_SPECS.md` (merged in #297): one photo becomes a whole kit, not just one pad.

- **`PhotoKit.build`** (new, `:synth`) cuts a photo into the MPC's own 4×4 grid (not PHOTO FIELD's 16×12) and renders each cell as a full SNAP **pad** — `Snap.render`, a note — instead of a grain. Cell (0, 0), the photo's top-left, lands at slot 13 (A13); (0, 3), the bottom-left, at slot 1 (A01) — `PadBanks`'s own numbering, the same geometry `KitArt`'s GRID style and `KitScreen` already draw. `AutoPlace` never runs: the layout is the picture's own.
- **Colour**: `Snap.Reading` gained `meanRgb` (a third accumulator pair in `Snap.look`), and `ArrangedPad` gained an optional `colorHex` that `KitAssembler.assembleArranged` now checks ahead of `AutoPlace.colorFor` — every other existing caller passes none and keeps today's class colour, unchanged.
- **Recipe**: each pad's recipe is its `SnapPatch` (`PadRecipe(patch = patch).toJsonValue()`), so a photo kit regenerates from its `kit.json` sidecar like every other synth kit — never a folder of anonymous WAVs.
- **Landing**: `KitShelf.landPhotoKit` (`:app`) mirrors `render`'s own shape (`freshName`, `KitAssembler.assembleArranged`, a fresh `Entry`). `App.buildPhotoKit` mirrors `fresh` line for line — the same whole-app busy overlay (`Copy.SNAP_KIT_BUSY`), the same shelf-list refresh, the same `open`/`screen = AppScreen.KIT` landing — since KIT ▸ leaves the SNAP screen rather than staying on it the way FIELD/CLOUD do.
- **Screen**: a KIT ▸ button beside FIELD ▸ and CLOUD ▸ on SNAP, builds off the main thread, always lands as a **new** kit on the shelf (never overwrites the open kit), and opens KIT on it.

Built with both of the spec's recommended decisions: a first-class shelf entry (not a bank B behind the open kit), laid out as the picture (not `AutoPlace`'s).

Docs updated: `README.md`'s `:synth` section, `docs/SYNTH_ROADMAP.md` (new §S7.3), `app/README.md`'s SNAP on-device verify checklist, and `docs/PHOTO_SPECS.md` itself marked §1 as built.

## Test plan

- [x] `PhotoKitTest` (new): sixteen pads each carry their own cell's colour; the photo's layout formula (top-left → A13, bottom-left → A01, checked all four corners); every pad's recipe regenerates byte-identical audio; the same photo built twice is byte-identical; a photo smaller than the grid still fills all sixteen pads; sixteen distinct cells never collapse to a shared class colour.
- [x] `SnapTest`: new `meanRgb` coverage (a flat tint, and a half-red/half-blue split).
- [x] `KitAssemblerTest`: new coverage that an explicit `colorHex` overrides `AutoPlace.colorFor`, and that `null` still falls back to it exactly as before.
- [x] `PersonalityTest` (reflective Copy-string sweep): new `SNAP_KIT_BUSY` constant checked.
- [x] `ConventionTest`, `PadRecipeTest`: unaffected, still green.
- [x] Ran the full `./gradlew --no-daemon test` (all JVM modules).
- [ ] On-device: `app/README.md`'s new KIT ▸ verify lines (can't be checked from this environment — no Android SDK / phone here).

Linear: https://linear.app/colife/issue/COL-39/真实-notion-测试工作区端到端验收与版本交付

候选提交: `43e112f873b7a20e6a93a8c7ec713828a9a1f2f2`

依赖：Draft PR #16 `78ac29928206476342c388f957214d3911040bb6`；本 PR 以 `codex/col-36-imported-restore-audit` 为 base。

## 变化与原因

- 恢复导入后，连接一直处于 `paused_after_restore`，此前界面没有入口核对备份记录与当前 Notion 结构。本次增加手动只读核对按钮和逐项结果。
- API 核对当前有效凭据所属工作区，以及根页面、四张表、四个关联的已确认记录、精确远端 ID、父级、标题、属性类型和关联目标。SDK 返回的根页面、database/data source ID 及 data source 的直接 database 父对象也必须匹配请求；回收站、字段变化、读不到、权限、限流和缺失记录都不能得到一致结论。
- 若读回期间本地数据集、连接、步骤记录或凭据改变，返回 409 丢弃结果。遇到权限或限流错误后停止后续远端读取，未检查项明确标注。
- 核对不写业务 SQLite，不确认初始化步骤，不扫描任务，不发送旧 outbox，也不解除恢复隔离。内部网关读回增加 `in_trash` 判断；无数据库迁移或业务备份格式变化。

## 验证

- `pnpm check`：最终候选退出 0；包含 lint、类型检查、单元与 API/SQLite 集成测试。假网关验证一致、远端 ID/关联错配、回收站、429 停止继续读取、并发替换备份时返回 409，以及连接保持隔离。SDK 假响应测试验证错 ID、错父级 ID 和错父级类型直接拒绝（API 245/245）。
- `pnpm build`：退出 0；Next 16.3.3 生产构建和 Worker dry run 通过。
- `pnpm test:e2e tests/e2e/notion-oauth.spec.ts --project=chrome --project=safari-webkit`：最终候选 18/18 通过；使用临时 SQLite 和浏览器假 HTTP 响应，覆盖新按钮、差异展示、390px 视口与发送入口继续隐藏。
- `pnpm test:e2e --project=chrome --project=safari-webkit`：最终提交 `43e112f` 上的完整浏览器套件 84/84 通过，退出 0；使用临时 SQLite、隔离端口、脚本模型和假 Notion HTTP 响应。
- `git diff --cached --check`：提交前退出 0。

## 待验收与交付说明

- 独立验收任务已对最终 head `43e112f` 完成代码层复核，未发现本 PR 差异中的剩余具体缺陷；它独立复跑结构 API 15/15、`pnpm check`、`pnpm build` 和相关 Chrome/WebKit E2E 18/18。仍需在用户指定的隔离 Notion 工作区验证真实授权、SDK 响应和恢复读回。当前证据不代表真实 Notion 验收、部署、G3 模型质量或 G4 七天使用效果。
- 独立验收在首个 head `3a26f45` 指出 data source 响应 ID 未核对，在第二个 head `6c8fe4d` 指出父对象类型未核对；最终提交已补齐直接 database 父对象检查与回归测试，前述发现已关闭。

- 回退本提交即可移除此入口；现有 `paused_after_restore` 隔离和业务数据保持不变。合并前请保持 Draft，并按依赖顺序审查堆叠 PR。

author: sasroque-beep
body: ## O que muda Testes **E2E em navegador real** para a camada 3D, com Playwright + Chromium, rodando contra o **build de produção**, num **job de CI separado** (`e2e`, em paralelo ao `verify`). **Nenhuma alteração em código de produto** — só `e2e/`, config, CI, dependência e docs. ### Justificativa da ferramenta (`AGENTS.md` §14) Registrada em [`docs/QUALITY_ASSURANCE.md` §9](./docs/QUALITY_ASSURANCE.md) (subseção nova; o exemplo aspiracional login→publicar **não foi alterado** — o diff do arquivo é só de adições): stack, o que já existia, compatibilidade, custo e necessidade, com as alternativas descartadas (Vitest Browser Mode, Cypress, Puppeteer, Selenium, manter manual). ### Decisões aplicadas - **Chromium obrigatório**; Firefox/WebKit declarados em `playwright.config.ts` via `E2E_BROWSERS`, **não executados nem validados**. - **Sem regressão visual por screenshot**: asserções de estado (`data-experience-mode`), DOM, rede e contagem de `requestAnimationFrame`. Screenshot/trace só como artefato de diagnóstico em falha. - **Job `e2e` dentro do `ci.yml`** existente. **Não é *required check*** — primeiro uma janela de ~10 execuções verdes; depois Issue própria para avaliar torná-lo obrigatório. - `@playwright/test` `^1.63.0`; o lockfile controla versão e binários. - `retries: 0` e `workers: 1` (ver "Estabilidade"). ## O que é validado (25 testes + 1 `fixme`) | Requisito | Como | | --- | --- | | Carregamento da 3D e `FULL_3D` | fallback do servidor vira cena; `` com tamanho; contexto vivo; `` segue no DOM | | `REDUCED_3D` / `prefers-reduced-motion` | no primeiro load, alterado em runtime, e dispositivo de baixa capacidade; render loop parado (0 frames) × 67–80 frames/1,5 s em `FULL_3D` | | `FALLBACK_2D` / sem WebGL | `getContext` de WebGL devolve `null` (padrão da web, igual em qualquer navegador); prova que a detecção rodou antes de afirmar | | Conteúdo e CTA | mesmo conteúdo e CTA **clicáveis** em `FULL`, `REDUCED`, `FALLBACK` e sem WebGL; sem JS o HTML do servidor já traz tudo | | Falha em runtime | perda de contexto WebGL e falha do download do chunk voltam ao fallback; modo forçado sem WebGL não derruba a página | | Lazy loading | nenhum chunk 3D no HTML inicial, nem em `/` e `/leads/new`, nem sem WebGL; baixado só após a hidratação (chunk "3D" = contém Three.js, sem depender de nomes com hash) | | Erros de console | **todo** teste falha em `pageerror`, `console.error` ou HTTP ≥ 400 da própria origem; exceções só declaradas por teste, com motivo | ## Estabilidade (medida, não presumida) - **2 workers**: 24 falhas em 250 execuções (~10%), quase todas timeouts de 30 s — WebGL por software satura CPU (máquina de 4 núcleos). Por isso `workers: 1` fixo. - **1 worker**: `--repeat-each=10` → **250 passaram, 0 falharam** (10 puladas = o `fixme`), 5,8 min. - O teste "modo forçado sem WebGL" (que falhou 2× sob carga com asserção real) rodou **30/30** isolado. - **O guard de console foi validado com um controle**: um teste que dispara `console.error`/erro não capturado de propósito **falha**, como deve. - **Spike na CI antes de escrever os specs**: o Ubuntu do GitHub Actions entrega WebGL2 via SwiftShader (mesmo renderer do local). ## Bug real encontrado (não corrigido aqui, por decisão de escopo) → #42 Descartar a cena (ex.: override `FALLBACK_2D`) faz o R3F disparar `webglcontextlost` no canvas **já desconectado**; o handler da #37 trata como falha real e trava `runtimeFailureReported` — depois disso "Automático" nunca volta a `FULL_3D`. Reproduzido com instrumentação (`webglcontextlost attached=false`). Coberto por um `test.fixme` que aponta para a #42 e deve ser reativado quando ela for corrigida. ## Detalhes do diff - `pnpm-lock.yaml`: além dos 3 pacotes do Playwright, a chave do `next` ganha `(@playwright/test@1.63.0)` — o Next declara `@playwright/test` como peer opcional e o pnpm reflete isso. Efeito colateral esperado. - `e2e/` é checado por `tsc` e Biome sem configuração extra; o Vitest **não** o coleta (58 arquivos / 367 testes, iguais ao da `main`). - Rodar localmente: `pnpm build` → `pnpm exec playwright install chromium` (uma vez) → `pnpm test:e2e`. ## Limitações conhecidas - A suíte usa `/dev/experience-3d-hero-showcase` (rota de dev que vai no build de produção — limitação já registrada, fora do escopo). - Firefox/WebKit e regressão visual: fora do escopo. - Integração com `site-builder` e editor: fora do escopo. Closes #41 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: google-labs-stitch[bot]
body:
## Summary of Changes

This PR updates the `Receive` function in `p2p_transport/internal/transfer/receiver.go` to ensure proper stream management and disk cleanup upon transfer errors and checksum mismatches:

1. **Named Return Error & Stream Lifecycle Management**:
   - Updated `Receive` signature to `func Receive(s network.Stream) (err error)`.
   - Added deferred stream handling: calls `s.Reset()` when `err != nil` to signal abrupt termination to the remote peer, and `s.Close()` on success.

2. **Partial Download File Cleanup**:
   - Added deferred file cleanup after output file creation. `outFile.Close()` is called prior to checking `if err != nil` to remove incomplete download files (`os.Remove(outPath)`), avoiding file lock conflicts.

3. **Explicit Checksum Error Handling**:
   - Checksum mismatch now returns an explicit error (`fmt.Errorf("checksum mismatch...")`) instead of returning `nil`, triggering output file removal and stream reset.

4. **Unit Test Suite**:
   - Added `p2p_transport/internal/transfer/receiver_test.go` covering successful transfer, header read failure, interrupted data stream, and checksum mismatch.

## Verification
- Ran `go test -v ./internal/transfer` - all unit tests passed.
- Ran `go test -race -count=1 ./...` - all package tests passed.

author: roprgm
body:
## Change

Follow-up to #28 from the reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude review of that diff, plus three findings from a correctness pass. Net **−101 lines** across 42 files with the same behavior, except where noted.

- **Effect commands.** `editEffect` creates the missing layer itself inside one history group and applies the command, so `setDetails`, `setColorMixer`, `setVignette`, and XMP clarity drop their create thunks and duplicate validation; `findEffect` serves the command lookups and `getState`. A vignette created through `setVignette` now starts at intensity 50 like the UI's (API.md updated).
- **Render graph.** The adjustments pass picks its exposure-only shader itself, so the image layer gets the fast path and a default image emits no pass. `composeLayer` folds through `composeLayers`; `maskModifiers` in `core/document` is the one rule for active submasks, shared by the mix and the overlay.
- **Layers panel.** Rows read selection and image size themselves, are memoized, and mount their menus only while open. Tree drag, gradient drags, and the preview store subscribers stop re-rendering on every pointer move, and the renderer skips a full re-render when a dropped curve input needs none.
- **Shared helpers.** `rotateCursor` serves crop and mask guides, `renderBitmap` serves thumbnails and export, `createImageLayer` replaces nine image-layer literals, and `readImage` takes sample points for the browser tests.
- **Keyboard.** Shortcuts pause while any popover is open, so Escape in the pill's Add/Subtract menu no longer deletes a freshly drawn mask; a drag on the mask canvas drops the focus of the button that armed the tool so Enter keeps the mask instead of clicking it again; a histogram draws as soon as it attaches so a selection change shows the curve input immediately.
- **Removed.** Unused `viewportClassName` and `Slider className` props, the single-variant `NewMask.kind`, and the `MaskPreview` export.

Skipped on purpose: `ImageLayer.children` stays in the model (removing it ripples through tree walking, depth validation, and row rendering), and the crop panel keeps its Enter guard because its handles are buttons that must apply on Enter.

## Validation

`bun run check`, `bun run build`, and **27 unit tests pass** (pass-name expectations follow the exposure-only naming). The full local Chromium suite ran at this tree: **9 workflows complete every step and HEIC skips** for the missing HEVC decoder; each is recorded as failed only by the console-error fixture catching the sandbox's blocked analytics request, which is not reproducible outside it. Verification gaps: physical GPU, Safari, Firefox, touch devices.

## Visual evidence

Not applicable beyond the behaviors above: the UI is unchanged in layout and controls, so the layer, editing, crop, and export workflows exercised the affected paths; no screenshots differ from #28.

## Rendering performance

Rendering work drops slightly: an image with default adjustments no longer runs its adjustments pass, and a layer with only exposure uses the lighter exposure shader that masks already used. No pass grew. No before/after timing was run in this sandbox's software adapter; pass counts are asserted by the unit tests.

author: linted
body:
The savings log records every eviction by tool_call_id, and the graphs' histories are checkpointed in the same MongoDB, so the report can join them: for each first-time eviction, look up the latest checkpoint of the graph (the outer part of the logged namespace) and check for a later tool call with the same name and arguments. That re-run rate is the best single check on whether the threshold is too aggressive; the log alone cannot see it.

New section at the end of the report, e.g.

  Evicted results the agent fetched again: 9 of 58 (16%), ~42,596 tokens re-sent once
    get_code: 8 of 32   read_file: 1 of 3

Evictions whose history cannot be read are reported as unchecked rather than counted either way. `--no-reruns` skips the checkpoint lookups.

body:
## Resumo
- O reconhecimento de titulares na importação de fatura dependia de duas condições frágeis ao mesmo tempo: o padrão exato "(final NNNN)" no cabeçalho E uma linha de total exata para fechar a seção. Faturas com um único titular, ou com pequenas variações de formatação, caíam no erro "não consegui identificar as seções por titular", exigindo intervenção manual a cada fatura diferente.
- Agora as seções são delimitadas apenas pelos cabeçalhos de titular presentes (quando existem) ou, na ausência deles, por uma única seção cobrindo todos os lançamentos de compras/saques da fatura (usando o nome do titular principal). A linha de total deixou de ser obrigatória — quando aparece, continua sendo usada como conferência (checksum) na tela de revisão, mas a ausência dela não bloqueia mais a importação.
- Quando a fatura só tem um titular (ou nenhum "(final NNNN)" identificável), o app pula direto para a tela de conferência em vez de pedir para escolher entre opções que não existem.

## Test plan
- [x] Reconfirmado com a fatura real de 4 titulares: os 4 continuam batendo exatamente com os totais informados pela própria fatura (nenhuma regressão).
- [x] Testado com dados sintéticos simulando uma fatura de titular único (sem "(final NNNN)"): a seção única é extraída corretamente, incluindo detecção de parcela e conferência do total.
- [x] Regressão completa das demais abas e da importação manual/aprendizado — sem erros de console.

author: rfx-agent[bot]
body:
This is not a physics change, and it is a breaking one for anyone who used Studio. Studio — the browser workspace, the experiment service behind it, the agent control plane and their command-line entry points — leaves the simulator package and becomes a separate add-on (PI decision, 2026-09-21). Nothing in the solver, the ports, the probes, the preflight or the I/O path is touched.

## Why the cut is clean

No module of the physics core imports the studio side. Checked two ways: a `git grep` for absolute and relative imports at any indentation, and an AST scan of every remaining tracked Python file (Codex's audit, reproduced in the report). `rfx/__init__.py` is unchanged and none of the 61 names the removed packages exported appears in any remaining `__all__`.

The one real link ran the other way and was at test level: `tests/interop/test_interop_shape_codec.py` read `rfx/experiments/canonical.py` as text to confirm a phrase in it. That half of the test goes with its subject; the half that binds the shape vocabulary to `rfx/config/_shapes.py` stays.

## What goes

66 files, about 20,900 lines:

- `studio/` — the React front end and its e2e tests.
- `rfx/studio/`, `rfx/experiments/`, `rfx/agents/`, `rfx/operations.py`, `rfx/telemetry.py`.
- `scripts/studio_clean_install_smoke.py` and `.github/workflows/studio-packaging.yml` (lint, typecheck, front-end build and the three-OS clean-wheel smoke of the studio install).
- `docs/agent/mcp-studio.mdx`, `docs/guides/studio_operations.md`, `docs/public/guide/studio-experiments.mdx`, and the rows, links and sentences that pointed at them in `README.md`, the public site map and index, the installation and support-boundaries pages, the agent runbook and `working-on-rfx`.
- `pyproject.toml`: console scripts `rfx-studio` and `rfx-agent-mcp`; extras `studio` and `agent`; `rfx-fdtd[studio]` out of `dev`, `agent,studio` out of `all`; the `rfx.studio` package-data entry; and `httpx`, which no remaining file imports.
- Six data files nothing reads: the four experiment specs in `tests/fixtures/experiments/` and the patch-antenna and WR-90 golden workflows. Their readers were the studio tests (#1144) and the studio smoke script.

Everything removed is retrievable from `main` at `f078385e`, the last commit that holds all of it together with its tests' removal record (#1144).

## What stays, on purpose

- **`rfx/cli.py`.** It is the simulator's own CLI, not Studio's. `rfx run`, `rfx plot` and `rfx export-geometry` remain, and their handlers and `main()` are AST-identical to `main`; only `build_parser` changes, losing the `experiment`, `studio` and `workspace` subcommands with their handlers.
- **`tests/fixtures/golden_workflows/multilayer_fresnel.json`.** The cv26 oblique-Fresnel comparator, the crossval records and `test_calibration_envelope_ownership.py` read it. It is the only studio-era data file with a live reader.
- **`rfx/dashboard`, the `dashboard` extra and `rfx-dashboard`.** Not Studio.
- **Records.** `docs/design_notes/**`, `scripts/vessl_931/**` and `CHANGELOG.md` keep their mentions; a historical docstring in `test_mixed_port_sparam.py` now says the names in it are history.
- **`.test_durations`** still lists the removed test ids; pytest-split ignores ids it does not collect, and the file is regenerated by its own workflow.

## Smaller edits

- `rfx/config/__init__.py`, `rfx/interop/_design.py`, `rfx/interop/_shapes.py`: docstring sentences that named the experiment document as a sibling layer now say it left with Studio.
- `rfx/interop/_design.py` (two places) and `rfx/preflight/waveguide.py`: comments that still named `tests/studio/test_interop_design_document.py` point at `tests/interop/`, where #1144 moved it.
- `.github/labeler.yml`, `.gitignore`, two contract tests (`test_ci_workflows_contract.py` used `studio/conftest.py` as its example of a nested conftest; `test_evidence_numeric_provenance.py` listed the removed public page).

## What this costs

- Users of `rfx studio`, `rfx experiment …`, `rfx workspace …`, `rfx-studio`, `rfx-agent-mcp`, or of `pip install rfx-fdtd[studio]` / `[agent]`, lose them in the next release. The changelog fragment says so.
- **Nothing in CI builds a wheel or calls mypy any more.** Both jobs lived in the removed workflow. Neither covered the simulator — the mypy job checked only the studio-side modules, the wheel smoke installed the studio extra — so no checking of what remains is lost, but the core package has no install smoke and `[tool.mypy]` has no caller. That gap is left open here, not filled.

## Evidence

- `python -m rfx.cli --help` lists `run`, `plot`, `export-geometry` and nothing else.
- `pytest --collect-only`: 10,831 selected after, exit 0. Against `main` the branch loses exactly six ids, all contract-test parameters keyed by the removed workflow and the two removed guide pages, and no test (the verification review reproduced this from a clean `git archive` of `main`).
- `tests/locks`, `tests/interop`, `tests/unit/api` (not covered by `local.sh`): 892 passed, 29 skipped.
- `scripts/ci/local.sh`: all 6 steps passed on the final commit; contract tests 3,476 passed, 6 skipped.
- Wheel: an isolated `python -m build --wheel` gives `rfx_fdtd-1.8.0-py3-none-any.whl` with no studio-side file and three console scripts (`rfx`, `rfx-dashboard`, `rfx-diagnose`); the verification review built it again from a clean export of the commit and found the same.
- Scope guard: under `rfx/`, only the removed paths plus `cli.py`, `config/__init__.py`, `interop/_design.py`, `interop/_shapes.py`, `preflight/waveguide.py` differ from `main`.

Two independent reviews ran on the first commit: one given no list of concerns, one given the author's ten claims to reproduce. Nine claims reproduced. The tenth — why the fixture directories stay — was wrong, and both reviews also found that an edited contract assertion no longer exercised the rule it is named for; the second commit answers both and the smaller leftovers.

Codex stopped, as instructed, on the five items it could not decide (the fragment number, the interop test's read of the removed file, a gate that reads the git index while deletions were unstaged, a historical comment, and a wheel build blocked by its sandbox's network).

author: slimatic
body:
Implements both halves of the decision: **leave stored records alone, offer a recalculation nudge.**

## Why the record has to be written first

Until 0.16.8 the exchange rates came from a table hardcoded in 2023 (EGP 42% low, TRY 45% low against the live provider). A saved calculation recorded **nothing** about which rate produced it — so a record computed at that stale rate was **byte-identical to a correct one**. There was no way to tell a user their figures were affected. The nudge is impossible retroactively unless the rate is captured at write time.

Two nullable columns on `zakat_calculations`:

```
fxRateUsed    the rate applied at calculation time (1 when no conversion needed)
fxRateSource  live | cache | fallback | unknown
```

Nullable **on purpose**. Existing rows keep NULL, which is the honest value — their provenance is genuinely unknown. NULL is distinguishable from a recorded rate, so a comparison can say *"we cannot tell"* rather than implying the record was verified correct. Those are different claims and the API keeps them different.

## New: `GET /api/zakat/calculations/:id/rate-staleness`

Reports whether the rate has moved and by how much. It **never modifies the record and never recalculates** — that is the user's decision, not something to apply silently to figures they may have already acted on.

Three distinct outcomes, deliberately not collapsed:

| state | result |
| --- | --- |
| no recorded rate | provenance `unknown`, `shouldRecalculate: false`, + a reason so the absence of a prompt isn't read as a clean bill of health |
| rate unavailable | `driftPercent: null`, `shouldRecalculate: false` — explicitly **not** a fabricated drift of 0, which would read as "all good" |
| rate recorded | drift percent, `shouldRecalculate` at ≥ 1% |

**The 1% threshold exists because FX drifts continuously.** A prompt firing on a 0.3% move would appear on nearly every record and train users to dismiss it — worse than not prompting at all.

## Migration is additive

Two nullable columns. No defaults, no backfill, no data touched.

## Test-isolation note worth recording

The test database is **not** migration-managed — its `_prisma_migrations` table doesn't exist, so `migrate deploy` fails `P3005` and `globalSetup` falls back to `db push`. Adding a column therefore requires syncing the test DB separately, or every integration test touching the model fails with `P2022 "column does not exist"`.

Also: Prisma resolves `file:./test/test.db` **relative to the schema directory**, so the real location is `prisma/test/test.db`. A URL written as if relative to the server root creates a stray directory instead. Both tripped me here — and the second time I did it, I first "fixed" it in the wrong place and had to go back.

## Tests (12)

Drift and threshold logic, plus **the two historical stale rates as regression cases**, plus an explicit assertion that "unknown provenance" stays distinguishable from both "stale" and "stable".

```
server   685 passed (64 files)   [was 673/63]
tsc      0 errors
coverage 38.42%
```

body:
純文件，只動 `docs/P3-CALIBRATION.md`（+55／−1），不碰任何程式。

## 先更正一則我自己的錯誤敘述

我先前對使用者說「排序表還缺一個成本模型要先問你」——**那是錯的**。費率在裁定 #54 Q6 就定好了（手續費 0.1425%×2 ＋ 證交稅 0.3% ＋ 滑價 0.2%×2，`docs/P3-CALIBRATION.md:162`／`:171`），我沒查就順口說的。本節定的是**套用方式**，費率一個字都沒改。

兩個常見分歧點也不存在：池子**不含 ETF**（`src/iching/universe.py:41` 依 `spec/P1-B1-market.md:157` 排除 ETF／權證／DR／特別股／興櫃），不必處理 0.1% 稅率；手續費採未打折公定價，偏保守。

## 四項裁定（使用者：「全照建議」）

前提：`fwd_ret` ＝ `adj_close(T+1+h) / adj_open(T+1) − 1`（`docs/P3-DATASET.md:45`），隔日開盤進、第 h 日收盤出。

- **Q9 乘法扣除、買賣兩端分開**：`net_ret = (1+fwd_ret)×(1−s)(1−f−t)/[(1+s)(1+f)] − 1`。成本是比例不是固定值，而 mid horizon 實測 `max|fwd_ret|` 到 3.26。**實算對照**：`fwd_ret=3.26` 時乘法 3.218208、算術 3.250150，差 **3.19 個百分點**；`fwd_ret=0.05` 時只差 0.045 個百分點；`fwd_ret=0` 時本式為 **−0.981%**，與 Q6 的一階估算 0.985% 差 0.004 個百分點（二階項）——是同一個成本模型的精確化，不是改口徑，排序表要把 0.981% 明寫以免日後被當成兩套數字。
- **Q10 排名依均值**，中位數並列作穩健性對照；**均值與中位數異號的卦另標示、不進高／低組**（與 `n<500` 歸中組是兩條獨立規則，標示要分得開）。Q6 原文只說「均值、中位數、排名」沒說排名依哪一個，這是規格本身的縫。
- **Q11 進出場不對稱**：`entry_limit_up=true` 整列排除（買不到的報酬不該計入）；`exit_limit_down`／`exit_reason=halt`／`delist` 保留（賣不掉、停牌、下市都是真實損失，排除等於美化）；`fwd_ret=null` 不計入 n。排除與保留的列數都要進揭露行。
- **Q12 滑價維持一律 0.2%、不分層**，表下註明「對低流動性個股偏樂觀」——分層等於引入一組沒有回測依據的新參數（鐵律 8）。

## 一併記下 R1～R6 驗收條件

在動手寫 `scripts/rank_table.py` **之前**寫的，含兩條容易被漏掉的：R5「只讀訓練段、驗證段一列都不讀」（測試注入一份驗證段檔斷言未被開啟），R4「`n<500` 與 Q10 的異號標示必須可分辨」。

author: the-da-vinci
body:
## Intent

Fix a real defect in the firstmate repository itself, at ~/firstmate (NOT the kaamos project).

Reproduced tonight at session start with a 28-task fleet:

~/firstmate/bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh: line 1991: /usr/bin/jq: Argument list too long

The snapshot builds a jq invocation whose arguments grow with fleet size, so it exceeds the kernel argument limit once enough tasks exist. The effect is that the supervisor's fleet snapshot silently produces nothing exactly when the fleet is largest and the snapshot matters most. It degrades with scale, which is the worst failure shape for a supervision tool.

Your task:
1. Reproduce it deterministically. Write a throwaway harness that drives the script with a synthetic fleet large enough to trip the limit, and capture the exact failure. Do not guess at the mechanism.
2. Fix the cause: stop passing unbounded data as command-line arguments. Feed it on stdin, or via --argjson from a file, or chunk it - choose based on what the surrounding code already does, and say why.
3. Prove the fix at a fleet size well beyond today's 28 tasks.
4. Make sure the snapshot's OUTPUT is unchanged for a small fleet. This is a transport fix, not a behaviour change. Prove that with a before/after comparison on the same input.
5. Check the rest of bin/ for the same pattern - any jq, xargs-free loop, or command invocation whose argument list grows per task - and report what you find even if you do not change it.

This is firstmate's own shared tracked material, so read the firstmate-coding-guidelines skill before editing and follow it: one sentence per line in prose, plain dashes, shellcheck-clean scripts, and no agent co-author on the commit.

Deliver through this repository's no-mistakes pipeline and open a PR. Do not merge it.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh` now hands the backlog and the per-task contribution rows to `jq` as slurped files instead of `--argjson` command-line values, so a large fleet no longer trips the kernel argument limit and aborts the snapshot.
- The temporary transport directory and backlog file are staged before the `--contribution-input` branch, and both that branch and the full snapshot path share a single `contribution_input_json` helper with status checks on every step, so an assembly failure reports an error instead of exiting 0 with empty output.
- `tests/fm-fleet-snapshot-view.test.sh` adds a case that drives `--contribution-input` with 64 tasks carrying 50 KB PR URLs and a 200-row backlog whose titles exceed 128 KB, asserting the output is complete rather than truncated.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: A well-bounded transport-only change: the jq invocation is value-identical after the --argjson to --slurpfile swap, every step of the deduplicated assembly is now status-checked so the silent exit-0 path is closed, the temp dir is still reaped by the existing EXIT trap, and the new regression fails before the fix by pushing both the backlog and the task corpus past the single-argument limit.

## Testing

I stood up synthetic FM_HOME fleets shaped like the operator home that hit this (its data/backlog.md is 119,639 bytes across 47 state metas, so the parsed backlog JSON passed as one --argjson value exceeds the 128 KiB per-argument cap) and drove the real CLI both pre-fix and post-fix. The failure reproduces exactly as reported at 28 tasks, including the silent exit 0 with empty stdout, and its end-user consequence is visible in persisted state: the supervisor's contribution poll wrote 0 of 28 durable records pre-fix and 28 of 28 post-fix. The fix holds well beyond the reported size — 150 tasks and a 2000-row backlog produce a complete contribution input, a complete `--json` snapshot with contributions.known=150, and a 2019-line rendered fleet view. Output equivalence is proven by byte comparison across all three output modes on two fleet sizes plus a clean diff of the rendered view, so this is transport-only. Adversarially I injected a failure into the assembly step: post-fix it exits 1 with a named diagnostic and the downstream poll aborts non-zero, where pre-fix both exited 0 with nothing to show, and the newly created temp transport directory is cleaned up on both paths. The authored regression is red against the pre-fix script and green against the fixed one. One behavior change worth a reviewer's eye rather than a fix: `--contribution-input` now needs a writable TMPDIR and refuses loudly without one, consistent with the `--json` path. This is a shell CLI with no rendered UI surface, so the reviewer-visible artifacts are command transcripts and the rendered fleet-view text rather than screenshots. The intent's fifth item — surveying the rest of bin/ for the same pattern — is a reporting deliverable rather than a drivable scenario, but driving all three output modes and both downstream consumers at 150 tasks would have tripped any remaining per-task argv growth on those paths and did not.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 11 of 11 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| On a 28-task fleet with a production-sized backlog, the supervisor's contribution input returns the whole backlog and fleet instead of failing with 'Argument list too long' | ✅ pass | live | ~/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M30S9SZJJF6BQGXBR0AN9784/01-repro-argv-overflow.txt — pre-fix: exit 0, 0 bytes, `line 1991: /usr/bin/jq: Argument list too long`; post-fix: exit 0, 883,892 bytes, t… |
| A fleet far beyond the reported size (150 tasks, 2000-row backlog) still produces a complete contribution input and a complete full snapshot | ✅ pass | live | ~/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M30S9SZJJF6BQGXBR0AN9784/02-fix-at-scale.txt — 3,119,923 bytes, tasks=150 backlog.records=2000, all 150 pr.url present; `--json` reports contributions.known=150 |
| The supervisor's contribution poll writes a durable record for every owned PR instead of silently observing none | ✅ pass | live | ~/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M30S9SZJJF6BQGXBR0AN9784/05-contributions-poll-before-after.txt — pre-fix 0 of 28 data/<task>/contributions.json written at exit 0; post-fix 28 of 28, with an obser… |

author: crazymunch
body:
**PR #100, branch `claude/fd-13a-formulas-tab`.** Groundwork for FD-13a item 2. None of it is the tab; all of it is what the tab cannot be built on top of until it is fixed, and each is a defect in its own right.

Order 35 reviewed FORM-2 and found two defects. Both were mine, both are fixed here in FORM-4, and verifying them turned up a third.

---

## FORM-1 — a nested option group lost its parent

`rules/formulae.ts` has documented the group as `Alchemical Formulae::Eye Options` since it was written, matched by containment so "a sub-group counts as its parent". No group in the dataset contained `::`. In `parse-battlescribe.mjs` a nested group **replaced** its parent's name:

```js
fromGroup(inner, clean(attr(inner, 'name')) || groupName);
```

So the one sub-group that comment names was the single case the predicate could not answer. `UnitAdvancementModal` writes an option's group as the purchase's `category`, and `formulaeOf` asks whether that category contains `Alchemical Formulae` — so a **Hawk Eyes bought in the app** wrote `Eye Options` and the model that bought it had no Formula by that name in `traitsOf`, in `chosenBy`, or in the card's Formula section.

`UnitOption.groupPath` carries the ancestry **beside** the leaf, the shape `newrecruit-paths.mjs` already uses. `group` stays the leaf: it is the heading a player reads, and several readers compare it exactly. **74 options gain one** — the twelve Eye Options and every Goetic Powers sin.

## FORM-2 — the prerequisites and exclusions, read from the sentence

Derived from the rules text, never the name. **Six shapes**, across five entries and two different phrasings of the same rule:

| Sentence | Entry |
|---|---|
| "Can only be bought if the Homunculus already has the Human Hands, Inhuman Strength and Massive Size Formulas." | Gargantuan Size |
| "Cannot be combined with the Wings formula." | Human Hands |
| "This formula cannot be combined with the Wings formula." | Massive Size |
| "Cannot be combined with Hawk Eyes without Two Heads." | Hypnotic Eyes *(Court form)* |
| "Cannot be combined with Hypnotic Eyes without Two Heads." | Hawk Eyes *(Court form)* |
| "A Homunculus cannot have the Hypnotic Eyes Alchemical Formula if it has the Hawk Eyes Alchemical Formula unless it also has the Two Heads Alchemical Formula" | the Takwin entry *(book form)* |

The conditional patterns are tried **before** the plain one: a sentence carrying an exception, read by the plain pattern, enforces the refusal and drops the way out of it.

Two Heads' own "can have both the Hawk Eyes and Hypnotic Eyes" is **deliberately not parsed as a rule**. It is the same fact from the other side, and two mechanisms for one fact means whichever ran last wins. (It *is* read, in FORM-4, as the permission that identifies a lifter — which is a different job.)

## FORM-3 — 280 unit options a player could buy for nothing

FD-13a item 2 asks for "a `quartermaster` debit". Checking what the existing purchase path does found it has none, and that this is not a Formulae problem.

`toggleUnitSpecialUpgrade` added the option's price to the model's `totalCost` and **charged nobody**. Measured across the shipped ruleset:

```
280 priced options, across 18 groups, free
```

Every Alchemical Formula, every Saga, every Goetic Power, the Strains, the Arts of Assassination, the Butcher Knight Ranks, and the Armour options at up to 50 Ducats each. The same defect as FD-05e-2 (equipping Battlekit), FD-05g (a Glory-priced item) and FD-05h (a Glory-priced model) — one layer further out, and the last of them.

Now booked through the ledger with `charge`/`refund`, reversible until the game it was bought in has been played, settled after that. Two details:

- **`ref` is the model and the option together.** The same option id is on every model that can take it, so keying on the option alone would let one Homunculus's refund cancel another's purchase. Pinned by a test.
- **The whole `Cost` is spent.** Devouring Jaws is the one Glory-priced option in the ruleset, and FD-05g's lesson is that an entry at zero Ducats and some Glory is free to anything reading only the first number.

## FORM-4 — Order 35's two defects in FORM-2, and a third found proving them

**First.** `formulaGate` resolved names against the whole ruleset. The six Homunculus entries do not offer the same Formulae: the Iron Sultanate's Takwin offers **Two Heads**; the five Golem copies offer **Additional Head** — *"The Homunculus has two heads and therefore can have two sets of eyes via Alchemical Formula"* — and their Eye Options still say *"without Two Heads"*. So the ruleset-wide lookup found a Two Heads a Golem can never buy, and **a Golem holding Hawk Eyes and Additional Head was refused Hypnotic Eyes against the sentence printed on the Formula it was holding.**

`known` is now the Formulae the model's **own entry** offers. Where the exception names something that entry does not offer, the lifter is the Formula on that entry whose text grants the same permission — matched on what it *says*, not on either name, so one Takwin entry and five Golem entries go through the same code. Both sentences are quoted where the regex lives.

**Second.** When the lifter did not resolve, the exclusion was pushed with `unless: null` and then **enforced** — turning "cannot be combined with X without Y" into "cannot be combined with X". That is precisely the direction of error the module header says it avoids, and it costs a player a legal purchase. An exception that resolves to nothing is now a **caveat carrying the sentence, never a refusal**.

**Third, found writing the test Order 35 asked for.** The Takwin entry states the rule in the **book's** wording, not the Court's short form (the sixth row in the FORM-2 table above). FORM-2 read neither that shape nor — because its survey regex looked only for "cannot be combined" — noticed it was missing. So the survey I described as catching a new shape arriving was itself blind to one already present. Both fixed; the survey now covers it. The Takwin's text ends without a full stop, so none is required.

**Naming:** Order 35 calls this FORM-3, which this branch had already used for the 280 free options. Kept as FORM-4 so the two are not confused in the history.

---

## What this settles about the tab

The open design question — replace the advancement sheet's list, or sit beside it — is answered twice over. Order 35 rules that the tab **replaces** the Formula groups while the sheet keeps Goetic Powers, Strains, Sagas and the rest. And measurement says there was never a competing surface to begin with:

```
distinct Alchemical Formulae:                     17   (15 before FORM-1)
reachable in the equip sheet:  equipment=0  weapons=0  armour=0
what the existing "formulae" chip shows:          (nothing)
```

`recruitable` builds the equip sheet's lists from **armoury rows**, and a Formula is a unit **option** — never an armoury row. That chip has shown an empty panel to every player who ever tapped it, filtered by a name regex over a list that structurally cannot contain a Formula. It is the name-pattern engine CLAUDE.md forbids and task #28 deleted elsewhere, and it goes with the tab.

## Verification

Run on `dd70494`:

- `npx next lint --max-warnings 42` — exit 0
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx vitest run` with local Postgres attached — **178 files, 2530 tests, all passing** (37 new)
- `npm run rules:check` — `OK`

`formulaGates.test.ts` drives the **shipped** sentences, not paraphrases, per entry — so a catalogue reword shows up as a test that stops matching rather than a gate that quietly stops gating. It includes Order 35's named cases: a Golem with Hawk Eyes and Additional Head may take Hypnotic Eyes and without it is refused; the Takwin with Two Heads may and without it is refused; an exception resolving to nothing is a caveat with the sentence.

author: cyanokobalamyne
body:
Every backend guarded its indexed operators with some variation on `if (op.idx0 < 0) throw IncorrectUsageException(...)`, eighteen of them across z3, mathsat and yices2 plus a dead disjunct in cvc5. `Op` stores indices as `std::uint64_t`, so none of those tests could ever be true, and the thing they were aimed at got through: a caller writing `Op(Extract, -1, 0)` converts to 18446744073709551615 at the call, walks past the guard, and is then narrowed to the `unsigned` or `uint32_t` the solver API takes, arriving as a plausible but unrelated width. `Op` also left `idx0` and `idx1` out of the initializer lists of the constructors that do not take them, and the Python properties read both without consulting `num_idx`, so `smt_switch.Op().idx0` returned indeterminate memory.

The new `narrow_index` in `solver_utils.h` does the conversion once and throws when the value does not fit, generalising the only real check in the tree, cvc5's; the eighteen guards give way to it at the sites that narrow. MathSAT takes `size_t` and bitwuzla `uint64_t`, so those two only lose dead code. The fields are now zeroed, and the Python properties return `None` rather than a value that was never set, which is distinguishable from an index that is genuinely zero. On the Python side the index casts become `<uint64_t?>`, so a negative index raises `OverflowError` instead of wrapping, which is what the C++ guards were reaching for. Nothing read those properties unguarded except the bindings themselves.

Replacing the three fields with a single list is the change that would make `num_idx` unable to disagree with the indices at all; it breaks an installed header, so it follows separately.

author: alseif0x
body:
Triage could import a boot outcome without the harness's acceptance decision, so deliberate panic/hang fixtures could still look like failures. The boot suite now emits per-mode `harness.json` with a fresh suite identity, the existing outcome/reached acceptance predicate, and hashes of the exact result and serial artifacts. Old reports are cleared before the suite; completed failed checks are recorded before raising, while pre-result exceptions remain unknown.

Add optional explicit `import-report --kind boot --harness PATH` validation and preserve source provenance before promoting acceptance facts. The existing deterministic guard suppresses failure hypotheses for accepted fixtures; v1 classifiers, prompts, thresholds and earlier evaluation records are unchanged. An offline CI check imports actual panic/hang controls, verifies their source hashes and shared suite identity, and requires guarded diagnoses. No API calls, credentials, guest, ABI or authority changes.

Validation: `cargo xtask check` passed 418 Rust tests plus formatting/Clippy/builds; the full Python suite passed 249 tests. Independent review identified and verified the fix for tuple-valued block results changing to JSON lists. Strict normalization preserves raw hashes and valid aggregate report shapes; large-log tests ensure native exports do not inherit research byte caps. No unresolved material review findings. Full final-head CI is required before merge. Scope remains boot reports supported by the existing bounded importer; terminal/recovery aggregates and sandbox acceptance need separate contracts. This supplies prospective collection infrastructure and controls, not new representative failure accuracy or routine JEV promotion.

author: omochairo
body:
## 何を直すか

#7892: fetch run が重なると、checkout (job開始) から push (job終了、実測60〜90分後) までの間に別のfetch runが先にmainへマージし、後発runのPRが `dirty` (コンフリクト状態) のまま作られていた。dirtyなPRには `pull_request` の checks が一切走らない (GitHubがマージコミットを作れないため) ので required check が永久に埋まらないまま auto-merge が詰み、run 1回ぶんのデータ更新が誰にも気づかれず捨てられていた (実例: #7853)。

issueが挙げた4案のうち、issue本文が推していた **1+2** を検証のうえ採用。3 (concurrency group) は fetch (1.5時間) を直列化する副作用が大きく、4 (コンフリクト検出でrun失敗) は 2 を入れれば実質不要になるため見送り。

## 変更内容

### 2. `01-fetch-products.yml`: push前にoriginのmainを取り込む
commit直後・push直前に `git fetch origin main && git merge origin/main` を挟む。競合したファイルは行単位でマージせず、この run が今取ってきたデータをファイル単位で丸ごと採用する (`git checkout --ours`)。data/ は生成物のスナップショットで、行単位マージだとJSONの途中に別runの断片が混ざって壊れるため。

issue本文は「data/ の衝突解決は別途要検討」として未決だった部分なので、`git rebase` ではなく `git merge` (ours/theirs の向きが直感的) + ファイル単位 `--ours` 採用という具体案まで詰めた。fetch-depth: 1 (shallow clone) の環境で実際に動くかは自明ではなかったため、ローカルの模擬リポジトリ (shallow clone → 別workerがmainを先行更新 → 同一ファイルで競合 → fetch/merge/resolve/push) で動作確認済み。

### 1. `recover_pending_pr_checks.py`: `needs human` をUIに出す
close→reopenを使い切ってもrequired checkが埋まらない (`recovered_by=none`) 状態は、今までPythonの `logger.warning` (stderrのみ) にしか出ておらず、run一覧・run詳細のANNOTATIONS欄に一切表示されなかった。今回の事故で復旧スクリプト自身は6時間以上前から「人手が要る」と気づいていたのに、それがどこにも見えなかった (#4793 と同型の再発)。`::warning::` workflow commandをstdoutに追加で出し、UIのANNOTATIONS欄に載るようにした。

## テスト

- `python -m pytest scripts/tests -q`: 4572 passed, 3 skipped (既存の失敗3件は本PRと無関係。`test_validate_article_pr_range.py` がサブプロセスから `python` コマンドを呼ぶが、このサンドボックス環境には `python3` しか無く `python` が無いため。venv越しの実行環境依存でPRの変更内容とは無関係)
- `recover_pending_pr_checks.py` の新規テスト (`emit_warning_annotation` が `::warning::` を吐くこと) を含め該当ファイルは全通過
- shallow clone + merge conflict + resolve + push のシナリオを `/tmp` に模擬リポジトリを作って手動検証 (fetch-depth:1 の状態からでもmerge-baseが正しく解決され、`--ours` 採用後に不正なJSONにならず、pushも成功することを確認)

## Test plan
- [x] 単体テスト (`scripts/tests/test_recover_pending_pr_checks.py`)
- [x] YAML構文チェック (`python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"`)
- [x] shallow clone環境でのfetch/merge/conflict解決/pushの手動再現検証
- [ ] 次回のfetch runでauto-mergeが正常に完了すること (本番でのみ確認可能)

author: alechill
body:
## FAFF‑1064 — build-claim on-box under `bundle_store` (pluggable claim transport)

Generalises `claimStoreCore` to a pluggable `ClaimTransport` so the build-claim mutex follows `bundle_store`: on-box under `bundle_store: local`, on `origin` under `git-remote`. Closes the origin leak where `refs/faff/build-claims/<issue>` was pushed to `origin` regardless of `bundle_store`, contradicting local mode's "nothing under `refs/faff/*` pushed to origin". This is the isolated, higher-risk half of the FAFF‑1059 local-mode work (the writer `--local` flags are FAFF‑1062, the onboard flow is FAFF‑1063).

### What changed

- `claimStoreCore` now touches a claim ref only through a four-primitive transport (`readHead` / `read` / `casWrite` / `casDelete`); no direct `git push` / `ls-remote` / `fetch` / `update-ref` remains in its verbs. Its second argument is now a transport, with a string (or unset) wrapped as `gitRemoteTransport(root, name)` so existing callers are unchanged.
- `gitRemoteTransport` — today's origin push behaviour extracted byte-for-byte, pinned by an argv-capturing spy over acquire / confirm / reclaim / release (the DONE oracle).
- `localRefTransport` — a never-pushed local ref via `git update-ref` compare-and-swap: create-only via an empty old-value, lease update via an old-value match, lease delete via `-d`. Its stderr failure classification maps a CAS miss (`reference already exists` / `but expected` / `unable to resolve reference`) to `cas_lost` and a lock/io fault to `error`, never conflated, so a transient lock never reads as `superseded`.
- `buildClaimStore` selects the transport from `resolveBundleStoreName(root)`; `recoveryClaimStore` and `landingClaimStore` keep the git-remote default unchanged.
- The build-claim now follows `bundle_store` (a decisions-register entry was added to `docs/decisions.md`).
- The pre-build kill-switch (validate `git update-ref` CAS: a create, a second create that must fail, a mismatched-old update that must fail) was run and passed against the repo's git before touching `claimStoreCore`.

### Reviewer note

Spec §3's "standard mode = `bundle_store` unset or git-remote" is imprecise: `resolveBundleStoreName` maps an unset `bundle_store` to `local`, so an unset-`bundle_store` repo now uses the on-box transport, per the human-ratified decisions-register intent (same resolution as the bundle and recovery stores) and consistent with faff's "nothing off-box by default" default. faff's own repo pins `bundle_store: git-remote`, so faff's builds are unchanged. The adversarial second-opinion review pass was unavailable this session (all backends hit the deadline before a first byte), so please give this concurrency-primitive refactor an extra manual look.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Under `bundle_store: local`, an acquire / reclaim / release cycle issues no `git push` and creates no `refs/remotes/*` entry
      Verified: `buildClaimSelftest` local fixture + `test/bundle.test.mjs::FAFF‑1064 buildClaimStore (local): ... issues NO git push and creates NO refs/remotes/*` — passing
- [x] With `bundle_store` git-remote, the build-claim behaviour is byte-for-byte identical to pre-change
      Verified: `buildClaimSelftest` argv-spy oracle (acquire / confirmHead / release / reclaim argv sequences) + `test/bundle.test.mjs::FAFF‑1064 buildClaimStore: under bundle_store: git-remote ...` — passing
- [x] `claimStoreCore` calls `transport.*` only; no direct git in its verbs
      Verified: static grep of the `claimStoreCore` body (only comments/detail-strings mention git; 13 `transport.*` calls)
- [x] `confirmHead` routes through the head-only `readHead`; malformed competitor head still reads `superseded`; standard-mode `confirmHead` is the same bare `ls-remote`
      Verified: argv-spy oracle `confirmHead is a bare ls-remote, no fetch/show` + selftest `confirmHead against a wrong sha refuses (superseded)`
- [x] `localRefTransport` uses `git update-ref` create-only / lease / delete; `readHead`/`read` use `show-ref`/`show`; failure classification maps mismatch to `cas_lost` and lock/io to `error`
      Verified: `test/bundle.test.mjs::FAFF‑1064 localRefTransport: a lock/io fault classifies as error, never cas_lost` + create-only race test — passing
- [x] `buildClaimStore` selects `localRefTransport` when `resolveBundleStoreName == "local"`, else git-remote; recovery/landing still git-remote
      Verified: `test/bundle.test.mjs` both-mode selection tests; recovery/landing bindings unchanged
- [x] Two concurrent same-box acquires: exactly one wins
      Verified: selftest local fixture + `localRefTransport: two create-only CAS writes ... exactly one wins, loser cas_lost`
- [x] A stale local claim is reclaimed via lease-matched `git update-ref`, epoch++; released claim re-acquirable; release-superseded a safe no-op
      Verified: selftest local fixture + `test/bundle.test.mjs` reclaim/release cycle — passing
- [x] `confirmHead`, self-recognition idempotence, and `buildClaimStaleAware` behave identically under the local transport; the local build claim is never nulled out
      Verified: `buildClaimSelftest` local fixture (56/56); `buildClaimStore` constructs and returns the store under local mode (never `null`)
- [x] Pre-build gate: `git update-ref` CAS validation run before touching `claimStoreCore`
      Verified: create / second-create-fails / mismatched-old-update-fails all behaved as assumed against git 2.39.5
- [x] `buildClaimSelftest` runs both transports; `regions selftest --region factory` green; `test/bundle.test.mjs` gains local-transport coverage and keeps the recovery local-store no-op test unchanged
      Verified: `buildClaimSelftest` 56/56 (both fixtures); `regions selftest --region factory` 106/0; full suite 4803/4808 (0 fail, 5 docker-skipped)

Closes FAFF‑1064.

Before: clicking Refresh Data on the Portfolio page while the visible page held only predraft, unlinked, or errored league cards posted an empty `leagues` list to `POST /api/portfolio/refresh`. The endpoint rejects that with 400 `invalid_request` (`routes/user_pages_bp.py:998`, `if not submitted`), so the refresh surfaced a false "Refresh failed" state even though there was genuinely nothing to refresh. This matches a production access log line: `POST /api/portfolio/refresh` returning 400 with a 50-byte body, which is the `invalid_request` category.

After: `brRefreshCurrentPage` detects the empty case and returns a no-op success without making the request. No failure is surfaced, the pointless round-trip is avoided, and the live-matchup timer is still rearmed by the existing `finally` block.

This is the client-side fix for a client-side defect. Only fully-valid (and loading) league cards carry `data-summary-card`; pending and errored cards do not (`app.py:29171`, `app.py:29188`). The paginator shows 4 cards per page (`app.py:29508`), so a page containing only pending or errored cards produced an empty `keys` array, which was still POSTed unconditionally.

How: the guard `if(!keys.length)return {success:true,refreshedAt:null};` is added as the first statement inside the existing `try` block in the portfolio `brRefreshCurrentPage` script (`app.py`), after `keys` is built and before the fetch. Placing it inside the `try` keeps the `finally` cleanup and live-timer rearm intact.

The server contract is intentionally strict about input validation, so it is left unchanged. `tests/test_refresh_singleflight.py::test_portfolio_refresh_contract_is_targeted` still passes.

author: pedrogoiania
body:
Continuação do #8, tudo testado no totem — foi de lá que cada um destes veio.

## O preview saiu
Ele nunca desenhou nada, e era a imagem errada de qualquer forma: **o leitor é um ponto fixo abaixo da tela**, não uma câmera que a pessoa mira. No lugar entrou uma seta apontando para ele, e o card ficou **por último na tela**, junto do leitor físico.

A sessão de leitura saiu da view nativa e virou `startDecode`/`stopDecode` no módulo. Com isso nada mais converte quadros NV21 a 10 fps para desenhar um preview invisível, e o `stopDecode` continua no cleanup — é ele que impede a segunda leitura de vir preta.

## Três bugs de layout, todos meus, encontrados no aparelho
1. **Card de busca com `flex: 1`** ocupava metade da tela parado e empurrava a instrução do leitor para fora. Ele só precisa crescer enquanto alguém digita, que é quando os outros cards somem.
2. Corrigir isso expôs **`column: { flex: 1 }`**: em retrato as duas colunas empilhadas dividiam a altura, abrindo um vão no meio e mantendo o leitor cortado. Proporção entre colunas só faz sentido em paisagem, onde vem de `columnMain`/`columnSide`.
3. E remover aquilo **quebrou a busca**: sem espaço para crescer, a lista de resultados renderizava com altura zero. Os nomes casavam e nada aparecia — nem a mensagem "Nenhum inscrito com esse nome", porque **havia resultados o tempo todo**, invisíveis. A coluna agora estica enquanto digita.

## Fechar o teclado reseta o totem
O campo não se limpa sozinho: quem desistia no meio da digitação deixava o próprio nome na tela para o próximo da fila.

## Verificação
`jest` — 130 testes ✓ (novo: o reset ao fechar o teclado) · `tsc` e `eslint` limpos · APK instalado no totem.

No aparelho: busca por "alv" retorna Higor Alves Dutra, Viviany Mamedio Alves e Alveri Silva Rocha; leitura de QR pelo leitor nativo credenciando normalmente.

## Resumen

- **Editar notas**: nuevo `PATCH /hoteles/:hotelId/notas/:id` + botón "Editar" en cada nota del frontend, que reabre el mismo formulario precargado con los datos existentes.
- **Filtro por fecha y tipo**: `GET /hoteles/:hotelId/notas` acepta `desde`/`hasta` (calendario Lima) y `tipo`. Por defecto el frontend muestra solo las notas de **hoy**, con un botón "Ver solo hoy" para volver rápido a ese estado.
- **Orden**: ya estaba de más reciente a más antigua (`fecha_hora` descendente) — confirmado, sin cambios.

## Bug real encontrado al probar (zona horaria)

El `<input type="datetime-local">` de fecha de inicio/fin de repetición manda `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"` en hora del navegador, **sin zona**. Al guardarse tal cual en una columna `timestamptz`, Postgres lo interpretaba con su timezone de sesión (UTC), no con la hora Lima real — una nota puesta a las 8:45pm aparecía mostrando 3:45pm (desfase fijo de 5 horas). Se corrige en `NotasService` (crear y actualizar) declarando el offset `-05:00` explícito antes de guardar, mismo criterio que el resto del sistema (Perú es UTC-5 fijo, sin horario de verano).

**Nota operativa:** las notas repetitivas de prueba creadas antes de este fix quedaron con la hora desfasada 5 horas — conviene editarlas (con el botón nuevo) o borrarlas y crearlas de nuevo.

Ninguna — no se tocó el schema.

author: ryanseery
body:
Closes #230

## Summary

Nine e2e specs drive two browser contexts, and each answers "does this transition propagate". None plays a game where every player is a real browser — `multiplayer.e2e.ts` puts its guests in through `addPlayer` and `makeSelection`. This adds one spec that seats three contexts at one table and plays the last three rounds entirely through the UI, so the question it answers is whether a table of three arrives at the results screen together.

## Changes

- `playwright/game/three-browsers.e2e.ts` (new): three `browser.newContext()`s, each signed in with `signIn`, then one `seedGame` at `round:3` with the three uids as players and rounds 10 to 4 already picked, so the spec plays three rounds rather than ten. Each round, every page types its own letter and submits through `pick-input`, `suggestion-item` and `submit-pick` — no `addPlayer`, no `makeSelection`. Under `OPTIONS_FIXTURES` the options are one title per letter, so no two pages can collide on a pick.
- The local `onEveryPage(pages, assert)` helper wraps each page's assertion in a `test.step` named for the player, so a convergence check is one line and a failure names the page that lagged. `test.slow()`: nine picks and three reveals across three browsers do not fit the 30s default.
- Not tagged `@smoke`, so it runs in the full suite and in CI's `e2e` job. Gate wall-clock for the spec was 12.4s.
- The spec asserts the nine picks it made through the UI with their points, the row count (7 seeded + 9 played = 16) and page-to-page convergence, but nothing about the order of the seeded rows. The tradeoff is in **Notes for reviewer**.

The round loop, once all three pages are on the round screen:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Round
    Round --> TwoIn: "host and guest 1 pick"
    TwoIn --> Round: "no page shows reveal-container"
    TwoIn --> Reveal: "guest 2 picks"
    Reveal --> Reveal: "guests have no reveal-skip"
    Reveal --> Round: "host clicks reveal-skip, rounds 3 → 2 → 1"
    Reveal --> Results: "after round 1"
    Results --> [*]
```

## Verification

**What the reader can see.** Nothing a player can see changes: this adds one Playwright spec and touches no file under `src/`.

**What the reader must do.**

- [ ] `mise run ci` — ran green on this branch: format, lint, types, 127 unit tests, then the full e2e suite, 37 passed in 3.6m, `three-browsers.e2e.ts` among them at 12.4s.
- [ ] `mise run test:e2e -- --retries 0 --grep "three browsers"` five consecutive times, and put the wall-clock of one run on #230. The gate ran the spec once, with the suite's retry settings; five clean runs at zero retries is the flake bar the ticket sets and one pass does not clear it.
- [ ] After this merges, read the `e2e` job's wall-clock off the `main` run and put it on #230 next to the number from before the spec landed.
- [ ] `git grep -nE "addPlayer|makeSelection" playwright/game/three-browsers.e2e.ts` returns nothing — the acceptance criterion that every pick in this spec goes through the UI.

## Notes for reviewer

- Look first at the round loop in `three-browsers.e2e.ts`: the two-of-three assertion (`reveal-container` at count 0 after the second pick) is the one that would catch a reveal firing early, and it is also the one most likely to pass for the wrong reason if the reveal is merely slow to render.
- What the spec gives up: the three pages are compared against the host's rendered order rather than against a known head of the list, so a table that converged on a *wrong* order would pass here. That ordering promise is asserted by `results.e2e.ts` (aggregation across shared picks, descending order), and duplicating it here meant asserting arithmetic on the seeded rows. Positions inside a points tie are the order selections were inserted in — an implementation detail, not something the screen promises — so they are not asserted either.
- No new dependency, no change under `.github/**` or `.claude/**`, nothing regenerated, no existing test changed.

## Summary
- **Entry/Current Price split**: refresh silently overwrote `entry_price` with the live quote, losing the real historical buy price on every refresh. `entry_price` is now set once at add time and never touched by refresh; a new `current_price` field is refreshed instead, alongside ATR.
- **Entry Price is now editable** in the grid (same pattern as ATR Multiple / # Tranches), so a real fill price — slippage, a limit order, entering after the fact — can be corrected by hand. Rejects 0/negative edits with a clear toast.

author: zxm-happy
body:
## Summary

Bug #76852: a Gauge (and, by shared base class, Thermometer/SlidingScale/Cylinder) script write
to `ranges`/`rangeColors` that is shorter than a prior write in the same live session left stale
trailing boundaries/colors visible in the render, because the backing arrays only ever grew, never
shrank.

## Root cause and fix

- `RangeOutputVSAssemblyInfo.setRanges`/`setRangeColors` (`core/src/main/java/inetsoft/uql/viewsheet/internal/RangeOutputVSAssemblyInfo.java`)
  grew `rangeValues`/`rangeColorsValue` on a longer write but only overwrote the prefix on an
  equal/shorter write, leaving old `DynamicValue`/`DynamicValue2` entries (and their stale runtime
  values) past the new length. Both setters now unconditionally construct a fresh, exactly-sized
  backing array on every write, matching the sibling `setRangeValues`/`setRangeColorsValue`
  pattern already used correctly elsewhere on this same class. This is a base class shared by
  `GaugeVSAssemblyInfo`, `ThermometerVSAssemblyInfo`, `SlidingScaleVSAssemblyInfo`, and
  `CylinderVSAssemblyInfo`, so the fix covers all four assembly types, not just Gauge.

- Once the setters resize independently to the caller's exact incoming length, `ranges.length` and
  `colors.length` can legitimately diverge in ordinary use (e.g. a script updates one property
  without the other). This is not just a hypothetical: three renderers had an early-return that
  refused to render *anything* when `ranges.length > colors.length`:
  - `VSCylinder.fillRanges`
  - `VSHorizontalThermometer.fillRanges` / `VSVerticalThermometer.fillRanges`
  - `VSSlidingScale.fillRanges`

  `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` risk once lengths can diverge. Added the missing bounds checks.

author: heyadamyoung
body:
Deploy 368 succeeded and took eighteen minutes. The whole of it is in four lines of its own log:

```
01:23:47  Container wayfare-api-1 Recreate
01:29:44  Container wayfare-api-1 Recreated     5m 57s
01:29:44  Container wayfare-web-1 Recreate
01:36:27  Container wayfare-web-1 Recreated     6m 43s
01:36:31  all healthy
```

Everything else — rsync, backup, pull, schema, health check, and all the housekeeping after it — is **under a minute put together**:

| | |
|---|---|
| rsync + release env | 10 s |
| backup | 15 s |
| login + pull | 15 s |
| health, Logto, census, sweep check | 11 s |
| cutover + image pruning + capacity | 23 s |

A recreate on this box normally takes **three seconds** — 367's rollback did five of them in as many seconds. Nothing was wrong with either container. The box was saturated: the old api was running a zoom pass over every place in the world while the sweep read the planet at seven thousand records a second on all sixteen cores, so Postgres and the disk were pinned and the Docker daemon queued behind them.

The zoom pass is gone as of that same release. The sweep is not.

## The sweep gets a share of the box, not the box

Four cores of sixteen and a low block-IO weight. The planet takes longer and nobody is waiting on the planet; a deploy is a person waiting, and a release that cannot be swapped in because a backfill has the disk is a backfill that has been allowed to matter more than the product.

Memory is deliberately left alone — the run holds ~1.5 M records across the cells still open, and a limit under that buys an out-of-memory kill two hours in rather than a share of anything.

## A shutdown is bounded, at both levels

The places worker awaited whatever was in flight, which included that same planet-wide pass; the api's signal handler awaited the worker. Waiting was never buying anything — the zoom pass commits a cell at a time and records which cells are done, the index build is `CONCURRENTLY` and idempotent, and an unfinished transaction is rolled back by the database the moment the connection drops. What the grace is really for is the ingest letting go of the cell it has claimed.

Three seconds for the worker, eight for the process, against Docker's ten before it sends a signal nothing can catch. A shutdown longer than that is not a graceful one; it is a killed one with extra steps.

## And the deploy ends at the health check

Logto's sign-in configuration, the day census, the sweep start, the media cutover and the image pruning now run **detached**, in a session of their own, writing to `/var/log/wayfare-after-release.log`. They were already unable to fail a release; they should also have been unable to hold one open. (Proven locally: the parent returns in 0 s and the child completes with its variables intact.)

A guard asserts the order and the detachment, and that nothing which could fail a release sits below the gate.

731 server tests, 29 deployment guards, biome clean, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Still to come for the 3-minute target: the server-test job is 3 m 24 s, and `places-worker.test.js` alone is 79.8 s of it.

author: bryceashey
body:
The `rasputin-os` half of geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#595. Pairs with rasputin-control-plane#382, which reads what this bakes.

## Why

The no-DHCP bootstrap address carries **no default gateway** by design (#53) — it exists for exactly the case where the Rasputin firewall isn't up yet and nothing serves DHCP. On that path the control plane can't reach `api.github.com`, so `GET /api/cluster/firewall-image` can't resolve a release, `flash.sh` dies before downloading anything, and the operator can't flash the firewall that would restore internet.

The control plane's only job there is **naming** the release — the laptop downloads and verifies for itself. So the name and checksum can travel in the image.

This is the chicken-and-egg `design/principles.md:28` already names, with the baked Headscale image called out as the pattern to copy.

## What

- **`board/rasputin/common/firewall-pin.txt`** — one bare CalVer line, currently `2026.09.4-dev.127` (the first firewall release publishing `manifest.json.sig`). Commented as a **compatibility statement**, bumped deliberately as its own reviewed change after the paired firewall release has been flashed and exercised — never a drive-by refresh, never automatic.
- **`post-build.sh`** — fetches that pinned release's `manifest.json` + `manifest.json.sig` and installs both at `/usr/share/rasputin/firewall/`, 0644. One code path, both SKUs.

**Pinned, not "latest".** Following a rolling upstream at build time is what burned `2026.09.2`: the firewall build followed an unversioned Snort3 rules URL, Talos republished between a green pre-flight and the tag build, the SHA mismatched, and because release tags are immutable the version was lost (geekdojo-brain#208, firewall PR #48). It also makes the image non-reproducible and records nowhere which firewall release a given OS image trusts.

## Verified at build time, fail-closed

The signature is checked **before** either file is installed, against the trust root the image itself ships — `$TARGET_DIR/etc/rasputin/trust/root-ca.pem`, which `release.yml`'s unconditional *Inject trust root* step writes from `vars.RASPUTIN_ROOT_CA_PEM`. Confirmed against the pinned Buildroot 2025.02.17 Makefile that the overlay copy precedes `BR2_ROOTFS_POST_BUILD_SCRIPT`, so the file exists when post-build runs.

Confirmed separately: the org variable's cert is **byte-identical** to the published root CA at `rasputin.geekdojo.com/rasputin-root-ca.pem` — same SHA-256 fingerprint `67:7E:57:06:…:C1:B9`.

The build **fails** rather than shipping an image without the fallback: a missing or malformed pin, a failed fetch, an unsigned release, a signature that doesn't verify, a missing trust root, or a correctly-signed manifest whose `version` doesn't equal the pin (which would otherwise defeat the pin silently). An image that quietly lacks the fallback is the invisible-failure mode this whole issue exists to remove.

**One behaviour change to note:** a *local* build with no `root-ca.pem` in the trust dir now fails instead of producing an image. Deliberate — an unverified descriptor is exactly what must not ship — and the error names the file and path. Flagging it because it narrows the dev-permissive mode the trust dir's README mentions.

## Tests

`test/firewall-manifest-test.sh`, 33 checks, wired into `ci.yml`. Throwaway EC PKI mirroring the leaf-003 profile, real `openssl cms` sign+verify, stubbed `curl` serving a fake release tree. No network, no root.

Covers the happy path (both files at the contract path, byte-identical, 0644, version named in the log, baked on rpi too) and the refusals — missing pin, comment-only pin, two-version pin, leading `v`, non-CalVer, failed fetch, a release with no `.sig` (what every pre-dev.127 release looks like), an untrusted-root signature, a wrong-version manifest, a missing trust root — each asserting **nothing was baked**. Plus a grep that `releases/latest` never appears.

Also verified locally: `dash -n` clean over every `board/**/*.sh`, and `clock-floor-test` / `fallback-address-test` / `atrest-modes-test` still pass.

The bake was additionally exercised for real — `post-build.sh n100` with no stubs against the live `2026.09.4-dev.127` release fetched, verified and installed byte-identical copies.

## Sequencing

Merging this is safe on its own — it only adds the bake. But the offline fallback doesn't work until the image also vendors a control plane containing #382, so the order is: **#382 merges → CP release publishes → this merges → CP pin bump in `rasputin-os` → OS build.**

The issue closes on whichever lands last; this commit deliberately says `Refs`, not `Fixes`.

## Ops(R435) — the self-read census re-taken at the head; the enumeration was one member short

R434's close left **R344's filed census** at the Ops queue's head. The clause
(`README.md` → *Review policy* → *A self-read is declared*) carries its own re-take
rule — *"a reading at its head, and re-taken by re-applying both limbs to the list"* —
and its last re-take was recorded at `49287a7`.

**Re-applied at `2ec0d1d`, the class yields seven members where the enumeration named six.**

The seventh is step 6's duty that the admitting read's **output** states what it found
under each of the four conditions — the count `0` included:

- **actor** — the step the editor performs (workflow step 6);
- **object** — *the step's own output* (the decision comment, or the comment that
  discharges a `[revision-complete]` re-check): an artefact the editor itself produces;

author: diaoyunxi
body:
## 问题描述

`main.py:221` 在 async 函数 `api_sample()` 中使用了 `subprocess.run()`，这会阻塞整个事件循环（ASYNC221）。

## 修复内容

将同步 `subprocess.run()` 替换为异步的 `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec()`：

```python
# Before
import subprocess
subprocess.run([...], check=True, capture_output=True, timeout=30)

# After
import asyncio
proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
    sys.executable, str(PROJECT_ROOT / "tools" / "gen_sample.py"),
    cwd=str(PROJECT_ROOT),
    stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
)
stdout, stderr = await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=30)
if proc.returncode != 0:
    raise Exception(f"Process failed with code {proc.returncode}")
```

## 影响

- 不再阻塞事件循环
- 保持原有的 30 秒超时机制
- 使用 `asyncio.wait_for()` 实现超时控制

## Summary by Sourcery

Use asynchronous subprocess execution for sample generation in the async API handler.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent the sample-generation subprocess from blocking the asynchronous event loop.

Enhancements:
- Preserve subprocess output capture, failure handling, and the existing 30-second timeout while using asynchronous execution.

author: r2cuerdame
body:
## Summary

Closes #75 (Linear: [R2C-63](https://linear.app/r2cuerdame/issue/R2C-63/codesamplex-공개-evidence-데이터-라이선스기여-조건-결정)).

This PR formally establishes and documents the public Evidence and aggregated compatibility data licensing and contribution terms under **CDLA-Permissive-2.0** (Community Data License Agreement – Permissive – Version 2.0), clearly separating the four licensing layers of the CodeSampleX project:
1. **Source Code**: Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`)
2. **Public Samples**: MIT-0 default, unless upstream origin specifies otherwise (`docs/sample-lifecycle.md`)
3. **Evidence & Aggregated Compatibility Data**: CDLA-Permissive-2.0 (`DATA_TERMS.md`)
4. **Local Evidence**: Stays local, never collected (`contract.txt`, `PRIVACY.md`)

## Key Decisions Implemented

Following decision alignment on Issue #75:
1. **Prospective Data License**: Adopted **CDLA-Permissive-2.0** for all Community Peer Evidence and aggregate compatibility data (read endpoints `/v1/*`, `/v2/*`, findings, wanted board, shards, and snapshots).
2. **Pre-cutoff Legacy Aggregate Posture**: Applied prospectively from effective date `2026-09-21`. Pre-cutoff aggregates are published relying on `contract.txt` disclosure given at collection time.
3. **Contributor Grant**: Contributors grant CodeSampleX a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to store, aggregate, compute upon, and republish submitted anonymous peer evidence under CDLA-Permissive-2.0. Switching to `local-only` mode stops future uploads; previously incorporated aggregates cannot be retroactively unmerged.
4. **Attribution Boundary**: Zero attribution required on computed query responses / agent tool answers (no LLM prompts or editor banners forced to cite CDLA). Attribution is required only when redistributing raw datasets, snapshots, or mirrors.

body:
## Summary
Native inference can now load CUDA and TensorRT from configured locations without requiring SDK DLL directories in the process PATH. Resolve and retain native libraries through the shared Context, validate runtime versions (major mismatch is an error; minor mismatch is a warning), and remove NVIDIA load-time imports from the executable and TensorRT shim.

Unify build and runtime SDK settings in `platform.toml`, exposed through `--platform-config` and `AUDIO2FACE3D_PLATFORM_CONFIG`. Preserve environment-based discovery when locations are unspecified, and pass the selected environment to child tools. Replace user CUDA architecture settings and the fixed compute_86 default with the lowest generic PTX target supported by nvcc at or above the kernels' verified baseline. Update CLI, CI, configuration tests and deployment documentation.

## Validation
- Windows x64/MSVC, CUDA 12.9 and TensorRT 10.16.1: formatting, workspace all-feature Clippy, configuration tests and release builds passed.
- Native library tests: 223 passed, 6 ignored. All four CUDA kernels compiled to compute_50 PTX; Regression and Audio2Emotion inference passed.
- Loader fixtures cover failures, version checks, concurrent initialization, resource lifetime and coexistence with a host using a statically linked CUDA Runtime. Earlier numerical captures matched the migration baseline.
- Latest UE 5.8 integration: WAV, SoundWave and Burst requests, twice each. All six completed playback with 157 frames, 52 weights, 166,958 audio bytes and zero receive-validation errors. No ACE plugin code changes were needed.

## Limits
Linux remains experimental; native Linux builds and GPU inference are unverified. Startup on a machine without an NVIDIA driver is unverified. The full performance gate remains inconclusive because repeated measurements crossed existing thresholds inconsistently; this PR does not claim a stable performance-gate pass. UE testing verifies transport and playback events, not subjective lip-sync quality.

🛡️ Sentinel: [security improvement] Clean up FastAPI security middlewares and config validators

**Severity:** LOW/MEDIUM (Security Hardening / Code Quality)
**Vulnerability:** Redundant, misconfigured, or overriding security middleware assignments (`CORSMiddleware`, `TrustedHostMiddleware`) and Pydantic validators for CORS/Host configs could lead to silent validation bypasses or unexpected runtime behavior for DNS rebinding/CORS checks.
