author: tushige
body:
## Problem

The module lab and its lint fences are the contract the building blocks get built against, and four gaps in them would each cost real work to undo later.

- **A demo could start a real game from the hidden page.** `no-restricted-imports` visits import and export declarations and nothing else, and a block hands the lab its demo as a dynamic `import()` — exactly the shape the fence cannot see — so `demo: () => import('../../boot')` would open a socket and start a real game from a page that is supposed to talk to nothing, with lint and every other check green.
- **A block could reach into another block's inner files.** The sibling-block expression assumed a block's file always sits two folders down, so it refused `../fixtures/x` and `../modules/live-grid` from the lab's own folder — where the demo wrappers go — and let `../other/inner/file`, `../../modules/x/y/z` and `../modules/other/inner` straight through.
- **Every block's branch would have had to edit the same two lines.** `apps/web/test/lab.test.ts` pinned all seven blocks as not built yet, by listing seven `undefined` demos and counting the words "not built yet" on the page, so the first block to be built would have had to change both — and the six after it would collide there.
- **`/lab` could quietly serve the game's page.** Nothing looked at the built lab page. The service answers with its one page for anything it cannot find, so a build that stopped emitting `apps/web/dist/lab/index.html` would serve the *game* at `/lab` on the public address — which starts a real game — while every check stayed green.

## What this adds

- A second fence, by shape rather than by name, on the folders that hold the blocks, their stand-in sources and the lab: a dynamic import of boot, the store, the page's socket feed, `autoStart`, `App` or the shared package's engine entry is refused, while the shapes a demo actually loads are left alone — another block through its `index` or its `fake`, the file's own folder, and the client-safe entry points including `@strike-desk/shared/feed`. It is set on both configuration blocks that cover those files, because a later block replaces a rule's options rather than adding to them.
- A sibling-block expression that reads the specifier rather than guessing how deep the importing file sits, so a block, a stand-in source, `lab/` and `lab/modules/` all get the same answer, and a folder that is not a block (`fixtures/`, `lab/`) is no longer mistaken for one. The comment above it now says what it matches and which folders it has to be told about.
- A lab test that no longer tracks which blocks are built: it pins the seven ids, their order, that ids and places are unique and that every entry is well formed — a block either has no demo or loads one. The two states are pinned on stand-in blocks instead, so a block turns itself from a placeholder into a built one by editing its own file and nothing else.
- Two checks on the built artefact, in `scripts/check-web-bundle.mjs` beside the engine-marker check that was already there: the lab's page must exist and be the lab's page, and nothing the lab loads — the script it runs and the shared chunks it preloads — may hold the key the page's socket feed keeps its session under. The game's own page must hold that key, so the search cannot pass by going stale. CI already runs this script, so no workflow step was added.

## Evidence

Every shape below was run through the repository's own `eslint.config.js`, from four paths: a block file, a stand-in source, a `*.lab.ts` and a file directly in `lab/`. All four paths agreed on every row, before and after.

Dynamic imports, before — every one of them allowed:

```
shape                             | want   | result
../../boot                        | refuse | allowed  <<< WRONG
../../store/hooks                 | refuse | allowed  <<< WRONG
../../feed/wsFeed                 | refuse | allowed  <<< WRONG
../../autoStart                   | refuse | allowed  <<< WRONG
../../App                         | refuse | allowed  <<< WRONG
@strike-desk/shared/engine        | refuse | allowed  <<< WRONG
@strike-desk/shared/engine/market | refuse | allowed  <<< WRONG
52 CELL(S) WRONG  (13 shapes x 4 paths)
```

Dynamic imports, after — 27 shapes x 4 paths, including the legal ones
(`../../modules/live-grid`, `…/index`, `…/fake`, `./fake`, `./inner/thing`,
`@strike-desk/shared/feed`, `/protocol`, `/money`, `react`):

```
ALL 108 CELLS AS EXPECTED
```

Sibling blocks, before — refusing legal shapes and letting inner files through:

```
shape                           | want   | result
../other/inner/file             | refuse | allowed  <<< WRONG
../../modules/x/y/z             | refuse | allowed  <<< WRONG
../modules/other/inner          | refuse | allowed  <<< WRONG
../../../modules/other/inner    | refuse | allowed  <<< WRONG
../modules/live-grid/inner/file | refuse | allowed  <<< WRONG
../fixtures/x                   | allow  | refused  <<< WRONG
../modules/live-grid            | allow  | refused  <<< WRONG
../../fixtures                  | allow  | refused  <<< WRONG
../../styles.css                | allow  | refused  <<< WRONG
../other/index.ts               | allow  | refused  <<< WRONG
57 CELL(S) WRONG  (32 shapes x 4 paths)
```

Sibling blocks, after — the same 32 shapes:

```
ALL 128 CELLS AS EXPECTED
```

The two fences were also checked against each other: the same specifier now gets the same answer written either way, `./store` and `./feed` included. Three shapes read differently on purpose and are left that way — a stand-in source refuses `react` (that is the React-free fence), and an extension-bearing *static* specifier such as `../../boot.js` is a separate matter this change does not touch.

`eslint --print-config` on a store file, `App.tsx`, a block file, a `fake.ts`, a `*.lab.ts`, a file in `lab/` and a file in `packages/shared/src` confirms nothing lost an option it had before. The store file and `App.tsx` are untouched; the shared package keeps all four of its determinism selectors; the block, stand-in and lab files keep both import groups and gain the new one. The only entry that goes away is the sibling expression that was replaced.

The lab test was checked by flipping one block to built and running both versions of the file against it. The old one fails in the two places the collision would have happened:

```
AssertionError: expected [ undefined, undefined, …(5) ] to deeply equal [ undefined, …(6) ]
  apps/web/test/lab.test.ts:51

AssertionError: expected 7 to be 8 // Object.is equality
  apps/web/test/lab.test.ts:91
```

The new one passes with that block built and with it a placeholder, unchanged either way.

The artefact checks were each broken on purpose and put back. With the built lab page removed:

```
BUNDLE FAIL: the build left no lab/index.html, so /lab would answer with the game's page — which starts a real game.
```

With the session key planted in one of the lab's scripts:

```
BUNDLE FAIL: the lab loads assets/lab-Bm6d46fJ.js, which holds "strike-desk.session": the lab has pulled the running game in.
```

And with the key renamed in the game's own script, so that finding nothing would have proved nothing:

```
BUNDLE FAIL: none of the game page's 2 script(s) hold "strike-desk.session", which the page's socket feed keeps its session under. The check was looking at the wrong or a stale build, or the key was renamed, so its result means nothing.
```

`pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm vitest run` (706 tests, 33 files), `pnpm run build`, `node scripts/check-web-bundle.mjs` and `node scripts/smoke.mjs` all pass on this branch.

author: foo-ogawa
body:
Fixes #97. A regression I shipped in 0.16.22 with the `DO` block analysis.

## What was broken

`stmt_location` and `stmt_len` count **bytes**; `statementText` passed them to `String.prototype.slice`, which counts UTF-16 code units. Any multi-byte character earlier in the file pushed the two apart, so the text handed to the PL/pgSQL parser was cut at the wrong place. Confirmed on the reported input: for `-- コメント\n`, the parser reports `stmt_location: 16` (bytes) while the JavaScript string is 8 units long.

The result was that a migration got its dependencies or not depending on the language its comments were written in. Measured on three files (create table / `DO`-wrapped GRANT behind a Japanese comment / genuinely broken `DO` body):

```
0.16.23   3 files, 0 deps, 3 leaves
          ⚠ 2 file(s) hold SQL the analyzer cannot read ...
            20260302_100000__wrapped.sql        ← not broken at all
            20260303_100000__broken.sql

0.16.24   3 files, 1 deps, 2 leaves
          ✗ 1 file(s) carry a body the parser rejected. Their dependencies are missing, not absent:
            20260303_100000__broken.sql — DO block: syntax error at or near "THIS"
```

## What changed

1. The statement text is cut out of the UTF-8 bytes.

2. A rejected body is no longer counted as `unanalyzedBlocks`. That bucket meant "this SQL does not exist until run time" (dynamic `EXECUTE`), and folding a parser rejection into it is what made the wrong cut invisible — the output above shows the two cases side by side under one heading, with nothing to tell them apart. `FileDeps.parseFailures` now carries the reason the parser gave, and `deps` prints those files separately, saying the dependencies are missing rather than absent. The same applies to a `LANGUAGE sql` body that does not parse. Neither changes the exit code.

3. The regression fixtures carry multi-byte text now — before, after, between and inside statements, plus a trailing `DO` block with no closing semicolon, which is the one case where `stmt_len` is absent and the slice runs to the end.

## Verification

- 547 unit tests pass (12 new).
- Negative controls: restoring the UTF-16 slicing turns 6 tests red; swallowing the `DO` body failure turns 2 red; swallowing the `LANGUAGE sql` body failure turns 1 red. All green again once restored.
- lint, typecheck, `contract:generate` diff, `dsl:generate --check`, `version-sync --check`, build, bundle tests, `npm audit` pass locally.

## Note on how it got through

The analyzer had ASCII-only fixtures, and the failure was indistinguishable from the "dynamic SQL" case it was bucketed with — a silent zero dressed as an expected limitation. Point 2 above is the part that makes the next one visible.

author: loverhythm1990
body:
## Summary

The combined CLI and Edge build enables multiple rustls providers, causing released Edge binaries to panic during TLS initialization. This PR explicitly selects Edge's ring provider and fixes tool settlement and result persistence on connection failure, preventing orphaned child processes, lost completed results, and reconnect loops caused by oversized results.

- Every Edge connection exit cancels and awaits its tool executions. Settlement drains the completion queue and persists actual results before reconnecting. A journal write failure stops further appends while still unblocking producers.
- The journal uses the server-owned 256 KiB complete WebSocket-message limit, including identity, generation, metadata, and JSON escaping. Oversized results become durable `outcome_unknown` records; legacy outbox entries are repaired on recovery and never re-executed.
- The release workflow runs direct and HTTP CONNECT TLS probes after the combined CLI/Edge build. They verify that Edge reaches the handshake, rejects an untrusted certificate, and does not panic while selecting its TLS provider.

## Related issue

Fixes matrixorigin/matrixflow#17717

Related: matrixorigin/matrixflow#17686. The MOI frontend bundle installation and managed-environment delete-and-recreate guidance are in matrixorigin/matrixflow#17724. This PR does not modify or upgrade OpenShell; in-place upgrades that preserve identity and files are out of scope.

## Change type

- [ ] Feature
- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Refactor or performance improvement
- [x] Test
- [x] Build, CI, or maintenance

## User and compatibility impact

After updating a local Runner, users stop the old process and reconnect. Managed Runners use a new image through the MOI-guided backup, deletion, and recreation flow. There is no protocol-version or database change, and existing journals remain recoverable.

`timeout_secs` requests cancellation and waits for the executor's bounded cleanup; it is not an executor-independent hard upper bound. Executors must observe cancellation and release child processes. This contract is documented so a dropped future and immediate reconnect cannot violate side-effect isolation.

## Architecture and complexity delta

- Canonical owner changed or extended: `EdgeInvocationJournal` owns persistence and replay; the protocol module owns the shared message budget; existing executor and shell owners handle cancellation and child-process cleanup.
- Existing implementations and callers searched: Edge connection loop, runtime process authorization, shell execution, journal, server WebSocket handler, and combined release workflow.
- Superseded code, states, tables, shims, or self-only tests removed: detached task spawning and timeout-driven future drops are removed. The complete-message budget replaces the body-only write budget; the former body limit remains only for legacy-format read validation.
- If parallel implementations remain, their boundary and retirement condition: no parallel executor or upgrade service was added.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed.
- `python3 scripts/ci/validate_repository.py`: passed; the new probe is tracked with mode 100755.
- `cargo test --locked -p astra-edge --bin astra-edge --no-default-features --target-dir /Users/lr90/runtime-agent/Astra/target --quiet`: 64 tests passed.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p astra-edge --bin astra-edge --no-default-features --target-dir /Users/lr90/runtime-agent/Astra/target -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo build --locked --no-default-features -p astra-cli --bin astra -p astra-edge --bin astra-edge --target-dir /Users/lr90/runtime-agent/Astra/target`: passed. The macOS linker emitted a non-failing CLI unwind-info-size warning.
- `python3 scripts/ci/probe_edge_tls.py /Users/lr90/runtime-agent/Astra/target/debug/astra-edge`: both direct and HTTP CONNECT probes rejected the untrusted certificate without a provider panic.
- Public entrypoint exercised: the actual Edge CLI TLS handshake, local WebSocket registration, tool dispatch, abnormal disconnect, reconnect replay, and ACK.
- Unhappy paths exercised: normal and managed Bash cancellation with child-process cleanup, full completion queue, journal write failure, exact complete-message boundary, UTF-8 and JSON escaping, legacy outbox recovery, generation growth, and stale ACK.
- Database verification: N/A; this change has no database modifications.
- A successful trusted-WSS registration, four-platform release builds, the full workspace offline/online/contract matrix, and deployment have not been run. CI and QA cover those stages. The TLS probe proves certificate rejection and provider initialization only; it does not replace successful-registration acceptance.

author: dangkhoi88x
body:
> **Correction, after this merged.** The claim below that the large logos were "most of why the Speed Index sat near 5s" was wrong. Measured on the live site afterwards (three Lighthouse runs each side): the logos went 279 KB → 42 KB, but the score, LCP and Speed Index stayed within run-to-run noise (77 → 76, 5.17 s → 5.40 s, 4.86 s → 4.95 s). The bytes saved are real; the late paint is caused by something else. The code comment is corrected in #103.

## Why

Lighthouse on the **live** site (3 runs, mobile) gave a median score of 77, against 99 locally. The largest difference was one thing: the ticker's coin logos.

The ticker draws each logo at **15×15 px**, but CoinGecko's markets endpoint names its **250×250 "large"** file. On the live site the 15 of them came to **287 KB** — more than the page's own script, stylesheet and HTML put together (~56 KB) — and the last one arrived **13.5 s** into a mobile load. That is most of why the Speed Index sat near 5 s there.

## What

The same file exists at 50×50 under `/small/`, which is still sharp at twice the icon's size on a retina screen. `ticker.js` rewrites the URL:

- **Only a URL of exactly CoinGecko's shape** (`coin-images.coingecko.com/coins/images/<id>/large/…`) is rewritten; anything else is used as it came.
- **A missing small variant falls back to the named file, once** — the comparison in `onerror` stops a second failure from looping.

## Measured

On the 14 logos the ticker currently shows, each fetched both ways:

| | total |
|---|---|
| `large` (250×250) | 272 KB |
| `small` (50×50) | **35 KB** |

**−88%.** Checked in the running page: all 28 icons (the strip is drawn twice for its loop) point at `/small/`, load at 50×50, and none fall back.

## Not in this PR

The live LCP element is the first-visit tour's text, which appears once the script bundle has run — so on slow mobile it waits on the network regardless. Rendering it without JavaScript would need the page to know it is a first visit before `localStorage` can be read, so there is no clean fix yet and this does not attempt one.

Frontend only; no Java changed.

author: xuzhougeng
body:
Manual `/compact` and the compact dialog always promised a checkpoint plus retained tail, but the pipeline still stopped at prune-only whenever tool/media tombstones already fit under the 80% target. On large-window models that left model view looking like the original transcript, with no `[context summary checkpoint]`.

Switching the session model also did not compact, and there was no idle prompt to fold a conversation that had been sitting for a day.

## Changes

- Compact dialog is two modes: **Regular compact** (prune-only, no instruction field) and **Semantic compact** (optional instruction, always installs a checkpoint + short tail).
- `/compact` is regular. `/compact --semantic [instruction]` forces semantic. A bare `/compact <instruction>` still opens the semantic path.
- Overflow recovery opens on semantic compact so "compact and continue" can actually shrink the working set.
- Settings → Conversation: **Semantic compact when switching models** (off by default) and **Prompt for semantic compact after idle hours** (default 24; 0 disables).
- Native English strings and settings-nav aliases regenerated.

## Verification

- `cd ui && cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passed.
- `cargo test -p wisp-core prune_only_intent_skips` and `forced_semantic_compaction_runs_when_prune_already_fits` passed.
- `cargo test -p wisp-tauri compact_command --lib` passed.
- Playwright `compaction-undo.spec.ts -g "slash compact opens|regular compact sends"`: 2 passed.
- Playwright session-settings tests for auto-compact and the new model-switch/idle controls passed.

## Manual smoke

- [ ] Open Compact. Confirm regular has no instruction field and leaves user/assistant turns in model view with archived tool rows.
- [ ] Choose Semantic compact (optionally with an instruction). Confirm model view shows a checkpoint at the top and a short tail.
- [ ] `/compact preserve QC blockers` opens semantic with that instruction filled in.
- [ ] Enable **Semantic compact when switching models**, switch models on a non-empty conversation, and confirm a semantic compact starts.
- [ ] Set idle hours to 24, open a conversation whose last activity is older than that, and confirm the prompt. 0 should not prompt.

## Limitations / follow-up

- Automatic 80% compact is unchanged: prune first, semantic only if still over target.
- The idle prompt is a one-shot per session in the current window; it is not persisted across app restarts.
- Browser tests use the mocked Tauri bridge. Native desktop with a private database was not retested in this change.

The isolated FFT mesh fails the dense-cluster force gate. Add an opt-in `--near-field` strategy that subtracts each nearby CIC pair contribution and replaces it with the exact Plummer pair force, while preserving the original mesh results and unchanged accuracy gates.

The bounded experiment includes mixed near/far pairs and a cutoff-crossing adversary. At 65³ the corrected force fixtures pass; the original cluster still fails at 5.833% RMS. Correcting every cluster pair reconstructs direct forces at extra cost, and the hard cutoff introduces a measured force discontinuity. This is a reference experiment, not a trajectory-qualified or faster backend.

Validation: ten pinned-NumPy tests pass, including analytic pair forces, no double counting, unchanged far-pair behavior and CLI decisions. A three-sample, 30-row local run retains all timings and failure decisions; original fixture baseline arrays are identical to the prior report. No KSP launch or installation.

author: rstuhlmuller
body:
Replace the chart's `KubeMemoryOvercommit` rule with a non-HA policy: warn when memory requests exceed total allocatable memory for 10 minutes. Current requests of 22.862 GiB against 30.402 GiB capacity evaluate clear; real overcommit still warns. Disable only the replaced chart rule, preserving pressure, usage, readiness, and unschedulable-Pod alerts.

Also suspend Dispatcharr and AFFiNE, including their dedicated PostgreSQL instances and AFFiNE Redis, to release 3.50 GiB of requests. Apps stop before databases; all six PVCs remain retained. Document resume steps and exclude suspended AFFiNE from its database alert and application probes while preserving other checks.

The underlying largest-node-loss shortfall falls from 7.363 GiB to approximately 3.863 GiB. The warning policy explicitly accepts that risk; this does not restore failover capacity. Ephemeral Redis queues are cleared by suspension; durable data remains retained.

Validation:
- Full static gate and rendered Conftest policies passed.
- Pinned Prometheus chart plus custom manifests render exactly one memory-overcommit rule; seven Promtool cases cover current/projected/exact capacity, real excess, firing delay, recovery, and cluster isolation.
- Pinned Dispatcharr/Grafana charts and Kustomizations rendered; five zero-replica workloads, shutdown ordering, and unchanged claim definitions verified.
- Server-side dry-run diffs passed for the alert and both apps; StatefulSet retention and all six Bound PVCs checked before rollout.
- AFFiNE probe regression, Grafana PromQL fixtures, YAML/Markdown lint, ShellCheck, and whitespace checks passed.

After merge, verify Argo CD sync, absent app/database Pods, unchanged Bound PVC identities, and one healthy memory rule with no pending/firing alert while requests fit total capacity. Keep the accepted node-loss shortfall documented.

author: youngsofun
body: I hereby agree to the terms of the CLA available at: https://docs.databend.com/dev/policies/cla/ ## Summary Follow-up to #20542. Adds lineage support for materialized views, modelled on the existing View support but with the addressing rules a materialized view actually needs. A materialized view is defined by a query like a View, but unlike a View it is a real Fuse table with a **persisted logical schema** (`MVDefinition.logical_schema`) and a **source binding pinned to the source table id**. Those two facts drive the design: | | VIEW | MATERIALIZED_VIEW | |---|---|---| | lineage_kind of the definition edge | `CREATE_VIEW` | `CREATE_MATERIALIZED_VIEW` | | source addressing | NAME (definition stores names; rename breaks the view) | **ID** (binding is by id; rename only invalidates temporarily, drop+recreate invalidates permanently — a NAME edge would report a false active edge in the recreate case) | | target addressing | ID | ID | | target column addressing | NAME (ids are plan ordinals) | **ID** (logical schema is immutable) | | reads | boundary at view output columns | boundary at logical columns in all three bind modes (fresh / hybrid / live fallback) — never the physical state columns or `_mv_source_row_id`, never the source table | | DROP | tombstone immediately | tombstone immediately (cannot be undropped) | `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` intentionally produces no DML edge: the definition edge is the lineage of the object. Queries over the source table that the optimizer could serve from an MV remain attributed to the source table (lineage is captured from the bound plan since #20542). ## Implementation **sql crate** - `lineage.rs`: `QueryLineageKind::CreateMaterializedView`, `QueryLineageRelationKind::MaterializedView`; `Plan::CreateMaterializedView` extraction from the bound `query_plan` against `logical_schema`; `query_lineage_for_materialized_view()` for REFRESH LINEAGE. - `metadata.rs`: `ViewLineageSourceColumn` carries its relation kind so the same boundary mechanism serves both views and MVs. - `bind_materialized_view.rs`: `bind_materialized_view_with_mode` returns a `MaterializedViewBindResult` (adds the definition used); the explicit-read entry point annotates the logical output columns as an MV boundary. The optimizer-rewrite candidate path is untouched and gets no boundary. A schema/column-count mismatch only logs a warning — lineage must never fail the query. **service crate** - `lineage_log.rs`: kind/object-type names; comments documenting why MV source is id-addressed. - `interpreter_materialized_view_create.rs` / `_drop.rs`: target id fix-up after create (same pattern as views); deletion tombstone on drop. - `interpreter_refresh_lineage.rs`: `REFRESH LINEAGE FOR ALL VIEWS` enumerates both engines via a small `ViewKind`, resolves MV definitions through the enterprise handler, reports `MATERIALIZED_VIEW` in `object_domain`, and backfills `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ...` as the canonical query text. - `get_lineage` / `get_lineage_neighbors`: new `MATERIALIZED_VIEW` object domain; `COLUMN` domain also resolves MVs; MV schema comes from the stored logical schema, not `table.schema()`; MVs are excluded from the `TABLE` domain. ## Tests - [ ] Unit Test - [x] Logic Test - [ ] Benchmark Test - [ ] No Test - _Explain why_ All coverage is in the licensed `tests/lineage` suite: - `setup/08_materialized_view.test` + `check/08_materialized_view.test`: aggregating and detail MVs; fresh read, stale (hybrid/fallback) read, and a source query an MV could answer; `MATERIALIZED_VIEW` vs `TABLE` domain resolution; column traversal through logical columns; downstream fan-out; neighbors; no DML edge from `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW`; ID/ID addressing; source rename keeps the edge resolving to the current name; source drop+recreate makes the edge inactive; MV drop leaves no edges. - `legacy/01_view.test`, `refresh/03_view_boundary.test`, `check/07_refresh_legacy.test`: a legacy MV created on the lineage-disabled node is backfilled by `REFRESH LINEAGE FOR ALL VIEWS` and reported as `MATERIALIZED_VIEW`. Local validation: `cargo check -p databend-query --tests`, `cargo clippy -p databend-common-sql -p databend-query --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`. The sqllogic suite runs in CI (`test_lineage`, licensed). ## Type of change - [x] New Feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) ## AI assistance - AI usage: A coding agent drafted the implementation and the sqllogic coverage based on a design reviewed with the responsible human (addressing rules, refresh semantics, REFRESH LINEAGE scope). - Responsible human: @youngsofun - [x] The responsible human has read every line of this diff and can explain each change - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/databendlabs/databend/20550)

author: mr-chris-weaver
body:
The agent cell can now open a bounded, **approval-gated** request for the
Workload Lab Kubernetes tab's ServiceAccount token: it asks, waits for a person,
proves with two reads that the token is *scoped* rather than merely working, and
gives the slot back.

## The correction first

§5b said the Workload Lab's four credentials had no consumer and the candidates
were hypothetical. **That was never true of this tab.**
`examples/playbooks/k8s/ci-deploy-with-ps-token.yml` and `ci-read-with-ps-token.yml`
ship with it as *"the first Kubernetes plays in this repo that authenticate with
something they fetched themselves"*, with the 403 refusals written as in-play
assertions precisely so they cannot be skipped.

What those plays rely on is `PASSWORD_SAFE_CLIENT_ID` and its secret, read from
the run's environment — and that is what #910 removed for the agent. So this is
not the tab's first consumer. It is the first that **holds nothing in order to
retrieve**:

| | The shipped plays | The agent cell |
|---|---|---|
| Who retrieves | an Ansible run, as the dashboard | a principal on its own host |
| What it holds to do so | a Password Safe client id + secret in the environment | nothing — workload identity → Workload Credentials → the client pair |
| When | operator-triggered | on request, and only after a person approves |
| What it proves | the RBAC scope | the scope **and** that the retriever had no standing credential |

`workload_k8s_service` is candid about the axis it loses on: *"The vault
authenticates whoever can retrieve. Anyone who can retrieve **is** the workload,
as far as this mechanism can tell."* This **narrows** that — what reaches the
vault is no longer transferable — and does **not** close it. Every page says so.

## The demo

```
[agent] spiffe://weaverlab.test/agent/mcp-reader · requesting deployer access to https://10.0.0.5:6443
[agent] holding nothing: the Password Safe client pair came from Workload Credentials against this machine's own identity
[agent] spiffe://weaverlab.test/agent/mcp-reader · WAITING for approval (40s) — this agent cannot authorise its own access
[agent] spiffe://weaverlab.test/agent/mcp-reader · approved — request 77 released a token
[agent] spiffe://weaverlab.test/agent/mcp-reader · scope proved — namespace-scoped: it can list pods in app and is refused in kube-system
[agent] spiffe://weaverlab.test/agent/mcp-reader · request 77 checked back in
```

The cell's existing closing beat is a revoke. This one happens *before* anything:
an AI agent that asks for access to a production cluster and cannot proceed until
somebody says yes.

Exit codes are the punctuation — **0** proved the scope, **3** was never approved,
**4** means a refusal did not refuse, the one outcome that would otherwise look
like success.

## Three traps, each already written down in this repo

- **"Awaiting approval" arrives as a soft-failure STRING, not a status code.**
  `services/btapi_service.py` learned it: *"It was not possible to get a credential
  for Request ID: N"*, returned in the credential position on a successful call.
  Read as failure it makes the request unwaitable; read as a value it hands a
  sentence to an API server as a bearer token.
- **Never check in while pending.** `ps_api_service._request_credential` checks in
  when the credential does not come back — right for auto-release, and exactly
  wrong here: it cancels the very request a human is being asked to approve. It
  must still give up, or an abandoned request holds the account's slot and the next
  attempt trips the concurrent cap (4035), reporting the cap instead of the
  approval it waited on.
- **The credential is a JWT, not a `vmcli_` PAT.** `password_safe_credential`
  hardcoded that prefix — which had *also* been catching the soft-failure sentence
  by accident. The shape is a parameter now and that guard is explicit.

## The row holds two states, not seven

`requested` and `released` — the only two the dashboard writes. The waiting, the
approval and the probes happen on the host, and **the worker cannot report them
back**: its PAT belongs to a non-admin user and these routes need
`config_mgmt:write`. Granting it that so it could file progress would hand a
non-human principal more authority than this cell argues for, which is a bad trade
for a status field. The journal is the truth; the row answers "is something out
right now".

The row records the **request** and never the credential —
`test_workload_lab_governance`'s no-credential-on-row rule now covers `AgentCell`
too, rather than relying on that being obvious.

## Fossils corrected

`LINKABLE_MECHANISMS` gains `kubernetes` beside a new `SPENDABLE_MECHANISMS`,
because a link that confers capability and one that confers only accountability
must not read the same way back to an operator. The refusal text and the
`AgentCell` comment claiming no worker could spend any of these are fixed rather
than left standing — both were superseded by #910.

## Verification

`tests/test_agentcell_k8s_episode.py` is new (23 tests, exercising a fake Password
Safe and a fake API server over real HTTP). Five mutations were each confirmed to
fail the suite: accepting the soft-failure sentence as a credential, checking in
while pending, never returning the slot on timeout, accepting any failure rather
than a 403, and accepting a non-token.

Full suite from a clean clone with no `vm_cli.db`, CI's per-file loop: 0 failing.

### A testing defect found along the way

A mutation appeared to pass when it had not: a stale `.pyc` was being loaded,
because the mutated and restored lines were the same byte length so the cache did
not invalidate. Two consequences, both addressed:

1. One probe assertion was genuinely weak — no case had the allowed read *succeed*
   while the denied read failed with something other than 403, so `deny_code != 200`
   slipped through. A 401 on the deny path means a broken token, not RBAC working;
   that is now covered.
2. The #911 mutations were re-run with bytecode writing disabled. All four still
   bite, so that report was accurate.

The new test file's standalone runner also caught `SystemExit` escaping `except
Exception` and ending a run mid-file, which reads as a pass.

## Unverified

No Password Safe tenant, no cluster, no approver. The client paths are unit-tested
against fakes and that is all they are. **Without an approval policy there is no
wait**, and the best beat silently does not happen — so the worker logs which path
it took. Ships behind the existing `agentcell_enabled` preview flag; no new flag.

author: chrischall
body:
All three writes declared `readOnly: false` and nothing more, so the spec default published them as destructive. **None of them is.**

| | |
|---|---|
| `modify_collection` | adds **or** removes from your own collection — the tool is its own inverse |
| `submit_rating` | sets your rating; setting it again replaces it |
| `submit_tags` | applies your user tags; removable the same way |

Zero destructive is the right answer for this server, and the point of *saying* it is that a client can now tell this apart from a server where everything really is dangerous.

Worth noting these **do** touch a shared public database — MusicBrainz tags and ratings are visible to everyone. They're still additive, because the line is whether the prior state can be restored with these same tools, and here it can.

mcp-utils 1.0.0 → 2.2.0 is a no-op; typecheck and full suite green. Wire: read 6, additive 3, destructive 0.

author: ranxianglei
body:
## Background

Issue #494 reported two distinct problems:

1. **The 20-minute hang itself did not enter BCP.** Verified against the pi-agent-core agent loop (`agent-loop.js`): when an assistant turn ends with `stopReason: "aborted"`, the loop emits `turn_end`/`agent_end` and returns **without** calling `executeToolCalls()`. Both compress calls in the session have complete args but no `toolResult`, which matches this path exactly. Root cause is upstream of this repo: the provider stream (gpt-5.6-luna endpoint / network / adapter) stopped delivering events after the tool-call arguments were fully streamed, before the terminal `done` event, and no client-side stream timeout fired for 20 minutes. This PR does not address that layer (no raw stream capture exists to localize provider vs adapter).

2. **Independent BCP defect (fixed here):** the `compress` and `decompress` tools accepted the host `AbortSignal` but never checked it (`_signal` was unused). Once `handleCompress()`/`handleDecompress()` started executing, a user abort could not stop them — in-flight work, including state persistence (`runtime.save()`), could continue after the user pressed Esc.

## Changes

- New `src/abort.ts`: `assertNotAborted(signal)` throws `AbortError` (message `Operation aborted`, matching pi's own convention) at phase boundaries.
- Thread the signal through `execute(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx)` into both handlers; checkpoints at entry, after `await runtime.stateFor(ctx)`, and after `core.applyCompression` / before block-mode file writes.
- An aborted run now surfaces as an `isError` tool result instead of hanging or persisting half-applied state.
- New `tests/abort-signal.test.ts`: unit test for `assertNotAborted` plus e2e cases (pre-aborted compress rejects with AbortError and leaves the sidecar byte-identical; pre-aborted decompress rejects; live un-aborted signal still succeeds).

## Scope notes

- `search_context` / `acp_status` left unchanged: single fast phase, not named in the issue.
- `_onUpdate` progress reporting intentionally skipped: kernel phases are ms-scale synchronous work; emitting updates would only add transcript noise.
- No version bump (release-branch-only per project rules).

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm run build` OK (dist self-contained, acp-kernel inlined)
- New tests 4/4 pass; full suite failures in my sandbox are all pre-existing environment artifacts (read-only `/tmp`) — verified against a stashed clean tree

Fixes the BCP-side defect reported in #494.

author: charlesli1989
body:
## Summary / 摘要

`tabletop-rules/creation` no longer replaces the default character-creation runtime. The opening form (identity / personality selection) runs as usual, the point-allocation form layers onto the created character in the same turn, and worlds without allocatable attributes skip allocation silently instead of failing setup.

跑团插件不再替换默认创角流程：开场身份/性格表单照常出现，配点表单在角色创建的同一回合叠加弹出并经 `update-character` 应用；无配点属性（纯对话向）世界静默跳过，不再报错阻塞开场。

## Type of change / 变更类型

- [x] Bug fix / Bug 修复 (fix)

## Motivation / 修改原因（未建 issue，在此说明）

Found through real-world playtesting; two defects in the current design:

1. **Enabling the plugin replaced character creation.** `tabletop-rules/creation` declared the `character-creation` capability, so `char-creator/player-init` was suppressed whenever the plugin was active — the player lost the opening identity/personality form and only ever saw the point-buy form.
2. **Worlds without point-buy data failed outright.** Starting a session in a world with no `abilities`-category integer attributes and no imported rules (e.g. dialogue-focused worlds) errored with `This world needs tabletop-rules/rules/creation configuration with allocatable attributes.` and blocked the whole setup phase.

## How it works / 实现方式

- `creation` drops the `character-creation` capability (no replacement) and declares weak `after` edges on `world-data-provider` and `character-creation`, so allocation runs behind the creator.
- An optional `inputs.playerId` capability binding reads the creator's same-turn `playerId` output. The creator's guard buffers the player as a proposal (invisible to `list-characters` until the turn commits), so the id travels through the runtime output and the allocation form appears in the same turn the character is created — no dead turn between the opening form and the allocation form.
- Rules derive and freeze from the first setup execution (same-turn `worldSchema` input first, committed-schema fallback), independently of the player. This preserves the world-import zero-LLM contract pinned by `tabletop-world-init.test.ts`, which passes unchanged. The player only gates the allocation form and its `update-character` application.
- Worlds without rules skip silently (`creationRules` returns `null` instead of throwing); the check runtime stays inert without rules instead of failing every turn.
- `validateAllocation` no longer requires `characterName` (the opening form owns the name).
- Late enable during play only initializes the rules; restarts and re-enables stay idempotent via the `setup/offered` / `setup/allocated` markers.

## Verification / 验证方式

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm test` — all suites related to this change pass. Six unrelated packages fail identically on the base commit in this Windows environment (e.g. `desktop-config` asserts POSIX 0o600 mode bits) — pre-existing, unrelated, expected green on the Linux CI runner.
- [ ] `pnpm e2e` — not run locally (Playwright browsers not installed); the affected `tabletop-check.spec.ts` only mocks the check handler, whose rules-present path is unchanged.
- [x] Manual check / 手动验证: live mistport session — opening form → allocation form in the same turn → submission applies the points → game enters playing; a world without point-buy data skips allocation silently with no error.
- New unit tests (12) covering rule derivation, allocation validation, and both handler store surfaces (builtin full-DataStore vs community session-bound view — the latter difference is why the phase read passes the session id explicitly). The third-party ZIP integration suite (7) was reworked around a coexisting default creator; the setup-stage golden test was updated. Also green locally: `prettier`, `oxlint`, `pnpm check:i18n`, `pnpm validate:plugin` across all plugins, `pnpm check:boundaries`, `pnpm peers check`, `pnpm deps:check`, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.

## Docs sync / 文档同步

- [x] `docs/reference/plugins.md` — setup-stage ordering paragraph + tabletop reference-implementation paragraph
- [x] `docs/CHANGELOG.md` — Unreleased entry
- [x] `plugins/tabletop-rules/README.md` and `PLUGIN.md` — behavioral description

author: nigelnh
body:
## The failure

Production, from the Research Assistant panel — the user asked *"what time does the vn market start"* and got **"An unexpected error occurred while generating the AI response."**

```
httpx: POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"
[ERROR] app.ai.ai_router: AI stream failed [INTERNAL_ERROR]
  File "app/ai/ai_router.py", line 237, in event_generator
  File "app/ai/openrouter_client.py", line 244, in stream_chat
IndexError: list index out of range
```

The provider answered **200** — the request was fine. The crash was ours.

## Root cause

OpenRouter closes a stream with a usage/accounting frame carrying `"choices": []`, and routes provider keep-alives the same way. The parser did:

```python
choice = parsed.get("choices", [{}])[0]
```

`.get(key, default)` only substitutes when the **key is absent**. An explicit empty list is a *present value*, so it went straight into `[0]`. The loop's only handler was `except json.JSONDecodeError`, which does not catch `IndexError` — so one unreadable frame tore down a stream that had already delivered tokens to the browser.

Whether such a frame arrives depends on which upstream provider OpenRouter routed to. That is why the same question failed only sometimes — the previous message in the same session answered fine.

## The fix

A frame the parser cannot read is skipped. Only the transport ends a stream.

Fixed by class, not just the crashing line: `delta` and the choice itself arrive as an explicit `null` in real relay output, so both use `or {}` rather than a get-default. The non-streaming `data["choices"][0]` path is already covered by its `except (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError)` and degrades to a clean `AiProviderError` — no change needed there.

## Tests

7 cases, each **proven to fail before the fix**: the usage frame mid-stream, a null choice, a null delta, a frame with no choices key, and a trailing usage frame that must not discard a `finish_reason` an earlier frame established.

Verified by stashing only the source file: **5 fail without the fix**, all pass with it. (The other 2 shapes were already handled and stay green either way — kept as coverage against regression.)

```
backend: 1564 passed, 20 skipped
```

The 15 failures in `test_historical_volatility_service.py` / `test_quant_engine.py` are **pre-existing** — confirmed by stashing this change and re-running them on the same tree. They are date-boundary-dependent and unrelated to this PR.

author: hensleyl
body:
## What

Adds `.gh/` to `.gitignore`. Second half of #89, which ignored `.env` — that one
merged before this rule was pushed to its branch, so it comes as its own PR.

Unlike `.env`, this one is **not hypothetical**: `.gh/hosts.yml` holds this
repo's fine-grained PAT on disk, inside the working tree, right now.

## Why the delegate uses a config dir rather than `GH_TOKEN`

dsh scrubs credential-shaped environment names before every model shell call:

```js
// @deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess/lib/index.js:32
const SENSITIVE_ENV_PATTERN = /KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN/i;
```

`GH_TOKEN` matches on `TOKEN` and never reaches the sandbox. There is no config
knob to exempt it — `bash-local` exposes only cwd/timeouts/output caps, and its
README states environment layering is fixed — and the `$DSH_HOME/.env` layer does
not help, because the scrub runs after materialization (verified empirically).

`GH_CONFIG_DIR` does not match the pattern, and `gh` reads its token from
`$GH_CONFIG_DIR/hosts.yml`. The store is **per repo** so a delegate only ever
holds the PAT for the repo it is working in, rather than one global store handing
every repo the same token.

## Evidence

```
$ git check-ignore -v .gh/hosts.yml
.gitignore:10:.gh/	.gh/hosts.yml
```

Unignored before this change (`git check-ignore` exited 1, no output).

## Limits, stated plainly

The ignore rule is easy to mistake for isolation. It is not.

**dsh's sandbox confines writes, not reads.** Probed directly: a delegate in this
workspace can `ls ~/src`, read arbitrary home-directory files, and was denied
only on writes outside the workspace (`touch ~/…` → `Operation not permitted`).
So a per-repo store stops a delegate *accidentally* acting with another repo's
authority; it does not stop one that goes looking — and on issue #87 a delegate
did go looking for a credential unprompted. Real isolation between repos needs an
OS boundary: separate accounts, containers, or VMs.

No test: there is no behavior to assert, and `AGENTS.md`'s "show the test
failing" rule governs tests and bugfixes. The `git check-ignore` output is this
change's observable check.

author: kellylford
body:
NHL team schedules showed the 2025-26 season in September 2026. ESPN numbers a winter season by the year it ends in — the 2026-27 NHL season is `season=2027` — and that number was hardcoded (2026 for NHL/NBA/NCAA, 2025 for MLB/NFL) rather than derived from the date. The season picker had the same ceiling, so the current season could not be reached at all.

## What changed

Both platforms derive the season year per sport, in one place — `get_current_season_year()` on Windows, `Sport.seasonYear(containing:)` on iOS (which replaces three separate copies of the old rule):

- **NHL, NBA, NCAA basketball and hockey** — the year the season ends in, rolling over in July. ESPN flips well before the first game (the 2026-27 season was live on 2026-09-15, its schedule published in July), so the old iOS `month >= 10` was too late.
- **NFL, NCAAF** — stay on the previous season year through January and February.
- **MLB and the rest** — calendar year.

Also here:

- The WNBA is no longer treated as a year+1 sport on iOS. ESPN keys it to the calendar year it is played in (`season=2026` → 45 games from May 2026; `season=2027` → none), so its seasons were labelled a year behind and Oct–Dec requests pointed at an empty year.
- Team schedules fall back to the previous season when the current one is empty, covering the weeks between a season ending and the next schedule being published.
- NBA standings track the current season instead of the `season=2026` frozen into the URL.
- Season pickers now lead with "2026-27" on both platforms.

## Verification

- Windows unit tests: 141 passed.
- Live ESPN, Windows: NHL team schedule returns 88 games of 2026-27 (was the 2025-26 slate); picker leads with `(2027, "2026-27 Season")`.
- Live ESPN, iOS: headless harness over the real `Services`/`Models` — NHL `season=2027` "2026-27", Bruins 84 games 2026-09-30 → 2027-04-11; NBA 2027; WNBA correctly 2026 (45 games); MLB/NFL/NCAAF 2026.
- iOS simulator build succeeds.

Includes the v0.9.6 version bump, release notes and changelog entry, and the iOS bump to 0.8 build 40 for TestFlight.

author: bogdanovich
body:
## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default Steel cloud runtime provider behind the existing first-party browser broker and direct Playwright-library driver
- persist one opaque managed Steel profile, enforce bounded billing and cleanup, keep provider credentials and connection identities private, and expose typed provider failures
- extend the canonical smoke runner with opt-in billable cloud, profile-reuse, and handoff/resume suites

## Scope

Goal: complete Browser Continuation Phase 4 with one self-service cloud provider while preserving the existing model-facing browser tools and lifecycle authority.

The provider supports create, CDP attach, observe/action/artifact operations, operator live-view handoff, same-session resume, profile persistence, disconnect, release, timeout, quota, authentication, and outage handling. Cloud failures do not fall back to gateway or companion.

Non-goals: Cloudflare or another provider, credential injection, attached-user control, managed Playwright distribution, Phase 5 recipes, and Phase 6+ artifact expansion.

## Validation

- `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -tags goolm ./cmd/mintclaw/internal/agent ./pkg/browser ./pkg/config ./pkg/gateway ./pkg/tools`
- `make test-browser-smoke`
- real Chromium Playwright-library conformance and process-loss tests
- `make fmt-check lint-docs`
- `make lint`
- `node --check runtime/browser/playwright-library/sidecar.cjs`
- `sh -n scripts/browser-capability-smoke.sh scripts/browser-capability-smoke-self-test.sh`

Billable Steel smoke is intentionally post-merge and requires deployed operator configuration plus `--allow-billable`; no provider key is accepted on the command line.

## Operational safety

- Steel is omitted and disabled by default.
- API authority is loaded only from the private security overlay and is never serialized into public config, tool results, traces, or smoke reports.
- API and CDP endpoints, live-view URLs, provider session IDs, and provider profile IDs remain runtime-private.
- Session, inactivity, concurrency, and maximum billable lifetimes are mandatory and bounded; current broker capacity is exactly one session.
- Provider release is retryable, profile identity is crash-safe, and the provider hard timeout bounds abandoned work.
- Initial site authentication uses visible human login and provider-managed profile persistence; site credentials are not injected or exposed to the model.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [pyparsing](https://pypi.org/project/pyparsing) from **2.4.7** to **3.3.3**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.3.3
   ```
   ------------------------------
- Added support for Python 3.15.

- Parse actions that return a tuple value for a named expression formerly saved
  just the first value of the tuple. Now they return the entire tuple. Partially
  fixes Issue 401, PR 640 submitted by Vincent Gao et AI.

- Fixed CI unit test jobs selecting a tox environment with no test commands.
  The matrix and fallback now select `py-unit`, as diagnosed and proposed by
  glaziermag in issue 662; submitted by Neal Lin et AI.

- Fixed `Dict` returning an empty nested `ParseResults.as_dict()` as `[]`
  instead of `{}`. Incorporates partial solution submitted in PR 635
  submitted by Leo Ji.

  Additional fixes found as part of this work:

  - Removed vestigial unused `ParseResults._modal` attribute.

  - Fixed incidental bug when Dict tries to create a dict with a `ParseResults`
    value for a key (not hashable).

- Fixed `Word(..., max=n)` raising instead of matching up to `max` characters
  when the character set contained whitespace - `Word(nums, max=3)` and
  `Word(nums + " ", max=3)` gave opposite results on
  the same input. Now both forms match up to `max` and leave the rest for
  the next parser. PR 646 submitted by Andrew Chen et AI.

- Fixed `QuotedString` stripping whitespace that is part of a multi-character
  quote delimiter, e.g. the leading newline in `QuotedString("\n;",
  multiline=True)`. The delimiter was silently collapsed to `";"`, so the
  newline was ignored when matching. `QuotedString` now only rejects
  quote_char/end_quote_char values that are empty or entirely whitespace, and
  preserves any surrounding whitespace that is part of a valid delimiter.
  Reported in issue 492.

- Fixed `pyparsing_common.as_datetime` raising `Invalid date/time: microsecond
  must be in 0..999999` for valid ISO-8601 timestamps whose fractional seconds
  round up to a full second (e.g. `2021-06-15T12:30:59.9999995`, common in
  nanosecond-precision timestamps). The rounded microseconds are now added via
  `timedelta` so the value carries into the next second instead of overflowing
  the `datetime` microsecond argument. PR submitted by Andrew Chen et AI.

- Fixed debug output corruption when a parsed line contains a carriage return or
  other control character. `set_debug()` printed the source line verbatim, so a
  stray `\r` returned the terminal cursor to column 0 and overwrote the "Match ...
  at loc" text. Control characters in the debug line are now shown escaped, and the
  marker caret stays aligned with the match location. Issue 496, reported by
  Matthew Rowles.

- Fixed `ParseResults.copy()` sharing its results-name bookkeeping with the original.
  The copy got its own token list, but the per-name lists of matched occurrences were
  shared, and `insert()`/`pop()`/`del` renumber those offsets in place - so mutating a
  copy silently corrupted the original's results names, and `get_name()` on the
  original could return `None`. PR submitted by Andrew Chen et AI.

- Fixed bugs in `ParseResults.__add__()` and `ParseResults.__radd__()`, where
  erroneous `AttributeError` or `RecursionError` could be raised when adding
  `ParseResults` objects to non-`ParseResults` objects, instead of expected
  `TypeError`. PR submitted by Vincent Gao et AI.

- Fixed `ParseResults.__iadd__` (``+=``) leaking an `AttributeError` about a
  private attribute when the right-hand operand is not a `ParseResults` (e.g.
  `results += [1]`). It now returns `NotImplemented` so Python raises a
  `TypeError`, matching the `__add__` operator. PR submitted by Andrew Chen et AI.

- Fixed `pyparsing_common.as_datetime` parse action incorrectly scaling fractional
  seconds, writing milliseconds into the `datetime` microsecond field (for example
  "1997-07-16T19:20:30.45" produced microsecond 449 instead of 450000). Fractional
  seconds are now scaled to microseconds, matching `convert_to_datetime` and the
  standard library. PR submitted by Vincent Gao.

- Fixed matching bug in `match_previous_expr()`, when expression is modified with
  `leave_whitespace(recursive=True)`. Issue 633, reported by Ahmed Mohamed Abdelaal,
  PR submitted by fcardosojr18 et AI.

- Fixed `match_previous_expr()` failing to match nested or repeated expressions, so that
  it can now be used for matching nested open/close tags. A new guard parse action was
  added on every match of the repeated expression and never removed, so all of them ran
  on each attempt to match and only one could succeed; a second pair anywhere in the
  input would fail, and after a failed parse the expression would keep rejecting valid
  input. The pending matches are now kept on a stack, so an inner match pairs with the
  nearest enclosing one. Issue 560, PR submitted by Rajesh Kanade et AI.

- Fixed `Located` reporting a `locn_start` that included leading whitespace when the
  wrapped expression delegates whitespace skipping to sub-expressions (such as
  `MatchFirst` or `And`). The leading whitespace is now skipped before the start
  location is recorded, while `leave_whitespace()` expressions keep their whitespace.
  Issue 621, reported by MeanSquaredError.

- Fixed `ParseResults.deepcopy()` not deep-copying results names that referenced
  nested `ParseResults`. Only the token list was copied, so a named token still
  pointed at the original; changing the original (or the copy) was visible through
  the other when the token was reached by name, and the same token could differ
  when reached by index versus by name. Results names now reference the
  deep-copied tokens. PR submitted by Sarath Francis.

- Update type checking to use `mypy 1.20.0`.

- Up to 30% performance boost in `ParseResults.__setitem__`, which benefits all pyparsing
  parsers. Inspired by work proposed in PR 650, submitted by Justin Zhang.

- Significant performance boost in `ParseResults.__delitem__`.

- 5-8% performance boost optimizing `ParseResults.copy()`. Inspired by similar changes
  made by Evan Hubinger in https://github.com/evhub/cpyparsing.

- Minor performance improvement in builtin quoted string expressions, using `Regex` instead
  of `And`.

- Added `docs/pyparsing_class.md`, a more comprehensive class diagram capturing the major
  classes and modules in the pyparsing package.

- Updated `examples/http_server_log_parser.py` to use more modern Python and pyparsing
  features, including PEP8 naming, datetime and timezone parsing and conversion, and
  associated railroad diagram.

- Fixed `RecursionError` when constructing a bounded repetition with a large upper
  bound, such as ``expr[..., 1000]`` or ``expr * (0, 1000)``. The optional tail was
  built as a deeply nested chain of ``Optional`` expressions, which recursed the upper
  bound number of levels deep during both construction and parsing. It is now built as
  a flat, bounded ``ZeroOrMore`` loop, so construction and parsing no longer scale with
  the upper bound -- and the loop still exits early (stopping at the first non-match),
  preserving the original early-exit behavior. Reported in issue 332.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.3.2
   ```
   -----------------------------
- Defined pyparsing-specific warning classes so that they can be selectively enabled
  or disabled without affecting warnings raised by other libraries in the same Python
  app:
  - `PyparsingWarning` - base warning for all pyparsing-specific warnings (inherits
    from `UserWarning`)
  - `PyparsingDeprecationWarning` - warning for using deprecated features (inherits
    from `PyparsingWarning` and `DeprecationWarning`)
  - `PyparsingDiagnosticWarning` - warning raised when pyparsing diagnostics are
    enabled and a diagnostic feature is used (inherits from `PyparsingWarning`)

- Added `as_datetime` parse action to `pyparsing.common` - a more g

author: navoditk
body:
Page 4 of the pm-mechanics tour: the Claude Artifact preview — the fallback when GitHub Pages is unreachable, which makes it the only way into this material in some environments.

## What was already right

Coverage holds. **All 89 reference pages are present**, so the README's "every reference page" claim is accurate. And the in-artifact cross-referencing was already good: **447 working xrefs, zero broken**.

My first measurement said "2 anchors in a 103-page document" — that was wrong. Navigation is button-driven from embedded JSON, not anchor-driven, so counting `<a>` tags measured the wrong thing.

## The defect: 45 dead relative links

Two causes.

**The resolver only ran on reference pages.** The overview, the curriculum, and the eleven use cases are built through a different path and got *no* link handling at all, so their relative paths shipped as written — `../../notebooks/fixed_income/08_bond_math.ipynb`, `./mastery-guide.md`, and 43 others.

**And its rule for anything unresolvable was to unwrap to plain text**, on the reasoning that a dead link is worse than none. That reasoning is sound as far as it goes, but it discards the reference entirely — and for a reader who cannot clone the repo, being able to drill through is the whole point.

## Three outcomes, in order

1. **A page the artifact contains** → in-page `xref`
2. **A real repository file it does not contain** (notebooks, use-case READMEs, docs) → **GitHub link**, so the reader can open it
3. **Anything resolving to no real file** → still unwrapped to plain text, so a renamed target degrades to prose rather than becoming a confident 404

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Working xrefs | 447 | **448** |
| GitHub links | 0 | **49** |
| External | 53 | 53 |
| **Dead** | **45** | **0** |

No GitHub link points at a missing file.

## Writing the tests caught one more

`reference/glossary.md` is embedded as `start-glossary` but is **not** a section entry in the taxonomy — so checking `TITLES` alone sent every link to the glossary out to GitHub when it could navigate in place. Found only because the test asserted the behaviour rather than the implementation.

## Verification

10 tests: one per resolution outcome, plus four over the built artifact as a whole — no dead links, every GitHub link resolves, every xref targets a real page, and coverage matches the taxonomy. All 5 gates pass.

## Next step, needing Claude Code

Per AGENTS.md rule 17, this change touches `reference/`, `curriculum/`, and `use_cases/`, so the artifact must be rebuilt and **republished to the same URL** (`902379a8-…`), never a new one. That is a separate action after merge.

## Resumen ejecutivo ### Qué cambia Al generar una canción, si otra pestaña ya había añadido un cue (y su audio) en la misma historia, el persist local ya no tira ese cue remoto en el siguiente guardado. ### Para qué sirve #447 evitó borrar un *candidato* hermano en un cue que el snapshot local ya tenía. Quedaba el mismo agujero a nivel de *cue*: `overlayCueMusicCandidate` solo hace map sobre `live.music.cues`, así que un cue que solo existe en el servidor no se reinyecta. El rebase 409 sí escribía ambos cues, pero el store perdía el remoto y el PUT listo reescribía la biblioteca sin él. ### Impacto para el usuario Dos pestañas (o Wizard + Story Lab) sobre la misma historia ya no se pisan: un cue nuevo (p. ej. Créditos) y la canción que la otra pestaña acababa de guardar no desaparecen al terminar Generate en esta pestaña. ### Riesgo - [x] Bajo - [ ] Medio - [ ] Alto ### Estado - [ ] En desarrollo - [x] Listo para revisión - [ ] Bloqueado por CI o revisión - [ ] Requiere migración o acción manual ## Summary `overlaySavedCueCandidates` upserted saved candidates onto cues that already existed on the live snapshot. After a 409 rebase the retry PUT already contained remote-only sibling *cues* (and their songs); dropping those cues in the store let the ready/job persist PUT the library without them and delete the other tab's song cue. The overlay now prepends saved cues that live never loaded, then continues to upsert every saved candidate by id. Local-only cues and unsaved candidate rows on live stay. ## Overview 1. Tab B adds a Credits cue (or generates audio on a new song) and the server accepts `cue-credits-remote` with `song-remote-tab`. 2. Tab A generates on the existing Opening cue; CAS 409 rebases onto the remote project and the retry PUT keeps both cues. 3. Before this fix, Tab A's store mapped over live cues only (no Credits row). The later ready persist PUT Story X without Credits and deleted Tab B's cue and audio. 4. author: izzhackt
body:
Replies currently retain only their root parent, so a flat timeline cannot identify the specific reply being quoted without breaking the existing thread contract. Define an additive A15e contract: a private direct-quote map, versioned post RPC and timeline reader, while preserving command171, reader223, sparse seen225, old message rows and frozen V1 requests.

The plan defines full-input receipt identity (including the direct target), request/channel lock order, current bounded quote projection, tombstone behavior, strict V2 acknowledgements/decoding and ordinary scoped Auth. It also bounds future local QA to four new labelled messages and edit/delete of its own new reply. ROOT reserved227; apply waits for226 and a coordinated window. UI cutover remains A15f/A15g with Impeccable.

Documentation only. Validation: source comparison, official PostgreSQL17 references and git diff --check. No product tests, runtime changes, SQL/Auth/browser operations or deployment. Independent precode review and protected checks precede implementation.

body:
## What this changes

Three cosmetic defects on the dashboards, two of which nobody had noticed until we went looking at the third.

- The four markers on an entry cell's corner — tick, dash, pending question mark, days-late count — were three different sizes, and the question mark sat 3px right of the others on the week and three-month grids, wore a dark ring nothing else had, and drew *under* the current-week outline instead of over it. They now share a `--entry-badge-size` token and one position.
- The partially-settled dash rendered as the characters `068`. The stylesheet held a literal form-feed control character where `\f068` belonged — written by a patch script that read the backslash as an escape. Both instances removed; the file is clear of stray control characters now.
- On the week and three-month dashboards, columns before an account's start date are dimmed, but the category group bands stayed bright, striping every dimmed column. `createGroupHeaderRow` received a column *count* rather than the dates, so it could not tell which columns were in the past. It takes the dates now, as every other row builder already did.

## How it was checked

- the three badge rules and the late badge compared programmatically: same size token, same `right`, same `z-index`, no borders
- the console on the live page is what found the real cause of the misalignment — computed `right` was −5px for the green pair and −8px for the pending one, because the scoped override that pulls markers inward on the narrower grids listed every marker except that one
- both inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check` after stripping Jinja — the check that exists because an unescaped apostrophe took out three dashboards in 1.42.9
- all 12 `createGroupHeaderRow` call sites updated, each of which was already passing `months.length`
- looked at on dev after a wsgi reload

- [x] Signed off
- [x] No inline styles; colours and the new size token come from `:root`
- [x] No Python, no migration, no dependency change

author: mrarejimmyz
body:
## Summary
Master orchestrator now includes `/api/cron/heartbeat-monitor` in its sub-cron list, so the watchdog fires on every master tick alongside the other 10 crons.

Without this, `heartbeat-monitor` (shipped in PR #191) would only run if separately registered as its own schedule in `jobs.zkward.com` — but the current dispatch model uses a **single** `master` schedule that fans out via a hardcoded path list. Every sub-cron gets pinged every 5 min this way.

15s timeout is more than enough: heartbeat-monitor only queries `cron_state.cron:lastRun:*` and posts a Discord alert if any cron is > 3× its expected cadence stale.

Ships alongside the 2026-09-20 recovery from the 24h `jobs.zkward.com` outage. The HMAC secret mismatch that caused that outage is a separate out-of-band fix — needs the operator to sync the correct `JOBS_SIGNING_SECRET` value from the laptop's `.env` (repo `.env.local` was pre-rotation).

author: stevehuang0115
body:
## Summary

A dead or invalid Slack bot token now degrades the Slack integration instead of taking down the backend. Any Slack auth failure (`invalid_auth`, `token_revoked`, `account_inactive`, or a network error reaching Slack) is caught at the Slack boundary, logged once as `WARN Slack integration degraded: … — Slack features are offline, the backend keeps running`, and reflected in `SlackServiceStatus.degraded` / `degradedReason`. The process stays up; everything except Slack keeps working.

WI `ab063364` (P0, from Sam/TL, origin crewly-orc).

## Why the rejection escaped (the actual crash path)

The un-awaited promise is **not in Crewly code** — it is inside `@slack/bolt` 3.22.0:

- `new App({ token, … })` → `initAuthorizeInConstructor` → `singleAuthorization` (`App.js:199`) → with `tokenVerificationEnabled` (default `true`) `runAuthTestForBotToken` (`App.js:761–776`) calls `client.auth.test()` **eagerly** and parks the promise in `cachedAuthTestResult`. Nothing attaches a rejection handler until the first inbound event is authorized.
- With a bad token that promise rejects ~300 ms later. Its stack is `platformErrorFromResult → WebClient.apiCall → processTicksAndRejections` — no app frame — which is exactly the two `Unhandled promise rejection` entries in `~/.crewly/logs/crewly-2026-09-21.log` (01:44:32.434Z, 02:19:24.724Z), both between `Checking Slack configuration…` and `Crewly server started`.
- **Ordering:** Slack init runs at `backend/src/index.ts:2498`, `registerSignalHandlers()` at `:2613` — *after*. So at boot the rejection fires before the fatal `unhandledRejection` handler (`:3426`) exists, and only `logger.service.ts:116` logs it. That is why today's process did **not** die from it.
- **Whitelist:** the `:3426` handler shuts down for any reason not in `['Unhandled event', 'socket hang up', 'ECONNRESET']`. `An API error occurred: invalid_auth` is not on it. The same rejection **after** boot — reconnect (`attemptReconnect` builds a new `App`), re-auth, a token revoked mid-run — would have gone `unhandledRejection → shutdown() → exit → wrapper restart`. That is the real bug.

(Today's exit-code-1 loops are the stale-build guard `assertBuildProvenance`, by design; untouched.)

## The catch boundary that was added

**Primary — `SlackService.preflightBotToken()`** (`backend/src/services/slack/slack.service.ts`), called in both `initialize()` (socket path) and `attemptReconnect()` **before** `new App(...)`:

- Runs `auth.test` on a bare `WebClient` built from the bot token.
- **Any** failure → `markDegraded()` (one WARN naming Slack + "degraded", `status.degraded = true`, `degradedReason` = Slack error code from `data.error`, or the network code from `original.code`) and rethrows into the caller's *existing* catch. `connectSlack` catches it and returns `{ success: false }` as before; nothing escapes past `connectSlack`. In `attemptReconnect` the throw is classified by the existing `isFatalReconnectError` (auth codes stop the loop, network errors retry).
- Because the App is never constructed on an unverified token, Bolt's parked promise never exists.
- On success the verified `botId` / `botUserId` are passed to the App constructor, so Bolt's `runAuthTestForBotToken` resolves without calling `auth.test` (`App.js:761–762`), and `cachedBotUserId` is seeded. **Net API calls with a valid token are unchanged** (one `auth.test` either way); no behaviour change on the happy path.
- `describeSlackError()` (exported) extracts the code so the log names it.

**Secondary — process-level whitelist** (`backend/src/index.ts:3426`): the inline list moved to `NON_FATAL_UNHANDLED_REJECTION_PATTERNS` (`backend/src/constants.ts`) and gained `SLACK_PLATFORM_ERROR_PREFIX = 'An API error occurred:'` (the prefix `@slack/web-api`'s `platformErrorFromResult` puts on every platform error). Classification lives in `backend/src/utils/unhandled-rejection.utils.ts` so it is testable without booting the server. The whitelist approach is kept; **genuinely unknown rejections still shut down.**

## Deviations from the brief (documented as asked)

- The brief assumed an un-awaited `this.client.*` call in our init path and suggested a `swallowSlackRejection(label)` helper on fire-and-forget promises. Reading the init path showed the parked promise is Bolt's own (above), so the boundary is a **pre-flight before the App**, not a `.catch` on our promises. All six `void …()` sites in the Slack init path (`slack-initializer.ts:386/506`, `slack-team-channel.service.ts:336/367`, `slack-instance-registry.service.ts:224/491`) already try/catch internally — no live call site for the helper, so it was not added.
- `process-recovery.ts:240` (wrapper process, only sees its own rejections) and `safe-restart.service.ts:137` (logs only) were checked: neither has the exposure.

## Tests

- `backend/src/services/slack/slack.service.bolt-preflight.test.ts` — drives the **real** `@slack/bolt` App with only `WebClient.auth.test` faked (the escaping promise is Bolt's, so a Bolt stub would not reproduce it). Detection note: Jest's sandbox `process` never receives Node's `unhandledRejection` event (a listener installed in-test gets 0 calls — verified), but jest-circus hooks the real process and fails the running test with the rejection, so an escaped rejection is itself a test failure; a `try/finally` keeps the wait inside the right test.
- `backend/src/services/slack/slack.service.test.ts` — service contract against the mocked App: invalid_auth, token_revoked, account_inactive, ECONNREFUSED all degrade; valid token passes `botId`/`botUserId` and seeds the cache; missing `bot_id` passes no ids; **reconnect** with a revoked token builds no App and stops the loop.
- `backend/src/utils/unhandled-rejection.utils.test.ts` — classifier, incl. the negative case (unknown rejection stays fatal).

### Mutation check (norm-mutation-check-base-ref: backup → `git checkout origin/main -- slack.service.ts index.ts` → run → restore from backup, 2 files reverted / 2 restored, verified by `cmp`)

| | fix reverted to `origin/main` (5ee24fe6) | with fix |
|---|---|---|
| all three suites | **9 failed / 128 passed / 137** | **137 / 137** |
| `bolt-preflight` (real Bolt) | 3 failed (invalid_auth escapes; network error; cache seed) / 1 passed (valid token, `auth.test` exactly once — passes on both, as expected) | 4 / 4 |
| `slack.service.test.ts` new describe | 6 failed / 1 passed (`omits bot_id → no ids`, true on both) | 7 / 7 |
| negative test `unknown rejection stays fatal` | ✓ stays green | ✓ |

### Pre-existing failures, verified on a clean detached `origin/main` (5ee24fe6) worktree, not touched by this PR
- `notify-reconciliation.service.test.ts`: 19 failed / 15 passed on baseline — identical list.
- `slack-orchestrator-bridge.test.ts`: `Test suite failed to run — ReferenceError: DOMMatrix is not defined` from `pdf-parse` import (environment).
- `slack-initializer.test.ts` (same `DOMMatrix` import error), `index.test.ts` (1 test, `DOMMatrix`), `reproduce_no_text.test.ts` (1 assertion): identical **2 failed / 25 passed / 27** on this branch and on the clean baseline, same errors. Heads-up: `slack-initializer.test.ts` and `index.test.ts` passed at 50d790cd (my original base) and fail at 5ee24fe6 — introduced upstream between those two, not here.
- root `npm run typecheck`: 20 errors across 9 unrelated test files — the error list on this branch is byte-identical to the baseline's (diffed). `tsc -p backend/tsconfig.json` is clean; `npm run lint` 0 errors.

## Not changed
Token, `.env`, stale-build guard, Bolt version.

author: lohandiasf-ctrl
body:
Três mudanças no repasse por FSA, vindas do teste em produção e do uso real.

## ⚠️ Antes de mergear

`npm run db:migrate:remote`, para aplicar `drizzle/0039_fsa_groups.sql`. Ela **apaga e recria** `fsa_classifications` e troca `fsa_payouts` por `fsa_groups` — as duas tabelas estão vazias em produção (confirmado depois do teste de ontem), então não há dado a perder.

Merge sem a migration quebra a fila de repasse: o código novo procura `fsa_groups`, que ainda não existe.

---

## 1. O grupo é a unidade de pagamento

Duas limitações do modelo anterior:

- **Só dava para classificar dentro de um atendimento preparado.** Agora o usuário seleciona várias FSAs na fila de chamados e usa **"Agrupar para repasse"** na barra de ações em lote. Não passa pela operação ao vivo.
- **Um chamado que voltava para a fila sobrescrevia a passada anterior.** A FSA marcada como evidência, que ficou aguardando spare e depois foi atendida como atuação — às vezes por outro técnico — perdia a primeira classificação, e com ela um trabalho já pago. A chave agora é **(grupo, chamado)**: o mesmo chamado pode estar em vários grupos, um por passada.

O grupo define a faixa de preço: dois chamados na mesma loja, no mesmo horário, com o mesmo técnico, valem R$ 100 no total. A tabela calcula; a gerência confere.

Foi considerado agrupar automaticamente por técnico + dia, e o usuário escolheu o grupo manual. A diferença é de dinheiro: 4 + 3 + 2 atuações em três lojas rendem **R$ 370** por grupo, contra **R$ 270** com o dia numa faixa só.

Duas decisões que valem revisão:

- **O técnico vem do cadastro (`technicians`), não do texto do Jira.** O Jira manda o nome como texto livre, e o mesmo técnico aparece como "Carlos Antonio" e "Carlos Antônio" — o que partiria o repasse de uma pessoa em dois.
- **O grupo guarda a descrição e a loja de cada FSA** no momento em que ela entrou. O Jira muda de status e de texto; o que foi atendido e pago não pode mudar junto.

## 2. Improdutiva vira categoria, não desconto

A tela mostrava o valor de cada grupo **já com o desconto aplicado**, mais uma linha de desconto informativa. O total estava certo, mas quem lia de cima para baixo fazia `70 + 2,50 − 2,50 = 70` e estranhava.

Agora são três linhas que somam, sem nada a subtrair — **Atuação**, **Evidências**, **Improdutivas**. Uma atuação de R$ 70 que não saiu aparece como improdutiva de R$ 35. A conta não mudou, só a leitura.

Junto veio o vocabulário da operação: "serviço" virou **atuação**, e o botão "Não consegui resolver" virou **Improdutiva**.

## 3. Evidência não tem improdutiva

Entregar a evidência é o trabalho inteiro — ou saiu, ou vira atuação improdutiva. Isso corrige uma suposição do #98, onde evidência improdutiva caía pela metade.

O botão some da tela quando a FSA é evidência, trocar o tipo limpa a marcação, e o servidor recusa mesmo que a tela deixe passar.

Com isso a repartição entre produtivo e improdutivo só acontece em atuação, que **sempre divide exato** pela quantidade. Há teste travando essa propriedade.

---

## Estrutura

- `fsa_groups` substitui `fsa_payouts`; `fsa_classifications` passa a apontar para o grupo.
- A `0038` de ontem foi **removida antes de ir para produção**: ela adicionava uma coluna a `fsa_payouts`, que a `0039` apaga.
- `/api/active-attendances/[id]/fsa-payment` e `/api/fsa-payouts` deram lugar a `/api/fsa-groups`, `/api/fsa-groups/[id]` e `/api/fsa-groups/report`.
- O botão "Repasse" saiu do card de atendimento. A lista de grupos fica na `/financeiro`: quem montou o grupo vê os seus, a gerência vê todos.

## Verificação

259 testes, `tsc --noEmit` limpo, `oxlint` limpo nos arquivos tocados, `npm run build` passa com as três rotas novas.

O único aviso de lint restante em `bulk-ticket-actions.tsx` (supressão de `exhaustive-deps`) já existia antes deste PR.

**Não testado em produção ainda** — as rotas de grupo dependem da migration. Depois dela, vale repetir o teste de ponta a ponta de ontem com um grupo.
