author: ford442
body:
The studio layer on top of the C++-owned song (#95/#96), the grid write-back (#98) and SAVE .RBS (#99) — items 1–3 of the tracking issue plus the mixer-fidelity half of item 4.

## 1. WebMIDI input

`src/wasm/js/player-midi.ts` — no npm dependency, `navigator.requestMIDIAccess` only.

| Input | Target |
| --- | --- |
| Note on/off, channels 1–2 | TB-303 A/B `setStep` note, accent at velocity ≥ 100 |
| Notes on channel 10 | 808/909 drum bits on the current step |
| CC 74 / CC 71 | cutoff / resonance (`DeviceParamId` 1 / 2) |
| Clock, transport, everything else | ignored — we own tempo |

`mapMidiMessage` is a pure decoder; the decoded actions go through the studio view's existing `setStep` / `setDeviceParam` paths and land in the same inverse-patch undo stack as a click, so a mis-hit pad is as recoverable as a mis-click. C++ is untouched. While the sequencer runs, pads punch into the step you hear; stopped, notes step-record forward.

It sits behind a hardware-styled MIDI LED that is hidden — not merely disabled — where the API is absent (iOS, insecure contexts).

## 2. Shareable studio URLs

`src/lib/studio-patch.ts` — compact tuple JSON → raw deflate (**fflate**, MIT, no WASM) → Base64URL in `?p=`.

- Carries the *working copy* (edited steps + moved knobs), never the song, so nothing round-trips through Embind and TRAK automation is untouched.
- Layers onto the existing `?play=` / `?src=` deep link and keeps the `/rebirth_website` base path.
- Capped at 2048 encoded characters; over that the link is refused with a pointer to SAVE .RBS rather than emitting something a proxy would truncate.
- Applied once, after the deep-linked file has loaded. A corrupt `?p=` decodes to `null` rather than throwing.

## 3. Catalog-scale Play (fetch classification)

`rbs-init-errors.ts` gains `corp-blocked` / `not-found` / `http-error` / `offline` / `parse`, each with its own LCD copy in the same register as the existing init-failure reasons. Under COEP an off-origin file without `CORP: cross-origin` fails as a bare `TypeError` — previously indistinguishable from "offline", which is the wrong advice: a CORP block needs the file mirrored into the playable core, a 404 needs the catalog entry fixed.

Not in this change: the hosting/mirroring side is ops, and the player has no "load mod from catalog" path to gate — `.rbm` files only arrive through the local file input and drop zone (the `storage.1ink.us` references in the pages are download anchors, not player fetches).

## 4. Mixer fidelity (C++)

SIMD is deliberately **not** here — it is a compile-time fast path over algorithms that just changed, and these goldens are what it would be measured against.

- **PCF** becomes a documented 2-pole TPT state-variable filter in `synth/dsp/Pcf.h`, driven by all three song bytes. `envAmount` was parsed and then discarded; it now opens the corner by up to 3.5 octaves from an envelope follower, which is the pumping character the effect exists for. The old one-pole smoother could neither self-resonate nor track.
- **Delay line** is sized from the sample rate in `init()` instead of a fixed 20000 samples (~0.45 s @ 44.1 kHz), which silently truncated every tap past a sixteenth at slow tempos and would have clipped outright at 48/96 kHz. One main-thread allocation; `process()` still never resizes. The DELY `time` byte now selects a tempo-synced subdivision rather than being parsed and ignored.
- **Compressor** `ratio` and `attack` come from the COMP chunk instead of `kCompressorRatio` / `kCompressorAttack`.

Five new golden tests in `test_mixer.cpp`: a DIST/PCF/COMP fixture differs from all-FX-off by well over RMS noise; `envAmount` and the ratio/attack bytes each demonstrably change the output; a dotted-eighth tap at 80 BPM (24806 samples — past the old ceiling) lands where it should; and the `time` byte picks measurably different subdivisions.

## Testing

`npm run check`, `contract:check`, `wasm:test` (12 mixer cases, all green), `build`, `eslint`, `prettier`, plus 8 new browser tests in `tests/studio-midi-share.spec.ts` covering the MIDI mapping, patch round-trip, URL layering, the size cap and the fetch classification.

Unchanged pre-existing failures: the `playwright.config.ts` `webServer` type error, and the `wasm-assets` / `wasm-engine` / `wasm-save-rbs` specs that need `npm run build:ship` (Emscripten) to have run.

author: laughingman7743
body:
## WHAT

Add an internal version 5 Pub/Sub approval schema that pins the trial and its resource, image, manifest and schedule inputs. Derive helper traffic limits from that trial, use four application and three control Pod slots in shared cleanup, and retain the trial in final receipts even when stopped before service creation. Let a finalization retry match a receipt that differs only in the refreshed plans' observation time (`plans.at`), so a crash between the receipt write and the lock release can be retried instead of stranding the environment lock.

## WHY

The offline proposal could not previously round-trip through the shared approval model, and smoke's Pod ceiling cannot cover Pub/Sub's three running Flink Pods plus a terminating replacement and the control Pods. This prepares the internal contract for later delivery and orchestration.

Recovery's placeholder control record finalizes only a run that never reached service intent. A measured retry records that a run whose cleaned Pub/Sub portion the record omits conflicts again and deliberately retains both the record and the lock, so restoring the verified snapshot is a procedure admitted execution still owes.

The dollar cap remains unestimated and the total-request cap is not an aggregate meter. No approval-generating CLI, runner admission, supervisor execution, image publication or GCP/GKE run is enabled by this change.

Validation: the Tier-3 Python suite, the repository Python suite, real CUE Pub/Sub manifest tests, `just lint`, and `just format`. Required review rounds and aggregate CI are completed before Ready.

Closes #1417

author: mistermathcake
body:
The production deploy fails at `RUN npm ci` in the Dockerfile:

```
npm error `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json ... are in sync.
npm error Missing: openapi-types@12.1.3 from lock file
```

**Cause:** commit `7f30773` (Swagger UI) added `@apidevtools/swagger-parser`, which lists `openapi-types` as a peer dependency. The lockfile has no entry for it, so `npm ci` refuses to install. Nothing to do with the generated-document work.

**Fix:** regenerated the lock with npm 10.8.2 (the version in the Docker image; newer npm is more lenient, which is why it can pass locally):
- adds the `node_modules/openapi-types` entry (12.1.3);
- flips 6 `"dev": true` to `"devOptional": true` (npm's own change now that a peer dependency reaches them).

`package-lock.json` only (+13 / −6). `package.json` and `yarn.lock` are untouched (the Dockerfile uses only `package-lock.json`).

**Verification:** on `main` (d5064d5), `npm ci --dry-run` with npm 10.8.2 fails with the error above; on this branch it passes. The real Docker build and deploy have not been run.

> ## Review scope — read this together with #13609
>
> **This PR is the second half of one change set. Do not review it as a standalone diff, and do not produce a separate analysis for it.** #13609 (merged as `228e764257`) introduced the UI snapshot / SWR cache and the cross-runtime invalidation that this PR removes; all three findings below were filed against that PR, after it merged.
>
> Read on its own, this diff reads wrong:
>
> - the code **deleted** here — `SwrCacheInvalidated`, `publishInvalidation`, `applyRemoteInvalidation`, the echo guard, the remote-origin bookkeeping — was **added in #13609**. Its absence is the fix, not a regression or a lost feature.
> - the invalidation **moved** into `kit/src/utils/swrCacheMutationInvalidation.ts` is the same per-event namespace mapping #13609's bg listeners had. Judge it against those listeners, not against a blank slate — a namespace missing from the new module is only a bug if bg used to drop it.
> - the rules that now open the renamed skill are the contract the two PRs converged on; the reasoning behind each one lives in #13609's review threads.
>
> **For an AI code review:** take #13609's diff and its review threads as part of the context for this one, and report a single analysis spanning both PRs rather than two disconnected ones. Findings that only make sense against #13609's intermediate state (e.g. "bg no longer deletes") have already been answered there — check the thread before re-filing.

## Problem

Follow-up to #13609, which is already merged. Three review findings landed after the merge:

1. **[P1] The snapshot store's owner re-announced a removal it was told about.** Applying `SwrCacheInvalidated` recorded the removal and flushed, and every flush ended in `publishInvalidation`. The echo guard only covered the local listener and `originNodeId` only the sender, so with two foregrounds open — an extension popup and a side panel are both store owners — each treated the other's announcement as a new instruction and answered with its own, for the life of the pages. ([r4058098777](https://github.com/OneKeyHQ/app-monorepo/pull/13609#discussion_r4058098777))
2. **[P1] "Background removals never reach disk unless a live owner applies them"** — this one does not hold, and the reply explains why: every deletion path is reached from the UI (a `@backgroundMethod` the UI called, or a bg flow that first prompts for a password), and `emit` runs bg's local listeners *before* `broadcastToForegrounds`, so the announcement leaves while the caller is still awaiting the promise. ([r4058932588](https://github.com/OneKeyHQ/app-monorepo/pull/13609#discussion_r4058932588))
3. **[P1] "Fast Jotai hydration copies sensitive persisted state into the UI runtime"** — also does not hold as stated: `jotaiBgSync` calls `getAtomStates()` with no names, which returns every atom, and the RPC path then force-sets each one over whatever the fast path injected. The fast path is a subset of what already crosses. Travel Mode, the one case where the RPC path *does* narrow, is the one case the fast path steps aside for. ([r4058950599](https://github.com/OneKeyHQ/app-monorepo/pull/13609#discussion_r4058950599))

## Changes

**`fix: stop the snapshot store's owner re-announcing a removal it was told about`**

A removal carried out for another runtime is tracked and left out of the announcement.

**`refactor: let the UI runtime invalidate its own snapshot entries`**

The structural version, which removes the class of bug rather than the instance. bg dropped these namespaces on wallet, account and bookmark mutations and announced it across the runtime boundary; the entries are written by the UI runtime's hooks, so that gave one file two writers with no lock between the runtimes, and the announcement had to be answered by whoever performed the delete.

The mutation events already reach every runtime, so nothing has to cross for the cache's sake:

- New `kit/src/utils/swrCacheMutationInvalidation.ts` drops the same namespaces on the same eight events, keeping bg's per-event mapping and its `flushNow` — a force-kill must not leave a deleted wallet to be primed and painted on the next cold open. Registered at module load, because the events can arrive before the component mounts.
- bg keeps its own work (the account caches, the events themselves) and touches the store only for the perps snapshots it owns and writes. `ServiceDiscovery` only announces now; `ServiceE2E`'s `clearAll()` goes, since the `WalletClear` it emits is what drops the namespaces.
- That removes the channel: `SwrCacheInvalidated`, `publishInvalidation`, `applyRemoteInvalidation`, the echo guard, the remote-origin bookkeeping and the startup subscription.

**`fix: drop the cache at the call site that asked for the deletion`**

The listener above covers it, but only once bg's event has crossed back. The runtime that called `removeWallet` / `removeAccount` is the one certainly alive at that moment — it is awaiting the call — so it performs the drop itself, and a process that goes down in between cannot leave the deleted entity in the store. Both paths delete, and a delete is idempotent.

**`docs: rename the cold-start skill to 1k-ui-snapshot-cache and state its rules`**

The skill is about the cache, not only the cold start it makes possible, and its contract was scattered through the prose. Four rules now open it: the cache belongs to the main thread; a mutation refreshes or removes an entry rather than patching one, in the UI runtime rather than via bg; the first frame reads a record synchronously; and nothing sensitive is persisted in it.

## Invalidation coverage audit

Every SWR namespace, and what keeps it correct after a create / update / delete:

| How | Namespaces |
|---|---|
| The new module, per event | `walletList`, `accSelList`, `accSelValues`, `bulkCopy{Wallets,NetIds,Accounts}`, `bulkSendSeed`, `disHomeBookmarks` |
| The owning hook refreshes after the mutation | `unsMeta` (selector done handler, `AddedCustomNetwork`, AllNetworksManager's own hook), `unsValues` (deps cascade off `compatibleNetworks`), `recentNets` (`clearRecentNetworks` → `run()`), `swapHistoryPreviewList` (`RefreshSwapHistoryList` → `run({ alwaysSetState: true })`) |
| The key carries the mutable input, so nothing needs invalidating | `allNetCompat` (`enabledNetworkIdsKey`), `netContent` (`networkIdsKey`), `chainSelNets` (`networkIds`) |
| The screen removes its own key | `tokenSelectorView`, `specifiedTokenSelectorView`, `marketHomeStocks`, `marketHomeTokenList`, `marketStockVariants` |
| Retention + revalidation on mount (no local mutation) | `market*`, `swapStock*`, `perps*`, `earn*`, `borrow*`, `fiatCrypto*`, `disHomePage` |
| Persistence gated on status by design | `historyTxDetail` (`swrShouldPersist` only while pending, with polling) |

One namespace has no refresh point: `homeWalletTabs` (`homeWalletTabSupport`, keyed by `scopeKey` alone). If tab support can change with the enabled networks, a cold start after that change paints one stale frame before revalidation. Worth confirming separately; not touched here.

## Verification

### Unit
- `packages/shared/src` + `packages/kit-bg/src` + `kit/src/utils` + AccountManagerStacks + Discovery: **538 suites / 7372 tests pass**.
- New: 6 cases for the main-side invalidation module (per-event prefixes, `flushNow` counts, idempotent registration); `swrCacheUtils.test.ts`'s cross-runtime block rewritten to assert the cache publishes nothing at all (`spyOn(appEventBus, 'emit')`, zero calls); `ServiceDiscovery.test.ts`'s two cases now assert bg announces without touching the store.
- `yarn agent:check --profile commit` 9/9 and `--profile pr` pass.

### On device (iOS 26.5 simulator, this branch served by its own Metro)

The branch was confirmed live before measuring anything: the bundle fetched from this worktree's Metro contains the new identifiers, and an intermediate error box named `registerSwrCacheMutationInvalidation` at the top of its

body:
Closes #45.

## What this adds

`ProgressionCycleClientTest` — one automated scenario covering the whole roguelite
cycle against a real client and a real dedicated server:

lobby with an empty profile → a run restricted by what nobody bought → currency
granted inside that run → a real death → the lobby, with the run left behind and
the money kept → the shop, bought by clicking squares with the mouse → a second
run that is a genuinely new world *and* a better one.

The four pieces each had their own test already. None of them asked whether they
are one loop, and the seam in the middle — currency earned inside a run that is
about to be deleted, spent on a screen in the world that is never deleted — was
covered by nothing.

`docs/manual-smoke-test.md` is the same loop by hand, for playing rather than
proving.

## Executable acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Scenario |
| --- | --- |
| one scenario covers the whole cycle | all six, in order |
| integrated boundaries, not mutated state | `/mhr run start`, a real `kill`, real mouse clicks on the shop |
| persistent progression survives | `progression-outlived-both-runs-and-the-runs-did-not` |
| disposable run state does not | `dying-ends-the-run-and-leaves-the-currency-behind` |
| the second run is fresh | `run-two-is-a-fresh-world-that-has-what-was-bought` |
| a purchase changes the second run | same, two ways: the starter chest and the border |

Run 1 is the control for both purchases — no chest at all, and the tiny tier —
so neither can pass because a chest is placed at every run start or because the
border never moves.

## Verification

`scripts/dev.sh gametest` — green at `5bc711d`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 173 scenarios,
0 failures, on the eero-pc cluster. Since then only documentation, one javadoc,
one method's visibility and one import have changed, all compile-verified.

Both runs use fixed seeds (`45000001`, `45000002`), so the terrain the test
asserts against is the same every run. Freshness is still read off the record's
own seed and run 1's marker blocks, never off the seed argument.

Negative controls, both run through the real suite:

1. `WorldBorders.selectOwnedTier` made to ignore purchases → red, but
   `ShopClientTest` caught it first and aborted the run, so it did not prove
   anything about the new test.
2. `RunLifecycle.stripRunState` made to wipe the purse at the run → lobby door
   → **only** the new test went red, and its first failure named the cause:
   *"what the run paid must outlive the run: the purse should still hold 20 and
   the file says 0"*.

Both were reverted and the tree re-verified green.

## Notes for the reviewer

The shop-screen input helpers and the client-arrival waits were moved into
`TestShop` and `TestRuns` rather than copied. `ShopClientTest` and
`RunLifecycleClientTest` now call the shared versions; no scenario or assertion
in either changed.

[AgentDeck session](https://bazzite.taile8d16e.ts.net/chats/7a020ff0c39b442093fdce58796aed8e)

Three correctness lanes and six architecture dimensions. Verdict: **Questionable**
— one gated dimension (Use cases/UX, 80).

**Fixed:**
- *The blocking one.* `docs/manual-smoke-test.md` step 3 was wrong on the

**Deliberately skipped:**

author: jkrumm
body:
## What was wrong

`setup.sh` installs the self-healing watchdog into **root's** crontab. Cron's `sh` (dash) reads no profile, and `scripts/homelab_watchdog.sh` calls `op whoami` / `op read` at runtime — so without `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` in the cron shell the script exits 1 in `load_credentials()` and the entire self-healing layer is dead. Nothing in this repo provisioned root's credential: every other path wrote `/home/<user>/.profile`, and the README documented the token going into `~/.bashrc`, which dash does not read either.

The failure is silent, which is what makes it worth fixing: the watchdog's Slack webhook is itself read through `op`, so the process that would report the problem is the one that cannot run.

Sourcing a profile made this worse rather than better, which is why this is one change and not two. `.` is a POSIX **special builtin**: dash abandons the rest of the command line when the file it names cannot be opened. Verified on the dev host — `dash -c '. /nonexistent; echo REACHED'` prints nothing and exits 2 — so an unguarded `. /root/.profile;` costs *every run* when the file is absent, not just the credential it was meant to supply.

## What changed

- **`setup.sh`** — the installed cron line is now `*/10 * * * * [ -r /root/.profile ] && . /root/.profile; <script> >> <log> 2>&1`, so a missing or unreadable profile degrades to no-credential instead of aborting the run. `setup.sh` creates `/root/.profile` (`0600`) when it does not exist, with a comment stating what must go in it.
- **Installing is no longer a no-op on a host that already has an entry.** The old guard was `crontab -l | grep -q homelab_watchdog` leading to `already exists`, so a host installed before the guarded shape existed would never be migrated. It now reads the crontab, drops any `homelab_watchdog` line and re-adds the current shape, leaving every other entry untouched.
- **The closing summary** reports `Watchdog credentials: configured | NOT CONFIGURED`, so a fresh install says out loud that the layer is dead instead of looking healthy. The check matches a real `export`, not the commented placeholder — verified against a commented-out export, which correctly reports NOT CONFIGURED.
- **Docs** (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `Makefile`, `docs/decisions.md`) — the token is documented in `~/.profile` (outside the `BASH_VERSION` guard) rather than `~/.bashrc`, root's copy of the same requirement is stated where the cron job is installed, and the rationale lives in one new `docs/decisions.md` section that the other sites point at.

### A pre-existing defect found while validating

`setup.sh` already had `(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "$CRON_ENTRY") | crontab -` under `set -euo pipefail`. On a host where root has **no crontab** — the fresh-install case this change is about — `crontab -l` exits 1, the subshell aborts at `set -e` before the `echo`, and `pipefail` makes the pipeline non-zero, so `setup.sh` dies there. It never installs the entry, never creates the watchdog state directory, never configures log rotation, and never prints its verification summary or the remaining manual steps. Reproduced in isolation. The read and the write are now separate with `|| true` on both, which also removes a read-modify-write against the crontab inside a single pipeline.

## Validation

- `bash -n setup.sh` — passes.
- **Crontab migration suite** — the shipped block extracted from `setup.sh` verbatim, run against a fake `crontab` that buffers stdin then installs (like the real one), over five scenarios: no crontab at all; rerun; legacy unguarded entry alongside unrelated entries; rerun on that host; watchdog as the only entry. 25/25 assertions passed: exactly one `homelab_watchdog` line, guarded shape present, legacy shape gone, unrelated entries preserved, no blank lines introduced, script reaches the end in every case.
- **dash semantics** — a failed `.` aborts the line; the `[ -r ]`-guarded form reaches the next command with the file missing, present, and mode 000.
- **`make test`** — `all 16 cases as expected`.

## Deliberately not included

- **`OP_SOCK`.** Two unmerged draft branches document pinning the op daemon socket. It is absent from `master`, and the investigation preceding this change could not verify what `op` does without it, concluding the profile-sourcing rule is load-bearing on the token alone. Adding unverified environment documentation to the same fix would make it harder to review, not safer to deploy; it deserves its own PR with a host-side check.
- **Collapsing the duplicated cron line.** It is still restated in `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/decisions.md` and `setup.sh` — made consistent rather than reduced to one pointer, because the README is where an operator copies it from. Drift between those copies is what produced this bug (`master`'s `setup.sh` already disagreed with `master`'s README), so a cheap consistency guard is a reasonable follow-up.
- **This branch was cut from `master`, not from the unmerged draft branches** for the earlier investigations of the same bug; it supersedes them.

## Not determinable here

Whether `/root/.profile` is *absent* or merely *unpopulated* on the real target — what is verified is that nothing in this repo creates or writes it. The live state of the homelab host's root crontab was also not inspected.

## Reviewer note

One operator action remains and cannot be automated: paste the service-account token into `/root/.profile` on the host. `setup.sh` reports it at the end of the next run; nothing here stores a secret.

---

If what you find on re-reading no longer supports that conclusion, say so in your own verdict and stop rather than forcing a change.

author: abhayla
body:
Closes item 11's two carried MAJORs. **This is a live bug, not the dormant one the card describes.**

## RCA

Both scorers compare `ipos.issue_size` against literal thresholds of `1000 / 500 / 100`. Those are **crore** figures; the column stores **rupees**. Because the gap is a fixed 1e7 multiplier, every real row lands in the same band.

## Proof (staging, read-only through the tunnel, 2026-09-21)

314 of 366 rows hold a rupee-shaped value (≥ 1e7). The **smallest genuine row** — PIYUSH, ₹0.70 Cr = `7,007,320` — is still **7,007× the top threshold**.

So the site's largest and smallest IPOs scored identically:

| IPO | stored issue_size | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| NSE | 265,796,400,000 (₹26,579 Cr) | 0.75 | **0.75** |
| Hero Motors | 10,000,000,000 (₹1,000 Cr) | 0.75 | **0.65** |
| ₹300 Cr issue | 3,000,000,000 | 0.75 | **0.55** |
| PIYUSH | 7,007,320 (₹0.70 Cr) | 0.75 | **0.45** |

Both terms were constants dressed as calculations. They contributed nothing to ranking.

## Class — two call sites, both fixed

| file | finding | reached from |
|---|---|---|
| `web/lib/services/ipo-scoring-realtime.ts` | F-95 | scoring service |
| `web/lib/utils/rating-calculator.ts` | F-77 | **live API route** `app/api/ipos/[slug]/rating`, `scripts/calculate-ratings.ts` |

## Fix

Convert at the **read**, using the `RUPEES_PER_CRORE` already exported from `web/lib/utils.ts` — not by restating the thresholds in rupees. OD-20 makes crore the stored unit, so the crore-denominated comparison survives the coming migration; a rupee-denominated one would have to be undone.

Worth noting: that constant **already existed**, with a comment reading *"one calc treated it as crores"*. The class had been seen and the constant created, without these two call sites ever being changed.

## Why the tests never caught it

The fixtures were typed in the same wrong unit as the code — `issueSize: 2500, // ₹2500 Cr`. They agreed with the bug. The shared `mockIPOData` used `1500`, so **every other test in that file was silently exercising the bottom band**. Those fixtures are corrected to rupees here; leaving them would have re-encoded the defect in the suite.

`rating-calculator.ts` had **no test at all** — which is precisely why F-77 stayed "documented, not fixed" while its twin was tracked. `calculateMarketScore` is now exported so the term can be pinned directly.

## Evidence

| check | result |
|---|---|
| new tests red first | 3 red (scoring, all returning max 0.75) + 5 red (rating) |
| after fix | 28 passed |
| mutation (revert both divisions) | **8 failed** — both mutants killed |
| `npm run lint:ci` | **PASSED**, 732 errors = baseline, 0 added |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| web unit suite | 2674 passed; 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (`tests/unit/config/playwright-prod-verify.test.ts` — untouched by this branch, **passes in isolation**: cross-file env pollution) |

## What this does NOT do

It does **not** convert any stored data. The columns still hold rupees; this only stops two readers misreading them. The actual OD-20 conversion is item 11's remaining half and is its own release — see #854, where I recorded the per-row unit measurement that its "not measured" section asked for.

## Detection

Registered `docs/reviews/failure-classes/threshold-in-one-unit-column-in-another.json`. The general check: a property test per banding rule — feed it the min and max values actually present in its source column and FAIL if the outputs are equal. That catches unit confusion, an inverted comparison and a dead branch in one assertion.

body: ## Summary Fixes the PR #7 review findings and the two runtime-test failures (remote alarms lost after hub restart; `/api/v1/live?node=unknown` accepted silently). **Alarm convergence** — new frame `TypeAlarms` (`Frame.Alarms []health.LogEntry`). The agent sends a full snapshot (`ClientOptions.Alarms func() []health.Alarm` → `SnapshotEntry`) after replay on every connect. Hub `Node.replaceAlarms(snapshot)` swaps the state map and appends only entries whose status differs (with `OldStatus` filled from the previous hub view, hub-local monotonic `UniqueID`) to the mirrored log / live feed. Alarms are now persisted in `nodes.json`, so a restarted hub shows them before the agent reconnects. **Node identity** — `authorize()` returns `sha256(key)`; a `Node` is bound to the key that registered it (`keyHash`, persisted). A `hello` for an existing id under a different valid key gets an `error` frame (`node is bound to a different api key`) and no takeover. Legacy nodes without a hash bind on next connect. Documented: give each agent its own key. **Quotas** — `hub.max_nodes` (1000), `max_charts_per_node` (5000), `max_dims_per_chart` (1000); excess nodes are rejected at hello, excess charts/dims are dropped with a warning. **Chart definitions** — a resent def with a different fingerprint now calls `Registry.ReplaceChart` (new): metadata, renamed/hidden dims and removals apply; last values of surviving dims are kept. **Replay watermark** — `welcome.Last[chart]` = *oldest* dimension's last timestamp (a dim with no data → replay the whole window). TSDB `Append` already drops `ts <= last`, so overlap is idempotent. **Client** — queue drained *before* `accepting=true`; `session()` returns `(connected, err)` and `Run` resets backoff to 1s after a successful handshake. **nodes.json** — `dirty` replaced by `gen`/`saved` counters; `saved` advances only after `os.Rename` succeeds, so a failed write retries on the next tick. **API/UI** — `/api/v1/live` goes through `handleLive` → `target()` before upgrade (404 for unknown node; in-band `{"node":...}` switches are validated too). Dashboard `refreshAlarms/refreshFunctions` discard responses if the selected node changed mid-flight. Tests: `TestHubAlarmSnapshotConverges`, `TestHubNodeBoundToKey`, `TestHubQuotas`, `TestHubChartDefinitionUpdate`, `TestHubLiveUnknownNodeRejected`, `TestSaveRetriesAfterFailure`. Verified with a real hub+agent: 20 alarms visible on the hub immediately after restart and after reconnect; unknown-node live → 404. 📝 Summary


# 🧩 Type of Change

Select one that best describes this PR. Release-relevant commits must use the
corresponding Conventional Commit type.

- [ ] feat: New feature
- [x] fix: Bug fix
- [ ] perf: Performance improvement
- [ ] refactor: Code refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] docs: Documentation only
- [ ] test: Tests only
- [ ] chore: Build/CI/Tools
- [ ] BREAKING CHANGE: Breaking API change

## 🔖 Release Rule Reminder

- `feat:` -> `minor + 1`
- `fix:` -> `patch + 1`
- commit message body 含 `BREAKING CHANGE:` -> `major + 1`
- `docs:`、`refactor:`、`chore:` 默认不触发正式版本发布
- `type!:` 不作为 breaking release 的唯一依据；如有不兼容变更，必须在 commit message body 写明 `BREAKING CHANGE:`

## Release PR Merge Strategy

Release PRs from `release/auto-release` to `master` must preserve the commits
from `dev`. Do not squash a release PR into the fixed `chore(release):` title;
use a merge commit or rebase merge so semantic-release can analyze the original
commit types.

author: profcarroll
body:
The return leg of the paid planner path. `--planner paid` parks a job at `needs-laptop`, `needs='plan'` — branch B of DECIDE[credential-model] keeps the credential off the node, so the planning happens wherever the key is. Nothing brought it back.

## What was already there, and what wasn't

I tested the route through the CLI before writing anything. Two thirds of it already worked:

- **Outbound** — `enqueue --planner paid` parks the job. Confirmed live: job 1228 reached `needs-laptop`/`needs=plan`.
- **Parse** — `plan --stub reply.txt` replays a paid model's raw reply through the *real* planner parser, validates the assertions against the closed vocabulary, and records the model that answered with empty tokens/durations because nothing was called.
- **Back** — nothing. `plan` takes no `--job` and never opens the database. `db` has `init` and `status`. The web UI has `post_laptop`, which sends a job *into* `needs-laptop`; no route takes one out. `db.TRANSITIONS` has allowed `needs-laptop -> executing` since 001 and nothing ever called it.

So an agent asked to test this path gets a validated brief sitting in a JSON file and no supported way to put it on the job. That is how the incident in #118 started: with no documented return leg, the agent reached for `worker --once` and raced the daemon.

## `plan --job N`

The prompt comes from the job, the reply is parsed as before, and the result goes back in the one `db.transition` the worker itself makes on the local path — brief, assertions, model, state. A job planned from the laptop is indistinguishable afterwards from one planned on the node.

Three rules, each borrowed rather than invented:

- **`--model` is the model that answered**, replacing the word `paid` in `jobs.planner`. The paid judge's rule: a verdict belongs to whoever gave it, not whoever was asked.
- **`--job` refuses a job in any other state.** A second writer of `jobs.brief` is a second worker by another name, and #118 is what that costs. Planning the same job twice is refused by the same guard.
- **A reply that will not parse leaves the job parked.** The raw text is saved beside the job and the same `--job` takes a better one. Only a parsed plan moves the job.

No hash travels with the prompt the way it does with the judge's claims: `jobs.prompt` is written once by `enqueue` and no code in this repo updates it, so what the laptop was shown is what the job still holds.

## The bug in my own first version

The write-back first moved the job to `executing`, copying the worker's `_plan`. The worker can do that — it already holds the job and runs on into `_run_job` in the same pass. Nothing holds a job planned from the laptop, and **`db.claim_next` selects on `state = 'queued'` alone**, so the job would have sat in a running state with nobody in it until `sweep_stuck` noticed, half an hour later by default.

It goes back on the **queue** instead, and `claim_next` reads the brief this command wrote and sends it to `executing` itself, skipping the planner. `needs-laptop -> queued` joins `TRANSITIONS` to allow it. The sweep's `REQUEUABLE` set is untouched — a job waiting for a person was never stuck.

## Verified end to end on the node

Against the real parked job, running the branch from a git worktree so the node's checkout was untouched:

```
$ sketchgen plan --job 1228 --model claude-sonnet-5 --stub reply.txt
plan: /home/ubuntu/sketchgen/jobs/1228/plan.json
prompt_version: planner-v1
assertions: motion(idle)
job 1228: planned by claude-sonnet-5, back on the queue — the worker claims it on its next pass
```

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| state | `needs-laptop` | `queued` |
| needs | `plan` | `None` |
| planner | `paid` | `claude-sonnet-5` |
| brief | `None` | the paid model's |

## Tests

`Ran 1266 tests ... OK (skipped=3)`. Twelve new, covering the write-back and its provenance, the prompt coming from the job, the default output directory, refusals for a job the worker is attending / waiting on something else / unknown / already planned, an unparseable reply leaving the job untouched, the argument grammar, and `claim_next` then taking the job straight to `executing`.

## Still missing

The executor and the critic have no equivalent. This is the planner leg only.

author: obvious-autobuild[bot]
body:
Human author: Mikey (mkglasky@gmail.com)

## Why
The download-import engine verifies imports but never reclaims disk: sources pile up because deletion was deliberately out of scope. This stage adds it safely (decision D4) — a source may be removed only after BOTH the import is verified AND the download client confirms the source is complete on its side (qBittorrent seed requirement per the Web API, NZBGet complete history entry). It also adds the homelab webhook (n8n → Task-a-Tron 9000 → Telegram) for import success, review-needed, and failure events.

## What
- **Source cleanup, off by default** — `downloadImportCleanupEnabled` (+ min ratio / min seed hours thresholds) in server settings. The manager runs a guarded per-row cleanup at import time and a periodic sweep; every gate must hold before `fs.remove`: cleanup enabled, row IMPORTED, not already cleaned, a typed download client configured, source/destination path overlap rejected, source exists, and `checkSourceRemovable` confirms client-side completeness. Filesystem-only roots are never deleted; batch behavior is per-row confirmation only.
- **Webhook notifier** — `WebhookNotifier.js`: best-effort JSON POST (never fails the pipeline), http(s)-only URL validated in settings PATCH and the notifier, flat payload n8n can map to Telegram. Events: `import_success`, `import_review_needed`, `import_failure`. Tested against a local mock server only.
- **Queue bookkeeping** — `cleanedUpAt` column + v2.37.0 migration + fork version bump (sync runs with `alter:false`).
- **Latent bugs fixed on the way**: the qBittorrent qualifier's export shape made it impossible to instantiate from the registry, and the registry never passed client config to qualifiers — client-side qualification could never have worked.

## How to review
- `server/downloadImport/DownloadImportManager.js` — cleanup gates (`attemptSourceCleanup`), sweep, notifier wiring.
- `server/downloadImport/qualifiers/*` — `isSourceRemovable` gates (seed states, history entries).
- `server/downloadImport/WebhookNotifier.js`, `ServerSettings.js`, `MiscController.js` — surface and validation.
- Intentionally excluded: frontend settings UI (follows once behavior is settled), any deletion without a typed client.

## Test evidence
Unit tests for cleanup gates (happy path + not-yet-complete source asserting no deletion), qualifier seed/history decisions, webhook payload shape and delivery (local mock). Server runs in CI.

body:
This is a documentation gap, not a bug — the file handling is correct and this PR changes no code. The MCP writes a second file into the credential directory, `login-pending.json`, and nothing documented it: `git grep login-pending` over `docs/` and `packages/` returned no documentation hits at all, and the whole Credential Storage section named only `credentials.json`. This extends that section with what the file is, where it lives, its mode, its TTL, and when it is cleared. It also adds the one line for `MEMWAL_MCP_TRANSPORT`, which was described only in `docs/reference/environment-variables.md`.

**Evidence:** on `dev`,

```
packages/mcp/README.md:147-153   the entire "Credential Storage" section — credentials.json and --logout, nothing else
packages/mcp/src/auth.ts:441     pendingLoginPath() — sits beside whichever credentials file credsPath() resolves to
packages/mcp/src/auth.ts:433     PENDING_LOGIN_TTL_MS = 24 * 60 * 60_000
```

**Impact:** documentation only. Nobody is broken by this; a user who finds the file has no way to know what it is, whether it is a leak, or how to get rid of it, and the answer to the last one (`--logout`) was already written down for the other file only.

**Test:** none — this is prose. The behaviour it describes is already pinned: `packages/mcp/test/logout-invalidation.test.mjs:681-689` asserts that `memwal_logout` removes `login-pending.json`, and `packages/mcp/test/login-write-ahead.test.mjs` covers the 0600 mode, the write-ahead ordering, and the clear on a completed sign-in.

One thing to know when merging: PR #920 (draft) deletes `packages/mcp/test/logout-invalidation.test.mjs` and rewrites `packages/mcp/README.md`, so it will conflict with this textually and the test reference above moves with it.

author: cmgs
body:
Whole-repo review round, 2026-09-21. Every production file read in full; the host→guest exec flow (cocoon `vm exec` → hybrid vsock → agent → child → framed reply), the reseed path and the Windows transport were traced end to end by a reader agent that ran eleven probes (framing edges, 1 MiB output, non-zero exit, ctx kill, mid-stream connection drop, 200 KiB stdin, 16 concurrent sessions, a real reseed with both RNG ioctls in a privileged Linux container); a docs lens verified every claim on all seven pages; a tests lens read the five test files.

## Commits

- `07a2edf` review: two comments claim less than they did
- `6be436f` review: remove dead code and align documentation
- `5d41245` fix: cancel active exec sessions on disconnect
- `89aa3b6` test: the disconnect test takes the started and ready frames in either order

## Findings

| # | where | claim | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `agent/sysproc_linux.go` | the comment promised background workers never outlive the session; the process-group kill runs on cancel only, a daemonized grandchild survives a normal exit by design (a probe showed `sleep 6 &` alive after a clean exit) | comment narrowed to the cancel path |
| 2 | `agent/reseed_linux.go` | the comment promised the entropy left no heap copy; the scanner buffer keeps the base64 form | comment narrowed; zeroing the scanner buffer would be over-defense at the agent's own privilege level |
| 3 | `cmd/transport_windows.go` `LocalAddr` | reports the host CID for the guest's own endpoint; reaches two log lines only | noted, no change |
| 4 | wire contract vs cocoonv2 | nine frame types, no version field, unknown fields decode away, unknown frame types ignored except as the first frame; cocoonv2 pins v0.2.3 == the round's base | correct, no skew; `5d41245` changes no frame |
| 5 | `agent/agent.go` `handleConn` (found by the owner after the round) | the stdin reader returned after `MsgStdinClose` and, on a clean EOF, returned without cancelling the child, so a client that vanished after closing stdin (or while a quiet child ran) left the child running until it exited or the server context ended; the round's read recorded that the reader exits, not that the child outlives the client, and the disconnect probe dropped the connection only while output was flowing | fixed `5d41245`: the reader drains the connection after stdin closes and cancels the exec context whenever it exits; `TestExecDisconnectCancelsQuietChild` fails on the pre-fix code (both subtests time out) and passes on HEAD; the exec-flow lens measured the same on archives of both trees (a quiet child whose client vanished after closing stdin is alive 5 s later on the old tree, reaped at once on the new one) and re-ran its nine exec probes unchanged. Host consumers (`cocoon vm exec` through this repo's client package) never half-close, so an EOF at the agent means the client is gone |
| 6 | `client/client.go` `Run`, `packaging/install-cocoon-agent.ps1` | a post-loop `sawExit` branch the read loop could never reach, and an unused `$binPath` variable; the LOC lens reported no dead code | cut in `6be436f` |

Docs: all seven pages verified against source in the round; `6be436f`/`5d41245` then reshaped README.md (highlights, related projects, Makefile targets, all checked against the Makefile) and the architecture page's error and StdinClose bullets, both checked against `handleConn` (an undecodable first frame is logged unless it is a plain EOF and the connection closed without a frame; `MsgStdinClose` ends input, not the session).

## Design notes (owner decision, no code)

- A client that half-closes its write side and then waits for `MsgExit` now loses its child: since `5d41245` an EOF on the connection cancels the session. No shipped caller does this (the client package only closes the whole connection, on context cancel), and the architecture page's new StdinClose sentence states the input side; if the guarantee is worth spelling out, one clause on that bullet ("closing the connection ends the session and the command") does it.

## Cut-list (report only)

The owner's `6be436f` cut the two dead items the LOC lens missed (`sawExit`, `$binPath`); nothing else is on the list — the standing rejections (Winsock `send()==0` guard, `Message.PID`, the two vsock reject loops, `processController`, `len(argv)==0`) stand.

## LOC (same counting on both ends)

- origin/main=7a8a406: prod=1506 test=853 comments=92 blanks=197 effective=1217
- HEAD=89aa3b6: prod=1495 test=949 comments=86 blanks=197 effective=1212 test_funcs=30 (was 28)

Per commit: `07a2edf` review 2/2 (comments +1/−1); `6be436f` review 0/14 (comments +0/−6); `5d41245` fix 10/7 · 83/0 (comments +4/−4); `89aa3b6` test 0/0 · 17/8.

## Gates

All gates re-run on HEAD `89aa3b6` (and on `5d41245` before the test commit):
- `GOWORK=off make fmt-check`: rc=0; `golangci-lint` on `GOOS=darwin`, `linux` and `windows`: 0 issues; `GOOS=windows go vet`: ok.
- `asl ./...` on darwin and linux: 0 findings.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`: green (agent, client on darwin).
- `TestExecDisconnectCancelsQuietChild` run against the pre-fix `agent/agent.go`: both subtests fail (5 s timeouts), so the test is red before the fix and green after; at HEAD it passes `-race -count=30`.
- linux/arm64 `golang:1.27` container: `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race -count=1 ./...` green (agent, client, cmd) on `5d41245` and `89aa3b6`.

## Codex

Round 1, thread `01a0c25f-d040-70c0-9e66-fe627417b63d`, read-only sandbox, on HEAD `07a2edf`; the prompt carried the discipline (no contrived scenarios, no over-design, idempotent fixes, no over-defense). Final message, verbatim:

> No blockers: this diff converges.

Round 2 on `5d41245` (the owner's two commits, same thread): the production fix judged sound; one finding on the new test, verbatim:

> [P3] agent/exec_cancel_test.go:56 — TestExecDisconnectCancelsQuietChild fails when cmd.Start's stdout copier forwards "ready" before runExec sends MsgStarted; their order is unsynchronized — accept both frames in either order before disconnecting.

Confirmed from `runExec` (`cmd.Stdout` is a writer, so the copier `Start` spawns races the `MsgStarted` encode) and fixed by `89aa3b6`.

Round 3 on `89aa3b6`, verbatim:

> No blockers: this diff converges.

## Follow-ups

None filed.

`PATCH /api/v1/notifications/todo-completed/read-all`로 안 읽은 할 일 완료 알림을 한 번에 넘깁니다. 줄마다 눌러야 했던 자리입니다.

## 버튼이 나오는 조건

`친구의 할 일 완료`를 보고 있고, 안 읽은 것이 남아 있을 때만입니다.

서버가 그 갈래의 안 읽은 줄만 받으므로 다른 갈래에서는 누를 것이 없고, 남은 것이 없을 때도 0건입니다. 눌러도 아무 일이 없는 버튼을 세워 두느니 그때만 내놓습니다.

확인은 묻지 않습니다. 읽음은 지우는 것이 아니라 표시를 거두는 것이고, 줄을 하나 누를 때도 같은 일이 일어납니다 — `ConfirmMenu`를 쓰는 다른 자리들과 달리 되돌릴 것이 없습니다.

무효화는 줄 하나를 읽을 때와 같은 `["notifications"]`이라, 목록과 갈래 칩의 점, 아래 네비게이션의 점이 함께 따라옵니다.

## 확인

누르면 `PATCH /api/v1/notifications/todo-completed/read-all` **1회**, 그 뒤:

- 줄의 안 읽음 점 2개 → 0
- 갈래 칩의 점 → 사라짐
- 아래 네비게이션 종의 점 → 사라짐
- 버튼 자체 → 사라짐 (남은 것이 없으므로)
- 알림 줄은 목록에 그대로 남음

`친구의 일기` 탭에서는 안 읽은 것이 있어도 버튼이 나오지 않는 것까지 확인했습니다.

`openapi.json`에는 해당 오퍼레이션만 저장소 스타일(명명된 `NotificationsReadAllResponse`, 영문 설명, 공통 응답 `$ref`)로 이식했습니다.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to the review on #1, fixing items 1–4 (stacked on `feat/ken-burns-gesture-frame`).

**1. EXIF orientation** — `derive._orientation` now reads tag `0x0112` and swaps `width/height` for orientations 5–8, so rotated iPhone portraits get `orientation="portrait"` instead of `landscape` (which caused Ken Burns to crop them heavily). Note: this only fixes classification; the browser still relies on `image-orientation: from-image` to display the pixels rotated.

**2. False "live" classification** — `library.has_embedded_motion` drops the `GCamera` marker (present on ordinary Pixel stills); only `MicroVideo` / `MotionPhoto` / `motionphoto` count. `derive._extract_embedded_motion` now requires `ftyp` in the first 64 bytes of the extracted clip, and `prepare_slide` downgrades `KIND_LIVE → KIND_PHOTO` when no motion clip could be produced:

```python
motion = _ensure_motion(asset, cache_dir, token)
kind = asset.kind
if kind == KIND_LIVE and motion is None:
    kind = KIND_PHOTO   # no more "playable" slides with motion_src=""
```

**3. Zero-byte media** — `demo_library._render_clip` no longer writes an empty `.MOV`/`.mp4` when ffmpeg is missing or fails (it unlinks the partial output and returns `False`). `library._iter_media_files` skips any 0-byte file, so stale empties on disk also can't be indexed.

**4. Malformed HTTP input** — `Range: bytes=abc-` previously raised `ValueError` inside the handler. Range parsing is extracted to `preview._parse_range(header, file_size) -> (start, end) | None`, which handles suffix ranges (`bytes=-100`), clamps, and returns `None` (→ `416` with `Content-Range: bytes */size`) for malformed/unsatisfiable specs. `do_POST` returns `400` on non-integer `Content-Length`, invalid JSON, or a non-object body.

Five regression tests added to `selftest.py`; `python -m frame.selftest` → `ok`, `pytest frame/selftest.py` → 22 passed. Manually verified against the demo server: `bytes=abc-` → 416, `bytes=0-10` → 206, `bytes=-100` → 206, bad POST body → 400, no tracebacks.

author: chchatzop
body:
Fixes #671 (audit L7). Stacked on #826 - merge that first; this one then retargets.

**What was wrong:** any channel member can register a "bot" in `runtime.known_bots` with one unauthenticated line (`Type: @<theirnick> For My List Of: 1 Files`; the RAR wording needs no identity claim at all). `_prune_known_bots()` evicted by `last_seen` ascending once the registry passed `KNOWN_BOTS_MAX` (2000) - and 2001 fresh nicks carry the newest `last_seen` of all, so the genuine bots that had advertised minutes earlier were the ones dropped: gone from the List Browser until their next advert, while the junk sat there for up to a week. The docstring claimed the opposite, for exactly the burst the cap was added for.

**What changed:** `_record_bot()` counts the adverts an entry is built from (`adverts`), and eviction sorts by that count first, then by `last_seen`. A nick that said it once is what goes; a bot that advertises every few minutes has said it more than once by the time a flood of that size can arrive. An entry with no count (an older `known_bots` file) counts as one - no more established than a nick seen once now, and no less. Hand-entered bots are still never candidates. Among one-offs, least-recently-seen still goes first, so `test_eviction_drops_the_least_recently_seen_first` holds unchanged.

**Test:** `tests/test_a_burst_of_new_nicks_does_not_evict_the_real_bots.py` runs the auditor's recipe through the real capture path - five bots seen twice minutes ago, then `KNOWN_BOTS_MAX + 1` one-off nicks in both advert wordings - and every genuine bot survives; plus the one-off ordering, the older-file case, the count itself and the hand-entered exemption. With `irc.py` unpatched, three of the six fail.

**Verified:** full suite 6098 tests OK. Both changelogs.

author: cmgs
body:
Whole-repo review round, 2026-09-21. Every production file read in full; the SandboxClaim → Sandbox → Pod → vk-sandbox claim flow (both the warm-pool and the cold path), the expiry and restart paths and the delete-authorization contract were traced end to end by reader agents that ran code probes against the real provider; the sandboxd wire contract was cross-checked against the sandbox repo's handlers; a docs lens verified every claim on every page; a tests lens read every test file.

## Commits

- `3899052` docs: the --tls-cert help names the self-signed fallback
- `f4f73b1` fix: an expired owner Sandbox authorizes the release of its microVM
- `f17761f` docs: the mutator sets net and size, and an expired owner releases
- `3bac37f` test: block the state write with a directory in the temp file's place
- `8ee1089` fix: converge sandbox retries and align deployment contracts (owner, after the round)
- `177cd97` docs: the retained claim is found by pod key, the claim id rides the status push, the owner read decides

## Findings

| # | where | claim | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `provider/ownership.go` `destroyAuthorized` | a Sandbox that expires under the operator's default Retain policy has its Pod deleted while the CR stays alive without a deletionTimestamp; the rule read the owner as alive, preserved the claim, and the microVM ran on with no Pod and no replacement ever coming until its 24 h lease (probe: `releases=0 claim-still-held=true`) | fixed: a Ready condition with reason `SandboxExpired` is teardown authority; `TestDeleteReleasesWhenTheOwnerExpired` |
| 2 | `main.go` `--tls-cert` help | "plain HTTP if unset"; the kubelet API is TLS-only and self-signs when the pair is absent | help string corrected |
| 3 | `docs/pod-contract.md` | `net`/`size` listed as inputs the operator's mutator never set; the mutator now sets all three axes from the shared pool key (sandbox-operator `96d50d2`) | docs corrected; expired-owner row added here and in the architecture table |
| 4 | `provider/provider_test.go` seven persist-failure tests | they removed the directory's write bit, which root ignores: the suite failed in a root container (pre-existing at the base, verified) | `test:` a directory in the `.tmp` file's place fails the write for every user |
| 5 | `inventory/publisher.go` | an entry without a `claim_ref` (SDK-direct claim) publishes name and claim ref as the node-local id and lands in the default namespace | harmless, noted |
| 6 | `provider/create.go` `CreatePod`/`UpdatePod` (found by the owner after the round) | a create whose persist and compensating release both failed left a tentative claim that nothing retried: `UpdatePod` only stored the Pod, so the Pod sat Pending on a live microVM until deletion | fixed `8ee1089`: the provider-side Pod carries the claim-id annotation, so virtual-kubelet's `createOrUpdatePod` (annotations differ → `podsEqual` false) calls `UpdatePod`, which re-enters `CreatePod` for a tentative key: the stranded claim is returned, a new one claimed, persisted and published Running. `TestTentativeClaimRetriesThroughUpdatePod` fails on the pre-commit provider code and passes on HEAD |
| 7 | `manifests/rbac.yaml` | virtual-kubelet's deletion flow deletes the API Pod (`node/pod.go` in v1.13.0) and the role had no `delete` on pods | fixed `8ee1089` |
| 8 | `provider.Config.NodeName`, `.golangci.yml` gosec exclusion for a package that no longer exists | dead configuration the round's read did not flag | cut in `8ee1089` |

Docs: `docs/pod-contract.md`, `docs/architecture.md` corrected in the round; `8ee1089` then rewrote README, docs (architecture, configuration, index, installation, pod-contract), CONTRIBUTING and SECURITY to the runtime contracts — every new claim checked against code: the `--sandboxd-advertise-addr` flag, the Makefile targets, the Go 1.27 requirement, the `pkg/sandboxd` + `pkg/scale` imports, the UpdatePod retry and tentative-visibility semantics, the lease-watch behaviour, the delete-authorization list (gone, replaced UID, deleting, expired).

## Design notes (owner decisions, no code)

- **A Pod deleted before it ever reported Running leaves its claim held (pre-existing, found by the claim-flow lens while probing `8ee1089`).** virtual-kubelet v1.13.0 (`node/podcontroller.go:576-581`) force-deletes such a Pod from the API without calling `DeletePod`; `running()` needs a container status, which a failed create never writes, so this is exactly the state a tentative claim sits in. The claim stays in the table with a live sandbox, `OrphanScan` cannot flag it (probe: `claim-held=true releases=0 orphans=[] staleClaims=[]`), and only a same-key replacement Pod (adopt or clear-stranded) or the 24 h lease ends it. Not fixable inside the provider's current information set: virtual-kubelet's post-force-delete hook is unexported. Options are an apiserver read the provider deliberately avoids today, or accepting the lease as the bound. Owner's call: backlog — no correctness impact (no false release, no false status), a bounded capacity cost on a rare path.
- **The `UpdatePod` retry never runs for a Pod whose template sets `restartPolicy: Never`**: virtual-kubelet marks a failed create `Failed` and skips `Failed`/`Succeeded` Pods before `createOrUpdatePod` (`node/pod.go:199-202`, `podcontroller.go:619-622`); the operator copies `restartPolicy` from the SandboxTemplate. A limit of the retry, not a defect; the pod-contract failure-and-churn paragraph now states it (`177cd97`).
- **Docs wording from that probe round, committed as `177cd97` (md only, no Codex round by the owner's call)**: pod-contract's "Pod deletion can still find and release the retained claim through `GetPod`" — `DeletePod` resolves by pod key (`heldClaimFor`), `GetPod` only makes virtual-kubelet take the Update branch, and virtual-kubelet passes the lister's Pod, not the `GetPod` copy (the revised `TestATentativeClaimCanStillBeReleased` would model the caller better if it deleted the Kubernetes Pod: left as is, behaviour identical); pod-contract's claim-id "out" row — on the branch where the annotation does not survive the `pods/status` push, the one `UpdatePod` the new stored-Pod shape provokes overwrites the provider's copy and drops it (measured: `stored claim-id=""` after resync 1, cost zero), so the id is published on the status push and may be absent from the provider's own Pod view; installation.md's RBAC bullet — "`get` on the owner CR, the read every controller-owned release is decided from" (the read enables the decision, it does not grant release).
- **Whether the claim-id annotation survives the `pods/status` push** could not be settled offline (pod status strategy source is not in the module cache); either way `UpdatePod` fires at most once per Pod and takes no VM action.

- A Pod deleted by an eviction that races the owner's expiry now releases the microVM; the outcome is the one the operator's expiry intends (the workload is torn down), so no separate handling was added.

Hygiene note: `8ee1089` carries a fix, two cuts, an RBAC change and the docs rewrite in one `fix:` commit; the round's convention is one concern per commit. Its comment delta is +6/−10.

## Cut-list (report only)

Nothing; the standing rejections (`Claim.PodUID`, `OrphanScan` returns, `TaintKey`, the listed WHY comments) stand.

## LOC (same counting on both ends)

- origin/master=c8165e8: prod=1916 test=1626 comments=324 blanks=174 effective=1418
- HEAD=8ee1089: prod=1934 test=1696 comments=320 blanks=177 effective=1437 test_funcs=57

Per commit: docs 1/1 · 0/0; fix 17/0 · 26/0; docs 0/0; test 0/0 · 13/28 (a directory in the temp file's place replaces the chmod and its cleanup); `8ee1089` fix 24/24 · 85/28 (comments +6/−10).

## Gates

All gates re-run on HEAD `8ee1089`:
- `GOWORK=off make fmt-check`: rc=0; `golangci-lint` on `GOOS=darwin` and `linux`: 0 issues.
- `asl ./...` on both GOOS: 0 findings.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`: green; the two tentative-claim te

author: amiridlan
body:
First of three stacked PRs. Merge this one first — #3 and #4 build on it.

## What this adds

- **Styling** — `src/styles/_tokens.scss` with every token from `docs/03`, Material 3 palettes generated from the brand colours at density -1, Plus Jakarta Sans / IBM Plex Sans / IBM Plex Mono, Material Symbols Outlined.
- **Locale** — `en-MY` with locale data registered, `MAT_DATE_LOCALE=en-GB` so typed dates parse as DD/MM/YYYY.
- **Models** — all nine model files as readonly interfaces with string-literal unions. `Candidate` carries no race, religion, health or disability field (PDPA 2010).
- **HTTP layer** — `ApiService` (snake_case ↔ camelCase in one place, including query parameter names), `ApiError` mapper, base-url and error interceptors, global `ErrorHandler`.
- **Auth** — `AuthStore` with three demo identities and the active-fair signal, plus `roleGuard` / `roleHomeRedirectGuard`.
- **Shell** — top bar, role-aware side nav (240px → 72px rail → drawer), role switcher, active-fair picker, 404.
- **Shared UI** — page-header, empty-state, error-state, skeleton, status-chip, kpi-card, placeholder-page, `maskEmail`.
- **Routing** — every route in the `docs/02` information architecture resolves, each feature lazy-loaded, `withComponentInputBinding()` enabled.

## Decisions worth a look

- **`environment.ts` is `production: true`**, not `false` as `docs/04` showed — the default file is what the production build uses. The `Environment` interface lives in its own module because `fileReplacements` swaps `environment.ts` out, so a type declared there would leave the development file importing its own replacement.
- **Initial bundle warning budget raised 500kB → 600kB.** The shell uses Material sidenav, toolbar, menu and snackbar on every route, putting the floor near 520kB raw / 122kB transferred. The 1MB error budget is unchanged.
- **Demo auth is not security** and says so prominently in `auth.store.ts`. Real authorisation comes from Laravel policies later.
- `maskEmail` is presentation only and says so — the API is what withholds contact details, since a pipe cannot be a privacy control once the unmasked value has reached the browser.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` | 519.84 kB raw / 121.95 kB transfer, no warnings |
| `npm test -- --watch=false` | 42 tests across 6 files |
| `npm run lint` | clean |
| Pattern audit | 0 `any` / `*ngIf` / `*ngFor` / `@Input(` / `ngClass` / `@HostBinding` / `NgModule`; 22/22 components OnPush; 0 constructor injection; 0 hardcoded hex |

Tests cover the API boundary case conversion, the `ApiError` mapper against Laravel's real 422/409/404 shapes, the role guards, and the masking pipe. The routing smoke test builds on `appConfig.providers` rather than a hand-rolled setup, so it tests the configuration the app actually ships.

## What to check on the deploy preview

1. Role switch (top right) between Farah (staff) and Daniel/Priya (hiring) — nav items change and you land on that role's home.
2. As a hiring manager, put `/staff/employers` in the URL bar — should bounce to `/hiring/talent-pool`.
3. Resize: full nav ≥1280, icon rail 768–1279, hamburger drawer <768.
4. `/nonsense` → "Page not found" with a role-correct button.
5. `/staff/fairs/fair-02` → renders "Fair fair-02", proving route-param binding.
6. Press Tab from the top — first stop is "Skip to main content".

Pages are placeholders naming the phase that replaces them; that is expected here.

author: moyamryia
body:
…the closed-source snapshot upload

复刻闭源版 repoSnapshotSidecar 的全链路：工作区扫描（.git 强制收录）→ tar.gz → AES-256-CTR + RSA-OAEP-SHA256 信封加密 → multipart 上传。差异只有两处，都是刻意的：

- 目标固定 127.0.0.1，assertLoopbackTarget 拒绝非回环
- RSA 密钥对本地生成，私钥落在用户自己的状态目录；因此 decrypt 真能还原， 而原版的私钥只在服务端，客户端产出的密文连自己都解不开

开关不进 GUI：只认 --parody-snapshot 或 ZCODE_PARODY_SNAPSHOT=1，默认完全静默。 不读 setting.json 之类的持久化配置——那正是原版让人无法拒绝的那条路。

spec.md 先于实现存在，列出全部收录/排除规则（含 .git 跳过体积上限与二进制检测）、
错误行为与 8 条验收场景。25 个测试覆盖开关、回环、扫描规则、tar 布局与长路径、
加解密与"换钥匙解不开"、multipart 解析，以及一条端到端（扫描→打包→加密→传
127.0.0.1→解密→逐条对账）。

不复用智谱任何凭据或端点。

author: zhi0467
body:
Three open issues in one scoped change. The fourth, #174, is closed as redundant: a side repository added under Settings and included in a turn's run scope is already a write root for that turn.

## #136 Provider launches leave no trace in the service journal

Every provider process writes one line when it starts and one when it ends: provider, capability, runtime, execution host, resolved executable, child pid, operation id, and on the end line the exit code, duration, and RCP's own reading of a non-zero exit. A failed task adds one line with its classification. Provider stdout and stderr never reach the journal, because a CLI can print token-shaped values there. The serve path attaches one stderr handler to the `rcp` package logger at INFO; uvicorn configured only its own loggers, so INFO lines were being dropped.

## #142 Transport classification: pre-provider losses, and two retry races

1. A link lost before the provider starts is classified `transport_lost`. The readiness probe types its unreachable host on the error event under whichever of its probes ssh died (discovery, version, auth, catalog, or Work), stage creation, the stage probe, the previous-pass check, and the input transfer raise `StateUnreachable`, a subclass of `StateUnavailable` raised only where ssh itself ran to a verdict and exited 255 (an ssh RCP could not start or stopped waiting for gives no verdict), and the execution is marked on that word alone, on the host the request is bound to even before a stage exists. The classifier reads it when no provider exit exists. A stage the host says is gone, or inputs it refused, are answers, not a lost link. An unreachable readiness answer is never cached, so a reattempt asks the host again instead of failing from memory.
2. The automatic reattempt claims its parent inside the admission transaction. `create_agent_task` refuses a second resume, retry, or handoff of a task that already has one. Experiment and Auto-research recoveries keep their own atomic claims, since their lineages carry children that are not recoveries.
3. Shutdown waits for a reattempt that has already begun admitting before it fences spawns, so the child it admits gets a worker and is paused with the rest instead of being left queued for a startup that would only interrupt it.

## #173 Update checkpoints and release trees grow without bound

After an update commits, the supervisor keeps the two newest checkpoints and release trees plus the live release, the rollback target, and every release a kept checkpoint sits between. Everything older is removed as the service account through the filesystem worker. An unrecorded checkpoint workspace is reclaimed only past a one-day age floor; the adoption workspace is protected. The prune refuses as a whole when the release pointer and the selected receipt disagree or an operation is unfinished, counts only journals whose recorded checkpoint exists toward the retained slots, leaves alone any build no completed deployment names so an in-progress install is never removed, and names every entry it leaves alone. A prune that cannot run is reported on the committed update, never as a failure. A pruned build keeps its sealed receipt; selecting that version again installs the verified bundle instead of failing against the missing tree. `rcp server prune` runs the same decision on demand; the public wrapper learns that route at the next `server install` converge.

## Checks

`uv run pytest` over the touched suites (background, storage, failure kinds, launcher, credential gate, providers, quiescence, transport loss, launch journal, acceptance lifecycle and watchers, transport, remote staging, api, auto-research stream, supervisor operations, retention, driver, integration, install, checkpoint, migration, server CLI, main, documentation) passes. `ruff` and `pre-commit` are clean over the changed files.

Closes #136. Closes #142. Closes #173.

author: ihwanudin
body:
## Summary

Adds `GET /sessions/{id}/answers` so a participant who refreshes mid-test sees their own already-autosaved answers rehydrated, instead of every field starting blank (found by GLM while designing the runner; PR #49's `GET /sessions/{id}` carries `answers_revision` but not the answer values themselves). Depends on and builds on #49 (merged) — this branch was rebased onto `origin/main` after that merge.

Design was sent as a plan and approved by Lead before implementation (touches the API contract), including one mandatory addition from review:

- **Separate endpoint, not a field on `GET /sessions/{id}`** — `AssessmentSessionResource` is already shared by the start/replay command and the resume read; keeping it untouched avoids widening that change surface for a concern a lightweight status poll doesn't need.
- **Readable exactly when writable**: only `status === in_progress` and before `ends_at`. `created` → `SESSION_NOT_STARTED`; `submitted`/`scored`/`expired`/`void` → `SESSION_CLOSED`; `in_progress`-in-storage but past the deadline → `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` — the same split `AssessmentSessionDeadlinePolicy` already uses on the write side, reused at the error-code level, not just the general rule. No new error codes.
- **Never writes**: unlike the autosave/submit actions, this read never seals an overdue session to `expired` itself — proven by an explicit before/after-row-equality assertion on a rejected past-deadline read.
- **One statement, not two, for revision + answers**: PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED gives a fresh snapshot per *statement*, not per transaction, so two separate SELECTs could let a concurrent autosave's commit land in between them and report a revision that doesn't match the returned answers. Fixed by reading both in a single `LEFT JOIN` statement, and proven empirically with a PostgreSQL-only fork+socket-barrier race test (this can't be demonstrated on SQLite's single-writer model).
- **Strict whitelist response**: `{session_id, answers_revision, answers:[{item_no,value}]}` — structurally impossible to leak answer keys or scores, since the `answers` table has no such columns at all.
- Same ownership mechanism as the rest of this lane (byte-identical 404 for nonexistent vs. foreign-owned), and the same DASS-21 exclusion mechanism proven in #49.

Full write-up in [`tasks/handoffs/f2/session-answers-readback.md`](tasks/handoffs/f2/session-answers-readback.md).

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/Architecture/AssessmentSessionHttpBoundaryTest.php` — extended with the fourth controller's route/dependency boundary proof
- [x] `tests/Feature/AssessmentSessions/AssessmentSessionAnswersReadbackTest.php` — 11 SQLite tests (happy path + ordering, empty list, all four non-readable states, exact-deadline boundary with no-side-effects proof, byte-identical 404, DASS-21 exclusion, strict-whitelist shape)
- [x] `tests/Postgres/AssessmentSessionAnswersReadbackControllerTest.php` — 3 tests, 23 assertions: happy path + foreign-404 through the real controller under the `psikotes_runtime` non-owner/`NOBYPASSRLS` role, plus the torn-read race test, green on the first run
- [x] Full SQLite sweep (`tests/Feature/AssessmentSessions`, `tests/Unit/AssessmentSessions`, `tests/Architecture`): 341 tests, 2428 assertions, green
- [x] Full `phpstan` gate (level 7): 0 errors

body:
## Summary
**Stacked on #4** (base is `docs/agents-md-rename`; GitHub retargets this PR to `main` once #4 merges). Only the three commits on top of #4 are in this diff.

Makes the backend architecture of `server/` explicit for agents **and** mechanical for CI.

- **`onion-architecture` skill (v1.0.0)** — `.claude/skills/onion-architecture/`: four rings (domain, application, infrastructure, presentation), seven rules, a "where does X go" table, module template, workflow and checklist, plus eight `references/` (layers, Fastify presentation, Drizzle persistence, ports/adapters for tools, composition root/DI, testing by layer, enforcement, DevDigest mapping with known drift and a suggested migration order). `README.md` holds the design decisions, versioning and the source list.
- **dependency-cruiser rules** — `server/.dependency-cruiser.cjs`: no cycles, pure domain/ports, ORM only in repositories (mappers may import row *types*), vendor SDKs only in `src/adapters/`, no service-locator `Container` in inner code, no cross-module internals, no import of the module registry.
- **Baseline** — the 33 pre-existing violations are frozen in `server/.dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json` and ignored with `--ignore-known`, so only **new** violations fail. It must only shrink.
- **CI** — new "Architecture rules" step in `server-unit.yml`.
- **Sources** — `docs/skill-research/onion-backend-sources.md`: every source with a verification status and the position taken where sources disagree (e.g. repository interfaces live in the application ring; the service owns the transaction).
- `server/AGENTS.md` points at the skill; three entries appended to `server/INSIGHTS.md`.

No file under `server/src/` is changed.

## Decisions taken with the owner
- Enforcement = skill **and** dependency-cruiser rules.
- Rules bind **new and touched code**; existing drift is baselined and migrated in separate tasks (order in `references/devdigest-server-mapping.md`).
- **Pragmatic** domain: contracts + pure functions, no entity classes or aggregates.

## Notes
- The CI step calls `depcruise` inline (no `arch:check` script) because `server/package.json` is `skip-worktree` in this repo.
- The installed dependency-cruiser (17.4.3) has `depcruise-baseline`; the `--baseline` flag from newer docs is not available there.
- `tsPreCompilationDeps: true` is on so `import type` leaks (e.g. `AgentRow` in a service) are caught.
- Validated before release by a dry run on a throw-away `notifications` module (contract → domain → port → service → table + migration → mapper → repository → route → container wiring → tests at every ring, incl. an integration test on real Postgres). It found one defect in the rules themselves (`mappers.ts` was flagged although the skill places it beside the repository) — fixed here. The module was **not** committed.
- **Not verified:** that the skill's `description` triggers in a fresh session; the new CI step has not run on GitHub yet (locally: depcruise exits 0 with the baseline, typecheck clean, 101 unit tests green).
- Sources marked 🔎 in the registry (dependency-cruiser rules tutorial, one InversifyJS article) were located but not opened; one Medium article returned 403 and is not cited.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI `server unit` is green, including the new **Architecture rules** step
- [ ] `cd server && pnpm exec depcruise src --config .dependency-cruiser.cjs --ignore-known` → no violations, 33 known ignored
- [ ] Add `import { eq } from 'drizzle-orm'` to a `routes.ts` → the check fails (revert afterwards)
- [ ] Markdown links inside `.claude/skills/onion-architecture/` and `docs/skill-research/` resolve
- [ ] Ask a fresh Claude Code session to "add a `notifications` module" and check it scaffolds `ports.ts` → service with narrow deps → repository/mapper → thin route, without `Container` in the service or `db/schema` in the route

author: nitunsi
body:
Dokumentation einer Datenrunde in Supabase (`trainer.html` unverändert).

## Der Duplikat-Check hat die Liste von 8 auf 6 korrigiert

Zwei der gemeldeten „Lücken" gab es längst — beide waren im ersten Durchgang durchgerutscht, weil dort über das Skelett der **Kursschreibung** gesucht wurde:

| Kurswort | gesucht als | unsere Zeile | Skelett dort |
|---|---|---|---|
| `samahni` | `smhn` | 563 `sama7ni` سَمَحْنِي | `sm7n` |
| `sba7` | `sb7` | 1478 `es-sbe7` الصُّبَاح | `ssb7` |

Uni-Wien schreibt ح als `h`, unsere Konvention als `7`; und ein Artikel (`es-`) steckt bei uns mit im `darija`. Beides verschiebt das Skelett. Dazu ein Präzedenzfall-Eintrag mit der Regel: vor der Suche in unsere Konvention übersetzen, Artikel abtrennen, und immer zusätzlich über die deutsche Glosse mit `\y` suchen — `\yentschuldig` hätte 563 sofort geliefert.

## 6 neue Zeilen (4598–4603), nicht fällig gesetzt

`3rousa` (Braut) · `sour` (Zaun/Mauer) · `soura` (Sure) · `sin` (Buchstabenname س) · `sabir` (geduldig) · `mazel sba7` (Es ist noch Morgen)

Keine `progress`-Zeile angelegt, Gegenprobe 0 — sie stehen in Bucket 0 und tauchen nicht in der Fälligkeitsschlange auf. Das weicht bewusst von der Standardvorlage in `COURSE_MODE.md` ab, die im selben Zug fällig setzen würde.

Interne Gegenprobe vor dem Schreiben bestanden: `_arabic_to_chatalpha(arab) = darija` und `_translit_skeleton(darija) = _arabic_skeleton(arab)` für alle sechs.

## Die س/ص-Falle, zweimal abgefangen

Ninjas `sin` ist صِين *China* und `soura` ist صُورَة *Bild* — beide gehören nicht zu unseren Wörtern. Diesen zwei Zeilen wurde deshalb bewusst **kein** Audio angehängt. Bei `soura` vermischt schon die Kursglosse „Sure; Form" zwei Wörter, die TUNICO getrennt führt; angelegt ist die س-Variante سُورَة, passend zum س-Block der Übung.

## Kursverknüpfung auf beiden Ebenen

- **`course_exercises.vocabulary_id`**: 8 weitere Übungen verknüpft → ohne Verknüpfung jetzt **4 statt 12**. Die vier sind 3 Eigennamen (gehören nicht in den Bestand) und `702 la bas`, das noch zur Entscheidung steht.
- **`course_lessons.vocab_lesson_refs`**: L2 und L4 um die Vokabeln ergänzt, die ihre eigenen Übungen per `vocabulary_id` referenzieren (L2 100→120, L4 63→82 ids). Kein Textabgleich, sondern die bestehende Verknüpfung — also keine Homograph-Gefahr. Beide Teile des Pflichtformats `ids:…|darija:…` getrennt geparst und neu zusammengesetzt.

## Nicht angefasst

3 tote ids in den Refs (3672 in L2, 4450/4451 in L4). Altbestand — die Ergänzung kann keine erzeugen, sie zieht ihre ids aus einem Join gegen `vocabulary`. Nach dem P4-Vorbild gehört dazu die Suche nach der Ersatzzeile, nicht das bloße Streichen.

## Abnahme

|---|---|
| `vocabulary` | 3.783 (vorher 3.777, +6) |
| `progress` für 4598–4603 | 0 |
| Gruppe A | 0 |
| Check 21 / 22 | 1 / 231 (unverändert) |
| `pronunciation` ohne Verknüpfung | 4 (vorher 12) |
