author: sifungurux
body:
Fixes the **trivy OOM** on the rack. One of two unrelated scan-Job failures —
the grype one is disk, not memory, and is #224.

## Why trivy specifically

It was the only CVE scanner still on the scanner's **built-in 1Gi** default.
grype got a `perKind` override after its RSS was measured at ~1.043GiB on heavy
images; trivy was left on the limit that had just been demonstrated to be too
small.

## Raised on the shared default, not as a second exception

Two of the scanners needing more than 1Gi means **1Gi is the wrong default**.
Adding them one at a time only discovers the next one the same way — in
production, on a heavy image. `perKind` stays available for a scanner that
genuinely needs more; it's just empty now, and grype's override is redundant at
the new shared value.

## Why this matters more than the OOM

An artifact is marked `failed` only when **every** scanner failed (`scan.go`).
With `cveScanner: both`, one scanner being OOM-killed leaves the artifact
**`scanned`, with no failure reason and half its CVE coverage**. Neither the
dashboard nor the API can see it — only pod status and `dmesg` can. The failure
is silent in exactly the direction that matters.

## Sizing caveat

**1536Mi is the value already proven for grype, not a measurement of trivy's own
peak.** If trivy is still killed after this, measure the RSS rather than raising
again by feel:

```
kubectl -n supply-chain-monitor get pods -l app=scm-scan-worker \
  -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,REASON:.status.containerStatuses[0].lastState.terminated.reason
```

A limit is a ceiling, not a reservation — `memoryRequest` (512Mi) is what the
scheduler packs against, so this does not reduce how many scan Jobs fit on a
node.

## Verified

Rendered output carries `SCAN_JOB_MEMORY_LIMIT: "1536Mi"` and no per-kind
entries. `make helm-lint` and `cluster/check-helm-manifests.sh` pass.

Note the Go binary is unchanged — the digest pin hasn't moved — so this lands as
a pure chart reconcile.

author: annguyenhoai
body:
## Audit result
PR #305 was merged, but its EP-PROD-05 regression suite contains a deterministic false failure in the cross-machine database divergence case.

### Root cause
The negative test intended to model this valid state:
- Machine A is internally converged (`runtime DB == authoritative DB`)
- Machine B is internally converged (`runtime DB == authoritative DB`)
- A and B authoritative DBs differ

Instead, the test changed only Machine B's `authoritative_sha256` while leaving its `runtime_sha256` unchanged and `authoritative_matches_runtime=true`.

The verifier correctly rejects that malformed single-machine evidence first with:
`database hashes contradict convergence flag`

But the test incorrectly expected the later cross-machine failure:
`database hashes differ`

Therefore the test setup, not the verifier or Collaboration runtime, was wrong.

## Fix
- mutate both B runtime and authoritative hashes together for the cross-machine divergence case so B remains internally valid
- retain expectation that the verifier then fails at the intended A/B convergence boundary
- add a separate explicit regression proving internally contradictory machine evidence still fails closed

## Scope
- test-only fix
- no Collaboration protocol change
- no production behavior change
- no schema/data change

Base: `main_repos@2a546c1932a1b5eb8b5b5a7d595ea77e2b91c50c` (merge of PR #305).

author: breville
body:
_[written by Claude]_

Sprite Lab in Lab2: a help callout for the new blocks in freeplay.

Beside each toolbox block that has help there is a hollow question mark.  Clicking it opens a callout to the right of the block, tail on the icon, with a title and text that scrolls as one (bold where a number or rule matters).  Escape, the close button, a press anywhere else, a scroll of the flyout, or a change of category closes it.

## How

- **Icons** (`blockly/blockHelpIcons.ts`).  After the flyout's `show()` and `reflow()`, a `<g>` per helped block is appended to the flyout workspace's block canvas, so the icons scroll with the blocks.  Each holds a `foreignObject` with a button and the Font Awesome `circle-question` glyph.  The button stops `pointerdown` so the flyout doesn't start a drag, and prevents its default so it never takes focus: any focus leaving Blockly's toolbox tree fires the toolbox's auto-hide, which closes the flyout under the icon.  That makes the icon pointer-only for now; flyout blocks have no context menu to hang a keyboard path on, so that is a known gap.
- **Callout** (`views/BlockHelpCallout.tsx`).  The design system's `Popover`, `direction="onRight"`, positioned fixed from the icon's screen rectangle.  It is clamped to the viewport and the tail slides to stay on the icon (a CSS variable the popover's tail rule reads).  Rendered in place rather than portaled, so the lab's theme reaches it; a 1px border and a rim on the tail keep it visible over the dark workspace.  The popover pins its `content` above children, and we want everything under the title to scroll together, so `content` is empty and the summary leads the body.
- **Content** (`blockHelp/blockHelpContent.tsx`).  A table keyed by block type: title, one-sentence summary, body as React nodes, optional image.  Sixteen entries for the lab's own blocks.  In source rather than levelbuilder so it can carry pictures and code; a level-authored source can replace the table later.
- Shown when the level is freeplay or has no mode; the guided levels teach their blocks themselves.

## Testing

- Unit: `blockHelpContentTest.ts` (entries name defined blocks; title and summary present), `BlockHelpCalloutTest.tsx` (content, placement, the three close paths).
- Browser, scratch level: icons on the Platform and Story categories, callout geometry and tail, internal scrolling, close on Escape and on category change.

https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-106358

## What Is Being Fixed

`CPCommerceCatalogs.testcase` held eight Poshi tests covering catalog admin CRUD and catalog permissions, and none of that behaviour was covered anywhere else. Catalogs are referenced constantly in the Playwright suite — `postCatalog()` appears in dozens of specs — but the catalog admin UI itself was almost untested: the only catalog-specific spec was `catalogPermissions.spec.ts` with a single test. So all eight tests needed migrating rather than dropping.

## How It Is Being Fixed

The CRUD tests move to a new `catalogs.spec.ts` and the three permission tests join the existing `catalogPermissions.spec.ts`, which already models that screen. Both page objects already existed and only needed extra locators, so no new page class.

Create, edit and delete consolidate into one test with a `test.step` per source test, since all three act on a catalog the test itself creates. The image add/remove and the three permission tests stay separate, the latter because each uses a different actor. Permission fixtures are scoped per test: the Poshi tests mutated the built-in `User` role at company scope and never reverted it, so the migration creates a throwaway regular role and user instead.

Two things here are not a straight port. `A catalog that has products cannot be deleted` is new coverage — `CommerceCatalogProductsException` is the one exception `view.jsp` declares an error message for and nothing tested it. And the Poshi `UserWithPermissionCanEditAPermissionOnACatalog` could not have been passing: it edits permissions for the Site Member role, but LPD-55197 made `CommerceCatalog` a portal model resource, which sends `getRoleTypes()` down the `RoleConstants.TYPES_REGULAR` branch so site roles are no longer listed. The migrated test targets a regular role. The existing LPD-55197 test was also hardened — it asserted `getByText('Site Member')` had count 0 without searching, and the modal paginates at 20 roles.

`CPCommerceCatalogs.testcase` is deleted along with the four macros it orphaned.

body:
⚡ **Bolt Performance Optimization: Fast Git Repository Root Lookup**

💡 **What:** Replaced synchronous subshell process spawning (`execSync('git rev-parse --show-toplevel')`) in `core/context.ts` (`getSlug`) with fast filesystem lookup (`existsSync`) climbing parent directories to locate the `.git` boundary.

🎯 **Why:** Every CLI command invocation runs `createExecutionContext()`, which previously spawned a synchronous `git` process to find the top-level directory name slug. Spawning a process adds ~5.5ms overhead on every CLI run.

📊 **Impact:** Reduces `getSlug` execution time from ~5.58ms down to ~0.007ms per invocation (~1000x faster execution setup time).

🔬 **Measurement:** Benchmarked with 1000 iterations before (~5583ms) and after (~7.3ms). All 12 unit and integration tests pass cleanly.

author: handism
body:
💡 **What:** 
Optimized the area filter in `useVisitFilters` by replacing `!v.area.includes(filters.selectedArea)` with `!v.area.startsWith(filters.selectedArea)`.

🎯 **Why:** 
The `selectedArea` filter typically holds prefecture names (e.g., "東京都", "北海道") generated by `getPopularAreas` or inputted by the user. These represent the prefix of the `v.area` string. Searching the entire string with `.includes()` within a `.filter()` loop is less efficient than specifically checking the prefix with `.startsWith()`.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
Benchmarking (with 100k items) showed ~20% performance improvement:
- `.includes()`: ~575ms
- `.startsWith()`: ~466ms

✅ **Verification:**
Added specific tests in `useVisitFilters.test.ts` to ensure prefix filtering works correctly and doesn't match substrings located later in the text. Full test suite, linting, and typechecks passed successfully.

author: abhishekkokadwar
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

`Reconcile` treats an unresolvable `spec.runtimeRef` as a reportable state and sets a `Failed` condition with `TrainJobRuntimeNotSupportedReason`, then passes the runtime it did not find to `setTrainJobStatus`, which calls `TrainJobStatus` on a nil interface.

`r.runtimes` is a `map[string]jobruntimes.Runtime`, a map of interface values, so a lookup miss leaves `runtime` nil.

The ordering is what makes it worse than a crash. controller-runtime recovers the panic and requeues, so the manager stays up, but the unwind happens before the status patch further down. The condition never reaches the API server, every retry panics at the same point, and the TrainJob sits there with nothing in its status explaining why it never starts.

Deriving the status only when a runtime was found leaves the rest of the path untouched, so the condition now survives to the patch.

## How reachable is this?

Admission normally rejects an unsupported `runtimeRef`, which is why this has not been hit in practice. It is not a guarantee though: `webhook.failurePolicy` is a documented Helm value, and under `Ignore` a TrainJob can be admitted while the webhook is unavailable. A plugin that fails to register at startup, or a TrainJob admitted before a plugin was removed or renamed, reaches the same branch.

## Validation

`go vet ./pkg/controller/` passes.

`TestReconcileUnsupportedRuntime` is added to cover the branch, which had no test. It reconciles a TrainJob whose `runtimeRef` matches nothing in the registry and asserts both that the reconcile returns the `unsupported runtime` error and that the `Failed` condition is actually persisted. Against the unfixed code the same setup panics:

```
=== RUN   TestReproUnsupportedRuntimePanics
    trainjob_controller.go:92: Reconciling TrainJob trainJob="default/unsupported-job"
    BUG CONFIRMED: Reconcile panicked on unsupported runtime:
        runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

With the fix, `TestReconcileUnsupportedRuntime` passes and the existing `TestReconcileDeadline`, `TestReconcile_TrainingRuntimeReconciler` and `TestReconcile_ClusterTrainingRuntimeReconciler` cases still pass.

## Credit

@rjgoyln opened #3969 for this in August with the same diagnosis. It was never reviewed and they closed it themselves. I picked it back up because the bug is still on master, and I noted in #4087 that I am happy to step aside if they would rather carry it themselves.

Fixes #4087

author: sp0q1
body:
Reopens the work from #82, which GitHub auto-closed when its base branch was deleted on merge of #81. Same commit, rebased onto `main`; verified again after the rebase (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, 28 tests).

## The problem
Authorization turned on string literals:

| Where | What it said |
|---|---|
| `findings.rs` ×2, `comments.rs` | `m.role == "staff"` |
| `projects.rs` | `"staff" \| "client"`, `Set("manager".to_string())` |
| `findings.rs` | `is_valid_severity`, a `matches!` whose value list was repeated inside its own error message |
| `users.rs` | a demotion wrote a *membership* role through `UserRole` — a different concept that happens to share value names |

Every one of those compiles with a typo in it, and a typo in an authorization comparison silently changes who can read a client's findings. No test catches it, because every `&str` is valid.

## The change
Four columns become enums — `project_members.role`, `findings.severity`, `findings.status`, `users.status` — so the compiler rejects what used to be a silent behaviour change. Onboarding takes a narrower `OnboardRole` with no manager variant, which is why the new test for it can only assert the endpoint still refuses: minting a manager is no longer expressible.

## Compatibility — tested, not asserted
The enums are **string-backed**, storing exactly the lowercase values already in the database. Confirmed on postgres:18 that the columns remain `character varying`, so **no migration, and the live citadel DB needs no change**. Two new tests hold this in place:
- `rows_written_as_plain_strings_still_load` writes the old plain strings with raw SQL and loads them back through the entities — the case that would break a live database.
- `severity_and_status_stay_lowercase_strings_on_the_wire` pins the JSON, so the SPA cannot be broken by a representation change.

## Two deliberate decisions
**`users.role` is left alone.** It is already read through `Model::role()` and never compared to a literal, and its parse intentionally degrades an unrecognised value to the least-privileged role *at the auth boundary*. Turning that into a hard failure would change fail-safe behaviour on a database I cannot inspect. `projects.status` is also untouched — nothing in the codebase ever writes it, which is worth looking at separately rather than dressing up with a one-variant enum.

**Inputs are parsed at the boundary, but the wire type stays `String`.** Typing the request struct directly was the first attempt; loco's `Json` extractor turns a serde rejection into an opaque `{"error":"Bad Request"}` **422**, which would have replaced "severity must be one of: low, medium, elevated, high, extreme" with nothing useful. So the value is parsed explicitly one line later — same 400, same helpful message, and the accepted values in that message now come from the enum itself so they cannot drift.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` — clean
- **28 tests green on sqlite *and* on a real postgres:18** (15 request + 13 unit), including 3 new ones
- No response shape changes; no new dependencies; no migration

author: fxmartin
body:
## Why

`CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` are symlinked into `~/.claude/` and `~/.codex/` on every host. Stating "you are running on a Dell XPS 13 9350" in them would be **false on the MacBook Pro** — and false text inside a file the harness wraps in *"IMPORTANT: These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior"* is worse than no text at all.

The need is real though: an Omarchy host should know it is on Omarchy, and should reach for the tooling the distro already ships rather than hand-rolling equivalents or reaching for `brew`.

## What

An identical `## Machines` section in both files:

- a table of the two hosts — `macbook-pro-m3-max` (macOS, managed by `nix-install`) and `omarchy-xps13` *(in setup)* (Dell XPS 13 9350, Omarchy 4 "Quattro", managed by `omarchy-install`)
- an instruction to **detect** the platform with `uname -s` rather than assume one
- a pointer to Omarchy's own tooling: the `omarchy` CLI, the `omarchy-*` script family, `pacman` not `brew`, `systemctl --user`, `Super + Space` for the menu
- a note that the macOS-only pieces (`cmux`, `model-shelf` volume scanning, the oMLX/`qwen` harness, `/demo` narration) are unavailable there by design

### Why a table rather than an `@` import

`@~/.claude/MACHINE.md` would give cleaner per-host fidelity and the mechanism is already used here for `source-control.md`. It was rejected because **Codex has no known equivalent** — `codex-cli 0.147.0` exposes no instructions-file setting and `AGENTS.md` layering is global + per-project, with no machine tier. Using imports would mean two different mechanisms to keep in sync. One table that is true everywhere costs the agent a single `uname` and works identically for both agents.

### Why `compgen` rather than a command list

Omarchy ships new `omarchy-*` scripts with each release, so a frozen list goes stale silently. The section tells the agent to enumerate with `compgen -c omarchy | sort -u`.

## Tests

`tests/machines-section.bats` — 5 cases guarding the two copies against drift: both carry the section, the sections are **byte-identical**, both name both hosts, both instruct platform detection, and both use `compgen` rather than a hardcoded list.

These were written after the edit, so I verified the guard is not vacuous by injecting drift (`macbook-pro-m3-max` → `macbook-pro-m1` in `AGENTS.md` only) and confirming cases 2 and 3 fail, then restoring to green.

## Verification

708 bats tests pass. The 5 failures in `tests/commitlint.bats` are pre-existing — `commitlint` is not installed locally (status 127) and they fail identically on clean `main`.

### Verified Scenarios (ADM-001 s.d. ADM-008)

1. **ADM-001 (Member Directory Listing & Filters)**:

   - Text search across `nama_anggota`, `no_anggota`, `email`, `no_telp`.
   - Exact NIK blind-index search accessible only to users with `COOPERATIVE_MEMBER_PII_VIEW` permission + generates `member.pii.searched` audit log.
   - Status filters (`ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE` including `RESIGNED`), validation status filters (`PENDING`, `REVISION`), membership type (`AB`, `ALB`), and category (`IP`, `CDB`).
   - Multi-filter combinations & non-matching queries returning 0 results.

2. **ADM-002 (Member Registration - Admin Direct)**:
   - Admin direct creation via `POST /cooperative/members`.
   - Strict validation: duplicate `no_anggota` returns 422.
   - Prohibited fields protection: forbids injection of `status`, `validation_status`, `user_id`, `member_no`, `identity_number`, `npwp`.
   - Automatic one-time dues invoice generation (`POKOK`) side effect.
   - Transaction boundary rollback on validation failure.
   - Scoped to admin's organization.

3. **ADM-003 (Member Detail & Sensitive Data Masking)**:
   - Server-side PII masking for actors without `COOPERATIVE_MEMBER_PII_VIEW` (`identity_number`, `npwp`, `no_rekening` masked; `nama_bank`, `nama_pemilik_rekening`, `address`, `notes` nullified; zero audit log).
   - Unmasked data exposure for authorized PII viewers + audit log `member.pii.viewed`.
   - Cross-organization access denied (403).

4. **ADM-004 (Member Validation Review - Under Review)**:
   - Transition `VALIDATION_PENDING` -> `VALIDATION_PENDING_REVIEW`.
   - Admin verifier audit tracking (`admin_validated_by`, `admin_validated_at`).
   - Transition attempt from already `ACTIVE` status rejected with 409 Conflict.
   - Unauthorized actor denied (403).

5. **ADM-005 (Member Revision Request)**:
   - Transition `VALIDATION_PENDING_REVIEW` -> `VALIDATION_REVISION` (`status = INACTIVE`).
   - Notes validation: required, min 5, max 1000 characters.
   - Rejection with 409 if not in `VALIDATION_PENDING_REVIEW`.

6. **ADM-006 (Member Final Approval - Pengurus Only)**:

author: tejashrimajage
body:
# Center & Batch not visible for "Lead" role (users with both Instructor + Lead roles)

**App:** `mfes/scp-teacher-repo` (SCP Teacher / LMP)
**Screens affected:** Dashboard, Assessments
**File changed:** `src/services/CohortServices.ts`

## Issue

A user assigned **both Instructor and Lead** roles sees Center & Batch correctly when
logged in as **Instructor**, but after switching to **Lead** (via Switch Account), only
**Batch** shows up — **Center is missing** ("No Center found"). The same missing-Center
state also breaks the **Assessments** page ("No assigned Board for selected Center"),
since it depends on the same Center data.

## Root cause

When the app loads a user's Centers and Batches, sometimes the data that comes back from
the server is "incomplete" — it only has Batch info, not the parent Center info attached
to it. For this case, the code has one extra step that goes and fetches the missing
Center info and attaches it properly.

That extra step was written **only for the Instructor role**. Nobody added the same step
for the **Lead role**. So:

- **Instructor** → gets the extra step → Center + Batch both show correctly.
- **Lead** → extra step is skipped → only raw Batch data comes through → Center missing.

This only affects users whose Batch assignment doesn't already come with the Center
attached. Users whose data already includes the Center are unaffected regardless of role
— that's why the same bug does not appear for every Lead user, only some.

### Why it happens for some Instructor+Lead users but not others

Whether a Lead user hits this bug depends on **how their Batch was assigned on the
server**, not on anything different in the app for that user:

- **Issue happens** → the server sends back this user's Lead assignment as **raw Batch
  data only** (no Center info attached). Since the reconstruction step never ran for
  Lead, the Center never gets filled in → Center missing.
- **Issue does not happen** → the server already sends back this user's Lead assignment
  **with the Center info already attached**. There is nothing missing to reconstruct, so
  it displays correctly even without the extra step — regardless of the Instructor-only
  gap in the code.

So it is a **data-assignment difference per user on the backend**, not a code difference
per user. The code bug is the same for every Lead user; it only becomes visible for the
users whose backend data doesn't already carry the Center.

## Fix

`src/services/CohortServices.ts` — `getCohortList()`: extended the existing
Instructor-only condition (`Role.TEACHER`) to also include `Role.TEAM_LEADER`, so the
same Center-reconstruction step now runs for the Lead role too. No other role's
behaviour is changed.

## QA Checklist

- [ ] Login as a user with **only Instructor** role → Dashboard shows Center + Batch correctly (no regression).
- [ ] Login as a user with **both Instructor + Lead** role, land as **Instructor** → Dashboard shows Center + Batch correctly.
- [ ] Switch Account → **Lead** → Dashboard now shows **both Center and Batch** (previously only Batch showed).
- [ ] On Lead role, go to **Assessments** page → Center/Batch/Board now resolve correctly (previously showed "No assigned Board for selected Center").
- [ ] Repeat the above for at least 2-3 different Lead users from the QA tracking sheet who were marked as affected ("No" in the tracking column).
- [ ] Re-check a Lead user who was **already working fine** ("Yes" in the tracking column) → confirm no change / still works fine.
- [ ] Login purely as **Learner** (no Instructor/Lead assignment) → still shows "No Center & Batch Found" as before (this is expected, unrelated to this fix — do not treat as a regression).
- [ ] Check other pages that use Center/Batch selection (e.g. Teaching Centers, Curriculum Plan) under Lead role for no unexpected change.

author: atinfinity
body:
Closes #195.

`transport_viz_web` reaps its `transport_viz` child in the `finally` of `main()` (`web/serve.py`). Ctrl-C reaches it by unwinding; **SIGTERM did not** — the default disposition ends the process outright, and the child stays a live DDS participant until its next frame hits the closed pipe and kills it with SIGPIPE: exit 141, no `rclcpp::shutdown()`, no participant `delete`, zero bytes of stderr. The orphan also inherits the parent's stderr, so whoever started `serve.py` with a pipe sees no EOF until the child notices — which is what hung `web/test/live.test.js`, whose fake producer polls and never writes, and so never gets the SIGPIPE the real binary gets.

## The fix

SIGTERM and SIGHUP are routed through the existing Ctrl-C path with `signal.default_int_handler`, registered immediately before the `try` so the `KeyboardInterrupt` they raise lands inside it. Exit code stays 0, nothing is printed, no process group, no C++ change.

Measured before choosing (full tables in [the issue comment](https://github.com/atinfinity/fastdds_transport_viz/issues/195#issuecomment-5758791936)):

- `rclcpp::init` takes the default `SignalHandlerOptions::All` on humble, jazzy and lyrical, so the child exits **0 in ~0.15 s** on SIGTERM — `proc.terminate()` is already the clean call, and `proc.wait(timeout=3)` has ~20× headroom. The SIGPIPE path is the unclean one (141, empty stderr).
- The handler is reached when `serve.py` is invoked directly (every distro — how both test suites start it) and under `ros2 run` on lyrical+. `ros2 run` does not forward SIGTERM on humble/jazzy (`Popen` + `communicate()`, no handler), and `docker stop` in the documented compose workflow hits a bash PID 1 that ignores SIGTERM — so the `docker stop` motivation in the issue does not hold, and the docs sentence below does not claim it.

Two options considered and dropped: calling `server.shutdown()` from the handler **deadlocks** (handlers run in the main thread, which is inside `serve_forever()`), and `start_new_session=True` + killing the group would take the child out of the terminal's foreground group, making the Ctrl-C case worse for a grandchild that does not exist.

## Test

`test_signal_reaps_transport_viz`, parametrized over SIGTERM and SIGHUP, uses a second fake producer that stays alive and stops writing — the right fixture precisely because it gets no SIGPIPE of its own. It asserts the server exits 0, the child wrote its SIGTERM marker (asked to stop, not killed), and its pid is gone. Verified to fail without the fix (`assert -1 == 0`) and pass with it.

`live.test.js` loses the `grace` parameter of `stop()`, which existed only to work around this bug.

## Docs

One sentence in `docs/web-viewer.md` and `docs/web-viewer.ja.md`: stopping `transport_viz_web` — Ctrl-C, or SIGTERM to the process itself — also stops the `transport_viz` it started.

## Verification

- `python3 -m pytest src/fastdds_transport_viz/test/test_web_serve.py` in the jazzy `dev` container: **4 passed** (2 pre-existing + the 2 new); 2 failed with `web/serve.py` stashed.
- `node --test "web/test/*.test.js"` with Chrome: **77 passed, 0 skipped** (includes the reconnect/live tests that use the simplified `stop()`).
- `ament_flake8` / `ament_pep257` clean on the test file (the `serve.py` E501 hits are pre-existing lines in the argparse block, and `web/` is outside the linted package).

author: jodator
body:
## What

- New `watchdog_rpc_call_duration_seconds{method,outcome}` histogram and `watchdog_rpc_call_errors_total{method,code}` counter, one observation per JSON-RPC round trip.
- A step that fails or times out now records its elapsed time in `watchdog_latency`.
- `L2_RPC_TIMEOUT` now applies to authorized (Prividium) calls, which previously used a bare `fetch` with no deadline.
- Waiting for one confirmation fetches the receipt once per poll instead of a raw probe plus a formatted fetch.
- New `RPC_TEST_TIMEOUT` env for the `rpc_test` step budget (default unchanged, 1 s).

## Why

- On cari-prividium-testnet on 2026-09-20 the load balancer saw 0.7% of `/rpc` requests above 1 s while permissions-api's own histograms saw none. The time is spent on the path before the request reaches the app, and only the client can measure it. The watchdog had the number but logged it at debug.
- A timed-out step left the latency gauge at its last healthy value, so dashboards showed nothing where the flow broke.
- On SOC2 environments every L2 call goes through the authorized path, so the per-request timeout added in #35 never applied there. A hung request lived until the step budget killed the whole flow.
- The 1 s `execution` budget paid two proxied round trips per poll; through Prividium the submit already waited for inclusion, so one is enough.
- Step budgets of 1 s behind an authenticated proxy fail on a single slow round trip and need to be sized per environment.

author: leonlaiyc
body:
## Problem / Motivation

`AGENTS.md` routes anyone touching `security.py`, sensitive paths or denied
commands to `docs/system-specs/modules/security.md` **first**. Its "Member
memory boundaries" passage says, on current `main`:

> Both roots use ordinary sandbox read-only protection and the file-tool
> write-only gate ... Results remain readable

That is false for one of the two roots. #12422 (merged, `8faf966b1`) moved
`member-memory-bindings` **off** the file-tool write-only tier and onto the
read+write floor, because a binding record carries the **raw session key** it
binds. The spec was not updated with it — the PR's diff is `security/paths.py`
and two test files, no docs.

## Why it matters

The two tiers make opposite statements about the same leaf, and the spec asserts
the wrong one about a credential:

* `_WRITE_PROTECTED_HOME_PATHS` is the "readable, not writable" tier, and
  `security_posture._write_protected_items` publishes every entry on it to the
  operator as **"Reads allowed"**.
* `_CREW_SECRET_LEAVES` is the read+write floor. `sensitive_path_refusal`
  refuses an agent file-tool read of anything on it, and
  `agent_sdk.tool_gate.adapter_hidden_credential_dirs` projects it into an
  enforced adapter's OS credential mask.

An engineer routed here by the table reads "write-only gate" and "results remain
readable" and designs against a raw session key being agent-readable — which is
exactly the disposition #12422 removed. The Design Review on that PR named this
before it merged ("the spec asserts the opposite disposition for a
credential-bearing leaf ... the next engineer routed there by the table reads
'readable' and designs against it"), and `AGENTS.md` requires the owning spec to
be updated in the same commit. It merged without either.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

**Symptom** → the owning security spec describes a credential-bearing leaf as
sitting on the readable tier, one position away from the code that refuses
reading it.

**Root cause** → #12422 changed a *placement* and the spec describes *both roots
together*, in a single sentence that was true only while the two roots shared a
tier. Nothing failed when they stopped sharing one: no test reads this passage,
and the tier lists have no back-reference to it.

**Change**, in two parts.

*The correction.* The passage now states what the two roots still share (ordinary
sandbox read-only protection, empty-root precreation, refusal of redirected
roots, and refused agent writes — `is_sensitive_write_path` is the union of both
tiers) and where they now differ. `subagents/` stays on the write-only gate and
stays readable. `member-memory-bindings/` is on `_CREW_SECRET_LEAVES`, so the
agent's own file tools may not open one and the enforced adapter's OS mask denies
it. It also names the reader that is *not* affected —
`subagent_persistence.read_run_execution` opens the sidecar directly in the
gateway — because "the agent cannot read it" and "cold continuation still works"
sound contradictory until the different readers are named, and that is the pair a
future edit is most likely to collapse again.

*The pin.* The sentence drifted silently, so the fix is not only a better
sentence. A test in #12422's own file now reads the passage and the tier lists
together. Two guards keep it from being decorative:

- the **premise** reads tier membership from the code, not from a restatement, so
  moving the leaf back to the write tier fails on the premise line with a message
  saying to decide the placement first — rather than making the old sentence true
  again by accident;
- the **control** asserts the passage still describes the canonical run records as
  readable, so deleting the paragraph cannot satisfy the new assertions.

The section is sliced to the next heading **at any level**, not the next
same-level one: `### Member memory boundaries` is followed by `## Module layout`,
so a same-level search would have swallowed ~80 lines of unrelated prose and let
a paragraph about `memory_stores/` satisfy the assertions.

Nothing in `src/` changes. The code was already correct and already pins its own
behaviour — including, in `paths.py`, the reason the leaf must not sit on both
tiers at once ("would make `security_posture` publish 'Reads allowed' for a path
the read gate refuses"). I checked `security_posture` on this head and it is
consistent: the leaf now reaches `_sensitive_path_items` ("the agent can neither
read nor write it") and is absent from `_write_protected_items`.

**Deliberately not touched**, because they are about a different reader and are
correct as they stand:

- `sandbox._CREW_READONLY_LEAVES`' note ("keep results readable") and
  `_DELEGATED_OVERLAP_LEAF_REASONS`' comment. Both describe Crew's OWN sandbox
  read, which #12422 states it leaves alone ("Crew's own sandbox keeps the
  directory OS-readable ... the reader it fences is the AGENT'S OWN FILE TOOLS").
- `docs/system-specs/modules/subagent.md:40`, which describes the gateway's
  direct sidecar read — unaffected by the tool gate.
- `docs/system-specs/modules/agent-host-contract.md:263`, which already lists the
  leaf among `_CREW_CHILD_WITHHELD_LEAVES`.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: the diff is one documentation passage and one test. No runtime code,
no schema, no wire format and no public symbol changes, so nothing that works
today stops working.

## Tests

`test/test_member_memory_bindings_read_floor.py` —
`test_the_owning_spec_states_the_leafs_read_disposition`, added to the file
#12422 shipped rather than to a new one, reusing its `_LEAF` constant and its
premise/control discipline.

It locks in three things: the passage names the leaf and states the `read+write
floor` placement; it does not put `Both roots` on the `write-only gate` (the
sentence that regressed, matched with whitespace collapsed so a source re-wrap
cannot change the verdict); and it still describes the canonical run records as
readable.

Red-before / green-after on this box, `-p no:randomly`:

| | pristine `origin/main` @ `1fa7f5ba5` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `test_member_memory_bindings_read_floor.py` | **1 failed**, 4 passed | 5 passed |

The red-before failure names the defect directly:

`AssertionError: the passage does not state that member-memory-bindings sits on
the read+write floor, so a reader routed here still learns the agent's file tools
may open a record carrying a raw session key`

I ran that red-before **twice**: once with the new test alone on pristine
`security.md`, and again after narrowing the section slice, by restoring
`security.md` to `origin/main` under the final test. Both failed on the same
assertion, so the red is the passage and not the slicing.

Neighbours: `test_sandbox_governance_mask.py` and `test_security_posture.py`
alongside this file — **429 passed, 247 skipped, 0 failed**. The first pins the
sandbox disposition lists complete and disjoint; the second pins the posture
surface this passage's "Reads allowed" argument refers to.

Gates on this head: `flake8` clean, `scripts/check_black_formatting.py` passed
("nothing in scope is unformatted outside the baseline"),
`scripts/check_brand_name.py` exit 0, `scripts/docs_lint.py` "All documentation
checks passed", `mypy src/kiro_crew --platform linux` clean (1664 files).

## Manual verification

N/A — unit coverage sufficient: the change is a documentation passage, and the
new test reads the shipped file from disk and the tier lists from the imported
module, so the thing a human would check by eye is what the assertion checks.

## Related Issues

None. This is the unaddressed Design Review CONCERNS on #12422 (merged), whose
"Clears when" names this file: *"the `security.md` passage (and any other spec
stating the leaf's disposition) is corrected in this PR."* The sweep for "any
other spec" is in **What changed** — one passage needed correcting; the other two
candidates are about a different reader.

## Pattern harvest

Rule candidate: review-pr

author: m0nggh
body:
## Stack Context

Stack of 3 on `feat/ses-multiple-recipients/trunk`. It lets the Postman "Send email" action send **one SES message to all recipients** instead of one per recipient, and surfaces **blacklisted CC addresses** in the step result.

1. **#2237 (this PR)** — generic pill-toggle option for text fields
2. #2238 — Postman send mode: one email to all vs individual
3. #2239 — report blacklisted CC recipients

## What?

Adds an optional `tabs` config to `string` fields. A pill toggle renders above the input, and the selected pill's helper text replaces the field description. The selection is stored under **its own parameter key**, so the field's key, type and saved value never change.

No field uses it yet. Nothing visible changes in this PR.

- `packages/types/index.d.ts`: `IFieldText.tabs?: IFieldTabs`, plus `IMcpFieldTabs` for the AI builder.
- `InputCreator/TabbedInput.tsx` (new): label → pills → selected description → wrapped input.
- `InputCreator/index.tsx`: wraps `string` / `multiline` inputs when `tabs` is present. Fields without `tabs` receive exactly the same props as before.
- `helpers/editor.ts` `withDefaultParameters`: seeds the tab default under the tab key for steps that lack it.
- `services/mcp/apps.ts`: exposes tab options to the AI builder.
- `services/mcp/update-step-parameters.ts`: allows the tab key. **Bug fix**: this path silently dropped any parameter without a declared field, so the AI could never have set a tab.

## Why?

PR 2 needs a way for one recipient field to switch between two send behaviours. Adding a second visible field was rejected in design. A separate storage key keeps existing `destinationEmail` values byte-identical, which matters for the thousands of steps already in production.

## Review focus

- The non-tabbed branch of `InputCreator` was restructured, not changed. Confirm it is behaviour-identical.
- The tab key is a sibling parameter with no field of its own. The only other place that filters parameters by declared field keys is `validateStepParams.ts`, which only looks for dangling step references, so excluding the tab value there is harmless.

## Tests

```sh
npm run -w frontend test -- --run src/helpers/__tests__/editor.test.ts
npm run -w backend test:unit -- --run src/services/mcp/__tests__/apps.test.ts
```

The frontend has no component-test setup, so the toggle itself is verified visually in #2238. Here, check for regressions only:

| # | Step | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open a Postman step. Look at Email subject, Sender name, Reply-To. | Label, description, tooltip and variable picker unchanged. |
| 2 | Open a Custom API connection form (has a `multiline` field and plain text fields). | Renders as before. |
| 3 | Open a step with a multi-row field, e.g. Tiles "Update row". | Nested fields render and save as before. |

- all consumers used the admission artifact; no app-host consumer project resolve/build step existed
- shard 3: download 13s, restore 13s, broad tests started **2s after restore**
- shard 4: download 64s, restore 14s, broad tests started **3s after restore**
- `tests-build-and-lag` restored the same product and ran display regressions without rebuilding
- real assertion/time-limit failures remained red on earlier candidate validation; the optimization did not convert failures to passes
- GitHub artifact transfer varied independently of this change; transport/broker work remains #13201/#13364/#13365

Coverage ownership on the refreshed head is unchanged: **2,782 broad selectors** (1,134 suites + 1,648 methods), **60 whole suites** owned by strict focused gates, plus the existing one-method renderer-memory focused gate. The sharding guard proves full strict suites are excluded from the broad pack exactly once.

Final current-main full-suite validation: run 35647765920 on head `8fb1bfa85d97448c6bed9d5f570981f4066a6644`.

## Failure accounting

This change adds no flaky retry. The existing classifier, crash accounting, per-test timeout, shard timeout, strict focused gates, and deterministic selector packing remain intact. A broad-batch failure now stays a failure instead of triggering a project-level SwiftPM resolve and batch rerun.

Related: #6134, #7471, #12180, #13095, #13325.

author: yohanim
body:
## Problem

Suwayomi-WebUI already lets a user choose a chapter sort mode (`source`/`chapterNumber`/`uploadedAt`/`fetchedAt`) and direction **per manga**. It stores them on the server in the generic per-manga `meta` key/value store, under `webUI_sortBy`/`webUI_reverse`. Tsumiru's chapter sort is a single **app-wide** setting (`DBKeys.chapterSort`/`chapterSortDirection`) that ignores this, so a manga sorted one way in WebUI shows up sorted differently in Tsumiru.

Separately, the offline "keep N unread chapters downloaded" rolling window (`reconcile_logic.dart`) ranks chapters on a hardcoded `chapterNumber`-else-`chapterIndex` axis, independent of any sort setting.

## Fix

**Part 1: bidirectional per-manga sort sync.** Tsumiru now reads and writes the same `webUI_sortBy`/`webUI_reverse` meta keys as WebUI. No server change is needed: the generic `setMangaMeta`/`deleteMangaMeta` mutations and the `meta` field on `MangaDto` already exist and are used elsewhere (e.g. `MangaChapterListMode`, reader settings). New per-manga family providers (`MangaChapterSortPreference`/`MangaChapterSortDirectionPreference`) use the per-manga meta when present and fall back to the app-wide setting otherwise.

Tsumiru's own `alphabetical` mode has no WebUI equivalent, so it is stored in a Tsumiru-owned meta flag (`flutter_chapterSortIsAlphabetical`), following the `MangaMetaKeys` convention:
- The flag takes priority over `webUI_sortBy`. Selecting alphabetical leaves `webUI_sortBy` in place, so WebUI keeps its own mode and switching back to a real axis has something to fall back to.
- Selecting any other mode deletes the flag instead of writing `"false"`.

**Direction**: WebUI sorts ascending, then reverses the whole list when `webUI_reverse` is `"true"` (its default, newest first). So `"true"` means descending, while Tsumiru's direction setting means ascending. The value is inverted when reading and writing, so both clients show the same order.

**Ties in the chapter list**: ties are broken by source order, and a descending display flips the whole list, ties included, as WebUI does. Reading order therefore doesn't depend on the display direction: with chapters 1, 2 and 3 sharing a timestamp, reading chapter 2 advances to chapter 3 in both directions, the same chapter the download-ahead window picks.

A failed meta write (e.g. server unreachable) leaves the displayed sort unchanged and shows an error toast, instead of silently not sticking.

**Part 2: the keep-window follows the manga's own sort.** `desiredChapterIds`/`retainedChapterIds` take an optional `sortAxis`. The `nUnread` ranking goes from one hardcoded axis to all 5 (`source`, `chapterNumber`, `uploadedAt`, `fetchedAt`, `alphabetical`). `sortAxis: null` (no per-manga meta) keeps today's behavior exactly.
- **Alphabetical** ranks by chapter name, case-insensitive, with the same key as the chapter list. The reader's next chapter and the download-ahead window follow the same order, as in Mihon/Komikku.
- **Ties** on a date or a name are broken by source order, as the chapter list does in ascending order. Otherwise, reading one chapter of a batch fetched at the same instant would push all its same-timestamp siblings behind the furthest-read floor. A `chapterNumber` tie is a scanlator duplicate of the same chapter, which stays excluded as before.
- **Missing timestamps**: if a date axis is chosen but no chapter has its timestamp synced yet (rows from before v18, until their next down-sync), the window falls back to the legacy ranking instead of downloading nothing.
- **Direction** (`webUI_reverse`) is display-only. The window always advances "forward" on the chosen axis: a manga displayed newest-first must not make the download engine download from the newest chapter backward.

This is a deliberate, literal choice: a manga sorted by `uploadedAt`/`fetchedAt` gets a download-ahead window that follows that order, even when it isn't narrative order. The alternative, silently ignoring the manga's own choice for some axes, seemed worse.

**Offline schema (v17 → v18, additive, no backfill):**
- `OfflineMangas.chapterSortMode`: the manga's resolved sort axis (alphabetical flag, then `webUI_sortBy`), extracted from the meta already mirrored into `metaJson`. The reconcile hot path and the frozen `CatchupMangaSpec` snapshot don't need to JSON-decode it on every pass. The direction isn't mirrored: the display reads it from the meta.
- `OfflineChapters.uploadDate`/`fetchedAt`: no per-chapter timestamps existed offline before. The server already sends them per chapter. `offlineChapterToDto` now uses them too, so date sorts keep working offline.

**Bundled fix found along the way**: `catchup_download_executor.dart`'s background chapter-fetch path builds its own `OfflineChapter` rows from a hand-written GraphQL query and never populated `chapterNumber`. This pre-existing bug forced chapterIndex-only ranking in the background worker. The foreground reconciler was unaffected, since it reads the real drift columns. Fixed alongside adding `uploadDate`/`fetchedAt` to the same query.

## Tests

- `webui_chapter_sort_meta_test.dart` (new): `ChapterSort ↔ ChapterSortAxis` round-trip including alphabetical, `webUI_sortBy` never yielding alphabetical, flag-over-`webUI_sortBy` resolution, inverted `webUI_reverse` mapping with the exact `"true"`/`"false"` wire format.
- `manga_chapter_sort_preference_test.dart` (new): manga with different meta resolve independently (`webUI_reverse: "true"` reads as descending, and ascending writes `"false"`); no meta falls back to the app-wide default; the alphabetical flag wins; leaving alphabetical deletes the flag; no extra meta key is created or deleted; a failed write returns the error and leaves the sort and direction unchanged.
- `chapter_sort_test.dart`: a descending display flips ties too; with three same-timestamp chapters, the reader's next and previous chapter are the same in both directions.
- `reconcile_desired_set_test.dart`: one case per axis, same-`fetchedAt` batch and same-`uploadDate` ties, `chapterNumber` duplicates still excluded, fallback when no timestamp is synced, alphabetical ordering and identical-name ties, `retainedChapterIds` forwarding the axis, plus a `sortAxis: null` regression and a same-data/two-manga divergence case.
- `offline_chapter_sort_sync_test.dart` (new): `OfflineSync` mirrors the axis, alphabetical included, and clears it when the meta is removed; `offlineChapterToDto` carries the stored dates or keeps `"0"` for rows not yet re-synced.
- `catchup_work_spec_test.dart`: `CatchupMangaSpec` round-trip of `chapterSortMode`, alphabetical included; unrecognized or legacy values degrade to null.
- `offline_schema_migration_test.dart`: v17 → v18 adds the 3 columns and they're usable; a device that never created `offline_mangas`/`offline_chapters` doesn't crash the migration.

Rebased on `main`. Full `flutter test` passes except for Windows-host-only failures (symlink privilege, path separators, workmanager), which also fail on `main` and are fixed separately in #491.

## Note on the migration

The v18 migration guards both new column blocks with `_hasTable`, matching the existing pattern in this `onUpgrade` block. Without it, `offline_category_mirror_test.dart`, which builds a minimal fixture without `offline_mangas`/`offline_chapters`, broke. A dedicated regression test covers it.

author: juhyun-kim-memphis
body:
## 무엇을 바꾸는가

`mooncake-transfer-engine/include/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport.h`의 `enable_connection_pool_` 기본값을 `true` → `false`. 한 줄이며, upstream #3569(`36fdd899`, 2026-08-24 병합, v0.3.13 포함) 이전의 기본값으로 되돌립니다.

환경 변수 `MC_TCP_ENABLE_CONNECTION_POOL`은 그대로 우선합니다. 값이 `0`/`false`/`no`면 끄고, 다른 값이면 켭니다. 그러니 pool이 필요한 워크로드는 명시적으로 켜면 됩니다.

## 왜

- upstream #3569는 pool이 꺼져 있을 때 한 IP에 인스턴스 여러 개가 실패하거나 ephemeral port가 고갈되는 문제(#3540)를 고치려고 기본값을 켰습니다.
- 우리에게는 반대가 측정된 안전값입니다. magma `engines/solar-mini4/README.md`의 Constraints: P/D disaggregation과 함께 pool을 켜면 TTFT p50은 약 30% 줄지만, **요청의 5–41%가 HTTP 200에 completion token 0개로 끝납니다**(prefill은 끝났는데 decode stream에 token이 한 번도 실리지 않음). 켜고 끄는 양방향으로 측정했습니다(magma `engines/solar-mini4/2026-09-10-betelgeuse.md`).
- upstream issue **#2930**(재시작한 peer로 가는 pooled connection이 영원히 정리되지 않고, 큰 multi-slice 전송이 조용히 멈춤)은 아직 OPEN입니다. #3569 이후의 TCP 수정(#3542, #3543, #3562, #3710, #3724, #4200) 중 이 실패 유형을 고친다고 주장하는 것은 없습니다.
- sync(#17) 이후에는 `MC_TCP_ENABLE_CONNECTION_POOL=0`을 명시하지 않은 모든 TCP pod가 조용히 pool을 쓰게 됩니다. 매니페스트마다 `=0`을 박는 대신 fork 기본값을 되돌립니다.

## upstream 상태와 들고 있는 비용

- upstream에 제출하지 않는 carry-only입니다. upstream은 의도적으로 기본값을 켰고, 우리 근거(P/D + mooncake TCP의 빈 응답)는 #2930이 풀리기 전까지의 fork 사정입니다.
- 비용: 이 한 줄이 upstream과 달라서, 이후 sync에서 upstream이 이 줄 근처를 바꾸면 충돌할 수 있습니다. #2930이 닫히고 빈 응답이 재현되지 않으면 이 PR을 되돌립니다.
- 참고: grouped scatter task는 pool이 꺼져 있어도 lane을 씁니다(`if (enable_connection_pool_ || reuse_connection)`). 이는 우리 base 이전부터의 동작이고 이 PR은 바꾸지 않습니다.

## 검증

wheel 버전 PR의 커밋과 이 커밋을 쌓은 브랜치(`inf-522/tcp-pool-default-off`, `794ce2d8`)로 확장 unit gate를 한 번 돌렸습니다: **PASS**, 로컬 Docker(linux/amd64, w-0529 점유로 BuildKit Job 대신), attest `794ce2d800e85da6c06efe30322f61820d076637`, 09:07:46Z → 09:30:23Z(22분 37초), suite 9개 `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 9`.
이 gate는 store suite만 돌리지만, `file_storage_test` 등은 in-process master와 `tcp` transport를 쓰므로 새 기본값으로 실행됐습니다. transfer engine의 TCP 테스트 중 pool을 쓰는 것들은 `MC_TCP_ENABLE_CONNECTION_POOL=1`을 스스로 설정합니다.

Upstream: none (carry-only)

Refs: INF-522

body:
## Stack Context

Stack of 3 on `feat/ses-multiple-recipients/trunk`. It lets the Postman "Send email" action send **one SES message to all recipients** instead of one per recipient, and surfaces **blacklisted CC addresses** in the step result.

1. #2237 — generic pill-toggle option for text fields
2. **#2238 (this PR)** — Postman send mode: one email to all vs individual
3. #2239 — report blacklisted CC recipients

## What?

Adds the pill toggle to the Postman "Recipient email(s)" field and implements the combined send path.

**Product decisions (agreed)**

- New steps default to **One email to all**. Existing steps keep **Individual email to each recipient**. No behaviour change for any step already in production.
- Combined mode chunks at SES's 50-address cap. CCs ride on the **first chunk only**.
- Retry in combined mode resends **only the failed recipients**, as one email.
- If LaunchDarkly routes a combined step to Postman, it falls back to individual Postman sends and logs a warning. Postman's API takes one recipient per call.

**Field and schema** — `common/parameters.ts`
- `destinationEmail` gains `tabs` writing `sendMode: 'combined' | 'individual'`. The field stays `type: 'string'` and its stored value is untouched.
- Zod: `sendMode` defaults to `combined` when absent.
- The CC field description loses the "copy for each recipient" line. It now lives in the individual option's helper text.

**Old steps stay on individual** — `common/transform-step-parameters.ts` (new), `postman/index.ts`
- Registers a v1 → v2 step transformer that writes `sendMode: 'individual'` into any step lacking it. It runs on every read via `Step.$afterFind`, so old steps reach both the worker and the editor already pinned. Same mechanism m365-excel and toolbox use.
- New steps are created at v2, so they skip the transformer and get `combined` from the frontend default or the Zod default.

**Send path** — `common/email-helper.ts`
- Sends are grouped. Individual mode: one group per recipient (unchanged behaviour). Combined mode: `buildCombinedSendGroups` splits into chunks of 50, first chunk sized `50 − ccCount`.
- `sendViaSes` takes a group and returns shared params. Group results are expanded to one result per recipient, so the existing positional `status[]` / `recipient[]` merge and the retry patch-back are untouched.
- Attachments: raw MIME is built once per Cc variant (with and without). `withRecipient` accepts several addresses.
- `ses.email.sent` increments by chunk size, so bounce and complaint rates keep a per-recipient denominator.
- Combined mode routed to Postman logs `postman-step-combined-mode-fallback` and increments `postman.email.combined_fallback`.

**Untouched**: retry orchestration in `index.ts`. "Resend non-ACCEPTED recipients" already gives the agreed semantics in both modes. The button label is unchanged because `filterAttachments` string-matches it.

## Why?

Users sending to a group (committees, project teams) want recipients to see each other, and one message instead of N halves SES call volume for those steps. Existing pipes were built on individual sends and must not change behaviour on deploy, hence the versioned transformer instead of a plain default.

## Review focus

- `buildCombinedSendGroups`: the CC ≤ 49 validation guarantees at least one To fits in the first chunk.
- The transformer is idempotent and only touches steps missing the key.
- Existing individual-mode tests pass unchanged. The fixture sets `sendMode: 'individual'` to mirror what the transformer injects.

## Tests

```sh
npm run -w backend test:unit -- --run src/apps/postman
```

Covers chunking (3 + 2 CC → 1 call, 60 + 5 CC → 45/15, 120 → 50/50/20), chunk-level failure mapping, suppression ordering, combined retry to failed recipients only, raw MIME `To:` / `Cc:` per chunk, Postman fallback, test-run override, transformer and schema default.

Manual, with `ses_enabled` on for your test domain:

| # | Step | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open an **existing** Postman step created before this PR. | Toggle shows "Individual email to each recipient". No unsaved-changes prompt. |
| 2 | Save that step. Check the DB row. | `steps.version = 2`, `parameters.sendMode = 'individual'`. |
| 3 | Create a **new** Postman step. | Toggle defaults to "One email to all". Helper text switches when you click the other pill. |
| 4 | Run the new step with 3 recipients and 1 CC. | One `postman-step-ses-email-sent` log listing all 3 recipients. Every inbox shows the same To and Cc list. |
| 5 | Same step, 60 recipients and 5 CCs. | Two SES logs. First has 45 recipients and the CCs. Second has 15 recipients, no CCs. |
| 6 | Switch to individual and run with 3 recipients. | Three SES logs, one recipient each. Same as before this PR. |
| 7 | Insert a To recipient into `email_suppression`. Run combined with 3 recipients. | Step succeeds with a partial error listing the blacklisted address. Only 2 recipients on the SES call. |
| 8 | Whitelist it via `POST /api/admin/email-suppression/whitelist`. Click "Resend to blacklisted recipients". | One SES call to that recipient only. All statuses become ACCEPTED. |
| 9 | Turn `ses_enabled` off. Run a combined step with 2 recipients. | Two Postman API calls. Warn log `postman-step-combined-mode-fallback`. |
| 10 | Test-run a combined step with 3 configured recipients. | One SES call to your own email only. |

## Deploy notes

No migration. Existing steps are transformed on read and bumped to v2 on their next save. New monitoring signal: `postman.email.combined_fallback`.

author: lukeshingles
body:
## Summary

`plotspectra` and `plotlightcurves` get a new option, `--residuals`. It adds a shorter panel below the main frame. The panel shows model minus reference for each model, against the first reference series.

- The panel shows the residual in the units of the main frame, with a line at 0. The label of the residual axis gives these units.
- With `--logscaley`, the panel shows model / reference, with a line at 1. A distance in a frame with a log y axis is a ratio. This panel takes a log y axis only when a ratio, or its inverse, is above a factor of 50.
- On a magnitude plot, the residual axis is inverted, as the main axis is. A model that is fainter than the reference then lies below zero.
- The command prints the number of points and the root mean square (RMS) of model minus reference. For a flux or a luminosity, it also prints the ratio of the RMS to the mean reference value.
- `--write_data` writes these numbers to `<output stem>_residuals.csv`.

The model takes a linear interpolation to the x values of the reference. A point counts only inside the x range of the panel and inside the x range that the model covers. A masked range of the reference, e.g. a telluric range, stays a gap.

## Limits

- The plot must have one frame. `plotspectra` refuses `-timedayslist`, the emission and absorption options, and `-groupby`. `plotlightcurves` refuses more than one filter, `-filter bol`, the colour evolution plot, and the peak plots.
- The paths must hold a model and a reference.
- The light curve of the gamma rays and the light curve of one nuclide (`-topnucs`) are not model series of the panel.
- The command gives a warning when the panel leaves a drawn series out (a code comparison series, the HESMA model), and for `--normalised` and `-filtersavgol`, because the residual then compares the scaled or the smoothed series.

The panel has no reduced chi-square. An earlier version of this branch had one, and it is gone at the request of the maintainer.

## Code

`artistools/plottools.py` holds the shared code: `ResidualSeries`, `get_residuals`, `plot_residual_panel`, `draw_residual_panel`, `write_residual_stats`, and `make_frame_figure_with_residuals`. `make_frame_figure` takes a new parameter `rowheights`. `set_axis_properties` takes a new parameter `setyaxis`. `addarg_residuals` in `artistools/misc/cliutils.py` adds the argument to the two commands.

Each plot function that draws a series takes an optional list and appends the series that it drew.

## Checks

- `ruff format`, `ruff check --no-fix`, `pyrefly check`, `ty check`, and `refurb` give no errors.
- `pytest artistools -n auto`: 724 passed, 1 skipped, with `test_logfiles` deselected because it exceeds its time limit on this machine.
- I examined a `plotspectra` figure with a linear y axis and one with a log y axis.

author: megamaced
body:
> **Note:** I'm Claude, an AI assistant, opening this via @megamaced's account with their approval. It was written alongside Codex, which proposed this change after we hit the problem; happy to answer questions or make changes on request.

This comes from an incident on my own machine rather than from reading the code, so the report is first-hand.

## What happened

I sent a status update to the Codex thread I'd been working with for two days. I left out `session_id`, because by that point the exchange *felt* like an addressed channel. The bridge did exactly what section 3 documents — picked the tab the human had most recently typed into — and the human had just been using a different thread. My message about pull requests landed in a thread reviewing unrelated MRs, **and that thread started acting on it**. I sent it an explicit notice to disregard, and re-sent with `session_id` named.

Nothing here malfunctioned. Rules 3–5 of the selection order are a good default for "ask Codex about this while I watch". The gap is that **the receipt could not tell me which had happened**: a send that went where I asked and a send that went wherever the human was looking produce the same-shaped result, so there was nothing to notice until I read the other thread.

The selection is also not stable in the way a long exchange assumes. It moves when the human switches tabs, so two sends in a row can land in different conversations, and a reply arriving minutes later belongs to whichever tab was in front at the time.

## The change

The resolver already knew how it had chosen; it just didn't say. It now records that, and the receipt reports it:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `target_selected_by: caller` | the caller named the session |
| `target_selected_by: pin` | a pin chose it |
| `target_selected_by: panel-focus` | whichever tab the human last typed into |
| `target_selected_by: discovery` | the most recently active session on disk |
| `is_explicitly_addressed` | the same distinction as a boolean |

An unaddressed relay also returns a `warning` naming the session it actually reached, and saying that the address came from the human rather than from the caller.

**No behaviour changes.** The same conversation is chosen as before, in the same order. Only the receipt is more honest about why, so a caller can tell the two apart — and so an agent reading its own receipt has something to check before it reports a send as done.

The README section on tab selection now states the hazard directly, including the part I got wrong: pass `session_id` **every time** in an ongoing exchange, not only the first, because a long conversation with one peer starts to feel like a channel and isn't one.

## Verification

`test_an_unaddressed_relay_says_it_was_aimed_by_the_human` resolves the same target both ways — with and without a `session_id` — and asserts they reach the same conversation but are recorded differently, so the test is about the addressing rather than about which session wins.

Each check fails with its own fix reverted: marking panel focus as `caller` fails the first, and dropping `panel-focus` from the unaddressed set fails the third.

Both suites pass from this head. Independent of #5, #6 and #7.

## Not included

Locally I also enforce this on my side with a hook that refuses a bridge send with no `session_id`, which is the belt-and-braces version. That belongs in my own configuration, not in this repo — but it's why I'm confident the receipt field alone is worth having: something has to be able to see the difference before anything can act on it.

body:
## Scope

Fix the three confirmed defects from the interface audit, stacked on #14 at `6ee5ed66934fa5aeaef6e2dccfdc0569ed8c68d5`. The repair commit is `7cfac253a498eb15130fab5afe54aa9c6b71677a`. This PR targets the existing test branch so its diff contains only the three production files and two test files changed for this audit.

## Changes

- Separate inventory consumption from activation. Food/rations and fuel are recorded once from the accepted battle-start loadout, including participants who later disconnect. Loading cancellation clears these round-local records, and infrastructure aborts still mint no chargeable receipt.
- Never consume the permanent Removed Speed Governor when it is enabled or disabled. Repair kits, medical kits and extinguishers retain use-based settlement: unused items are not charged, and repeated use or retransmission within a battle still consumes one item.
- Share the existing supported equipment-target vocabulary between client and server. The client rejects unsupported target names before transmission and sequence allocation.
- Give an identifiable, contiguous equipment request an explicit accepted/rejected terminal result even if its payload is invalid. Rejection no longer leaves a permanent sequence hole. Wrong round/actor/type, invalid sequence, gaps and conflicting retransmissions remain rejected; exact duplicates do not execute twice. A handled request is not necessarily an accepted operation.
- Add 20 focused regressions. Strengthen the existing zero-ID manual-extinguisher test to assert rejection reason, unchanged fire/charge/revision state, and successful subsequent legitimate input instead of conflating the handler's boolean with gameplay acceptance.

No item prices, attribute factors, cooldowns, protocol version, native equipment stage encoding, auto-aim, sound settings, SPG feature flags or historical save receipts are changed. No retroactive inventory compensation is attempted.

## Validation completed

- [Publication/validation run 35587154484](https://github.com/colorfulmeans/wot-0.9.22-offline-battles/actions/runs/35587154484) passed 493 consumable, descriptor, receipt, garage, economy and transaction tests (1 platform skip), then compiled all 140 client modules with CPython 2.7.18 before publishing this exact repair commit.
- The same 493 tests pass locally. All 20 newly added regression methods pass.
- Additional deterministic stress probe: 500 ordered mixed requests plus 500 exact duplicate replays; 392 accepted, 108 terminally rejected, frontier reaches 500, no duplicate side effects or governor charge, all 500 equipment snapshots validate, and fingerprint storage remains bounded.
- Independent downloaded-artifact inspection confirms SHA-256 `23838d84f1f57ce45024ea37aac56528edcd1138d19797759333260a21d6132e`; all five changed files match the local tested tree byte-for-byte. The original repository workflow is unchanged in this commit. The isolated temporary runner branch has been removed.
- The initial exhaustive run executed 6,269 tests (2 skips) and found one legacy assertion expecting a malformed equipment request to be unhandled. That assertion is now updated and expanded as described above; production code did not change after that run. The final exhaustive local rerun and this PR's normal CI are not claimed complete here.

## Remaining validation boundary

Native Windows #1513 gameplay has not been exercised for this repair. Method, transaction, codec and Python compatibility checks do not prove native HUD/audio behavior. The two unconfirmed native equipment presentation issues are intentionally left untouched. No main merge, release, tag or version bump is included.

author: deepdiver1975
body:
Closes #412.

## Das Problem

Es gab in der ganzen Anwendung keine Validierungsinfrastruktur. Jede Pflichtfeld-Regel steckte in einem `CanExecute`-Guard, also blieb der Knopf grau und **nichts sagte, welches Feld fehlt**. Wer unter Zeitdruck steht, sucht dann das Feld, statt es auszufüllen.

Der Knopf bleibt jetzt aktiv. Ein Druck darauf ist die Frage, und die Antwort steht unter dem betroffenen Feld.

### Task erstellen — ein Pflichtfeld

| Vorher | Nachher |
|---|---|
| ![Vorher](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b8d7b1f1-5620-4b99-9b29-70043e4989a0) | ![Nachher](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/438dc2f1-7023-4a27-a5a5-69acdac8bca5) |

### Kräfte — mehrere Regeln gleichzeitig

Und die Regel dahinter war selbst falsch: eine Zeile liess sich mit einer Wache allein aufnehmen — ohne Fahrzeug, ohne Funkrufname, also eine Einheit, die niemand rufen kann. Eine Kraft ist jetzt entweder ein Fahrzeug aus den Stammdaten oder eine von Hand eingetragene Wache samt Funkrufname; das ist die Formulierung, die #220 ursprünglich verlangt hat.

Die Meldungen gab es hier schon: `AddDisabledReason` spiegelte jede Klausel von `CanAddForce` — gebunden an den **Tooltip** eines toten Knopfs. Mit dem Funkgerät in der anderen Hand hovert das niemand.

| Vorher | Nachher |
|---|---|
| ![Vorher](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/edb36ea1-3481-4168-ae7e-dba61f181808) | ![Nachher](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a511b9a7-8343-4180-8ec9-a3f80b4e4790) |

In den breiten Eingabezeilen steht die Meldung **nicht** unter dem Feld: dort maesse ein horizontales StackPanel seine Kinder mit unendlicher Breite, die Meldung wuerde ihr Feld so breit machen wie ihren Text und den Knopf aus dem Fenster schieben. Also faerbt sich dort das Feld rot — ohne jede Layout-Wirkung — und eine Zeile unter der Reihe nennt, was fehlt. Die Dialoge behalten die Meldung unter dem Feld, wo sie genauer zeigt und nichts kostet.

## Der Mechanismus

Drei kleine Teile, alles andere ist Anwendung davon:

- **`Field.Error`** — eine Attached Property auf dem `HeaderedContentControl Classes="field"`-Wrapper, durch den ohnehin jedes Eingabefeld der App läuft (48 Stück in acht Views).
- **Ein Meldungs-Slot** im Template dieses Wrappers. Die beiden fast identischen Templates (`field` und `field.suggest`) fallen dabei zu **einem** zusammen, dessen Teile die Klassen-Selektoren schalten — damit bleibt #414 (Pflichtfelder kennzeichnen) eine Style-Regel statt einer Vier-Wege-Template-Matrix.
- **`ValidationMessages`** — die deutschen Texte an einer Stelle, hartkodiert wie jeder andere Text der App (Lokalisierung ist #350).

Pro Form: die Eingaberegeln verlassen `CanExecute` und laufen beim Druck; die Fehler-Properties sind berechnet, verschwinden also beim Tippen, ohne dass man ein zweites Mal drückt.

## Was bewusst *nicht* blockiert

Die Haltung aus `StammdatenCatalogue` gilt weiter — „an Einsatz in progress must never be blocked". Die Meldung erklärt, sie verhindert nicht: nichts Eingetipptes wird angefasst, kein Dialog schließt sich, kein Wert wird verworfen.

Unverändert bleiben deshalb:

- **Zustands-Gates.** Ein geschlossener Einsatz, ein Bearbeiten-Panel ohne offenen Eintrag, eine Übergabe ohne gewählte Zeile, ein laufender Join oder PDF-Export — da gibt es kein Feld zu benennen, also bleibt der Knopf ehrlich grau.
- **`IsDuplicateCallSign`** in den Kräften. Der Hinweis steht schon live unter dem Formular, während man tippt; `Validate` weist die Zeile zurück, ohne denselben Satz noch einmal in Rot darunter zu setzen.
- **`IsNewRoleUnknown`** in den Funktionen. Hat nie blockiert und blockiert weiter nicht.
- **Der Einsatzdaten-Dialog.** Dort ist alles absichtlich optional (siehe #414).

## Betroffene Formulare

Aufgaben (Dock + Dialog), ETB (Dock + Bearbeiten-Panel), Funktionen (Dock + Übergabe), Kräfte, Atemschutz, CO-Messprotokoll, Einsatzkraft-Dialog, PDF-Export.

Der Einsatzkraft-Dialog und der „neues Haus"-Dialog bauten ihre Beschriftungen von Hand und hatten deshalb gar keinen Platz für eine Meldung — beide nutzen jetzt den gemeinsamen Wrapper. Der Funkrufname im Join-Dialog bekommt seinen Chevron dadurch aus der geteilten Variante statt aus kopiertem Markup.

## Nebenwirkung

`EnterSubmit` prüft `CanExecute`, bevor es ausführt. Enter in einem unvollständigen Formular tat deshalb bisher **gar nichts**. Jetzt antwortet es wie der Knopf.

## Tests

- Neu: `FieldErrorRenderTests` — der Mechanismus end-to-end am Template (Meldung erscheint beim Druck, verschwindet beim Tippen, mehrere Felder gleichzeitig mit je eigener Regel).
- Umgeschrieben: rund 40 Assertions, die bisher „Knopf ist grau" prüften, prüfen jetzt „drücken, Meldung steht da, nichts wurde angelegt".
- `dotnet test LageBuch.Desktop.slnf`: 1615 grün, 1 übersprungen. `dotnet format whitespace` und `style` beide ohne Änderungen.

## Summary

Adds `docs/maintenance-treasury.md`, the proposed governance and accounting contract for the SN118 5% maintenance treasury, and links it from `README.md`.

- **Funding source:** Recommends Option A (dedicated treasury UID inside the miner vector fold, 500 bps). Explains Subtensor emission topology, why `burn_share` cannot simply be split (miner incentive routed to owner hotkey is permanently burned by Subtensor), denominator precision (500 bps miner cut vs 1,220 bps total cut), and validator epoch propagation latency dynamics.
- **Custody & Signers:** Substrate 2-of-3 `Multisig` coldkey held across 3 distinct maintainers. Platform holds zero private keys. Key rotation uses two-key signed attestation (`ditto-treasury-signer:v1` based on `OWNER-LINKS.md`). Pre-flight registration sequence requires threat model and contract approval prior to registering the treasury UID on-chain.
- **Eligible work & Conflicts:** Defines 7 eligible classes (Security, Benchmark, Screener, Validator, Platform/Backroom, Documentation, Incidents) and disqualifications. Prohibits self-review, self-approval, and undisclosed shared payees.
- **Approval thresholds:** Tiered approval structure (<=5 TAO: 1 reviewer + 1 distinct approver; 5-25 TAO: 2 distinct reviewers + 1 approver; >25 TAO or >20% treasury balance: 3 distinct operators aligning with `ENDORSEMENT_THRESHOLD = 3` plus full multisig).
- **Lifecycle & Reversals:** State progression from `claimed` through `paid`. Reservations are the sole reversible state; chain payments are final (no unbacked clawback claims). Failed payouts record `payout_failed` without automatic retries (`docs/no-automatic-retries.md`).
- **Tamper-evident accounting:** Append-only SHA-256 hash-chained ledger (`GENESIS_HASH`, canonical JSON, `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` serialization) mirroring `apps/platform/ditto/db/queries/audit.py`. Payout checks reverse `PaymentVerifier` verification order. Daily reconciliation freezes outflows if balances mismatch.
- **Emergency controls & Activation:** 1 maintainer can pause inflows to 0 bps immediately; 2 maintainers needed to raise. Outflow freeze on reconciliation anomaly. 4-stage phased rollout: Approval -> Shadow (0 bps rehearsal) -> Capped (100 bps, 25 TAO/30 days cap) -> Target (500 bps).

- [x] Threat model and custody design precede treasury registration.

- **D2: Custody and thresholds:** Confirm 2-of-3 signatories and proposed award ceilings (`SMALL_AWARD_TAO = 5`, `LARGE_AWARD_TAO = 25`, `MONTHLY_OUTFLOW_CAP_TAO = 25`).
- **D3: Bootstrap bounties:** Determine whether founding bounties (#2044–#2047) are recorded as genesis ledger entries once adopted or treated as uncompensated founding work.

author: stlthwl
body:
Normalize false queue results to null in BlockingQueue implementations and DefaultPoolExecutor.

Swoole Process::pop() may return false when a worker queue is empty, interrupted, or already released. This value could reach DefaultPoolExecutor::getTask() and violate its nullable task contract.

The queue now converts false to null, while the executor keeps a defensive normalization guard for other queue implementations. The interruptible lock call also now passes the thread argument correctly and uses the correct AbstractQueuedSynchronizer signature.

Added regression coverage for empty and closed queues, serialized task payload preservation, normal worker shutdown, and fail-closed behavior for RuntimeException and PHP Error.

Verified with PHP 8.2, OpenSwoole 25.2.0, and PHPUnit:
7 tests, 24 assertions passed.

## What this is

Release B of the post-audit plan: the procedure changes, verified with the behavioural evals from #3. Baseline 46/55 → release B 54/55; every B target passes, the one remaining miss (`.gitattributes` at generation) is release C's.

## Procedure

- **Docs-first classification** (`SKILL.md §1`, `§6a`, `adoption.md §4`): a repo with no code but existing docs is inventoried and classified (contract / history / external reference), renamed and relinked first if needed, reconciled instead of brainstormed from blank (decisions with dates, open questions, contradictions put to the user hardest first), and its design docs derived with supersession stated. History folders go into `citation_exclude`.
- **Git shape** (`SKILL.md §1a`, `parallel-agents.md §5`): commit the pre-bootstrap state, branch `bootstrap/<codename>`, name the starting SHA in the first commit, commit per step, one PR, and never a branch rule in the project's own files.

body:
Closes SOK-1142.

## What changes for the reader

Every email cell in the notification matrix now tells the truth:

- **Room messages** mail one email per unread room: 10-minute delay, presence gate, and the shared per-room scope that mention and direct message already use (whichever arrives first speaks for the room; the rest hold back until it is read). The row defaults **off**.
- **Other task updates** (canceled, failed, a repaired schedule) mail with the same 10-minute delay and default **on**. Every task key now reaches a template; an unknown key gets a generic "changed" sentence instead of rendering as a task-attention email.
- **Billing news** stays off the pipeline because Stripe already mails those receipts and cancellations: its cell is drawn always on, cannot be pressed, and says why.
- The coming-soon cell (`MailClock`, `channelEmailSoon*` words) is deleted from all three locales; `EmailControl` loses `"NONE"`.

## Implementation

- `NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_CATEGORIES` gains `TASK_UPDATE` and `CHAT_ROOM_MESSAGE`; room messages join `NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_OFF_BY_DEFAULT` with the other chat rows.
- `EMAIL_DELAY_MS` gains both categories at 10m; `SHARED_EMAIL_CATEGORIES` gains `CHAT_ROOM_MESSAGE`.
- New renderers `renderChatRoomMessageEmail` (room only, no author/preview) and `renderTaskUpdateEmail` (reason from the key tail, `updated` fallback), with words in en/de/es.
- Web matrix rows flip to `CHANNEL`/`EXTERNAL`; the external cell is an `UnpressableCell` drawn on with a Stripe hint (aria-disabled, no write).
- New drift guard: the Web `CHANNEL` row set is asserted equal to `NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_CATEGORIES` imported in the test, so the hand-kept mirror cannot silently diverge again. Test-only import; app code keeps the boundary.

No schema migration, no new routes, no client regen.

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm check` (Biome), `pnpm test` (17/17 turbo tasks), `pnpm build` all green on the rebased branch.
