Closes #1203
Closes #1204

The furnished castle now has full-depth barred windows and placed candle fixtures, with verified day/night routes. This is the final delivery for furnishing (part 5/5) and lighting (part 3/3), after the renderer and catalogue parts already merged into `develop`.

- Open 18 main-wing windows and the four accessible tower apertures, clearing exterior trim while preserving roofs and guards. Advance worldgen to 37.
- Place 92 supported cosmetic fixtures alongside 117 furnishings (209 roots total), with complete rotated movement and placement checks.
- Tune the shadowed candle pool to four lights. Exclude celestial meshes from shadow casting so the sky dome cannot occlude sunlight; preserve existing ambient, weather and solar curves.
- Extend the production capture harness with real server-encoded prop snapshots, matched lighting/furniture switches, live entity counts and synchronized frame distributions. Keep distinct wing/lane traces and cover the bridge explicitly.

## Acceptance evidence

[Combined report](https://github.com/FabioSM46/voxelheim-v2/blob/24cf4785c3d65ddd5d79c3722ac90a69a4d4c624/docs/reviews/castle-lighting-acceptance.md) records 32 GPU stills, nine complete night videos (6,865 frames), fixed settings, provenance and reproduction. Four rotated open/blocked comparisons measure 11.92–20.06 times the blocked floor luminance. Final banquet capture: 1,403 live entities, 6 main / 79 shadow mesh submissions, four shadowed points, 12.121 / 12.917 ms p50/p95. These are bounded-scene synchronized CPU+GPU measurements, not full-game FPS.

All mandatory furnished routes pass in four rotations; fixture support, collision/clearance, roof shelter and snapshot decoding are verified. Artifact manifests validate source, digests, complete frame sequences and gate-to-gate trace endpoints. Large render artifacts remain local; the committed report describes their exact reproduction.

## Validation

- Server: format, vet, golangci-lint, native/386/ARM builds, complete tests.
- Client: format, clippy with warnings denied, locked build, 2,900 passed / 27 opt-in ignored tests.
- Complete automation helper suite and DeepSeek review tests.
- Publication and commit privacy scans.
- GPU captures on RX 9070 XT / Vulkan; matched window pairs and full night walks validated.

## Review size and ordering

Estimated final part before implementation: 60,000–75,000 reviewable characters, combining final placement with acceptance after the independent foundations. Measured: **88,510 local diff characters**, below the 90,000 cap. The increase includes GPU-discovered sky/trim corrections, route-export coverage and the measured acceptance report.

Targets `develop` after #1284 and #1285, whose exact-commit Integration runs passed. No remaining dependent PR is required for activation. The merge must be followed by exact-commit Integration verification.

## Acceptance criteria (including previously merged foundations)

### #1203

- [x] The great hall contains at least two long banquet tables with repeated place settings: plates, cups or drinking horns, bread, fruit, platters and serving vessels, with chairs/benches on both sides. Table legs, seat backs and tabletop objects have recognizable geometry at normal player distance.
- [x] An elevated high table or throne dais forms the end of the hall, with a clear central approach, carved seat, banners and a bordered carpet leading toward it.
- [x] Furnish distinct spaces: council room with map table and chairs; kitchen/pantry with preparation surface, shelves and barrels; guard room with benches and equipment racks; library/study with bookcases and writing desk; upper tower rooms with lookout seating or a scholar's desk. Keep existing NPC work areas usable.
- [x] Lay colored woven rugs and runners through selected halls, galleries and stair landings. They sit on the floor without z-fighting, floating edges, trip hazards or visual clipping through steps.
- [x] Add coherent Norse details: timber carving, knotwork-inspired rug borders, hanging banners, shields and trophy displays. Use a consistent dark stone, warm timber, iron and deep red/ochre palette; keep silhouette and useful sightlines readable.
- [x] All mandatory routes and reserved clearances from the architecture issue remain open after dressing. No table, chair or display intersects a doorway, resident anchor, stair landing or spawn/respawn position.
- [x] Furniture placements and orientations agree between players, survive reconnect and chunk unload/reload without duplicates, and disappear cleanly on world/session exit. Any collision or targeting behavior is defined and enforced server-side; small tableware and textiles may be explicitly cosmetic.
- [x] Deliver a placed inventory of rooms and prop families and in-client captures of the banquet, throne approach, study and at least one tower interior; show them from player height rather than only an overhead drawing.
- [x] Record before/after entity, draw-call and frame-time measurements on the same castle route, with bounded creation and distance-based visibility for detail props.

### #1204

- [x] Install large framed windows with iron grilles in the great hall, audience room and upper galleries, plus appropriate openings in accessible tower rooms. Main hall windows have at least a 3-by-5-block clear opening before the grille; preserve structural piers between them.
- [x] Grilles have visible narrow bars and open gaps. Daylight enters the room through the opening instead of the whole window behaving like an opaque dark cube. A standing player cannot escape through the barred opening; collision agrees with the server.
- [x] At the same camera, time and exposure, an open/grilled window demonstrably lights the interior more than a temporarily blocked opening. Preserve sheltered-room weather behavior and avoid rain/snow appearing through a roof simply because a window was added.
- [x] Add multi-arm tabletop candelabra to banquet/high tables, standing candelabra at major landings and wall-mounted candle sconces along main corridors and stairs. Flames sit on actual candle wicks; holders attach to their supporting surface.
- [x] All mandatory night routes between gate, halls, stairs, galleries and tower lookouts have visible next steps and doorway edges. Use repeated sconces to guide movement, while retaining darker recesses and the dark Norse atmosphere.
- [x] Use warm localized candlelight, restrained flame motion and contrasting cool daylight. Room dividers block light sufficiently to avoid an obviously lit room through a solid wall; opening a window must not be approximated by globally raising ambient light.
- [x] Props and lights rotate with the castle, agree across reconnect/chunk reload, never duplicate, and are removed on world/session exit. Define and enforce a bounded active-light/shadow budget with distance/visibility prioritization; unselected candles may retain visible emissive flames.
- [x] After adding windows and candelabra, repeat the complete furnished castle walk: no blocked stairs, snagging furniture, obstructed resident anchors or unsafe spawn/respawn points.
- [x] Deliver matched day/night captures from gate, banquet hall, corridor, stair landing and tower lookout, a window open-versus-blocked comparison, and before/after frame-time, draw-call and active-light counts at identical settings.

## Scope verified

Changes remain within deterministic castle dressing, windows, bounded built-in lighting and acceptance tooling. Sitting/food/storage interactions, fuel/fire mechanics, player-placeable lamps, a lighting-engine rewrite and unrelated weather/fauna/audio changes remain outside this delivery.

Stacks on PR #72. No merge or deployment is authorized.

This slice connects the already server-issued bounded offline lease to the actual Electron main-process runtime without enabling offline checkout.

### Changes
- Adds a native offline-authority service that reads the existing OS-protected enrolled-device credential only in Electron main.
- Calls `issue_device_offline_lease` with tenant/branch/device/credential binding.

- Offline checkout remains disabled.
- No lease token is exposed through preload/renderer IPC.

author: m0nggh
body:
## Stack Context

Stack of 3 on `feat/ses-multiple-recipients/trunk`. It lets the Postman "Send email" action send **one SES message to all recipients** instead of one per recipient, and surfaces **blacklisted CC addresses** in the step result.

1. #2237 — generic pill-toggle option for text fields
2. #2238 — Postman send mode: one email to all vs individual
3. **#2239 (this PR)** — report blacklisted CC recipients

## What?

SES sends now report `cc` and `ccStatus` in the step output. Blacklisted CCs raise a partial error that names them and are included in the owner's blacklist email. There is **no CC-only retry**: CCs ride along on the next To send.

- `common/data-out-validator.ts`: optional aligned `cc` / `ccStatus` arrays. `cc` was already written at runtime but missing from the schema.
- `common/email-helper.ts`: suppressed CCs push a `BLACKLISTED` error so `errorStatus` fires even when every To send succeeded. `getCcStatuses` computes per-CC status. A healthy CC is never marked BLACKLISTED just because every To recipient was.
- `actions/send-transactional-email/index.ts`: `blacklistedCcs` merged into the owner notification and passed to the error builder. A retry routed to Postman reports no `ccStatus`, since Postman cannot track it.
- `common/throw-errors.ts` `BLACKLISTED` case: separate To and CC sections. The retry button and the removal-form prompt appear **only when a To recipient is blacklisted**. CC-only shows just the list.
- `ErrorResult/SpecificErrorResult.tsx`: the button renders only when `buttonMessage` is non-empty. **Bug fix**: the invalid-attachments error used to render an empty button.
- `get-data-out-metadata.ts`: "CC status" variable label.
- `common/parameters.ts`: CC tooltip updated. It used to say CC status is not tracked.

## Why?

Today a blacklisted CC is dropped from the SES call with nothing shown anywhere. Pipe owners had no way to know a CC never received anything. To recipients already get a partial error and a resend button, so this brings CCs to parity on visibility while deliberately stopping short of a retry, which was agreed as unnecessary.

## Review focus

- `getCcStatuses`: when no To send was accepted, a non-suppressed CC takes the top **send** error, never a suppression `BLACKLISTED`. Otherwise it would be reported to the owner as blacklisted itself.
- The Postman path reports no `ccStatus`. It does no pre-send suppression check.

## Tests

```sh
npm run -w backend test:unit -- --run src/apps/postman/__tests__/actions/send-transactional-email.test.ts
```

Covers CC-only blacklist (partial error, no button, no form prompt, owner email), CC + To blacklist (button, both sections, form prompt), all-To-blacklisted with a healthy CC, Postman path has no `ccStatus`, retry replaces `ccStatus`, Postman-routed retry drops it.

Manual:

| # | Step | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Insert a **CC** address into `email_suppression`. Run a step with 2 To and that CC. | Step succeeds. Partial error titled "Blacklisted CC email" lists the CC. No button, no form link. Owner receives the blacklist email naming the CC. |
| 2 | Open the step output variables. | `CC status` shows `BLACKLISTED` for that address. `CC recipient email(s)` still lists it. |
| 3 | Also blacklist one To recipient. Run again. | Error titled "Blacklisted recipient email" with a To section, a CC section, the form link and the "Resend to blacklisted recipients" button. |
| 4 | Whitelist both. Click resend. | One send to the failed To recipient with the CC. `CC status` becomes `ACCEPTED`. |
| 5 | Run a step with an invalid attachment. | The partial error shows **no** empty button under the text. |
| 6 | Run a Postman-routed step (`ses_enabled` off) with a CC. | Output has `cc` but no `CC status`. |

## Security closure

### CSRF protection

Yakable authenticates browser requests with an HttpOnly session cookie, so stateless server-side authentication alone is not sufficient protection against CSRF.

This PR enables Spring Security CSRF protection with `CookieCsrfTokenRepository`:

- readable `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie
- `X-XSRF-TOKEN` request header
- SameSite=Strict CSRF cookie
- CSRF protection for POST / PUT and other unsafe methods
- token bootstrap on GET requests, including anonymous `GET /api/auth/me`

The frontend `HttpUtils` automatically reads `XSRF-TOKEN` and sends `X-XSRF-TOKEN` for unsafe HTTP and SSE requests.

The authentication session itself remains in the separate HttpOnly `yakable_session` cookie and is never exposed to JavaScript.

### Login timing

The previous login path skipped BCrypt when the username did not exist, while an existing username with a wrong password executed BCrypt.

The login path now always performs password verification using a fixed dummy BCrypt hash for missing users before returning the existing generic invalid-credentials error.

This keeps the PRD behavior unchanged while reducing an obvious username-enumeration timing discrepancy.

## PRD acceptance regressions

Adds / strengthens tests for:

- login requires CSRF
- authenticated user mutations require CSRF
- anonymous auth bootstrap receives an XSRF token
- valid CSRF reaches the real Controller contract
- frontend unsafe requests send the XSRF header
- missing username still executes password verification
- disabled user can be re-enabled and then log in with the existing password
- existing disable / session-revocation behavior remains protected
- existing password reset / password change session revocation remains protected
- existing last ACTIVE ADMIN and self-operation protections remain protected

## PRD status

`docs/prd/system/user-management-v1.md`:

```text
Draft -> Done
```

The V1 acceptance scope is now closed:

- login / logout / current user
- user list / search / filters
- create / edit
- enable / disable
- current-user profile
- current-user password change
- admin password reset
- ADMIN / USER authorization
- last ACTIVE ADMIN protection
- immediate session revocation
- first administrator initialization
- frontend login flow
- frontend users management
- CSRF protection

## Out of scope

Still intentionally excluded by the PRD:

- Workspace / Tenant / Membership
- RBAC / custom permissions
- registration
- invitations
- email verification
- password recovery
- OAuth / SSO / LDAP / MFA

author: malteclaassen-create
body:
Three separate bugs, one commit each.

## 1 · Achievement bars always looked finished

Every locked achievement's bar ran to full width whatever the number beside it said. **1/5, 1/10 and 20/100 all read as all but complete** — only the count gave it away.

The percentage was never wrong. The width was passed the wrong way:

```css
@keyframes grow-x { from { width: 0 } to { width: var(--w, 100%) } }
.bar-fill { width: var(--w, 0); }
```

`.bar-fill` takes its width from `--w`, and this call site set an inline `width` instead. With `--w` unset the keyframe fell back to its own `100%` and held it (`animation-fill-mode: both`), and an inline width never stood a chance against a running animation.

The same `--w` is what the reduced-motion and lite-graphics rules read (`width: var(--w, 0) !important`), so for anyone with either switched on these bars were **empty** rather than full. One property, both symptoms.

Every other `bar-fill` on the site already passes `--w` — this was the odd one out.

## 2 · The third league could not be reached

The **Applies to** picker was `inline-flex flex-nowrap` with no scroller of any kind, inside a card that clips. For somebody racing in two leagues, the third pill ran past the card's edge with no way to get to it: not by scrolling, not by wrapping. The one control deciding which league an edit saves to could not be fully used.

Measured before and after:

| | `overflow-x` | reachable |
|---|---|---|
| before | `visible` | ✗ |
| after | `auto` | ✓ |

The scroll goes **on** the bar, which is also what makes `SlidingTabs` centre the active pill — it only does that when its own wrapper scrolls.

## 3 · The bottom sheet had two square corners, and clipped

It was rounded along its **top edge only** — the shape of a sheet that sits *on* the bottom of the screen. It does not: the overlay's `p-4` floats it 16px above the edge, so two hard corners hung over a strip of scrim with a rounded top above them. All four corners now (measured `16px 16px 16px 16px`), which is what it was already doing from `sm` up where it becomes a centred card.

Measuring that also turned up a second problem: **no maximum height and no scroll**, so content taller than the screen ran off the bottom. Nine rows plus a header lose their last one on a short phone. The panel is a column capped at the viewport now with the body scrolling inside it — verified at 412×430, where the body scrolls and the panel still fits, and at 412×740 where it does not need to.

## Verified

- `npx eslint src` — clean
- `npm run build` — passes
- `node --test "frontend/src/**/*.test.mjs"` — 14/14 pass
- All three reproduced and then re-checked in Chromium at phone width: the bars rendered side by side old-way/new-way (20%, 10%, 20%, 91% against four full ones), the picker's `overflow-x` and scrollability measured in the DOM, and the sheet's four corner radii and body scrolling measured at two viewport heights.

author: sfmskywalker
body:
Closes #1913.

## What was wrong

When the gate went red on 2026-09-21 (#1910), the entire diagnostic record was:

```
Apply_then_validate_against_sqlite_round_trips_and_exits_zero [FAIL]
Assert.Equal() Failure: Expected: 0  Actual: 4
```

Exit 4 is `DatabaseFailure`, and `EfToolingHost` flattens **every** non-refusal exception raised while a module is applied or validated into that one code (`EfToolingHost.cs:719-723`). So the bare number says only that something went wrong. The message naming the module, provider, context type and the underlying failure was already sitting in the response, and the test never read it. The cause of #1910 still cannot be named.

## The change

`AssertExit` asserts the code and, on mismatch, reports `error.code`, `error.message` and `details`. Applied to all 26 exit-code assertions in the class — negative paths included, since a test expecting exit 1 that got exit 4 was equally mute. A raw-stream overload parses the response only once the assertion has already failed.

One assertion is deliberately left alone: `:763` checks that the response body *echoes* its exit code, which is a different property.

Test-only. No production behaviour changes.

## Evidence, not assertion

The test passing proves nothing here — it passed before this change too. So the guard was proved by forcing the #1910 failure mode: pointing the round-trip test's apply at an unopenable database.

Before:

```
Assert.Equal() Failure: Expected: 0  Actual: 4
```

After:

```
Expected exit 0, got 4. error.code='module-apply-failed'
error.message=''Secrets' could not be applied for Sqlite from SecretsSqliteDbContext:
SQLite Error 14: 'unable to open database file'.'
```

The forcing was reverted and the suite re-run green.

That run also settles the safety question empirically rather than by reading: the connection string `/nonexistent-dir-BITEPROOF/apply-validate.db` does **not** appear in the output. `EfToolingRedaction.Redact` scrubs it before it reaches the response, and the existing `A_connection_string_never_appears_in_a_database_failure` pins that with a sentinel.

## Second fix

`Dispose()` now clears the SQLite connection pool before deleting its temp directory, and swallows a residual lock so teardown cannot fail an otherwise-green test. #1884 gave ~20 EF test classes that treatment through a shared `TemporarySqliteDatabase`; this class landed two days later with #1906 and was missed.

It owns a whole temp directory rather than one database path, so it clears the pool and removes the tree itself instead of delegating to that type's per-file teardown — which is why that file is not compiled into this project.

**This is not claimed as the cause of #1910.** That was checked and is unproven either way.

## Gate

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Build (`Elsa.Persistence.EntityFrameworkCore.Migrations.Tests`) | 0 errors, no new warnings |
| `Elsa.Persistence.EntityFrameworkCore.Migrations.Tests` | **190 passed**, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| `Elsa.Architecture.Tests` | **242 passed**, 0 failed |
| `Elsa.Maps.Generator -- check` | `Generated maps still describe the tree.` |
| Revert-to-red bite-proof | above |

The architecture guard first reported 15 failures. Those reproduce identically on unmodified `main` and are the missing-restore trap — `Restore Elsa.Server.slnx for both Release and Debug`. After `tools/architecture/restore-ci-project-graph.sh` it is 242/242. Recording it because a red guard here looks alarming and is usually not about the diff.

## Note on #1910

This clears the diagnosability blocker; it does **not** close #1910. That issue's cause is still unidentified, and it should close only once understood or after a sustained green period.

## Note on signing

Committed with `--no-gpg-sign`: the local signing key could not be unlocked in this session. The squash-merge re-signs with GitHub's key, as every commit on `main` already is.

author: orosotne
body:
Rieši upozornenia Google Search Console v sekcii **Štruktúrované dáta → Záznamy obchodníka** (hlásené 21. 9. 2026). Nešlo o blokujúce chyby — položky ostávali platné — ale chýbali polia, ktoré Google pre záznamy obchodníka očakáva.

## Čo sa menilo

**Chýbajúce polia (pôvodné zadanie)**
- `offers.shippingDetails.deliveryTime.transitTime` — hlásených 30 položiek
- `offers.validFrom` — hlásených 18 položiek

Doplnené v `lib/productSchema.ts`, čo je zdroj pravdy pre všetkých 12 stránok `/produkt/<slug>` (prerender aj klientský render), a v ItemList Offeri na `/obchod`, aby oba markupy hlásili to isté.

`validFrom` je pevná konštanta `OFFER_VALID_FROM`, nie `new Date()` — dynamický dátum by sa menil pri každom builde a Google by ponuku videl ako „platnú od dnes". Pri zmene cenníka sa prepíše na dátum jeho účinnosti.

**Dodacia lehota**

`handlingTime` znížený z 1–5 na 1–3 dni. S prepravou 1–2 dni tak vychádza doručenie na **2–5 pracovných dní** — presne to, čo web aj FAQ sľubujú zákazníkom. Predtým si stránka doprava („expedícia do 1–5 dní") a FAQ („dodanie do 5 pracovných dní") protirečili.

**Cena za m²**

Web komunikuje ako hlavnú cenu sadzbu za m², ale `Offer.price` musí zostať transakčná (celá platňa) — inak by sa rozišla s `g:price` v Google Merchant feede a s tým, čo zákazník zaplatí v košíku, čo býva dôvod na pozastavenie účtu v Merchant Center. Sadzbu za m² preto nesie `UnitPriceSpecification` s `referenceQuantity` 1 MTK, rovnako ako to feed už rieši cez `g:unit_pricing_*`.

Pri tom sa odstránil rozpor, ktorý v repe bol: ItemList na `/obchod` posielal ako cenu produktu sadzbu za m² (386,52 €), kým `/produkt/<slug>` posielal cenu platne (1 978,98 €) — Google videl pre ten istý produkt dve rôzne ceny.

**Ochrana proti regresii**

`scripts/validate-dist.ts` teraz kontroluje `validFrom`, `handlingTime`, `transitTime` aj `hasMerchantReturnPolicy`, takže build zlyhá, ak sa niektoré pole stratí.

## Overené lokálne

- `tsc --noEmit` čistý
- `vite build` + prerender + `generate-seo-artifacts` + `validate-dist` → **50 routes OK**
- Vo vygenerovanom `dist` má všetkých 12 produktových stránok `transitTime` aj `validFrom`
- Cena v Merchant feede (`g:price` 1 978,98 EUR) sedí s `Offer.price` na produktovej stránke

## Tretia položka z GSC — neplatný GTIN

Bez zmeny v kóde: repo `gtin` neposiela nikde, ide o starú verziu jednej stránky v indexe. Vyrieši sa revalidáciou v GSC po nasadení.

## Po nasadení

Spustiť v GSC „Overiť opravu" pre `transitTime`, `validFrom` aj GTIN.

author: volkmarr
body:
`imports.ResolveAsync` was the one pass of a build that reported no phase.

It runs at `IndexBuilder.cs:57`, after the whole walk — by design, because a name resolves against every other file in the project. The last report before it is the ingest's counting one, so its cost was read back under **"Reading '<repo>' into the shadow index"**: a label belonging to a repository the pass is not about.

That is the same fault #91 fixed for the overview and the full-text build, left in the pass sitting between them. It undercuts what #92 is for — reading what a refresh spent off its finished status instead of measuring it again with a bespoke poller.

It is not a small pass. `ResolvePathsAsync`'s own comment: *"On a large project that map is a lowercased copy of every path in it."*

## What this does

One report before the pass, and a constant for the phase:

```
"Resolving the imports to the files they name"
```

**A phase of the reading step, not a step of its own.** The import names were appended by the walk and resolve once the whole project is in the shadow, so it finishes the job step 2 started — which is exactly the model `CONTEXT.md` describes, where one step reports several phases when it does several separable things. The seven steps are what the counter is read for, and nothing here asks to change them: no renumbering, no `TotalStepCount` bump, no `CONTEXT.md` or ADR change.

## Tests

Both timeline tests now pin the new phase in its position, in `expected`, between the ingest and the attribution:

- `Each_piece_of_a_build_reports_its_own_phase` — the reports a build makes, in order
- `A_finished_refresh_says_what_each_phase_cost` — the same phases read back off a finished status

`StepOf` maps it to 2. That map is deliberate double-entry — its doc says *"a renumbering has to be written down twice and cannot pass by agreeing with itself"* — so the new phase is written down in the test independently of the constant, as the others are.

## Not changed

`phase` is still a string and `RefreshProgress` / `PhaseCost` keep their shape, so `web/src/features/refresh/api.ts` needs nothing. A finished refresh simply has one more entry in `phases`.

## Verification

- Build clean, 0 warnings (`TreatWarningsAsErrors` on)
- 627/627 tests pass
- `RefreshTests`: 19/19

## Context

Came out of analysing the "make a Step a module" candidate from the architecture review. That larger restructure — an ordered list of `(phase, pass)` replacing the hand-threaded `Action<RefreshProgress>` — is **not** in this PR, and on reading the code I don't think it should be: it fights the shadow index's `using` scope (which must close before the swap), the `catch` that discards a half-built shadow, and the counting reports that live inside the passes because only they know their own `Done`/`Total`.

The part of that candidate still worth doing is separate and smaller: making a phase carry its step, so `RefreshProgress(step, total, phase)` stops taking two facts that must agree and nothing makes them. That touches the wire shape the web app hand-mirrors, so it belongs in its own PR rather than riding along here.

author: ulli2060
body:
Authentication is a per-route dependency, so the schema pages (`/openapi.json`, `/openapi-3.0.json`, `/swagger`, `/docs`, `/docs/oauth2-redirect`, `/scalar`) and `/metrics` are readable without an API key on every deployment. There was no setting for the reference pages, and `DOCLING_SERVE_OTEL_ENABLE_PROMETHEUS=false` only left the Prometheus reader and the RQ/Ray collectors unregistered while the `/metrics` route stayed mounted, still publishing `python_info` and `process_*`.

- New setting `enable_api_docs` (`DOCLING_SERVE_ENABLE_API_DOCS`, default `true`). When `false`, FastAPI gets no `openapi_url`, which drops the schema, its Swagger UI and ReDoc pages and the OAuth2 redirect page, and the offline Swagger UI/ReDoc, Scalar and OpenAPI 3.0 routes are not registered either. The paths answer 404 like any unregistered route.
- `/metrics` is registered only while `otel_enable_prometheus` is `true`, which is what the configuration docs already promise for that flag.
- The CLI banner omits the docs links when they are off (and its Scalar link pointed at the ReDoc URL).

**Behaviour change:** a deployment with `DOCLING_SERVE_OTEL_ENABLE_PROMETHEUS=false` now gets 404 on `/metrics` (before: 200 with the Python process metrics only), so a scraper still pointed at it fails visibly instead of collecting an empty page. The separate `metrics_port` server is not affected and stays additive.

Design notes, in case they come up:

- 404 rather than the 403 used by `show_version_info` and `enable_management_endpoints`: an unregistered route reveals nothing about the deployment, and it is what FastAPI's own `docs_url=None` yields.
- The gate is `otel_enable_prometheus` alone, not `metrics_port`: with the flag on, the in-app route serves the same registry as the separate port. Hiding it when a port is configured would be a second behaviour change; easy to add if wanted.
- Hiding the pages instead of putting them behind the API key: the built-in OpenAPI route takes no dependencies, and a deployment that wants its schema private usually wants it invisible too.

Tests (`tests/test_api_docs_and_metrics_toggle.py`, 27 cases): all six reference routes with and without static assets (200 / 404), the API itself unaffected (`POST /v1/convert/source` -> 422), `/metrics` 200 / 404 by flag. The orchestrator dependency and the OpenTelemetry setup are stubbed as in `test_batch_endpoint.py`.

## AI disclosure

The change and its tests were prepared with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code) under my direction; I reviewed the code paths against v1.34.0 and ran the tests, ruff and mypy locally.

# Bead godot-test1-7ami — bike-path traffic lights: a visible cycle, and riding through a RED costs one coin

## STEP 0 finding (web debug export, camera ~3 m from a real head)

The lamps **do** change on web: green → amber → red, on the Compatibility
renderer, through the existing `set_instance_color` path. Suspect (a) is
cleared — no plumbing fix was needed, and the `set_instance_color` write was
left exactly where it was (one Timer tick per head; no new bucket, no
re-upload seam, so no perf delta to measure beyond "unchanged": the write
count and the dirtied buffer are what they were).

What the owner saw is **readability, not plumbing**: 0.16 m lenses stepping
every 2.2–4.5 s do not read as a traffic light at riding distance. So:

- dwell is now a real light's rhythm: green ~8 s, amber ~2 s, red ~8 s
  (`SIGNAL_DWELL_GREEN/AMBER/RED` + `signal_dwell()`, three consts, not one
  range). The PHASE stays `randomize()`d per head — ambience, never seeded,
  never on the wire.
- lamps grow to the city's own 0.22 (`BIKE_LAMP`), and an unlit lens goes
  clearly dark (`BIKE_LAMP_DIM` 0.62 → 0.80; at 0.62 an unlit lens still
  reads as lit at riding distance).
- the tick **restarts** the countdown on the new phase's own dwell
  (`start(signal_dwell(phase))`): assigning `wait_time` inside the callback
  lands a cycle late (steady-state amber would hold 8 s and red 2 s).

author: yyangatlassian
body:
## What

Adds an opt-in `squashIncrementalCommits` flag. When enabled, XTable folds an
N-snapshot incremental backlog into a **single** target-format commit instead of
one commit per source snapshot.

Default is OFF — existing behaviour is unchanged.

## Why

Atlassian's Data Export path emulates an upsert on an Iceberg table as
`DELETE` + `INSERT` + `rewrite_data_files()`, because StarRocks has no
`MERGE INTO` for external catalogs. That produces 3 Iceberg snapshots per batch.

Without squashing, XTable publishes **one Delta commit per snapshot**, so the
customer-visible Delta table is transiently published in a torn state — measured:
after the `DELETE`+`INSERT` commits, Delta held **two rows for the updated key**
until the compaction commit landed.

## Measured result

| | Delta versions | add | remove |
|---|---|---|---|
| flag OFF (control) | 3 | — | — |
| flag ON | **1** | 2 | 2 |

Verified on StarRocks-written Iceberg metadata on S3 (StarRocks 4.1.1,
format-version 2), not just synthetic fixtures.

The squashed commit correctly **nets out** a file that the `INSERT` added and the
compaction then removed — it appears in neither `add` nor `remove`. Emitting an
`add` for an already-deleted parquet would have produced a broken Delta table.

## Tests

- `TestTableChangeSquasher` — 9 tests, incl. add-then-remove net-out, single-change
  identity, schema/partition-spec taken from the head change
- `TestConversionControllerSquash` — 2 tests for the controller seam

## Note for reviewers

This branch **also contains spike evidence** (36 files: findings docs, SQL
transcripts, `_delta_log` captures, run scripts) alongside the 6 source/test files.
That's deliberate — it's the record of how the behaviour was measured. If you'd
prefer a source-only PR for upstreaming, the history separates cleanly.

## What is the new behavior?

`ConnectivityGraphCache` no longer rebuilds the va-diff connectivity graph when a circuit breaker is toggled.

The graph only contains edges for closed non-CB bus-bus switches (`aggregate_switch_pairs` -> `closed_non_cb`), but the cache fingerprint hashed the `closed` state of *all* bus-bus switches. Every contingency and every interactive CB operation therefore invalidated the cache and rebuilt an identical graph (~100 ms on a 22k-bus grid).

- Fingerprint is now `closed & et == "b" & type != "CB"`; disconnector toggles still invalidate, CB toggles do not.
- `build_connectivity_graph_for_contingency` inserts whole element tables via `add_nodes_from` / `add_edges_from` instead of one `itertuples` row at a time. Nodes, edges and node attributes are identical; ~35% faster on case9241.

author: kalms
body:
## The bug

`search_code` kept the first 50 lines ripgrep emitted and stopped — collecting in emission order, ranking nothing, and saying nothing about what it dropped. ripgrep's parallel walker emits in **nondeterministic** order, so those 50 were an arbitrary sample that differed between identical runs, and a partial answer read as a complete one.

Reported from a consuming repo as "search_code is missing `packages/core/src/`. It reported no hits for `parseClaudeLine` in the file that defines it. I only caught it because tests failed."

Measured there — `parseClaudeLine`, 150 matches across 32 files:

| class | hits |
|---|---|
| test | 81 (52 of them in one file) |
| docs | 50 |
| source | **18** |
| fixture | 1 |

The file that **defines** the symbol sat at emission index 68, 82, 90, 137 and 137 across five identical runs. Never once inside the 50-hit window. The agent concluded the symbol was absent from its own definition site and fell back to raw `grep` — the one thing this tool exists to make unnecessary.

## The fix

**Ranking runs over every match, before the window is taken.** Whole files are ordered `definition → source → test → docs → fixture`, then by path, then by line, with a file's hits kept together. "Definition" is a graph fact: a symbol of that exact name declared in that file, one indexed query, only when the pattern is a bare identifier.

**A per-file cap of 5** in the MCP window, with `… +N more in this file`. One test file held 52 of those 150 matches; at any budget a single chatty file otherwise crowds out every other file that matched.

**A truncation footer** — `⚠ showing 50 of 150 matches` — so a partial result can never again be mistaken for an exhaustive one.

The old `rankSearchHits` (kind-weight × path, CLI-only — the MCP tool never called it) is gone. It scored a hit by its enclosing symbol's `KIND_WEIGHT`, which reads as "is this code"; but a vitest `it()` callback is a `function` node, so all 52 matches in that one test file tied with the line defining the symbol, and an alphabetical tiebreak decided which survived. Tests and docs are not low-value because of the kind of node that encloses them.

The CLI (`cortex code search`) keeps its 500-hit window and gains the same ordering, no per-file cap (it paginates, and a cap would hide matches `--offset` could never reach), and a footer that reports the true match count rather than the size of its own window.

## Also fixed

A pattern beginning with a dash was parsed as a **flag**: `search_code("--max-count")` exited 2 with a usage error, and `classifySearchExec` — seeing no output and no regex parse error — reported `empty`. A false negative shaped exactly like a genuine "no matches", which is the one failure a caller cannot tell from an answer. Both argv builders now pass `--` immediately before the pattern.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — 2433 tests, 342 files, green
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` clean
- `node scripts/check-release-consistency.mjs main` — OK (2.4.2, CHANGELOG section + link ref)
- New regression tests cover tier ordering, the definition-first case, the per-file cap and its overflow marker, the true-total/`truncated` reporting, and a leading-dash pattern.

author: jroedel
body:
The gate drove the program by hand. A real machine is not driven by hand: a task starts the daemon at logon, the daemon watches the clock, and the backup happens while nobody is looking. **That is the product, and nothing had ever watched it happen.**

Now it does:

```
-- The scheduled task
   ok   nothing was running until now
   ok   the task started the program (pid 7184)
   ok   the status page is listening on 127.0.0.1:7391
-- Waiting for the scheduled backup at 10:09
   ok   the machine backed itself up with nobody driving it (2 -> 3 snapshots)
```

### What changed

The gate **installs the way a machine is installed** — `install.ps1 -Elevated`, the binary where the installer puts it, the task the installer registers — rather than running a loose binary out of a build directory. Then it makes two separate claims:

- **That the task starts the program** and the status page comes up. This is about `install.ps1`: the path it registered, the account, the privileges.
- **That a backup then happens on its own.** This is about the daemon's scheduler, reading a slot the script put four minutes into the future before any hand-driven backup ran.

The wait is real wall-clock, about three minutes of it, and it is the only way to assert the thing. A scheduler asserted by calling the function it calls is a test of arithmetic.

### A bug this found: zero jitter could not be expressed

The gate scheduled a backup for 09:50 and watched the machine decide on 10:06. Sixteen minutes of jitter, on a config that said `jitter_minutes = 0`:

```go
if c.Schedule.JitterMinutes > 0 {          // 0 is indistinguishable from unset
    schedule.JitterMinutes = c.Schedule.JitterMinutes
}
```

So the 30-minute default applied. It is the same distinction `UseFSSnapshot` and `OneFileSystem` are pointers for — unset and zero are different answers — and this field missed it. The consequence is not only a confused harness: **a machine could not be asked to run at exactly the time its own config names**, which is what somebody typing that line is asking for. Now a `*int`, with a table test over unset, zero and explicit.

### A thing that looked like a bug and was not

One hand-driven run produced two snapshots. Registering the task **starts the daemon** — the account is signed in, so the logon trigger is satisfied the moment the task exists — and a daemon that finds no run history is due by definition and backs up. All correct, and all in the middle of the gate's own backups.

So the task is disabled the moment it is registered and enabled again when the script is ready to watch it. The phase that asserts a backup nobody asked for should be the only thing that could have produced one, and it now asserts `nothing was running until now` first.

### And a comment that was wrong

Above the triggers: *"At logon, and again at startup for a machine that is left signed in"* — there has only ever been a logon trigger. Nothing is missing; a task running as the signed-in user with `LogonType Interactive` has no session to start in at boot. The comment was what was wrong.

### Diagnostics

Because the first two runs of this phase reported failures without explaining them: the gate lists the snapshots — id, time, host, paths — whenever the count surprises it, dumps the run's own output, and on a schedule that never fires prints the task's record of its last run, whether the daemon is alive, the status page's next-run line, and `doctor`.

Verified green end to end on `windows-latest` before opening this.

author: gvladika
body:
# Which Linear task belongs to this PR?

Fixes [EXSC-1039](https://linear.app/lifi-linear/issue/EXSC-1039/bun-healthcheck-runs-zero-checks-and-exits-0-false-all-clear)

Also closes part 1 of [EXSC-971](https://linear.app/lifi-linear/issue/EXSC-971/port-shipped-script-modules-off-bun-only-runtime-apis-importmetamain) (the `import.meta.main` half). The `Bun.*` half of that ticket is untouched and still open.

# Why did I implement it this way?

`tsx` drops `import.meta.main` for `.ts` entry modules, so every CLI guarded with it loaded, evaluated the guard as `undefined`, and exited 0 having run nothing. The reported symptom was `bun healthcheck` (`package.json` → `bunx tsx ./script/deploy/healthCheck.ts`), but the same guard sat in eleven other modules, two of them invoked from CI: `healthCheckAllNetworks.yml` ran the daily production-fleet sweep as a no-op — never writing `warned_count`, which coerces to `0`, so the Slack composer stayed silent and the "Fail if any network failed" step saw success — and `deploymentAddressConsistency.yml` passed its PR gate the same way. A silent `exit 0` is indistinguishable from a real all-clear, which is why this is worse than a crash.

EXSC-1023 already built the fix — `isEntrypoint(import.meta.url)` in `script/utils/is-entrypoint.ts`, which realpaths both sides — but only converted four call sites. This routes the remaining twelve through it. I did not switch `package.json` to bare `bun run`, the other option the ticket floated: `200-typescript.md` says scripts are invoked with `bunx tsx` so the pinned local `tsx` and `node_modules` resolution are used, and the two CI jobs invoke `bunx tsx` directly where a `package.json` edit would not have reached them anyway. Fixing the guard fixes every caller at once. Conversely I left `healthCheckForNewNetworkDeployment.yml` and `deploy-smoke-test.yml` on bare `bun`: moving them onto `tsx` would run `script/utils/utils.ts` under Node, which still has 15 `Bun.*` call sites (EXSC-971 part 2).

While converting I found seven hand-rolled variants of the same check and folded them into the helper too, so there is one spelling to get right rather than eight. Five were realpath copies (`shared/assert-direct-broadcast-gate`, `tasks/proposePeripheryWithWhitelist`, the three `resources/*Reminder` modules). Two were not on anyone's list: `safe/verify-rehearsal` and `safe/rehearsal-teardown` guarded with `process.argv[1].endsWith('verify-rehearsal.ts')`, a suffix match that fails the opposite way — it fires for any entry sharing that basename rather than silently not firing.

`safe/execute-pending-timelock-tx.ts` stays deliberately unguarded. Its comment explains why: no guard, however spelled, should be able to silence the scheduled executor, and logic there that needs coverage moves to `safe/timelock-prefetch.ts` instead. I only updated the wording of that comment and its sibling, not the decision.

The new `script/entrypoint-guard-placement.test.ts` is a source assertion because a behavioural test cannot catch this class: under `bun test` the module is never the entrypoint, so the guard is correctly `false` however it is spelled. It holds `import.meta.main` at zero and asserts `is-entrypoint.ts` is the only non-test module that reads `process.argv[1]`, which keeps both the silent variant and the hand-rolled ones from coming back. I verified both assertions go red — reverting one guard, and adding a tracked module that reads `process.argv[1]` — before going green again.

Verification beyond the suite: `bun healthcheck --network sepolia` now runs the full invariant set (3 warnings, "Deployment checks passed"), confirming it reaches no `Bun.*` call under `tsx`; `bunx tsx script/tasks/checkDeploymentAddressConsistency.ts` now genuinely reports a pass; `contractDependencyReminder` and `assert-direct-broadcast-gate` both fire. `bun test script/` is green at 5795 tests.

author: scottmss
body:
## Why

A real install showed most skills missing, and it looked like a file-mapping bug. It wasn't — all 48 paths resolved. The cause was the **skill-listing budget**: Claude Code loads every installed skill's description into context on every turn, inside roughly 1% of the context window (~8,000 characters at 200k). Our 48 descriptions totalled **43,491 characters — 5.4× over**. Over budget, Claude keeps the skill *names* but drops the *descriptions*, least-used first; on a fresh install that is nearly all of them, so skills stop triggering. Eleven descriptions also exceeded the 1,024-character Agent Skills spec maximum, which the validator never checked.

## What changed

**Packs.** One 48-skill plugin becomes 8 packs: `hse-core` (13), `hse-hazards` (10), `hse-plant` (6) and five `hse-sector-*` packs. `skills/` stays flat — each pack is `"source": "./"` + `"strict": false` + an explicit skills list (the same layout as `anthropics/skills`). Every install carries the whole `skills/` tree, so the ~1,067 `../other-skill/` cross-references keep resolving whichever packs a user picks. `plugin.json` is removed: at a shared root it would stamp one name and version on every pack.

**Bundles.** Six one-step installs under `bundles/` — `hse-for-construction-industrial`, `hse-for-primary-industries`, `hse-for-transport-ports-rail`, `hse-for-energy-resources`, `hse-for-care-hospitality`, `hse-everything`. Each is only a `dependencies` list of packs and carries no skills.

**Descriptions.** All 48 rewritten to ~250 characters (43,491 → 12,172 total). The exhaustive trigger vocabulary lives in the `hse-advisor` routing map, which loads on demand and costs nothing against the budget. Only frontmatter `description` blocks changed in `skills/` (plus `hse-advisor`'s body).

**`hse-advisor`.** Routing rows added for the six plant specialists, and a new *Packs* section: when a specialist's pack isn't installed, read its method from `../<specialist>/SKILL.md` and tell the user which pack to add.

**Tooling.** `validate-skills.py` now enforces the 1,024 maximum (300 soft target), reports listing cost per pack and bundle, and guards the new structure (strict:false on shared-root packs, no root `plugin.json`, one pack per skill, one version everywhere, bundle integrity, a routing row per skill, pack table and README roster in sync with `marketplace.json`). New `scripts/bump-version.py` sets the release version in all 14 places. README leads with the bundle table; CONTRIBUTING replaces the "trigger-rich description" advice that caused the problem.

Also carries `plain-language-reviewer` to `main` — #57 merged into the `energy-based-safety-specialist` branch rather than `main`, so it never shipped.

## Listing cost after this PR

| Install | Skills | Description chars | vs ~8,000 budget (200k ctx) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hse-for-primary-industries` | 27 | 6,597 | 0.8× |
| `hse-for-care-hospitality` | 25 | 6,094 | 0.8× |
| `hse-for-construction-industrial` | 33 | 8,155 | 1.0× |
| `hse-for-transport-ports-rail` | 33 | 8,159 | 1.0× |
| `hse-for-energy-resources` | 34 | 8,511 | 1.1× |
| `hse-everything` | 48 | 12,172 | 1.5× |
| *before: `hse-core` v1.x* | *48* | *43,491* | *5.4×* |

On 1M-context models every bundle fits comfortably, including `hse-everything`.

## ⚠️ Breaking for existing users

`hse-core` used to hold every skill; from 2.0.0 it is the 13-skill core pack. After updating the marketplace, install the bundle for your industry (it keeps `hse-core` and adds the rest). The README covers this under *Upgrading from v1.x*.

## Testing

- `python3 scripts/validate-skills.py` — passes; each new guard mutation-tested on a scratch copy (9 cases, all caught).
- CI self-tests (`risk_matrix_scorer`, `energy_calculator`, `readability_check`) — pass.
- All 48 frontmatters parsed with a real YAML parser (Ruby Psych) — 0 problems.
- **Claude Code CLI 2.1.278, isolated `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`:** `claude plugin validate . --strict` passes; installing one bundle auto-installed its packs (`+ 4 dependencies`); `claude plugin details <pack>` showed each pack loading **only its own skills** (`hse-plant` 6, `hse-core` 13, `hse-sector-primary` 4) and bundles loading 0.
- `python3 scripts/bundle.py` — 48 per-skill zips + collection zip build.

## After merge

Tag and release: `git tag v2.0.0`, then `python3 scripts/bundle.py` → `gh release create v2.0.0 dist/*.zip --target main`. (No tags exist after v1.24.0.)

author: 0xsline
body:
Follow-up to the second small item reported in #148 — the client's best-effort `POST /api/agent-runs/<id>/draft/clear` returning 403 at the end of every turn. It is not specific to that backend, so it is here rather than on that branch.

## What happens

`finishRecoveredRun` (`src/agent/serverRunRecovery.ts`) is the fallback for a terminal that arrives with **no in-memory turn** — server restart, browser reload, a detached tab. It settles the run and then calls `clearStoredServerRun`, which removes the sessionStorage record that holds the run capability.

The only remaining code that cleans up the run's recovery draft is the abandon hook the stream lifecycle calls immediately afterwards (`serverRunStreamLifecycle.ts` -> `onRunAbandon` -> `clearServerRunDraft`). By then `readStoredServerRun` returns nothing, so the request goes out with **no** `SERVER_RUN_CAPABILITY_HEADER` and `boundRun` rejects it with 403 (`server/agent-runs/routes.ts:101-128`). Two consequences:

- every completed turn logs one rejected request — the client swallows it, so nothing is user-visible;
- in that fallback path the draft artifact is **never deleted**, because the 403 request was the only attempt. It survives until retention prunes it on the next write.

On the ordinary path the draft is cleared correctly inside the terminal handler, while the stored run is still readable; that request is unaffected here.

## The fix

- The fallback clears the draft itself, immediately before it drops the stored run — i.e. while the capability the request authenticates with still exists.
- `clearServerRunDraft` returns without sending anything when it has no capability for the run. Such a request can only be refused, so issuing it is noise; the comment records why.

## Verification

`src/agent/serverRunSessionStorage.verify.ts` now records what actually reaches `/draft/clear` and asserts both halves: the fallback sends exactly one request carrying the run capability, and a clear attempted after the stored run is gone sends nothing.

Against the pre-fix code those assertions fail as:

```
AssertionError: the orphaned recovery draft is cleared once, with the run capability attached
  actual: []
  expected: [ { runId: 'run-1', capability: 'raw-tab-capability' } ]

AssertionError: a clear attempted after the stored run is gone sends nothing: it could only 403
  actual: [ { runId: 'run-1', capability: null } ]
  expected: []
```

The second one is the 403 request from the report, reproduced: `capability: null`.

`npx tsc -b --force`, `npm run lint`, `scripts/verify-gate-coverage.verify.mjs`, and `serverRunSessionStorage`, `serverRunModelHistory`, `serverRunDraftStore`, `external-draft-persistence`, `agent-hydration-recovery` and `server/agent-runs/routes` verifies all pass on this branch.

author: ericxue92
body:
## Problem

实时监控 · 逼近突破位 took ~9s to load while every other endpoint answers in under 1s.

## Root cause (measured on .134)

| step | time |
|---|---|
| 3403 `/api/swap-klines` (live stock prices, 363 stocks) | ~9.0s, every time |
| ohlcv 52-week query | 0.21s |
| 4002 `/quotes` | ~0.4s |

`/watch` called 3403 inline with an **8s timeout**, and 3403 needs ~9s (it runs three full-table self-joins on `stock_swap_klines` per request, uncached). So every request waited the full 8s, timed out, and **dropped the stock section** — the 🏢 股票 group has always been empty. `watch.stocks timed out` repeats in the log. Not related to the key-levels change; the 8s timeout is older code.

## Change (server.py only)

- The stock section is computed by a background thread into a snapshot (25s timeout for 3403). Requests only read the snapshot and never wait for 3403.
- While someone has requested `/watch` in the last 3 minutes the thread refreshes itself every 60s, so the page never gets data older than one cycle; after that it stops, so 3403 is not hit when nobody is watching.
- A failed refresh keeps the last good snapshot; a snapshot older than 10 minutes is no longer served. `/watch` now returns `stocks_updated`.
- First snapshot is kicked off at startup.

## Result (live on .134)

- `/watch`: ~9s → 0.56–0.85s steady state (occasional spike when 4002 `/quotes` is slow, e.g. during the ~9 min 52-week prewarm after a restart).
- Stock group now has content (29 US stocks near their 52-week extremes at the time of testing); rows render and open correctly in a real browser.
- Polling every 60s like the page does: snapshot age stayed at 14–16s.

## Testing

`tests/test_watch_stocks.py`: 12 cases (filtering, timeout, snapshot replace / keep-last-good / expiry, single refresh at a time, loop runs while watched and stops when idle, lock released on error, request thread never calls 3403 or ohlcv). 253 unit tests pass. The idle-stop is covered by unit tests only, not observed live.

## Not in this PR

The real fix for the 9s belongs in 3403 (`sector-strength`): cache `/api/swap-klines` for 30–60s or index/rewrite its three queries.

body:
Groundwork for tokenized stocks (NVDAc ships in a follow-up PR). Those protocols only exist under the backend's `async_strategy`, which the SDK had no notion of — protocol and pool filtering were hardcoded to `safe_strategy` / `degen_strategy`, so an async-only asset would have resolved to zero protocols and been unreachable. This makes `async_strategy` a first-class strategy and exposes the withdrawal lifecycle it implies.

## Strategy

Adds a third public strategy `"yieldmaxxing"`, mapping to the backend's `async_strategy`.

- `toInternalStrategy` / `toPublicStrategy` / `isValidPublicStrategy` handle it, including the `"async"` short form the backend returns in some payloads.
- `getMatchingProtocolIds` now drives eligibility from an `ELIGIBLE_PROTOCOL_STRATEGIES` map instead of branching per strategy.
- `filterProtocolIdsWithPools` takes the internal strategy and forwards it to `/customization/pools`; it previously always sent `degen_strategy`, which returns nothing for an async-only asset.
- `DeploySafeAccountConfig.strategy` widened to `InternalStrategy`.

## Async withdrawals

Withdrawing from a delayed-withdrawal pool is a two-step process: the immediate portion transfers in the returned tx, the rest is redeemed over ~1 day (Ipor) to ~3 days (Superform) and forwarded to the EOA by a cron, with no claim call needed. The portfolio payload already carried this; the SDK typing did not.

- `PortfolioDetailed` gains `pendingAsyncWithdrawals`, `pauseMessageByToken`, and a fix to `staleBalances` (was typed `string[]`, is an object array).
- New `AsyncWithdrawal` / `AsyncWithdrawalStatus` types, exported.
- New `getAsyncOpportunities()` over `/opportunities/async`.

## Balance semantics

The part most likely to be integrated incorrectly, so it is documented in the JSDoc, the README, and [ondefy/sdk-api-docs#49](https://github.com/ondefy/sdk-api-docs/pull/49).

An in-flight redemption has left its position and has not reached the Safe, so it is in no balance field. Integrations need two numbers:

| Number | Formula | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Total balance | `portfolioByAssetType` + `REQUESTED`/`CLAIMABLE` | Display |
| Requestable | `portfolioByAssetType` | Withdraw form, max button, validation |

Once requested, an amount is no longer withdrawable and a second `withdrawFunds` call neither speeds it up nor errors — it silently returns what is left. Two double-counting traps are called out: `staleBalances` are the same idle balances `portfolioByAssetType` already sums, and `CLAIMED` entries linger 24h after the funds are back.

## Testing

`npm run check` — 37 unit tests pass, typecheck and build clean. New coverage in `strategy.test.ts` (conversions both ways, short forms, unknown values) and `protocol-selection.test.ts` (per-strategy eligibility, asset and chain filtering).

No integration test: this PR adds no new execution-API behaviour, the endpoints it reads were already live.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

body:
Fixes #1788

## Scope and overall risk

Scope: the language-learning sentence storage write boundary in `apps/pomo/src/features/language-learning/storage.ts`, its append/save callers, sentence-storage consumers, and injected-boundary tests in `apps/pomo/src/features/language-learning/__tests__/storage.spec.ts`.

Overall risk: low after the fix. Before the fix, a reproducible P2 data-integrity defect allowed multiple stored sentence records for one `dialogueId`; after the fix, no P0, P1, or P2 findings remain.

## P0–P2 findings

### P0

none

### P1

none

### P2

#### P2-1 — Duplicate language-learning sentences for one dialogue ID — fixed

- Risk: repeated saves could put duplicate records for one dialogue in the language-learning collection and produce duplicate library entries.
- Root cause: `appendLanguageLearningSentences` concatenated the current collection and incoming records, while `writeLanguageLearningSentences` persisted the result without enforcing `dialogueId` uniqueness.
- Before verification: the #1788 reproduction—append the same `dialogueId` twice, or write the same record twice—produced two stored records (GitHub issue evidence).
- Changed files and behavior: `storage.ts` now filters every write through a `Set` keyed by `dialogueId`, preserving the first record and collection order. This covers direct writes, appends, deletes that rewrite the collection, and future callers of the write boundary. `storage.spec.ts` adds direct-write and repeated-append regressions.
- After verification: the focused storage suite passed 1 file and 4 tests; the language-learning relevance suite passed 37 files and 152 tests. Both duplicate-input cases now persist one record.
- Rationale/tradeoff: first-seen data wins, matching the existing language-learning word-storage deduplication contract and avoiding an unrelated replacement policy.

## Review pass summary

Two passes completed: an initial relevance-cone/root-cause review and a fresh post-fix P0–P4 review. Behavior, refactoring, and naming/structure perspectives were reviewed across the changed storage boundary, callers, callees, schema, consumers, tests, and configuration. No additional P0–P2 findings were found in the final pass.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/pomo/src/features/language-learning/__tests__/storage.spec.ts --project unit` — passed, 1 file and 4 tests.
- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/pomo/src/features/language-learning apps/pomo/src/components/language-learning --project unit` — passed, 37 files and 152 tests.
- `pnpm typecheck` — passed, 17 successful Turbo tasks. The runner emitted non-fatal cache `Operation not permitted` warnings; all scheduled typecheck tasks succeeded.
- `pnpm lint` — passed with exit code 0. It emitted existing warnings in unrelated files; neither changed file emitted a lint warning.
- `pnpm exec oxlint apps/pomo/src/features/language-learning/storage.ts apps/pomo/src/features/language-learning/__tests__/storage.spec.ts` — passed with no output.
- `pnpm format` — passed; oxfmt processed 4,856 files.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `graft check .` — passed; the wiring graph is in sync.

## Verification gaps

1. V1 — The repository-wide `pnpm test` command was not run. The changed path and its component callers were covered by the 37-file relevance suite; unrelated package tests remain outside this verification pass.
2. V2 — Browser E2E was not run because the fix changes a synchronous storage boundary and no route or UI structure. The injected-storage tests verify the persistence contract, but do not exercise a real browser's `localStorage` implementation.
3. V3 — The commit hook could not run because `lefthook` was unavailable in `PATH`. The required unit tests, typecheck, lint, formatting, targeted oxlint, diff check, and graph check were run manually and passed.

## P3–P4 findings and proposals

none in the reviewed relevance cone.

## Out of scope

The issue body contains an unrelated, unverified note about `/whats-new` not calling `writeViewedRelease`; that path does not intersect language-learning sentence storage and was not investigated or changed.

## Pull request status

No existing PR was updated. This report belongs to the new draft PR against `dev`.

`, not an ``: the link to the Google Form disappears from the built HTML altogether, so a form that accepts nobody is unreachable rather than merely discouraging. The pulsing halo is dropped too; - the pill keeps the geometry of the live button, so the page does not reflow on the day. ## `closed = true` is a manual switch — merge on 26/09 at 10:00 This is deliberately **not** a date comparison at build time. No recovery retry, spend, Notion Agent use, ROOT/Genesis merge, credential mutation or Forge activation is authorized by this PR.

author: adarsh-chiriyamkandath-jose
body:
**Design only. No runtime behaviour changes.** This PR adds one document,
`docs/intent-and-authority-rfc.md`. Nothing is implemented, no flag moves, no
schema changes. It is a decision document: the question it exists to answer is
whether this architecture is worth building, not how to build it.

It closes Phase B of the autonomy work, following the eight-PR truthfulness
audit (#77, #78, #79, #80, #81, #82, #83, #84).

---

## Revisions from first review (`19a47b6a`)

Five changes, all tightening rules rather than changing the architecture.

1. **Competitive absence claims were stronger than the evidence.** §21.5 now has
   an explicit legend separating a **documented limit** (the vendor positively
   states the boundary, as Convex does with "the human keeps the merge button")
   from **none found** (absence of evidence, not evidence of absence). §22 no
   longer asserts that no competitor has built observer-bounded authority; it
   reports no documented equivalent found, flags that row as the
   weakest-evidenced in the analysis, and marks the explanation as hypothesis.
2. **An Authority Decision is a lease, not a certificate** (new §10.4,
   normative). A stored `AUTO_EXECUTE` would otherwise have introduced a
   time-of-check-to-time-of-use gap: *decision valid → world changes → stale
   AUTO_EXECUTE → mutation.* Execution must now revalidate intent version, grant
   validity, sensor status and freshness, resource fingerprint, capability
   revisions and conflicting recent changes — **inside the single-flight lock**,
   with a failed revalidation read treated as `FREEZE`, never as a pass.
3. **`FREEZE` silences the repair, not the system.** Redefined from "do not act
   and do not propose" to **no mutation and no executable repair proposal**,
   while requiring a diagnostic that names the failed prerequisite and permitting
   remediation of that prerequisite. A frozen action that says nothing reproduces
   the failure it exists to prevent.
4. **Unsafe action and over-refusal are no longer weighted equally** (§18.4).
   Split into a Tier 1 safety constraint (**release gate: zero observed unsafe
   actions in the lab before an action class gets automatic authority, not
   tradeable**) and Tier 2 utility metrics, where over-refusal remains
   first-class but is reported separately rather than netted against safety.
   The zero-observed gate is explicitly labelled a weak guarantee, to be replaced
   by statistical budgets once real traffic exists.
5. **Sensor freshness promoted from Q3 into the core model** (new §7.2).
   `clean` describes demonstrated capability, not current health — a probe that
   fired in June and broke in July still reads `clean` today. A requirement is
   now four parts: probe + current execution success + confidence state +
   freshness bound, with bounds per action class rather than one global TTL.

Also carried from review as non-blocking (§23.1): `authorizedBy` may need an
authorization chain with a named root once org policy grants authority (Q9), and
external PostgreSQL-role attribution is documented as **weak attribution by
construction** — a shared role identifies a credential and a context, never a
person.

Three principles were added to §3 to match: P13 (revalidate before mutating),
P14 (confidence decays), P15 (a refusal explains its blocker).

---

## Two findings that challenge the thesis

These are near the top because they are the ones that should decide the review.

**1. Convex already has most of the generic story.** Researched from vendor docs
and published skill listings (September 2026):

- `schema.ts` is declared, versioned, provenance-carrying intent, enforced at
  runtime at write time. **For document shape this is stronger than
  detect-and-repair**, because prevention beats reconciliation wherever
  prevention is possible. Backenly's `SchemaIntent` is weaker than `schema.ts`
  today, not stronger.
- `convex-self-heal` already wires capture, diagnose, repair, certify, human PR,
  promote, certifying fixes on a preview deployment before review.
- `deploy-guard` already takes standing consent per fix class.

So "intent-aware self-healing" is not by itself a differentiator, and the RFC
says so rather than working around it. What survives is narrower: intent that is
**not a property of application code** (ownership and authorization semantics,
performance objectives, explicit "do not touch" boundaries), reconciled with
nobody in the session, under authority that contracts when the observers
degrade. InsForge separately scans every project daily, so scheduled *detection*
is commoditized and no claim in the RFC rests on it.

**2. Q8 is a blocking product decision, not an engineering one.** Convex stops at
a human PR and never mutates production unattended, which is why it needs no
execution-bound rollback, no stale-state guard and no `FREEZE`. That is simpler
and arguably safer. Most of Backenly's extra machinery is the cost of choosing
unattended execution. If users overwhelmingly prefer PR-gated remediation, much
of the autonomous recovery machinery is operational cost rather than
defensibility.

Q8 blocks **Phase 3**, not Phases 0 to 2: measuring the current system and
building principal and decision observability are worth doing either way.

---

## What the RFC proposes

**Adapt the existing primitives rather than replace them.** Ten of the twelve
mechanisms it touches are kept as-is and re-used as inputs. Only two things are
genuinely new.

- **Centralize on an Authority Decision** — four-valued (`AUTO_EXECUTE`,
  `PROPOSE_ONLY`, `FREEZE`, `DENY`), recorded as a receipt whether it permits or
  refuses, and valid only while its inputs hold. `FREEZE` is the value that did
  not exist during the audit: every bug from #77 to #83 was a case where the
  system could not say "I cannot establish this" and therefore said something
  else.
- **Introduce a unified principal contract** separating `requestedBy`,
  `authorizedBy` and `executedBy`.
- **Connect sensor confidence to authority**, degraded per action dependency
  rather than globally, and including liveness and freshness.
- **Evolve `SchemaIntent` beyond code-shape intent** with provenance, versioning,
  and ownership, objective and boundary scopes.
- **Unify causal identity** across healing and maintenance under one
  `Adaptation`, keeping `Incident` separate.
- **Extend the existing PostgreSQL lab** rather than building a new one.
- **Test one vertical slice: ownership / RLS intent**, with an explicit kill
  criterion.

---

## Four corrections to the Phase A handoff

Checked against merged main. Three of the four make the work smaller.

| Phase A said | Actually |
|---|---|
| No principal model exists; it must be introduced | `BackendEvent.actorType` already exists (`lib/operational-memory/ledger.ts:22`). There are four actor vocabularies, not three. The real gap is that `lib/autonomy/` never writes any of them |
| `SchemaIntent` may miss later columns | Confirmed, with the mechanism: one writer (`lib/ai/minimal-executor.ts:3966`), and the type advertises an `add_column` source no caller produces |
| Sensor health has two callers | Correct, but neither is a decision. The daily 00:40 UTC cron's entire effect is a `console.warn` |
| The evaluation lab must be designed | A substrate already exists: `tests/lab/scenarios.ts` and `seed.ts`, six real-PostgreSQL scenarios. It validates subsystem clustering, not autonomy outcomes |

---

## Review guidance

The sections most worth disagreeing with:

- **§22.1 "Where this is not a moat"** and **§21** (competitive analysis). If the
  narrowing is wrong in either direction, everything downstream changes. Note
  that the *authority contracts when observers degrade* row is `none found` in
  every competitor cell, which is the weakest evidence in the document.
- **§19 first vertical slice** and its kill criterion: if the result is not
  materially better than *Supabase advisor + MCP + an agent that applies the
  fix*

author: rachelpaul68
body:
## FLTR-21131 — Android trailer flickers black when closing fullscreen

[FLTR-21131](https://insight-timer.atlassian.net/browse/FLTR-21131)

### Problem
Closing the course trailer's fullscreen page on Android shows one black frame on the hero just as the fullscreen page finishes fading, right between the poster leaving and the live video. The app also has no way to know when a freshly created Android view has actually painted, so it takes the poster off on the "playing" report, which arrives before the first frame.

### Root cause
Every new platform view attaches the shared player to its own `PlayerView` as it is created (init, the init post, attach-to-window), so the rebuilt hero already draws while the fullscreen page fades over it. When the fullscreen view is then disposed, `SharedPlayerManager.unregisterView` asks **every** surviving view to `reconnectSurface()`. That `player = null; player = current` swap on a view that is already drawing clears its output and blanks its TextureView for a frame until the next frame lands.

Separately, `readyForDisplayChanged` is emitted on iOS only (from `AVPlayerViewController.isReadyForDisplay`); Android had no per-view first-frame signal.

### Fix
- `SharedPlayerManager` records which view's surface the player draws into (`claimSurface` after every attach site, `releaseSurface` in dispose). The disposal notification now only re-attaches survivors when the owner itself went away, so a drawing view is never blanked by a sibling's disposal. Views that were not drawing behave as before.
- `VideoPlayerObserver.onRenderedFirstFrame` emits `readyForDisplayChanged { isReadyForDisplay: true, viewId }` when the view was created with `observesReadyForDisplay`, mirroring the iOS payload. The Dart widget already filters this by view id and forwards it to `onReadyForDisplay`, so no Dart change is needed.

### Verification (Pixel emulator, rainbow debug, frame-by-frame screen recording)
| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Close fullscreen → hero | 1 black frame after the fade | none; hero live under the fading page |
| Plugin log on fullscreen dispose | survivors re-attach | no re-attach (owner still drawing) |
| `readyForDisplayChanged` | never on Android | once per view first frame, with view id |

Not yet confirmed on a physical device.

---

AI Prompt Used:
"we have fixed 1bf8b86826e25fe03f2cafcc458778d33c223b57
Description

On Android a landscape course trailer was cropped to portrait in fullscreen, and after closing fullscreen it played letterboxed inside the portrait course hero.

Root cause. The shared native player keeps a single aspect-fill flag. The plugin sends setUseAspectFill only to the view that currently holds the method channel,
and a newly created platform view copies the flag into its creation params while it is being built. A view only registers with the plugin after the platform round trip,
which is after that frame's post-frame callbacks. On Android the hero view is a fullscreen-context (TextureView) view that holds the channel only while it is alone, and
the fullscreen page's view takes the channel from registration until it is disposed. So:

Opening fullscreen: the page's off-then-on toggle left the flag at the wrong value while the fullscreen view was being built, so it came up cover-filled from the hero's
setting and the later corrective writes landed on the hero underneath.
Closing fullscreen: the hero rebuilt its view while the flag still said letterbox, and the store's post-frame cover-fill write landed on the fading fullscreen view.
When the hero later inherited the channel nothing reapplied.
Portrait trailers were unaffected because both hosts resolve to cover-fill, so the flag never changed. iOS is unaffected because the hero stays the primary view there.

Fix. Two small changes so both views copy the right mode as they are built:

The shared fullscreen view sends a single aspect-fill write on Android instead of the off-then-on toggle. The pre-build apply already runs before the view is created,
so the view now copies the correct policy. iOS keeps the toggle its setter needs.
The trailer store applies cover-fill on Android before bumping the inline view generation, so the rebuilt hero copies cover-fill at build time. The write is delivered
to the closing fullscreen view, where the existing post-frame write already went.
