author: svenger87
body:
## What had happened

[Discussion #277](https://github.com/svenger87/kinboard/discussions/277). On WSL the page loaded from `localhost:3001` and the family-name step worked. After that came "Kinboard-Server nicht erreichbar", sometimes cleared after 2–3 minutes, while "Live-Updates pausiert" stayed on permanently and nothing got saved.

**The page and the data travel separately.** The browser client is built from `window.__ENV.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` (`src/lib/supabase/client.ts`). That is an absolute URL taken from `API_EXTERNAL_URL` (`docker-compose.yml:483`), and `next.config.mjs` has no same-origin rewrite for it. So:

| step | goes to | |
|---|---|---|
| load page | `localhost:3001` | ✅ |
| family + device (`/api/session/join`) | same origin | ✅ that is why he got that far |
| `useValidateStoredFamily` → `supabase.from("families")` | `API_EXTERNAL_URL` | ❌ timeout → "nicht erreichbar" |
| realtime socket, every write | `API_EXTERNAL_URL` | ❌ |

`setup.sh` suggests that address, and the suggestion was backwards:

```bash
if [[ "$public_ip" != "$lan_ip" ]]; then   # "server with public IP (VPS)"
  suggested="http://${public_ip}:8100"
```

On a VPS the public address sits on the interface, so the two values are **equal**. Behind any home router they always **differ**, because the public address belongs to the router. The result: a home install was offered an address it could only reach from inside through a port forward with hairpin NAT. Under WSL2, `hostname -I` additionally returns the VM's internal 172.x, and the same branch fires.

**This is not WSL-specific.** Measured on an ordinary VM behind a home router:

```
detected: public=91.96.77.x  own=[10.10.10.60 10.221.0.1 172.17.0.1]  route=10.10.10.60  wsl=0
old logic -> http://<public ip>:8100     (the router's address)
new logic -> http://10.10.10.60:8100
```

## What changed

The decision is now `suggest_api_url()`. It takes the detected facts as arguments, so it can be tested without a network:

- **WSL** (`/proc/version` names microsoft) → `localhost:8100`. The VM's address is invisible to the LAN and changes on restart, while the Windows browser reaches localhost through WSL's forwarding.
- **A public IP** only when it is one of this machine's own addresses.
- Otherwise the **source address of the default route**, not whichever address `hostname -I` lists first. On a Docker host that can be the docker0 bridge, as the output above shows.

`install.sh` only calls `setup.sh`, so this is the one place to change.

## Verification

New spec `e2e/setup-suggested-url.spec.ts`, 6 cases. Red was taken against the **old logic moved into the function unchanged**, not against a missing function, so the failures are the bug itself:

```
home server behind router   old: http://87.1.2.3:8100   -> now LAN IP
WSL                         old: http://87.1.2.3:8100   -> now localhost
docker0 listed first        old: http://87.1.2.3:8100   -> now LAN IP
VPS / no public / nothing   unchanged, passing before and after
```

Fast suite **2712 passed / 0 failed / 87 skipped**. I did not run `setup.sh` itself on the devbox, because it rewrites tracked templates there. Only the detection commands and the function were executed.

## Docs

`Windows-WSL-Host.md`, shipped in #276, was wrong in three places and is corrected here:

- it said to open `localhost:3000`, but the webapp is on **3001**
- it assumed Docker Desktop, but the reporter ran **Docker Engine inside WSL**, which is reachable only through localhost forwarding
- it said nothing about **`API_EXTERNAL_URL`**, which was the actual cause of #277

It now has a section on the second address: the exact symptoms, the three `.env` lines, and the mirrored-networking setting other devices need.

Quick start said setup "auto-detects a sensible default … usually just press Enter", which promised exactly what was broken. It now says what gets suggested in which situation, and that re-running `setup.sh` keeps a wrong address, so the `.env` has to be edited by hand.

## Still open, deliberately not in here

- Existing installs that accepted the public IP keep it, because `setup.sh` never overwrites an address it already wrote (by design). The docs explain the manual fix.
- WSL mirrored networking is documented, not tested; this machine does not run WSL.

author: abhay-yemekar
body:
## What

The candidate side of the story — the v1.1 headline from `docs/competitor-analysis.md`. Every competitor treats candidates as the object being screened; this makes them a participant.

**Recruiter side** (candidate detail page → "Share outcome with candidate"):
- Generate a per-candidate link with an optional note; the token is shown exactly once, supersedes earlier links, and shows read counts + instant revoke. Every lifecycle step is hash-chain audited (`candidate_report.created/revoked`).

**Candidate side** (`/report/<token>`, no account, token = credential):
- Plain-language block explaining what the numbers are *before* any score appears.
- Overall score + friendly band (Strong / Good / Partial / Emerging match) — a band, not a leaderboard rank.
- Per-criterion cards: score, the model's rationale, the exact quoted resume lines behind it, and the anchored 0–5 scale with the awarded level highlighted.
- Never shows: contact info, resume files, other candidates, org internals. Privacy projection enforced server-side.
- Branded (ink/cream/coral), accessible states for missing / revoked / error.

## Design decision worth noting
The public endpoint joins scoring runs on **actual score rows for that candidate** — a newer completed run whose batch failed (rate limits, provider outage) must not blank a report the earlier run already produced. Caught during live verification, not by the initial tests.

## Tests & verification
- New `candidate-report.int.test.ts` (5 tests): setup, supersede semantics, public projection (asserts absence of other candidates AND the candidate's own contact info), read counting, revoke → 410, unknown token → 404.
- Live browser verification: generate → once-only URL → public report rendered (overall 12/100, Emerging match, 5 scored criteria, evidence quotes, scale) → read count climbed → revoke → revoked page.
- 53 API + 88 core tests, typechecks, biome clean; migration 0006 applied to local + Neon (simple CREATE TABLE — no Wave-3-style cast risk).

author: kratobal
body:
## What this does

Card `2f961a10`. The internal status note leaves the **partner's** downloadable
document package. The partner-facing status label and the colleague's name
stay.

Balázs, 2026-09-21: *"a megjegyzes nem kell a nev igen"*, then *"keruljon ki
onnan is"*. The first sentence was about the portal's ticket log (#889); this
is the PDF.

## Why a parameter, not a caller's memory

The same service builds the package for **our own** readers too
(`scope.kind === "internal"`), and there the note is still due. If the
difference were decided by which caller remembers to pass something, a later
change would take it from both.

`belso` is a required parameter, so whoever builds a package has to say who it
is for. The line moved into a pure function (`service-job-package-log.ts`), so
all of this is measurable without a database.

## Four assertions, and two of them are about how this goes wrong later

| assertion | what it protects |
| --- | --- |
| the partner package has no note | the decision itself |
| the internal package **has** the note | a later "simplification" taking it from both |
| the name survives in both | Balázs said the name stays |
| the service derives `belso` from the scope | a hardcoded `false` |

The second one is the card's own requirement and it earns its place: the
partner-side assertion would happily pass while the internal reader silently
lost the note — the partner is not supposed to see it, and the internal reader
would not know they should.

The fourth earns its place for the mirror-image reason: **all five** function
assertions stay green against a hardcoded `belso: false`. Only a separate
assertion on the call site catches it.

## Gates

`format:check` clean, `typecheck` 7/7, `test` 12/12, `build` 7/7, all with
`--force`.

## Calibration

Four deliberate breaks, prediction written to a file first. Each turns exactly
its own assertion red, run count 3250 throughout.

body:
One field, and it changes no claim in the entry.

`surfaces.mcp` moves from `https://docs.allium.so/ai/mcp/overview`, a page about the server, to `https://mcp.allium.so/`, the host this entry's own probe record ([`p-20260920-allium-mcp-unauthenticated`](https://public-agents.com/evidence/p-20260920-allium-mcp-unauthenticated.json)) measured. Version 2, `updated` refreshed, one profile section saying why. The overview page stays cited in Provenance, where it was read, so no reader loses a link.

**Why now.** The cto's [reach note on issue #123](https://github.com/PublicAgents/public-agents/issues/123) graded 8 of 35 access claims ON RECORD: re-runnable by a human reading the entry, never asked by the nightly sweep, and therefore able to decay silently. Four of those eight carry a documentation page in `surfaces.mcp`, and all four claim `noAccountNeeded` in the generous direction or rest on a measurement the sweep cannot repeat. That note is an input to this change, not the change itself.

**What settled it is a measurement, and it says only one of the four can be fixed this way.** From this container, 2026-09-21 12:14Z, no credentials, HEAD then GET then a `--json '{}'` POST:

| endpoint | HEAD | GET | POST `{}` | `check-links` verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mcp.allium.so/` | 405 | 405 | 406 | **alive** |
| `api.bitrefill.com/mcp` | 400 | 400 | 401 | dead |
| `catalog.shopify.com/api/ucp/mcp` | 404 | 404 | 422 | dead |
| `mcp.api.coingecko.com/mcp` | 404 | 404 | 406 | dead |

`linkAnswers` counts `405` as alive for a HEAD/GET target, so Allium's endpoint can be named here today with no change to any rule. The other three answer a browser method with `400` or `404` while answering a real client perfectly well, so their entries hold a documentation page because this repository's link gate refuses the endpoint, not because the vendor hides it. That part is recorded on #123 rather than here; the narrow change that would fix it (retry a dead `surfaces.mcp` or `surfaces.api` with a POST of `{}` before calling it dead) is a change to the gate that decides what I may file, so I have argued it there instead of writing it.

Local checks: `validate --base origin/main`, `pr-class` **data**, `verify-ownership --author researcher-public-agents-bot` (1 decision), `check-links --changed-only` 21/21, `lint:prose`, `git diff --check`. Profile 11,105 bytes.

author: maxonfjvipon
body:
closes: #958

`select-starts-with-double-slash` complained that an expression scans the whole
document, and then asked a different question: whether the characters `//` open
an attribute literally called `select`. The scan and the spelling came apart in
three directions, two under-reporting and one over. It reads the cost now:

```js
const scanning = function(found) {
  const paths = gathered(found, ['path'])
  const results = []
  if (!once(found)) {
    parseOf(found).tokens.forEach((token, at) => {
      if (token.type === TOKENS.DOUBLE_SLASH &&
        paths.some((one) => one.from === at)) {
```

A `//` counts where it opens a path of its own, whichever attribute carries the
expression and wherever in the parse it stands — so an `xsl:when`'s `test`, an
`xsl:key`'s `use` and the braces of a literal result element draw it, and so do
both scans of `distinct-values((//o/@name, //o/@local))`. `items//item`
descends from a step, `/objects//o` from an absolute one, `$root//node` from a
binding and `.//item` from the context node; none of the four starts at the
root, and none is reported. That is the test `owned` already applies one
language over.

`once` is the other half. A top-level `xsl:variable` or `xsl:param` is bound
once for the transformation, against the source root, so the scan there is the
one traversal there is no cheaper way to ask for — and hoisting an expression
into a global binding is what the motive teaches for the repeated-scan case, so
the check was telling those authors to do what they had done.

What a global binding binds is its *content* as much as its `select`, so `once`
climbs to the declaration rather than reading the element the expression hangs
off. Between the two, only an instruction whose content runs per item breaks
it — `REPEATING` is those five and not a rule about depth. eo's
`restore-aliases.xsl` is the shape: four `xsl:sequence` children of one global
binding, of which reading the carrying element answered two and reported the
other two.

The name moved with the question. `scans-whole-document` says the harm where
the old one named an attribute this no longer singles out and a position it no
longer asks about; a `--suppress` substring, an `.xslint.yml` override and the
docs page move with it. One thing falls out: the `SHADOWED` table in the speed
gate is empty now, that rename having removed the only pair whose names nested.

Over the three pinned corpora, 131 rows keep their place, the 16 standing under
a global binding are withdrawn, and 175 arrive. The pattern pair beside it is
untouched — `starts-with-double-slash` and `use-double-slash` name different
harms in a different language, and one of them carries a fix this one cannot
have since #949.

author: hyperpolymath
body:
## Why

The guard in `dogfood-gate.yml` counted `.a2ml` files only:

```
COUNT=$(find . -name '*.a2ml' -not -path './.git/*' | wc -l)
```

so a repo whose manifest is written in the current grammar is reported as having none, and the
summary/compliance row is skipped by the same predicate (`if find . -name '*.a2ml' ... | grep -q .`).
The validator itself has scanned both grammars for a while -- the caller's predicate is the bug.

## Authority

- `rsr-template-repo/.github/workflows/deed-validate.yml` (the mint source) is what this wording is
  copied from, byte for byte, including `-type f`-free `find` and the dual-accept stance.
- `standards#837` — "DEED conversion campaign", campaign step 4: *"flip ... RSR gates from `.a2ml`
  presence to `.deed` presence alongside". Gate predicates, not document contents.
- `deed-ecosystem/README.adoc`: *"The DEED format name and `.deed` extension are final, not A2ML."*

## Deliberately not done

- No `.a2ml` file is translated or renamed. #837 makes classification into the four DEED forms and
  per-family mapping specs a prerequisite for mass translation; that is not this PR.
- No gate that *reads* a retained file is touched (`CLAIMS.a2ml`, `.machine_readable/Debtfile.a2ml`,
  `contractiles/INDEX.a2ml`); rewriting those would fail gates that currently pass.
- No job-id or shell-var renames (`a2ml-validate`, `A2ML_COUNT`): they are referenced from `needs:`
  and `${{ needs.*.outputs }}`. The Checks-UI label is updated, as it has no references.

_Estate-wide `.deed` gate convergence, 2026-09-21. Script: `estate-audit/engine/deed_gate_migration.py`._

author: gregra81
body:
The reflection loop sends a batch back to `extract` when the critic rejects more than `CRITIC_REJECT_RATIO` of it. The critique it carried named the rejections only, and the standing instruction is "Try again. Be stricter. If nothing survives the test, return an empty list." A retry replaces the batch wholesale, so the claims the critic had just kept went out with it.

The critique now carries those claims as well, under `CRITIQUE_KEPT_PREAMBLE`, and asks for them back unchanged. With nothing kept it renders byte for byte as before, so fixtures recorded on that path still replay. `14-prompts.md` has the new Retry block.

### How this surfaced

Scenario 007 has covered nothing since 2026-09-18. `19-value-to-a-user.md` read that as the critic rejecting the privacy claim once it could see CLAUDE.md. It did not: it kept that claim and rejected the other three, and 3 of 4 is over the ratio. Fixture `018af95a…` is the retry prompt and an empty candidate list. Any session whose one good claim arrives beside several weak ones lost it the same way, so re-authoring the transcript — the fix the doc proposed — would have hidden this.

007 now runs as written: step 1 records the privacy claim, step 2 contradicts it, the resolver answers `undecidable`, and the `add` is held under `unresolved_contradiction`.

### Cost and scope

Eight recorded cases retried with something kept, about a fifth of both sets: scenarios 002 and 007, golden 004, 009, 013, 025, 028 and 030. Re-recorded for \$1.46 of list price (signposts-eval `93748ba`). No golden expectation moved. The 22 fixtures the old 007 recording left behind are deleted here; signposts-eval keeps its own store whole.

### Existing tests changed, with agreement

Two in `test/unit/graph/nodes/critic.test.ts` asserted that the critique never names the kept claim, which is the behaviour that lost it. Both now assert the kept claim appears under the preamble and that its reason stays out of the rejection list.

`pnpm verify` exits 0, `src/graph` back at 100. 1725 tests pass with the network denied.

author: ormeilu
body:
## What

`POST /api/v1/ui-events` and `POST /api/v1/mcp-logs` turned a failed ClickHouse insert into an `ApiError` and did nothing else. The dashboard swallows ingest failures on purpose, so a deployment with a missing `ui_events` table lost its whole UX stream and nothing at either end said so. The 500 body also quoted ClickHouse's error text and the insert URL back to the browser.

## How

Every lost write now goes through the new `crates/rolter-control/src/ingest_failure.rs`:

- **counter**: `rolter_control_ingest_failures{stream, reason}` sits next to the other control-plane metrics in `ControlHistograms`. `stream` is `ui_events` or `mcp_logs`. `reason` is `insert` (the store refused the write or couldn't be reached) or `unconfigured` (no `CLICKHOUSE_URL`). The store's error text is never a label.
- **rate-limited warn**: a lock-free `WarnGate` (two atomics and a compare-exchange) allows one `tracing::warn!` per stream per minute. Each warn carries a `suppressed` count of the failures since the previous one, so the rate is still visible. The log keeps the store's full error, but any `user:password@` inside a URL is masked, because `CLICKHOUSE_URL` can carry credentials.
- **generic 500**: the client now gets `store error: the event store did not accept the write; the control-plane log has the detail`. The status stays 500 on purpose, because `ux.ts` treats 500 as transient and keeps sending, so capture resumes when the store comes back. When `CLICKHOUSE_URL` is unset, the body still names the setting, since that message is useful to the operator.

author: glennmichael123
body:
Closes #2637.

`returningAll()` in bun-query-builder 0.2.69 appended ` RETURNING *` on every dialect, so on MySQL every such write was a syntax error that wrote nothing: 63 call sites, four behind dashboard PATCH routes. 0.2.70 (stacksjs/bun-query-builder#1160) routes it through `returning('*')`.

## Commits

1. **`fix(deps)`**: six manifests require `^0.2.70`. Both lockfiles move with them. `pantry.lock` was edited by hand and **CI's pantry 0.11.60 found nothing to change** (the `compile` job's lockfile check passed).
   - New `commerce/tests/returning-all-writes.test.ts` runs the issue's own calls on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL.
2. **`test(cms)`**: the page-document round trip now runs on MySQL too; it had been held back by exactly this.
3. **`fix(orm)` update/delete precedence**: 0.2.70 started shipping native static `update(id, data)` and `delete(id)`. Stacks installed its own only when the builder had none, so the upgrade silently replaced both:
   - A guarded attribute stopped throwing `MassAssignmentException`. `{ name, is_admin }` wrote the name, dropped `is_admin`, and reported success.
   - Async `set:` hooks stopped being awaited, so **`User.update(id, { password })` threw**, because `set.password` is bcrypt. No plaintext was stored; the write failed.
   - Stacks' versions now win, which restores 0.2.69's behaviour exactly.
   - A tripwire test fails if the builder ships another Stacks helper natively.
4. **`fix(orm)` forceDelete**: `forceDelete` skipped `withTrashed()`, so it could not purge a row that was already soft-deleted, and it answered `true` regardless. 0.2.70 routes its native `remove(id)` there. This was latent: no caller in the repo.
5. **`fix(orm)` types**: `Model.update` was typed as never `undefined`, because the builder's signature came first in the intersection. Verified with a type probe both ways.

## How it was checked

| | 0.2.69 | 0.2.70 + this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| returning-all-writes on MySQL | all six fail, "near 'RETURNING \*'" | all six apply and return their row |
| page-document on MySQL | errno 1064 | passes |
| `Model.update(1, { is_admin })` | `MassAssignmentException` | `MassAssignmentException` |
| `Member.update(1, { password })` with an async setter | hashed | hashed |

- **Every core package suite**: 89 packages, 13k+ tests, against 0.2.70 with SQLite, PostgreSQL 16 and MySQL 8.4.5. The only failures are the local-only ones main shows here as well: a stale `dist/`, and Redis being stopped.
- **Typecheck**: the framework, app and views typechecks add no error.
- **Compatibility audit**: each of the 14 upstream commits was traced to every Stacks call site, by five independent auditors, and every finding had to survive two skeptics.
  - The raw-fragment binding change and the `whereRaw` change: no affected site.
  - The update/delete shadowing and both `orm` defects above: found independently of my own diagnosis, and fixed here.
  - `query_logs` now receives real SQL and bindings on PostgreSQL/MySQL, where it used to log `[object Promise]`. Both skeptics refuted this as not new: SQLite has always stored bindings verbatim. Whether bindings belong in that table at all is a separate question.

body:
Owner report: every screen shows a spinner for a noticeable time on every open. Closes #209, closes #217.

## Backend
- **Timing:** `Server-Timing` header on every response (app ms, DB ms, query count, cache hit/miss); requests over 300 ms logged (`SLOW_REQUEST_LOG_MS`); Sentry tracing at 5% (`SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE`).
- **Batched access checks:** `getMembershipsOnFarms` / `getAccessiblePondIdsForFarms` replace per-farm loops in Today/alert-center, daily brief, `pond-context?scope=mine`, lunar list and `GET /farms`. `pond-context?scope=mine` for a 3-farm owner: ~42 queries → 16 (0 on cache hit). **Permission path — review carefully**; `batched-access.spec.ts` proves equivalence with the per-farm calls.
- **Per-user Redis read-through cache** (`@CachedRead`): alert-center today/briefing/live-briefing/all, daily-brief, pond-context (60 s); `GET /farms`, `/ponds/mine` (120 s). Key `rc:u:<userId>` hash, field = URL — never shared across users. Any successful write by a user clears their cache and every co-member's **before** the response returns. Redis calls capped at 250 ms; errors/timeouts = no cache. Bodies > 512 KB not cached.
- **#217:** `GET /ponds/mine` now honours per-pond scoping (a pond-restricted worker saw every pond on the farm). Test in `pond-read-scope.spec.ts`.
- No migration.

## App
- `useCachedFetch` (`src/query/hooks.ts`): last answer paints instantly, background refresh on focus, full spinner only when nothing is on screen, failed refresh keeps rows + `StaleNotice`. In-memory only; team/attendance/leave excluded (C5.4).
- 19 screens migrated: 11 log histories, feeding-tray checks, health check, cycle list/detail/result, expenses, transactions, harvest plans.

## Verification
Merged latest development (no conflicts). Backend: tsc clean, 174 suites / 2240 tests. Frontend: tsc clean, 213 suites / 1724 tests. Not run on a device.

## Risks
Shared permission code (batched access); +1 Upstash command per cached GET and per write; on a cache hit the lazy photo drain and critical disease push skip that request (catch up on the next miss, ≤60 s). Free-plan cold start (30–60 s) is untouched — only a paid plan fixes that.

Do not self-merge.

author: derkoenigeu
body:
Letzter Rest aus dem Rebranding, gefunden beim Grep über alle Repos der Organisation.

Die `composer.json` steht seit dem Rebranding korrekt auf `zebra-group/personio-jobs`. Der eingecheckte generierte Stand hing hinterher:

| Datei | Problem |
|---|---|
| `vendor/composer/installed.php` | trug weiterhin `mindbox/personio-jobs` |
| `composer.lock` | `content-hash` passte nicht mehr zur `composer.json` — Composer warnte bei jedem Lauf, die Lockdatei sei veraltet |

Beides mit `composer install` bzw. `composer update --lock` regeneriert.

## Warum der Diff so klein ist

Der lokale Composer (2.10.2) hätte bei der Gelegenheit auch `autoload.php`, `ClassLoader.php`, `InstalledVersions.php` und `platform_check.php` neu geschrieben. Diese Änderungen sind **bewusst nicht** übernommen: sie heben die mit ausgelieferte Composer-Runtime auf eine neuere Version und ändern deren Verhalten im Fehlerfall von `exit` / `trigger_error` auf `throw`. Das ist eine Verhaltensänderung in produktiv ausgeliefertem Code und gehört nicht in eine Namenskorrektur.

## Verifikation

- `composer validate` — sauber (nur der übliche Hinweis zum `version`-Feld)
- Smoke-Test mit der **unveränderten** Runtime gegen die neue `installed.php`: Root-Paket wird als `zebra-group/personio-jobs` gemeldet, PSR-4-Autoloading der Klassen in `classes/` funktioniert
- `php -l` über alle PHP-Dateien des Plugins

## Kontext

Das Plugin ist **nicht** auf Packagist veröffentlicht (404 für beide Paketnamen, Vendor `zebra-group` existiert dort nicht) und auch nicht im offiziellen GPM-Index gelistet. Es wird per Git bezogen. Ein Packagist-Rename, wie ursprünglich vermutet, entfällt damit — diese Änderung ist rein kosmetisch und beseitigt die letzte `mindbox`-Zeichenkette in den Repos neben der bewusst offengelassenen `appId` in drift.

author: ai-zaytsev
body:
`simple-vpn.download` заблокирован, `simple-app.download` его заменяет. **Ничего не выкачено** — новый домен не должен нигде появиться, пока страница не чистая.

## Три факта, установленных до правок

**Обновления не сломаются.** Адрес APK приходит с сервера, в приложение не вшит. Установленные приложения пойдут на новый домен сами, без релиза.

**Блокировали не origin.** Домен всё время стоял за прокси Cloudflare — искать было нечего. Значит совпало **имя или страница**, и твоя гипотеза подтверждается.

**HTTPS на origin есть.** `nginx.conf` слушает только 80, но `certbot --nginx` выпускает сертификат при выкате. Значит `proxied: false` не дефект, а необходимость для HTTP-01. Здесь я сначала прочитал наоборот — увидел `listen 80` и решил, что TLS даёт Cloudflare.

## Что изменено

Домен в пяти местах. `server_name` держит **оба** имени: старое резолвится вне России, розданные ссылки продолжают работать и получают ту же чистую страницу.

Продукт на сайте — **Simple**. Где слово несло смысл, фраза переписана, а не выкинута: «до 10 Мбит/с через защищённое соединение», «российские приложения работают напрямую». Название приложения не тронуто — краулер читает сайт, а не APK.

## Guard дважды был неправ

Он важнее обычного: домен тратится один раз, и тратит его первый краул.

| версия | что делала |
|---|---|
| `grep -i` | **пропустила** страницу со словами «Обход блокировок» — в этой локали `-i` сворачивает только ASCII |
| классы `[Вв]` | **отметила почти каждую строку** — класс многобайтовых символов читается побайтово |
| перечисление слов | работает; испытана семью подделками в обоих регистрах |

Ни одну из двух ошибок не нашло бы чтение кода. Обе выглядели работающими.

## Осталось со словом

**Автоблокировка** в инструкции — имя настройки Samsung, переименовать значит сломать инструкцию.

**Архивная ссылка 0.1.0** ведёт на `simple-vpn-0.1.0.apk`: имя в манифесте и в хранилище, не в репозитории. В долге, с тремя вариантами закрытия.

## Что нужно от тебя — до выката

1. **Проверь, что токен `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` видит зону `simple-app.download`.** Если нет — выкат упадёт на «Cloudflare zone was not found». В Cloudflare: My Profile → API Tokens → у токена в Zone Resources должна быть и новая зона.
2. **Создай `support@simple-app.download`** — проще всего Email Routing в Cloudflare с пересылкой на твою почту. Пока не создан, ссылка «Поддержка» на сайте будет отбивать письма.
3. **Оранжевое облако.** Выкат поставит серое, чтобы certbot выпустил сертификат. После выката вернёшь прокси, если он нужен — но учти: в прошлый раз он не спас.

Скажешь, когда готово — мерджу и выкачу.

author: copilot
body:
The `daily-quotes-record` Actions job was failing on transient upstream responses from EastMoney because the export step exited before its retry logic could run. This change makes the workflow honor its existing retry policy for non-zero `skr` exits while preserving clear failure reporting when all attempts fail.

- **Retry control flow**
  - Capture the `skr eco --export-latest-csv` exit status explicitly instead of letting `set -euo pipefail` terminate the step immediately.
  - Retry up to the existing `max_attempts` when `skr` exits non-zero.

- **Failure reporting**
  - Continue surfacing `[FATAL]` log lines when present.
  - Fall back to a generic `skr exited with status ...` error when the command fails without a `[FATAL]` marker.
  - Preserve the existing hard failure for `"partial failures"` output.

- **Workflow change**
  ```yaml
  status=0
  ./_skr/output/bin/skr eco --export-latest-csv --export-dir ./monthly 2>&1 | tee export.log || status=$?

  if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
    # retry or fail with captured context
  fi
  ```

author: masalasev-ops
body:
Five corrections from the phase 9 second sign-off review, one commit each against the checkpoint that built the work (A, B, C and E are 9.2; D is 9.1), then one commit filling in the figures.

Before any test was written, mutations A and B were re-run over 7d17213 and **both left 1156 of 1156 green**, which confirms the review's finding.

## A (9.2): a pass that starts in the same second as its claim

The drain reads a request's own run as one of the name's passes started **at or after** the claim. Both instants are stored to the second, and on the live drain the pass started inside the claim's own second (claim at about 05:41:02.9, run stamped 05:41:03Z). Every test put the pass five seconds later, so making the bound strict left the suite green. With a strict bound, a pass that wrote would settle as "refused, the pass left no run at all".

**No code change.** New test: claim at 12:00:05, pass run stamped 12:00:05, and the request settles written under that run.

## B (9.2): the drain loop is now reachable from a test

The instant each request is claimed at was chosen inside `Program.Drain()`, which no test can call. Passing `DateTimeOffset.MinValue` there left the suite green, so the defect repaired in 35be7c6 could come back on the live path unnoticed.

**Code move, behaviour identical.** The loop moved unchanged into `RequestDrain.DrainAsync(databaseFile, clock, pass)`. `Program.Drain` calls it with the system clock and `ResearchPass`, then prints the same line. Everything else is the same as before: one connection per request, the same claim, the same verb and flags per lane, the same run read, the same settlement and settle instant.

New test: the loop runs over a name that already holds an older passing run, with a fixed clock and a pass that writes no run. The request settles refused with a null `run_id`.

## C (9.2): "already in the queue" said only when it is true

The surface answered every constraint failure with "is already in the queue". That is false when the **primary key** refuses a press made in the same second as an earlier request that has since been withdrawn or settled. The review reproduced it live.

**Fix.** `AskAsync` tells extended code 1555 (key) from 2067 (index):
- An index refusal keeps its answer.
- A key refusal checks whether the name has a request waiting. If it has, the answer is the queue's, because when both constraints are broken SQLite may name either. If not, it says the name was asked for earlier in this same second, names what that request is now, and says pressing again writes a new one.

New test, through the route with the host clock fixed: the same-second answer for a withdrawn row, then 202 one second later, then "already in the queue". `PassHost` now takes a clock. The review's case was also re-run on the rehearsed copy with the fixed build: 409 naming the request withdrawn, then 202, then 409 already in the queue.

## D (9.1): the ask button covered the end of "not written"

**Cause.** `form[method='post']` and `form[method='post'] button` come later in the stylesheet with the same specificity as `form.ask` and `form.ask button`, so they won. The 8px margin became 0.

**Measurement.** Headless Edge at 1400px, scale 1, over the rehearsed copy, with the boxes read through the DevTools protocol:
- Before: all 20 rows had the label's right edge and the button's left edge on the same pixel, and the last glyph ran under the button.
- After: an 8px gap on all 20 rows.

**Fix.** Only the gap changed: `form.ask[method='post']{display:inline-block;margin:0 0 0 8px}`. The button keeps the size and colours the approved list has been drawn with. The `form.ask button` rule loses in the same way and was left alone, because changing it would change how the approved page looks.

**Test.** The suite has no browser, so it resolves the cascade itself. It matches every top-level rule against the ask form and the elements holding it, as the renderer draws them, and asserts the winning left margin is at least 4px. It also checks that the resolver ranks rules correctly.

## E (9.2): SCHEMA's `settled_at` note

The note said `settled_at` is null only while a request is outstanding. A claim writes `state` alone, so a request being written also has a null `settled_at`. The note now says it is null while `outstanding` or `writing`, and the prior text is in CHANGELOG.

**Check against recurrence.** A new test moves requests through all five states using the real statements, records which states left `settled_at` null, and compares that with the states the note names before and after "null while".

## Mutations

Each mutation ran over the whole suite in a scratch worktree at the branch head, never a filter, and was reverted afterwards.

|---|---|---|---|
| MA | `>=` to `>` in the run bound | new test red | red, 1 test, 1160 of 1161 green |
| MB | `DateTimeOffset.MinValue` as the loop's claim instant | new test red | red, 1 test, 1160 of 1161 green |

author: igorshevchik
body:
`Button` labels its own root `data-slot="base"`, but it is also the element **fifteen other components** reach for when they need a button inside themselves. Each passes its own `data-slot` down:

| marker | sent by |
| --- | --- |
| `close` | Modal, Alert, Banner, Drawer, Sidebar, Slideover, Toast, CommandPalette |
| `toggle` | Header |
| `first` / `prev` / `next` / `last` / `ellipsis` | Pagination |
| `fileTrailingButton` | FileUpload |
| `trailingClear` | InputMenu, SelectMenu |
| `back` | CommandPalette |
| `handle` | EditorDragHandle |

**Every one of those markers was dropped.** The root bound `v-bind="slotProps"` *before* its static `data-slot="base"`, so the default overwrote whatever the caller sent. Upstream binds the two the other way round.

Nothing failed, which is why it survived: the element still rendered, its classes still merged, and the only symptom was a selector that matched nothing. It is also why `9ea37c16` had to be ported against a positional selector in #617 — upstream's own `[data-slot="trailingClear"]` found no element here.

## Diagnosed by measurement, not by reading the ordering

A probe passing three attributes to a `B24Button`:

```
data-testid  -> reaches the root
aria-label   -> reaches the root
data-slot    -> does NOT; "base" wins
```

So fallthrough worked in general and only this one attribute was special. Swapping the two lines and re-probing turned the caller's value into the winner (`probe-slot`) while an absent caller still left `base`. That is the whole fix — one line moved.

## 617 snapshots move, verified as a conserved relabelling

Not read line by line — checked as a whole-suite invariant:

```
total data-slot attributes   72083 -> 72083   (unchanged)
base                          5070 ->  4252   (-818)

item                +276     first        +52     ellipsis        +10
close               +170     prev         +52     trailingClear    +8
toggle               +72     next         +52     handle           +6
fileTrailingButton   +68     last         +52
                                                  gains total     818
```

`base` falls by exactly as much as the rest gains, and the total is conserved — so nothing was added or lost, only relabelled. **Nine of those markers stood at zero occurrences across the entire suite before this.**

The remaining changed lines carry no value change at all and differ only in attribute order, since `data-slot` now serializes earlier.

## Both halves pinned

The fix is an ordering, and either half is lost by moving one line:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| revert the order | red — `lets a caller override data-slot on the root` |
| drop the static default | red — `keeps data-slot="base" on the root when the caller sends none`, plus 212 snapshots |

## Also

The `InputMenu` / `SelectMenu` clear tests added in #617 now use upstream's `[data-slot="trailingClear"]` selector instead of addressing the button by position, so that divergence is closed too.

## Verification

Gate with `CI=true`: `dev:prepare` · `lint` · `typecheck` · `build` · `test:coverage` (**357 files, 8131 passed, 6 skipped**) · `test:module` — all green.

author: ranxianglei
body:
## What

Ports headroom's two output-token levers to bili's forward boundary. Output tokens cost ~5x input and are billed the moment they stream out, so the only lever is at request time. Both levers are **default off** — zero behavior change until a user opts in.

**1. Verbosity steering** — appends a byte-stable conciseness directive (levels L0-L4, default L2) at the **tail** of the system prompt. Never prepends (that would bust the prefix cache), **skip-if-absent** (never fabricates a system carrier the client didn't send), and idempotent (re-applying the same level is a no-op; a level change replaces the block in place). Covers all four wires: Anthropic `system`, OpenAI `system`/`developer` message, Responses `instructions`, Google `systemInstruction`.

**2. Effort routing** — structural turn classification of the *final* message list (block composition only, no content pattern-matching). On a mechanical continuation turn it lowers an **already-present** effort field to its floor (`reasoning_effort`, `reasoning.effort`, `output_config.effort` + `thinking.budget_tokens`->1024, `generationConfig.thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget`->128). Never injects an effort field the client did not send, never toggles `thinking.type`; dynamic budgets (`-1`) and non-mechanical turns are left untouched.

Both run at the forward boundary **after** `compat.roles`, so the classifier sees the final wire list; the launcher / native-plugin / `/bili/` lanes inherit it automatically, and compress-retry re-sends share the same idempotent transform.

## Config

```jsonc
// billion-context.json — default OFF
"outputSteering": { "enabled": true, "verbosityLevel": 2, "effortRouting": true }
```
A per-provider route entry overlays the global block: `"providers": { "<url>": { "outputSteering": { ... } } }`.

## Files
- `src/output-steering.ts` (new): directives, idempotent tail placement, structural classifiers, clamp-only effort lowering, wire-shape detection.
- `src/config.ts`: `outputSteering` in the global + per-route schema.
- `src/server.ts`: forward-boundary hook (initial forward + retry re-sends).
- `tests/output-steering.test.ts` (new): 23 regression tests across all four wires.

## Pre-flight
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run build` — success
- `npm test` — **2185 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped** (the skips are the env-gated e2e)
- The full-client `e2e-codex` run needs a live Responses-compatible upstream (see `tests/e2e/README.md`), which isn't available in this environment; its zero-token preflight confirms the codex binary + built dist are ready. Because both levers are inert by default and the entire existing suite passes, the request pipeline is unaffected unless a user enables the feature.

While validating I caught and fixed a bug in this very change: the resolved steering config wasn't defaulted when a `ProxyOptions` object omitted the new field (hand-built options in the test harnesses), which threw a `TypeError` on every forward (surfacing as 502s). Fixed by null-coalescing to `DEFAULT_OUTPUT_STEERING` in `forward()`.

Closes #1093

author: michaelihc
body: > 本 PR 由 Claude Opus 5 编写。 修复 `main` 分支代码审查中发现的全部问题。 ## 改动规模 本 PR 共 `+2129 / -593` 行，其中近六成来自 hint 模板的移植，而非缺陷修复本身： | 部分 | 行数 | |---|---| | 移植的 hint 显示模板（`Services/` + `HintDisplayConfig.cs`，已扣除删除的 `HsmHelper.cs`） | +1245 / −159 | | 实际缺陷修复（`Events/`、`Core/`、`Commands/`、`MainClass`、`Config`、`Scp181Hints`） | +643 / −326 | | 文档与工程配置（README、CHANGELOG、LICENSE、.gitignore、csproj） | +241 / −108 | 需要说明：hint 模板的替换属于**规范一致性**改动，不是缺陷修复。原先的 `HsmHelper.cs` 反射接口 经与 HintServiceMeow 源码比对后确认是正确的。如果认为这部分不值得，可以单独剥离出去，剩余 部分约为 `+880 / -430`，每一行都能对应到一个具体缺陷。 ## README 中记录的 SCP-173 问题 README 将「一掐就死 / 完全没有伤害」列为未修复，并推测 SCP-173 绕过了 `Hurting` 事件。 实际并没有绕过：`PlayerStats.DealDamage` 会在 `handler.ApplyDamage` 之前触发 `Hurting`。 真正的原因是游戏的**秒杀哨兵值**。`Scp173Role.cs:55` 构造的是 `ScpDamageHandler(hub, DeathTranslations.Scp173)`，其 `Damage = -1f`；而 `StandardDamageHandler.cs:49` 把 `-1` 当作「立即清空血条」处理，完全跳过 `ProcessDamage`。 在这个前提下原有逻辑必然失效： - `ev.Amount > 10f` 即 `-1 > 10` 为假，SCP 限伤永远不触发 → 一掐就死。 - `ev.Amount >= victim.Health` 即 `-1 >= 100` 为假，绝境生还永远不触发。 - 在减伤表里加 `"Scp173": 0.5` 会把 `ev.Amount` 变成 `-0.5`，不再是哨兵值， 于是 `ApplyDamage` 落到 `if (Damage <= 0f) return Nothing` → 完全没有伤害。 两种现象，同一个根因。现在 SCP 来源的秒杀会在任何算术运算之前先被换算成 `ScpDamageCap` 伤害，同时覆盖 SCP-049 的秒杀（`Scp049AttackAbility.cs:83`）与 SCP-106 的抓取 （`Scp106Attack.cs:144`）。EXILED 本身就提供了 `HurtingEventArgs.IsInstantKill`。 ## 两个功能此前是死代码 - **口袋空间逃生**：判定条件是 `GetType().Name.Contains("PocketDimension")`，但根本不存在这个 类型 —— 口袋空间的死亡走的是 `UniversalDamageHandler`（`PocketDimensionTeleport.cs:109`） 或 `ScpDamageHandler`（`Scp106Attack.cs:144`），配合 `PocketDecay` 翻译。此外它取消的是 `Dying` 事件，而游戏是在清零血量**之后**才触发该事件的，所以即使判定命中，也只会留下一个 0 血还在走动的玩家，并且因为 `PocketCorroding` 从未被清除而继续掉血。现在改用 `DamageType.PocketDimension` 判定，逃生逻辑移到 `Hurting`，并完全对齐游戏自己的 `PocketDimensionTeleport.Exit`：最佳出口位姿、`Disabled` + `Traumatized`、清除腐蚀效果、 重新随机化传送点。 - **持续伤害免疫**：判定条件是类型名包含 `"Bleeding"` / `"Corroding"`，但流血伤害由 `UniversalDamageHandler` 结算（`CustomPlayerEffects/Bleeding.cs:26`），腐蚀由 `ScpDamageHandler` 结算（`Corroding.cs:25`）。现在改用 `DamageType.IsStatusEffect()`。 ## 撤离后被动立即失效 减伤效果原本在 `ChangingRole` 中重新施加，而该事件在换角**之前**触发， `StatusEffectBase.OnRoleChanged` 会在换角时清除所有效果，因此刚施加的效果随即被抹掉。 现已移至 `Spawned`。 效果等级的含义也与注释不符：`DamageReduction` 保留的伤害是 `1 - intensity * 0.005` （50 级是 −25%，不是 −50%），`BodyshotReduction` 会被游戏钳制在只有 5 项的表内 （50 等价于 4，即 −15%）。两者现在均可配置，并按真实公式写入文档。 ## 物品复制会销毁被拾取的物品 复制发生在 `PickingUpItem` 期间，此时真正的拾取尚未入库。背包已有 7 件物品时， 复制品会占满第 8 格；随后 `ItemSearchCompletor.Complete` 从 `ServerAddItem` 拿到 `null`， 却仍然调用 `TargetPickup.DestroySelf()`，于是物品被删除且从未交付 —— 而提示还在显示 `物品数量+1`。现在只有在两者都放得下时才复制，且仅在复制真正成功时才显示提示。 ## 其余修复 - `Remove` 从未关闭自己施加的增益，导致 `scp181 set <其他人>` 之后，前任仍保留长达一小时的 减伤增益。`Clear` 还会跨回合泄漏绝境生还次数。现在所有清理都走同一条路径。 - `scp181` 指令没有权限检查，任意等级的 RA 用户都能指派该角色。现要求 `PlayersManagement`。 - `Assign` 对已经是 D 级的目标也强制换角，会清空背包并改变出生点。 - 开门概率每次按键都会重新掷骰，连续按键必然开门。失败结果现在会保持 `UnlockRerollCooldownSeconds` 秒。 - `damage_reduction_table` 为 null 时，回退查表会抛 NRE。 - 绝境生还未计入 AHP 与 Hume 护盾，被护盾吸收的伤害也会消耗次数。 - 重复指派会叠加 debuff 守卫协程；死亡广播的 `` 位置错误；注释与实际不符 （注释写 30% 复制但配置是 0.1，注释写「10 级减伤」但代码是 50）。 ## 需要确认的行为变更 - **脚本化处决不再受任何减伤影响** —— Alpha 核弹（`WarheadDamageHandler` 的 `Damage = -1f`）、 坑洞碾压、SCP-079 重新收容、友伤检测器以及 RA `kill` 指令。此前 50% 免伤对它们同样生效， 意味着 SCP-181 有一半概率从核弹下走出来，管理员的击杀指令也可能静默失败。如果希望保留 核弹的概率判定，回退很容易。 - **缺少 HSM 时的表现** —— hint 现在统一走共享的 `HintDisplayProvider` 模板，按工作区的 hint 规范，在 HintServiceMeow 缺失时只记录一次日志、不显示任何内容。原实现会回退到 Broadcast 和每秒一次的原生 hint。如需恢复，将 `hint_display.enable_vanilla_fallback` 设为 `true`。 ## 工程整理 - `SCP181.csproj` 引用了 `..\..\Managed\` 与 `..\packages\ExMod.Exiled.9.14.2\`， 仓库里两者都不存在，任何 clone 都无法构建。现替换为 SDK 风格的 `Scp181.csproj`， 引用路径可通过属性覆盖。 - `HsmHelper.cs` 由移植的共享 provider 取代；补充 `.gitignore`（此前 `bin/`/`obj/` 既未提交也未忽略）、 与组织内其他仓库一致的 MIT `LICENSE`，以及 `CHANGELOG.md`。 - 仓库文档、代码注释与日志改为英文；游戏内文本保持中文。 ## 验证情况 针对 SCP:SL `Managed` 与 EXILED 9.14.2 编译通过（0 warning，0 error）。 **尚未在实机服务器上验证** —— 尤其是伤害相关路径值得走一遍实机流程： SCP-173 拧脖、SCP-049 秒杀、SCP-106 抓取与走错出口、以九尾狐/混沌身份撤离、 背包接近满时拾取物品，以及核弹。 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: hyperpolymath
body:
## Why

The guard in `dogfood-gate.yml` counted `.a2ml` files only:

```
COUNT=$(find . -name '*.a2ml' -not -path './.git/*' | wc -l)
```

so a repo whose manifest is written in the current grammar is reported as having none, and the
summary/compliance row is skipped by the same predicate (`if find . -name '*.a2ml' ... | grep -q .`).
The validator itself has scanned both grammars for a while -- the caller's predicate is the bug.

## Authority

- `rsr-template-repo/.github/workflows/deed-validate.yml` (the mint source) is what this wording is
  copied from, byte for byte, including `-type f`-free `find` and the dual-accept stance.
- `standards#837` — "DEED conversion campaign", campaign step 4: *"flip ... RSR gates from `.a2ml`
  presence to `.deed` presence alongside". Gate predicates, not document contents.
- `deed-ecosystem/README.adoc`: *"The DEED format name and `.deed` extension are final, not A2ML."*

## Deliberately not done

- No `.a2ml` file is translated or renamed. #837 makes classification into the four DEED forms and
  per-family mapping specs a prerequisite for mass translation; that is not this PR.
- No gate that *reads* a retained file is touched (`CLAIMS.a2ml`, `.machine_readable/Debtfile.a2ml`,
  `contractiles/INDEX.a2ml`); rewriting those would fail gates that currently pass.
- No job-id or shell-var renames (`a2ml-validate`, `A2ML_COUNT`): they are referenced from `needs:`
  and `${{ needs.*.outputs }}`. The Checks-UI label is updated, as it has no references.

_Estate-wide `.deed` gate convergence, 2026-09-21. Script: `estate-audit/engine/deed_gate_migration.py`._

body: ## Root Cause The `auth whoami` command in `src/commands/auth/whoami.ts` silently swallows `setUserInfo` failures in a `catch {}` block with no logging. While the cache update is non-essential (the user identity was already fetched from the API), the complete absence of logging masks database issues like permission problems, read-only filesystems, or corruption that may affect other commands. ## Reproduction Path Run `sentry auth whoami` when the CLI's SQLite database is in a bad state (read-only, corrupted, or locked). The command succeeds but the cache write failure is completely invisible — no log, no warning, no diagnostic output even with `--verbose`. ## Fix Replace the empty `catch {}` block with `catch (error) { log.debug(...) }` using the existing module-level `log = logger.withTag('auth.whoami')`. Remove the `biome-ignore lint/plugin: grandfathered silent catch` suppression comment.

author: fainta7x
jonattanva
body:
BP-5 llegó a `fix/use-client-banner` por #105, pero esa rama ya había entrado en main por #103, así que el commit quedó fuera. Esto es el mismo arreglo sobre main.

## Qué cambia

`logger` es como la librería avisa a quien escribió el formulario de lo que tiene que corregir: una expresión de validación que no compila, un nombre de campo que alcanza un prototipo y no se envía, el error que lanzó una acción. Escribe fuera de producción, y en el build publicado esa pregunta ya venía contestada -- siempre con "producción" -- así que nada de eso llegaba nunca a una consola. Tampoco en un build de desarrollo de la aplicación.

Lo contestaba el minificado: esbuild define `process.env.NODE_ENV` como `"production"` mientras minifica para la plataforma por defecto, de modo que la comprobación se plegaba dentro de la librería en vez de quedar para el bundler de quien la instala. `define` devuelve la expresión, y el build se niega a publicar una salida que lleve `[Luna Form]` y haya contestado la pregunta por su cuenta.

`logger` pregunta además si hay un `process` que leer. La expresión ahora la resuelve la aplicación, y donde nada la resuelva -- un navegador sin bundler -- leerla lanzaría, y cambiaríamos un aviso ausente por un `ReferenceError` en mitad de validar.

## Verificación

Sin el `define`, el build sale 1 y nombra las seis salidas que resolvieron la expresión: `config`, `schema` y `client`, en ESM y CJS. Con él sale 0. La entrada del servidor no usa `logger`, así que no aparece.

`typescript`, `lint`, 803 unit y 1773 e2e en los tres navegadores.

## Corrección respecto a #105

#105 traía además un caso e2e que afirmaba que el aviso llega a la consola en un build de producción. Es lo contrario del contrato: en producción `logger` debe callar, y en `next start` calla. Ese caso no va aquí. La comprobación de build es el guardián, y tiene la forma del defecto que guarda -- lee la salida publicada y falla cuando la librería contesta por su cuenta. Probar la otra mitad de punta a punta exigiría una aplicación construida en modo desarrollo, y el arnés e2e corre producción a propósito, porque los presupuestos de render solo significan algo contra uno.

author: trevorotts1
body:
## Why

The persona selector was dying at the Command Center's spawn budget, so `--blend` never landed and content tasks stalled behind it.

cProfile on a live client box, `23-ai-workforce-blueprint/scripts/persona-selector-v2.py --blend`:

| run | wall clock | inside `llm_score._post_chat` |
|---|---|---|
| profiled | 46.6s | 43.7s (94%) |
| second | 206s | — |
| third | 258s | — |

Twenty-two sequential HTTPS chat calls: four per finalist, one per scoring layer, taken one at a time. The work was never CPU-bound, it was a queue of network waits.

## What changed

- **`23-ai-workforce-blueprint/scripts/persona-selector-v2.py`** — the Stage-D list comprehension becomes `score_personas()`, which maps `score_persona` over the finalists on a `ThreadPoolExecutor`. `executor.map` yields in INPUT order, not completion order, so the returned list is element-for-element what the comprehension produced and variety sampling, the perspective and craft bonus passes, and the tie-breaks are untouched. `PERSONA_SCORE_WORKERS` sets the width (default 6, capped at the finalist count). `PERSONA_SCORE_WORKERS=1` takes a literal sequential path that creates no thread at all.
- **`shared-utils/semantic_task_fit.py`** — the task-embedding cache is locked behind one new `_task_embed()`, used by both `semantic_task_fit()` and `semantic_persona_ids()`. Unlocked, every worker would miss the cache at the same instant and fire its own Gemini embed call, turning the G13 "one embed per selection" contract into one embed per finalist. The lock also removes a race in which `_task_cache_get`'s `move_to_end` could hit a key an eviction had just popped.
- **`shared-utils/llm_score.py`** — `_secret_helper()` sets its `_SECRET_HELPER_TRIED` latch only after `_SECRET_HELPER` holds its final value. Setting it first left a window where a second thread saw the latch with the module still `None` and silently degraded to exact-name-only credential resolution, so a key stored under an alias would not have resolved for that call.
- The PRES-053 vendored copies under `.../persona_service/resources/` are re-vendored, staying byte-identical to their canonicals as `docs/LEGACY-RETIREMENT.md` requires, so the presentation department gets the same fix.

## Thread-safety audit of the per-persona path

| shared state | verdict |
|---|---|
| `apply_weight_overrides` (`persona-selector-v2.py:1670`) | read-only, own per-call sqlite connection, `sqlite3.Error` swallowed — safe |
| `llm_score` score cache (`_cache_get` / `_cache_put`) | connection opened and closed per call, never shared, `sqlite3.Error` swallowed — safe |
| `llm_score._post_chat` | builds its own `urllib` request per call — safe |
| `_COMPANY_CONFIG_CACHE` (`persona-selector-v2.py:1764`) | keyed by the one config path every thread in a selection shares; worst race is a duplicate file read — safe |
| `semantic_task_fit._TASK_EMBED_CACHE` | **needed a lock** — fixed here |
| `llm_score._SECRET_HELPER` | **latch window** — fixed here |
| `semantic_task_fit._try_import_genai` | sets its global only after the import resolves; a racing thread redoes a `sys.modules`-cached import — safe as written |
| `_persona_embedding_from_index` | read-only, own per-call connection — safe |
| `match-score-log.jsonl` append | belongs to `persona_blend.py`, not on the `score_persona` path at all |

`score_persona` writes nothing.

## Why `decompose-task.py` is NOT parallelised

Its sub-task loop is ordering-dependent by design, and its own comment says so: each sub-task's `record_selection` write is what the NEXT sub-task's variety penalty and sticky-assignment read. Running the five sub-tasks concurrently would have every one of them read a database missing its predecessors' picks, so the whole decomposition could converge on a single persona. That is a behaviour change, not a speed-up. Concurrent writes to the dashboard DB would also contend, and those writes are best-effort-guarded, so losing them would silently break stickiness.

## Tests

New: `tests/unit/stage-d-parallel-scoring.test.py`, five hermetic cases (no DB, no network).

- input order survives when the LAST persona is made the FASTEST
- six personas each blocking 0.2s finish inside 0.6s with six workers
- `PERSONA_SCORE_WORKERS=1` runs on the calling thread
- an empty list and a single-persona list never ask for a pool
- `scoring_mode` reaches the scorer on both paths, and a raised exception still reaches the caller

Fail-first proven: re-pointed at the pre-fix comprehension, the timing case fails at 1.19s against the 0.6s bound.

Pre-existing suites re-run green: `semantic-task-fit-lru` 8/8, `semantic-task-fit-failure-cache` 17/17, `persona-fallback-invariant` 8/8, `persona-grounding-health-probe` 21/21, `shared-utils/test_f25_llm_score_secrets.py` 31/31. `python3 -m py_compile` clean on all six edited Python files.

`tests/unit/dep6-craft-slot-coverage.test.py` reports 20 passed / 1 failed (persona count triad expects 83, repo has 99). Pre-existing and unrelated: a pristine `origin/main` worktree gives the identical 20/1.

## Version

v25.1.52 → v25.1.53 via `./scripts/bump-version.sh`; `--check` reports all 10 version markers agree. CHANGELOG entries in the root and in `23-ai-workforce-blueprint/`.

author: molayodecker
body:
## Summary
- Return the persisted booking lifecycle status from Direct Paystack verification instead of hard-coding `pending`.
- Capture the status under the same booking row lock used to settle the payment.
- Preserve the real status on idempotent verification retries after a booking has advanced.
- Add regression coverage for both the first verification and an already-paid retry.

## Why
A booking can legitimately advance to `confirmed`, `scheduled`, or another lifecycle state while payment verification is retried. The API currently reports `status: "pending"` regardless of the database state, which can push the mobile client back into stale UI/state handling.

## Validation
- Added focused regression coverage in `DirectPaymentsTest`.
- CI should run formatting, warnings-as-errors compilation, and the full test suite on this PR.

## Follow-up review
I also started tracing cancellation-vs-late-payment races separately because that path can affect money state and deserves its own isolated fix if confirmed.

author: bluesxu
body:
国际服（繁中）上的三个问题，都来自 9/20～9/21 的运行日志。每个问题都附了日志证据，并有用真实处理函数写的测试。

## 1. 出击模式 BOSS 选择页卡 11～23 秒

`handle_boss_selection` 用 `请选择.*遇见的首领` 匹配标题，繁中服的标题是「請選擇在核心遭遇的BOSS。」（转简体后为「请选择在核心遭遇的BOSS。」），匹配不上。结果这页没有处理函数认领：

- `handle_confirm` 看到「確認」是灰色的，跳过；
- 画面静止 10 秒后，`handle_stuck_log` → `handle_unknown_page` 在屏幕中间随机点一下，碰巧点中 BOSS 卡后「確認」才亮。

9/21 出击模式日志里，这种「確認灰色 → 静止 10 秒 → `handle_unknown_page` 随机点击」出现了 9 次，每次约 11～23 秒，其中一次随机点了 9 下。

**改动**：正则同时认「遇见的首领」和「遭遇的BOSS」（不区分大小写）。两个 BOSS 名字的点击位置 (0.358, 0.706)、(0.641, 0.706) 已对照繁中服截图核对。

## 2. 休息区读不到生命值/信用点时判断出错

刚进入休息区时，左上角生命值和右上角信用点常常还没显示出来：

- **出击模式**：读不到生命值时按 100% 处理，所以低血量时也会闪光。9/21 的 44 次闪光里有 9 次是这样闪的，例如 19:28:36 闪了光，而 3 秒前读到的生命值只有 11%（235/2048）。读不到信用点时按 0 处理，所以满血也不闪光，例如 14:50:55 生命值 90%，连续 3 次读到信用点 0。
- **卡厄思模式**：休息和冥想都可选时，读不到生命值会选冥想，低血量时不回血。

这两个数字两三秒后通常就能读到。9/20 装加速补丁前后读不到生命值的比例差不多（20% 和 9%～13%），与加速补丁无关。

**改动**：新增 `_retry_rest_reading`，读不到时本帧先不做选择，返回 True 等下一帧重读。连续 3 帧仍读不到时按保守方式处理：出击模式把生命值当作 0%（选择休息），卡厄思模式选择休息。能读到时判断与原来完全相同。信用点可能真的是 0，这种情况多等 3 帧后照原逻辑继续。

## 3. 休息/闪光后每次白等 2 秒，且 `flash_or_rest` 没有复位

`_wait_for_rest_confirm` 用 `wait_ocr(match=re.compile("确认"))` 等确认按钮。`wait_ocr` 的结果不经过 `_simplify_texts`；框架的 `fix_texts` 只在**软件界面语言**为 zh_TW/zh_HK/zh_MO 时才自动繁转简。所以国际服游戏配简体界面时，OCR 结果是「確認」，永远匹配不上：

- 9/21 出击模式 83 次休息/闪光，83 次都打印了「等待休息确认按钮超时」，每次白等 2 秒；
- 超时后直接 `return True`，`node_status['flash_or_rest']` 没有复位。确认按钮其实就在等待区域内：随后由 `handle_center_confirm` 点击，位置 (0.570, 0.669)。

**改动**：同时匹配「确认」和「確認」。另一处直接调用 OCR 的 `utils_chaos.py:819` 只读数字，不受影响。

## 测试

新增 `tests/TestInternationalFixes.py`，共 10 个用例，直接调用真实的 `handle_boss_selection`、`handle_rest_sortie`、`handle_rest`、`_wait_for_rest_confirm`，只替换 OCR 文字、模板匹配和 `wait_ocr` 的结果：

- 繁中 BOSS 标题能选中 BOSS；国服标题照常；其他页面不处理；
- 「確認」「确认」都能等到；
- 出击休息区：读不到生命值时本帧不选，下一帧读到 12% 后选择休息；一直读不到时 3 帧后选择休息；读不到信用点时下一帧重读；能读到时判断不变；
- 卡厄思休息区：读不到生命值时 3 帧后选择休息；能读到时判断不变（25% 休息，92% 冥想）。

在未修改的代码上运行，6 个针对上述问题的用例失败，4 个「判断不变」的用例通过；修改后 10 个全部通过。`tests/TestMain.py` 通过。

与 #9（加速模式）、#10（「赋予灵光一闪」按钮）互相独立，可以分别合并。

## Description

Make the owned-element replacement contract explicit: an owner replaces its mounted element by returning a fresh node or supplying a `reactiveElement` accessor. Assigning `element` on an already mounted node remains unsupported.

Current Symbol, shape, and flow-control consumers already use the accessor path, so no additional renderer behavior is needed. Update the runtime guide, public type documentation, and renderer comments. Runtime behavior and type signatures do not change, but the rewritten `DOMNode` TSDoc is emitted into the published `@tachui/types` declarations, so the changeset is a patch on `@tachui/types`. `@tachui/core` gets no bump: its half is an inline comment the bundler strips.

Also fixes a flaky timing floor in `packages/primitives/__tests__/integration/error-recovery.test.ts`. The backoff assertion required at least 30ms against 10ms + 20ms of delays, so a timer firing 1ms early failed it (`expected 29 to be greater than or equal to 30`). The wall-clock check is replaced with a structural one: a pass-through `setTimeout` spy asserts the scheduled delays are exactly `[10, 20]`, so the exponential schedule is verified without depending on timer precision. Removing the multiplier fails it (`[10, 10]`).

author: dovacrii
body:
chore(git): dejar de versionar los auxiliares del WAL de SQLite

`services/api/aerobim.sqlite3-shm` y `-wal` estaban versionados por error, y aparecian como
modificados o borrados cada vez que alguien levantaba el servidor de desarrollo. Con eso
`git status` salia sucio en cada rama, y una copia de trabajo ajena entraba en cualquier commit
distraido.

**El motivo era un asterisco.** `.gitignore` tenia `*.sqlite3`, que coge la base pero no sus
acompanantes: en modo WAL, SQLite deja al lado un `-wal` con las escrituras aun no volcadas y un
`-shm` con la memoria compartida entre procesos, y el nombre **sigue** despues de la extension
—`aerobim.sqlite3-wal`—, asi que el patron no los alcanzaba. Ahora es `*.sqlite3*`, con el porque
escrito donde se lee.

Son archivos efimeros y de una sola maquina: SQLite los crea al abrir la base y los borra al
cerrarla limpiamente. No hay ninguna version de ellos que le sirva a nadie mas.

Comprobado creando los dos archivos a mano con el servidor levantado: `git status` no los menciona,
y `git check-ignore -v` senala la regla nueva para los tres.

author: janwelker
body:
## Description of the change

`templates/config.yaml`, the `nextcloud-config` volume in `deployment.yaml` and `cronjob.yaml`, and the `defaultConfigs` loop in `nextcloud.volumeMounts` were all gated on `nextcloud.configs` being non-empty. On a default install every enabled `nextcloud.defaultConfigs` entry was therefore ignored.

This PR adds one helper, `nextcloud.configs.enabled`, that is true when `nextcloud.configs` holds a file or any `defaultConfigs` entry is enabled, and uses it in all four places. The ConfigMap is still skipped entirely when both are empty.

Also: `Chart.yaml` bumped to 9.3.1, the outdated "Will be used only if you put extra configs" comment in `values.yaml` replaced, and README rows added for the two `defaultConfigs` entries that were undocumented (`helm-metrics.config.php`, `imaginary.config.php`).

## Benefits

- `nextcloud.openmetrics.allowedClients` works on its own. Its only consumer is `helm-metrics.config.php`, which never reached the pod unless an unrelated `nextcloud.configs` entry was set, so Nextcloud kept its built-in `127.0.0.1` and refused Prometheus with 403. The chart's own `metrics.enabled` + `prometheus.serviceMonitor.enabled` defaults produced a permanently down target for the same reason.
- The documented Imaginary setup (`nextcloud.defaultConfigs.imaginary.config.php: true`) works without the extra `nextcloud.configs` workaround (#761).
- `defaultConfigs` now means what the values file says it means.

## Possible drawbacks

- On upgrade, every install now gets the ConfigMap and a mount per enabled default. That is the same set of files that already mounted for anyone with `nextcloud.configs` set, but it is new for default installs, and the existing `nextcloud-config-hash` annotation restarts the pod once.
- Anyone who edited one of the image's config files in place on the PVC will see it shadowed by the chart copy. Setting that `defaultConfigs.<file>: false` restores the PVC file.
- The chart copies now shadow the image copies for everyone, so they need to track `nextcloud/docker`. Today they are identical except `s3.config.php`, which lacks the image's SSE-KMS block (`OBJECTSTORE_S3_SSE_KMS_ENABLED` / `OBJECTSTORE_S3_SSE_KMS_KEY_ID`). Happy to send that sync as a separate PR.

The all-enabled behaviour is intentional rather than mounting only the two chart-only files: the image entrypoint seeds `/var/www/html/config` from `/usr/src/nextcloud/config` only when the directory is empty ([docker-entrypoint.sh](https://github.com/nextcloud/docker/blob/master/docker-entrypoint.sh#L207-L211)), so mounting any single file into it on a fresh install would suppress the image defaults. Mounting all of them is the existing design for that case; this PR just applies it consistently.

## Applicable issues

- fixes #887
- fixes #761

## Additional information

Verified with `helm lint` and `helm template`:

- default values: ConfigMap renders with the 12 enabled defaults, 12 mounts in the app container, `helm-metrics.config.php` among them
- all `defaultConfigs` false and `configs: {}`: no ConfigMap, no volume, no mounts
- `defaultConfigs` all false with one `configs` entry: ConfigMap and mount for that entry only
- every file in `test-values/` renders; `imaginary.yaml` mounts `imaginary.config.php`
- `cron-cronjob.yaml`: the CronJob pod gets the volume too

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nextcloud/helm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests) doc.
- [x] DCO has been [signed off on the commit](https://docs.github.com/en/github/authenticating-to-github/signing-commits).
- [x] Chart version bumped in `Chart.yaml` according to [semver](http://semver.org/).
- [x] (optional) Parameters are documented in the README.md

author: kaan362
body:
## Problem and result

The industry citation report currently streams every GEO record and filters the selected sector in Python. This change stores a normalized, indexed `sector_key` and applies the sector predicate in PostgreSQL, so an e-commerce report retrieves only e-commerce GEO records before citation validation and ranking.

Depends on #68.

## Changes

- Add nullable, indexed `geo_records.sector_key` through an Alembic-autogenerated migration.
- Centralize spelling normalization; `ecommerce`, `e commerce`, and `e-commerce` map to `e-commerce` without semantic synonym inference.
- Derive the key whenever the ORM assigns or updates a GEO record's sector.
- Add a preview-by-default, repeatable backfill command for existing rows.
- Group the sector catalog by `sector_key` and add `WHERE geo_records.sector_key = :sector` to ranking retrieval.
- Keep the existing authenticated endpoints and ranking/evidence rules unchanged.

## Rollout

Run the schema migration before starting the updated application, then preview and apply the backfill while legacy GEO writers are stopped:

```bash
alembic upgrade head
python -m app.services.backfill_geo_sectors
python -m app.services.backfill_geo_sectors --apply
```

The reader uses `sector_key` directly, so existing rows must be backfilled before serving industry rankings.

## Validation

- Full backend suite: 1,274 passed, 22 environment-dependent skips
- PostgreSQL migration suite: 4 passed (upgrade, drift check, downgrade, seeded catalog)
- Ruff, mypy (141 application source files), and whitespace checks passed
- Local backfill: 178 rows updated; repeat preview reported zero
- E-commerce output stayed at 99 candidates, 30 eligible answers, 10 questions, 34 sites, and 36 pages
- PostgreSQL `EXPLAIN` confirmed `ix_geo_records_sector_key` is usable; the current 180-row table correctly prefers a sequential scan because it is cheaper

No API response schema or frontend change is included.

`php translator generate tr` surfaced 639 untranslated strings, all of which are now filled in:

### Not in this PR

Per the checklist in the PR template: the translations were drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by a native Turkish speaker before committing. Terminology decisions (`entry`, `asset`, `container`) and the capitalisation convention were made by hand, not by the model.

author: xvrh
body:
The MCP server never started on Windows, and the plan for the rest of Windows
support is written down.

## The MCP server

`.mcp.json` ran `sh tool/mcp_server.sh`. On Windows the client spawns servers
through `cmd.exe`, where `sh` is not on PATH, so the server never started —
`'sh' is not recognized`, in the client's own log — and every session there ran
with no flutterware tools.

The entry is now `fvm dart run flutterware mcp`: the same command `fw init`
writes into a user's project, with fvm naming the SDK, so this checkout
exercises the launch path users get. `cmd.exe` resolves `fvm.bat` by itself, so
one entry serves Windows, macOS and Linux, and `tool/mcp_server.sh` is deleted.

What the script did is either gone or documented. The client now waits 300s
rather than 30s, and `dart run` resolves a stale workspace on the way in. What
remains is fvm narrating an uncached SDK download onto stdout, so CLAUDE.md says
to run `fvm install` after the pin moves.

The launcher also looked for the built CLI at `bundle/bin/fw`, which on Windows
is `fw.exe`. Spawning worked anyway — Windows appends the suffix — so the only
symptom was a CLI rebuild on every single run.

Measured on Windows 11 with the pinned SDK, through the command the client runs:

| | |
|---|---|
| Connect, warm | **3.4s** (24.6s before the `fw.exe` fix, every time) |
| First connect after an edit under `app/` | 24.8s, rebuilding the CLI |
| stdout | JSON-RPC only; the launcher narrates to stderr |
| Client killed | children exit within ~4s, when the pipes close |

## The plan

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-windows-support-plan.md` records what works
and what breaks, measured rather than guessed: the root suite passes 1471 of
1486 tests, previews, scenarios and device discovery work, and `run/launch`
refuses outright. Most breakage is in one layer — anything that keeps a process
alive — plus relative paths used as names.

It also records four decisions with their evidence: state under
`%USERPROFILE%\.flutterware` (the 103-byte socket cap decides it), relative
paths that name things are POSIX, detached launch through a Dart shim (the
alternatives were measured and fail), and the embedder guest in scope with a
Windows native layer later.

## Not done here

`tool/prepare_submit.dart` loops forever on Windows — diagnosed in the plan,
fixed in the next change. The two Dart files here were formatted with the same
`dart_style` settings it uses, and neither moved.

body:
## Summary

Proposal only — **zero code changes**, per the Architect process. Adds a design doc: `docs/architecture/proposals/2026-09-21-retire-legacy-gateway-entrypoint.md`.

**Proposal:** Remove `gateway.py`, the "legacy" entry point that duplicates ~90% of `main.py`'s startup wiring with zero shared code, and consolidate on `main.py` as the single entry point.

**Why now:** `gateway.py` (180 lines) reimplements `main.py`'s (664 lines) provider/memory/skills/brain wiring, heartbeat loop, and restart-on-update dance line-for-line, but has none of `main.py`'s newer features (preflight checks, setup wizard, watch mode) and will keep drifting further out of sync. It's explicitly labeled "legacy" in three places (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `skills/self_inspect/tool.py`) and is unreferenced by any test, CI workflow, or Docker/systemd config — pure unexercised duplication.

**Risk:** low. No test/CI coverage means nothing automated can break; the only real risk is an external caller (a user's own cron/systemd unit) invoking `python gateway.py` directly, which the proposed migration's Stage 1 shim fully covers.

**Migration:** staged and backward-compatible — see the doc for the 3-stage plan (deprecation shim → strip duplicated bodies → delete + doc cleanup), each stage under a day.

⚠️ **Note:** this routine's standing brief includes "Repository-Specific Constraints" written for a FastAPI + MongoDB + React stack (fastapi-users, `/api/*` contracts, Mongo indexes, Zustand). None of that exists in this repo — Atlas is a single-process Python personal agent with no HTTP API or database. Those constraints don't apply here and appear to be a leftover from a different project's routine config; this proposal is written against Atlas's actual architecture per `CLAUDE.md` instead.

## Who should review

Repo owner (@cleanunicorn) — single-maintainer project.

## Test plan

- [ ] Confirm `tests/test_channels.py` already exercises `main.py`'s `_run_agent` path (not `gateway.py`'s)
- [ ] If approved: implement Stage 1 shim, smoke-test `uv run python main.py run --cli`/`--discord`/`--web` for parity
- [ ] If approved: Stage 2 — strip duplicated wiring bodies from `gateway.py`
- [ ] If approved: Stage 3 — delete `gateway.py`, update the 4 doc references

body:
## What
- feat: `MalwareForm` validates probabilities instead of clamping them
- feat: scenario-level DSL: `scenario`, `network`, `malware`,
  `startingNode`, `seed`, `maxIterations`
- refactor: `SimpleScenario` and `ExampleScenario` are now defined with the
  scenario DSL (same topologies, malware values, seeds and iteration
  counts; `Either[String, Scenario]` signatures unchanged for callers)

## Why
Scenarios can now be declared with the same DSL style as topologies, and
user-typed probabilities behave the same way in the DSL and the UI: an
out-of-range value is an error naming the field, not a silent clamp.
Values computed by the simulation rules still use Probability.clamped.

## Behaviour change
MalwareForm.toDomain returns Left for values outside [0,1] (including
NaN); the UI shows the message in the existing error dialog.

## Design notes
- `network` wraps the existing `topology` block, so its errors and the
  star/ring/mesh shapes carry over and accumulate with scenario errors.
- The starting node is resolved only when the network is valid, to avoid
  cascading "unknown node id" errors (`Left(Nil)` in ScenarioBuilder).
- An undeclared seed is drawn once at build time and stored in
  Scenario.seed, so runs stay reproducible.

author: hyperpolymath
body:
## Why

The guard in `dogfood-gate.yml` counted `.a2ml` files only:

```
COUNT=$(find . -name '*.a2ml' -not -path './.git/*' | wc -l)
```

so a repo whose manifest is written in the current grammar is reported as having none, and the
summary/compliance row is skipped by the same predicate (`if find . -name '*.a2ml' ... | grep -q .`).
The validator itself has scanned both grammars for a while -- the caller's predicate is the bug.

## Authority

- `rsr-template-repo/.github/workflows/deed-validate.yml` (the mint source) is what this wording is
  copied from, byte for byte, including `-type f`-free `find` and the dual-accept stance.
- `standards#837` — "DEED conversion campaign", campaign step 4: *"flip ... RSR gates from `.a2ml`
  presence to `.deed` presence alongside". Gate predicates, not document contents.
- `deed-ecosystem/README.adoc`: *"The DEED format name and `.deed` extension are final, not A2ML."*

## Deliberately not done

- No `.a2ml` file is translated or renamed. #837 makes classification into the four DEED forms and
  per-family mapping specs a prerequisite for mass translation; that is not this PR.
- No gate that *reads* a retained file is touched (`CLAIMS.a2ml`, `.machine_readable/Debtfile.a2ml`,
  `contractiles/INDEX.a2ml`); rewriting those would fail gates that currently pass.
- No job-id or shell-var renames (`a2ml-validate`, `A2ML_COUNT`): they are referenced from `needs:`
  and `${{ needs.*.outputs }}`. The Checks-UI label is updated, as it has no references.

author: ericmj
body:
`stream/2` and `recv/3` document `responses` in `{:error, conn, reason, responses}` as "a list of responses that were correctly parsed before the error", in the same order as the `{:ok, conn, responses}` list. `HTTP1.handle_data/2` and the two HTTP/2 catch clauses reversed the accumulator only on the success path, so on the error path the list came back newest first: `{:done, ref}` before `{:status, ref, 200}`.

A caller that walks the list in order, or takes `List.first/1` to find the status, gets the wrong answer, and only on the error path, which is the path least likely to be covered by a caller's tests.

Two tests, one per protocol: a chunked HTTP/1 response with a bad chunk size after the first chunk, and an HTTP/2 response followed by a GOAWAY. The existing `max_header_list_size` test in `test/mint/http1/conn_test.exs` and the WINDOW_UPDATE test in `test/mint/http2/conn_test.exs` asserted the reversed order and now assert parse order.

author: leonshimizu
body:
## Summary
- move Rack::Attack counters and Clerk JWKS caching off database-backed Solid Cache and into a bounded process-local memory store
- add a public, minimal `/health/dependencies` readiness endpoint that detects primary connectivity, read-only/recovery state, and stale Solid Queue workers without mutating data
- preserve `/up` as Render liveness so a dependency incident does not trigger a restart loop
- document the current single-Puma-process constraint and the Redis/Valkey requirement before horizontal scaling

## September 20 root cause
During the PostgreSQL read-only interval, ordinary GET requests such as `/api/v1/auth/me` still attempted writes through Rack::Attack because its counter store was `Rails.cache`. Production uses Solid Cache on PostgreSQL, so those defensive request-path writes raised `PG::ReadOnlySqlTransaction` and turned otherwise read-only traffic into 500 responses. Clerk JWKS reads shared the same database-backed cache dependency.

## Verification
- `bundle exec rspec` — 3,012 examples, 0 failures
- focused resilience coverage — 13 examples, 0 failures
- `bundle exec brakeman --no-pager` — 0 warnings
- `bundle exec bundler-audit check --update` — no vulnerabilities
- `bundle exec rails zeitwerk:check` — all good
- RuboCop on changed Ruby files — no offenses (the existing routes file still contains unrelated legacy spacing offenses)
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm test -- --run` — 159 tests passed
- `npm run build`

## Deployment notes
No migration or environment-variable change is required. After deploy, `/health/dependencies` should return `200 {"status":"ok"}` while `/up` remains the Render platform health check.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

- Hardened request paths during read-only PostgreSQL incidents by moving Rack::Attack counters and Clerk JWKS caching to a bounded, process-local `ActiveSupport::Cache::MemoryStore`.
- Added `GET /health/dependencies`, which returns `200 {"status":"ok"}` when database connectivity, writability, recovery state, and Solid Queue worker heartbeat checks pass. It returns `503 {"status":"degraded"}` otherwise and sets `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Kept `/up` as the Render liveness endpoint to avoid restart loops during dependency incidents.
- Disabled Rack::Attack in test environments and cleared process-local request-path cache state after each spec.
- Documented the single-Puma-process limitation. A shared Redis or Valkey store is required before horizontal web-tier scaling.
- No database migration or environment-variable changes are required.
