author: decksx
body:
Closes #26.

## What was missing

Not an evidence protocol — one already exists. `POST /controller/tasks/{id}/reconcile`
takes `integration_reconciled_landed` / `_absent` / `reconciliation_failed`, and
`states.py` already records why a reconciled landing reaches COMPLETE through its own
event rather than `integration_completed`: "the ledger distinguishes an integration
observed by the integrator from one reconstructed afterwards. They are not the same
evidence."

What was missing is **reachability**. `INTEGRATION_UNCERTAIN` was entered only from
`INTEGRATING` via `integration_outcome_unknown` (lease expiry). T-INGRESS-05 reached the
same uncertainty down the other road — `integration_rejected` → `CHANGES_REQUESTED` →
`budget_exhausted` → `NEEDS_HUMAN` — and `NEEDS_HUMAN` had no edge into reconciliation.
The task was closed `SUPERSEDED`, which loses that the work succeeded.

## What this adds

One event and two transitions:

```
("NEEDS_HUMAN",       "out_of_band_merge_reported") -> INTEGRATION_UNCERTAIN, ADMIN
("CHANGES_REQUESTED", "out_of_band_merge_reported") -> INTEGRATION_UNCERTAIN, ADMIN
```

ADMIN rather than OPERATOR: a worker able to report its own out-of-band merge could walk
unreviewed work into a state that exists to trust reports.

`POST /controller/tasks/{id}/out-of-band-merge` (admin-gated) records the report, and the
existing reconcile route still decides what landed. Landing stays one decision in one
place, however the task arrived at the question.

## What it checks, and what it cannot

Three checks, all answerable from the ledger alone:

- the task is in `NEEDS_HUMAN` or `CHANGES_REQUESTED`;
- the task carries an approval in its log — without this, a report is a way to launder
  unreviewed work into COMPLETE;
- the candidate reported, if one is named, is the commit the controller issued the
  approved review against.

`tasks.approved_candidate_sha` cannot answer the last two: `integration_rejected` is in
`engine.APPROVAL_CLEARING`, so the column is NULL on precisely the tasks this serves. The
approval is read from the event log and the candidate from the review activation, never
from the reporter — the property `engine._approved_candidate` is written around.

**The merge itself is not verified and cannot be.** Nothing in the controller has a
working copy. The event kind says `reported`, the payload carries `verified: false` and
the authenticated `reported_by`, and the task stops in `INTEGRATION_UNCERTAIN` rather than
advancing.

## The payload

```json
{
  "merge_sha": "ea27537…", "candidate_sha": "607c5a2…",
  "target_ref": "refs/heads/main", "merged_by": "…", "pull_request": 11,
  "merged_at": "2026-09-12T22:57:58Z", "reason": "…",
  "reported_by": "admin", "approval_seq": 210, "verified": false
}
```

Answers the issue's "how did this land?", and by `approval_seq` + `source_event_id`, what
it was allowed to land against.

## Notes for review

- `controller/reconciliation.py` is a new module rather than more of `api.py`, because
  `api.py` crossed `DEFAULT_FILE_VIEW` (52,300 > 50,000) and
  `test_a_module_a_task_writes_fits_in_one_file_view` says a module past the window is one
  the swarm cannot be given a task about. Split rather than raise the cap: the cap is paid
  by every prompt. api.py is 46,114 after.
- `ROUTED_ELSEWHERE` gains an entry, so the generic `/transition` route cannot apply the
  kind with none of the checks above. That widens
  `test_the_refused_set_is_exactly_the_escalation_exits`, whose docstring asks that
  widening be a decision rather than a drift — renamed and documented accordingly.
- `activations._SHA_RE` is now `activations.SHA_RE`; the route validates shas and a second
  copy of the pattern is a second chance to spell it differently.
- Each guard was mutation-tested. Removing the approval check makes only
  `test_a_report_against_an_unapproved_task_is_refused` fail, and it fails with an
  unreviewed task reaching `INTEGRATION_UNCERTAIN` on a 200 — not with a crash.

## Open question

Reporting from `NEEDS_HUMAN` leaves the escalation unanswered: no `operator_response`
event and no version bump, so attempts authorized before the escalation stay valid. A
required `reason` is recorded in the payload instead. Pairing it with the version advance
`/operator-response` makes would mean that route's `NEEDS_HUMAN`-only precondition, and
`CHANGES_REQUESTED` would still need this route — so the dedicated route handles both.
Worth arguing before it ships.

| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/ -k "not bypass"` | 1780 passed, 8 deselected |
| `pytest tests/ -k "bypass"` | 8 passed |

author: guimunhoz13
body:
## O que motivou

A dashboard abria com quatro contagens — clientes, processos, audiências e documentos — e nenhum número de dinheiro, embora contratos, parcelas, horas e despesas já estivessem no banco. Para saber quanto havia a receber era preciso abrir contrato por contrato.

## Backend

`_indicadores_financeiros()` alimenta um novo bloco `financeiro` em `/api/dashboard/stats/`:

| Indicador | O que soma |
|---|---|
| A receber | parcelas em aberto de todos os contratos |
| Recebido no mês | parcelas quitadas desde o dia 1º |
| Vencido | valor e quantidade de parcelas que passaram do vencimento |
| Horas faturáveis no mês | tempo apontado e valor correspondente |
| Despesas a reembolsar | adiantadas pelo escritório e ainda não cobradas |

Uma decisão que vale registrar: **o vencimento é comparado com a data de hoje na hora da consulta**. O status `"atrasado"` existe no model `Parcela` mas nada o atribui em lugar nenhum do sistema — confiar nele deixaria de fora toda parcela vencida. Há um teste cobrindo exatamente isso.

## Frontend

- `FinanceiroSection` renderiza os cinco indicadores logo abaixo dos cartões de contagem. O cartão de vencido fica em vermelho quando há parcela atrasada e diz quantas são.
- `formatarMoeda` e `formatarHoras` saíram de `relatorio.js` para `utils/formato.js`, agora compartilhados entre o relatório impresso e a dashboard. Aceitam tanto o texto que os serializers mandam quanto os números dos agregados.

## Limitação conhecida

"Horas faturáveis no mês" mostra o que foi **apontado**, não o que falta **cobrar**: `ApontamentoHora` não tem marcação de hora já faturada. Adicionar esse campo seria uma mudança de modelo à parte — deixei de fora para não ampliar este PR.

## Validação

- Backend: 222 testes, incluindo 9 novos em `IndicadoresFinanceirosAPITestCase` (isolamento entre escritórios incluído).
- Frontend: 88 testes, incluindo 8 novos para as formatações. `npm run build` limpo.
- Conferido no navegador em dois estados: sem parcela vencida e com uma parcela atrasada, para ver o cartão de alerta.

body:
## Scope

Behavior-level test coverage for the GNN bridge's verify-document surface plus the adjacent untested `bridge status` fail-closed branches. Tests only — no changes to `src/`, so the W2 source-custody seal (owner bytes on `src/fep_lean/**/*.py`) and the W1 syntax-pin JSONs are untouched (custody discipline respected).

## Why

`bridge verify-document` had 2 tests total (1 error branch + 2 sibling-gated happy-path tests that skip in CI's python lane and in fresh worktrees). Coverage of the verify-document surface on the recorded gate (`pytest --cov -m "not serial_lean"`, no sibling GNN checkout, no lake build):

- `src/fep_lean/bridge/operations.py`: **57% -> 94%** (`_probe_sections` 369-453, `_probe_lean_code` 458-459, and the whole `verify_document` body 493-559 were unexecuted)
- `src/fep_lean/bridge/cli.py`: **79% -> 87%** (the verify-document arm 105-115 was untested)

## What is covered

`tests/test_bridge_verify_document.py` (+488 lines):

- **Synthetic GNN checkout fixture** (`gnn_stub`): a minimal stdlib stand-in for `gnn.extract.pomdp_extractor` / `gnn.schema` written into `tmp_path` — mirrors the existing `pair` fixture philosophy ("no installed sibling required") for the extraction seam `verify_document` binds at runtime. `sys.modules` caches are restored around each test so sibling-backed tests keep working.
- Orchestration branches: missing document file (`FileNotFoundError` before any verification, no receipt written), non-POMDP document (`ValueError`), skip-without-lean-workspace (status `skipped` deterministically, recorded as warning, receipt written, document sha + families in payload), family mismatch (warning recorded, skip still dominates status), matching family (no mismatch warning), `--fail-on-warnings` (warning escalates to status `failed`).
- Probe-construction contract (pure, no Lean): `_lean_escape`, `_lean_number` (bool-before-int ordering guard), `_lean_payload` (scalar/row/map/nested), `_probe_sections` (frozen 13-kind inventory: identifier sanitization + fallbacks, directed/undirected edges, `.lit`/`.ref` dims, `.floatT`/`.intT`/`.boolT`, sorted parameterization, optional sections omitted, declared-variables precedence, footer), `_probe_lean_code` (import + `GnnDocument` + `documentWellFormed ... := by decide` with every section embedded).
- CLI level (`cli.run` end to end): missing `--document` (error JSON, exit 1), missing file (error JSON, no receipt), skipped verification is fail-closed (exit 1, never 0), `--fail-on-warnings` produces status `failed` + exit 1.
- Extended the existing emission-flags rejection test with `verify-document` (it was the only bridge operation missing from that parametrize).

`tests/test_gnn_bridge_operations.py` (+42 lines) — `bridge status` fail-closed branches:

- Un-pinned syntax surface: drift on either pinned syntax file fails `checks.syntax_surface` and `status` (no re-pinning write).

## Known remaining gaps (deliberate)

- `operations.py` 541-544 (status `ok` from a real compile and `failed` from a real compile error) require an actual `lake env lean` probe run. The `ok` path is covered by the existing sibling-gated `test_verify_document_well_formed` on machines with lake + GNN checkout; a compile-failure test would need to deliberately construct an ill-formed probe, which cannot be done reliably through the public document interface. No full Lean build was performed locally (this worktree has no `lean/.lake`); per the brief, real-Lean tests stay skipif-gated rather than building inline.

author: henrrrik
body:
Follow-up to the architecture review (finding #9).

The POI-drift guard, ambiguity auto-resolution, `exact_match_shadowed` warnings and deviation enrichment ran on only one of three code paths:

- **`verbose=true`** returned from `fetchVerboseTrips` before any guard ran. The review reproduced the `TestTripsTool_SilentPOIResolutionRejected` fixture ("Järfälla kyrka" → go-kart track) returning journeys with no error under `verbose=true`, while the README promises the tool "refuses rather than silently planning from the wrong place".
- **The ambiguity-retry body** was never re-checked. The first body carries no journeys whenever ambiguity is flagged, so `rejectPoiResolutionIfNeeded` at the top of the flow was a no-op exactly when auto-resolution happened — a retry ending at a POI destination succeeded.
- **A retry that itself came back `-8011`** was passed through as raw `systemMessages`, dropping the collected warnings.

Changes:
- `TripsTool` runs one guard chain (`fetchTripsWithAmbiguityResolution`) and only then branches on `verbose`. The verbose shape gets `resolved` **and** `warnings` injected at top level (`injectVerboseExtras`).
- The retried body goes through `rejectPoiResolutionIfNeeded`; a still-ambiguous retry returns the structured picker with the candidates already fetched.
- `resolveAmbiguity` restructured around a small `ambiguousSide` type: gocyclo 16 → under the limit. `TripsTool` split into `buildTripsParams` / `verboseTripsResult` / `trimmedTripsResult`: 12 → under.
- Per-leg deviation enrichment stays trimmed-shape only; `verbose` and `skip_deviations` descriptions and the README now say so.

Four new tests, one per scenario above. All existing trips tests pass unchanged.

author: jclaveau
body:
Firefox profiles from `browser-perf-record.yml` (run 35604039153) name nothing: libxul.so is stripped in `bundle-dist.sh` and there is no unstripped twin, so 95% of a layout kernel's samples are `[.] 0x...`. WebKit got its names from the pre-strip dist served through a symfs (`symbols_image` / `symbols_path`, geometry-guarded since #282).

- `bundle-dist.sh`: copy `libxul.so` to `<work>/firefox-symbols/` before the strip loop.
- `Dockerfile` + `Dockerfile.iter` artifact stages: `COPY /work/firefox-symbols /symbols`. `Dockerfile.alpine` and the conformance runner COPY `/firefox` only, so the shipped images are byte-identical.

Cost: ~200 MB more in the `sha-<sha>` artifact image (never pulled by consumers). The scripts are content-addressed into the prebuilt base, so the push to main is a cold firefox rebuild (~5–6 h) followed by promote.

Then: `browser-perf-record.yml -f browser=firefox -f symbols_image=ghcr.io/jclaveau/playwright-alpine-browsers:sha-<merge sha> -f symbols_path=/symbols` against a consumer republished from that build.

TinyAGI ships meaningful first-party multi-agent infrastructure: transactional queue/retry/dead-letter/stale recovery, per-agent serialization, isolated workspaces, validated team handoffs/chat rooms, schedules/heartbeat, persistent memory indexing, APIs and TinyOffice management.

author: seofood
body:
Microphone capture used to wait for accessibility inspection, workflow lookup, dictionary loading and provider preparation. Speaking immediately after the shortcut could therefore lose the beginning of a recording. Capture now starts first, with recording feedback and timing published immediately; a bounded handoff preserves streaming audio until the provider exists and delivers it in order. Startup failures discard the unfinished capture, while a streaming-buffer overflow falls back to the complete recording.

Validation: 1,281 presentation tests, 274 portable-host tests and two immediate-capture tests passed. Opt-in integration comparisons passed with cold-loaded Whisper Large V3 Turbo and live Soniox: all 70,881 samples were retained. A simulated 300 ms late-start control lost exactly 4,800 samples, even though both models reconstructed the first word for this sentence. The development host builds and runs; Marco confirmed speaking immediately after the shortcut with both local Whisper and Soniox.

The opt-in test setup and manual checks are documented in docs/testing/immediate-capture.md. They distinguish deterministic capture-adapter tests from the real microphone/shortcut check.

### Before / after comparison

The before case deliberately simulates a **300 ms delay before microphone capture**. It is not a measured baseline of the old application's startup latency. Both cases use the same German test audio, with leading silence removed.

| Check | Before: simulated late capture | After: immediate capture + buffering |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retained audio at 16 kHz | 66,081 samples (4.130 s) | 70,881 samples (4.430 s) |
| Missing beginning | 4,800 samples / 300 ms | 0 samples / 0 ms |
| Local Whisper Large V3 Turbo | Reconstructed the complete sentence despite missing audio | Complete sentence; weights loaded after capture began |
| Soniox cloud | Reconstructed the sentence, with a comma after “Morgen” | Complete sentence; prefix retained before stream creation and during delayed connection |
| First word, “Morgen” | Reconstructed by both models for this particular sentence | Present in the captured audio and both transcripts |
| Manual immediate-speaking test | No measured manual baseline claimed | Confirmed by Marco with local Whisper and Soniox |

The transcript alone can conceal clipped audio. Sample-by-sample preservation is therefore the primary regression check; model accuracy is not claimed to have improved from this single sentence.

Settings reference (existing screenshot; this change does not alter the settings UI):
![Development settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TypeWhisper/typewhisper-win/seofood/immediate-dictation-capture/docs/screenshots/discover-without-breadcrumbs.png)

author: pierorios2000
body:
## What
The owner wanted everything consolidated so nothing is started in parts. A single container would be a worse image (Postgres, S3, Superset and the catalog are different processes; OpenMetadata alone is five containers), so this is **one Compose project and one command** (ADR 0032):
- The root `docker-compose.yml` `include`s `bi/docker-compose.yml` and `openmetadata/docker-compose.yml`; their services sit behind the `bi` and `catalog` profiles. One group in Docker Desktop, one network.
- `make up` = storage + Postgres + Superset; `make up-catalog` adds OpenMetadata; `make status` lists what runs and the URLs; `make down` stops everything **keeping the data**; `make poc-down` deletes the data as before.
- No more external-network trick: Superset's setup and the OpenMetadata connector reach Postgres as `postgres:5432` in the same project (`bi-init` waits for Postgres to be healthy).
- The project name stays `pfp-poc`, so an existing install keeps its lake and Postgres volumes. `make up` stops the old `pfp-bi` / `pfp-om` projects first (their ports would clash). CI and `make poc-up` are unchanged (they name `seaweedfs postgres`).
- Every `docker compose` call in the Makefile goes through `$(PFP)` (one place names the project); a test enforces it.
- OpenMetadata's Postgres volume is renamed `om-postgres-data` (it clashed with PFP's `postgres-data`). Included files cannot use required-variable interpolation, so `make bi-check` verifies the `PFP_BI_*` variables.

## Verification
- Static tests, red first (8): includes, profiles, one network, no duplicate service/volume names, no required variables in included files, `bi-init` waits for Postgres, no hardcoded project.
- Live, on a throwaway project `pfp-t46` with its own ports: `make up` -> storage + Postgres + Superset healthy; `make up-catalog` -> OpenMetadata healthy, the native Postgres connector ingested with **0 errors** and the lineage check passes; `make down` kept the data and a second `make up` found it (3 reconciliation rows); `make om-down` removed only the catalog and its volumes.
- `make ci-local` PASS.

## Incident (my mistake) and its fix
While verifying, I ran `make poc-down PFP_PROJECT=pfp-t46`; that target still hardcoded `-p pfp-poc`, so it ran `down -v` on the **owner's real stack** and deleted the lake and Postgres volumes. Nothing original was lost: the 83 archived PDFs and the manual Excel were untouched. I rebuilt it the documented way (PDFs back to the inbox, `pfp ingest`: 83 archived, 0 duplicates, 0 needing review; `import-manual`; `dbt build` 166/166; Superset re-imported) and the per-account movement counts are **identical** to before, reconciliation 8 accounts / 0 differences. What was not restorable: Superset's own metadata (users, anything made by hand in its UI) and Elementary's baselines.
The fix in this PR: every target now uses `$(PFP)`, so `PFP_PROJECT=...` really redirects `poc-down`; a test fails if a literal project name comes back.

## Notes
- After merging: `make down` is not needed for an existing install; run `make up` (it stops the old `pfp-bi`/`pfp-om` projects, keeps your data).
- Dagster stays a host process (`uv run dagster dev`).

author: gokay-ai
body:
Fixes #154834

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a subagent whose completion delivery already failed and finished cleanup is still injected into every later parent turn under `## Child results awaiting delivery`.

## User Impact

User impact: exhausted failed child deliveries stop burning tokens and pretending they are still owed. Retryable failed deliveries (cleanup not finished) still appear until the owner retries or gives up.

## Why This Change Was Made

`finalizeResumedAnnounceGiveUp` writes `delivery.status="failed"` and completes cleanup with no remaining requester wake. Resume then returns early, so nothing advances the row. `hasOutstandingCompletion` still treated `failed` as outstanding, so the same dead entry was re-rendered on every LLM boundary, including after gateway restarts.

This change excludes failed deliveries with completed cleanup from awaiting-delivery context. It does not drop all `failed` statuses (retryable rows stay visible), does not rewrite persisted disposition, and does not touch closed-wake recurrence (#151771) or successful artifact reconcile (#153550).

## Evidence

Owner tests: `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-active-context.test.ts` — 16 passed.

Named regressions:

- failed + `cleanupHandled` + no wake must not render awaiting-delivery
- failed without completed cleanup still renders awaiting-delivery

Red/green: the exhausted-failed case failed on the pre-fix predicate (`expected undefined`, received `## Child results awaiting delivery`) and passed after the owner change.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-active-context.test.ts
```

Also passed: `pnpm format:check` and oxlint on the two changed files, `git diff --check`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`.

Deslop: no extra comments, shims, or type-laundering in the diff.

## Summary

Fixes the reported issue on `https://smart1.agency/suite/` where the page "keeps reloading" / flickers.

- `modules/suite_panel/public/index.html` hard-coded `<script defer src="/hub-help.js">` and `<script defer src="/hub-demo.js">` right before `</body>`.
- `/suite/` is mounted through `DispatcherMiddleware` in `wsgi.py`, and `HubBar` already injects those same two scripts (plus the rest of the shared bundle) into every mounted module page automatically, right before the page's closing `</body>`.
- Net effect: both scripts ran **twice** on every load of `/suite/` — two independent `DOMContentLoaded` handlers each fetching `/api/help` and `/api/demos`, and two sets of `window` resize/scroll listeners for the help-bubble and tour-ring widgets, both acting on the same DOM. That double init is what read on screen as the page flickering/re-rendering.
- `modules/pdf_optimizer/static/index.html` had the identical hard-coded tags with the same dispatcher-mount exposure, so it carried the same latent bug — fixed alongside.

author: gittem
body:
## What

Wave 4 composition-root work from the compliance review: findings **#4** (creating screen models during view update; no eviction) and **#5** (the `dashboardModel` IUO + `fatalError` create path). Two commits:

1. `refactor: own screen-model lifecycle at the composition root`
2. `docs: document screen-model ownership at the composition root`

## Why

- **#4:** destinations called mutating accessors (`container.cardDetailModel(cardID:)`, …) *during body evaluation*, and every model built lived until the container deinited — so a popped screen's live subscription tasks leaked. `AppContainer.prepareScreenModels(for:)` now materializes one model per route outside the body path (from `MainNavigationView`'s `.onChange(of: router.routes, initial: true)`) and evicts the models whose route has left the stack. Destinations are pure, non-mutating lookups with a non-crashing loading fallback. Eviction is real: the models cancel their subscription tasks in a non-isolated box `deinit`, so the tasks end with the screen. `resetDemo()` evicts through the same single path.
- **#5:** `dashboardModel` was an implicitly-unwrapped optional stored alongside `dependencies`, and the accessors `fatalError`ed when no graph existed. It is now a computed `DashboardModel?` derived from `dependencies` (no separate copy to drift), and all three `fatalError` paths are gone.

Docs updated: `architecture.md` §9.1 / §11.2 / §11.3 / §13 Step 8.

author: rpgmem
body:
PR 3 of #1368 — **the repair**. #1377 delivered the queue; this writes.

The check digit says a number is wrong and never what the right one is, so the corrected value arrives from HR and this is what stores it.

## What one confirmation does

`IdentityRepair::repair( $subject_hash, $new_rf )` rewrites the ciphertext and the hash across every store carrying the old value, repoints the identity index and grants the owning account the certificate capabilities — **inside one transaction**, because the index and the rows disagreeing is worse than not repairing at all: every later read would resolve the account to a value its own rows do not carry.

| store | `rf_encrypted` | `rf_hash` |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| `ffc_submissions` | ✔ | plain index |
| `ffc_self_scheduling_appointments` | ✔ | plain index |
| `ffc_recruitment_candidate` | ✔ | **`UNIQUE KEY uq_rf_hash`** |
| `ffc_user_profiles` | — | the identity index, hash only |

The two `rf_normalized` columns are **not** repair targets: both live in `*_import_staging`, which is a scratch buffer per import job.

## Three refusals, each protecting something no later check can

**A value failing the check digit.** Otherwise the screen becomes a way to store a second wrong number.

**A finding naming two accounts.** A finding is a *hash*, and two people can mistype into the same wrong number — writing one confirmed value across both puts one person's RF on the other's row, **silently**, because both then hold a value whose check digit is fine. Nothing downstream can tell them apart afterwards. (Chosen over per-row selection: that makes the confirmation a set of ids to eyeball, and a mis-tick fails the same silent way.)

**A corrected value that already exists.** That is a merge, not a typo fix. `ffc_recruitment_candidate` declares `UNIQUE` on the hash, so *there* the database would refuse it anyway — as a duplicate-key error that says nothing an operator can act on — while the other two stores would accept it in silence. Refusing here makes both cases the same legible answer.

Plus idempotence: a finding somebody else already repaired resolves to nothing, which is a result rather than a failure.

## Four decisions worth not re-deriving

**Re-evaluated at write time.** The form posts the subject hash and the value — never the row ids the screen rendered. Between listing a finding and confirming it the operator went and asked a person, and rows may have arrived or left. A test pins that no row ids are passed.

**The pair comes from `SensitiveFieldRegistry::encrypt_fields()`**, the same policy source the forward path uses, so a repair produces the pair a submission would. Re-implementing `encrypt()` + `hash()` here would be a second policy that agrees today and drifts later.

**Overwriting the index is the decision.** `UserCreator::feed_identity_index()` never overwrites a populated column, deliberately. Reusing that rule unexamined would make this write silently do nothing in exactly the case it exists for — the operator has decided *against* the value the index holds (#1368).

**The outcome travels in a per-user transient, not a query argument.** The audit card next door passes its message as one; prose in a URL is a message anybody can choose to show an administrator. It also removed a duplicated message map — the service is now the single owner of the wording, so the two cannot drift.

**Capabilities move with what becomes readable** — `ffc_grant_certificate_capabilities`, the action #1367 introduced, so no `Maintenance → UserDashboard` edge is created. `ModuleBoundaryTest` is green with no baseline change.

## Evidence

- **Full suite: 8,446 tests / 65,462 assertions green**, on the rebased branch. Required here — the change is in `includes/`.
- PHPStan 2.2.14 (level 8) and PHPCS clean over `includes/` and `tests/`.
- **11 mutations, each fails a test**: every refusal removed; both rollbacks flipped to `COMMIT`; the ciphertext dropped from the write; the `UPDATE` keyed on the new hash instead of the old; a direct `$wpdb` write on the page; the nonce check removed; the capability gate removed.
- **One of those mutations found a real gap**: flipping the store-failure `ROLLBACK` to `COMMIT` left the suite green, so a half-written repair — some stores on the new value, the rest on the old — could have shipped. `test_a_store_refusal_rolls_back` closes it.

## One correction carried in this PR

`test_the_screen_performs_no_write()` from #1377 asserted the screen is read-only. That stopped being true the moment the repair landed, and **a test whose premise is false still passes**. It is replaced by `test_the_screen_never_writes_directly()`: the screen does write now, but every write goes through `IdentityRepair`, which owns the transaction and the refusals. It matches call shapes (`$wpdb->`, `global $wpdb`) rather than the bare token, because this class's own docblock explains the query seam and says `$wpdb` doing it.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking)
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation only

## Test plan

- [x] Full suite green, run with no arguments
- [x] PHPStan level 8 + `Row shapes` (level 9) clean
- [x] PHPCS on `includes/`, `phpcs-tests.xml.dist` on `tests/`
- [x] 16 new source strings across `.po` / `.pot` / `.mo` / `.l10n.php`; one string PR 2 left saying correction "is not offered here yet" was rewritten and its orphaned catalogue entry removed
- [x] `identity_rf_repaired` has a label and a category — `ActivityLogActionLabelsTest` caught its absence
- [ ] **Manual smoke on testes** — not yet run; this is a destructive write and deserves one real repair before it is used in anger

## What this does not do

Split and merge (the other two populations in #1368) are not here. Neither is the `438` / `5537` question the issue leaves open.

author: dotimothy
body:
## Summary

`sima-neat/core`'s Vulcan Docs build fails on every push, because `autodoc`
validates this repository's translations when it pulls our docs:

```text
[autodoc] [sentinel] FAILED: ko translation is stale: docs/panels/thermal.md;
ko translation is stale: docs/run-comparison.md
[autodoc] summary: 4 ok, 0 skipped, 2 localization failures
```

The translations are **not** stale. Two commits updated the English page and all
four localized copies together:

```text
b1105c5  Read Modalix temperatures through kernel hwmon instead of direct MMIO
  docs/panels/thermal.md            docs/i18n/{ja,ko,uk,zh-Hant}/panels/thermal.md

3e7db50  Append recording samples and keep live views independent of history
  docs/run-comparison.md            docs/i18n/{ja,ko,uk,zh-Hant}/run-comparison.md
```

Neither updated `docs/i18n/translation-sources.json`, so the recorded hash still
describes the prior English. The ledger was reporting a real inconsistency —
between the sources and its own record, not between English and the
translations.

Confirmed before changing anything: the ko thermal page carries the hwmon
wording introduced by `b1105c5` (`simaai_modalix_thermal_sensor`,
`temp1_input`…), so the content is current and only the bookkeeping was missing.

This records the current hashes for two sources across `ja`, `ko`, `uk` and
`zh-Hant` — eight entries, one file changed. No prose changes, and no
translation regenerated.

## Verification

```text
before:  8 entries stale
after:   0 stale or unrecorded entries
sima-i18n check:  24 findings -> 16
```

The 16 remaining are pre-existing structural drift (inline code spans, heading
levels, protected content between headings) unrelated to this fix and untouched
by it; `autodoc` checks only staleness and missing records, so they do not
affect the docs build.

## Note

The companion failure in `sima-neat/llima`, in the same CI log, looks identical
but is not: those pages are genuinely untranslated and are fixed by translating
the content (sima-neat/llima#254), not by recording hashes. Worth keeping the
two distinct — recording hashes there would have marked stale instructions as
current.

author: initial-neko
body:
## Summary

Adds Character Space V2 autonomous social life on top of the merged Space V1 foundation.

### Daily life
- one restart-safe Space opportunity per active character per local day
- opportunities are distributed across 18:00-21:59 local time
- posting is optional; no post is a valid result
- the decision only uses existing Persona, Mental State, Memory and recorded events
- archived characters never receive a new opportunity

### Social loop
- autonomous posts select a sparse audience (current normal max 5, hard max 10)
- viewers receive SPACE_POST_SEEN through the existing PersonRuntime
- Space-only actions are SPACE_LIKE / SPACE_COMMENT / silence
- wrong-channel chat actions are dropped before persistence
- comments cause SPACE_COMMENT_RECEIVED for the author
- the author may reply once or remain silent
- Space observations can therefore update the same Mental State / Memory / Intent / Trace as the persistent person

### Dev testing
- Dev Console adds a Character Space Autonomy card
- Trigger Daily Life runs the full real loop immediately
- Re-run Audience processes a specified post again
- manual Dev opportunities do not consume the persisted daily opportunity

### Persistence / safety
- adds space_daily_runs for character+date restart safety
- fixes causal comment ordering
- scheduler is stopped before shared SQLite/model resources close
- CHARACTER_SPACE_AUTONOMY=0 disables automatic scheduling
- CHARACTER_SPACE_POLL_SECONDS controls scheduler polling

## Validation

Adds tests for:
- Space channel isolation from private chat
- post -> view -> like/comment -> author reply
- daily scheduler once-per-day behavior
- Dev trigger not consuming the daily run
- Dev Console control/route presence

author: kaydgn
body:
Kullanıcı isteği: tablo ve kanvaslar *"çok amatör"* duruyordu. Üç yönlü tasarım tezgâhından **C · Kart Listesi** seçildi (*"C çok güzel. Çok profesyonel duruyor. C'yi yapalım."*). İki yüzey birden yeniden kuruldu.

## TABLO — ızgara kalktı, her satır bir KASNAK

| Ne | Önce | Sonra |
|----|------|-------|
| Taşıyıcı | `<table>` + `<colgroup>` + `<thead>` + `<tfoot>` | `.ve-fead-krt` kart listesi, üç bölge |
| Girdi/çözüm ayrımı | `<col class="coz">` şeridi | **bölgenin kendisi** (gömülü zemin) |
| Kayış boyu | `rowspan="6"` hücre, ~170 px boş | künyede (`Kayış boyu`) |
| Σ toplam | yapışkan alt şerit | künyede |
| Dönüş Yönü | `<select>` ×6 | iki durumlu segment ×6 |
| Kart ölçüsü | 870×340 | **770×360**, bölge toplamıyla TAM oturuyor |
| Sağdaki ölü şerit | 12 px (782 px'lik kartta ölçüldü) | **0 px** (`coz` = `1fr`) |
| En küçük ölçü | = kart genişliği (sütunlar sessizce silinirdi) | **564 < 770** — bölgeler daralır, alan kaybolmaz |

Bölgeler: `kim` (sıra · ad düğmesi · rol çipi) · `gir` (X · Y · D · Yön) · `coz` (Ø eff · Sarım · Span). **Defterin sütun SIRASI bölgelerin içinde korunuyor.** Alan etiketleri kısa (`Ø eff`), defterin tam adı `title`da (`Efektif Çap (mm)`).

## KANVAS — dört yatay bant kalktı

| Bant | Yüksekliği nereden alıyordu | Şimdi |
|------|------------------------------|-------|
| İki seçici şeridi | çizimden 44 px | yüzen tek çubuk (Kol · Devir · Titr · Katmanlar) |
| Durum şeridi | çizimden 20 px | sağ üst rozet |
| Kazanç şeridi (titreşim) | çizimden 20 px daha | çubuğun üstünde yüzer |

Ölçüldü (440×500 kart): çizime **436 px** kalıyordu, titreşim açıkken **416**. Şimdi çizim kabuğun **tamamını** alıyor.

Rozetin birincil okuması duruma göre değişiyor: yolunda olan hâlde tek sayı (Σsarım) + soluk künye, yolunda olmayan hâlde arızanın cümlesi ve künye yok.

### Ölçülen iki hata (ikisi de bu turda doğdu ve bu turda kapandı)

1. **Yön gülü tamamen görünmez oldu.** Bantlar kalkınca gülün varsayılan yeri (sağ alt) tam yüzen çubuğun altına düştü. Gül süs değil — *"montaj açısı −3,18°"* gibi bir sayının hangi yöne baktığı yalnız ondan okunuyor. Çözüm çizimi küçültmek **değil** (o, bandın geri gelmesi olurdu): yalnız gül yukarı alınıyor (`altPay`), ölçek aynı. Pay yalnız canlı kartta; rapor ve dışa aktarma etkilenmiyor.
2. **Çubuk dört satıra sarıyordu.** `left:50%` ile ortalanan mutlak bir kabın sığdırma genişliği "kap − left" oluyor (440'lık kartta 220) ve çubuk 40 → **110 px**'e çıkıyordu — yüzen çubuğun bütün kazancı geri gidiyordu. Ortalama `left`+`right`+`margin-inline:auto` ile.
3. **Titreşim şeridi kartın sağından 91 px taşıyordu** ve `overflow:hidden` onu sessizce kırpıyordu (`text-overflow:ellipsis` tek başına yetmiyor: `min-width` varsayılanı `auto`).

## `main`de ZATEN KIRMIZI OLAN İKİ KAPI

`origin/main` ayrı bir çalışma ağacında koşturuldu: `tests/unit/guide-fead.test.js` **2 kırmızı**. Birleştirmeyle gelmedi, burada düzeltildi:

1. **Kart sökücüsü kutuyu bulamıyordu.** Paneller ortak dile geçince (#960) kart kutusu `<section class="ve-fp-card">` oldu ve satır içi `border:1px solid` kalmadı; `veGuideCard` yalnız o çapayı arıyordu, bulamayınca panelin ilk div'ine kadar geri yürüyüp alakasız bir parça döndürdü. **"Algılanan Model" sahnesi kılavuzdan sessizce düştü** — belge üretildi, hata çıkmadı, yalnız o yüzeyin resmi yok.
2. **Sahne önek listesi eksikti** — yeni bir sınıf ailesi listeye girmezse kuralları hiç sökülmez ve sahne stilsiz çizilir.

Ayrıca bu turun kendi kaçağı: kart listesinin doğal genişliği bölgeler toplanarak okunuyordu ve `coz` bölgesi `1fr` olduğu için kendi sayısını yazmıyor — **768 yerine 534** (234 px eksik), yani sahne sığmadığı hâlde "sığıyor" sayılırdı. Kart artık toplamı ayrıca basıyor (`--fead-krt-en`); ölü veri değil, tek okuyucusu kılavuzun sahne ölçekleyicisi.

## Kapılar

- **Birim: 5585/5585 yeşil** (176 paket).
- **E2E: 66/66 yeşil** — FEAD altı spec + üç ürün spec'i (published · viewer · CAN Çözümleyici).
- **Mutasyon: 17/17 yakalandı.** Gül alt payı · rozet sınıfı · çubuğun sarması · çubuğun akışa düşmesi · rozet rengi · `coz`un sabitlenmesi · kart genişliği · segment işareti · künyedeki defter adı · sahne genişliğinin okunamaması · kimlik bölgesinin gölgeyi kırpması · `section` dalı · sarma denetimi · önek listesi · toplam genişlik · künye sütununun toplama girmesi · sahne payı.
- **Yeni e2e:** `tests/e2e/fead-kanvas.spec.js` — bant yüksekliği 0, çubuk tek satır ve taşmıyor, gül açıkta, titreşim şeridi çizimi küçültmüyor, rozetin iki hâli.
- **Gerçek tarayıcı:** 0 sayfa hatası, 0 konsol hatası.

## Yazı ölçeği

İki `font-size:8.5px` ve bir uydurma `--fs-nano` jetonu, ölçeğin `--fs-micro` basamağına bağlandı (`typography-scale.test.js`).

author: bc-devle
body:
Refs #256

### Reason for change

`Payments::addOrder()` is the only method of `Endpoints\Payments` that builds an entity out of the response without checking `$res->isError()` first, although its docblock already declares `@throws RequestError`.

When the API answers an error payload, `end($res->json)` returns a **string**, which is then handed to `Entities\Order::__construct()`. On PHP 8, `$orderDataArray['comment']` on a string raises `TypeError: Cannot access offset of type string on string` - an `Error`, not an `Exception`, so callers that catch `AlmaException` / `RequestError` cannot catch it and the whole request dies.

Hit in production on 2026-09-21 with alma-installments-prestashop 4.16.0 (which bundles this client 2.6.1), PrestaShop 8.2, PHP 8.1: the module pushes the tracking number from `actionObjectUpdateAfter`, a hook PrestaShop fires during a partial refund, on an order flagged as Alma but with no real Alma payment behind it. The merchant gets PrestaShop's generic "unexpected error" page, no refund and no credit slip - while the refund handler has already put the products back in stock. Full write-up in #256.

### Code changes

- `src/Endpoints/Payments.php`: `addOrder()` now throws `RequestError` when the response is an error, before building the `Order` entity. Same shape as `trigger()` a few lines above, with `$req` passed for context.
- Behaviour on a successful response is unchanged.

### How to test

Call `payments->addOrder()` with a payment id the API does not know (or anything that makes the API answer an error):

- before: `TypeError: Cannot access offset of type string on string` in `src/Entities/Order.php:99`, uncatchable by the caller;
- after: `RequestError` carrying the API error message, catchable like everywhere else in this class.

### Checklist for authors and reviewers

<!-- Move to the next section the non applicable items -->

- [ ] The title of the PR uses business wording, not technical jargon, for the changelog readers to understand it
- [ ] The PR implements the changes asked in the referenced task / issue
- [ ] The automated tests are compliant with the [testing strategy](https://www.notion.so/almapay/Backend-testing-strategy-06c642cec1bf47b9b8feca3a91ea8d4a)
- [ ] The tests are relevant, and cover the corner/error cases, not only the happy path
- [ ] You understand the impact of this PR on existing code/features
- [ ] The changes include adequate logging and Datadog traces
- [ ] Documentation is updated (API, developer documentation, ADR, Notion...)

author: stormer78
body:
## Problem

A user's openvtc join failed at *Creating persona DID* with:

> trust task failed [internalError]: internal error: the consumer could not complete this task; the request itself was accepted

The VTA's own log had the real cause:

```
cause=bad gateway: `did:webvh:Qmbxds…:dids.ic3.dev` did not answer over TSP after re-establishing the relationship
```

The did-hosting log showed the path was reserved, but the reply was refused by the mediator (`e.p.limits.queue.sender`). So the fault was upstream, yet the wire said "this VTA had an internal error". That's because `app_error_to_reject` sent every `ServiceError`, including the `bad_gateway_error` that every peer failure produces, through the opaque catch-all.

## Change

- `ServiceError` at **502/504** → `taskFailed`, `details.reason: upstream_unavailable`, with fixed text: *"a service this VTA depends on did not answer or refused the request; the VTA's log names which one and why"*.
- The cause is **still not put on the wire**. Bad-gateway messages can carry a peer's URL, its transport error, and (from `send_rest`) the peer's response body, which is the same class of detail the `Internal` arm withholds. It goes to the log at `error`.
- `vta-sdk`: new `trust_task_reject_reasons::UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`; `trust_task_error` recovers it as `VtaError::Server { status: 502 }`, which is what `from_http` already gives a REST caller.
- Other `ServiceError` statuses stay opaque `internalError` (tested).

Additive on the wire. An older SDK sees `taskFailed` with a reason it doesn't know and falls back to `Protocol` (existing behaviour for unknown reasons). No version fields touched (release-plz owns them).

## Tests

- `an_upstream_failure_is_named_as_one_without_its_cause` (502 + 504; no URL/DID leak; not the internal text)
- `other_service_errors_stay_internal`
- `an_upstream_failure_arrives_as_a_bad_gateway` (SDK)
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib trust_tasks`: 268 passed; `cargo test -p vta-sdk --lib`: 380 passed; clippy clean.

Companion: an openvtc PR that makes `explain()` say what both cases mean.

body:
An over-limit stream could show the refusal popup and then start playing after the client retried. The guard treated a matching "now playing" item as an existing playback, but the browser reports playback start even when the initial launch fails.

Require a successful FFmpeg launch for the same user, device, item, and playback session before granting the continuation exemption. Refused retries remain blocked after the count and notification caches expire, while seeks within an admitted playback session remain allowed. Failed launches and GPU refusals do not grant that exemption.

Validation:

- Reproduced the original bypass with two regression tests against the old implementation.
- All 338 tests pass, including repeated fallbacks with unchanged or replacement playback IDs, admitted seeks, user/session changes, and raising the configured limit.
- Release build passes with no warnings or errors.
- Whitespace and C# style checks pass for both projects.
- Live Jellyfin playback validation remains outstanding.

author: pgielniak
body:
## What

**E11-S05-T02 — the release gate.** `RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md` holds five lines, each resolving to a **run id** rather than a judgement; `research/release-gate/rc-2026-09-21.md` is the first walk, against release commit `474d7c3`. A gate whose lines are opinions ("tests look fine") can be walked by nobody but its author and audited by nobody at all.

### Walking it is the deliverable, and it found the line with no evidence

Four lines resolved by lookup. **The fifth did not exist.** `Real-run parity (L6)` had never been dispatched — E11-S05-T01 exercised `scripts/realrun.ts` locally, and a local result is precisely what that line exists to exclude: an un-dispatched workflow is a claim about CI, not evidence from it.

It was dispatched with `reuse_run: 553`, re-reading a finished Azure run instead of queueing one, so the whole CI path — secrets, `pnpm build`, extractor, comparison, artifact upload — was validated for **zero new hosted-agent minutes**. The assertion is two-sided by construction, because a job gated out by `ORACLE_ENABLED` or a script that no-opped is indistinguishable from success at the conclusion level: the log must show *both* `reusing completed run 553` and `PARITY across 13 facts` (C-E12-063).

| # | Line | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | L1/L2/L4 green | `ci.yml` **35614680104** — four `test` legs `success` |
| 2 | L5 green | `e2e (L5, containers)` job of the same run |
| 3 | L3 nightly ≥ 3 consecutive days | **35576108449** / **35497974655** / **35429351169** — streak unbroken to 09-10 |
| 4 | L6 spot-check | **35617191948** — `PARITY across 13 facts`, artifact uploaded |
| 5 | Residual risk stated | filled in, below |

### Six tiers do not map onto three workflows — and the checklist says so

L1, L2 and L4 have **no CI job of their own**; they are vitest projects and a bats file inside one `test` matrix, so "L1–L4 green" resolves to a single job matrix, not four results. L2 does not gate the shipped path at all, having been re-scoped by E12-S03-T01 to the offline fallback (the default expansion is the service's own, PLAN D3). A checklist implying a job per tier overstates its granularity invisibly to whoever walks it next (C-E12-064) — the same defect as a comparator claiming parity over rows it never compared.

### The residual-risk section is filled in, not boilerplate

A checklist of green things tells a release manager nothing about what is dark:

- **L6 covers one fixture** where L5 has four — parity there is not parity in general
- **The corpus is 12** against a docs/06 §3 target of ≥ 30
- **14 tasks are `[!]`** — unverified surface, not deferred work — concentrated in **E08 deployment (6)** and **E09 auth (5)**, i.e. the Azure/K8s priority group and the auth paths in front of it
- **One `VERIFY` is genuinely open** (C-E12-045 — transitive vs direct dependency closure), and it is *now settleable*, since the oracle turned out to be available (C-E12-056). C-E12-052's is retracted, not open.
- **One cosmetic defect carried knowingly** — E11-S05-T03

None blocks a release. All of them are things the release notes have to say.

### Deliberately not built

No gate-checking script. The **Do** says document the checklist and encode it as a template; a tool that resolves evidence links is a separate deliverable with its own grounding questions (which `gh` queries, what counts as "the" run for a tier, how a fork without `ORACLE_ENABLED` behaves). If the manual walk proves tedious, that is a follow-up task, not something to answer in passing.

**This closes every `[ ]` task in the backlog except E11-S05-T03.**

## Grounding checklist (BACKLOG.md §3 — reviewer rejects unproven behavior changes)

- [x] Every implemented Azure DevOps behavior cites a source — **no Azure DevOps behaviour is implemented here**; this task documents a process and its evidence is GitHub Actions run ids
- [x] GitHub references are **commit-pinned permalinks** — n/a, no GitHub source cited
- [x] Claim entries added — C-E12-063/064 in `research/E12-testing-parity.md`
- [x] No behavior implemented from model/author memory — every run id in the walk was resolved live with `gh`, including the one that turned out not to exist
- [x] `VERIFY` items resolved — none consumed; the walk *counts* the one that remains open and notes it is now settleable. `scripts/check-verify-markers.sh` green
- [x] `research/REFERENCES.md` statuses updated — **no change needed and none made**: this task's Ground field asks for CI evidence, not external sources

## Quality gates

- [x] Tests per the task's **Done** criteria — the Done criterion is the walk itself, committed at `research/release-gate/rc-2026-09-21.md` with every link resolved
- [x] `pnpm lint` green; typecheck, claim-coverage and verify-markers green; unit suite green. No bash or runtime code touched
- [x] No secrets — run ids and workflow names only
- [x] Backlog bookkeeping — E11-S05-T02 `[x]`, changelog appended, docs/06 §3's L6 row now names what implements it

author: paoloirrera
body:
## Summary

Evaluation run status never reached the UI in real time. `publishEvaluationUpdate` and
`receiveEvaluationUpdate` had shipped in `schema.graphql` with **neither a publisher nor a
resolver**, so the mutation was unresolvable and the subscription delivered nothing. The
evaluations manager compensated with a flat 2s `setInterval` that only worked if *that tab*
had started the run; the run-results page and the run-history modal loaded once and showed
`Running` forever.

This wires the path end to end: the executor publishes a terminal status after its DynamoDB
write, AppSync relays it through a NONE data source, and one hook drives the three UI
surfaces. The notification carries `(evaluatorId, runId, status)` and is **never rendered** —
it names a record worth re-reading, so DynamoDB stays the only source of run state. That rule
is recorded in ADR 0007, because agent lifecycle, KB sync and experiments will need it when
they migrate.

`schema.graphql` is unchanged (zero-line diff), and no new IAM statement, Lambda env var, or
dependency is added in either language — the executor already held `APPSYNC_API_ENDPOINT` and
an `appsync:GraphQL` grant commented *"for progress updates"*.

## Changes

- **AppSync (`iac-cdk` + resolvers):** NONE data source plus `publish.js` / `subscribe.js`
  (`APPSYNC_JS 1.0.0`), mirroring the existing `runtime-update` pair. The subscription filters
  on `evaluatorId` only; clients filter `runId` themselves, which is what keeps the schema
  unchanged.
- **Executor (`src/api/functions/evaluation-executor/`):** `appsync_publisher.py` signs one
  mutation with `botocore` SigV4 over `urllib` — no new dependency, and deliberately not the
  `httpx`-based `shared/sigv4_auth.py`, which reaches the bundle only transitively. Called at
  the end of `_finalize_run` and `_update_run_failed`; every failure is logged and swallowed,
  so a notification problem cannot lose a completed run or fail the SQS batch.
- **`useEvaluationRunWatcher` (new hook):** subscription + re-read on Amplify's
  `Connecting → Connected` + a safety-net poll. Returns `void`, stores no run state, and reads
  only `runId` from the payload.
- **Three surfaces adopt it:** the manager (the 2s `setInterval` and its `pollingRun` state are
  gone; in-flight runs are derived from `listEvaluators`), the run-results page, and the
  run-history modal.
- **Terraform:** mirrors the CDK side — NONE data source, both resolvers, and both fields
  registered in the evaluation module's `operations` output. **Needs a `state mv` before
  applying** — see "Deploying this" below.
- **ADR 0007** records the rule and, honestly, its costs.

## Deploying this

Two things a reviewer should not discover at apply time.

**CDK:** `Mutation.publishEvaluationUpdate` already had a resolver, created by
`HttpApiBackend`'s schema-driven loop — it was in no `operations` array before this branch.
Registering it there removes that resolver and adds a NONE-backed one, and CloudFormation
creates before it deletes in the cleanup phase, so a naive change collides with a still-live
resolver and rolls the stack back. The new resolver is therefore created on `props.api` with
the same construct id the proxy loop used, reusing logical ID
`ChatbotApipublishEvaluationUpdateresolver188EC96E` so the deploy is an in-place
`DataSourceName` update. `TypeName` and `FieldName` are unchanged, and those are the only
create-only properties. Verified against a pre-story synthesized template, not inferred.

**Terraform:** the same AppSync one-resolver-per-field constraint applies, but here the two
addresses are the same resource with the same Terraform ID. Adopt it rather than racing a
destroy against a create:

```
terraform state mv \
  'module.http_api_resolver.aws_appsync_resolver.mutation_resolvers["publishEvaluationUpdate"]' \
  'module.evaluation.aws_appsync_resolver.publish_evaluation_update'
```

The command is also recorded in a comment next to the resource. Check per environment with
`terraform state list | grep publishEvaluationUpdate` — an environment that never applied the
proxy version has nothing to move and applies cleanly.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd iac-cdk && npm test` — 62 tests, 6 suites. Covers the NONE-backed wiring, the
      resolver bodies executed against a stubbed `@aws-appsync/utils` and tied to the asset
      bytes CloudFormation deploys, the eleven existing evaluation `resolverId`s unchanged, the
      reused logical ID, and a full-stack case asserting the field resolves exactly once.
- [x] `uv run pytest src/api/functions/evaluation-executor/tests/` — 43 tests. Payload shape,
      the three publish failure modes, and `_finalize_run` / `_update_run_failed` /
      `_update_progress` all completing with DynamoDB writes intact when the publisher raises.
- [x] `git diff --exit-code origin/main...HEAD -- src/api/schema/schema.graphql` — empty.
- [x] `cd src/user-interface/react-app && npm run build` (`tsc && vite build`) clean;
      `make precommit-run` clean; `terraform validate` clean.
- [x] `make run-ash` — **0 actionable findings on PR-touched files.** 3 actionable exist
      repo-wide, all in untouched files (see below).
- [x] `cd iac-cdk && npx cdk synth` — exits 0, no `AwsSolutions-` errors, so cdk-nag passes.
      Worth knowing: cdk-nag runs *only* via the `AwsSolutionsChecks` aspect in `bin/aca.ts:85`.
      `aca.test.ts` does not apply it and ASH's cdk-nag scanner reports `MISSING` in this
      environment, so `npm test` and ASH alone do **not** cover nag — the synth above is what
      does.
- [x] Deploy-safety of the logical-ID reuse verified against the real synthesized app template,
      not just the test stack: `Mutation.publishEvaluationUpdate` is
      `ChatbotApipublishEvaluationUpdateresolver188EC96E` (identical to the pre-story proxy
      resolver's logical ID) now pointing at `evaluationrelaysource` with `APPSYNC_JS`.
- [x] **Deployed manual pass, still owed.** Start a run, then: switch tabs and return; reload
      mid-run; force the subscription to fail. Each surface should reach the terminal status
      with no user action. Best done on a fresh stack or after confirming the in-place resolver
      update above.
- [ ] Verify `terraform plan` shows **zero destroys** after the `state mv`.

**The three UI surfaces have no automated coverage.** `src/user-interface/react-app` has no
test runner — no vitest, no jest, no testing-library — and adding one is out of scope for this
PR. The hook, its timer lifecycle, the backoff, and the `runId` filter are code-reviewed and
audited but not executed by any assertion. That is why the manual pass above is not optional.

## Known scan findings (non-blocking)

- 24× bandit **B101** (`assert` in tests) and 2× **B105** (`_FAKE_SECRET_KEY = "fake/secret"`),
  all confined to the two new pytest files. Both are what a pytest suite looks like.
- `urlopen` is now pinned to `https://` before use, with bandit **B310** and the semgrep
  urllib rule suppressed *against that check*. I confirmed the guard rejects
  `file:///etc/passwd` rather than only silencing the scanner.

## Pre-existing repo-wide findings (not introduced by this PR)

ASH reports **3 actionable findings, none on a file this PR touches**:

- 1× detect-secrets `SECRET-HEX-HIGH-ENTROPY-STRING` on `cli/src/args.rs:264` (the Rust CLI,
  untouched here).
- 1× checkov `CKV_AWS_394` on `iac-terraform/modules/experiments/main.tf:58`.
- 1× checkov `CKV_AWS_174` on `iac-terraform/modules/user_interface/cloudfront.tf:30`.

Plus, not actionable but worth naming:

- 2× semgrep `path-join-resolve-traversal` on `iac-cdk/test/aca.test.ts:84` — the `findFiles`
  helper, which predates this branch. Left alone rather than fixed, to keep the diff honest.
- 180 checkov findings suppressed repo-wide via `.ash/.ash.yaml`, unchanged by this PR.
- ASH's `cdk-nag`, `cfn-nag

| #27 | Unlinking a role line wipes every group and sets `share = True` | high | `2468756` |
| #28 | Revoking an API key breaks the audit log | medium | `590d9fa` |
| #29 | Un-renamed `base_user_role` XML id crashes the role button | low | `67869a5` |

Versions: `pan_mcp_pro_governance` 19.0.1.23.2 → 19.0.1.24.0 (two new columns), `pan_mcp_user_role` 19.0.1.0.4 → 19.0.1.0.5 (view changes, so existing databases need `-u pan_mcp_user_role` too, not only the governance module).

## Two calls worth a second opinion

**#27 changes what removing a role means.** The guard now holds under `force`, so unlinking the last role line no longer withdraws the groups that role granted -- they stay on the account. That is what the reporter asked for, and the alternative is the current behaviour, which strips the account bare and flips it to a share user. Combined with #26 (roles are no longer a user-management surface at all) it is coherent, but it is a behaviour change, not a pure bugfix.

**#26 removes view content from a vendored folder.** ADR-013 permits three kinds of edit inside `pan_mcp_user_role/` and this is a fourth. The folder already drifts past that list, so it is not a new precedent, but the ADR is now stale -- filed as #32.

## Notes

- **#28 has no backfill migration.** Rows logged before this version show a blank API Key cell instead of crashing. Rows whose key is already deleted are unrecoverable; their identity is gone.
- **#28 also covers `auditlog.log`**, not just `auditlog.http.request`. The related field dangled the same way and the reporter had to clean that table by hand too.
- **#26's second half is not in this PR.** The seeded `Administrator` role implying `base.group_system`, and `is_default` auto-assigning roles to new users, are design calls -- filed as #31.

## Verification

Fresh database, stock `odoo:19` image, all three addons mounted: **58 tests, 0 failed, 0 errors**, plus the fresh-install gate. Each fix carries a test; #27's was confirmed to fail on the pre-fix guard and pass after.

author: 0xferit
body:
Preserves comments before a variation’s first move, separately from comments after it. For example, `1. e4 ({Prefer d4} 1. d4 {White's choice} d5) e5 *` now keeps both annotations in their original positions on save.

Leading comments belong to the first variation node because the temporary parser root is discarded. Node copies snapshot both comment strings; subtree undo reattaches the original nodes. The existing comment serializer also preserves bodies containing `}` through semicolon export. Separate comment blocks are still merged, and post-move comments do not retain their placement relative to following variation parentheses.

Regression tests cover nested and Black-first variations, repeated save/reopen, recovered-game edits, and mutable-string isolation. The sanitizer suite, Release build, and document-level open/save/reopen check passed.

author: arielankora
body:
## מה קרה

שלושה מסכים שלחו לדפדפן את ה-hash של הסיסמאות.

ב-Next.js, ה-props של client component עוברים serialisation לתוך ה-HTML של העמוד. אם מעבירים שורה מהדאטהבייס, כל עמודה בשורה הזו נוסעת איתה. `listUsers()` ו-`prisma.user.findFirst` מחזירים את מודל ה-User המלא, כולל `passwordHash`:

| מסך | מה דלף |
|---|---|
| `/app/users/[userId]` | ה-hash של המשתמש שנפתח |
| `/app/important-dates` | ה-hash של **כל** המשתמשים |
| `/app/important-dates/[id]` | ה-hash של **כל** המשתמשים |

זה ה-hash של כל חשבון בחברה, בתוך view-source של מסכים שמנהל פותח כל יום, נגיש לכל תוסף דפדפן, ונשמר בכל cache או proxy בדרך. bcrypt איטי, וזה קונה זמן; זה לא הופך hash גנוב לבטוח, ושום דבר כאן לא מתחלף אוטומטית.

## למה TypeScript לא תפס את זה

`ImportantDateForm` כבר הגדיר `users: { id, name, role }[]` — נכון. אבל משתנה (בניגוד ל-object literal) רשאי לשאת תכונות שהטיפוס המוצהר שלו לא מזכיר. הטיפוסים נראו נכונים בזמן שהבייטים לא היו.

## התיקון

בכל שלושת מקומות הקריאה מועבר עכשיו אובייקט מפורש עם השדות שהקומפוננטה באמת משתמשת בהם. בנוסף: ה-prop של `EditRoleStatusForm` צומצם ל-`Pick<User, "id"|"role"|"status">`, והשאילתה במסך פרטי המשתמש עברה מ-`include` ל-`select` — כך שה-hash לא נשלף מלכתחילה.

## שתי הגנות שנוספו

התקלה בלתי נראית על המסך ואף code review לא תפס אותה, אז:

1. סריקת המסכים המאומתים בודקת עכשיו בכל מסמך שנשלח: prefix של bcrypt, שדה `passwordHash`, שדה `tokenHash` — תחת סשן של עובד.
2. אותה סריקה רצה שוב תחת Super Admin, בתוספת מסך פרטי המשתמש דרך לחיצה על קישור אמיתי. סשן המנהל הוא זה שחשוב: לעובד רוב המסכים האלה מציגים הודעת הרשאה בלי שורות, ודליפה צריכה נתונים כדי לדלוף.

שתיהן sweeps מעל ה-manifest ולא בדיקות על שלושה מסכים, כי הטעות מבנית: כל מסך עתידי שיעביר שורה מהדאטהבייס ל-client component יחזיר אותה.

## למה זה מחכה לאישור שלך

זה קוד מוצר, לא בדיקות, אז לפי מדיניות המיזוג אני לא ממזג בעצמי.

נמצא על ידי סוכן ה-QA, שזו בדיוק המטרה שלו.

author: felixtjdietrich
body:
### Summary
Make the client UI modernization — retiring Bootstrap, ng-bootstrap and PrimeNG for Tailwind and the TUM UI kit — the main CodeStats dashboard, updated hourly with a full snapshot for every first-parent commit on `develop`. Bootstrap is measured with Artemis's own definition of the migration (lint rule and lock list); PrimeNG, ng-bootstrap and TUM UI by what each unit uses, matched against the kit's selectors at the same commit. The signals and DTO dashboards stay reachable as archives; their collection stops.

### Motivation and Context
Artemis defines the migration in three synchronized artifacts (the `no-bootstrap-classes` lint rule, its regression-lock path list, and the Tailwind `@source` allowlist) and ships `pnpm migrate:status` / `migrate:check` for the burndown. A dashboard that counts something else cannot answer the questions a migration lead asks weekly: is the number going down and how fast, which pull requests moved it, what is the cheapest next lock, which shared component blocks the most, which section is next, did anything regress.

Milestones used as references: the [TUM UI pilot (Artemis #13226)](https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/13226) and the [package adoption (Artemis #13323)](https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/pull/13323). This PR does not modify Artemis.

### Description
**Measurement (`report/ui/analyze.ts`)**
- Loads `rules/no-bootstrap-classes.mjs` from the analyzed Artemis commit and counts hits with its `isBanned` / `bannedClassesInBindingExpression`, so template counts agree with Artemis's `migrate:status` (7,617 vs 7,618 at HEAD; the one difference is commented-out markup). Also counts the forms the lint cannot see: inline templates, static parts of interpolated class lists, host class bindings and `addClass` literals. SCSS residue follows the stylelint lock (`--bs-*`, hex, `rgb()`/`hsl()`) plus Bootstrap Sass imports.
- Unit = one `@Component`/`@Directive` declaration with its template and stylesheets. Its modernization stage is legacy-free (no Bootstrap hits, no PrimeNG or ng-bootstrap usage), "PrimeNG or ng-bootstrap remain", or Bootstrap; the Bootstrap lock status (`locked`) is tracked alongside.
- PrimeNG and ng-bootstrap usage per unit (elements, directives, services such as `DialogService` and `NgbModal`), each mapped to the TUM UI component that covers it when the kit of that commit ships it; usages without one are reported as kit gaps.
- Import graph through decorated classes (standalone `imports`, dialogs opened from code, `import()`): "imports with hits" per unit, and which shared units block the most Bootstrap-free units.
- Lockable directories: unlocked, with templates, zero hits and zero imported hits; the dashboard copies the three lock entries per directory.
- Inventories of remaining Bootstrap classes (with the guideline's targets), PrimeNG and ng-bootstrap elements/directives/services, and TUM UI kit usage against the kit's selectors at that commit.

- Routed pages: walked from `app.routes.ts` through `children` and `loadChildren` with full paths; a page is ready when it, what it imports and its parent route components carry no Bootstrap. The global shell (navbar, footer, overlays) is reported separately.

**Dashboard (`src/features/migrations`)**
- **Module scope**: a Module picker (and clicking a module in the Modules table) sets `?module=`; every view then counts that module only — headline tiles, trends, contributors and commit tables from its per-commit row, units, pages, next steps and inventory from its units, lock and page counts from the scoped detail. The Modules view shows the selected module's units (selectors), stylesheets and lockable directories inline; a banner names the scope with a "Show all modules" link. "Section" is called module everywhere (data field stays `section`).
- Any commit can be the snapshot or the comparison: both pickers are searchable comboboxes over every snapshot (date, commit, subject); the comparison defaults to a week earlier.
- Headline: legacy-free share, Bootstrap hits with 4-week and since-adoption pace, units using PrimeNG and ng-bootstrap with kit coverage, units using TUM UI; a legacy-free / components remain / Bootstrap stage bar and the Bootstrap gate (locked, lockable).
- Views (URL `?view=`): **Overview** (units where legacy grew, one trend per dependency — Bootstrap hits, PrimeNG, ng-bootstrap, TUM UI — with lock-list changes, commits that moved the numbers with PR links), **Modules** (stage bar, Δ vs comparison and since adoption, units per library and locked with their change, last progress with idle modules marked; heatmap of Bootstrap hits by kind of work plus SCSS, PrimeNG and ng-bootstrap occurrences; the selected module's units by stage with library usage and kit components inline), **Pages** (legacy-free / components left / blocked / Bootstrap per module; every page as selector with its route, colored state, hits in the page, imported and in layouts, and a *Units to fix* popover listing the exact components in the way), **Next steps** (quick wins with the exact changes, lockable directories with copyable lock entries and new-since-comparison marks, shared units with Bootstrap that block the most, kit gaps, sections closest to legacy-free), **Inventory** (Bootstrap classes with exact targets, PrimeNG and ng-bootstrap with kit components, coverage and gaps, TUM UI kit usage, stylesheets with residue; every row with its change and disappeared entries struck through), **Contributors** (second view; leaderboard of progress per credited author, each commit split by its branch credits with GitHub avatar and profile: PRs with progress, Bootstrap hits removed and share, net legacy-free / PrimeNG / ng-bootstrap / TUM UI units, directories locked, hits added, last progress, active since; top three called out; window since adoption or since the comparison; latest 15 commits with progress). The overview's commit table shows authors too.
- Every table is one generic `DataTable` (`src/components/data-table.tsx`, the shadcn recipe over TanStack Table): every column sorts with `aria-sort` on the header (numbers descending first), the large tables search across all columns and scroll under a sticky header. Sections sort by progress (legacy-free share, Δ legacy-free, Δ hits, since adoption, last progress) or by any library; Inventory rows carry a sortable Δ; Blockers show units unblocked per hit; Quick wins sort by section to batch a pull request.
- Built from the repository's shadcn/ui components (Card, Command, Table, Sheet, Popover, Tabs, ToggleGroup, Accordion, Alert, ChartContainer, sonner); state lives in TanStack Router search params.

**Data and operations**
- Each snapshot records its first parent, its author (GitHub login resolved from noreply addresses or the commits API with `GITHUB_TOKEN`; avatars load from github.com), the rule hash and `credits`: the generator fetches `refs/pull/<n>/head` (kept by GitHub after the squash merge), walks the branch commits from the merge base, measures every changed client file before and after each commit, and splits the commit's change by the legacy each author removed there (client lines when nobody touched legacy). Authors without a GitHub account (unlinked addresses, coding agents) and shares under 5 % fold into the PR author; credits are deferred to a later run when a login lookup is unavailable. `Co-authored-by` trailers are not used (they mostly name coding agents and applied review suggestions). Only commits whose parent is the previous snapshot are attributed; rule changes are not credited with hits; `[bot]` accounts are not listed.
- Every one of the 407 commits has a detail file, like the archived dashboards had a report per run: weekly commits and the two milestones hold the full detail (~0.7 MB), every other commit a patch of the units and stylesheets that changed since the base (~50 KB on average); the client resolves a patch through its base. `index.json` (~540 KB) holds totals,

author: conan0h
body:
## What

Two commits, both making the repo's description of itself match the repo.

1. **`go.mod` module path** — backlog P0 #2. It declared
   `github.com/conanohara/alert-platform`; the repository is at
   `github.com/conan0h/alert-platform`, so the import path named a module
   nobody can fetch.
2. **Documentation** — the README claimed things about production it has no
   way to know, and told the reader to do work that was already done.

## Why

P0 #2 was the next unblocked backlog item. The docs pass came out of a sweep
for stale content: I checked every claim I could check from git rather than
guessing at what looked old.

The zip is already gone — `alert-platform-launchpad.zip` was removed in #1,
along with restoring `.claude/` into git. Nothing else in the tree is cruft:
every image under `docs/img/` is referenced, build and cache directories are
already gitignored, and the largest remaining files are the two console
screenshots (712 KB) which the README and architecture doc both use.

## How

**Module path.** `go.mod` plus the import block of all 13 files that named it.
`vendor/modules.txt` lists dependencies only and never named the main module,
so the vendor tree is untouched and the dependency set is unchanged.

One thing deliberately **not** done: `go install …/cmd/alertctl@latest`
resolves to the newest *tag*, and `v0.1.0`–`v0.1.2` all carry the old path, so
it keeps failing until a release is cut from this commit or later. Cutting a
tag to prove a rename is not a reason to release, and rolling the fleet onto
it is a deploy-path change I cannot verify without Phase 8, so it waits for a
change that earns a release. Recorded in the backlog.

**Docs.** Three claims were wrong, in different ways:

- *"Phases 2–7 … have not yet run against the production host."* This repo
  cannot know that either way — there is no read path to the host, which is
  precisely what the unbuilt pipeline provides. Replaced with an explicit
  statement that the README reports no evidence about production and that the
  host's own `status`, `drift` and audit log are the sources of truth. The
  phase list also stopped at 7 and read as finished, so the deploy pipeline is
  now an unchecked Phase 8.
- *"cut the `v0.1.0` tag"* as a pre-deploy step. That tag has existed for a
  while and the fleet has since moved to `v0.1.2`, so the instruction sent
  people to redo completed work. Fixed in the README and marked done in
  `migration.md`, whose "Before the first deploy" section now says plainly
  that only the tag is confirmable from git — token rotation, SSM contents and
  host prep are not, so nobody should read silence there as progress.
- A spec comment calling `v0.1.2` the "post-migration baseline". `v0.1.0` was.

`CLAUDE.md` §10 is that file's own "verify and update as you learn" block, so
it now records green CI and both root causes, the corrected module path, and
the environment facts every run has so far had to rediscover.

## Proof

```
go vet ./...                                     ok
gofmt -l cmd internal                            (empty)
go test ./... -race                              ok — all 5 packages
go build -o bin/alertctl ./cmd/alertctl          ok
ruff check services tools                        All checks passed!
python3 tools/validate.py                        OK: 4 service spec(s) valid
python3 tools/gen_observability.py --check       ok
python3 -m pytest services/tests -q              31 passed
```

The module rename is the kind of change that compiles and still breaks the
cross-language seam, so the pytest run matters here: `services/tests/test_contract.py`
executes the rebuilt binary and parses what it renders, which is what proves
the rename did not disturb the env contract.

`gen_observability.py --check` passing confirms the spec comment edit did not
drift the generated Prometheus/Grafana config.

`golangci-lint` not run locally — image ships v2.5.0 against a v1-format
config. It runs in CI.

## Production

No runtime change. The Go rename does not touch the Python services, and the
only spec edit is a comment. No release, no deploy.

**No production report**: Phase 8 does not exist, so there is still no read
path to the host and this PR makes no claim about the four services. That is
now also what the README says.

## Review notes

- **The honesty change is the one to scrutinise.** I removed a claim
  ("has not run in production") and did not replace it with the opposite
  claim, because I cannot verify either. `CLAUDE.md` §10 does carry a
  reported-but-unverified production state from you; I deliberately did not
  promote that into the README, since a reader cannot tell reported from
  observed once it is on the front page.
- **Why `migration.md` was edited at all**, given it is a historical record:
  only its forward-looking "Before the first deploy" checklist, which is
  instructions, not history. The record of what moved and what the specs got
  wrong is untouched.
- **The module rename is wide but shallow** — 13 files, import lines only. The
  useful check is that nothing outside `vendor/` still says `conanohara`
  except `.claude/log.md`, where it is a historical entry and should stay.
- **`go install` still will not work** after this merges, and I would rather
  say so than have it look fixed. First tag cut from this commit or later
  makes it work.
- **Likely question: should the console screenshots be shrunk or dropped?**
  They are 712 KB of the repo's 13 MB, both referenced, and `docs/img/console.png`
  is flagged in the backlog for replacement with a real capture once Phase 8
  can port-forward to the console. Churning them now would waste that.

### Questions ?
