body:
## Summary

Implements **FIN-FE-011 — Journal and Account Explorer foundation** as a read-only Finance workspace over the released ledger/reporting APIs.

### Account explorer
- Adds `/app/finance/accounts` as the default Finance entry point.
- Lists the authoritative Chart of Accounts with search and explicit System / Control / manual-posting protection badges.
- Preserves the existing Supplier Bill matching workspace and Finance-domain active navigation.

### Account activity
- Adds `/app/finance/accounts/[accountId]`.
- Consumes the FIN-RPT-011 cursor-based account-activity contract.
- Displays backend-authoritative opening/activity/closing balances and running balance.
- Preserves canonical ledger ordering and source references.
- Supports cursor pagination without recomputing accounting values client-side.

### Journal + source trace
- Adds `/app/finance/journals/[journalId]`.
- Separates **accounting date**, **created timestamp**, and **posted timestamp**.
- Displays immutable journal lines, posting profile/rule identity, reversal relationships and correlation evidence.
- Resolves the authoritative Journal → FinancialEvent → source-reference chain.
- Links journal lines back to account activity.

### Read-only boundary
The feature API module exposes **GET hooks only**. It does not import or expose the backend adjustment/reversal commands, and SYSTEM journals are presented as system-generated/read-only.

### Contract coverage
Adds strict Zod contracts and Vitest coverage for:
- protected/control-account metadata;
- account activity and source references;
- backend-authoritative running balance fields;
- accounting-date vs created/posted timestamps;
- balanced journal line fixtures;
- journal-to-source trace.

### Generated OpenAPI note
The frontend's checked-in generated OpenAPI snapshot predates FIN-RPT-011; this feature follows the repository's current Finance pattern of strict runtime Zod contracts over the released backend API. No generated file was hand-edited.

author: bbasinsk
body:
## What
Reference-based OpenAPI now shares concrete record cases across unions and reuses wrappers only when discriminator keys and values match.

- `SpecAdapter.kt` uses the existing definition-name resolver instead of inventing per-union record identities.
- Compatible cases share one wrapper. Different keys or values produce distinct, reference-safe names.
- Generic command/event fixtures cover required fields, codec round-trips, distinct DTOs, reference resolution, and endpoint-order independence.
- Existing recursive and generic schema assertions now use canonical case names.
- `http-openapi/readme.md` explains affected generated-client names and regeneration.

## Why
[COOK-1195](https://linear.app/basinski/issue/COOK-1195) reports duplicate concrete DTO definitions when two sealed unions share one record schema.

## How to verify
1. Run `./gradlew :http-openapi:jvmTest :schema:jvmTest :schema-json-kotlinx:jvmTest --console=plain`. All 174 tests passed.
2. Run `./gradlew build --console=plain`. The full build passed with 574 actionable tasks, including OpenAPI JVM and macOS ARM64 tests.
3. Review `SharedUnionCaseTest`: `Command.Rename` appears once, both unions share its wrapper, and incompatible discriminators remain distinct.

Linux test execution was skipped by Gradle on this host. No release was published.

## Simplification review
No unaddressed findings. Reused `DefinitionNameResolver`, removed duplicate component generation, and kept discriminator naming stateless. No registry or new dependency.

## Out of scope
Consumer-specific fixtures, structural deduplication of unrelated DTOs, codec changes, and a general naming redesign.

Per Ben's decision, this remains a draft for review. Merging and Maven Central publication require separate approval. The release acceptance criterion remains unmet.

## Risk + rollback
Affected generated type names change. Regenerate clients after upgrading. Reverting this commit restores the previous duplicate definitions without changing wire payloads.

author: phicks-debug
body:
## Summary

When an SSE client disconnected, the pump threw and left the model stream unread. Nothing was persisted or metered, the span stayed open and the provider request kept running.

- One `AbortController` per run, passed to `streamText`. `ensureFinalized(drained)` aborts when the reader left early.
- `readAgentFullStream` moved to `harness.ts` and cancels its reader. The SSE and NATS pumps are one `pipeAgentStream(stream, send)`.
- The NATS publish is awaited, so frames keep their order.
- An aborted run records the usage and step count of the steps it finished. On abort the SDK calls only `onAbort`, so `onStepEnd` sums them; `onEnd` still replaces both with its own totals.
- A reader that leaves while `onEnd` is still persisting no longer turns a finished run into a failed one. `ensureFinalized(false)` drains the stream first, and the SDK closes it only after `onEnd` returns.
- `LiveNatsPublisher` keeps a failed connect for its one run. Before, every chunk retried the connect, and with the awaited publish the model waited out a timeout per chunk.

## Description

A dropped SSE client now fails the run cleanly; `apps/docs/docs/sdk.md` says so and points at `background: true`.

NATS publishing stays best-effort: `nats.ts` swallows publish errors, so a dead NATS connection does not fail the run. What now propagates out of the pump is the ownership check. `assertCurrentOwner` runs before each frame and is awaited, so a transient error from that Convex query now fails the run, where the old fire-and-forget pump dropped it. #589 cuts how often that query runs; do not deploy this PR without it.

A disconnect is still noticed at the next `enqueue`. A `cancel()` on the SSE body was left out: the run's abort is private to `runAgentLoop`, the body outlives several streams across continuation passes, and stopping the wait between passes needs a signal through `runParentContinuationLoop`.

`bench/cases/core-agent-run.ts` passes `true` to `ensureFinalized`; both callers drain fully. That was the `validate` break.

## Verification

Focused: `tests/harness.test.ts`. The abort test checks the provider call's abort signal and that step 1 never starts. New: an aborted run meters the one step it finished (15 tokens, `stepCount: 1`), and a reader leaving during `onEnd` still records `completed`. Each of the three fails with its fix removed.

Two scripts on the real SDK with a mock model, no network: after an abort the SDK fires `onStepEnd` then `onAbort` and never `onEnd`; `consumeStream()` resolves only after a running `onEnd` returns.

`bun run --filter @broods/core check`, `bun run bench:types`, root `bun run lint` (exit 0, no new warning), `bun run format:check`: all clean. Core suite 1260 pass, 33 skip, 0 fail. `bun run bench:test` 17 pass.

author: mcfearless75
body:
Reported as *"Javan Moussa isn't in the Year 2 chat."* He was in the **Year 1** chat, correctly — his profile said Year 1. The real problem was that **nobody could change it.**

## The gap

`users.year_group` has a DB `DEFAULT 1`, and there was **no write path for it anywhere in the app**:

- the Users table rendered Year as **read-only text**
- the create form never asked
- no API route accepted it

So every Year 2 joiner silently became a Year 1 student — wrong timetable, wrong calendar, wrong squad and cohort grouping, and the wrong auto-synced chat. **29 students created since 2026-09-01 currently sit on the default.**

And worse: the in-app help I added earlier today told staff to *"set their year group on their profile"* — advice for a control that didn't exist. That copy now points at the Users page, where the control now is.

## The fix

- **`UserRow`** — Year is a Year 1 / Year 2 picker for students (staff stay as a dash; `year_group` is meaningless for them). Changing it moves the student between the auto-synced chats via the `sync_year_group_chat` trigger, in the same transaction.
- **`CreateUserForm` + `create-user` route** — year group is asked for and persisted at creation, so a new joiner never lands on the default by accident. Rejected rather than coerced if it isn't 1 or 2.

## Security: unguarded server actions

While adding the action I found `updateUserRole` and `updateUserCourse` were **completely unguarded**. They run with the service-role client, which bypasses RLS, and a Next.js server action is reachable by anyone holding the action id from the client bundle — it is **not** protected by the `/admin` layout.

`updateUserRole(anyId, 'admin')` was therefore callable by anyone. That's privilege escalation — the same class as `050_prevent_role_self_escalation` and `051_signup_role_metadata_ignored`, but bypassing RLS entirely.

All three actions now call `requireStaffAction()`, exactly as [`lib/auth/requireRole.ts`](lib/auth/requireRole.ts) instructs ("every route or action that uses it MUST verify the caller's role in application code") and as `student-matches/actions.ts` already did. Granting a staff role additionally requires an **admin** caller, matching the rule the create-user route already enforced, so a coach cannot mint an admin. Roles and year groups are validated against allow-lists.

## Testing

12 new tests — the year picker (student vs staff, null fallback, save) and the guards (non-staff refused, coach blocked from granting admin, invalid role/year rejected, staff-only year group).

- **1337 tests / 148 suites, all passing**
- `npm run build` clean

## Already done in production

Javan is fixed: `year_group = 2`, now in Year 2 Students (19 → 20 members), out of Year 1, his other 9 rooms untouched.

body:
## WP-723 / EC-760 / D-24544 — X-Gene discard-pile class-presence condition

Un-hollows X-23's printed **X-Gene** on the two tractable cards. Per the
`keywords-full.json` glossary, *"X-Gene [class]: <effect>"* means *"If you have a
[class] card in your discard pile, <effect>."* — a discard-pile class-**presence**
condition, **not** the play-this-turn `heroClassMatch` the co-located
`[hc:instinct]` was wrongly parsed as (a `hero/x-gene/onPlay/parse-unrecognized`
hollow observed live on `df9291f0`).

### Design (D-24544)
A new **bare-string `HeroCondition` `heroClassInDiscardPile`** plus a **parser
directive** — **NOT** a new `HeroKeyword`. `HeroCondition` is a bare-string type,
so drift counts are unchanged: `HERO_KEYWORDS` stays **61**, `HERO_EFFECT_HANDLERS`
stays **45**.

- **Condition** (`hero/heroConditions.evaluate.ts`): new `heroClassInDiscardPile`
  case + `discardHasHeroClass` helper (scans `G.playerZones[id].discard` ×
  `G.cardTraits.heroClass`/`heroClass2`, **printed class only** — no Size-Changing
  grants; explicit `for...of`, no `.reduce()`) + `describeFailedCondition` wording.
- **Parser** (`setup/heroAbility.setup.ts`): `X_GENE_CARDS` allowlist,
  `xGeneSupported` option threaded from `buildHeroAbilityHooks`,
  `X_GENE_MARKER_PATTERN` + `lineHasXGene`, a Step 1a suppression that drops the
  spurious `heroClassMatch` and injects `heroClassInDiscardPile` with the class read
  from the co-located `[hc:X]` token (never hardcoded), and a Step 2 consume branch.
- **Per-card allowlisted** (transform / teleport precedent): **adamantium-foot-claws**
  (`[keyword:draw:1]`) and **bioengineered-assassin** (`[keyword:optional-ko-hand-discard]`,
  the shipped WP-667 keyword reused) resolve. **heir-to-wolverine** stays an honest
  `parse-unrecognized` hollow (count-scaled "Berserk that many times" needs a
  discard-class `HeroCountSource` + a count-scaled re-trigger node, neither of which
  exists) → `_deferred`. Recognizing X-Gene globally is deliberately avoided.

### Verification
- `pnpm -r build` 0; game-engine suite **3971 → 3987 / 0** (+16: 5 condition +
  5 parser + 6 end-to-end behavior tests).
- `apply-hero-ability-markers.mjs` updated exactly 2 lines (idempotent re-run 0).
- `cards:check`, `effect-index:check`, `mechanics:metadata:check`,
  `ledger:heroes:check`, `sim:runtime-observed:check`, `roadmap:counts:check`,
  `ledger:numbers:check`, `workindex:rows:check` all exit 0.
- Sentinel `finalStateHash` byte-identical (sentinel core-only, X-23 non-core — **no
  re-pin**). The hero-mechanic ledger flips the two cards to `draw` /
  `optional-ko-hand-discard` executable; heir-to-wolverine's X-Gene stays hollow.
- `runtime-observed-hollows.json` regenerated byte-identical (no content change,
  CRLF-only) — nothing to land; its `:check` passes against the committed baseline.

### Govern-close
D-24544 → Active; WORK_INDEX WP-723 checked (Done 2026-09-21); EC_INDEX EC-760 →
Done; mindmap node 📝 → ✅; STATUS.md updated. Two-commit topology
(`EC-760:` impl, then `SPEC:` govern-close).

**D-24026 live-verify is operator-pending post-merge** on `play.legendary-arena.com`.

body:
Implements the first operational Review/MR workflow after the architecture foundation.

- Review worklist now supports governed patient/case segmentation.
- Patient segments carry internal segment key, identifiability status, source-evidenced demographics, products, events and evidence.
- Labeling / expectedness is patient-product-event specific.
  - EXPECTED / UNEXPECTED require reference label key, version and effective date.
  - Missing label evidence remains UNRESOLVED.
- Causality is patient-product-event specific.
  - Non-UNRESOLVED conclusions require approved causality method key/version.
  - No causality is inferred from chronology alone.
- Medical Review finalization is a distinct permission/action.
  - MR cannot finalize before patient segmentation + labeling + causality governance.
  - APPROVED requires at least one patient segment.
  - APPROVED/EXCLUDED moves workflow to REVIEW_COMPLETE; REVIEW_REQUIRED keeps REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS.
- All Review mutations require a specific audit reason and write audit events.
- Adds Review-specific RBAC permissions and MEDICAL_REVIEWER role.
- Intake remains separately gated behind completed Review/MR.

## Resumen

decreditos no tiene API pública. Mientras se gestiona un acceso de partner con ellos, se agrega un simulador propio **aproximado** (queda explícito en toda la UI) dentro de `/panel/financiaciones`, usando los precios que ya están cargados en el stock.

### Tabla de topes por año
Confirmada probando el simulador real de decreditos con 12 autos/años reales distintos (no inventada):

| Categoría | Tope |
|---|---|
| Hasta 2015 | 50% |
| 2016–2017 | 55% |
| 2018–2020 | 60% |
| 2021+ (usado) | 65% |
| 0km | 70% |

### Qué calcula
- Capital máximo a financiar = precio de venta × tope según año.
- Gastos (transferencia + prenda) = precio × % configurable (default 11%).
- Anticipo en efectivo = (precio + gastos) − capital máximo.
- Cuota mensual estimada por plazo (12/18/24/36/48), sistema francés, con una TNA de referencia por plazo derivada de la grilla real de decreditos (perfil "Desde"/mejor crédito) — configurable en Configuración → Empresa → Financiación.

## 🔒 Security Audit Implementation

This PR applies critical security fixes and comprehensive audit documentation following a full security review of the HRD-Security/firewalker fork.

### 🎯 Primary Objective

Prevent data exfiltration and secure the supply chain for this private fork.

## ✅ Audit Verdict

**NO RUNTIME DATA LEAKS DETECTED**

The library source code, dependencies, and native binary loading do not send data or telemetry to external destinations. The library is purely local computation with no I/O except initial binary loading.

---

## 📋 Changes in This PR

### 1. Critical Security Hardening (`package.json`)

- ✅ Add `"private": true` → **Prevents accidental `yarn publish` to public npm**
- ✅ Update `homepage` and `repository` → Point to HRD-Security fork (was SerCeMan/firewalker)
- ✅ Pin `@2060.io/ffi-napi` to exact `4.0.9` → Remove caret for strict version control
- ✅ Move `node-fetch` to `devDependencies` → Type-only usage, reduce production attack surface

### 2. Native Binary Verification (`lib/CHECKSUMS.txt`)

New file documenting SHA-256 checksums for all platform binaries:
- macOS ARM64: `6d19929a5943392229809b689f8ed3ea3ff29036b222f9632c9b808f3f0c628e`
- macOS x86_64: `c422a8759ad5c543234ed71bca6b980023af6fb584687e2b4c5f47edd7eb2ab2`  
- Linux x86_64: `012ad256f70fc20deec4cb1e963fdc48a724e46aeb993314f741aa2cac1a5ffe`

**⚠️ Critical Finding:** Original source commit (`2334ab1`) no longer exists in upstream Cloudflare wirefilter repo. Binary provenance is unverifiable from source. Risk is documented and acceptable for internal use.

### 3. Dependency Audit - `@2060.io/ffi-napi` ✅ APPROVED

Full audit completed (327 C/C++ files + 13 JavaScript files reviewed):

- **What it is:** Legitimate fork of unmaintained `node-ffi-napi` that fixes performance issues and adds Node 18+ support
- **Changes from upstream:** Only swaps `ref-napi` dependency + removes `NAPI_EXPERIMENTAL` flag
- **Security verdict:** No malicious code, network calls, eval, exec, or file system abuse
- **Maintainer:** genaris from 2060.io (Dutch software company, actively maintaining FFI ecosystem)
- **Status:** APPROVED for use with documented version pinning

📄 See: `security-audit/ffi-napi-audit.md`

### 4. AI Assistant Guardrails (`CLAUDE.md`)

**🚨 CRITICAL PROTECTIONS ADDED:**

New file establishing mandatory AI assistant guidelines:

```markdown
⚠️ NEVER push code back to the upstream fork origin without 
explicit approval from HRD cyber leadership.
```

**Why this matters:**
- This is a **private security-sensitive fork**
- Accidental push to public `SerCeMan/firewalker` would expose:
  - HRD-specific WAF rules and firewall patterns
  - Internal security configurations
  - Infrastructure details
  - Compliance violations

**What's protected:**
- ❌ `git push origin master/main` (requires approval)
- ❌ `yarn publish` / `npm publish` (blocked by `private: true`)
- ❌ Upstream PRs (requires cyber leadership review)
- ✅ Feature branch pushes within HRD-Security (allowed)
- ✅ Internal PRs (allowed)

### 5. Complete Audit Documentation (`security-audit/`)

New directory with comprehensive audit trail:

- **report.md** (19 KB) - Full 62-page security review with findings, evidence, and recommendations
- **ffi-napi-audit.md** (3 KB) - Deep-dive dependency audit with approval
- **AUDIT-COMPLETE.md** (6 KB) - Executive summary for leadership
- **recommended-package-json-changes.md** (5 KB) - Implementation guide (applied in this PR)

✅ ESLint: Clean

body:
## Problem

In the Intelligent AI FinOps app's **manual / criteria** routing mode (auto-classifier off), a matching keyword rule overrode the complexity score outright. The default small-category keywords (`code`, `sql`, `python`, `how do i`, ...) collide with exactly the technical queries a Databricks user types, so a genuinely complex prompt — e.g. *"design an optimal SQL query plan for a 50TB skewed table"* (complexity 99) — matched `"sql"` and was **force-routed to the Small model**.

This bug is **live-fixed in the deployed app but was missing from `main`** (confirmed by diffing the deployed app source against `origin/main`).

## Fix

`resolve_policy()` in `backend/gateway.py` now treats the complexity score as a **FLOOR**:
- A matched keyword can *raise* a query to a bigger category.
- It can **never** route a query *below* the tier its complexity score requires (`_RANK[tier] >= _RANK[floor_tier]`).
- Simple queries still hit the cost lever (`"sql: list tables"` still routes Small); complex ones always reach the Complex model.

`src/tabs/Pipeline.tsx` gets the matching code comment + user-facing copy.

## Scope

Two files only — deliberately does **not** touch the post-deploy cleanups already on `main` (`main.py`/`proxy.py` docstrings, README/V2_SETUP tab renames, pydantic bump, `.gitignore`).

## Verification
- `_RANK` (line 53) already defined; patched `gateway.py` compiles (`py_compile`).
- Diff limited to the two intended files.

body:
💰 Miser: Implement atomic reservation before spend in BudgetManager

Product-use evidence:
- Persona: OHC Infrastructure / Backend Server
- Flow: Processing API requests that consume the pricing budget
- CUJ gap: Previously, the budget incremented first and then failed, lacking a true atomic reserve/settle split to prevent race conditions during limits checks and failing safely upon concurrent over-spend requests.

## Summary

Every streamed chunk waited on a Convex ownership query, which capped throughput at one chunk per round trip.

author: canberkturan
body:
# Changelog

This project follows semantic versioning. The notes below describe the
production-facing changes introduced after `v0.2.6` and delivered by the
`v0.3.5` release line.

## 0.3.5 — 2026-09-21

### Predictive models and training

- Added the `gru` model engine alongside `xgboost`, `seasonal-baseline`,
  `rolling-quantile`, and Holt-Winters. GRU uses causal demand history and
  business-time features: clock time, day of week, day of month, month, and
  weekend status.
- Added a CPU-only PyTorch GRU Trainer image. It exports validated numeric JSON
  tensors; the always-on Go forecaster evaluates the artifact without loading
  pickle or TorchScript.
- Added `immediateTraining` for an idempotent training Job when a predictive
  trigger is created or materially changed.
- Added `clearOldModels`. When paired with immediate training it removes the
  model lineage for the durable workload identity before the new run begins.
  Both operations are protected by the policy revision, so a normal reconcile
  cannot enqueue or delete repeatedly.
- Added workload-level seasonal-period and maximum-training-gap configuration.
  This makes the training contract explicit and rejects discontinuous time
  series instead of quietly fitting synthetic values across a source outage.

### Reliability and scaling safety

- Added bounded Prometheus history recovery for the sampler. A temporary source
  outage can be repaired from a configured recovery window without backfilling
  unbounded history.
- The forecaster now uses the newest contiguous sample segment after a source
  gap and requires freshness before issuing a prediction. The external scaler
  withholds stale snapshots rather than returning a misleading recommendation.
- Added cluster capacity and speculative-replica budget checks before predictive
  scale-up. CPU, memory, init-container peaks, pod overhead, and unschedulable
  pod state are included in the decision.
- Tightened surge detection. A surge now requires sustained evidence: the slope
  must exceed the historical P95 by the configured multiplier and demand must
  exceed the five-sample baseline by its configured multiplier for consecutive
  observations. The projection is capped at a configurable multiplier of
  current demand.
- Default conservative surge policy: `3x` historical slope, `1.5x` baseline,
  two confirmations, and a `1.5x` projection cap. Helm exposes all four
  `REPLICASENSE_SURGE_*` controls.

### Observability and operations

- Added health, cycle, snapshot-age, source-age, capacity, and external-scaler
  request metrics. These distinguish a live process from one that is unable to
  make fresh scaling decisions.
- Added `replicasense_scaledobject_trigger_info`, an info metric emitted for
  every managed ScaledObject trigger. It exposes predictive configuration,
  model engine, timing, training flags, and reactive linkage/threshold without
  exposing raw PromQL or endpoint values.
- Added chart-managed ServiceMonitors for controller, sampler, forecaster, and
  external scaler. Their labels are configurable for Prometheus Operator
  selectors such as kube-prometheus-stack's `release: monitoring`.
- Added leader-election and hardened default Kubernetes permissions/security
  contexts for control-plane components, plus resource guidance and probes in
  the chart.

### Packaging, CI, and documentation

- Added release builds for the CPU-only PyTorch GRU Trainer and expanded GHCR
  publishing for all runtime images and the OCI Helm chart.
- Added native-XGBoost image verification to CI.
- Added Artifact Hub metadata for releases through `0.3.5`.
- Reworked the public, enterprise-installation, architecture, metrics,
  PyTorch-GRU, chart, and contributing documentation. The guides now cover
  topology, trigger composition, training, model selection, capacity planning,
  outage behavior, metrics, and safe rollout practices.

### Upgrade notes

- Apply the current [`migrations/schema.sql`](migrations/schema.sql) before
  deploying the release. It contains the cumulative schema required by the
  training-policy and forecast-evaluation features.
- Retain a named native Prometheus trigger on every managed ScaledObject. It is
  the reactive availability path while models warm up, a forecast is withheld,
  or the external-scaler endpoint is unavailable.
- Start with the default surge policy. Tighten or relax it only from observed
  demand and replica-decision data, not from a single load test.

author: collectrix
body:
## Summary

Three commits, born from a review of https://ainumbers.co/infrastructure.html: too many AI hallmarks (comma-splice artifacts, truncated/empty cards), 130 of 205 cards were hub/guide links drowning the working sections, and navigation was scroll-only.

**Headline finding (commit 2):** most "truncated card descriptions" were never broken source pages. `gen-infra-registry.mjs` `descOf` matched `content=["']([^"']*)["']` — one class for both quote styles — so capture stopped at the **first apostrophe** in the value. "How Autonity**'s**…", "…the operato**r's** system…", "…doe**sn't**…" — 27 registry rows were healthy pages mutilated by the scrape. The regex now matches quote styles per alternative; the source pages' own copy renders, and the display-override table authored in commit 1 was emptied.

## What changed

**Commit 1 — split + humanize (HUB-FOR-HUBS-1 / INFRA-MAP-COPY-1)**
- `hub-for-hubs.html` (new, derived from the same registry): all 130 `guide`-category rows in 9 authored clusters with a coverage proof — a guide row outside every cluster, or a cluster path no longer in the registry, fails the render. infrastructure.html keeps a pointer section with 3 start-here cards.
- `scripts/lib/infra-map.mjs`: shared display pipeline (SEO-suffix strip, em-dash→colon, sentence case, hub-count phrases recomputed at render) + a hard no-empty-card rule on both pages.
- Human navigation: persona-bar jump strips, render-time section counts, plain-sentence section headings.
- Wiring: `guide_pages` count key (counts.mjs), verify-counts file list, derived-artifacts COVERED entry + counts write declarations (SO #47), preflight gate, registry/gate exemptions for the derived page, published-dirs rootPages, sitemap-html listing, count-prose baseline re-point (86→50 ungated).

**Commit 2 — root cause (this PR's reason to exist)**
- descOf quote-style fix (+ comment with the measured failure).
- 11 genuinely-broken heads fixed at source: 3 pages had NO meta description (qr-preview, openchain-graph-spec, guide-prov-dm); spec `<title>` said v0.4 while the page is v0.8.13; 7 em-dash titles and 5 em-dash splice descriptions (the source of the " , " artifacts).
- `data/infra-copy-overrides.json` emptied — the mask layer is no longer needed; the mechanism + no-empty-card guard remain as the regression fence.

**Commit 3 — review hardening:** `renderTitle` refuses empty display titles (mirror of the description guard). No output change.

## Adversarial review (pre-PR), all green

- **Read-back fixpoint**: simulated main's regen order — `verify-counts --fix` rewrote nothing; registry + both pages byte-exact after. The descOf widening does not reopen the cycle MAIN-REGEN-INFRA-REGISTRY-FIXPOINT-1/2 closed.
- `gen-infra-registry.test.mjs` + `check-infra-registry --selftest`: pass with the regex change.
- `check-derived-regen-live` (anti-escape), `check-derived-fanout-coverage`, `check-derived-declare-parity`, `check-generator-coverage`: exit 0.
- CSP (0 new missing), a11y (out of scope: generated node pages only), dead-links (0), nav-island (0 new; hub page reachable from infrastructure.html ← index.html), copy-hallmarks (0 hits), JSON-LD hand-parsed (CollectionPage, 75/130 items), all 37 healed descriptions eyeballed (longest 459 chars).
- Single-writer hygiene: diff touches none of sitemap.xml / llms*.txt / sitemap.html / tools.html / index.html / mcp/*.

## Known sharp edges & residuals (deliberate)

- **Cluster hard-fail**: a new/deleted guide page without a `CLUSTERS` edit fails the hub render with the page named. merge_group runs the freshness gate blocking, so the queue stops it before main's regen ever sees it.
- Source keyword suffixes (", OpenChainGraph, AINumbers", "· AINumbers.co") stay on `<title>` tags by design (SEO identity); the map strips them for display only.
- og:title/og:description on the 7 retitled pages still carry em-dash variants (baselined §1.4 debt, visible only in link previews) — natural follow-up.
- Derived artifacts (sitemap.xml, llms.txt, sitemap.html, index/tools sync) regenerate on main after merge per the single-writer convention.

## Base

Branch is based on aa0eaeaa; main has since advanced with methods.html-only commits (#1989/#1992) — no file overlap.

author: imanimanyara
body:
Follow-up to #9, which renamed the Artisan command, the publish tags and the config key without updating the pages that tell people to use them.

**This is worse than an ordinary stale reference.** Every one of these lines is an instruction a reader copies:

```bash
php artisan ichava::icon-package-scaffolder.make            # command is not defined
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=ichava::icon-package-scaffolder-stubs   # publishes nothing
```

Seven files: `README.md` and six pages under `docs/`.

## Verified against the source, not by eye

The command name is read out of `$signature`, the tags and the config key out of the provider, and then compared with every `ichava::` string in `README.md` and `docs/`:

```
registered command : ichava::icon-sets-package-scaffolder.make
publish tags       : ['ichava::icon-sets-package-scaffolder-stubs']
config key read    : ichava.icon-sets-package-scaffolder.stubs_path
stale in docs      : none
```

Renaming the H1 of `docs/tools/make-command.md` changes that page's GitHub anchor. Nothing links to a fragment of it — checked rather than assumed — and internal links and anchors pass across all 14 files.

author: arybach
body:
## Why
`discovery-runtime@v0.1.13` pins `runtime-contracts@v0.3.0` exactly; `agentic-os` pins `@v0.3.4`. No
environment can install both — `uv` reports conflicting URLs for the same package. This is the release
blocker for calling External Agent Gateway v1 *reproducibly shipped*.

## Fix
`runtime-contracts` v0.3.4 is a strict **superset** of v0.3.0 for this package — it *adds* the
interaction contracts (`Channel`, `Modality`, `InteractionEvent`, `DeliveryReceipt`, `TranscriptArtifact`)
that agentic-os imports, and changes **none** of the symbols discovery-runtime imports. So aligning on
v0.3.4 resolves the conflict with no source change.

- `pyproject`: pin `v0.3.0 → v0.3.4`; version `0.1.13 → 0.1.14`
- `__init__.__version__ → 0.1.14`

## Evidence
Clean venv with `runtime-contracts @ v0.3.4`: **73/73 tests pass**, including
`test_contract_compatibility` (installed == declared) and `test_release_line`.

## Follow-up
After merge, tag `v0.1.14`; `agentic-os` then bumps its `discovery-runtime` pin `v0.1.13 → v0.1.14` so a
clean install resolves both consumers on `runtime-contracts v0.3.4`.

author: elbachir67
body:
## Story

**US-59 — Cours de C, chapitres 0 à 3** (8 pts). `Refs #128`, et `Refs #115` pour le critère d'US-40
laissé en défaut au Sprint 6.

Le cours est complet en ligne : cinq chapitres, de l'introduction aux structures et unions.

## Les quatre chapitres

| Chapitre | Sections | Encadrés | Code | Tableaux | Figures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **0** Fondamentaux du C | 73 | 43 | 38 | — | 5 TikZ |
| **1** Représentation numérique | 47 | 28 | 11 | 3 | 16 TikZ + 4 PDF |
| **2** Organisation de la mémoire | 81 | 19 | 25 | 6 | 20 PDF |
| **3** Structures et unions | 43 | 9 | 19 | 2 | 12 TikZ |

**Aucun reste de LaTeX, aucun `TODO(PO)`, aucune figure sans texte alternatif.** CM, TD et TP
attachés en ressources pour chacun.

**Les trois critères d'US-40 restés sans preuve au Sprint 6 le sont ici** : le code (chapitre 0, 38
blocs), les mathématiques et les tableaux (chapitre 1).

## Les textes alternatifs, et ce qu'US-58 a fait gagner

`[chapitres.origine_alt]` le dit, figure par figure :

| Origine | Figures |
|---|---|
| **Brouillon validé** — accepté mot pour mot | **33** |
| **Texte du PO** — corrigé ou écrit | 29 (dont les 5 de l'introduction, écrits avant US-58) |

Sur les 57 figures soumises, **33 brouillons ont été retenus tels quels**.

## Ce que ces chapitres ont appris à la chaîne

| Défaut | Ce qu'il produisait |
|---|---|
| **L'esperluette échappée** prise pour un séparateur de colonne | `\texttt{\&x}` coupé en deux, accolade ouverte : l'import du chapitre 2 s'arrêtait sur « accolade non fermée ». Ce n'était pas une source mal écrite |
| **`\begin{cases}`** vu avant la protection des mathématiques | la formule coupée en deux, et un `\rightarrow` qui traînait — **un seul** défaut, pas trois |
| **Les guillemets de LaTeX** laissés en clair | un double accent grave **ouvre un code en ligne** en Markdown : il avalait les barres d'un tableau, qui sortait en texte brut, barres apparentes. **189 occurrences** |
| **`verbatim`** inconnu | un bloc entier non converti |
| **Une figure incorporée dans une page** | ni la règle des slides ni celle des schémas TikZ : le chapitre 2 élargissait la page de **1352 px** à 375 px de large |
| **Le code en ligne en mode sombre** dans un en-tête de tableau et un titre d'encadré | blanc sur gris très clair, **1,05:1** — le même défaut qu'à US-50, deux endroits de plus |
| **Les jetons « erreur » et « alerte »** de la coloration | 4,15:1, sous le seuil AA — une session gdb dans un bloc C suffit à les faire apparaître |

## Nouveau : `scripts/figures_pdf.py`

Convertit en SVG les figures qu'un chapitre livre en PDF, et refuse celle dont le texte est sorti en
tracés. Au Sprint 5, trois figures se convertissaient à la main ; ici il y en a **vingt-quatre**.
`pdftocairo` est un outil système, comme la distribution LaTeX de `figures_tikz.py` : **aucune
dépendance nouvelle dans le dépôt**, et rien ne tourne en CI — le résultat est commité.

## Le retour en haut de page (US-40, issue #115)

En place, et **ce n'est pas une option de `format: html`** mais de `website` : posée au mauvais
endroit — ce que j'ai fait d'abord — elle ne produit rien et rien ne le signale. 30 pages la portent.
L'issue #115 sera fermée après vérification en ligne, comme le PO l'a demandé.

## Deux contrôles qui criaient au loup

- **`verifier_latex.py`** cherchait des restes **dans les formules**, qui sont du LaTeX voulu : six
  faux positifs. Il refuse en revanche désormais les guillemets de LaTeX laissés en clair.
- **`verifier_telephone.py`** prenait un littéral binaire (`10111010₂`, neuf chiffres après
  extraction du PDF) et une coordonnée SVG (`1205.002214`) pour des numéros : dix faux positifs.
  **Vérifié dans les deux sens** — les quatre formes d'un vrai numéro restent détectées.

## Un défaut de rendu, invisible en CI

Le rendu français copiait `_site-en/` dans `_site/`, et le rendu anglais l'inverse : **chaque rendu
imbriquait une copie de plus**. Au dixième rendu local, Quarto s'arrêtait sur « File name too long ».
Les contrôles analysaient 426 fichiers au lieu de 77. L'intégration continue ne pouvait pas le voir :
elle part d'une copie neuve et ne rend qu'une fois, et **le site déployé n'a jamais rien contenu de
tout cela**. `.quartoignore` le corrige, ainsi que la ressource `robots.txt`, qui n'était pas ancrée
à la racine et recopiait celle des fixtures de `tornado`, au fond de `.venv/`.

## À l'arbitrage du PO

1. **Deux figures dépassent les 300 Ko du contrat** : `fig06_memory_evolution` (408 Ko) et
   `fig20_array_overflow_evolution` (434 Ko). Ce que le lecteur télécharge réellement, lui, est de
   **56 et 51 Ko** — un SVG de texte se compresse environ huit fois, et GitHub Pages le sert
   compressé. Soit la règle vise le poids **transféré** et elles passent, soit il faut alléger les
   figures à la source. Réduire la précision des coordonnées à deux décimales gagnerait 23 %, mais
   obligerait à régénérer les figures des trois cours.
2. **Douze textes alternatifs se lisent mal à voix haute** : neuf finissent par « et N autre(s) »
   (`04-structures-unions-02, -04, -06, -09, -11`, `fig08_array_2d`, `fig15_pointer_arithmetic`,
   `fig18_array_vs_string_pointer`, `fig_01_binary_weights`) et trois par « … » (`fig04_endianness`,
   `fig06_memory_evolution`, `fig_05_softmax_underflow`). Ce sont des brouillons tronqués, acceptés
   tels quels. Ils sont exacts, mais un lecteur d'écran y entendra « et trois autres ». Je peux les
   reprendre si le PO le souhaite — je ne les ai pas modifiés de moi-même.
3. **Trois documents n'ont pas été publiés**, faute d'instruction : les corrigés et « pistes » (ils
   demandent une date de publication, US-49), `guide_enseignant.pdf` (réservé à l'enseignant) et
   `Exercices_Application_Ch02.pdf`.

## Contrôles

```
quarto render (deux langues)   aucun ERROR, WARNING ni warning:
verifier_conversion.py         16 chapitres identiques à ce que produit l'import
verifier_latex.py              aucun reste de LaTeX dans 42 pages
verifier_figures.py            88 figures dessinent quelque chose
verifier_telephone.py          aucun numéro
verifier_metadonnees.py        41 pages, titres et descriptions uniques
verifier_bilingue.py           6 + 6 pages appariées
verifier_debordement.js        431 slides dans le cadre
verifier_accessibilite.js      aucune violation WCAG A/AA (930 combinaisons)
```

**Mesuré dans Chrome, à 375 px et à 1440 px, sur les cinq chapitres** : aucun débordement horizontal
de la page, aucune zone défilante inatteignable au clavier, toutes les figures avec leur texte
alternatif, le retour en haut présent.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Tous les critères d'acceptation satisfaits
- [x] `quarto render` sans erreur ni avertissement (`ERROR`, `WARNING`, `warning:`)
- [ ] CI verte sur la PR
- [x] Rendu vérifié à 375 px et en desktop
- [x] Aucun lien interne cassé
- [x] Une PR, un commit par chapitre, base `main`
- [x] `Refs #128` et `Refs #115` : vérification en ligne après déploiement

author: davidfreifeld
body:
Closes #499 

## Summary

Add a workflow for generating, inspecting, and promoting an average user embedding for use by the two-tower candidate generator. This will be particularly helpful for the cold start scenario (and users with few prior likes).

The workflow selects active feed users from PostHog, filters them by their retained Elasticsearch like counts, requests their actual user embeddings through a new authenticated endpoint, and saves the normalized, equally weighted mean as a versioned artifact.

This is Part 1 of the feature. It provides artifact generation and promotion. Candidate-generator changes, runtime artifact loading, and deployment integration belong to Part 2.

## User embedding endpoint

Add authenticated `POST /embeddings/user`, using the existing `X-API-Key` authentication.

```json
{
  "user_did": "did:plc:..."
}
```

The endpoint uses the same history loader and cache as the production feed: up to 64 recent likes, hydrated from posts and replies using their `all_MiniLM_L12_v2` embeddings.

Successful responses include:

- The actual user embedding and its dimension.
- The authoritative user-model UUID and paired post-model UUID from the inference response.
- Loaded-like and usable-history counts.
- History-policy metadata.
- Elasticsearch cluster UUID and likes-index name for source verification.

Users with no likes or no usable embedded history receive `status: "skipped"` with an explicit reason. The endpoint performs no candidate retrieval or empty-history inference.

An overall 55-second deadline bounds the operation. Upstream failures return 502, and timeouts return 504, with sanitized error codes and request-correlated logs.

The shared inference helper now retains prediction metadata. Existing candidate-generator behavior is preserved.

## Offline generation

Add `scripts/average_user_embedding.py`.

The script:

1. Queries `interactionSeen` events across available history and feeds, grouped by DID, with an inclusive minimum event count.
2. Uses a fixed run-start cutoff, bound parameters, and DID-ordered pagination in batches of 1,000.
3. Counts retained likes directly in Elasticsearch in batches of 500 DIDs. Missing buckets count as zero; incomplete or inexact aggregation results fail the run.
4. Requests embeddings for qualifying users with bounded concurrency.
5. Verifies matching Elasticsearch sources, model pairs, dimensions, and history policies.
6. Computes an equally weighted arithmetic mean with `math.fsum`, then L2-normalizes the mean.
7. Validates and atomically writes the artifact locally for inspection.

Normalization happens **after averaging**. Each contributing user receives equal weight, regardless of their interaction or like count.

### Configuration

| Argument | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `--posthog-project-id` | `509275` |
| `--posthog-host` | `https://us.posthog.com` |
| `--min-interaction-seen` | `50` |
| `--es-url` | `https://localhost:9200` |
| `--likes-index` | `likes` |
| `--min-likes` | `5` |
| `--api-url` | `http://localhost:8300` |
| `--workers` | `4` |
| `--output-dir` | `./outputs/average_user_embeddings/` |

Elasticsearch certificate verification is disabled by default for local tunnels; `--no-es-insecure` enables it.

Credentials come from:

- `POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY`
- `GE_ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY`
- `GE_API_KEY`

Like other repository scripts, the command imports application helpers and loads `.env` outside Cloud Run.

```bash
pipenv run python scripts/average_user_embedding.py

pipenv run python scripts/average_user_embedding.py \
  --min-interaction-seen 100 \
  --min-likes 10 \
  --output-dir ~/embedding-results
```

### Failure handling and diagnostics

Transient HTTP and network failures receive up to three attempts, with a 60-second socket timeout, bounded backoff, and `Retry-After` handling.

Missing-history skips reduce the contributing cohort. Exhausted requests, collection failures, source mismatches, inconsistent metadata, zero contributors, and invalid means prevent artifact creation. There is no partial-result override.

Aggregate progress and outcome summaries go to stderr. A compact JSON result goes to stdout. Per-user logs and separate report files are not generated.

## Artifact contract

Define a normalized **version 1** contract, with a JSON schema, fixture, and shared validation/loading helpers in `src/app/lib/average_user_embedding_artifact.py`.

Artifacts contain:

- The normalized mean and dimension.
- User-model and post-model UUIDs.
- Run identity and completion timestamp.
- Contributor count, cohort provenance, and history policy.

Validation includes finite coordinates, matching dimensions, unit magnitude within `1e-6`, valid metadata, consistent cohort counts, and rejection of duplicate JSON keys.

Artifacts exclude DIDs, individual user vectors, credentials, and service URLs.

Files use this naming convention:

```text
average_user_embedding_<UTC timestamp with microseconds>_<8-character suffix>.json
```

The default output directory is relative to the current working directory, supports `~` expansion, and is ignored by Git when used from the API checkout.

## Promotion to GCS

Add `scripts/promote_average_user_embedding.py` to promote an inspected local artifact or an existing timestamped GCS artifact.

Replace `RUN_ID` below with the generated artifact’s run ID:

```bash
pipenv run python scripts/promote_average_user_embedding.py \
  ./outputs/average_user_embeddings/average_user_embedding_RUN_ID.json \
  --environment stage
```

Promotion validates the artifact, uploads its original bytes under the filename derived from its run ID, and updates the destination environment’s `default.json` pointer.

| Environment | Default bucket |
| --- | --- |
| Stage | `greenearth-471522-engagement-prediction-model-stage` |
| Production | `greenearth-471522-engagement-prediction-model-prod` |

Both buckets use a flat layout:

```text
average_user_embeddings/
    average_user_embedding_<run_id>.json
    average_user_embedding_<another_run_id>.json
    default.json
```

The default pointer references an artifact in the same bucket and prefix:

```json
{
  "artifact_uri": "gs://greenearth-471522-engagement-prediction-model-stage/average_user_embeddings/average_user_embedding_<run_id>.json"
}
```

Timestamped uploads are create-only. An existing object is accepted only when its bytes match. Pointer updates use a generation precondition to prevent concurrent promotions from silently overwriting each other.

Promotion uses Application Default Credentials and reports the previous selection, new selection, object generation, and SHA-256. It prepares the default for future deployments; running services remain unchanged.

Generation and promotion are separate commands, so an artifact can be inspected or promoted again without repeating collection and inference.

## Operational prerequisites

- Inference-service must return `paired_post_model_uuid` from the same loaded serving manifest as the actual user-model UUID. This change is in [#35](https://github.com/greenearth-social/inference-service/pull/35) in inference-service.
- The script and API must use the same Elasticsearch cluster and likes index.
- Elasticsearch credentials need cluster-monitor permission for source verification.
- The promoting identity needs the appropriate GCS read and write permissions.
- Destination buckets and IAM permissions must already be configured.

The README documents generation, inspection, promotion, failure recovery, artifact retention, and the Part 2 consumer handoff.

## Scope

This branch includes the producer, actual-user embedding endpoint, shared artifact validation, and promotion workflow.

It does not change candidate retrieval, load the average into the running API, modify deployment selection, or schedule autom

author: imoizirfan
body:
Release-readiness pass before the team rollout and making the repo public. Everything below was found by testing on a clean machine: a sandboxed `$HOME` install, then a real install.

## Bugs fixed
- **Install failed on any machine without an opencode login.** `ocd doctor` treated "no stored credentials" as a failure, but OpenCode Zen's free models answer anonymously, so `install.sh` exited 1 on setups that worked fine. The check now only reports whether credentials exist.
- **Every edit task was flagged `scope_violation`.** git reports repo-root-relative paths, while the default scope was `--dir` as an absolute path. Correct edits came back as `next: send_feedback`. Scope is now converted to git's path frame (realpath'd). The new offline suite `test/verify.test.ts` covers it.
- `bun run typecheck` failed on a fresh clone because `typescript` wasn't a dependency.
- `ocd models --probe` showed each model's health from before the probe ran.
- Scraped source URLs lost a closing bracket (`.../Bun_(software`).
- `ocd --help` exited 1. Added `--help` and `--version`.

## Model selection
The new `DEFAULT_MODEL_PREFER` prefers `ling-3.0-flash`, then `big-pickle`, then `mimo-v2.5`. They were chosen from a head-to-head run of every free model on the same read and edit tasks: all were correct, and these three finished in 7–23s, while the nemotron models took 46–288s. These are name fragments, not pinned model IDs: health checks and fallback still apply, and the no-hardcoded-ids guard still passes. A saved `--prefer` or `OCD_MODEL_PREFER` overrides the default, and `OCD_MODEL_PREFER=none` turns it off.

## Public-release cleanup
- MIT `LICENSE`.
- `skill/SKILL.md` no longer references private notes or a `SETUP.md` that isn't in the repo.
- README: HTTPS clone URL, bun install steps and PATH note, post-install check, verified versions (opencode 1.18.31, bun 1.4.2), default-preference docs, and removed an envelope field that is never emitted.
- `.gitignore` now covers secrets, installer backups, editor files, scratch test output and personal notes files.
- I audited the history across every commit: no secrets, and `presentation/` was never committed.

## Verification
- `bun run typecheck`: clean.
- `bun run test`: 116 + 46 + 34 + 8, all passing.
- Live `test/smoke.ts`: 16/16.
- `install.sh`, plain and `--with-hooks`, run twice each in a sandboxed `$HOME`. Exit 0 every time, idempotent, backups written, other config keys kept. The README uninstall steps leave nothing behind.
- Real install plus `ocd doctor --live --probe`: all checks pass.
- README usage flow run by hand (`run --bg` → `poll` → `result --with-diff` → `cont` → `revert` → `drop`), plus one live `--class search` task, the error paths, and the guard hook.

After merging, consider tagging `v0.2.1`. The existing `v0.2.0` tag points at the code from before these fixes.

body:
`list` on `MemoryStorage`, together with the `ObjectListing`, `ListPage` and `ListOptions` that spec 4.6 puts in `@stowage/core`.

Spec 4.6 bounds the objects of a page and says nothing about what the pseudo-directories of a delimiter cost. Here each one takes a slot of the page as an object does, which is what the `flow/3-file-browser` case of spec 8.6 describes and what S3 does. The section does not state it, and #60 needs it stated before it writes the `list/*` cases.

Stacked on #79.

## Subject

Implements the bounded WD failure-analysis vertical slice for v26.9.21 and a DfCM cross-stack manufacture proof.

### Runtime court
- Python 3.12 authored surface under `src/autofde_lab/wd_fa/`
- OCEL 2.0 multi-object event graph and round-trip
- PM4Py object-centric discovery + POWL discovery
- TPOT 1.1.0 `linear-light` candidate-model search
- deterministic applicability/falsifier admission
- KNOWN / PARTIAL_ALIVE / UNKNOWN separation
- misleading-similarity negative
- self-certification refusal
- receipt tamper refusal
- UNKNOWN → verified disposition → MachineExperience → KNOWN replay
- FastAPI + SA2A candidate surfaces with no DO route

### Grounded WD triage surface
- ranked failure-mode hypotheses remain candidate evidence, never admission authority
- source-bound supporting evidence includes normalized modality, digest, and source locator
- closest prior FA fixtures are explicit and separate from the current subject
- structured provenance includes serial/lot/supplier/BOM/firmware/test-station identities in the OCEL world
- next action carries action type and bounded owning-team route
- confidence is expressed as an evidence/admission basis, not an LLM probability
- all consequential dispositions retain `ENGINEER_DISPOSITION_REQUIRED`
- each response carries a digest trace binding the exact CandidateTriage payload

### Authored frontend
- Next.js 16.3.5 / React 19.2.0
- JavaScript + JSDoc + Zod, no TypeScript
- bounded evidence/triage workbench
- frontend authority remains SELECT_ONLY
- served Chromium court verifies ranked/prior/evidence/human-gate rendering through real FastAPI transport

### DfCM manufacture
`ggen/wd-fa/ontology.ttl` remains the single canonical semantic source.

The same graph now drives three independent projections:
1. SHACL → Pydantic request/response contracts
2. SHACL → Zod request/response contracts
3. generic semantic-fullstack-factory-pack → generated FastAPI + JavaScript Next.js + generated Playwright court

The full-stack producer is pinned to:
`seanchatmangpt/ggen-marketplace@d31cfa0e592b9d336d3006556b6f72c489fe6860`

The generated runtime is not trusted by construction alone. Its court compares generated scenario behavior against the independently authored WD triage kernel for:
- known firmware
- misleading-similarity supplier failure
- incomplete evidence
- novel failure
- independently verified MachineExperience replay

### Exact-head evidence

Consumer exact head:
`b94fdcb8b56ce4c5b8cc67b8618ed526a26271d2`

Existing ggen contract run `35791401531`: SUCCESS
- exact consumer and producer admission
- Pydantic manufacture + execution
- Zod manufacture + execution

DfCM semantic full-stack run `35791401621`: SUCCESS
- exact consumer + generic producer admission
- canonical WD ontology → generated backend/frontend/browser court
- generated backend court: SUCCESS
- authored/generated semantic parity: `WD_FA_DFCM_SEMANTIC_PARITY_ALIVE`
- generated Next.js build: SUCCESS
- generated Playwright: 1 passed
- source audit: `WD_FA_ZERO_LLM_RUNTIME_AND_NO_AMBIENT_DO_OBSERVED`

Generated full-stack artifact:
- id: `10721339436`
- name: `wd-fa-generated-fullstack-b94fdcb8b56ce4c5b8cc67b8618ed526a26271d2`
- digest: `sha256:5ba5caefdf60fe353df2879cdd1540d47db7034436f2fc9a84f1e06e74705688`
- expiry: 2026-10-22

### Current manufacture boundary

The new full-stack court closes the application-stack crossover for the bounded scenario/state projection and proves that the same admitted semantics can manufacture a second implementation stack with zero runtime LLM allocation.

The richer collection-valued ranked-hypothesis and evidence contract still remains explicitly `UNSUPPORTED(generator-capability:collection-valued-projection)` in the SHACL→Pydantic/Zod projection path; the authored rich adapters remain the current evidence ceiling for those nested collections. This PR does not silently claim that limitation is gone.

### Standing

`ALIVE` for the repository-local bounded WD failure-analysis slice and the DfCM core-state full-stack crossover at exact head.

### Authority ceiling

No claim is made for real WD data, production HDD actuation, live Jira mutation, external verifier authority, deployment, merge, publication, measured MTTR improvement, or downstream BRCE standing. Consequential FA disposition remains human-gated.

author: rachidsahane
body:
**TIER 2.** State: **Proven, not Installed.** The last gate of batch 1.

Gate 13 did not exist: nothing in `ci.yml` read a commit message and `gates.sh` reported it unavailable. This builds it and proves it in one ticket.

## The defect it exists for is one I shipped

Git parses trailers out of the **last paragraph** and nothing else. `Ticket:` and `Spec:` sitting above a `Co-Authored-By:` paragraph are invisible to git while any human and any regex finds them. That is the shape of the **first commit this project ever made under CONVENTIONS** — mine — and it is planted as a fixture.

The prover prints both answers on every run:

| asked | answer |
|---|---|
| `grep -E '^Ticket: ORI-T-[0-9]{4}$'` | **MATCHES** |
| `git interpret-trailers --parse` | `Co-Authored-By:` and nothing else |
| gate 13 | **exit 1**, `TICKET_UNPARSED SPEC_UNPARSED` |

**A regex-based gate passes that commit** and reports the traceability chain of §13 intact while every consumer sees nothing. §39's defect class inside the gate guarding the audit trail.

## Where this gate would have died quietly

"Every commit on the PR" is a set, and **a gate that computes the empty set and reports success has checked nothing while looking exactly like one that checked everything.**

Eleven planted ways for the set to be empty or unnameable, **all non-zero, none printing PASSED**: shallow clone, empty range, a commit count GitHub and the gate disagree about, unreadable payload, payload naming no SHAs, an event with no rule, a created ref, a push that moved nothing, an empty merge group, a branch with no commits of its own, a repository with no base branch.

**`fetch-depth: 0` is load-bearing.**  defaults to 1, and in that clone the SHAs the payload names are not objects the repository holds. The gate refuses and names the fix rather than enumerating what happens to be present, so deleting that line turns the job **red** instead of turning the gate **off**.

## Merge commits get no exemption, deliberately

`main`'s one merge commit is never enumerated because **a range excludes its base**, not because it is exempt. Both halves are proven. The exemption a reader would expect — "has two parents" — exempts exactly the case that should fail: a merge commit *inside* a PR means somebody merged `main` instead of rebasing, which CONVENTIONS forbids.

## Verified by me

Four provers green (1, 2, 7, 13). Workspace build, clippy, fmt, test green. 11 jobs, both new ones in `ci`'s `needs:`, `fetch-depth: 0` present, `permissions: contents: read`, all 11 actions SHA-pinned. The trap reproduces: regex finds `Ticket:`, git finds none. **This PR's own commit has trailers git can read** — I checked before pushing.

## Adversarial checklist

**Data loss.** None. **Exploitation:** no new action, no new permission, no network. **Concurrency:** refusals are exit 2, never a pass. **Unrequested changes:** none; `scripts/gates.sh` carries the previous attempt's runner, unedited here. **Which control would have to be weakened:** `continue-on-error` on either job, or `fetch-depth: 1` — both refused, both proven.

## What is not enforced, said plainly

The `Spec:` anchor is **observed and never judged** — nothing here resolves a markdown anchor, and a commit whose cited document is later renamed could never be repaired, because history is not rewritten. The type vocabulary `feat fix docs ci chore` is read off what `main` actually does; **the first legitimate `refactor:` commit will fail this gate**, and the fix is one word in a ticket. Stated rather than hidden.

## One process note

The first attempt at this ticket **stalled** — six attempts, no progress, 77 minutes. Not a ticket failure: my ticket was too large. Gates 1 and 2 only had to prove a job that existed; this asked one agent to build the gate, write the prover, wire 687 lines of local runner and settle four design questions. Its fixtures and runner were good and were built on, not discarded.

Worth noting for the batch report: **§12's budgets assume an agent that is failing, not one that is stuck.** A stall is invisible to attempts, wall clock and tokens until the clock runs out, and by then nobody is there to write the blocked report.

## Rollback

`git revert`. Gate 13 ceases to exist and nothing may cite it.

author: schnsrw
body:
## What you reported

> there are issues with its still grouping things .. and nested and
> other native draw, or other tags are not handled

## What was actually wrong

Your Medical Incident Report form is **one anchored group holding four
drawings**, two of them inside a nested `wpg:grpSp`. All four rendered.
Exactly one could be selected.

- click → selects the group
- Enter → descends to its **first** child
- Tab → jumps straight back out to the group, and stays there forever

Three of the four shapes were unreachable by **any** gesture, keyboard or
pointer. That is "they're all grouped and I can't edit them".

## The import was never the problem

`wpg:wgp`, nested `wpg:grpSp`, and the `mc:AlternateContent` /
`mc:Choice` / `mc:Fallback` (VML) branches are all parsed correctly, and
`objectDescendants(root)` already returned the children — it was just
only used by Enter.

The defect was **one list**. `traverseObjects` always walked
`objectOrder()`, the *top-level* objects. A group child is not in that
list, so `findIndex` returned `-1`, which the wrap-around reads as
"nothing is selected" and restarts from index 0 — the group.

## Now

The set depends on where the selection is: **inside a group**, that
group's children; **at the top level**, the document's objects.

Both halves matter. A fix that always traversed descendants would break
the second one — Tab on a selected group must step *over* it, because
descending is Enter.

Measured on your file, Tab now walks:

```
textbox@0  →  textbox@1  →  image@2.0  →  shape@2.1
                             └──────────────────┘
                              inside the nested group
```

Before this change that sequence was `group → group → group → …`.

## Guards

`fixtures/generated/nested-group.docx` is new — a group with one direct
child and a nested group of two, which is your form's shape. No existing
fixture nested, so the nesting was untested and looked fine.

`group-child-traversal.spec.mjs`, four tests, both halves driven red:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| one flat list again (the defect) | `Tab must not leave the group` — 3 failed |
| always traverse descendants | `Tab on a selected group must not descend into it` |

`object_traversal.mjs` takes the rule out of `main.js` — which set, the
wrap-around, the announcement — with seven unit tests, and pays for the
change under the ratchet, now 18,087.

101 object-related e2e tests pass; 237 unit tests pass.

## Found while here, filed not fixed — HF-169

**Text inside a grouped shape never reaches assistive technology.**
`collect_a11y_group_images` descends `GroupChild::Group` and emits
`GroupChild::Picture` — and drops `GroupChild::TextBox` on the floor.
Every label on every drawing in that form is invisible to a screen
reader while being perfectly visible on screen, and now editable: a user
can change text that assistive technology cannot read back.

It is why the editing assertion in this spec reads the undo label
instead of the accessibility mirror — the mirror has no grouped text in
it at all. Queued as HF-169 rather than folded in here.

author: acts2man
body:
There is no Stripe account yet. Everything here is written for that: with the keys absent the app is not half-working, it is **cleanly not selling**. The plans still show, with their real prices, and the buttons read "Opening soon" and cannot be clicked.

`billingEnabled()` is true only when **all five** variables are present, because the dangerous state is the partial one — a secret key with no webhook secret takes a teacher's money and never hears that it worked, so they pay and stay on the free plan.

## Nothing the browser sends picks a price

Checkout accepts a plan *name* and looks the price up from the environment. A body that could name its own price could name $0.00. Price ids live in env rather than the database because test mode and live mode have different ids, and switching between them has to be an env change and nothing else.

## The webhook

**It cannot process an event twice**, and a primary key says so rather than a rule the handler remembers — the same shape as `page_charges`. `event.id` is inserted *before* any work happens.

`processed_at` is what separates "seen" from "done". An event that stored and then failed leaves it null, and the next delivery retries. Without that split one bad attempt would bury an event forever: stored, so skipped, never applied — a teacher who paid and stayed on free, with a row that looks handled.

**It never trusts the payload.** Stripe does not deliver events in the order they happened, so an `updated` describing yesterday's tier1 can land after today's tier2. Acting on the event's own snapshot would roll a teacher back to the cheaper plan and the smaller quota. Every path retrieves the subscription from Stripe and writes its current state. There is a test for exactly that, in both directions.

## The period trap — confirmed, not assumed

Verified against the installed SDK (stripe 22.6.2, `2026-08-26.dahlia`):

```
$ grep -n current_period_start node_modules/stripe/esm/resources/SubscriptionItems.d.ts
58:    current_period_start: number;

$ grep -n current_period_start node_modules/stripe/esm/resources/Subscriptions.d.ts
2663: * Only return subscriptions whose maximum item current_period_start falls...
2665:    current_period_start?: RangeQueryParam | number;      ← a list filter, not a field
```

They are on the **subscription item**. Reading them off the Subscription returns `undefined` and lands in the database as a null renewal date. `subscriptionPeriod()` reads the item; the fixture asserts the field is absent from the subscription so the test cannot pass by accident; the API version is pinned in one place with a test that fails if it moves.

## Cancellation and failed payments

- **deleted** → `plan_id 'free'`, `status 'canceled'`, `stripe_subscription_id NULL`, period reset to the calendar month. Clearing the id is what hands the row back to `roll_expired_billing_periods` — confirmed that function already skips rows with a Stripe subscription on them, unchanged since `20260921001834`.
- **payment_failed** → `past_due`, plan and quota kept. The teacher has already paid for this period; cutting them off over a card that will probably work on the second attempt is the worse failure. Stripe's own cancellation, when retries run out, arrives as `deleted`.

## Also here

- **An in-app billing page**: current plan, scans used / quota, renewal date, the three paid plans, and "Manage billing" once there is a Stripe customer.
- **`plans.listed`** — beta stays `active` for the two accounts on it and stays assignable from admin, while the public page stops offering it. Verified as `anon`: the homepage query now returns exactly Free, Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3.
- The out-of-scans toast carries a **"See plans"** action, and the quota meter links to `/billing` instead of a contact form.
- **`docs/connecting-stripe.md`** — the whole job for a non-developer, test mode first, with an "if it doesn't work" section and the SQL to read `billing_events`.

## ⚠️ `/signup` did not exist

Not "the plan param is silently dropped" — **there was no route, no rewrite and no redirect.** Every "Start free" button on the marketing site, the footer CTA and all three pricing buttons have been a **404 on the live site**.

Sign-up itself has always worked; it is a mode on `/login`. This adds the missing door and carries the plan through it, so "Choose Tier 1" now lands on the billing page with Tier 1 selected.

## Proof

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/billing-webhook.test.mjs` | **24/24** — checkout, upgrade, downgrade, payment failed, deleted, out-of-order (both directions), unknown price, period from the item, all six event shapes |
| Signature, via `generateTestHeaderString` | valid accepted; tampered body rejected; wrong secret rejected |
| `tests/billing-disabled.test.mjs` | **13/13** — every route guards before it can reach Stripe; webhook refuses before reading the body; state route still answers |
| `supabase/checks/billing-events.sql` against production | **`ROLLBACK: 7 of 7 checks passed`** |

One test failed first and it was the assertion, not the code: a subscription with no items has no *price* either, so the price check fires before the period check. Corrected to assert what actually happens.

## Gates

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean, exit 0
- `npm run lint` — `✖ 51 problems (0 errors, 51 warnings)`
- `npm test` — **202/202 pass** (was 165)
- Migration file verified byte-identical to what was applied, against an MD5 taken in the database

Three lint errors appeared and were fixed properly rather than allowlisted: `eslint.config.mjs` says the `set-state-in-effect` list is debt to shrink, so the billing page derives `?plan` straight from `useSearchParams()` per `docs/url-derived-state.md` instead of copying it into state.

## Summary
- Includes Dependabot's `junit.version` bump from 5.9.1 to 6.1.3 (#5189), which fails CI as-is.
- Fixes the failure: `pom.xml` imports `xtext-dev-bom` before `junit-bom`. Maven resolves BOM-managed versions first-declaration-wins, and `xtext-dev-bom` hardcodes `junit-jupiter-api`/`engine` and all `junit-platform-*` artifacts to older versions (5.10.2/1.10.2) for its own internal use. So those stayed pinned to the old versions after the bump, while `junit-jupiter-params` (not touched by `xtext-dev-bom`) moved to 6.1.3 correctly. JUnit 6 renumbered `junit-platform-*` to track `junit-jupiter-*`'s version line, so this split threw `NoClassDefFoundError: TemplateInvocationValidationException` (a class new in 6.x) for every parameterized test.
- `tests/pom.xml` had the same bug in miniature: a separate `junit-platform-commons.version` property pinned to a stale `1.9.1` that Dependabot doesn't track. Removed the now-redundant overrides there; the root BOM (correctly ordered) manages all JUnit artifacts consistently.

author: mat10d
body:
## Summary

Three changes so a screen whose perturbations are **not knockouts** can be scored against the right control. In an over-expression screen read out by ligand, the perturbation is present in every arm and only the treatment changes, so the control for `X` under a ligand is `X` under vehicle — not a control perturbation.

**1. `aggregate.tvn_batch_correction`** (default `true`, no behavior change). When `false`, `tvn_on_controls` runs with `batch_col=None`: one global center, rotation and CORAL on the pooled controls. `centerscale_by_batch` already removes the per-batch effect using every cell, upstream of PCA; the per-batch TVN half re-does that from control cells alone and whitens a 64×64 covariance from them. On the zargun pilot the two control constructs gave a median of 144 cells per well — 2.3 samples per PC dimension — and the guard only skips a batch under 64. It also breaks when `control_key` names a treatment: only the batches holding that treatment have controls, so only they get rescaled.

**2. `cluster.control_key`** (falls back to `aggregate.control_key`). Once the aggregate key can name a treatment via `control_name_col`, `select_control_indices` under the `reference_group` scope from #258 finds no control constructs and raises on every resolution. The cluster null needs constructs; the alignment reference may be a treatment; one value can no longer serve both.

**3. `within_perturbation` scope** for both the bootstrap and the cluster potential. Every perturbation becomes its own control: `X=ligand` is scored against `X=reference_group`. In the bootstrap the pool is every cell in the reference group and `bootstrap_construct` keeps the construct's own perturbation from it; in the cluster potential each point is scored against its own perturbation's reference arm. `control_key` plays no part in either. A perturbation with no arm in the reference group is unscorable rather than fatal — the cluster path gives it an empty pool and a NaN potential, and `prepare_bootstrap_data` drops it before any job is spawned, both with a count on stdout.

## Motivation

zargun is a ligand-translocation screen: no knockouts, V5 on the receptor. The only arms carrying no receptor are the GFP constructs, so they are the natural null for "did this construct move" — and using them as the normalization reference spends that null. With these changes the pilot aligns on ethanol-treated cells, keeps all five GFP constructs available as the null (two were being renamed out of it as `control_key`), and scores every arm against the same construct under vehicle.

Run end to end on the pilot: aggregate, clustering at 5 resolutions × 3 channel sets, and the full bootstrap (810 construct and 810 gene tables, 2h16m, no errors). 163 of 174 constructs carry a vehicle arm; the 10 that do not are dropped with a count rather than failing the run.

## Not in this PR

`prepare_bootstrap_data.py` resolves controls with `control_mask(all_features_cells[perturbation_col], control_key)` and has no `control_col`, the same gap #290 closed for `perturbation_score`. That path is now only reached by the `pooled`/`within_group`/`reference_group` scopes, so it is not a blocker here, but a treatment-valued `control_key` under those scopes still writes a header-only controls array. Worth a follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/` — 122 pass, plus 5 new tests for `within_perturbation` in `test_cluster_control_scope.py` (22 in that file). Two pre-existing `test_omezarr` ND2 failures are untouched by this diff
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on every changed Python file
- [x] Default config path unchanged: `tvn_batch_correction` absent → `batch_col="batch_values"`; `cluster.control_key` absent → aggregate key; scope absent → `pooled`
- [x] Scope verified against real data before running: 836 points each pinned to their own construct's vehicle arm, and every vehicle arm lands at exactly zero distance from itself
- [x] Full pipeline run on the zargun pilot — aggregate, cluster, bootstrap — with no rule failures

author: saoudrizwan
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** Follow-up to #14361 (the SDK v0.0.84 / CLI v3.0.63 release) and #13524.

### Description

Changelog-only. #13524 merged into `main` a few minutes before the release PR #14361 did, so it is inside the v0.0.84 and v3.0.63 trees but was documented in neither changelog. Nothing has been published yet, so this closes the gap before the publish workflows run.

This matters more for the CLI than the SDK: `cli-publish.yml` extracts the top `^## [0-9]` changelog section verbatim into both the GitHub release body and the Slack announcement, so an omission there ships publicly. `sdk-publish.yml` does not read `sdk/CHANGELOG.md` at all, but it should still be accurate.

**SDK bullet** covers the user-facing surface of #13524: the `appendContext` channel on `beforeRun`, the `<hook_context source="RunStart">` injection point (including the resumed-session-with-trailing-`tool_use` placement), and the new opt-in `blockingRunStartHooks`. The bullet is explicit that the flag defaults to today's fire-and-forget behavior, since that is the part hook authors need to know: `agent_start`/`agent_resume` have always run detached with stdio ignored, and turning blocking on by default would stall every run start for hosts whose existing scripts linger. It also flags the stdio guidance for hook authors who background a child.

**CLI bullet** is deliberately narrower, because the run-start control path is *not* live in the CLI — `blockingRunStartHooks` is not flipped there, so `cancel` and context injection from `agent_start`/`agent_resume` scripts stay inert. The only behavior a CLI user actually sees is the drive-by fix: `prompt_submit` and the audit logger no longer fire on injected hook-context messages, which carry the user role but a system display role. The bullet says the rest is still pending so hook authors reading the SDK notes don't assume it reached the CLI.

No version numbers, package manifests, or lockfile entries are touched — those are already correct on `main` from #14361.

### Test Procedure

Markdown-only change to two changelog files; nothing to execute.

- Verified `main` already carries the correct versions post-squash: all five SDK packages at `0.0.84`, `apps/cli` at `3.0.63`
- Verified both new bullets sit inside the correct top section (`## 0.0.84` and `## 3.0.63` respectively), so the CLI publish workflow's `^## [0-9]` extraction picks the bullet up
- Confirmed #13524 is the only SDK-touching commit that landed between the release branch point and the merge commit, so this is the complete gap and not a partial fix

### Type of Change

-   [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
-   [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
-   [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
-   [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes
-   [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes
-   [x] 📚 Documentation update
-   [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes

### Pre-flight Checklist

-   [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs)
-   [x] Tests are passing (`bun test`) and code is formatted and linted (`bun run format && bun run lint`)
-   [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

### Additional Notes

Publishing is blocked on this merging, to keep the shipped release notes accurate. Once it lands the sequence is unchanged from #14361: dispatch `sdk-publish.yml` on the `latest` channel, wait for green, then tag `cli-v3.0.63` on the resulting `main` commit and dispatch `cli-publish.yml`.

For a capped requirement, Dependabot's version update is a PR that **widens the cap**. #234 (`mcp` `<2` to `<3`) and #235 (`pydantic-ai-slim` `<2` to `<3`) touch `pyproject.toml` only. `uv.lock` still pins 1.x, so every check on them is green while the protection is removed; the next `uv lock` would resolve the new major and break main. Same shape as #193: a green PR that says nothing about the resolve it gets later.

The auto-merge policy already holds both (majors, in the schema-emitting guard set), so nothing would have merged by itself. The `ignore` entries remove the monthly green-but-wrong PR and the chance of a distracted manual merge. In the repo rather than as `@dependabot ignore` comments, so the decision is visible and reviewable, like the npm block's entries.

Each entry goes when its migration lands: #236 (mcp 2.x), #237 (pydantic-ai 2.x). Closes #234 and #235 by superseding them.

**Verification:** `check-jsonschema` passes, which after #231 is known to be necessary and not sufficient. The real check is server-side: a config change re-runs every ecosystem, so Dependabot update jobs starting after this merges is the proof it parsed.
