author: tati-agil
body:
## Contexto

Na Construção da Aposta, **Sintoma** e **Ideia de solução** (só essas duas) passam a permitir a decisão explícita "Pular esta etapa", para quando o Conselho Jedi já tem o problema claro (não precisa do Sintoma) ou já quer seguir direto para o experimento (sem se comprometer com uma Ideia formal).

**Nunca** deve ser tratado como dado faltante: sem erro, sem bloqueio de CONTINUAR, sem aparecer no Mapa/exportações/prompts de IA como "não informado"/"pulado".

## Modelo de estado escolhido

Cada etapa ganha `pulada: true` no próprio objeto de dados (`dados.sintoma.pulada` / `dados.ideia.pulada`) — reaproveita o mecanismo já existente de `salvarEtapa` trocar o objeto inteiro (o mesmo padrão já usado por "decisao"/"missao"), sem campo novo em outro lugar do banco e sem migração.

Três estados distintos, uma função única (`etapaEstaPulada`) decide todo mundo:
- **não visitada** — sem `pulada`, sem conteúdo;
- **preenchida** — com conteúdo;
- **pulada** — decisão explícita, nunca convive com conteúdo (pular com texto já digitado pede confirmação e descarta).

## Comportamento no menu (trilha lateral)

Pulada conta como **concluída** (libera a próxima etapa, entra no "X de 9") e ganha um selo discreto **"Pulada"** — nunca tratada como erro, nunca vermelha/bloqueada.

## Comportamento no Mapa da Aposta

Regra crítica cumprida: a etapa pulada **simplesmente não aparece** — nenhum card, nenhum "não informado"/"pulado"/"—". `cardsDoCicloHtml` (Ideia, dado do ciclo) e o bloco fixo Missão/Sintoma de `renderMapa` (e do Mapa histórico) agora **filtram** a etapa pulada da lista antes de desenhar — os cards e as setas se reencaixam sozinhos (Missão → Problema direto, Hipótese → Experimento direto), sem espaço vazio nem card fantasma.

## Comportamento em "Analisar com IA"

- `apostaBaseIA` monta só as seções presentes antes de juntar — nunca um separador `--------------------` dobrado quando falta uma seção.
- O texto comum (`contextoComumIA`) e a lente "Defende" citavam a cadeia fixa "Missão → Sintoma → ... → Ideia → ..." — viraram genéricos ("os elementos efetivamente presentes na aposta"), já que as lentes Desafia/Investiga nunca citavam Sintoma/Ideia por nome (não precisaram de mudança).
- **Novo núcleo obrigatório** em `faltamParaAnaliseIA`: Missão, Problema, ≥1 Mudança mensurável, Hipótese, Experimento planejado, ≥1 Evidência planejada — Sintoma e Ideia só precisam estar **decididas** ("preencher ou pular"), nunca preenchidas à força.

## Compatibilidade com multiciclo

Ideia é dado do **ciclo** (não da aposta inteira): um ciclo novo que recomeça **antes** dela nasce com a decisão em aberto de novo — nunca herda "pulada" (nem o conteúdo) do ciclo anterior, porque a arquitetura já existente (`montarDadosNovoCiclo`) só clona etapas anteriores ao ponto de reinício. Um ponto de reinício **depois** dela a herda como qualquer outro campo, e editá-la/pulá-la nesse caso já aciona a mesma cascata de "revisandoHerdado" que qualquer campo herdado — nenhum código novo precisou disso, só confirmado por teste dedicado (bloco 16e).

## Arquivos alterados

- `forca-agil/aposta.js` — todo o comportamento acima.
- `forca-agil/pages.css` — `.aposta-pular-*` (link discreto), `.aposta-pulada*` (estado dedicado), `.aposta-trilha-badge`/`.is-pulada` (selo na trilha).
- `.github/scripts/teste-aposta.js` — 48 novos casos + 1 teste existente atualizado.
- `forca-agil/manual.js`, `forca-agil/mapa.js`, `forca-agil/testes.js` — docs internas.

## Testes

Blocos novos "16a"–"16e" em `teste-aposta.js`, cobrindo:
- **Sintoma**: botão existe e é secundário; pular vazio não pede confirmação e avança direto para Problema; trilha marca "Pulada" sem bloquear; `resumoEtapa` devolve vazio; reabrir mostra o estado dedicado com "Preencher agora"/"Manter como pulada"; "Preencher agora" reabre o formulário sem confirmação e o conteúdo digitado depois é salvo normalmente; conteúdo digitado + Pular pede confirmação, cancelar preserva o texto, confirmar descarta e avança.
- **Ideia**: vazia (sem decidir) continua bloqueando CONTINUAR — a regra de frase estrita não mudou, só ganhou uma saída explícita; pular avança direto Hipótese → Experimento; trilha marca "Pulada".
- **As duas puladas juntas**: Mapa fica Missão → Problema → Mudanças → Hipótese → Experimento → Evidência → Decisão; os 3 prompts de IA são gerados e nenhum revela "SINTOMA"/"IDEIA DE SOLUÇÃO"/"pulado"/"não informado"; aposta-base idêntica nos três; `faltamIA()` considera a aposta completa.
- **Multiciclo**: Ciclo 1 com Ideia preenchida, Ciclo 2 com Ideia pulada — o Mapa do Ciclo 2 nunca usa a Ideia do Ciclo 1.

Um teste existente (`faltamIA()` com aposta incompleta) foi ajustado para a nova mensagem "Ideia de solução: preencher ou pular" (verificação por conteúdo, não igualdade exata).

**Suíte completa**: 950/950, **3 execuções limpas seguidas** (desktop + celular). `teste-consistencia-docs.js`: 12/12. `node --check` limpo em todos os arquivos alterados. `teste-tela-preta.js` em execução no momento da abertura desta PR — sem indício de regressão nas checagens já concluídas (esta mudança não toca telas de autenticação/carregamento).

## Fora do escopo

As demais sete etapas (Missão, Problema, Mudanças mensuráveis, Hipótese, Experimento, Evidência, Decisão), criação de ciclo/execução, grupos, isolamento, Security Rules, integração externa com IA, Teams, Fases 6/7 — nada disso foi tocado.

## Riscos residuais

- "Manter como pulada" (ao reabrir uma etapa já pulada) foi implementado como uma confirmação simples (toast), sem navegar — a navegação continua sendo CONTINUAR, sempre visível na tela. O pedido descrevia as duas ações lado a lado sem detalhar o efeito exato de "Manter"; essa interpretação evita duplicar a semântica de CONTINUAR. Vale validar com uso real se esse comportamento atende a expectativa.
- Não foi criado nenhum teste automatizado para o caso "ponto de reinício DEPOIS da Ideia herda o estado pulado do ciclo anterior" (só o caso mais comum, ponto de reinício antes dela) — a leitura de código confirma que a arquitetura existente (`salvarEtapa`/`revisandoHerdado`) já cobre esse caso genericamente, mas não há um teste E2E dedicado a ele especificamente.

Aguardando revisão antes do merge.

author: rasmussoot
body:
FU-242 spike run (2026-09-21, operator-authorized throwaway VM on nx-02; created, deleted with its disk, and the pool read before and after).

**Verdict: NO. Keep the hand-rolled `mgmt-*` loops.** Adopting this verdict, or retiring FU-242, is the operator's call. This PR edits only the spike doc: no FU, ADR or TICK-LOG changes.

- **Q1 Versions:** the runner image ships OpenTofu 1.12.1 (we pin 1.12.5), and `upgradeOnInit` defaults to true, which floats providers. Our pinned tofu from `/nix/store` plus the provider mirror do work, but `-lockfile=readonly` needed a wrapper script, because terraform-exec forbids `TF_CLI_ARGS_*` and always passes `-upgrade`.
- **Q2 Roots as-is:** Garage, `TF_ENCRYPTION` and creds from a Secret all work, and the saved plan is encrypted. But `backendConfig.disable` breaks the saved plan, so the backend block has to be duplicated, and `plan_exclude_types` has no field (that same wrapper had to handle it).
- **Q3 Approval:** an approval committed in the same repo moves the revision, so the plan is re-planned under a new id forever. It only works from a second repo. Matching is by prefix, and staleness is checked by plan name, which is weaker than the FU-248 plan-id apply.
- **Q4 Drift:** drift is detected (`Ready=False DriftDetected`). There is no notification path, because Flux Alerts reject `Terraform`, and there is no condition metric. The plan text lands in a plaintext ConfigMap and in the condition message.
- **Q5 Failure:** a stuck lock and an erroring plan both show as named states. An unreachable provider stayed silent in "Terraform Planning" for more than 36 min.
- **RSS:** about 1.4 GiB idle.

Side finding: a k3s API bound to loopback breaks in-cluster clients (MB4 layer 7).

author: baltacavazos
body: ## Qué pasaba Helios registró el SAT vivo (RFC UIPD9211257I0, certificados) mientras IMSS e Infonavit devolvían 503 de mantenimiento. AuditaPatrón mostraba «Hoy no pudimos confirmar con IMSS, SAT e Infonavit», «SAT — sin respuesta hoy» y el chat de que las tres no contestaron. El mismo caso lo vio la sesión `tester@auditapatron-smoke.test` / `000000`. Cerca de esa consulta, `guest-official` falló con «En el acceso gratuito solo puedes revisar un proveedor…» y `providerId` null. ## Por qué 1. La respuesta del puente es un JSON grande y el SAT vivo va al final. AuditaPatrón recortaba el cuerpo a 2000 caracteres antes de parsearlo. El JSON quedaba inválido y las tres fuentes se leían como pendientes. A los 60 segundos ese pendiente se vuelve «sin respuesta». 2. Aunque el JSON se leyera, una opinión `pendiente` podía tapar `honesty: live`. Si no venían hechos, la tarjeta rellenaba «Todavía no hay una respuesta oficial nueva de SAT» y escondía el RFC. 3. La consulta oficial (la del humo autenticado y la de `guest-official`) no manda `providerId`. Si el cliente cortaba el POST y reintentaba, el segundo choque con el tope de un proveedor volvía como 403. AuditaPatrón lo trataba como fallo de acceso y pintaba las tres oficinas en silencio, aunque el cuerpo todavía trajera el SAT vivo. Ese 403 también tapaba un acuse vivo ya guardado. ## Qué cambia - Se parsea el cuerpo completo. El recorte queda solo en el acuse guardado. - `honesty` / `resultado: vivo` / `satHonesty: live` ganan sobre una opinión pendiente. Si el SAT está vivo y no hay hechos citados, se muestra el RFC. - La espera de la consulta sube a 45 segundos, lo que alcanza una ronda del puente. Un timeout ya no dispara otro POST. - Un 403 del tope de un proveedor no se traduce en «IMSS, SAT e Infonavit no contestaron». Si ese cuerpo trae el SAT vivo, la tarjeta dice «Confirmamos con el SAT…». Si no trae consulta, se queda en espera y no pisa un SAT vivo anterior. Ni el humo ni `guest-official` muestran el texto del tope. ## Pruebas `pnpm exec vitest run` sobre la consulta oficial, la copia, el briefing, el chat y el puente. Cubren el cuerpo largo con SAT vivo, `satHonesty: live` con opinión pendiente, el 403 del tope con SAT vivo en el mismo JSON, y un tope vacío que no esconde el acuse vivo.

author: danielddhm
body:
### Problema
Particionar uma string em substrings palindromos e retornar todas as partições possíveis.

### Abordagem
Usar backtracking para explorar todas as partições. Pré-computar uma matriz DP de palindromos (iterando de trás para frente) para verificação eficiente de substrings em O(1), evitando recomputação.

### Implementação
Matriz DP preenchida bottom-up para garantir que quando precisamos de isPalin[i+1][j-1], já está calculada. Backtracking simples com pruning baseado na matriz.

### Complexidade
Tempo: O(N * 2^N). Espaço: O(N^2) para a matriz DP.

### Testes
Inclusos todos os exemplos oficiais mais casos de fronteira: string de um caractere, todos caracteres iguais, e sem palindromos contíguos.

author: hank-moogy
body:
## The dead end

Choosing a different plan on `/pricing` took an existing subscriber to checkout, which refused with a 409 and an error card. The refusal is correct — an account cannot hold two subscriptions — but the page had offered the click, and upgrading is a real thing a customer wants. Studio is a plan change in the billing portal, not a second purchase.

Found while chasing "I want to upgrade to Studio and I'm told I already have a subscription."

## The change

`useActiveSubscription` reads the account's subscription, and the cards say what is actually possible:

| Card | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| The plan you're on | "Choose Producer" → 409 error | "Current plan", disabled |
| Any other plan | "Choose Studio" → 409 error | "Switch in Billing" → `/billing` |
| No subscription | unchanged | unchanged |

## One status list, not two

The statuses that block a second checkout moved into `payment-contract.ts` as `BLOCKING_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUSES`, imported by both the checkout function and the page. They were previously only in the edge function, so any frontend copy would have been free to drift — and a page offering a plan the server then refuses is exactly the bug being fixed. A test pins the list.

`blocksNewCheckout` covers the statuses that are easy to forget: `unpaid`, `incomplete` and `paused` all block, while `canceled` and `incomplete_expired` do not.

## Failure behaviour

A failed billing query falls back to "no subscription" rather than blocking the page. A pricing page that cannot read billing state should still sell; checkout was making that call alone until now anyway.

## Verification

`npm run build` passes, 117/117 tests, eslint clean on changed files.

## Deploy note

`create-managed-checkout` changed (it now imports the shared constant instead of declaring its own), so it needs a redeploy. Behaviour is identical — same six statuses.

author: joaovmour4
body:
## Resumo

Dois erros de forma equivalentes do cliente, no mesmo campo, devolviam status incoerentes:
discriminador de tipo **desconhecido** respondia 400 e discriminador **ausente** respondia 500.
O `SystemTextJsonInputFormatter` converte `JsonException` em erro de model state, mas deixa
escapar a `NotSupportedException` — a única forma com que o desserializador reporta união
polimórfica sem discriminador. Ela chegava ao tratador global como falha inesperada.

Como o discriminador do projeto é `$tipo` (ADR-0058), e não o `type` que a maioria das
bibliotecas usa por convenção, errar o `$` é o modo de falha esperado de quem integra pela
primeira vez — e a resposta a isso era "erro interno do servidor", num status que endpoint
nenhum declara.

Agora a recusa sai em 400 **nomeando o campo e a propriedade que falta**, em vez de mandar reler
um documento que está bem formado.

```
400 uniplus.requisicao.malformada
detail: A requisição não pôde ser lida: o campo 'predicado' não declara '$tipo',
        a propriedade que identifica qual variante do contrato o objeto representa.
```

Closes #1410

## Como funciona

**`PolymorphicDeserializationInputFormatter`** envolve o formatter JSON já registrado e converte
em recusa de model state toda `NotSupportedException` que escapa da leitura. Envolve em vez de
acrescentar um formatter novo: um novo teria de disputar precedência com o que já lê JSON, e
quem ganha depende da ordem da lista.

Três decisões que sustentam o resto:

- **A mensagem da exceção não entra no `ModelState`.** É dela que sairia o nome completo do tipo
  CLR que falhou a desserialização, e o `InvalidRequestProblemFactory` existe justamente para que
  isso nunca chegue ao cliente. O que entra é a chave — o caminho do erro dentro do documento —,
  que é o sinal de que houve documento e quem o reprovou foi o desserializador.
- **O recorte é pelo contrato, não pelo texto.** A recusa só vira 400 quando o caminho do erro
  endereça, no contrato do modelo, um tipo que de fato é união polimórfica — é isso que confirma
  que quem errou foi o documento. A mesma `NotSupportedException` sai de um tipo abstrato que
  ninguém declarou como união, e aí o defeito é de configuração do servidor: a exceção segue em
  frente e o 5xx continua acusando o que só o servidor pode corrigir. Ler a frase do framework
  para decidir isso apostaria justamente na parte que menos se controla.
- **O discriminador é lido do contrato, não de constante nossa.** O caminho do erro localiza o
  tipo dentro do `JsonTypeInfo` da ação, e o nome vem de `TypeDiscriminatorPropertyName`. Por isso
  vale para união na raiz, aninhada e dentro de coleção — e continua valendo se alguma união
  deixar de usar `$tipo`.

## Alcance real das uniões polimórficas

A issue supõe que os quatro tipos-raiz são alcançáveis por corpo de comando. Hoje só dois são:

| União | Como chega |
|---|---|
| `PredicadoObrigatoriedade` | corpo, propriedade direta (`$.predicado`) |
| `ArgsRegraAjusteDistribuicao` | corpo, dentro de coleção (`$.configuracoes[0].argsAjuste`) |
| `ArgsCriterioDesempate` | montada no handler a partir de campos escalares de `CriterioDesempateInput` |
| `ArgsRegraEliminacao` | montada no handler a partir de campos escalares de `RegraEliminacaoInput` |

É o caso aninhado em coleção que descarta qualquer detecção por reflexão de um nível a partir do
tipo do parâmetro: a propriedade polimórfica não está no comando, está dois níveis abaixo. Daí a
navegação pelo caminho do erro.

## Testes

- **`PolymorphicDeserializationInputFormatterTests`** — o núcleo. Cobre união na raiz, aninhada e
  dentro de coleção; discriminador declarado por outro nome; tipo abstrato que não é união
  seguindo como falha de servidor; as recusas que o framework já tratava seguindo intactas; a
  mensagem do framework fora do `ModelState`; e a delegação dos content types, sem a qual o
  `requestBody` do OpenAPI sairia sem media type.
- **`InvalidRequestProblemFactoryTests`** — a resposta nomeia campo e discriminador, fala do corpo
  quando a união é a raiz, e continua genérica quando a recusa tem outra causa.
- **`PolymorphicJsonDeserializationTests`** — as duas premissas externas que o conserto consome,
  nas quatro uniões-raiz: o nome da propriedade discriminadora e a forma da recusa do
  desserializador, de onde sai o caminho do campo.
- **`ObrigatoriedadeLegalAdminEndpointTests`** — ponta a ponta pelo endpoint real: `tipo` e `type`
  no lugar de `$tipo`, predicado vazio e discriminador inexistente, todos em 400 com o mesmo
  `code`; e o corpo correto continuando a criar a regra.

Verificado por sabotagem: com o registro do envoltório desativado, os casos novos voltam a
responder 500 `uniplus.internal.unexpected`.

author: ernstgodoy
body:
On macOS,  the `tr` command can fail with an `Illegal byte sequence` when processing `/dev/urandom` under a multibyte locale. 

Supascale uses `tr` to generate random vales for several secrets. When this command fails, the generated values are empty, which can result in an invalid `.env` file and prevent the supabase db from starting.

For example:
```
tr: Illegal byte sequence
```

This can result in empty values for:
- POSTGRES_PASSWORD
- JWT_SECRET
- DASHBOARD_PASSWORD
- VAULT_ENC_KEY

### Fix
Set LC_ALL=C for the `tr` invocation in both `generate_password()` and `generate_encryption_key()`.

This makes random byte processing locale-independent while preserving the existing generation logic.

### Testing 
Verified on macOS that:
```
tr -dc 'a-zA-Z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 40
```
fails with:
```
tr: Illegal byte sequence
```
while:
```
LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'a-zA-Z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 40
```
successfully generates a random value.

Also verified that a newly created Supascale project generates non-empty values for the affected secrets.

author: jeronimorepetto
body:
Your grouping, as asked: Panel shortcut + Position together, then a rule, Typography, a rule, Audio, a rule, Notifications, a rule, Jev, then the Data Base / Application cluster.

## Why

Settings grew from the design's **three** sections to **eight**, each drawing its own heading, all in one column with nothing between them. `screens/settings.md` records the growth itself — *"previously listed three sections and now lists four"*, then five. Eight headings in a row is not a list any more.

## The decisions inside it

**A rule between groups, never between every section.** The point is to say which sections belong *together*; a rule after each one says nothing at all.

**The first group is the design source's own pair.** `Panel shortcut` and `Panel position` share that prefix in its headings — putting them together is reading the source, not inventing a grouping. The last group keeps Data Base with Application, which `DataBaseSection`'s own comment already treats as one bottom cluster.

**No group headings.** Every section already draws its own name; a heading above them would print half of those names twice.

**1px, where the title's rule is 2px.** The heavier line belongs to the panel's own name, and a group boundary matching it would flatten the two into one level. The design source draws no grouping at all — it has grown by maintainer amendment three times without one — so this weight is ours, recorded at the token the way `--size-scrollbar-width` and `--elevation-5` record theirs.

## Tests

`+4`, none removed (census `32 → 36`, exit 0).

The main one asserts the **sequence**, not a count:

```
title, Panel shortcut, Position, ---, Typography, ---, Audio, ---,
Notifications, ---, Jev, ---, Data Base, Application
```

A rule in the wrong place groups the wrong things, and a count would pass for any arrangement. Three more pin the edges: no rule directly under the title (it has its own), none at the end (it would underline the panel), and every rule marked `role="presentation"` since it names nothing.

Seven CI checks green: `pnpm test` 8147 passed / 5 skipped.

author: einsteindark-edgm
body:
## Qué pasaba
En Órdenes "no funcionaba el filtro": el botón **Filtros** del encabezado no tenía acción, no había filtro por fecha y los KPIs del tablero ignoraban cualquier filtro. Además **"Ingresos mes" estaba mal**: sumaba toda orden activa con entrega agendada en el mes (incluidas las que seguían en preparación o sin cobrar). Con datos de prueba mostraba $1.8 M cuando lo realmente cobrado era $275 k.

## Cambios
- **Calendario de Chats en Órdenes**: movido a `shared/ui/DateRangeFilter` + `shared/lib/date-range.ts` (los plugins no se importan entre sí) y montado bajo el buscador de Órdenes. Chats lo usa desde shared, sin cambios de comportamiento.
- **Día de una orden** (`orderDayIso`): entrega agendada; si no está agendada, día de creación en hora Colombia (`Order.createdIso`, derivado de `created_at_ms` en el mapper, que sigue sin leer el reloj).
- **Alcances** en `useOrderFilters`:
  - sidebar = búsqueda + rango
  - KPIs = búsqueda + rango + modalidad (**no** la vista: resumen del período)
  - kanban = todo lo anterior + vista
- **Ingresos** (`isCollectedRevenue`): solo columna **Entregada** con pago **Pagado**. Sin rango → "Ingresos mes" (mes en curso); con rango → "Ingresos" del período, con el rango en el subtítulo.
- **Quitado el botón "Filtros"** del encabezado (resto del prototipo sin acción).

## Verificación
- `vitest` local: suite completa en verde (el CI no corre los unit tests del frontend), incluidos los tests nuevos, que fallaban antes del cambio (`OrdersSection.daterange.test.tsx`, casos de Ingresos y del botón en `OrdersHeader.test.tsx`, `createdIso` en `api.test.ts`).
- `tsc -b`, `test:arch` 23/23, `build`.
- En navegador (página de preview con órdenes sembradas): mes en curso → $275 k; rango 15–21 sep → 5 órdenes, contadores acotados, Ingresos $190 k.

## Para tener en cuenta
Una orden **contra entrega** entregada solo suma a Ingresos cuando su pago queda en "Pagado".

Solo frontend: sale con el deploy del frontend, sin rebuild de API.

author: badjams
body:
Empilée sur la **#28** : elle en reprend la couche `inland_waters` et modifie les mêmes lignes, d'où une base sur sa branche plutôt que sur `main`. GitHub la reciblera sur `main` dès que la #28 sera fusionnée.

## 1. Le repli libre passe au Plan IGN

Le repli s'appuyait sur OpenStreetMap standard, pauvre en fluvial. Il sert désormais le **Plan IGN v2** — déjà utilisé par `ign_public_hybrid`, gratuit et sans clé — surmonté des amers OpenSeaMap. Canaux, écluses et cours d'eau y sont nettement mieux dessinés.

Contrepartie assumée et documentée : le Plan IGN couvre la France, ailleurs les tuiles reviennent vides. C'est le compromis retenu pour un usage métier français.

## 2. Deux couches SHOM

| Couche | Service | Accès | Contenu |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shom_raster` | `services.data.shom.fr/<clé>/wmts` | abonnement ou convention (`SHOM_API_KEY`) | cartes marines scannées (`RASTER_MARINE`) |
| `shom_inspire` | `services.data.shom.fr/INSPIRE/wmts` | libre, sans clé (`SHOM_INSPIRE_LAYER`) | couches thématiques INSPIRE |

Même motif que la clé IGN privée : la clé vit dans `config.private.js`, jamais dans le dépôt, et la couche reste masquée sans elle.

**Deux points à connaître avant de s'en réjouir** :

- Les cartes marines scannées sont **sous abonnement** — le service INSPIRE libre ne les sert pas, seulement les données thématiques (bathymétrie, trait de côte). Retrouver les fonds SHOM passe donc par une demande au SHOM, pas par un flux ouvert.
- Le SHOM couvre la mer, les estuaires et les approches, **pas les canaux ni les rivières intérieures**. Ces couches complètent le fond « Eaux intérieures », elles ne le remplacent pas.

## 3. `tools/shom_layers.py`

Les identifiants de couches du SHOM ne se devinent pas et diffèrent d'un service à l'autre. L'outil les relève sur le `GetCapabilities`, avec leur `TileMatrixSet` et leur plage de zooms, et imprime la ligne à coller dans `config.private.js` :

```bash
python3 tools/shom_layers.py                      # service INSPIRE, libre
python3 tools/shom_layers.py --cle MA_CLE         # service sous abonnement
python3 tools/shom_layers.py --filtre raster      # ne garde que ces couches
python3 tools/shom_layers.py --fichier capa.xml   # parse un GetCapabilities déjà téléchargé
```

Bibliothèque standard uniquement, aucune dépendance. C'est aussi pourquoi `SHOM_INSPIRE_LAYER` est **vide par défaut** : une couche absente du sélecteur vaut mieux qu'une couche qui ne renverrait que des tuiles vides.

## Documentation et release

- `DOCUMENTATION.md` / `.html` : nouvelle **§7.6** (deux services, relevé des identifiants, conditions d'emploi, portée), §7.5 mise à jour pour le nouveau repli, deux lignes au tableau §7.2, template `config.private.js` en §11.1.
- `version.js` → 23.23 avec son entrée de changelog, `sw.js` → `cado-cache-23.23`, conformément à §10.5.

## Vérifications

Test sous Chromium (Playwright), tuiles distantes interceptées — rien ne part sur le réseau, seules les URL sont relevées :

| Contrôle | Résultat |
|---|---|
| Sans clé : repli proposé, aucune couche SHOM | OK |
| Sans clé : `data.geopf.fr` **et** OpenSeaMap demandés, plus aucune requête OSM sur cette couche | OK |
| Sans clé : mentions IGN et OpenSeaMap affichées sur la carte | OK |
| Avec clé : les deux couches SHOM proposées, eaux intérieures en version privée | OK |
| Avec clé : clé dans le chemin (`/CLE_DE_TEST/wmts`), `LAYER` et `TILEMATRIXSET=3857` transmis | OK |
| Avec clé : `TILEMATRIX`, `TILEROW`, `TILECOL` substitués en nombres | OK |
| Couche libre : vise bien `/INSPIRE/wmts` avec l'identifiant choisi | OK |

`tools/shom_layers.py` testé hors ligne sur un `GetCapabilities` d'exemple : liste, filtre, clé refusée (réponse illisible) et service injoignable.

**Non vérifié ici** : le service SHOM lui-même — le réseau de cette session ne l'atteint pas. L'identifiant `RASTER_MARINE_3857_WMTS`, la plage de zooms (18 retenu) et la réponse CORS sont donc à confirmer au premier branchement, l'outil étant fait pour ça. `DOCUMENTATION.pdf` n'est pas régénéré, comme sur les releases précédentes.

author: arcadalabs-jason
body:
Rows M290, M304 and M309 from river's launch-work assignment. Certified clean by assay (delta cert binding c5fc781).

**M290 — two defects under one symptom**, either of which alone would have looked like a fix. The SessionStart hook read `.kijito_persona` with `tr -d '[:space:]'`, deleting *interior* spaces, so `name (purpose)` silently became a different persona — those are the literal filenames in beta feedback #14/#16, and it happened before any sanitizer ran. Separately, the hook's own sanitizer neither casefolded nor understood Unicode where the producer does both (`Loom`→`Loom` vs `loom`). The producer now publishes the rule as `--safe-persona`; consumers ask it, and when they cannot, they read the persona stamp the producer writes into every event line rather than falling back to a local rule — evidence instead of inference, and it keeps existing seats working before the producer upgrade lands.

**M304 — the install proves the wake path instead of declaring it.** It now pushes a real message through and names the hop that broke (producer · stream · consumer). A broken wake path fails as *silence*, indistinguishable from a working one with no mail on it, so an installer that only verifies its own file copies can exit 0 over a dead inbox — which is what happened on the first external install. `--require-consumer` gives the agent-driven onboarding flow the stricter contract it needs, since it runs after arming a consumer and must report a machine-checkable verdict.

**M309 — the status line says which persona a pane is**, through a shared marker reader so it cannot become a third copy of the rule that caused M290.

Tests: topology 24/0 including three mutants (each restoring a real shipped defect), inbox self-test 5/0, statusline 5/0, monitor suite 455/455. Certified on ext4 deliberately — APFS is case-insensitive, so a green Mac run proves nothing about the casefold defect being fixed.

author: npiobject
body:
Un extracto real no daba ninguna fila y el texto leído salía invisible. La causa: el PDF usa **fuentes Type0 (Identity-H)**, donde cada cadena del flujo es una lista de códigos de glifo (`<00010002…>`) que solo significa algo a través del CMap `/ToUnicode` de la fuente. Antes se interpretaban como bytes.

## Qué cambia

- `docs/app/extracto.js` → `textoPDF()` recorre el documento **por páginas**: parsea los objetos, resuelve `/Resources → /Font → /ToUnicode` para cada nombre de fuente, lee el CMap (`bfchar` y `bfrange`, destinos sueltos y por tramos) y traduce las cadenas hexadecimales con el mapa de la **fuente activa**, que el operador `Tf` va cambiando. El barrido a pelo de los flujos se conserva como respaldo para PDF sin `/Type /Page` reconocible.
- Al reconstruir filas, una línea sin importe se cose a la anterior **solo si esa fila sigue abierta** (aún sin importe). Antes, el pie legal de la página acababa dentro del concepto del último movimiento de cada página.

- **483 filas** reconocidas, de `2025-01-02` a `2025-12-31`; 0 sin fecha, 0 sin importe, 0 descripciones vacías y **0 descripciones contaminadas por el pie** (eran 24 antes de la corrección del cosido).

author: beinan
body:
## Why I'm doing:

`PaimonMetadata.getPartitions` calls `updatePartitionInfo` — a full `Catalog.listPartitions` round trip — for every requested partition name that is missing from the cache. A single listing already reflects all partitions of the table, so the additional calls only add latency and catalog load. This shows up when several partitions are requested that no longer exist (e.g. dropped partitions during MV partition sync) or on a cold cache with a missing name: N misses cost N catalog listings.

## What I'm doing:

Track whether the partition cache has already been reloaded within the current `getPartitions` call and skip further reloads. Also guard against a `null` per-table map so a partitioned table that disappears from the catalog cannot NPE.

This PR is stacked on #79443 (cold-cache NPE fix) and only adds one commit on top; once #79443 merges the diff reduces to this change alone.

Validation:

- `PaimonPartitionRefreshOnceTest` (4 new tests), `PaimonPartitionColdCacheTest`, and the existing `PaimonMetadataTest` all pass (51/51) on JDK 17.
- Without the fix, `testMultipleMissingPartitionsListOnlyOnce` and `testColdCacheListsOnlyOnce` fail with `TooManyActualInvocations` on `listPartitions`.

author: henriqueluza
body:
## Resultado

Consolida a landing com quatro fotografias como a única home da LexIntegra, aplica a logo enviada com o nome atualizado e melhora navegação, dúvidas frequentes, rodapé e informação jurídica.

- Logo LexIntegra e favicon com o símbolo da balança; legenda da hero com a ordem das frases alterada.
- Navbar: visitante vê Entrar/Cadastre-se; usuário autenticado vê seu nome e carrinho, com link para a área do perfil. Underline animado no hover e foco.
- Quatro respostas do FAQ com abertura/fechamento animados, atributos acessíveis e respeito à preferência de movimento reduzido.
- Rodapé responsivo com logo pequena, proposta, navegação, orientação de atendimento e links legais. Conteúdo institucional ampliado.
- Remove o seletor de imagens; `/todas-as-imagens` e `/com-movimento` redirecionam para `/`.
- Termos com 14 seções e privacidade com 12, ambos com índice. O checkout usa a mesma fonte dos termos; aceite atualizado para `checkout-v2-minuta-2026-09`.

## Validação

- `pnpm quality`: 2.466 testes aprovados, lint e cobertura dentro dos limiares.
- Build de produção e 15 verificações de pré-renderização sem JavaScript aprovados.
- 9 cenários de sessão nos emuladores aprovados (cliente, advogado e admin em três larguras), incluindo reload e logout.
- 72 verificações públicas de navegador, responsividade, acessibilidade, imagens e FAQ aprovadas; referências visuais atualizadas e inspecionadas.

## Decisões e limites

A navbar agora restaura a sessão real pelo SDK dinâmico de Firebase Auth também nas rotas públicas. Não consulta a API da aplicação nem Firestore na home. O token de liberação do catálogo não é tratado como autenticação. O carrinho continua disponível dentro da jornada de compra para visitantes, embora seu atalho na navbar fique oculto conforme solicitado.

Os textos jurídicos permanecem minutas para revisão do escritório. Identificação jurídica, canal formal e responsabilidades específicas não foram inventados; a revisão precisa completar esses dados antes do uso definitivo. Aceites anteriores continuam vinculados às versões originais. As regras de pagamento e Teams permanecem inalteradas.

Decisões visuais, prompts e caminhos dos assets: `docs/identidade-navegacao.md`.


### Apresentação institucional

A landing incorpora recorte diagonal na fotografia principal e alternância entre vinho escuro e vinho profundo nas seções, inspirados na referência da contratante, mantendo a marca, as fontes e a redação LexIntegra. As aberturas públicas recebem divisores; navegação e rodapé usam a logo branca transparente. O convite explica o cadastro inicial, o conteúdo de atendimento aparece na seção de acompanhamento e o aviso de limites contratuais fica nos termos.

Validação deste refinamento: build de produção com 26 rotas, lint sem erros e 72 testes visuais, responsivos, de acessibilidade e interação aprovados. Capturas de referência atualizadas nos três tamanhos de tela.




As fotografias usam recorte diagonal e acompanham a altura do conteúdo adjacente no desktop; em telas estreitas, usam proporção 3:2. A fotografia da seção “Seu próximo passo merece uma base segura” foi realocada para o convite final ao cadastro, com o botão abaixo dela. Logos e QR de pagamento preservam a geometria funcional. Testes e capturas foram atualizados para as quatro fotografias restantes.



O rodapé foi extraído para um componente compartilhado e está presente na landing, login, cadastro e serviços, com os mesmos links, identidade e comportamento responsivo.

author: amroksaleh
body:
Follow-up to #1274, which corrected what `TENANT_ISOLATION.md` said **wrongly**. This adds two things it did not say **at all**, and fixes one it stated incompletely — all three flagged by WHIT-93's own acceptance criteria, which name `active_tenant_id` resolution and verified-email login explicitly.

## `resolve()` does not read `tenant_id` first

The page said it "reads the `tenant_id` claim". Since the identity cutover it reads **`active_tenant_id` first and treats it as authoritative** — that is the claim the tenant switcher re-mints and the one gated against `memberships` — falling back to `tenant_id` only for a legacy token that lacks it entirely. Naming only the fallback describes the pre-cutover system.

**The asymmetry is the part worth writing down.** A malformed `active_tenant_id` throws and *never* falls back. If it degraded to the legacy claim, a caller holding both could corrupt the new one deliberately and have the system fall back to a `tenant_id` of its choosing — downgrade-picking its own tenant. Present-but-invalid throws; only absent falls back.

## Where `active_tenant_id` comes from

Nothing on the page explained this. It is decided once, at authentication, from the profile's active memberships and never from client input:

- one membership → used directly;
- more than one → a selection prompt, and **no session exists** until the caller picks one that validates against their memberships;
- with 2FA, the same rule one step later — a single membership rides the short-lived `temp` token, a multi-membership profile defers the choice until after the second factor.

That is what earns `TenantContext` the right to treat the claim as authoritative, and it is precisely what separates this claim from the declared-target signals documented further down (`X-Tenant-Id` and friends), which say which tenant a request *addresses*, never who the caller is.

## Verified-email login

The page mentioned the globally-unique email but never that verification gates it. An unverified address **never** authenticates (ADR 0005 §2) — it is an unproven claim to an identity, and the whole tenant boundary hangs off which profile the caller turns out to be.

The refusal is the **generic** invalid-credentials response and is latency-compensated. "That address exists but is unverified" is a user-enumeration oracle; saying it *faster* than the password path is the same oracle with extra steps.

## Verification

Every statement was read out of `TenantContext::lockTenantFromPayload()` and `AuthHandler` rather than inferred — including the dual-claim comment citing WC-d4340daf / ADR 0005 §5, and the login flow's single-vs-multiple membership branches.

`docs/wiki` still has **zero broken relative links**.

Docs only — no code.

### Why this is a second PR

#1274 was checked against "is anything here false?" and passed. It was not checked against "does this cover what the task asked for?", and two of four required clauses were missing. Splitting the correction from the gap-filling keeps each reviewable on its own terms — and the omission is worth naming rather than quietly folding in, because "nothing is wrong" and "nothing is missing" are different questions and only the first one got asked.

author: bscott711
body:
## Summary
- `ArgusStreamSession`'s `SESSION_START` header sent `output_dir` + decon/PSF fields, built against an older receiver draft. The current `opym-receive` requires `raw_root` (`StreamReceiver._handle_session_start` does `Path(header["raw_root"])` inside a `try/except KeyError`) and never reads decon parameters from the handshake at all -- those are resolved entirely server-side from `OPYM_DECON_PSF`. The mismatch meant every `SESSION_START` was silently rejected and every frame dropped as an unknown session: this feature could not have worked at all until this fix, independent of the `enabled` flag.
- Drops `psf_paths`/`dz_psf`/`iterations`/`sheet_angle_deg`/`interp_method`/`rl_method` from both the wire header and `ArgusStreamSettingsV1` (dead now that nothing reads them) and updates `gpfs_scratch_root`'s docstring to match: it's the declared `raw_root` itself, not a `.../Decon` output dir.
- Adds a protocol contract test asserting the header contains every key the Argus-side receiver actually requires, so this class of drift between the two repos gets caught here next time.

Base branch is `feat/mda-ux-perf-fixes` since `_argus_stream/` only exists there (not yet on `main`). Pairs with https://github.com/bscott711/opym/pull/4 on the receiver side.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/test_argus_stream.py` -- 23 passed (removed 2 tests for the now-deleted PSF-routing logic, fixed the happy-path assertions, added a header-contract test)
- [x] `pytest tests/` (full suite) -- 175 passed, 2 pre-existing skips
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` / `mypy` / `pyright` all clean on changed files
- [x] Live smoke test against the real Argus receiver confirmed the fixed header is accepted (paired with the receiver-side ACK fix in the linked PR)

author: 77mdias
body:
The Secret scan job failed once with "Failed to FinalizeArtifact: (403) Forbidden" even though gitleaks reported "no leaks found" and the blob upload had completed. Re-running the same commit passed, and every other push and pull_request run for months passed with the same permissions block (actions: read) and no fork involved, so this is a transient fault in GitHub's artifact service.

gitleaks-action intends the upload to be best-effort -- it passes continueOnError: true to the artifact client -- but @actions/artifact still rethrows on FinalizeArtifact. The supported escape hatch is GITLEAKS_ENABLE_UPLOAD_ARTIFACT, so disable the upload and let the scan result alone decide the job status. Exit code 2 on a leak still fails.

The SARIF artifact has no consumer today: there is no upload-sarif step,
and security-events: write is only used by CodeQL.

author: wilplus
body:
## What broke

Founder 2026-09-21, project j, Take 1: Yes on the Confident Voice bookmark, the rooting phrase chosen, then **"Decide every suggestion on this chunk first"** on Lock and on Keep evolving alike. A 409 `UNDECIDED` from `PUT /explore/arc/<arc>/parts/<part>/lock`, every time. No paragraph carrying a V3 bookmark could be locked or kept evolving.

## Why

The lock gate trusts one invariant: a change still served IS an undecided one, because every lane drops what the student decided. `_immutable_membership` honours it for V2 by removing every row whose id carries a self-report. `_first_client_feedback` then **replaces** the rows with V3's, rebuilt from the policy frame with no knowledge of any answer, so an answered V3 item came back on every read and the gate counted it as pending.

## Fix

A new stage, `_drop_answered_service_items`, runs right after the V3 replacement (only when V3 replaced the rows) and drops what the owner answered, from both places an answer can live:

- the legacy route's `take_feedback_self_report`, keyed by item id (the path the founder's Take took, since the served rows carried no service fields);
- the service route's `feedback_v3_owner_responses`, keyed by membership and candidate, which the served row carries under `mlc3_service` (new read `DatabaseService.list_feedback_v3_owner_response_keys`).

Drops only; never invents or reorders (L2). A failed service read degrades to "not answered", the state the gate was already in.

Tests in `tests/test_ideal_text_changes.py`: legacy answer drops the row, service answer drops the row, unanswered Take unchanged, failed read degrades rather than blanks, and the stage sits between the V3 replacement and the claim.

`FILTER: ADVANCE-F1-SURFACE — cat F1-SURFACE — fences clear — locks clear — redirect: n/a (Ideal Text protect: lock and keep-evolving)`

CI override: GitHub Actions minutes exhausted; verified locally via `scripts/local_ci.sh` (python 3.12, ruff 0.15.8, mypy 2.3.0): manifest, runner, ruff, mypy, complexity, unit tier and F1 floor green. No migration, rehearsal tier not required.

author: michieluijting
body:
## Doel

Repareer **Foto maken** in Catalogusdetail zodat deze optie niet langer een Windows-bestandskiezer opent, maar een echte live camerafunctie in Inhuis gebruikt.

TEST_LEVEL_PROVISIONAL: M

STYLEGUIDE_IMPACT: updated

STYLEGUIDE_REASON: Het bestaande Catalogusdetail-fotopatroon wordt aangescherpt: Foto maken gebruikt voortaan navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia() met live preview, expliciete capture/annuleeractie en directe stream-opruiming. De canonieke styleguide is hierop bijgewerkt.

## Probleem

De vorige implementatie gebruikte een verborgen `<input type="file" capture="environment">`.
Op Windows-desktop is `capture` slechts een browserhint; Firefox/Chrome mogen deze negeren en dan opent Windows Verkenner. Dat gebeurde lokaal.

## Oplossing

- **Foto uploaden** blijft de gewone bestandskiezer.
- **Foto maken** gebruikt nu `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia()`.
- De app toont een live camerabeeld in een Inhuis-dialog.
- De gebruiker maakt de foto met een expliciete knop **Foto maken**.
- Op mobiel wordt waar mogelijk de achtercamera gevraagd via `facingMode: environment`.
- Op desktop/laptop wordt de beschikbare webcam gebruikt.
- Bij annuleren, navigeren of na het maken worden alle MediaStream-tracks direct gestopt.
- Begrijpelijke meldingen voor geweigerde cameratoegang, geen camera en een reeds bezette camera.
- Het gemaakte camerabeeld loopt daarna door dezelfde bestaande 640px/JPEG-compressie en backendopslag als een geüploade foto.
- De camera-route bevat geen file-input meer en kan dus geen Windows Verkenner openen.

## Regressies

Frontendcontract:
- vereist `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia`;
- vereist `facingMode: environment`;
- bewijst dat `capture="environment"` en de camera-file-input zijn verwijderd;
- vereist live cameramodal en canvas-capture.

Frontend E2E:
- klikt **Foto maken**;
- bewijst dat de live cameramodal opent;
- bewijst dat `getUserMedia` exact wordt aangeroepen;
- controleert de gevraagde achtercamera-constraint;
- bewijst dat er geen camera-file-input meer bestaat;
- bestaande upload/compressie/opslagflow blijft getest.

## Versie

**Rezzerv-MVP-v01.12.166**

## Basis / kandidaat

- base: `main@7a8c623fe032f55fe8dbbe974421eeead60f8a65`
- kandidaat-SHA: `43e4ea5ac14890e1847962815baf37f80a5d05c6`
- 0 commits achter `main`

## Relevante open PR's

De bestaande oudere Draft-PR's raken deze live camera-fix niet direct. PR #469 raakt wel Catalogus/OFF en versiebestanden en moet bij eventuele hervatting opnieuw tegen actuele main worden beoordeeld.

## Status

Draft tijdens normale CI/preflight. Pas na volledig groene normale checks wordt deze kandidaat Ready gemaakt en wordt F7 op exact deze head-SHA uitgevoerd.

Niet mergen zonder expliciete PO-GO voor de dan gecontroleerde kandidaat-SHA.

body:
## Summary

Complete overhaul of the Persian RTL personal-brand site (Omid Adli — Performance Marketing & CRO):

### Design & UX
- Full redesign inspired by webild.io: light/airy surfaces, big bold typography, rounded cards, glass pills — adapted to RTL Persian with an indigo-violet brand accent.
- Day/night theme switch with **two separate palettes** (never inverted colors); default dark; anti-FOUC inline theme script.
- Kept and refined the flashy extras: custom cursor, QuickActionDock, blobs, 3D icon badges, cinematic hero; removed the splash screen and trust bar per feedback.
- Full consultant funnel on home: HERO → PATH_NAV → PROOF → SERVICES_TABS → HOW_I_WORK → WHY_OMID → INSIGHTS → FAQ → FINAL_CTA.
- All 9 pages restyled, RTL carousels, modals with Esc + scroll-lock, accessible focus states.

### CMS / Admin (WordPress-like)
- Cloudflare Pages Functions backend + **D1** database: `GET/PUT /api/content`, slug generation, comments CRUD, media upload/serve/delete, HMAC session auth with rate limiting (8 fails/IP/15min).
- Admin panel with 15 tabs: every section of the site is editable via a recursive `FieldsForm` (content + SEO + slug fields on every item, exactly like WordPress).
- `schema.sql` includes all tables; deploy guide in `CMS-DEPLOY.md`.

### Free media storage (no R2 / no international card required)
- Media falls back to storing files as base64 in D1 (`media_files` table, ~1.4MB cap) with **client-side canvas compression** (≤1600px, JPEG .82).
- R2 code path stays dormant: if a `MEDIA` bucket binding is ever added, uploads automatically prefer R2; old D1 files keep serving. No migration needed.

### AI consultant + behavior management
- Floating chat widget that answers **strictly from the site's own data** (live digest of personal info, services, packages/prices, case studies, products, blog posts, work steps, capacity pulled from D1).
- Two engines: **Gemini 2.0-flash** when `GEMINI_API_KEY` is present, otherwise a zero-cost Persian keyword matcher with commercial-intent synonym expansion.
- Admin tab «دستیار هوشمند (AI)» manages behavior: enable/disable, title, greeting, persona (system prompt), quick questions, CTA text, fallback message — plus full conversation history monitoring (`chat_messages`, mode ai|local).
- Public rate limit: 15 messages/hour/IP.

### SEO & correctness
- Per-page SEOHead, sitemap now includes published blog posts, canonical domain omidadli01.site, fixed admin login auth bypass (promise-truthy bug), fixed duplicate/invalid Tailwind classes, `compatibility_date` in wrangler.toml.

## Testing
- `tsc` clean for both `src` and `functions`; `npm run build` passes.
- Backend smoke-tested via local wrangler: login, content PUT, media upload→D1→serve→delete (404 after), chat flows (price question → real packages from digest; case-study question → matched; irrelevant question → polite fallback), chat history logging, rate-limit 429.

## Deploy notes
1. `npx wrangler d1 execute omidadli01-site-db --remote --file=./schema.sql`
2. Secrets: `ADMIN_USERNAME`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `AUTH_SECRET`; optionally `GEMINI_API_KEY` (enables AI answers + real English slugs).
3. `npm run build && npx wrangler pages deploy dist`

author: ga1ien
body:
The compose default for `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` was a `service_role` JWT that did not verify against the stack's own `PGRST_JWT_SECRET` (Supabase's published local default). So it never worked as the "local stub" the README describes, and nothing records which secret did sign it. This repo is public, so it is removed as an unknown credential.

The replacement is `role=service_role` signed with the published default the same file sets: it works against this compose stack and grants nothing anywhere else. `harness credentials` verifies that by signature; the diff scanner takes a same-line `git-secret-allow` with the reason.

Whoever owns the old value should rotate it: it stays in this public repo's history.

author: areeb-ansari43
body:
Implements Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) via email code and a one-time Terms & Conditions popup modal for driver login on Virtual Car Hire driver portal.

### Summary of Changes:
1. **Two-Factor Login Flow (`portal/login.html`)**:
   - Password authentication step transitions seamlessly into a 6-digit numeric verification code entry screen.
   - Generates and stores 2FA code in Supabase via RPC (`create_2fa_code`).
   - Invokes the shared `send-email` Edge Function specifying `auth@fa-ibi.co.uk` as sender and the `2fa_code` template.
   - Shows a 30-second rate-limiting cooldown timer on the "Resend Code" button to prevent spamming.
   - Shows a checkmark success animation transition upon correct code entry.

2. **One-Time Terms & Conditions Popup (`portal/login.html` & `portal/dashboard.html`)**:
   - Triggered immediately after a driver's first-ever successful 2FA verification.
   - Covers automated email reminder enrollment for MOT, service, and PCO renewals, automatic cessation upon contract termination, and re-enrollment if returning later.
   - Requires simple acknowledgement ("I Understand & Continue") and records acceptance server-side in Supabase (`driver_tracks` & `drivers` tables via `accept_driver_terms` RPC).

3. **Database Migration (`supabase/migrations/20260330000002_driver_portal_2fa_and_terms.sql`)**:
   - Creates `portal_2fa_codes` table with hardened RLS.
   - Adds `terms_accepted_at` and `terms_accepted` columns to `driver_tracks` and `drivers`.
   - Security-definer RPC functions: `create_2fa_code`, `verify_2fa_code`, `accept_driver_terms`, and `check_driver_terms_accepted`.

4. **Automated Testing & Verification (`tests/test_2fa_and_terms.test.js`)**:
   - Complete unit and integration test suite verifying 2FA code generation, verification, resend cooldown, Edge Function email payload formatting, terms popup copy, and SQL migration definitions. All test suites pass 100%.

author: datagen24
body:
## What and why

`victual.openapi.json`'s `ExposedEntityEditRequiresAdmin` enum has carried
`["userfields", "userentities"]` since `7c4a60a0` (2026-09-04), and
`GenericEntityApiController::IsEntityWithEditRequiresAdmin()` reads it to gate `POST`,
`PUT` and `DELETE` on those two entities behind `ADMIN`. Four records still described it
as an empty enum with an open populate-or-delete question — the one reading that makes a
live permission gate look like dead code, and an invitation to "clean up" a working
check.

Comes from [`docs/architecture-rigor-review.md`](docs/architecture-rigor-review.md) row
**A7** and [plan 11](docs/plans/11-api-error-handling.md) **Q6**, which owned the
decision. Documentation only — no behaviour changes here.

Each document is treated as what it is, rather than uniformly rewritten:

- **The two architecture reviews are dated, point-in-time records, so they are
  annotated.** The rigor review states that convention itself at `:78-83`: the status
  table is the living tracker and finding bodies stay as written (A4's body still
  describes a method that has since landed, while its state cell reads closed). Row A7
  closes against 2026-09-04 with the evidence and notes the finding's second half is
  spent too — `BaseApiController` is now the only `HttpSpecializedException` catcher,
  not `UsersApiController`. It also corrects the body's `victual.openapi.json:6003` to
  `:11193`. The recommended-action item bundling A7 with A8 is marked done in both
  halves. The 2026-08-27 review's bullet is annotated in place, pointing at plan 11 for
  the whole list rather than pretending only the enum moved.
- **Plan 11 is a landed plan, so its open question is closed as answered.** The real gap
  was structural: `### Mass assignment` was the one proposed-change section with no
  `> **Landed**` blockquote, unlike `### API-key hygiene` which has two, though the work
  shipped 2026-09-04 and is recorded in the Today-section blockquote. It gets one,
  covering the blocklist, the populated enum, and that Q5's schema-derived allowlist is
  the half still waiting on 14 piece 2. Q6's response ended with an escape clause —
  delete the enum instead — that was never taken; it is now closed explicitly.

## Compatibility

- **Schema change?** None. No migration.
- **Changes an existing API response?** None. No code, spec or test file is touched —
  the diff is three Markdown files. The 403 this documents has been live since
  `7c4a60a0`.
- **Needs a manual step on upgrade?** None.

## Verification

Prose only (3 files, +34/−1), so the suite is not the gate for the change itself. What
is verifiable is that every fact asserted in the new text is true, and each was checked
against the tree before being written:

- `ExposedEntityEditRequiresAdmin` reads `["userfields", "userentities"]` (JSON read of
  `victual.openapi.json`), and `git show 7c4a60a0` confirms the `"enum": []` → two
  entries change.
- Both entities are in `ExposedEntity` (58 entries) and in neither `ExposedEntityNoEdit`
  nor `ExposedEntityNoDelete`, so the gate is reachable rather than shadowed.
- The three call sites are `:60` `AddObject`/POST, `:175` `DeleteObject`/DELETE and
  `:264` `EditObject`/PUT, each calling `CheckPermission(PERMISSION_ADMIN)`; verbs
  confirmed against `routes.php:192-194`.
- `grep` confirms `BaseApiController` is the only `HttpSpecializedException` catcher.
- The rigor review's A7 row still renders three cells against its header.

The suite was run anyway, after merging master into this branch, to confirm the branch is
green on a real database — `.devtools/pgsql/run-tests.sh wirecontract` → **OK (34 tests,
1172 assertions)**, and `run-tests.sh all` → **exit 0, SUITE PASSED**. Run under podman
against a session-private `victual-pg` container and network, per the collision note in
`memory/reference_local_environment.md`.

- [x] Exercised the changed paths on a running instance — n/a for prose; the documented
      gate was verified statically as above, and the full suite was run green
- [x] `.devtools/pgsql/run-tests.sh` — `all` passed, though the change touches no SQL
- [x] Result sets compared before and after — n/a, no query rewritten
- [ ] `SUITE_COVERAGE=1` — not run; no source file is touched, so coverage cannot move

## Notes for review

**The gate is still pinned by no test on `master`.** My brief said it was pinned by
`testTheRuntimeVocabulariesAreReadByTheApplication()` in
`tests/Pgsql/WireContractTest.php`. That test does not exist on `master` or on this
branch — it was added by `988281c0`, which is contained only by
`claude/vibrant-swanson-a638fb` and is unmerged. So the documentation is now right while
the enum's contents remain unpinned; nothing in this PR's text cites that test, so
nothing here goes stale if that branch changes shape.

**Four occurrences of the stale phrasing survive deliberately**, each with an adjacent
annotation: the rigor review's A7 finding body (per the doc's own convention), the
2026-08-27 review's bullet, plan 11's Today-section bullet, and Q6's question text. Plan
11's Today section is written in pre-landing voice by design — its neighbour describing
the missing `CalculateNextExecutionAssignments` permission check is equally superseded
and equally untouched. If the preference is to strike them instead, that is a one-line
change per site, but it would break the convention the rigor review states about itself.

**Nothing else tracks A7 or 11-Q6** — no ADR mentions the enum, and
`docs/plans/README.md` carries only the general pointer at `:134` plus a plan-11 row
whose open item (Q5's allowlist waiting on 14 piece 2) is still accurate and unchanged.

**This branch also carries master's merge** (fast-forward to `349cbce9`, the ADR-0028
timestamp work), so the diff against `master` should be the single documentation commit.

Chains removed:

| Chain | Identifiers | Linear |
|---|---|---|
| Astar zkEVM | `astar-zkevm` | PAY-16349 |
| Mode | `mode`, `mode-sepolia` | PAY-16352 |
| World Chain | `world-chain`, `world-chain-sepolia` | PAY-16354 |
| Plume | `plume`, `plume-testnet` | PAY-16355 |
| Old testnets | `zkatana`, `zkyoto`, `polygon-mumbai`, `ethereum-goerli`, `base-goerli`, `optimism-goerli`, `zora-goerli` | PAY-16356 |

What changed:

- `@crossmint/common-sdk-base` — dropped the names from `EVMBlockchain` and `EVMBlockchainTestnet`, and their rows in `BLOCKCHAIN_TO_COPY_NAME` and `BLOCKCHAIN_TO_CHAIN_ID`.
- `@crossmint/wallets-sdk` — dropped them from `TESTNET_AA_CHAINS`, `PRODUCTION_AA_CHAINS`, the `toViemChain` switch and `MAINNET_TO_TESTNET_MAP`. Also dropped the now-unused `mode`, `modeTestnet`, `plume` and `plumeTestnet` imports from `viem/chains`.
- `@crossmint/client-sdk-base` — dropped the `astar-zkevm` and `polygon-mumbai` cases in `getNFTLocator`.

### Two things to review

1. **`zora-goerli` is removed, `zora` and `zora-sepolia` stay.** Goerli is in the "deprecate old testnets" ticket (PAY-16356) and the network is long dead, so I read `zora-goerli` as part of that ticket rather than part of "Deprecate Zora". Say the word and I will put it back.

2. **The other 13 chains in the project are not in this PR.** Atleta, Astar, Boss, Rari, Xai, Coti, U2U, Zenchain, Hedera, Lightlink, Viction and Soneium appear in this repo **only** in generated files — `packages/wallets/src/openapi.json` (regenerated by `pnpm generate` from the backend spec) and `packages/client/base/src/lib/hosted-checkout/Order.ts` (a mirror of a backend type). Editing them by hand would be reverted on the next regeneration. They drop out of the SDK once the "Remove from Crossbitmain" tickets land. Their "Remove from Crossmint SDKs" tickets are therefore **not** linked here.

- `pnpm build:libs` — 16/16 packages build, so no dangling references to the removed names.
- `pnpm test:vitest` — 13/13 packages, 993 tests pass, 0 failures.
- `pnpm lint` — the changed files are clean. The repo's 36 pre-existing biome errors are unchanged (verified against a clean tree).
- The wallets build runs `pnpm generate` first; it produced no diff, which confirms the generated files are untouched.

## Package updates

`.changeset/deprecate-chains.md` — **patch** for `@crossmint/common-sdk-base`, `@crossmint/wallets-sdk` and `@crossmint/client-sdk-base`. These chains are already dead in practice, so the team is shipping the removal as a patch.

author: radnams
body:
## The report

An n8n dashboard showed: `Failed to save installed package. Cause: invalid input syntax for type integer: "1.1"`.

## Cause

n8n before 2.33.0 stores an installed community node's newest version in an `integer` column on PostgreSQL (`installed_nodes.latestVersion`), and takes that version from the last entry of the node's `version` array. Ours has been fractional since 0.2.3 (`1.1`, then `1.2` in 0.4.0), so every install on a PostgreSQL-backed n8n older than 2.33 fails. n8n changed the column in n8n-io/n8n#34717 (first released in 2.33.0). SQLite does not enforce the type, which is why it was never seen locally.

## Fix

The action node's versions are `[1, 1.1, 1.2, 2]`. Version 2 behaves exactly as 1.2; the earlier versions remain for saved workflows. A unit test keeps each node's newest version a whole number, and `RELEASING.md` states the rule.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on n8n 2.32.4 + PostgreSQL 16 with the published 0.4.0: the same error, with `"1.2"`.
- The 0.4.1 build installs on that same n8n (served from a local registry): `installed_nodes` records 2 and 1. It also installs on 2.38.1.
- New `scripts/check-postgres-install.sh` does that install through n8n's community-package API and now runs in CI. The existing Docker checks load `dist/` as a custom extension on SQLite, which records nothing in the database, so they could not catch this.
- `npm run check` (224 tests) and the other two Docker checks pass.

Not tagged or published.

Prepare Vela 1.25.0 so the merged framework APIs can ship together with compatible package versions. Consume 49 changesets into 24 version bumps, generate package changelogs and skill metadata, and prepare a 26-package publication plan. The plan carries forward the still-unpublished `@velajs/authz-cedar` and `@velajs/crypto` packages from the previous release.

Core and CRUD become 1.25.0; RPC and GraphQL become 1.1.0 and their packed peer ranges require core `^1.25.0`. Update the migration guide with these minimum versions, include the RPC changelog in its archive, and document the direct-publish permission required by npm trusted publishers.

Validation: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm release:check` (full workspace verification, Workers, peer/audit checks, exact archive consumers, and publication dry run), and inspection of all 26 archives and 40 internal dependency ranges. Frozen installation succeeds and the versioning command preserves the prepared plan when no changesets remain. Local verification passed 4,445 workspace tests, 145 CRUD conformance tests (4 skipped), 110 Workers/ALS tests, and 7 release-tool tests. [GitHub CI](https://github.com/velajs/vela/actions/runs/35654858940), Node 24/26, CodeQL, dependency review, secret scanning, and the high/critical audit all passed for `091c9d6`.

Publication requires a coordinated first-publication step: npm currently has no public package for `@velajs/authz-cedar`, `@velajs/crud-durable-objects`, `@velajs/crypto`, `@velajs/graphql`, `@velajs/rpc`, or `@velajs/tenant`. Follow `RELEASING.md` for maintainer publication using the CI-signed archives and trusted-publisher setup. Merging this PR triggers the main release workflow. No packages have been published during preparation. Update CLI starter pins after the new framework versions are available in the registry.

author: martinsousaa
body:
## 1. O modelo de imagem não existia

`gpt-image-2` **não existe** — os modelos são `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` e `gpt-image-2.5-flare`. O nome estava escrito à mão em **cinco lugares** e toda chamada voltava `404 model_not_found`.

Era a causa das imagens ruins, e a corrente inteira estava no código: o primário nunca gerava → tudo caía no Gemini → o pedido ao Gemini não mandava tamanho → voltava retangular → o enquadramento preenchia as sobras com faixa lisa. **"Imagens extremamente pequenas" e "fotos com margens laterais" eram o mesmo defeito.**

O conserto não foi trocar o nome nos cinco lugares — isso reabre no próximo rename. O nome mora num lugar só, é configurável por `OPENAI_MODELO_IMAGEM`, e em `model_not_found` o Studio **pergunta à conta** quais modelos de imagem ela tem e repete com o primeiro.

## 2. A paleta azul fixa saiu

`#E8EEF5` / `#1A3A6B` / `#4A7EC7` e a proibição de **marrom, laranja, vermelho e verde** valiam em toda peça de todo produto. Isso proibia literalmente a cena da caixa de relógios que o dono mostrou como referência — nogueira e dourado são marrom e laranja.

| | |
|---|---|
| Identidade da loja | Tipografia, ícones, cards, hierarquia, espaçamento — **não a cor** |
| Direção de arte | Deduzida do produto: cor, material, categoria, ocasião |
| Protagonismo | **55–70%** do quadro com texto, **65–80%** sem; produto enquadrado primeiro |
| Fundo desfocado | Quando cenário ou texto competirem com o produto |
| **Campo Ambientação** | Opcional, nas três telas. É tema, não roteiro: a cena varia entre as 8 |
| Tipo 8 | "ZERO TEXTO" + "escreva esta frase" era contradição — virou exceção única |
| Lista fixa de cômodos | Removida: marcador de taça não pertence a estante de livros |

## 3. Gemini passa a receber proporção

`responseFormat.image.aspectRatio: "1:1"`, e **repete sem o campo** se a API recusar (400). A documentação do Google se contradiz sobre o nome; chutar em silêncio seria o pior dos mundos — acharíamos que estava resolvido.

O preenchimento de faixa continua como último recurso, mas passa a **aparecer no diagnóstico da tela**. Ele só existia no `stderr` do Railway, e foi assim que as tarjas ficaram sem explicação por semanas: o Studio sabia e ninguém lia.

## A correção ficou num caminho só três vezes — por isso há uma varredura

Trocar a paleta no `PADRAO_VISUAL` e deixar `#E8EEF5` no preset do tipo 2, no do 7 e no bloco em inglês de `gerar_imagem_ia` seria mandar ao modelo a regra nova e a ordem contrária **na mesma mensagem**. Um caso de conferência monta os 8 prompts e reprova qualquer cor de marca que volte como obrigatória.

**O branco da capa continua** — não é cor de marca, é exigência de marketplace, e há caso para isso.

## Conferência

- **39 casos novos**, 0 falhas em 7 módulos
- `compileall` e `checar_ordem` limpos

body:
## Summary
- Practice and exam submissions ignore/reject client-authored `isCorrect`, scores, accuracy, and tier fields; correctness is computed only on the server inside a transaction.
- Answer IDs must belong to the submitted question; duplicate answer/question IDs are rejected; unknown item types fail closed instead of falling through to single-select grading.
- Practice retries use `Idempotency-Key` so network replays cannot double-insert attempts or inflate progress; exam resubmits return the finalized result without adding rows.
- Exam scores always use the assigned question count as the denominator (unanswered = incorrect), with safe clamping for zero/negative edge cases.
- Adds migration `011` for attempt idempotency uniqueness and integration tests covering foreign answers, duplicates, inactive questions, another user’s exam, empty/partial submits, concurrent submits, and client score injection.

## Test plan
- [ ] `cd backend/server && npm test` (unit + DB integration)
- [ ] Apply migration `011_attempt_idempotency_key.sql` on local DB
- [ ] Practice: submit a select-one answer; confirm feedback comes from server only
- [ ] Practice: retry the same request with the same `Idempotency-Key`; progress count unchanged
- [ ] Practice: submit an answer ID from another question; expect 4xx and no attempt row
- [ ] Exam: partial/empty submit; score denominator equals assigned count
- [ ] Exam: submit twice; second response is `alreadySubmitted` with no extra attempts

body:
## Summary

Stacked on #17 (`feat/storage-diagnostics`); no existing PR is merged or retargeted.

- Probe the actual SQLite version using an independent in-memory connection before persistent writable kernel file creation/open or migration. Recognize upstream 3.51.3+ and branch-specific 3.44.6+/3.50.7+ fixes; unknown/probe failures block writes without a runtime override.
- Preserve read-only history, in-memory kernels, separate DELETE-journal task cache, schema, UNKNOWN/no-retry, pairing and host-owned permissions.
- Add build-free `doctor:runtime`, expose the gate in both first-run doctors, and clarify that Node >=22.16 is only the API floor. No automatic global upgrade or worker termination.
- Log runtime versions in CI and add pinned Node 22.16.0 negative jobs on Ubuntu/Windows.

## Validation

- Windows Node 22.23.2 / SQLite 3.51.3 and Node 24.19.0 / SQLite 3.53.3: 707 tests each, 706 passed, zero failed, one existing expected symlink skip; all six offline demos each.
- Eight new regressions and scoped independent review/root verification passed; both final doctor suites 26/26 on each runtime.
- Official SHA256-checked portable Node 22.16.0 / SQLite 3.49.1: 11 synthetic negative scenario groups passed, including no new ledger/directories, no migration of existing marker fixture, preserved read-only and in-memory paths, doctor output, and empty production hook CLI responses.
- Exact-head remote CI must be checked separately after publication. See `docs/VALIDATION-SQLITE-RUNTIME-T001.md`.

## Limits

The upstream corruption race was not reproduced. Version gating is not database integrity, custom binary authenticity, other-worker attestation, or absence of all SQLite defects. Read-only opens can maintain WAL/SHM metadata. No actual host application, real model, real user ledger or backup/restore was exercised in this increment.

Upstream sources: [SQLite notice](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html#the_wal_reset_bug), [Node 22.16 bundled header](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v22.16.0/deps/sqlite/sqlite3.h#L143).

## Problem

Human acceptance #865 found that the deployed VIEPS runtime no longer resolves `MJB7703AA` when the stock-only filter is enabled, even though this dedicated #607 fixture previously had verified live stock.

Historical evidence in #626 confirms migration `0013` was applied remotely and live fixture stock/locations previously passed. The failure is therefore treated as fixture-row D1 drift/mutation, not as an un-applied original migration.

The repaired rows are explicitly synthetic fixture/test data, not real Jagports inventory evidence.

author: kazu-yamamoto
body:
GCM managed 2797 MB/s on the x86 machine measured, where counter mode with the
same key does 7194 -- and openssl's GCM does 4895.  The reason is that the two
halves were taken in step: the GHASH of a group could not start until the rounds
that produced it had finished, so the multiply unit sat idle through the rounds
and the round unit sat idle through the multiplies.

### Three changes, all on the x86 side

**The GHASH is of the group before, not this one.**  Held a group apart, its
inputs have been ready since the previous turn of the loop, so the processor can
run it through this group's rounds; AESENC and PCLMULQDQ do not want the same
port.  It costs one group of ciphertext kept aside and one more GHASH after the
loop.  This is where most of the gain is -- with it removed and everything else
kept, the loop drops back to 2669.

**The multiply is called directly** rather than through the branch pointer the
other GHASH callers use.  A call the compiler cannot see through cannot be
scheduled against anything.  The cost is that the GCM loops are then compiled
with the instruction, so `crypton_aes.c` installs them only once cpuid has
reported it -- which is what the AArch64 table already does with PMULL.

**The round keys are read from memory** rather than preloaded into registers.
Eight blocks and eleven to fifteen round keys do not fit in sixteen registers,
and the compiler was spilling: ninety-six stack accesses around a hundred
AESENCs.  AESENC takes a memory operand and the round keys stay in L1 between
groups, so the loads cost nothing and the blocks get the registers.  The rounds
are written out rather than looped, which is what `-funroll-loops` had been
recovering.

### Measured

| | before | after | openssl 3.5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AES-128-GCM | 2797 | 3458 | 4895 |
| AES-256-GCM | 2458 | 3053 | 4205 |

### What is left, and why it stops here

The rest of the gap is instruction-level interleaving -- the multiplies spread
among the rounds rather than following them -- which openssl does in
hand-written assembly.  Written in intrinsics it does not survive the compiler:
with `GH(j)` placed after round `j + 1` in the source, the disassembly comes
back as seventy-two AESENCs, then eight AESENCLASTs, then all twenty-seven
multiplies together, and the measurement is unchanged.  Two other things were
tried and dropped: a block at a time with the folds accumulated over eight
(2539, worse than the baseline) and `-fno-schedule-insns2` (3081).

Also measured and not pursued: `-funroll-loops` on top of this gets 3737 and
3227 by unrolling the group loop, so that the tail of one group and the head of
the next land in one basic block.  That is a library-wide build flag for a
change that belongs in one loop.

### Testing

Every mode at every key size, encrypted and decrypted -- ECB, CBC, CTR, CTR with
32-bit wrapping, XTS, GCM -- gives byte for byte what a build without the
instructions gives, in both the PCLMUL and non-PCLMUL configurations.  The GCM
known-answer tests, which #158 extended to 192 and 256, pass.

## Preview Settings

- [ ] Show commit-level mainnet preview links (Cloudflare creates deployments automatically)

## Summary

Make established NIP-46 sessions truthful and recoverable. Conduit now owns request correlation and relay-subscription lifecycle, detects unusable transports immediately, verifies the exact account after resume, and preserves the established account workspace while signing is recoverable.

## Planning and Public Context

- Implementation plan prepared: Yes; this is PR 1 of the four-PR signer reliability sequence.
- Existing public context checked: `docs/knowledge/decentralized-network-product-posture.md`, `docs/knowledge/external-nostr-references.md`, current NIP-46, and current Clave compatibility guidance.
- Public context delta: None. Platform-specific connection guidance follows in PR 2.

## Implementation

- Add a Conduit-owned NIP-46 RPC lifecycle over nostr-tools cryptography and relay primitives.
- Classify unavailable, malformed, rejected, and unsupported responses without leaving pending requests stranded.
- Track each relay response subscription, survive partial failure, and invalidate the session when every route is unusable.
- Abort timed-out requests and fence late responses and superseded subscription callbacks.
- Replace the one-use nostrconnect listener with the same established transport used by bunker sessions.
- Add adapter draining so a request already awaiting signer approval can finish exactly once across an app switch while new requests remain gated.
- Reopen subscriptions and verify the exact account after foreground/online resume without replaying a domain action.
- Separate established account ownership from live signer readiness so a recoverable transport failure does not reinterpret the workspace as guest state.

## Acceptance Criteria and Evidence

| ID | Observable criterion | Evidence / test | Environment and signer fidelity | Current-head result | Gap / owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC-1 | Partial relay failure remains usable; all-route failure becomes recoverable instead of falsely connected | `tests/nip46-rpc.test.ts` | Deterministic relay-pool seam | Pass | Real relay loss remains device QA |
| AC-2 | `auth_url` approval may background Conduit; request A settles once, request B is gated, exact identity is reverified, then request C is admitted | `tests/nip46-rpc.test.ts`, `tests/remote-signer.test.ts`, `tests/remote-signer-resume.test.ts` | Owned transport and adapter seams | Pass | Current Clave device QA required |
| AC-3 | Null, empty, malformed, rejected, unsupported, canceled, and late responses settle deterministically | `tests/nip46-rpc.test.ts`, `tests/remote-signer.test.ts` | Protocol seam | Pass | None |
| AC-4 | Restores cannot install a transport that closed after its final identity response | `tests/remote-signer.test.ts` | Restore lifecycle seam | Pass | None |
| AC-5 | Recoverable NIP-46 loss retains the verified account scope but removes signer capabilities and protected signer leases | `tests/auth-context.test.ts`, `tests/account-network-hook-authority-timing.test.ts` | Auth/session seams | Pass | Surface adoption follows in PRs 3-4 |
| AC-6 | No app/default relay, NIP-65, or kind `10050` authority changes are included | Changed-file and diff review | Repository diff | Pass | None |

- Critical flows changed: NIP-46 pairing handoff, restore, request lifecycle, background/foreground recovery, account/readiness state.
- Playwright or smoke tests added or updated: No browser shard; this PR adds deterministic protocol and auth lifecycle coverage.

body:
## Phase 7 §36: global search across the current workspace

A search box in the portal topbar. **Ctrl/Cmd+K**, or **/** when you aren't typing in a field, opens it. It finds jobs, sites, contractors, documents, invoices, quotes and people, **in the current workspace only** (owner decision). Cross-workspace search belongs to the Platform console.

**`GET /api/search?q=`:** the workspace comes from the session, never from the request. Each result group applies its own screen's access rule. A group the caller may not see is left out entirely rather than shown empty.

| Group | Who sees it |
|---|---|
| Jobs, sites, contractors | `board.view`. Jobs and sites also respect the member's site restriction, and binned jobs are excluded |
| Documents | Served by **the document register's own handler**, called with the caller's own request, so its capability check, live-document filter and site rules (including Q5) apply unchanged |
| Invoices, quotes | Same rule as the Invoice Tracker: Administrator rank plus the ledger/quote capability |
| People | `users.view` |

**Bug fixed along the way:** `like()` is case-sensitive on Postgres, so the **document register's own search** missed "Invoice.pdf" when you typed "invoice" in Production. Both searches now use `app/lib/search-text.ts` (lower-case both sides; `%` and `_` are stripped).

**UI:** debounced; keyboard navigation; results grouped by type. A job opens its drawer in place, a document opens in a new tab, and sites and invoices/quotes link to their own screens. On a phone the box collapses to an icon.

### Verified locally
- Source suite: 4440 tests, **0 failing**.
- tsc 22 and lint 19/59, both identical to baseline. Build passes.
- 8 live suites green, including `global-search` 6/6 and `phase-nine-security` 15/15.
