body:
## Context

Current `dev` already includes the motion-side solution from #716: planner-certified short pivot joins plus the FTC `PIVOT` state. Reintroducing a second distance-based sub-path transition protocol would duplicate that state machine and could convert obstacle-related boundaries incorrectly.

This follow-up closes the remaining anti-fragmentation verification gap for #593 without changing motion or blade behavior.

## What changed

- Single-source the existing 25% connector split warning threshold in a pure helper, preserving the current INFO/WARN behavior.
- Test zero, below-threshold, and exact-threshold warning cases.
- Add a non-vacuous recorded-area regression using shipped settings: five headland passes, 0.16 m operation width, 0.18 m headland, zero chassis inset, and 0.20 m connector/minimum radii.
- Exercise production-equivalent pivot sweep and soft-boundary limits.
- Bound both planner diagnostics and the executor-facing result: at most 4 splits, at most 20% split share, `subpaths == splits + 1`, and at most 5 sub-paths.
- Document the warning and regression contract in the coverage codemap.

## Alternatives considered

- The older proposal to infer a direct transition from endpoint distance alone was rejected because a short Euclidean gap can cross a hole or obstacle.
- A separate planner-metadata/behavior/FTC-phase protocol was rejected after #716 merged; #716 already owns safe tiny-gap motion with explicit pivot geometry and sweep checks.
- A production rejection threshold was not added. Existing real geometries can legitimately need multiple obstacle-routing splits, and there is not yet evidence for a safe universal reject percentage. The regression bound and warning are intentionally evidence/diagnostic controls.

## Validation

- Clean non-root Lyrical build: `mowgli_interfaces`, `mowgli_coverage`
- Full `mowgli_coverage` suite: 97 tests, 0 errors, 0 failures, 7 skipped
- clang-format 18 dry-run on every touched C++ file
- `git diff --check`
- Independent Sol review and final Astra review; the Astra finding about disabled pivot limits was fixed before this PR

## Safety and hardware status

This follow-up changes no planner decisions, FTC state transitions, blade commands, or robot motion. It only extracts an equivalent logging predicate and adds regression evidence. The blade-on pivot motion merged in #716 remains **HARDWARE_REQUIRED**: no physical mower or field validation was performed here.

Fixes #593

author: arcavenai
body:
## Why

A returning user cannot get a working seat from this README, and the gap is
exactly the thing the repo is about.

Install ends at the skill and the command, which is honestly all `install.sh`
does: it installs `skills/director` and `commands/director.md`, then creates
the state root. It does not install `director-mcp-seat`, does not create
`~/.director/bin`, and says nothing about a broker.

Meanwhile the fleet runs on the seat. marvel roles on this cluster launch
`~/.director/bin/director-mcp-seat` as their MCP server, and the source lives
at `probe/nats-phase-0/director-mcp-seat`. So there is an undocumented manual
step between "I followed the README" and "my seat can send a message", and
everything needed to close it was already in the repo, just not written down.

I verified the absence before writing rather than trusting the report: grep
for `director-mcp-seat`, `global tier`, `global-tier`, `leaf` and
`nats-global-tier` returned zero hits across both README.md and docs/.

## What changed

Install gains a "bus seat, by hand" section covering the two files under
`probe/nats-phase-0/`, the one-time registration that is correct both for a
marvel-managed session and a hand-started seat, a table of what the launcher
needs and where it reads it from in each mode, the cluster `bus.seat` block
the hand-run password depends on, and the codex `env_vars` line together with
its diagnostic.

Every value in that section is read out of `director-mcp-seat` itself rather
than written from memory: the `DIRECTOR_MCP_BIN` default, the
`director-seat` identity fallback, the `DIRECTOR_TEAM` and
`DIRECTOR_WORKSPACE` refusal, the `~/.marvel/state/nats/director.pass` path,
and the `nats://127.0.0.1:4222` default.

It says plainly that this is Phase 0 probe material being run in anger rather
than a packaged install, because that is the honest state and a reader who
expects a packaged install will otherwise think they did it wrong.

The Layout block listed `probe/nats-phase-0/` but not
`probe/nats-global-tier/`, which holds the brief, the mechanics note, the
mokuzai recipe, the `hub/` directory, the leaf config example and the verify
scripts. Added, and `director-mcp-seat` is now called out under
`nats-phase-0/` so Install has something to point at.

No installer written. This documents what exists, per the ticket.

## One process note

The shared checkout of this repo on mokuzai is currently in use: it sits on
`test/global-roundtrip-receipts` with two untracked scripts in
`probe/nats-global-tier/` that were modified minutes before I started. Rather
than switch branches under another session, I made this change in a separate
clone at the same commit as `origin/main`. Nothing in the shared checkout was
touched.

author: acontrer31
body:
## Valor de tabla DNRPA: que lo traiga JARVIS

El valor de tabla es el número del que cuelga toda la financiación: el arancel del registro es el **1%** y el honorario de la agencia el **2,5%**. Hasta ahora lo traía una persona a mano. Si esa persona no está, o no sabe que el valor declarado va **siempre en 1**, la cotización sale mal o no sale.

Ahora hay un botón **"Consultar"** al lado del campo, en la ficha del auto.

### Por qué Claude y no un parser

El registro no tiene API: la única forma es leer la página que devuelve el formulario. Un parser con expresiones regulares contra el HTML de un sitio del gobierno es de las cosas más frágiles que se pueden escribir — el día que cambien una tabla por un `div`, devuelve el número de al lado **sin avisar**. Claude lee la página como la leería una persona, y con `output_config.format` la respuesta viene validada contra un esquema.

### Que no invente un número es la regla principal

De este número sale un presupuesto que se le muestra a un cliente. Cuatro capas para que no pase:

1. El esquema tiene `encontrado` y `motivo`, así que **el camino de salida ante la duda es decir que no lo encontró**.
2. Las instrucciones lo dicen explícito: no estimes, no deduzcas del total, no uses conocimiento previo del modelo.
3. Una verificación después, por si vuelve un valor absurdo (0, negativo).
4. **La pantalla no toca el campo cuando no se encontró** — con test que lo protege.

### Decisiones que importan

- **La clave de Anthropic es de servidor**, como `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`. Nunca sale del backend.
- **La patente se lee de la base, no del pedido.** Si viniera del cliente, cualquiera con sesión podría hacer que el servidor consulte patentes ajenas.
- **Rate limit de 20/hora por usuario**: cada consulta cuesta plata y sale un pedido al registro desde la IP del despliegue.
- **"No encontrado" devuelve 200, no 500.** El pedido se procesó bien y la respuesta es "no está". Con 500 la pantalla mostraría "algo salió mal" en vez del motivo, que es lo único accionable.
- **La URL del registro es variable de entorno**: los sitios del gobierno mueven las URLs, y conviene que el arreglo sea cambiar un valor en Vercel y no desplegar.

## Tests de componentes, que no había

Los tres errores de esta semana — los puntitos del dashboard, la carga de fotos que se cortaba, el campo que mostraba "automatica" en un aviso publicado — estaban **los tres en componentes**, y toda la batería apuntaba a los módulos puros. Estaba probando bien justo la parte que menos se rompía.

Van vitest + jsdom + testing-library y 15 tests nuevos (**115 en total**).

## Verificación

- `tsc --noEmit` limpio · `eslint` limpio · **115 tests** · `next build` compila

## ⚠️ No funciona hasta configurar dos variables en Vercel

| Variable | Qué es |
|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | console.anthropic.com → API Keys |
| `DNRPA_URL_CONSULTA` | La dirección del formulario de consulta de aranceles |

Sin ellas el botón contesta con un mensaje claro ("falta X en el servidor") en vez de romperse. **Esta parte no pude probarla de punta a punta**: el entorno donde desarrollo tiene bloqueado `dnrpa.gov.ar` por política de red, así que el pedido al registro está escrito pero nunca se ejecutó contra el sitio real.

author: homesignalg
body:
**NO PRODUCERS / NO ACTIVE FEEDS / NO IDENTITY / NO LIFECYCLE RESOLUTION / NO GEOGRAPHY / NO RESIDENT READERS / NO MAP1 / NO MAPS / NO CUTOVER.**

Atlas and Epoch are seeded `active_state = 'NOT_ACTIVE'` with `schedule_cron` NULL. Nothing that already exists is touched: `app_projects` (3,224,655 rows), `app_zip_projects_markers`, `national_dc_for_zip`, `development_reports`, `geo.*`, `homesignalmap.html`, `lib/map.js` and the MAPS generator are all unchanged.

## Three tables, not four

`dc_source_record_state` is **DEFERRED**, and that is a finding rather than a deferral of work. It was an artifact of the v2 contract's own identity error: v2 keyed observations `UNIQUE (source_key, semantic_observation_fingerprint)` **globally**, which collapsed a repeated publisher assertion into one row and therefore destroyed the very history `last_seen` would have to be derived from. With **acquisition-scoped** observation identity, every one of those facts is a query over immutable rows — `first_seen`, `last_seen`, `current`, and not-seen as an anti-join between consecutive complete runs. Materialising them would be a cache with its own staleness and a second owner of truth.

| table | holds |
|---|---|
| `public.dc_source` | mutable registry, **versioned** capability contract |
| `public.dc_acquisition_run` | one row per **attempt** + an **immutable contract snapshot** |
| `public.dc_source_observation` | immutable evidence, **acquisition-scoped** identity |

## Enforced in the database, not in a producer convention

- Only `completeness_state = 'SUCCESS_COMPLETE'` may advance observations — as a CHECK constraint *and* in the observation insert guard.
- `SUCCESS_COMPLETE` is a comparison, never an opinion: HTTP 200 + artifact sha + schema fingerprint + `records_parsed = records_seen`, **and** at or above the source's anti-truncation floor. A short artifact cannot be declared complete and later read as removals.
- Capability enforcement reads the **run's frozen contract**, never the live registry, so a registry edit cannot reinterpret an earlier acquisition. Checks 45/46 are the headline: with the same geometry payload, the pre-edit run still accepts and the post-edit run refuses.
- Observations refuse UPDATE, DELETE **and TRUNCATE** (a row trigger never fires for TRUNCATE, so immutability needed its own statement trigger or it was one command from being untrue). Runs refuse DELETE and TRUNCATE and are immutable once completed, except `advanced_observations` / `notes`.
- Same-run duplicates fail three ways (ordinal, publisher id, semantic fingerprint). The **globally**-unique variants of the last two are pinned **absent**, because dropping that prohibition would otherwise move no number.
- Unknown stays NULL: no empty-string sentinels, no fabricated publisher id, geometry, status or record-byte hash. A publisher that literally publishes the word "Unknown" is stored verbatim — the prohibition is on *our* fabrication.
- RLS on, **zero policies**, zero `anon`/`authenticated` privileges.

## Tests

`public.dc_step2a_selftest()` — **54 checks, 54 passing** against the live database. Every guard above appears as a negative, each paired with a positive control so a blanket deny cannot score green (a well-formed observation is accepted; the same fingerprint and the same publisher id in a *different* run are accepted; a `SUCCESS_ZERO` release is representable). `dc_step2a_expect_fail()` requires the error to **match the guard under test**, so a typo reports as a failure rather than banking as a refusal.

**Proven load-bearing by mutation against the live guards** (each inside a rolled-back subtransaction): drop the observation guard → 11 checks fail; add the forbidden global unique → 2 (the structural pin **and** its positive control); drop `dc_run_only_complete_advances` → 1; widen either seeded floor → 1; flip a seeded capability → 1; flip Atlas to ACTIVE → 1; grant `anon` SELECT → 1. Restored → 0.

⚠️ **One mutation originally survived, and check 52 exists because of it.** Widening Atlas's floor 1000 → 1 moved no check: check 20 proves the floor *mechanism* on the selftest's own fixture source, and nothing defended the *measured value* on the seeded ones. Found by mutation, not by review.

## Committed vs live

All 7 function bodies are byte-identical to `docs/dc-step2a-foundation.sql` (md5 of `pg_proc.prosrc`, recorded in the file header), all `SECURITY INVOKER` with a pinned `search_path`. Object set matches exactly: 22 check constraints, 3 FKs, 12 non-pkey indexes, 6 triggers, 0 policies, 0 anon/authenticated grants. Live rows: `dc_source` 2, `dc_acquisition_run` 0, `dc_source_observation` 0, selftest leakage 0.

Security advisors report exactly three entries for these tables, all the same informational *"RLS enabled, but no policies exist"* — which is the designed posture (zero resident access), the same one `dashboard_admins` and `dashboard_snapshots` already carry. No other advisory.

## Isolation gate

`check-dc-step2a-isolation` fails if any resident-facing file names one of these tables. It ships a `--self-test` proving it can fail, refuses a suspiciously small scan (an instrument must prove it ran), and is token-bounded so `national_dc_source_key_unique` cannot manufacture a violation. Mutation-verified against a real file: planting a reference in `lib/map.js` turns it red, removing it turns it green.

## Rollback

`docs/dc-step2a-rollback.sql` drops every object explicitly and **never with CASCADE** — an unexpected dependent is a reason to stop loudly, not to delete more. It fails closed on an external foreign key, a dependent view, or any other function whose body names these objects (a body reference is not a catalog dependency, so nothing would otherwise refuse the drop), and reports the run/observation counts it is about to destroy.

## Concurrency

Re-checked against `115f8f0` immediately before this PR: zero occurrences of these object names on `main`, and of 253 remote branches only this one carries them. The single `dc_source` substring elsewhere in the repo is inside `national_dc_source_key_unique`. **GENUINE GAP.**

## Review question

> Does this change preserve one canonical truth path, or does it create a shortcut/second way to decide the same fact?

It preserves it and defends it in CI. These tables hold what a *publisher asserted*; they carry no canonical entity identity, no lifecycle resolution and no geography, so they cannot express a HomeSignal answer. The canonical result owner remains `app_zip_projects_markers` and the canonical classification owner remains `lib/map.js::statedDataCenter`; neither is touched, and the new gate fails the moment a resident surface reads around them.

---

Offline unit suite: 145 passed, 0 failed. The 20 `.browser.test.mjs` files fail in this sandbox with `Cannot find package 'playwright'` — environmental and pre-existing, unrelated to this change; CI installs Playwright.

author: anandsundaram-hash
body:
The NDA authority repository grew a `signatureEvidence` object and one exhaustive expectation wasn't widened with it, so a governed suite on the **NDA stage** ran 3 of 4.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `nda-authority-repository` suite | 3 of 4 | **4 of 4** |
| Signature-evidence fields asserted | 0 of 7 | **7 of 7** |
| Production change | — | **none** |

## The fixture had to change first

Six of the seven fields came back `undefined`, because the fixture row didn't carry those columns. **Asserting `undefined` would have been worthless** — it passes whether or not the repository reads the column at all, so it makes the suite green while pinning nothing about the mapping it exists for.

The fixture now carries real, distinct values (document hash, signature method, two signatory names, certificate hash, private evidence ref) and the expectation asserts each. `signedAt` is asserted against `effective_from`, because there's no separate `signed_at` column and the repository says so in its own comment.

## `toEqual` kept, deliberately

The case is named *reads only one tenant, event, and declared supplier entity* — its exhaustiveness is how it proves nothing extra leaked into the row. `toMatchObject` would have turned it green in one line while **deleting the fencing property the case exists for**: a gate satisfied by weakening the gate.

**Mutations:**

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `certificateSha256` mapped to the wrong column | **1 fails** |
| an extra field added to the returned object | **1 fails** |

The first proves the new assertions are real, not `undefined` placeholders. The second proves exhaustiveness survived — it's precisely the mutation `toMatchObject` would have let through.

`nda-authority-repository.ts` is byte-identical to `origin/main`.

## Known gaps

- **The fixture values are invented**, not drawn from a real NDA. Distinct and internally consistent, which is what a mapping assertion needs — but not evidence that a real row looks like this.
- **This asserts the mapping, not the authority.** Whether a signature method or certificate hash is *correct* for a given executed NDA is a different question no case here reaches.

Lane: `global-control-lane`. One test file — no product surface, tenant data, schema, migration, flag, code path, or runtime behaviour.

### Work issue

Addresses #668 (control #667)

### Stage 2 audit

Corrects the two valid findings from #686's completed Stage 2 audit of merged PR #683 (merge commit 68f18cbdc0a8471ea779b03fdd2e672d186c0d26):

1. **A newer registration alone was treated as proof an older same-lineage checkout is inactive/disposable.** `isSuperseded` (registration ordering) was previously sufficient by itself to make a same-lineage predecessor removal-eligible. `reconcile()` now additionally requires the same durability (branch tip provably merged into the default branch) AND staleness (no worktree-local git activity within the grace period) test the legacy/unattributed branch already used, via a new shared `isDurablyObsolete()` helper. author: egurucharri
diegosouzapw
body:
Closes #13931

## Root cause

`getComboBuilderOptions()` writes `qualifiedModel` as `${providerId}/${modelId}` (the raw `provider_nodes`/connection id) for every provider except the hardcoded `"opencode"` special case. A custom OpenAI-compatible connection (e.g. embeddings) backed by a `provider_nodes` row with its own routing `prefix` never gets that prefix applied, so the combo the builder creates is unresolvable by `/v1/embeddings`, whose resolver (`parseEmbeddingModel` + the `providerConfig` fallback) only ever matches a static registry id or a `provider_nodes.prefix`, never a raw node/connection id.

- `src/lib/combos/builderOptions.ts:203` — `providerVisual.alias` for a non-system provider already computes `providerNode?.prefix || providerId`, but that value was never reused for the routing prefix.
- `src/lib/combos/builderOptions.ts:307-309` — `addModelOption` sets `qualifiedModel = ${providerId}/${modelId}` (raw id).
- `src/lib/combos/builderOptions.ts:710-711` (pre-fix) — `routingPrefix = providerId === "opencode" ? providerVisual.alias : providerId`, so only `opencode` was rewritten.
- `src/lib/combos/builderOptions.ts:567-577` — `rewriteQualifiedModelPrefix` is a no-op whenever `routingPrefix === providerId`, i.e. for every other provider.

## Fix

Generalize the routing-prefix rule in `getComboBuilderOptions()`: any provider backed by a `provider_nodes` row with its own `prefix` now uses that prefix (the same mechanism the `opencode` → `oc` alias already relies on), instead of only the hardcoded `opencode` special case:

```ts
const nodePrefix = toStringOrNull(providerNode?.prefix);
const routingPrefix =
  providerId === "opencode" ? providerVisual.alias : nodePrefix || providerId;
rewriteQualifiedModelPrefix(modelMap, providerId, routingPrefix);
```

Verified chat-side resolution already accepts `<node-prefix>/model` for a `provider_nodes`-backed connection (`src/sse/services/auth.ts:955-980` expands a user-facing node prefix back to the internal connection id during combo/credential resolution) — so this generalization is safe for chat combos too, not just embeddings.

## Regression test

New file `tests/unit/13931-embedding-combo-builder-prefix-repro.test.ts` — seeds a `provider_nodes` row (`prefix: "sf"`) and a connection whose `provider` is that node's raw id, then asserts `getComboBuilderOptions()` emits the prefixed `qualifiedModel`.

RED (unfixed code):
```
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: combo builder must emit qualifiedModel "sf/BAAI/bge-m3" (node prefix) so /v1/embeddings can resolve it — got "openai-compatible-embeddings-conn-9c1f0a3b8e2d4c56/BAAI/bge-m3"
```

GREEN (fixed code):
```
✔ #13931: combo builder qualifiedModel for a custom embeddings connection uses the node prefix, not the raw connection/provider id (13915.46367ms)
tests 1
pass 1
fail 0
```

## Gates run

- `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/13931-embedding-combo-builder-prefix-repro.test.ts` → pass 1 / fail 0
- `node --import tsx/esm --test` over the touched-area suite (13 files: `combo-builder-options-route`, `combo-builder-opencode-prefix`, `issue-11433-opencode-alias-collision`, `radar-combo-suggestions`, `repro-6975`, `combo-builder-model-source-5477`, `repro-6957`, `combo-hidden-update-12836`, `combo-fingerprint-pin-6696`, `combo-builder-effort-variants-8072`, `hard-session-lease-bypass-inventory`, `combo-builder-eligible-connection-2057`, `combo-builder-fingerprint-expansion`) → pass 46 / fail 0
- `npm run typecheck:core` → exit 0
- `npx eslint --suppressions-location config/quality/eslint-suppressions.json <changed files>` → exit 0
- `node scripts/check/check-file-size.mjs` → no offenders on touched files
- `node scripts/check/check-complexity.mjs` → OK — 2904 violations (baseline 3218)
- `node scripts/check/check-cognitive-complexity.mjs` → OK — 1316 violations (baseline 1437)
- `node scripts/check/check-changelog-integrity.mjs` → OK

## Existing tests aligned

`tests/unit/combo-builder-options-route.test.ts:259` — updated the assertion from `provider.models[0].qualifiedModel === "openai-compatible-demo/gpt-custom"` to `"gd/gpt-custom"`. The test already asserted `provider.prefix === "gd"` two lines above; it previously locked in the buggy raw-id output as "expected". This is an alignment to the corrected contract, not a weakening — the assertion still checks an exact string, just the correct one.

Plan-file: `_tasks/pipeline/bugs/2-implementing/13931-fix-api-combo-builder-writes-members-as-connection-provider-un.plan.md`

author: ice1x
body:
## Summary

First slice of **#523 (multi-database support)**. Introduces the multi-database catalog for the native engine: one process can hold several named databases side by side behind an always-present, **protected default**, served over HTTP. A client that names no database sees exactly the previous single-graph behaviour — **zero behaviour change by default**.

After epic #444 removed the KV engine, multi-db serving was greenfield (only a hardcoded `DEFAULT_DB` const + a hardcoded `GET /databases` existed; `src/cypher/admin.rs` was orphaned with no callers). This lands the catalog type and its HTTP lifecycle.

## Scope boundary (intentional)

Lifecycle only. **Routing a query to a chosen non-default database** — the HTTP path selector, the Bolt `db` field (today parsed into `_extra` and ignored), and reviving Cypher `USE` — is **slice 2**, as are per-database durable WAL directories. A created database is listable and droppable but not yet a query target, mirroring Neo4j's split between `CREATE DATABASE` and `USE`. Non-default databases are in-memory for now.

## Changes

- **`src/database_registry.rs` (new)** — `DatabaseRegistry` (`name -> Arc<NativeService>` over a sorted `BTreeMap` behind an `RwLock`, plus a direct `default` handle so `default_service()` is lock-free and infallible), `validate_db_name` (1–63 chars of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, alnum/underscore first), and `RegistryError` {`InvalidName`, `AlreadyExists`, `NotFound`, `ProtectedDefault`}. Gated behind `http` (its only consumer is the native HTTP surface, and it shares that module's `DEFAULT_DB`).
- **`src/native_api.rs`** — `NativeApiState` gains a `registry` field whose default entry is the **same `Arc`** as `service`, so existing single-db handlers are untouched. `GET /databases` now enumerates the registry; new `POST /databases` (create → 201) and `DELETE /databases/{name}` (drop → 200); `From<RegistryError> for ApiError` (400 / 409 / 404). Module doc refreshed.
- **`src/api.rs`** — new `CreateDatabaseRequest` DTO.
- **`src/lib.rs`** — register the http-gated module.
- **`tests/http_api_tests.rs`** — 5 integration tests for create/list/drop and the 400/409/404 error paths.

## Tests & gates

- 10 inline unit tests (default-only listing, **id/node-space isolation across databases**, sorted list, duplicate = conflict, invalid-name rejection, drop protected/missing) + 5 HTTP integration tests.
- Local gates green: `cargo fmt`; `clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`; `cargo doc -D warnings`; full `cargo test` (structural meta-tests intact); doctests; `cargo check -p drevo-py --lib`; wasm (`--no-default-features --features wasm`). The existing `/databases == ["drevo"]` durable-server test still passes unchanged.

## Summary

The harness could silently corrupt a measurement: a missing or malformed agent outcome became a zero-cost run, a negative token value passed through, and the compare kept only lane totals so a malformed outcome counted as a failure.

author: iryna-kahamlyk
body:
JIRA: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/TINKERPOP-3248

**Summary**

Adds support for the Gremlin Character type to gremlin-go, in both GremlinLang text generation and GraphBinary serialization.

Go's rune is only an alias for int32, so it can't be distinguished from an int in a type switch. This introduces a new exported type, Char, that callers use to explicitly mark a value as a Character (e.g. g.Inject(gremlingo.Char('a'))).

Some simple instruction updates

Summary by Bito

This PR corrects the CLI v2 TUI upgrade instructions for environments where the experience design system is consumed through a local pnpm workspace checkout. author: feliperun
body:
Three defects found in one week share a shape, and naming the shape is worth
more than the three fixes:

- a Definition of Done proof whose `--test-name-pattern` matches no test prints
  a tick for the file, reports `tests 1 pass 1 fail 0`, and exits `0`;
- a gate killed for memory reports a failure indistinguishable from a red test;
- a check that never ran renders as "no checks reported" — exactly like one
  that passed.

**An absence that looks like an approval.** A gate that did not run and a gate
that passed have to be distinguishable from the outside, or whoever reads it
trusts the silence.

## The newly found one

"No checks reported" has two causes and GitHub renders them identically:

1. A release pull request opened by `GITHUB_TOKEN` gets no workflow run,
   deliberately, to avoid recursion. Benign and expected — our own
   `release-please.yml` header documents it.
2. A **conflicted** pull request also gets none, because the merge ref is never
   built. That branch is conflicted *and* untested.

The reasoning "release PRs run no checks, so the main-branch CI is the real
gate" is correct for case 1 and would merge an untested conflicted branch in
case 2. It was caught this week only because a `git merge-tree --write-tree` was
run for an unrelated reason.

## What this adds

`AGENTS.md` gains a fourth authoring rule beside the three already paid for by
incidents: ask `mergeable` and `mergeStateStatus` separately before merging,
and treat `UNKNOWN` as "ask again" rather than an answer — GitHub computes
mergeability on demand, so the first reply is often not final. Verified while
merging four PRs this week.

It also names the shared shape, so the next instance is recognised rather than
diagnosed from scratch.

`docs/ROADMAP.md` gains `RM-050` for the general shape and `RM-051` for the
undecided part: whether the merge rule also wants a mechanical guard, or whether
a written rule is enough when the one cutting releases is always an agent.

Found by the session driving `durable-state-integrity`; the mergeability
refinement was verified here.

## Verification

`npm run check` 302 files; `npm run typecheck` clean; `docs-map`,
`declared-paths`, `root-pointers` and `ci-policy` 33/33.

Closes #7

Implements the minimal Python realization of the durable execution-state contract defined in FlossWare/loom-ai#1012.

- Adds a small `ExecutionStateStore` protocol.
- Adds a filesystem-backed JSON implementation so process-boundary behavior can be qualified without selecting a database.
- Persists execution identity, Intent, resumable state, evidence/provenance, status, metadata, and representation version.
- Distinguishes missing state from corrupt state.
- Uses atomic file replacement for snapshot publication.
- Treats interruption as distinct from successful completion.
- Keeps persistence outside Worker and Arbiter responsibilities.

This deliberately does not add a resume subsystem, transport endpoint, database integration, scraping, or model/provider behavior. Those belong to the next process-boundary qualification slice once this boundary is reviewed.

## The intake (walt/math convention, adjudication PENDING)

- **Verbatim parent** `walt/math/outcome_grounded_policy_learning_v0.1.md` (*Outcome-grounded autonomous policy learning for Texas 42*, hand-delivered 2026-09-21), checksum-pinned `bd259eff…`; written against main `afd46420` exactly.
- **Maintained intake companion**: claim-by-claim audit (**no unsound claim found**), vocabulary and code-boundary audits, candidate obligations OG-O1..O10, the OG-A adjudication agenda (still Jason's to rule), dated markers recording each in-session build authorization. The parent's §10 verifier pair was not delivered — recorded, on the agenda.
- **Intake-authored scratch verifier**: 10 exact-rational check families, **3,886 instances PASS** twice.

## The instrument (`experiments/og-learning/`, exploratory tier)

A Rust crate consuming the walt engine read-only (32 law-sized gates, clippy clean, no floats anywhere):

- **Actor**: rational multiplicative-weights softmax over typed scheme expressions (θ = log r never materialized; every probability and draw exact-rational).
- **Signal**: on-policy complete deals, make/set only — no teacher, no solver, no human tactics; LOO baselines; multi-step generations under the §4 L1 audit.
- **Constructor** (§5): a declared typed language of 539 bounded expressions; panel dedup; g_F covariance scores at coefficient zero; top-3 admitted per generation at weight 1; admissions persisted as canonical s-expressions.
- **Evidence rules** (§8): fixed-checkpoint Hoeffding and empirical-Bernstein (exact-rational upper bounds), and **anytime-valid promotion** consuming the adjudicated CE-T4/T5 betting mixtures (`walt::solver::evidence::BoundedMeanMixture` is the authority; the campaign's gcd-free integer hot path is gate-checked equal) — one α_k = δ/(k(k+1)) per candidate, optional stopping at every n.
- **Multifidelity harness** (§6): declared proxies, two-batch estimator with per-batch EB radii, measured covariance/costs/allocation per stream, plus a `pilot` subcommand for real-policy-pair pilots.

## The campaigns (records govern; EXPLORATORY, target-specific; disjoint seed ranges; untouched exams)

| Campaign | Lineup | Rule | Exam (uniform → learned) | Paired | Exact 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| og-v1 | random-legal | fixed library, Hoeffding | 424‰ → 550‰ | +125.9‰ | [83.3, 168.5]‰ |
| og-v2 | random-legal | constructor open | 437‰ → 638‰ | +201.1‰ | [158.5, 243.7]‰ |
| og-v3 | σ0 (L0-8) | constructor open | 296‰ → 482‰ | +186.0‰ | [143.4, 228.6]‰ |
| og-v4 | gym field | MF promotion (τ=1/25) | — (**the §6 pilot**: no promotion) | — | — |
| og-v4b | gym field | direct-EB (τ=1/100) | 431‰ → 507‰ | +76.1‰ | [15.9, 136.4]‰ |
| og-v5 | gym field | **CE anytime-direct** (τ=1/100) | 417‰ → **518‰** | **+101.0‰** | [40.8, 161.3]‰ |

Highlights:

- **The constructor's admissions track the lineup**: count husbandry vs random seats; trick contention vs σ0; lead discipline beside the L1 partner — including `beats`-composite relations no human wrote into the seed grammar.
- **§6, measured twice**: og-v4's stream-pilot (all-L0 proxy, ρ ≈ 0.35) and the fair real-policy-pair pilot (same-architecture gym-4 proxy, ρ = 0.38) both find Var(D_H−D_L) > Var(D_H): paired make/set differences are proxy-resistant on this game, and direct sampling beats optimal-allocation MF by 1.8–2.4× at measured costs. "A proxy with poor correlation can cost more than it saves," quantified.
- **The anytime rule harvests what fixed checkpoints cannot**: og-v5's promotions resolved at n = 6,656 / 12,288 / **60,416** — the last a **+1.9% edge, the first certified resolution inside the 1–2% band across all six campaigns** — plus a futility dismissal at 22,528. Five decisive verdicts in eight streams, less risk spent per candidate, and og-v5's exam is the program's strongest gym-field result.
- Every campaign ended by its declared rule; every unresolved candidate stays typed UNRESOLVED; every exam range touched exactly once.

## Records and bookkeeping

`experiments/og-learning/campaigns/{og-v0-pilot,og-v1,og-v2,og-v3,og-v4,og-v4b,og-v5}/` — generations.jsonl, exam.json, panel.json, state.txt, RESULTS.md (results files govern prose), plus the pilot records. author: mjohnsonwellabe
body:
Implements the owner's decision of 2026-09-21. **This amends a hard rule**, so the documentation change is part of the PR rather than a follow-up.

## The decision

CLAUDE.md read: *"Freed legendaries volunteer, with one durable recipient per world offer."*

The owner replaced it with: **every participant in the fight that freed the legendary receives their own offer, and each who accepts keeps their own.** Asked explicitly whether that meant one creature contested between participants or one each, the owner chose **one each** — in a four-player game, up to four Veridians in the world.

Amended together, as the routing rules require:

| Document | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (identical twins) | one durable recipient per world offer | every participant receives and keeps their own |
| `CREATURES.md` | "One host-owned world offer has one durable stable-character recipient" | per-participant offers bound to stable characters |
| `BOSSES.md` §Warden | "the one legendary offer uses stable-recipient ownership" | each participant receives their own offer |
| `BOSSES.md` out-of-scope | **"copied co-op legendary rewards"** barred | removed; what stays barred is granting to a non-participant, or twice to one character |

## The defect this answers

Recorded in `MEADOWS-PAYOFFS/hall-coop/LEGENDARY-RECIPIENT.md`, found while building the Hall witness in #182:

`stronghold_climax.gd::_hand_over_the_legendary()` added the creature to the **local** `Game.party` with **no session, host, ledger or authority seam anywhere in the file** — while the climax is **built on both peers** (measured: identical geometry on host and guest). Every peer running it took one, participant or not, and nothing stopped one character taking one twice across a reload.

## What changed

`may_receive()` is a **pure rule** taking its three inputs as parameters rather than reads, so it is testable without a world, a session or a save: who this peer is, who fought, and whether this character already resolved this freeing.

Each peer decides only **for itself** — which is why no host arbitration is needed and why two peers cannot race for one grant.

Participation comes from the **world's own reward journal**, not a live encounter record: the record is gone by the time the legendary is freed. The Warden pays through the same per-participant `reward_grant` machinery every shared payout uses, each accepted delivery carries the recipient's **stable character id**, and it replicates to every peer. #179's tournament witness already proved that journal carries both participants' ids and survives reload.

### The empty-set case — the one that could have broken solo

A solo freeing publishes no shared receipts at all, so the participant set is empty. Refusing on an empty set would strand **every solo ending**. The rule reads an empty set as "this is the only player", which is what it is — while an empty *character id* is still refused when others did fight, so an unidentified peer cannot claim a place in a known set.

## Evidence

`tests/test_legendary_per_participant.gd` — **7 tests, 9 assertions, 0 failed**, including the one that matters most for the amendment: *every* participant receives one, not just the first.

`tests/smoke_gate_e_finale.gd` — the **solo ending still passes end to end**: the tether fails, `legendary_freed` is set, the freed creature steps clear, the garrison withdraws, the objective chain terminates. That was the real regression risk in gating this path.

## Boundaries — not proven

- **No two-peer runtime witness exists yet.** Nothing drives two peers past the Warden into the chamber, so "two participants each end up holding a Veridian in a live session" is **unproven and not claimed**. The rule and its inputs are unit-proven; the end-to-end claim is not made.
- The journal lookup keys on the Warden's trainer id (`warden_aldis`, config-overridable). A chapter whose legendary is freed by something paying no per-participant reward yields an empty set and falls to the solo reading — Stormwood and Tidewake must verify their own freeing paths.
- Belt-full behaviour unchanged: the five-creature release ceremony still resolves on the receiving peer.

author: rickparapinski
body:
## Summary

Companion PR to [fraud-game#1](https://github.com/rickparapinski/fraud-game/pull/1) — the backend stopped broadcasting `sessionId` and moved to a stable public `pid` for identity, and this PR updates the frontend to match, plus fixes the reconnect gap that same identity handling was causing, a critical dependency vulnerability, and a chunk of dead code found during review.

- **Real reconnect handling**: `useGameLogic` previously had no `connect`/`disconnect` listener after the initial join — a dropped socket silently and permanently desynced the client (confirmed regression vs. a discarded older page component that did handle this). Now registers real connect/disconnect/connect_error listeners and re-runs the resume-then-join negotiation on every reconnect, not just the first one. Event handlers are registered *before* any join/resume call, so a `role-sync` the server sends ahead of its ack is never missed.
- **`resume-player` response now fully consumed**: role, deadline, and totalMs restore the role UI and a live countdown on a mid-game reload instead of leaving the player stranded.
- **Identity matching moved to `pid`**: "who am I" (`me`, `PlayerRoster`'s `isMe`, audit/protect history keys, teammate alive-status) now matches on the new public `pid` instead of the no-longer-broadcast `sessionId`.
- **Critical dependency fix**: `package.json` declared `next@15.5.9` but `node_modules` had `15.5.3` installed (`npm ls` reported it invalid) — a real bug independent of any vulnerability. Resyncing surfaced 17 audit findings including a **critical unauthenticated RCE** in Next's Image Optimization API and a Windows-hosted RCE, both fixed by bumping to `15.5.25` (still 15.x, not a major jump). One low/moderate `postcss` advisory remains and needs a Next 16 major upgrade to fully clear — deliberately left alone pending a separate decision on that scope.
- **Dead code removed**: the entire discarded `old_page.jsx` tree (18 files — the legacy page plus ~9 UI components and the `pixelact-ui` subfolder only it referenced), the now-orphaned `cn()` utility, 4 unused npm packages, and the unused `resetSocket()` export.
- **Three small state/UI bugs**: dead `hasVotedDay` state removed (a locally-derived, server-authoritative value under the same prop name was the one actually used); `me`'s fallback stub no longer defaults `isActive: true` on a roster lookup miss; the countdown now computes its first tick synchronously instead of showing a stale value for up to 1s after every phase change.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — clean after every commit (including post dependency-bump and post dead-code-removal, to confirm nothing broke)
- [x] `npm run dev` — live smoke check of `/` and `/room/[roomCode]`, both 200
- [x] Live smoke test against the running backend confirming reconnect restores role/deadline/roster correctly
- [x] Bundle size check confirming the removed dead code (and its CSS) was truly unreferenced (127kB→124kB JS, 12.9kB→10.1kB CSS)

## Deploy note

This branch gets a free Vercel preview URL on push — worth a sanity check there before merging, per the repo's existing workflow.

> 「静」のプレイリストにもビートが効いている曲も多いので、瞑想できるような終始静かな曲だけのプレイリストを作りたい

## ご指摘の裏付け

実データで確認しました。

```
静61曲のうち   ドラム 31曲 ／ パーカッション 11曲 ／ ドラムマシン 7曲
気配に        「高揚感」13曲 ／「力強い」11曲
```

**静の棚の半分にドラムが入っています。** ビートが効いて聞こえて当然でした。

## 自動では分けられないと判断しました

曲中の起伏を表す `development` という項目があり、これがあれば「終始静か」を測れるはずでした。ところが——

```
108曲中 85曲が、同じ値「75」
```

分析はGemini 2.5 flash で全曲同じ版（v1.2）なので、不具合ではありません。**モデルがこの項目にほぼ一律の答えを返している**だけです。

つまり「**全体として静か**」は測れても、「**終始静か**」は測れません。だから耳で選びます。

## 作り

`listen.html` の `MEI` に番号を並べるだけで棚が変わります。

```js
var MEI = [];      // ← ここに番号を足すだけ
```

曲目の取得は「全」と同じ `/api/archive` を使い、番号で絞るだけです。**バックエンドには一切手を入れていません。通信も増えません。**

- 門は 静・動 の隣、全 の手前（幅731で4つ横並び、幅390で **2×2**）
- `MEI` が空のときは**門そのものを消します**。押しても空の棚が出るだけの門は置きません
- 住所からも開けます（`?gate=mei`）

## 選ぶ道具（このPRには入りません）

`_dev/mei_picker.html` を手元に作りました。`_dev/` は gitignore 済みなので**公開されません**。

- 公開中108曲を「静けさの点」順に並べ、各曲に **頭 ／ 中 ／ 終** の3か所を聴くボタン
- 「終始静か」は耳でしか分からないので、ここが要です
- `瞑` を押すと選択。選択は端末に残るので、途中でやめて後日続けられます
- `選んだIDをコピー` で `142,162,147,...` の形で取り出せます

## 確かめたこと（手元・本番API）

```
空のとき        門は 静・動・全 の3つ
仮に5曲入れた    門は4つ。押すと 44,61,142,147,162 だけが流れた
幅390           2×2 に収まり、横に溢れない
```

## 次

**併合しても、曲を選ぶまで瞑の門は出ません。** 安全にお試しいただけます。
選んだIDをお送りいただければ、`MEI` に入れて門を開けます。

author: brandon-coproduct
body:
Every red `gatehouse/required` on nucleus today was a **timeout, not a disagreement** — and the cause is a declaration in this repo.

## What the builder measured

From 519 `gate_measured` events in the lane's own log:

| gate | declared | observed worst | timeout | ratio | undecided |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fmt | 123 s | 207 s | 300 s | 1.45× | 6 / 100 |
| ci-spec | 92 s | **448 s** | **300 s** | **0.67×** | **27 / 115** |
| clippy | 584 s | 1151 s | 2600 s | 2.26× | 7 / 101 |
| test-core | 907 s | 1656 s | 2100 s | 1.27× | 10 / 100 |
| text-gates | 713 s | 874 s | 1800 s | 2.06× | 7 / 103 |

`ci-spec`'s timeout was **below its own worst runtime**, so 23% of its runs returned `gate_undecided`. Three consecutive undecideds exhaust the job; a *required* gate that is exhausted leaves the roll-up permanently undecided; `gatehouse/required` then sits `in_progress` until the controller's 5 h timeout ends it as `failure`. Every such `failure` has `completed_at - started_at` of exactly 18000 s.

`fmt` (1.45×) and `test-core` (1.27×) were under the 2× floor and would have followed.

## The fix

Measurements become the worst run observed **here**, which is what `pipeline.writ` already said they were for — *"a worst that a later run beats is not a measurement, it is a hope"*, written by a revision that was itself being beaten on all five gates. Timeouts are set just over the 2× floor `timeoutMeasured_b` holds them to. `fmt` and `ci-spec` needed their hermetic capabilities raised alongside, since `timeoutCoherent_b` refuses a timeout above `capWallMs`.

That broke `builderBudget_b` (11 300 000 ms × 2 commits > 21 600 000 ms) and the kernel refused the plan — working as intended. The slack came from **lean-build**, whose 1 200 000 ms timeout stood against a 145 000 ms measurement taken *in a container* for a gate the lane cannot run at all. At 400 000 (2.8×) everything fits in 21 000 000, and the loosest multiplier in the plan belonged to the one gate that never executes.

All three descriptions move together — the writ, the committed elaboration, and `.gatehouse/gates/*.json`. `check-gate-defs-match-plan.sh` compares them and caught each one left behind.

## Verification

- `gate plan check` at the pinned ref `067869b5`: **admissibility proved, root `admissible` kernel-checked**
- `gate plan gates` regenerates `.gatehouse/plan-gates.json` with exactly the intended diff
- `check-gate-defs-match-plan.sh`, `check-ci-spec.sh`, `check-ci-assurance-ledger.sh`, `xtask gatehouse-pin`, `xtask assurance-required` — all green

## Not fixed here

The `failure` conclusion is deliberate and stays: `Conclusion` is `Success | Failure` only, because GitHub counts `timed_out` and `neutral` as **passing**. A verdict that is not a verdict must read red.

The lane also had **eleven commits in flight** against a plan proved for two, because a push enqueues a gate request and supersedes nothing. No timeout fixes that, and it is gatehouse's queue to change.

author: jackie-sdx
body: ## Summary (Issue #87 — autonomous edge-cutting crawler-resilience benchmark) **1. Crawler fix — malformed `` corrupts/drops subsequent links** Diagnosis: `scripts/simple-web-crawler.js` `scanAnchors()` matched each anchor's closing tag as the first `` in the *entire remaining HTML*. A malformed `` whose text illegally contains another `` opening (an `` cannot nest in HTML and is implicitly closed by the next ``) was therefore "closed" by a later anchor's ``, silently swallowing that healthy link and mislabeling its text — and when no `` remained at all, the scan `break` dropped every later link. Reproduced: `first` / unclosed `unclosed.jpg` / `second` / `third` → crawler reported `[first, unclosed.jpg, third]`, dropping `/second`. Fix: skip the malformed anchor and resume scanning at the nested opening, so one broken tag can no longer degrade extraction of the rest of the page (scripts/simple-web-crawler.js). Regression coverage: new deterministic `/malformed-anchor` fixture + assertions that all healthy links after the unclosed tag survive with intact text (scripts/test-simple-web-crawler.js). **2. CI workflow repair (pre-existing corruption)** The head commit of `main` shipped `enterprise-agent-validation.yml` with ~580 bytes of binary garbage replacing the final smoke-test line, which made the entire pull_request workflow unparseable — silently disabling the only PR CI surface and making CI observation impossible. Repaired the tail to its intended assertion, verified against the runner's actual `GITHUB_OUTPUT` for the mock exit-7 script (`grep -Fq "termination_reason=failed" "$out"`). ## Validation executed - `npm test` — ALL TESTS PASSED (incl. new malformed-anchor case) - `npm run lint` — clean - `npm run test:invariants` — 16 checked, 0 failures - `.github/scripts/validate-application.sh` — PASS - `.github/scripts/test-oc-target.sh` — 50 passed, 0 failed - `.github/scripts/test-ingest-evidence.sh` — 7 passed, 0 failed - `.github/scripts/test-opencode-live-output.sh` — OK - `git diff --check` — clean CI observation in progress for this PR head.

body:
Thunder's USD visual meshes are instance proxies, which the LiDAR loader previously skipped. Traversal now includes them and anchors non-physical proxies at their editable instance root. An explicit subtree exclusion supports omitting the emitting LiDAR housing while retaining other robot surfaces.

The Thunder adapter uses visual surface meshes for optical occlusion; coarse physics collision boxes remain active for physics. This avoids treating a collision box or the emitter's solid CAD housing as a wall around every ray origin.

Validation: Isaac Sim 5.0 on RTX 3090; existing geometry assertions plus instancing, instance movement and emitter exclusion passed. Four-environment Thunder plane and rough tasks each completed two PPO updates with actual terrain returns entering the map. Standalone geometry and plane runs saved passing results but timed out in simulator shutdown; the rough run exited normally. See docs/thunder_mesh_support.md. No hardware calibration or trained locomotion claim.

author: davidcozens
body:
## Purpose

Close-out for the fourth QEMU lane and the three packs it proves - CMSIS-RTOS2 (E40),
LittleFS (E36) and lwIP Sockets (E35).

Closes #854

## Change Description

**Branch protection is already updated** - it is a settings change, not a file, so it
is not in this diff. Three jobs existed in `ci.yml` without being required status
checks, meaning any of them could go red without blocking a merge:

| Context | Proves |
|---|---|
| `build-cmsis-target-lwip` | the fourth target cross-builds over the three new packs |
| `bdd-cmsis-qemu-lwip` | its 69 scenarios against the oracle |
| `integration-linux-littlefs` | LittleFS durability against a real filesystem |

The third is not named in #854. It is included because leaving E36's suite advisory is
the same hole in a different pack, and that suite exists precisely because a fake
cannot prove `lfs_file_sync` committed anything. Required contexts went 35 -> 38;
`deploy-docs-pages` remains the only non-required job, correctly, since it is main-only.
Neither CMSIS lane ever set `continue-on-error`, so "advisory" only ever meant "absent
from the required set" - no workflow change was needed.

**`docs/ci.md` claimed every job was a required check bar `deploy-docs-pages`,** which
was wrong in exactly those three ways. It also described `build-cmsis-target-lwip` as
linking the same packs as the lwIP lane - stale since the swaps - and
`bdd-cmsis-qemu-lwip` as "Advisory until S40.05". `integration-linux-littlefs` had no
row in the lane table at all. All four corrected.

**The containers table no longer enumerates each image's consumers.** That column had
drifted twice, once when the lwIP lanes arrived and once when consumer-smoke did, and
it duplicated what `ci.yml` and the two Compose files already state executably. Each
row now says what the image is for, with a line above the table pointing at those files
as the authority for who uses it. The "Files to update" table below it is untouched -
that is the pointer for a bump and still earns its place.

Em dashes on `containers.md` were converted with the table rewrite, per CLAUDE.md's
rule about converting a page you are already rewriting. One was left alone: line 64 is
quoted CMake output, where changing the character would misquote the build.

## What this story needed and did not get

**Capability matrix rows were already there.** Each pack claimed its own dot as it
landed - CMSIS-RTOS2's OS-primitives and time dots in #852, lwIP Sockets' network dot
in #858, LittleFS's files dot in #881 - so the criterion was satisfied before this
story opened. `check_platform_docs.py` is green.

**No CHANGELOG entry.** `docs/release-process.md` puts the two written parts of the
release notes into the release PR at release time, and the generated list is
release-please's own from the Conventional Commit types. 0.2.0 still has open issues,
so notes written now would be revised before they shipped. The criterion is satisfied
by process rather than by an edit here.

**E35 #692 and E36 #693 are already closed**, by hand as their last stories merged.
E40 #849 goes to 5/5 when this merges and will be closed then.

## Test Evidence

Documentation only, so CI green is the bar. Locally: markdownlint over all 72 files,
`check_references.py`, `check_platform_docs.py`, the 104 docs hook tests and
`mkdocs build --strict` all clean.

The protection change was verified by reading it back: all three contexts present, 38
total, and `enforce_admins`, `allow_force_pushes`, `allow_deletions` and the
review-requirement setting unchanged. The previous state is backed up should it need
reverting.

This PR is itself the first to run under the new required set.

## Areas Affected

- Branch protection on `main` - three more contexts must pass before any PR merges
- `docs/ci.md` - lane table and the branch-protection section
- `docs/containers.md` - the image table's third column, and the prose above it
- No code, no workflow file. #854 puts any code change out of scope as a defect needing its own issue

## 6a: the figure strip at the passage floor

v14 said three or four lines of prose were left at the floor.  I measured it in Chromium with the real strip, over all 642 strip items in five packs: **0.51 lines** showed on arrival, at every viewport.

- The thumb is now `clamp(44px, 35cqh - 18px, 96px)` of the passage's content box.  It is unchanged at 96px from a 326px box up, and falls to 44px (the touch floor) at the 178px floor box.  Width stays 128px.

- `container-type: size` sits behind `@supports (height: 1cqh)`, so older browsers keep the fixed 96px.

## 6b: the lightbox caption

- Caption and credit now share `.mv-lb-foot`: the scrim's own colour at full opacity, edge to edge.  Page text no longer shows through on the caption rows.

## Gate

`tests/figures-offline.js` now computes the expected thumb from the passage it actually measures.  It adds two checks:

- **Floor:** at least 2.5 lines of prose and a thumb of at least 44px.  A negative control turns the container off and must fall under the bar (0.51 lines).
- **Band:** the caption band is opaque, full width, and holds both the caption and the credit.

Demo copy of https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/10243 at commit a9359ec64336, for Greptile Plus/Apex evaluation. Original description follows.

## Summary

Three small fixes to `DiffViewProvider`:

1. **scrollToFirstDiff()**: add missing `await` on `scrollEditorToLine()` — currently fire-and-forget, so the scroll may not complete before subsequent operations
2. **revertChanges()**: use `getDocumentLineCount()` instead of regex `(contents.match(/\n/g) || []).length + 1` — the regex can be off-by-one with mixed line endings (CRLF vs LF)
3. **BOM preservation**: track whether the original file had a UTF-8 BOM. `update()` correctly strips BOM during streaming to prevent duplication, but `saveChanges()` never re-adds it — files that originally had a BOM silently lose it after editing

## Test Procedure

**Scroll fix (#8885):**
1. Open a large file, make an edit near the middle
2. Verify the diff view scrolls to the first change reliably

**Line count fix (#8884):**
1. Open a file with CRLF line endings
2. Revert changes
3. Verify the full content is restored correctly (no extra/missing lines)

**BOM fix (#8883):**
1. Create a UTF-8 file with BOM (e.g. via Notepad with "UTF-8 with BOM" encoding)
2. Let Cline edit the file
3. Approve the edit
4. Verify the saved file still has the BOM (check with `xxd` or hex editor — should start with `EF BB BF`)

## ✨ Show deferred retries and recovery actions

**Task:** `am-eey.10`

### 📝 Summary

Make the dashboard distinguish deferred automatic retries from actual human intervention. Show the retry time and failure reason, and provide explicit retry-now and abandon actions for recoverable tasks.

### 🚀 How to use

When a transient harness failure (quota, rate limit, overloaded model, flaky network) defers a task, it parks in the `retrying` state instead of needing a human.

- The Board gets a separate orange **Retrying** column (no longer lumped into In progress), and every retrying card shows when the next attempt fires (e.g. "retries in 45s") and the failure reason.
- A retrying task is absent from Overview/Inbox **Needs attention**, and its detail page shows a "Deferred automatic retry" panel with the retry countdown and reason.
- **Retry now** button (task detail, retrying tasks only): skips the remaining backoff and starts the next attempt immediately. Backed by `POST /api/repos/:repo/tasks/:id/retry`; answers 409 unless the task is deferring a retry.
- **Close** (task detail, retrying tasks only): abandons the task, stopping the backoff, deleting the worktree and closing the tracker issue as abandoned. The Reclaim button is hidden on retrying tasks because the runner still owns them.

## Summary

Implements Stage 4 Point 3: BSR packaging and release preflight validation.

- Configures `buf.build/hdev-hm/logging` as the canonical BSR module.
- Preserves `proto/` as the module root and Google APIs as an external dependency.
- Validates committed `buf.lock` consistency using Buf.
- Adds explicit `LAST_BSR_COMMIT_ID` baseline handling.
- Runs breaking-change validation against the last immutable BSR commit.
- Adds tag-driven, non-publishing release preflight validation.
- Separates deterministic validation from BSR authentication so `BUF_TOKEN`
  is exposed only to the authentication step.
- Serializes release-preflight executions.
- Adds automated tests for BSR baseline and validation behavior.

## Compatibility policy

- `INITIAL` explicitly represents the first/new compatibility baseline.
- A valid BSR commit ID requires `buf breaking`.
- Missing, blank, malformed, or unresolvable baselines block release validation.
- Breaking changes in v1 cannot be bypassed.

## Security

- Workflow permissions remain least-privilege with `contents: read`.
- `BUF_TOKEN` is exposed only to the BSR authentication step.
- No publication credentials are exposed during deterministic validation.
- No package or schema publication is performed by this workflow.

## Validation

- Release build: 0 warnings / 0 errors
- .NET tests: 12 passed
- Release-versioning tests: passed
- BSR validation tests: passed
- Buf format: passed
- Buf lint: passed
- Buf build: passed
- Buf lock consistency: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

## Scope

This PR implements only the BSR foundation and preflight validation.

NuGet/BSR publication, retry/recovery orchestration, BSR commit persistence,
provenance/attestation, and the complete release workflow remain deferred to
the subsequent Stage 4 points.

author: baiye-banned
body:
## 类型

<!-- 必选。至少勾选一项（校验脚本要求本节至少有一个 [x]），可多选 -->

- [x] 🐛 Bug 修复
- [ ] ✨ 新功能
- [ ] 📝 文档
- [ ] ♻️ 重构
- [ ] 🧪 测试
- [ ] 🔧 其他

## 变更概述

给 `vite.config.js` 的 dev server 加 `strictPort: true`，端口被占用时直接失败，不再静默顺延到 5174。

## 背景·问题

**现象**：5173 被占用时执行 `npm run dev`，vite 只以 info 级别打一行 `Port 5173 is in use, trying another one...`，然后在 **5174** 正常启动、退出码 0。而 README:330 把 `http://localhost:5173` 作为既定地址给出，此时打开该地址打到的是占用端口的另一个服务，且整条链路没有任何环节报错。

**根因**：`server` 块只有 `port: 5173`。在 vite 6.4.3 里 `server.port` 只是「首选端口」，不是「必须端口」——`httpServerStart` 收到 `EADDRINUSE` 时，`strictPort` 为假就自增端口重试，为真才 `reject(new Error('Port 5173 is already in use'))`。

**影响范围**：本机多工作区并行开发时很常见，只影响本地 dev server；构建产物与 `vite preview` 不受影响（见下方验证）。

**同类场景的不对称**：团队在其它同类场景已经显式用了 `--strictPort`（`.github/workflows/e2e.yml:166`、`README.md:648`），只有 dev server 这条路径漏了——本 PR 把 dev server 拉到同一口径。

## 关联 issue

Closes #159

## 变更内容

- `vite.config.js`：`server` 块加 `strictPort: true`，并留一行注释说明为什么不允许顺延。选实现面根治而不是在 README 补一句「以终端输出为准」：后者要求每个读者记住每次都要核对终端地址，而顺延发生时没有任何报错，属于静默劣化；前者让错误在发生的那一刻就暴露。

## 日志·验证证据

占位端口用一个 node net server **同时**绑定 `127.0.0.1` 与 `::1`，这样无论 vite 把 `localhost` 解析到哪个地址族都必然撞上。

**1）修复后：`npx vite` 拒绝启动（退出码 1）**

```text
$ node occ.js 5173          # 同时占住 127.0.0.1:5173 与 [::1]:5173
occupier: bound 127.0.0.1 {"address":"127.0.0.1","family":"IPv4","port":5173}
occupier: bound ::1 {"address":"::1","family":"IPv6","port":5173}
occupier: 5173 taken, holding for 120s

$ timeout 40 npx vite
exit=1
error when starting dev server:
Error: Port 5173 is already in use
    at Server.onError (file:///C:/code/aaa-wt-fix-34/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-Dm0c1Wj2.js:25119:18)
    at Server.emit (node:events:519:28)
    at emitErrorNT (node:net:1977:8)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:89:21)
```

**2）对照臂：同一份配置、只把开关取反（`--no-strictPort`），复现修复前的静默顺延**

```text
$ timeout 25 npx vite --no-strictPort
exit=124        # 124 = 超时才被杀掉，即服务一直在跑
Port 5173 is in use, trying another one...

  VITE v6.4.3  ready in 717 ms

  ➜  Local:   http://localhost:5174/
  ➜  Network: use --host to expose
```

两臂只差这一个开关，配置文件的其它内容完全相同——差别确实来自本 PR 加的那一行，而不是环境抖动。

**3）反向影响排查：`strictPort` 会不会改变 `vite preview`，进而影响 CI e2e？**

查 vite 6.4.3 源码，`preview` 的该字段是**回退**到 `server` 的：

```js
function resolvePreviewOptions(preview2, server) {
  return {
    port: preview2?.port ?? DEFAULT_PREVIEW_PORT,
    strictPort: preview2?.strictPort ?? server.strictPort,   // ← 会继承
    ...
```

实测确认继承成立（占住 4173 后裸跑 `npm run preview` 会直接失败；加 `--no-strictPort` 才顺延到 4174）。**但 CI e2e 不受影响**：`e2e.yml:166` 与 `README.md:648` 都显式传了 `--strictPort`，命令行显式值走 `preview2.strictPort` 分支，继承不参与，行为与改动前完全一致。唯一变化的是**没有任何参数的**裸 `npm run preview`：原本会静默挪到 4174，现在会明确失败。这条路径未在文档中出现，且 e2e 的 `E2E_BASE_URL` 同样写死 4173，让它失败比让它指向别的服务更安全。

**4）配置本身仍可用**

```text
$ node --check vite.config.js
syntax OK

$ npm run build
✓ built in 7.33s
build_exit=0
dist/index.html: present
```

## 测试情况

- `npm run build`：退出码 0，产物 `dist/index.html` 存在（与 `build.yml` 同一命令，同一条 `test -f dist/index.html` 判据）。构建日志里的 `Chat` chunk 体积提示是 README:587 已说明的已知提醒，退出码仍为 0。
- `node --check vite.config.js`：语法通过。
- 未改动 `src/`、`backend/`、`.github/`，因此不涉及后端 pytest 与前端 `npm test`。
- 说明：本机工作区的 eslint 工具链不完整（`npx eslint` 报 `Cannot find package '@eslint/js'`），该文件也不在 CI 的 `npx eslint src` 作用域内，故无 eslint 结论可报，未据此声称通过。

## 截图

无需截图（无 UI 变更）

## 后续计划

无。

author: seanpvera
body:
Audited every exposed control on the macOS/iOS app and the web client, tracing each one from the interaction through app state, the bridge where one exists, the protocol encoder, and the device reply. Fixed the confirmed defects and the one test that was already failing at checkout.

## Baseline

| | |
|---|---|
| Checkout | `21c45f07` on `main` ("Make room-wide power and per-light controls reachable from the Plan (#100)"), clean tree |
| Environment | Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.2, npm 10.9.7, Python 3.11.15. **No Swift toolchain, no Xcode** — Swift is verified by CI only |
| Bridge tests at checkout | `npm test` in `web/bridge`: **55 pass, 1 fail** — `music frame paints one solid colour per fixture and never invents razer`, deterministic across 5 runs |
| Web app build at checkout | `npm run build` (tsc -b + vite) passes |
| Swift build/test at checkout | Not runnable here. `.github/workflows/build.yml` on `macos-15` is the verification path |
| Physical lighting hardware | **None available.** No LIFX bulb, no LIFX Luna, no Govee device of any SKU. Every device-level observation is against the fake LIFX/Govee devices in `web/bridge/test/fake-devices.js`, which speak the real wire protocols over real UDP on loopback |
| Existing user work | Preserved. No schema version bump, no migration, no change to `ApplicationState.json` layout or `~/.lumendesk/bridge-state.json` layout. Archives written by older versions still import |

## Prioritized defects fixed

| # | Severity | Defect | Surface |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Misleading success/failure** | LIFX colour commands can never confirm; false "did not confirm the change" after 3.5 s on nearly every colour and theme | Desktop |
| 2 | **Incorrect lighting** | Bridge colour command reverts a brightness set moments earlier (20% → 50%) | Web |
| 3 | **Misleading preview** | Scene rehearsal previews a solid wash where Apply paints Govee segments, and never sends Govee brightness | Desktop |
| 4 | **Silent data loss** | Configuration export fails silently; user believes they have a backup | Desktop |
| 5 | **Silent data loss** | White-mode per-light setting persists locally but drops out of every export | Desktop |
| 6 | **Misleading control** | Per-light colour/brightness/white accept changes an effect overwrites one frame later | Desktop |
| 7 | **Broken automation** | Bridge `updateSchedule` stores an empty weekday list, which its evaluator reads as "never" while the native engine reads it as "every day" | Web |
| 8 | **Abandoned state** | Web Music Mode Stop freezes the last frame on the lights forever | Web |
| 9 | **Unfounded state** | `/music/frame` records `power: true` for a path that sends no power command | Web |

## Checks actually run

- `node --test web/bridge/test/*.test.js` — **58 pass, 0 fail**, three consecutive runs (55/1 at checkout; +3 new tests).
- Each new bridge test verified to **fail with its fix reverted**, then pass with it restored.
- `npm run build` in `web/app` (`tsc -b` + vite) — passes.
- `git diff --check` — clean on the `base...head` range CI actually checks.
- Brace/paren/bracket balance check on every changed Swift file.
- Swift symbol existence checked by hand for every new reference (`LumenSecondaryButtonStyle(compact:)`, `Lumen.surface`/`hairline`/`beamBright`, `GoveeSegmentColor(red:green:blue:)`, `GoveeSegmentState(colors:gradient:isActive:)`, `DeviceSnapshot(...segments:)`, `ReportedDeviceState(...)`).
- **`xcodebuild test` could not be run in the authoring environment** (no Swift toolchain), so the four new/extended Swift tests were written unexecuted. **CI has since run them:** `Validate and build` on `520ddd3` is green, with `Test macOS Debug` passing in 90 s and `Build generic iOS device` passing after it. `xcodebuild test` exits non-zero on any failing test, and all four tests were added to files already in the pbxproj (`CommandCoordinatorTests.swift`, `DomainTests.swift`, `PersistenceStoreTests.swift`) as methods on existing `XCTestCase` subclasses, so they compiled and ran as part of their suites. What CI has **not** established is anything about real lights: every hardware row in `CONTROLS_AUDIT.md` still stands.

## Full findings tables

Both inventories — one row per exposed control and per materially different integration, capability, supported combination and failure path, with evidence and remaining hardware verification for each — are committed as [`CONTROLS_AUDIT.md`](CONTROLS_AUDIT.md). They were too large for a PR body and belong in the repository anyway.

- **Desktop table**: discovery and diagnostics, power/brightness/colour/white per brand, rooms and global actions, scenes, rehearsal, themes, effects, undo/redo, schedules and automation, Music Mode, the Govee Segment Studio and LIFX Luna Studio, persistence and import/export, Demo Mode, the menu bar.
- **Web table**: bridge reachability and origin gating, discovery, per-command confirmation, device control per brand, rooms, scenes, schedules, Music Mode, persistence, and the capabilities the web client does not provide at all.

The expansion plan below is also in that file.

## Web expansion: the smallest useful next feature

### Where the two clients stand today

| | Native | Bridge + web client |
|---|---|---|
| Govee per-segment **live** paint | `razer` streaming, volatile | none |
| Govee per-segment **durable** write | `ptReal` relaying 20-byte BLE packets | none |
| Govee stream-hold families (H60B0, string, curtain) | layout held and re-asserted every 30 s | none |
| LIFX Luna matrix | `GetDeviceChain` → `Get64` / `Set64`, 26 zones | none |
| Encoders present in the bridge | — | `scan`, `turn`, `brightness`, `colorwc`, `devStatus` only |

`web/bridge/src/govee.js` is 72 lines and stops at the five documented LAN commands. `lifx.js` has no `Set64`. So today a web scene captured on an RGBIC strip stores one blended colour, and web Music Mode washes a 15-segment strip in a single hue.

### Recommendation: port `razer` only, and ship a read-only-plus-live Segment Studio

**Do not** port `ptReal` in the first step. `razer` is one packet family, fully described by an existing byte-for-byte Swift test, and it is **volatile** — the worst outcome of a bug is a wrong colour until the overlay drops. `ptReal` writes durable state into firmware with no acknowledgement and no read-back; getting it wrong leaves a user's strip permanently wrong with no way for the bridge to detect it. Earn the second with the first.

**User experience.** A Govee RGBIC device gains a "Segments" panel in the web Devices view: a strip of N colour wells, a gradient toggle, and a live preview that streams while the panel is open. The panel states plainly that the layout is live-only and will fall away when the panel closes or the light is power-cycled, and that durable layouts still need the Mac app. Music Mode gains per-segment frames for the same devices.

**Supported devices.** Govee RGBIC models the native `GoveeSegmentProfile` catalog recognizes (H619x COB strips, H70Cx string lights, H60B0 lamp, curtain families). The bridge needs the SKU, which it already stores from the scan reply (`registry.upsert(..., {sku})`); `GoveeSegmentProfile.detect` has to be ported alongside so segment counts and the H60B0 two-of-three zone rule come with it.

### Changes required

**Protocol (`web/bridge/src/govee.js`)** — port three functions from `GoveeProtocol.swift`, unchanged in behaviour:
- `xorChecksum(bytes)`
- `razerModeRequest(on)` → `[0xBB, 0x00, 0x01, 0xB1, on ? 1 : 0, xor]`, base64 into `{"msg":{"cmd":"razer","data":{"pt":…}}}`
- `razerFrameRequest(colors, blend)` → `[0xBB, lenHi, lenLo, 0xB0, blend ? 0x00 : 0x01, count, …rgb triplets…, xor]`, colours capped at 255 and clamped 0–255

**Protocol tests (`web/bridge/test/protocol.test.js`)** — the lockstep rule in `CLAUDE.md` is the binding constraint. Add vectors byte-identical to the ones in `LumenDeskTests/ProtocolTests.swift` for both functions, in the same file that already do

author: djantzen
body:
`canvas cr-init`'s one-line help in `canvas --help` said it "sets up the 'cr' remote", but `_ensure_cr_remote` configures **`origin`**. The rationale is in the code (`canvas_cli/apps/control_room/commands.py`): Control Room is the plugin's authoritative git home, so it *is* the repo's `origin`, and naming it that rather than a side remote means plain git, and Studio's build agent which uses `origin`, push and fetch it with no special-casing.

The `cr_init` docstring that typer renders as the command's long help already describes `origin` throughout, including the `git push origin HEAD:main` example. Only the `short_help` string in `canvas_cli/main.py` disagreed, so the two halves of the same command's help contradicted each other.

A repo-wide sweep for other variants of "cr remote" found no further occurrences.

Before:

```
cr-init            Connect a plugin's git repo to Control Room (sets up the
                   'cr' remote).
```

After:

```
cr-init            Connect a plugin's git repo to Control Room (sets up the
                   'origin' remote).
```

Flagged by Promptless while generating docs for `cr-init`; the generated docs correctly followed the code rather than this string.

## Testing

Rendered `CONTROL_ROOM_BETA=true canvas --help` to confirm the corrected text. `uv run pytest canvas_cli/` → 266 passed (the 16 errors are pre-existing `INTEGRATION_TEST_URL is not set` integration tests, identical on `main`). `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and the repo pre-commit including `mypy` all pass.

author: gregory91g
body:
**Why** — credits reached Silver only inside `class_ai_dev_usage`, which is the wrong carrier for spend twice over. That model admits a row on activity counters, because its contract derives `active_day` from a row existing, and a person can spend credits while every activity counter the vendor publishes reads zero — continuing an existing session spends without starting one. And it has no column for credits at all: `cost_cents` is NULL because credits are not a currency. Closes #3512.

**What changed** — credits get their own relation, and the money they become feeds the measures that already mean it. Descriptor 3.0.0 → 3.2.0 (MINOR: the dbt step re-runs so the new model materialises).

**No new measures.** Codex on-demand spend contributes to the existing `daily_extra_usage_usd` and `extra_usage_usd`, so `ai.daily_approximate_extra_usage_cost` and `ai.extra_usage_cost` start covering Codex with no metric work. A parallel pair of credit measures would split one economic quantity across two metric families.

**The two vendors derive those measures in opposite directions, and both are right.** Claude publishes a cumulative month-to-date amount, so its month is the fact and a day is the difference between two readings. Codex publishes an exact per-day charge, so its day is the fact and its month is the sum of the days that have arrived. `ai_cost_metric_observations` groups on `metric_date`, so a day's row dated at the start of its month contributes to that month and stays its own drilldown row.

**A partial month is reported, not suppressed.** The `ai_cost` source already declares `revision: billing_month`, so a month still accumulating is served as unsettled and a later backfill raising the sum is the ordinary case that rule describes.

**One current pricing configuration, not a rate history.** `config.ai_credit_pricing` holds `credit_price_minor_units`, `billed_currency` and `native_minor_to_usd_cents_rate` per tenant and vendor — no validity intervals, no second table. The rate is USD cents per one native minor unit, which keeps the arithmetic free of the currency's exponent: a currency whose minor unit is the unit itself needs no special case, and the provenance carries minor units rather than a major-unit figure computed by dividing. Dating the price would have bought less than it cost: neither number comes from a vendor API, and with no source of historical FX a dated price beside a current rate still cannot reproduce a year-old USD figure. The exception is written down rather than engineered around, as `cpt-insightspec-aicost-principle-codex-pricing-is-current` in DESIGN and in decomposition entry 2.12: a Codex monetary value is an estimate and restates when the configuration changes, while the credits behind it never move. No configuration yields no money at all, never a zero.

**A withdrawn charge can be withdrawn.** The contributor emits zero-credit person-days on purpose: its relation is a ReplacingMergeTree keyed on (tenant, source, email, date) and not on the figure, so a reading revised down to nothing has to arrive as a row or the earlier positive one stays stored forever. The `credits > 0` test lives in gold's monetary branch instead, where a stored zero produces no evidence row rather than a $0 charge.

**The price lookup carries no disjunction in any `ON` clause.** ClickHouse 25.7 refuses a join mixing equality with `OR` (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, code 48), and `IN` with a column on the right is unsupported too, so the scope test is `has()` over a literal array and precedence is resolved by ranking: an instance-scoped configuration beats the vendor default.

**Provenance travels with the estimate** — credits, billed currency, price per credit, native amount, rate applied. Not declared as `detail_columns`: the validator fails a declared detail no row carries, and on an installation with no priced Codex credits none would.

**Out of scope** — `extra_usage_utilisation` for this vendor (it needs a per-seat limit as of the day spent, and the settings endpoint reports current state only), and seat/subscription cost (blocked on billing endpoints above the collection identity's role). Both recorded in `DECOMPOSITION.md` as 2.12 and 2.13.

**Note on merge order** — this bumps the `chatgpt-team` descriptor to 3.2.0 assuming #3511 lands first with 3.1.0.

**Verified**
- [x] `dbt parse` — clean; both new models and the `config.ai_credit_pricing` source resolve
- [x] `cargo +1.95 test -p analytics metric_definitions` — 99 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format` on the new data-path module — clean
- [x] `git diff --check` — clean
- [ ] clean bootstrap, `silver.sql` convergence and warm upgrade — CI
- [ ] the new data-path case `ai_credit_revised_to_zero` — runs on a compose stand; it covers the collapse to the newest reading within one build and gold's refusal to charge a zero, and deliberately does **not** cover the incremental path, which the spec runner cannot express without a second seed-and-rebuild phase

author: meltface-80
body:
The server logs settle it. The profile augmentation was read and applied - "using augmented profile Sonos" - the sample rate limit was evaluated correctly, "192000 > 48000", and then:

    MDE: Selected protocol http; container:
    ...: Direct Playing due to no transcode profile
    Transcode=4005,Cannot convert this item.
                   No conversion profile found for protocol http.

The container is blank because the transcode target never took. Two reasons, both visible in the same logs next to a music transcode that does work on this server and returns ten megabytes of audio:

The profile matched is Plex's own built-in Sonos one, because the request announced X-Plex-Device=Sonos. It offers no music over plain HTTP, and being already furnished it swallows an added target rather than taking it. The request that works is matched to Generic, so this one stops claiming to be a Sonos device; nothing else about it was ever Sonos-specific.

The limitations were scoped to the transcode target. The working request scopes them to the codec being produced and marks them onlyTranscodes, which is the distinction that matters: a limitation without it describes what may go in, so a 24/192 file is measured against the very ceiling it is meant to be brought under and the server calls it unplayable.

Everything else now follows that same working request: /audio/:/transcode/ universal/start rather than /music/..., with no extension, since the output format comes from the declared target and not from the path; replace=true written first in the target, as Plex's own clients write it; and none of the parameters it does without.

One more thing the logs made plain: a working client takes a new session for every track. A transcode session belongs to one track, and starting a second on the same id ends the first - so a room sharing one id across a queue would have each track Sonos prepares cut the stream out from under the track that is playing.

author: lesleh
body:
## Summary

- The header's "New recipe" link and each recipe page's "Edit" link point to `/recipes/new` and `/recipes/[slug]/edit`, both gated by Basic Auth in `src/proxy.ts`.
- Next.js `Link` prefetches these routes in the background from public pages. The prefetch request has no `Authorization` header, so it gets a `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic`, which makes the browser pop its native sign-in prompt over a public page the user never tried to leave (e.g. the home page).
- Added `prefetch={false}` to both links so browsing public pages no longer triggers background requests into the gated routes. The routes themselves stay gated — clicking through still prompts for the password — so unauthenticated visitors never see a form they can't submit.

## Test plan

- [x] Traced the request flow: `Link` prefetch → `src/proxy.ts` matcher on `/recipes/new` and `/recipes/:slug/edit` → 401 + `WWW-Authenticate` → browser's native auth prompt.
