author: frankxai
body:
## What

Adds the two generated bands to this repo's `AGENTS.md`. Band C — the existing 174 lines — is untouched.

## Why

45 hand-maintained agent contracts drift, and the drift is measurable: 16 repos had no contract at all, and this estate's own substrate file was carrying 170 cp1252 double-encodings. The fix is not another hand-written copy — it is generating the parts that are identical everywhere and leaving only the local part to a human.

Three bands, per [`AGENTS-MD-CONTRACT.md`](https://github.com/frankxai/Starlight-Intelligence-System/blob/claude/agent-docs-structure-roles-k0fv2d/docs/architecture/AGENTS-MD-CONTRACT.md):

- **A — inherited.** DNA, the five guardrails, decision discipline, branch/PR protocol, attestation, the non-waivable safety rules. Identical estate-wide.
- **B — company projection.** FrankX.ai · routes through Starlight Holding BV · brand register `brand:frankx` with its `COPY.md` pin · accountable seat `agent:starlight-cmo` · **T1, revenue surface**, deploys `surface:frankx.ai`.
- **C — repo-local.** Yours. Hand-written. **Outranks A and B on any conflict inside this repo**, and the generated preamble says so.

Generated from SIS by `scripts/agents-md-project.mjs`, shipped in [Starlight-Intelligence-System#175](https://github.com/frankxai/Starlight-Intelligence-System/pull/175).

## How

Both bands are fenced, and each fence carries the `sha256` prefix of the body the generator wrote. A later hand-edit inside a fence no longer hashes to its declared `sha`, so `--check` reports it by name instead of silently overwriting it. Change either band upstream in SIS and regenerate — never here.

## Checks

- [x] **Band C preserved byte-for-byte** — verified by stripping the fences from the result and diffing against this branch's previous `AGENTS.md`. Identical, not asserted.
- [x] **Idempotent** — a second generator run writes nothing.
- [x] **No money, jurisdiction, or credential in the projection** — the generator runs the INV-7 scan *before* writing, using the same regex as the estate-graph validator.
- [ ] `pnpm run type-check` / `lint` / `ai-slop:audit:strict` / `build` — **not run, and not applicable.** This diff is one markdown file. It touches no path under `app/`, `components/`, `content/`, `lib/`, or `data/`, so no required gate in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` reads it.

## Screenshots

None — no UI in this diff. No route renamed, no page removed, no homepage surface touched.

## Summary

Daily quantcurb.com run. **Premise check first:** today's scheduled prompt again pointed at boards with no quantcurb section — both boards (Portfolio SEO Watch, Portfolio Content Engine) already carry an extensive quantcurb history through PR #92. Confirmed via `list_pull_requests` that **PR #89, #90, #91 and #92 are all still open and unmerged** (base `main` unchanged at `ef70d17`, PR #86's merge) — a 4-PR backlog, oldest from 17 Sep, now 4-5 days with no merge. This PR is scoped to avoid any overlap with those four (Tier-1-banks claim, stale Methodology/FAQ tax figures, footer copyright year, 34 overlong titles/descriptions) — all reconfirmed still live in production via direct `curl`, fixes already pending, not duplicated here.

## Health check (live `curl` against production)
- Homepage: title 60 ch/2026, meta description 138 ch, canonical self-referencing, robots `index, follow`, H1 present, og:image present. No "banking-grade"/"100% ACCURATE" language.
- `robots.txt`: byte-identical to the tracked copy, all 4 `Sitemap:` lines present.
- `/sitemap.xml`: 425 URLs; lastmod split unchanged from the already-investigated-and-ruled-out pattern (345 build-date, 65+6 real per-file blog/academy dates) — not a new blanket-date bug.
- Calculator spot-check, 3 for 3: `/salary-tax-estimator/`, `/mortgage-payment-calculator/`, `/quarterly-tax-calculator/` all render real computed values.
- Footer copyright still reads "© 2025" — confirmed live, fix already pending in open PR #91, not duplicated.

## New finding, fixed — homepage names two real, specific commercial platforms as an unverifiable comparison point
`Dashboard.tsx`'s "Market Ecosystem Triage" banner (rendered on the live homepage, above the fold) read: *"QuantCurb's proprietary AI engine audits the global financial stack. We bridge the gap between low-latency institutional platforms (**FactSet, Aladdin**) and modern retail convenience (Robinhood, Wise)."*

FactSet and Aladdin (BlackRock's institutional risk-management platform) are real, named commercial products QuantCurb has no actual relationship to, integration with, or benchmarked comparison against — this is a bigger trust/E-E-A-T liability than the generic "banking-grade"/"Tier-1 global banks" language already fixed in PR #67/#89, since it names specific real companies' products rather than a generic superlative. Confirmed via `grep` this was the only remaining instance of FactSet/Aladdin naming in rendered site copy (a second reference in `services/geminiService.ts` is an AI-prompt for the separate Market Insights tool, not static site copy, and doesn't reach the crawlable HTML — confirmed via a live `curl` of `/market-intelligence-pulse`, no Bloomberg/FactSet/Aladdin/score text present in the SSR output; logged as a lower-priority follow-up below, not fixed today, since it would need a look at the tool's actual runtime output over several checks, not a one-line edit).

Replaced with the sourced-claim pattern this site already uses on its About page (IRS tax tables, Federal Reserve rates, exact amortization formulas) instead of naming unrelated third-party products.

**Also reconfirmed, not fixed today (flagged for a future run):** the homepage H1 ("Institutional Financial Modeling for Daily Wealth") and About page H1 ("Institutional Logic, Daily Wealth") both lean on "Institutional" as core brand positioning — not a false/unverifiable claim on its own the way naming a specific competitor product is, but worth a second look given today's brief explicitly flags "Institutional" as a jargon/trust-risk pattern. Left untouched today to keep this PR to one smallest-safe-slice; a full brand-copy pass is a bigger, separate decision.

## Competitor watch — mortgage/PITI cluster (rotating to this pillar; salary/paycheck and DCF clusters are both fully shipped/queued)
Ran the three brief-specified queries via WebSearch:
- `"mortgage PITI calculator"`
- `"how much house can I afford 2026"`
- `"mortgage payment calculator PMI property tax"`

Field is unchanged from the 17 Sep read logged on the Content Engine board: Bankrate, Zillow, NerdWallet, Wells Fargo, Fannie Mae, U.S. Bank, Fidelity, Credible, Ameriprise, plus thin single-purpose tool sites (usmortgagecalculator.org, mortgagecalculator.org, quickmortgagecalculator.org, smartermortgagecalc.com). No new entrant. The already-established "no upsell agenda + breadth" wedge holds — Zillow's business is real-estate lead-gen, bank calculators exist to sell their own loan products.

**Two new, genuine content gaps found** (queued to the Content Engine board, not written today — today's SEO fix plus a 4-day-old PR backlog is enough for one run, and neither gap has been scoped/sourced yet per this board's own "don't ship same-day as brief" discipline):
1. Why the first real mortgage payment doesn't match the calculator estimate — post-purchase property tax reassessment (a new purchase price usually triggers a reassessment above the prior owner's frozen assessed value, so the "T" in a pre-purchase PITI estimate is often understated). None of the 9+ competitor calculators/pages read today explain this.
2. The year-two escrow shortage — mortgage servicers recalculate escrow annually, and a common surprise is a lump-sum shortage payment demanded after year one when tax/insurance premiums rise. Not covered by any of the read competitors either.

Both target real, checkable IRS/servicer mechanics (not invented figures) and extend the existing Mortgage Payment Calculator's own honest limitation, the same pattern already used for the local-tax and SDI/PFL pieces on the salary side.

author: copilot
body:
This PR adds a real Voice Studio flow to V5 without regressing the existing V4/V5 YouTube/project/pipeline features. It introduces configurable voice providers, guarded voice cloning, subtitle-timed dubbing, and V5-native UI/pipeline integration with honest failure modes when providers are not configured.

- **Voice provider architecture**
  - Added a provider-based voice service with:
    - local/offline **Windows SAPI** adapter
    - configurable **HTTP/API** adapter
  - Preserved the no-fake-provider boundary: unconfigured providers now fail with explicit guidance instead of pretending to generate audio.
  - Enforced authorization gating for voice usage and cloning; cloning only proceeds when the user explicitly confirms ownership/authorization.
  - Added validation for:
    - voice sample format / size / duration
    - output format (`wav` / `mp3`)
    - provider settings (speed, pitch, pause, fit strategy)

- **Subtitle dubbing and media assembly**
  - Added timed dubbing from `.srt`, `.vtt`, and `.txt` sources.
  - Rendered audio per subtitle/sentence segment, preserved silence between segments, and added overflow handling with `speed`, `trim`, or `warn`.
  - Composed final audio tracks safely and muxed them into video via FFmpeg.
  - Preserved non-audio source streams during muxing instead of collapsing the source container to a single video stream.

- **Pipeline / workflow integration**
  - Extended the background pipeline with Voice Studio tasks:
    - `preview_voice`
    - `generate_voice`
    - `dub_video`
  - Stored warnings/logs for timed audio and dubbing paths.
  - Kept status transitions compatible with the existing V5 workflow state machine.
  - Added backward-compatible project metadata for provider/settings/source-path persistence.

- **UI integration**
  - Added a dedicated **Voice Studio** page in the V5 UI.
  - Exposed:
    - provider selection
    - voice profile
    - language / speed / pitch / emotion / pause
    - sample upload
    - text/subtitle/video source selection
    - preview / generate / dub / cancel / download
  - Kept source-path state consistent across `.txt` and subtitle-driven flows.
  - Improved status refresh so background updates are reflected without stale UI state.

- **Config / packaging / docs**
  - Extended config templates with voice-specific settings such as HTTP timeout and provider guidance.
  - Updated README to document:
    - local vs API provider behavior
    - FFmpeg / ffprobe expectations
    - model-weight handling outside the repo
    - authorization requirements for voice use/cloning
    - Voice Studio and subtitle dubbing boundaries

- **Focused regression coverage**
  - Added/expanded unit coverage for:
    - voice settings validation
    - authorization failure paths
    - subtitle timing segmentation
    - malformed / non-WAV audio validation
    - project metadata persistence for source paths
    - pipeline success/failure behavior for preview, generate, and dub flows

Example of the new provider/settings path:

```python
from app.services.voice import VoiceProvider, VoiceSettings, VoiceStudioService

settings = VoiceSettings(
    provider='http',
    voice_profile='vi_female_01',
    language='vi-VN',
    speed=1.0,
    output_format='mp3',
    clone_enabled=True,
    sample_path='sample.wav',
    text_source_path='subtitle.srt',
```

author: codeabraham16
body:
Dos superficies **vivas y sin guarda**, encontradas preguntándole a cada guarda existente «¿se puede satisfacer **sin** arreglar el defecto?» y midiendo la respuesta con sonda de control.

## 1 · La columna que nadie leía

`CapsDesdeTexto` convierte la columna `caps` de la base en la lista que decide quién puede qué. `TestCapsIdaYVueltaYBasuraSeDescarta` la prueba con `[metrics, exec]` y con `"metrics, root ,,screen"`: **nunca le pasa `screen:view`**. Y en todo el repo hay **un** solo test que escribe ese literal, y sólo mira un mensaje de error.

O sea que la capacidad cuya razón de existir es la asimetría entre mirar y controlar era la única que el parser podía leer mal sin que nada se enterara.

**Medido** — con `case CapScreenView: set[CapScreen] = true`, una fila que concede sólo MIRAR se lee como CONTROLAR:

```
sonda, árbol MUTADO:  la columna `screen:view` se leyó como [screen]
                      MALO: la fila que sólo concede MIRAR permite CONTROLAR
sonda, árbol SANO:    la columna `screen:view` se leyó como [screen:view]

ok  musubi/internal/fleet   ok  musubi/internal/mcp   ok  musubi/internal/memory
```

`TestCadaCapacidadVaYVuelveSiendoEllaMisma` recorre el **enum entero**, no los dos casos de siempre. Lleva su control de que la tabla no se quedó corta —contra `CapsDelTier(TierAgente)`, el tier que las admite todas— y dice **en qué caso ese control deja de servir**, para que no se descubra con una guarda callada.

## 2 · `Permite` podía inventar implicaciones que `Implica` niega

`TestMirarNoEsControlarYControlarSiEsMirar` verifica los 25 pares de `Implica`. `TestElAparatoQueAdmiteControlarAdmiteMirar` dice custodiar «la implicación vale también en la matriz del aparato» y prueba **una** pareja, la de pantalla — nunca comprueba que no se cuele ninguna otra.

**Medido** — agregarle a `Permite` un `shell` ⇒ `exec` deja las dos guardas en verde, y los tres paquetes también:

```
sonda, árbol MUTADO:  MALO: aparato con caps [shell] → Permite(exec) = true,
                            pero Implica(shell, exec) = false
```

El hermano sano acota el hallazgo: una de las dos recorre la matriz entera y la otra no, y el agujero está exactamente en la que no.

`TestPermiteNoInventaUnaImplicacionQueImplicaNiega` recorre las 25 celdas con un aparato de **una sola capacidad** por celda —con varias, `Permite` devuelve en la primera que implica y la celda dejaría de decir cuál decidió— y cierra con el control del par que **sí** tiene que implicar: sin él, un `Permite` que devolviera `false` para todo pasaría la matriz salvo la diagonal.

> **La esperanza va clavada y no derivada de `Implica`**, y es la trampa de esta guarda: escribir `esperado := Implica(tiene, pedida)` es cómodo y la deja inútil — una mutación de `Implica` movería los dos lados a la vez y la guarda la certificaría sana. Se clava la regla del dominio.

## La colisión, contestada después de leer los dos motivos

El sabotaje de `TestCapsIdaYVueltaYBasuraSeDescarta` le rompe el ancla al nuevo. Se corrieron los dos:

| guarda | motivo del rojo |
|---|---|
| ida y vuelta | «obtuve `[root metrics screen]`» — una cap **desconocida** |
| la nueva | «la columna `screen:view` se leyó como `[screen]`» — una **conocida** leída como otra |

Dos guardas sobre el mismo `switch` desde ángulos que no se tapan. El `colision_ok` va en el **agresor**, que es de quien sale el `a` que rompe.

## Medido

- 3 sabotajes corridos: **3 ROJO** con motivos distintos, 0 verdes, 0 sin veredicto, 0 repetidos, 0 sospechosos.
- `arnes -validar`: 916 anclas · 903 mecanizadas · 12 exentas · 1 en prosa · 98,6 % — 0 rotas, 0 huérfanas, 0 colisiones sin contestar.
- `go test ./...` verde · `golangci-lint` 0 issues.

author: fonvillanueva
body:
## 📋 Planning only — nothing is implemented

**This PR adds one Markdown file and nothing else.** It exists so the Phase 4 security model can be reviewed *before* any of it is built.

**Revision 3**, head `dabc654`, **rebased onto the post-PR-#4 `main` (`15c9669`)**.

### ✅ The sequencing requirement is now satisfied

PR #4 (the Tailwind scope prerequisite) **merged as `15c9669`**, and this branch has been rebased onto it. That was the one thing blocking this PR from merging: until #4 landed, any change under `docs/` — including this document — altered the shipped CSS.

**A build from this branch is now byte-identical to the post-#4 `main` baseline**, so merging this plan changes no shipped byte.

| Artifact | This branch | Post-#4 `main` | |
|---|---|---|---|
| CSS | 24 469 bytes · `bfc854089977` | 24 469 bytes · `bfc854089977` | **identical** |
| JS | 224 373 bytes · `cce022c033bc` | 224 373 bytes · `cce022c033bc` | **identical** |
| `.fixed` / `.invisible` / `.grow` | absent | absent | ✅ |
| `.visible` | present | present | ✅ retained via `src/App.test.jsx` |

Still a **draft** — held for the reviewer, not for a blocker.

### The entire diff

```
A	docs/phase-4-auth-plan.md
 1 file changed, 1120 insertions(+)
```

Verified by assertion, not by eye: exactly one path, status `A`, and that path is `docs/phase-4-auth-plan.md`. No `.sql`, `.mjs`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.json`, `.css`, `.html`; nothing under `src/`, `supabase/` or `scripts/`; no dependency or `.env` change. Secrets sweep clean.

### Post-rebase verification

```
diff scope        1 file — docs/phase-4-auth-plan.md
CSS               24 469 bytes, md5 bfc854089977 — identical to main @ 15c9669
JS                identical to main @ 15c9669
classes           .fixed absent · .invisible absent · .grow absent · .visible present
Test Files        10 passed (10)
Tests             275 passed (275)
eslint .          exit 0, no output
vite build        ✓ clean
secrets sweep     clean
```

### Not done

No Supabase change · no Vercel change · no deploy · no app connection · no user creation · no data import · no migration · no dependency · **PR #3 not merged** · PR #5 not begun.

---

## 📐 §11 measurement, corrected — and now confirmed by the merge

Revision 3 originally said PR #4 removes **51 bytes and two rules**. That was measured against *this planning branch* rather than `main`. Corrected throughout §11, and the merge has since borne it out:

| Variant | CSS bytes | Δ | md5 | Rules removed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (`main` @ `3dc59ae`) | 24 491 | — | `baf6880ea9bb` | — |
| `scripts/` only | 24 491 | **0** | `baf6880ea9bb` | none |
| `docs/` only | 24 469 | **−22** | `bfc854089977` | `.fixed` |
| **`docs/` + `scripts/` (PR #4, merged)** | **24 469** | **−22** | `bfc854089977` | `.fixed` |

- Against `main` at `3dc59ae`, PR #4 removed one generated rule — `.fixed{position:fixed}` — **22 bytes**.
- **`.invisible` was absent from `main`**: its only remaining source is `supabase/`, excluded since Phase 3.
- **This document's prose would otherwise have introduced `.invisible`, 29 bytes.** A second instance surfaced while writing the correction: the word *"grow"* emitted `.grow{flex-grow:1}`, 18 bytes, so pre-rebase this branch carried **47 bytes** over `main`.
- **PR #4 removed 22 bytes immediately and prevented the further 47 this branch would have added** — confirmed above: all three rules are now absent and the bundle is byte-identical. The old 51-byte figure came from comparing against the planning branch; `22 + 29 = 51`.
- **`.visible` remains generated** from `src/App.test.jsx`, which stays scanned.
- **Excluding `scripts/` was a byte-identical no-op**, same md5 as baseline — kept so a future script cannot quietly grow the bundle.

The wording that generates `.grow` was left as written rather than contorted to dodge the scanner. That trade is backwards: documentation should read well and the build should stop reading documentation — which is exactly what PR #4 arranged.

---

## What the document contains

| Section | Covers |
|---|---|
| **0. One role, three people** | Why every signed-in person is the same database role, and what that means for reading the matrices |
| **1. Permission matrix** | Every table × operation for fon, abigail, accountability, anon, and the *authenticated-but-unprofiled* state a stray signup lands in |
| **2. Auth flow** | Supabase Auth free tier, invite-only enrolment, and the assertion that **nothing auto-creates a profile** |
| **3.1 – 3.2** | Role-function properties; complete grant enumeration |
| **3.3** | **Exhaustive expected-policy table** — source of truth for Check 4 |
| **3.4** | Checks 4, 5, 5a and 6 as exact bidirectional allowlists, with injections and the named test files |
| **3.5 – 3.9** | Policy shape, session-scoped stamping, view design, Check 20, Phase 3 preservation |
| **4. Threat model** | T1–T22 with controls and residuals |
| **5. Migration & rollback** | 11 steps, import **last**; rollback is database-only |
| **6. Tests** | Cross-user negatives, catalog-shape checks, failure injection |
| **7. Session controls** | CSP, JWT lifetime, refresh rotation, sign-out — blocking prerequisites for import |
| **8 – 10** | Environment variables; manual steps; verified Vercel protection scope |
| **11. Tailwind scope** | The corrected measurement above |
| **12. PR sequence** | Ordered by **merge order**, with acceptance criteria for #5 and #6 |
| **D1–D6** | All resolved; **D5a** open, with an invariant keeping it open |

---

## The correction that reshaped revision 2

**PostgREST authenticates all three people as the same database role, `authenticated`.** There is no per-person database role. Table grants are therefore *identical* for Fon, Abigail and the accountability viewer; **all separation lives in the RLS policies**.

Two things follow that a reviewer should check directly:

1. `DELETE` **must** be granted on `tasks` for Fon's delete to work at all. Abigail is blocked by the **absence of a DELETE policy**, not by the grant. Reading only the grants gives the opposite answer.
2. Phase 3's Check 4 (*"Zero policies"*), Check 5 and Check 6 **necessarily start failing** the moment Phase 4 adds a policy or a grant. All three are redefined as **exact, bidirectional allowlists** — never relaxed.

---

## Resolved decisions — D1–D6

| | Decision | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| **D1** | Abigail's delete rights | **Archive-only.** No DELETE policy for her; `status='archived'` is permitted by her UPDATE policy. |
| **D2** | Can Abigail see Fon's *private* Family/Home tasks? | **No** — `visibility='shared'` in both `USING` and `WITH CHECK`. PR #6 must keep sharing state **visibly** indicated. |
| **D3** | Role-management surface | **Dashboard/SQL only, permanently.** No write policy *or grant* on `profiles`, ever. |
| **D4** | Vercel deployment protection | **Leave exactly as-is and depend on nothing about it.** Verified scope is `all_except_custom_domains` — broader than "preview-scoped". |
| **D5** | MFA | **Fon enrolls TOTP before real data import.** Mapped to *credential compromise*, not session theft. |
| **D5a** | MFA for the other two | **Open — Fon's call.** Held open by an invariant (below). |
| **D6** | Accountability and School task content | **Titles yes, notes never.** Recorded deliberately: anything in a School task title is visible to the accountability viewer. |

---

## Key requirements in revision 3

**Check 4 is an exact, bidirectional policy allowlist** keyed on `(table, policy name, command, roles)` and pinned to `PERMISSIVE`. An unmatched row on either side fails. Nine over-policy injections, including a `profiles` write policy and an unexpected second `tasks` policy `using (true)` — permissive policies are OR-ed, so one such policy silently defeats every other row predicate.

**§3.3 enumerates exactly 15 policies** — 7 on `tasks`, 7 on `area_notes`, 1 on `profiles`, **0 on `audit_log`**, `idempotency_keys` and `import_batches`.

author: sisshiki1969
body:
Tests only, following #1550 (#1460). Measured against CRuby 4.0.6.

That PR's cells were well covered, but codecov flagged 14 lines of the new `jis_direct_one` as untested — all of them the arms that decide what an **ill-formed** byte run reaches. Those are exactly where the error class and the run boundary get decided, so they are worth pinning:

- a lead byte with a bad trail (`\xA1A`, `\xA1 `, `\xA1\xFF`, `\x81 `, `\x81\x7F`, `\x81\xFD`)
- a `8E` half-width katakana prefix with a bad second byte
- a `8F` JIS X 0212 prefix, truncated and with a bad second byte
- a lead byte at end of input, both encodings
- each of the above again under `invalid: :replace` / `undef: :replace`, which is where it shows whether the disproving byte was **read again** or swallowed with the run
- the same three through `Encoding::Converter`, where an incomplete tail is the next call's to finish rather than an error, plus the `primitive_errinfo` it reports

`\x80` and `\xFD` are deliberately left out: those never begin a Shift_JIS sequence, and the run monoruby reports for them is **#1546** — the pivoted paths get it wrong in the same way, so it is not this path's to fix and the test would pin the wrong answer.

Full suite green (4310 tests).

body: ## Summary Challenge and silent drill sheets were unreadable: the title (`The Lord is the board`) and section labels (`Steadfast`, `Guided prayer`, `Silent touch`, `Reflection`) rendered black on the `#12141c` card. author: sara-agent
body:
On a 390 px phone the live site showed **"Long March 6A | Unknown Payload 1"** and **"… Payload 2"**
as one unreadable line.

## Measured

Pairwise overlap of visible label boxes, sampled every 500 ms for 20 s of a live boot at 390×844:

| | samples with an overlap | worst frame |
|---|---|---|
| production | **33 of 40** | 3 overlapping pairs |
| this PR | **0 of 40** | 0 |

Examples from production: Long March 12A over Long March 6A over Nuri — every fresh launch.

## Why

`chooseLabels` drops a label whose **anchor** is within 24 px of another's. A label is not an anchor;
it is a box as wide as its name. Two payloads from one launch fly metres apart, their anchors land
thirty-odd pixels apart on the same row, both pass, and the boxes overprint. `clampLabelX` can also
slide a box sideways into its neighbour after the anchor test has passed it.

## Fix

Both need the real width, which exists only after measuring — so the check runs there. `update()`
already measured every box in one layout pass; it now places them and `keepClearOf()` keeps each
one only if it overlaps no box kept before it. The order is `chooseLabels`' own — selection, train,
nearest notable — so the more important name survives.

`keepClearOf` is pure; `tests/test_labels.mjs` pins it starting from the reproduction.

body:
Fix the Advanced Security finding in battle replay formatting and simplify the release pipeline. Replay details now convert only the engine’s line separators and rely on React text escaping; nested-markup regression coverage protects that behavior.

Same-repository PRs targeting `staging` now deploy the exact verified merge artifact when opened or updated. Merges into protected `master` continue to deploy production. One shared deployment job replaces duplicate staging/production jobs, serializes alias uploads, and preserves artifact provenance and required check names. CodeQL now runs on staging PRs too. Fork/Dependabot PRs validate without deployment credentials; manual runs validate only.

Remove redundant staging-push builds and standalone typechecking (already included in build), reduce artifact compression, and add structural workflow validation with 11 regression cases. Keep canonical production verification mandatory, but fail immediately with the Cloudflare Ray ID when an interactive challenge makes polling futile.

Validation: 154 unit tests; lint; TypeScript; workflow policy; bundled data; scale characterization; production build and full browser suite; zero npm audit vulnerabilities.

The canonical production failure was caused by Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode. After the domain owner disabled it, rerunning only the failed canonical verification job passed both readiness/indexability and the deployed browser suite, without redeploying production: https://github.com/JacobGain/pvpoke-team-lab/actions/runs/35448901981.

L'audit geometrico cittadino mantiene difetti documentati, non risolti da v11. Nessuna operazione su Netlify.
